  • The reconciler is level-triggered. Every 10 seconds, it compares each active run with the status from the executor. This status is the source of truth for liveness. If a run sends no events, the reconciler only marks it stalled. If an execution disappears, the reconciler tries it again as a new attempt (in a cost window). The reconciler adopts orphaned executions by their nonce.
  • The finalizer changes a finished execution into a model version (see Storage and integrity).
  • Events: the orchestrator verifies them and removes duplicates on (run, attempt, seq). It keeps one run_progress row for each run. It also keeps run_events for state changes, warnings, diagnostics and metrics. A PostgreSQL NOTIFY starts the SSE streams of each API process again.

The Run protocol gives the state machine, all the transitions and the owner of each transition.

docs.title: The run sandbox
docs.text:
Each run gets a new pair of processes: a trusted supervisor and an untrusted worker. This applies to all types of run (ingest, describe, validate, fit, score).

sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant S as Object store
    participant X as Executor
    participant R as Supervisor
    participant W as Worker (SDK + plugin)
    D->>S: PUT bootstrap/{nonce}: RunSpec (signed URLs, HMAC key, limits)
    D->>X: submit(MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE)
    X->>R: start (no secrets in argv or env)
    R->>S: GET bootstrap/{nonce}, then DELETE it
    R->>S: GET inputs (signed, generation-pinned, CRC32C-checked)
    R->>W: spawn: scrubbed env, separate uid (where possible), python -I
    W-->>R: progress, logs, results (framed JSON over a socketpair)
    R-->>D: stdout: one HMAC-signed event per line
    R->>S: POST outputs (V4 POST policy on the attempt prefix)
    R->>S: PUT manifest.json (signed claim of every object)
    R-->>D: "complete" event, exit 0
  • No credentials in the environment. The executor sends only MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE. The signed URLs of the run and its event HMAC key are in a one-time bootstrap object. The supervisor reads and deletes this object before model code starts.
  • The worker is untrusted. It runs the SDK harness and the plugin with an allow-listed environment (with all MAPI_* removed), in its own session. When the supervisor runs as root (containers, Cloud Run), the worker runs under uid 10001 with no_new_privs. It communicates only with the supervisor, through length-prefixed JSON frames. Each frame must agree with its schema.
  • Only the supervisor writes events. Its stdout has one JSON event on each line. Each event has a sequence number and an HMAC. All text that the worker prints becomes a log event. The log event has a size limit and has no control characters.
  • Limits everywhere. There are limits for log lines (4 KB) and total logs (20 MB), event size, output objects and bytes, and a scratch budget for each resource class. If a run goes above a limit, the result is SANDBOX_VIOLATION or RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The platform never cuts results silently.
  • Checkpoints. On SIGTERM or near the deadline, a PyMC fit writes its last segment, and the supervisor uploads a partial manifest. The run can continue from that point.

On a laptop, the worker cannot change the user, so runs report DEV_MODE_ISOLATION. The process split, the scrubbed environment, the event signatures and the output verification continue to apply. But the worker runs as you. See the security model.

docs.title: Storage and integrity
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph buckets["Buckets: mapi-{env}-*"]
        q["quarantine<br/>uploads, 7-day lifecycle"]
        b["bootstrap<br/>one-time RunSpecs"]
        r["runs<br/>attempt scratch"]
        bun["bundles<br/>write-once, retention lock"]
        d["data<br/>content-addressed datasets"]
    end
    browser(("browser /<br/>client")) -->|"signed PUT"| q
    q -->|"signed GET"| ingest["ingest run"]
    ingest -->|"POST policy"| r
    r -->|"verify, then<br/>server-side copy"| d
    fit["fit / score run"] -->|"POST policy"| r
    r -->|"verify, then<br/>server-side copy"| bun
    bun -->|"signed GET, minted after<br/>the manifest signature checks"| client(("client"))
Bucket Who writes Who reads quarantine Browsers and clients, through a signed PUT for one object Ingest runs, through a signed GET bootstrap The dispatcher The supervisor, with a principal that can only get and delete there (no list) runs Runs, through a POST policy with a limit to their attempt prefix and a size range The finalizer (metadata) bundles Only the finalizer, with a server-side copy. Write-once under a retention lock Clients and runs, through signed GETs that the platform makes after verification data The finalizer, with a server-side copy of ingest outputs Runs, through signed GETs

Outputs are claims. When a run ends, the finalizer lists the attempt prefix. It reads the metadata of each object: the size, CRC32C, MD5 and generation that the store calculated. It compares these values with the signed manifest of the run. It refuses missing, changed or unexpected objects (INTEGRITY_FAILURE). It validates the small JSON sidecars under size limits and sanitizes the plots. Then it copies the verified generations into the bundles bucket.

Then the finalizer signs a bundle manifest. The manifest binds the tenant, the run, the spec hash, the data hash, the catalog digest and each destination generation. Locally, an EC P-256 key replaces Cloud KMS. The platform makes each subsequent download link only after it checks that signature. Thus, it can never serve an object that was replaced. Bundles are zarr zips and JSON. The platform does not use pickle.

docs.title: The event path
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    W["Worker"] -->|"frames"| S["Supervisor"]
    S -->|"stdout:<br/>{mapi_event, hmac}"| P{{"local executor:<br/>stdout pipe"}}
    S -.->|"v0.3: Cloud Logging<br/>→ Pub/Sub push"| I["POST /internal/events"]
    P --> V["Verify HMAC ·<br/>dedupe (run, attempt, seq)"]
    I --> V
    V -->|"progress: upsert"| RP[("run_progress")]
    V -->|"state, warning, diagnostic,<br/>metric, complete, error"| RE[("run_events")]
    RE -->|"NOTIFY"| SSE["SSE streams<br/>Last-Event-ID resume"]
    RP --> SSE
    SSE --> C(("web app ·<br/>CLI · client"))

Locally, the executor reads events directly from the stdout of the supervisor. In the cloud, the same lines go through Cloud Logging and Pub/Sub to POST /internal/events. The verification is the same. The platform combines progress into one event every two or three seconds and keeps it as one row. Thus, a long fit does not write thousands of rows. The platform keeps only state changes, warnings, diagnostics, checkpoints, metrics and terminal events. It sends these events again to a client that connects again.

docs.title: The integration paths (v0.4)
docs.text:
Three paths send the results of a model out of the platform. No path gives more data to the outside world than it needs. An endpoint call runs in a sandbox, as all scores do. A webhook sends only ids and states. An embed link shows one chart.

flowchart LR
    subgraph out["Outside"]
        app["Sheets · BI ·<br/>your app"]
        rcv["Your webhook<br/>receiver"]
        viewer["A viewer's browser<br/>(Notion, Looker Studio, …)"]
    end
    subgraph cp["Control plane"]
        ep["POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score<br/>score:<alias> token · input contract ·<br/>CoordPlan · rate limit and budget"]
        outbox[("events outbox<br/>written in the same<br/>transaction as the change")]
        relay["Worker relay<br/>retries · SSRF guard ·<br/>HMAC signature"]
        embed["GET /v1/embeds/{token}<br/>no credentials ·<br/>one platform-recipe plot"]
    end
    sb["Score run<br/>(fresh sandbox)"]
    bun[("Verified bundles")]
    page["Plot sandbox origin<br/>/embed/<token>"]

    app -->|"inline XrJSON"| ep --> sb --> bun
    ep -->|"signed links to the outputs"| app
    sb -. "score.completed" .-> outbox
    outbox --> relay -->|"Mapi-Signature"| rcv
    viewer --> page -->|"fetch, CSP-limited"| embed
    embed -->|"data inlined from the<br/>verified bundle"| bun
  • Endpoints freeze the input contract of the model version at promotion. Thus, the platform checks a call statically (dims, coordinates, future covariates) before it starts a run. The platform keeps the payload as a run input and decodes it only in the sandbox. Promotion goes through the scorecard gate.
  • Webhooks: the platform writes them to an outbox in the same transaction as the change that they report (a finished run, a model version that is ready, a promotion). Then the worker delivers them through the SSRF guard. The worker signs, retries and logs each delivery.
  • Embeds: the platform serves them to a page on the origin of the plot sandbox. This page can get only the public embed view. The API puts the data of the plot from the verified bundle into the page, and does not decode it (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Where to read more
docs.text:
• Run protocol: states, bootstrap, the wire format of events, exit codes, manifests and the storage layout.
  • Runner: the guarantees of the supervisor.
  • GCS shim: the local object store, its buckets and principals.
  • Security model: the controls on a laptop, and the controls that production adds.
  • HTTP API and the OpenAPI explorer.

docs.title: Bundles
docs.text:
A bundle contains all the results of a fit that scoring needs. Its form is safe to store, move and read again. A bundle is one bundle.zarr.zip and four JSON sidecars.

fruit-demand-v1/
├── bundle.zarr.zip      # one zarr v3 zip: the whole fitted model as an xr.DataTree
├── manifest.json        # identity, provenance, lineage and the hashes of every file
├── metrics.json         # holdout metrics (computed through the score path)
├── diagnostics.json     # convergence and sanity checks, expert and plain-language
├── plots.json           # rendered, sanitized plots for outputs.plots
└── evaluation/          # evaluate_then_refit: the train-only bundle behind the metrics

docs.title: Write, read, verify
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

Bundle.read calculates the size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of each file again. Then it compares them with the manifest. If a bundle is damaged or changed without permission, Bundle.read raises BundleError (INTEGRITY_FAILURE).

docs.title: What is inside
docs.text:
print(manifest.role, manifest.plugin["id"], manifest.spec_hash[:19])
# production tabular.regressor sha256:...
print(manifest.files["bundle.zarr.zip"])  # size, crc32c, md5 (GCS forms) and sha256
print(manifest.lineage["evaluation_bundle"])  # the train-only fit behind the metrics

tree = again.to_tree()  # the whole bundle as one xr.DataTree
print(sorted(tree.children))
# ['binding', 'fit_coords', 'model', 'native', 'preprocess', 'schema', 'spec']
print(sorted(tree["preprocess"].children))  # ['cal', 'logy']: one node per step
Node Holds /spec The canonical spec and the resolved spec (pinned versions, the schema of each stage) /schema/raw, /schema/model The data contract at the input and at the model stage /binding Canonical ↔ dataset names, reversed on each output /preprocess/<step> For each step: the learned JSON state, labelled arrays and the context tail for each group /model The manifest, settings, fit config and learned JSON /model/<group> ArviZ-named groups: posterior, sample_stats, log_likelihood, observed_data, … /terminal_state Sequential models: the filtered state at the last fitted step /native Safe native artifacts: skops files, xgboost JSON, … /derived/<name> Derived quantities cached at fit (contributions, response curves) /fit_coords/<stage> The fitted coordinates at each stage (CoordPlan checks against them) /side_tables/<name> pinned side tables, frozen with the fit /thin The thinning index for draws, for the full bundle

docs.title: No pickle, ever
docs.text:
Pickle runs code when it loads. Thus pickle must not be in an artifact that moves between users, services and sandboxes.

  • Model groups are labelled arrays in zarr. Settings, states and manifests are JSON.
  • Native estimators are stored as skops or xgboost JSON. When skops loads a file, it first lists the types in the file. It refuses all types that are not on the allow list of that estimator.
  • Some FitOutput.native entries look like pickle (.pkl, .joblib, .pt, pickle magic bytes, …). The platform rejects these entries when it writes a bundle and when it reads a bundle. The contract kit checks this for each plugin.

docs.title: Hashes in the forms object stores report
docs.text: The platform records CRC32C and MD5 in base64, the same as Google Cloud Storage calculates them on upload. The platform binds a signed manifest to the object generations and to the hashes that the server calculated. Thus a person cannot replace or replay an uploaded artifact (see Storage and integrity). The platform also records SHA-256, for content addressing.

docs.title: Lineage
docs.text:
The manifest records the spec hash, the data hash, the version of the plugin and of each step, and the library versions of the fit. manifest.lineage links a production bundle to its evaluation bundle. Thus you can always find which data and which code made a forecast.

Next: Coord plans and typed errors.

docs.title: Capabilities and manifests
docs.text:
A model plugin describes itself with a manifest. The manifest is static JSON. It tells which data the plugin needs, what it can do, what it returns and which settings it accepts. The control plane validates specs and score requests against manifests. The Guided UI makes its forms from manifests. Neither of them imports the plugin.

from mapi_sdk import default_registry

registry = default_registry()
manifest = registry.model("mmm.bayesian@^1").manifest()
caps = manifest.capabilities

print(caps.representation.value, caps.inference)  # draws mcmc
print(sorted(caps.score_modes))
# ['counterfactual', 'evaluate', 'forecast', 'predict']
print(caps.decision, caps.contribution_scale)  # True additive
print(sorted(caps.owns))  # ['carryover', 'inverse_units', 'scaling']: mmm-framework owns them
print([d.name for d in manifest.derived])  # ['contributions', 'response_curves', 'marginal_cost']

basic = [k for k, v in manifest.settings_schema["properties"].items() if v.get("x-ui-level") == "basic"]
print(basic)  # ['adstock', 'saturation', 'trend', 'seasonality', 'hierarchy']: what Guided shows
print(manifest.about.title if manifest.about else None)  # Marketing mix model

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Field Meaning inference mcmc, vi, map, smc, kalman, point, bootstrap or custom representation draws, quantiles, interval, point or moments. See Representations score_modes The modes from predict, forecast, counterfactual, simulate, filter, evaluate that the model can do. All other modes give MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED. decision The model has an objective(fitted, decision) that returns a value for each draw, for budget optimisation. recommend The model can recommend candidates (Bayesian optimisation). fast_score The model has a compiled path for fast scoring (PyMC FrozenPredictor). contribution_scale additive, multiplicative or none. With additive, the sum of the contributions is the prediction. The contract kit checks this. loo_valid, loo_invalid_reason Tells if pointwise LOO has a meaning. The steps of an HMM are dependent. Thus ts.gaussian_hmm declares LOO invalid, and validation rejects elpd_loo. identified_quantities The parameters that are identified (for models with label switching or rotations). owns The preprocessing that the model does itself: scaling, carryover, inverse_units, recursion. The platform does not do these steps, and it labels the outputs to agree. deterministic_given_seed Tells if the same seed gives the same fit (nutpie: no). If a model claims this, the contract kit checks it. checkpointable Long fits can write checkpoints and resume. conditions_on_actuals Forecasts can have actuals. The model updates its state with them through its fitted parameters. Then it forecasts from the last actual (Forecasts with actuals). Without this capability, a forecast payload with target values gives ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED.

docs.title: The manifest
Steps have manifests too
docs.text:
Each step exports a catalog entry. The entry contains these items:

  • the settings JSON Schema and the kind of the step
  • if the step is stateful or invertible
  • the settings that name variables, dims and side tables
  • the context that the step needs
  • a schema effect template.

The runner images export the catalog when they are built. The API validates specs against the catalog. To see the catalog, read the steps catalog.

python -m mapi_steps.catalog --splits > catalog.json   # what the control plane loads

docs.title: Browse the built-ins
docs.text:
• Models catalog: the capabilities, outputs, derived quantities and settings of each installed model.
  • Plot recipes catalog.
  • Spec schema: all fields of ModelSpec and ScoreRequest.

docs.title: Coord plans and typed errors
docs.text: Before a score request goes to a model, the platform compares its coordinates with the fit coordinates of the model. These checks are the CoordPlan. Almost all of them need only metadata: the fitted coordinates of each stage (in the bundle) and the request. Thus, the API can reject a bad request in milliseconds, and it does not start a sandbox.

docs.title: The checks
docs.text:
Code HTTP Raised when What to do UNSEEN_LEVELS 422 A label of a fixed dim (or of a new_levels dim with strategy error) was not in the fit Remove the label. Or declare the dim new_levels with a strategy, and fit again COORD_NOT_ALLOWED 422 An extend dim starts before the fitted range, or a label cannot exist Send labels in the fitted range or immediately after it NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION 422 New time labels leave a gap after the fitted range Send the missing periods (context tails need them) HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT 409 The forecast goes past max_extension Fit again with a larger max_extension MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE 422 A future_required variable is missing in the horizon Put it in the payload CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 422 The output asks for a thing that the representation cannot give (the sum of quantiles, draws from a point model, an HDI from quantiles) Ask for a valid summary, or use a model with joint draws RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED 422 A target lag is shorter than the horizon Use longer lags, or use a model that owns recursion MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 The model does not declare the requested mode Look at the capabilities of the model SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE 422 A side table does not cover the periods that a step needs Supply a table that covers them ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 A forecast payload has target values (actuals) and the model cannot condition on them Fit again with the new data, or leave the target empty. See Forecasts with actuals ACTUALS_INVALID 422 Actuals leave a gap after the fit, or actuals after the fit do not have their drivers Fill the gap, or send the drivers

HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT is a 409, not a 422. The request is correct, but the model is not ready for it. To correct the problem, fit the model again. Do not change the request.

docs.title: Metadata only: what the API checks
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import CoordPlan
from mapi_spec import load_score_request, validate_score_request

# What the API stores next to a model version: JSON only, no arrays, no plugin code.
meta = CoordPlan(load_score_request(FORECAST), bundle.resolved, bundle.fit_coords).metadata()
print(f"{len(meta.model_dump_json()) / 1024:.0f} KiB of metadata")

request = load_score_request(FORECAST + "output: {summary: [hdi_90], draws: 100}\n")
for issue in validate_score_request(request, meta):  # no data, no model: milliseconds
    print(issue.code, issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE /data - forecasting needs future values of ['price', 'promo'] ...
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/draws - draws were requested but the model's
#                                        representation is 'quantiles'
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/summary/0 - summary 'hdi_90' cannot be computed from
#                                            'quantiles' output

The API reports all problems at the same time. Each problem has a JSON pointer into the request. The metadata is a few kilobytes of JSON for each model version. The API does not decode arrays and does not import plugin code.

docs.title: In the runtime: the same checks, then canonicalisation
docs.text:
score_bundle does the same checks on the real payload, so it can also see which values are present. It raises the most specific error. It keeps the other notices in the issues attribute of the output (for example "1 new level of store will use strategy pooled").

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))

Then it canonicalises the data at the model stage. Thus, a plugin does not have to know about the request order or new labels:

  1. Reorder each fixed and new_levels dim to the fit order. Posterior arrays use position as the index, so county_03 must have the same position as at fit time.
  2. Pad requested subsets to the full fitted set (masked), so that the shapes are the same as in the fit.
  3. Append new levels after the fitted levels. A boolean coordinate <dim>__is_new flags them. <dim>__requested marks the real labels (not the padding).
  4. Call plugin.score(...).
  5. Select the requested labels again, in the request order, and remove the helper coordinates.
flowchart LR
    R["request: county_07, county_02, county_new"] --> O["fit order<br/>county_00 … county_07"]
    O --> P["+ county_new<br/>county__is_new = True"]
    P --> S["plugin.score"]
    S --> B["select back:<br/>county_07, county_02, county_new"]

In a plugin, mapi_sdk.new_level_mask(ds, "county") gives the __is_new flags. ScoreContext.strategy("county") gives the new-level strategy that applies. PyMC models get all of this automatically through ctx.hier_effect(...). See Bring a PyMC model.

docs.title: Errors are values, not strings
docs.text:
Each error is a MapiError with:

  • A stable code (an ErrorCode) and an HTTP status.
  • A detail that the platform writes, and the list of issues that cause it. Each issue can have a suggested_action.
  • A JSON pointer to the field that has the problem.
  • untrusted_text: all text from a dataset or a plugin. The platform keeps it separate from the message. Thus, a UI can show it as plain text, and an agent can use it as data, never as instructions.

On HTTP, an error is an RFC 7807 problem document. For the full list, see Error codes.

Next: Capabilities and manifests.

docs.title: Forecasts with actuals
docs.text:
You fit a model one time, but new numbers continue to come. For example, the sales of last month arrive, or a preliminary figure gets a revision. A forecast request can send these actuals together with the dates to forecast. The model updates its state with the actuals and the parameters of the fit. It does not estimate the parameters again. Then it forecasts from the last actual. Thus, you do not have to fit again to move the forecast origin forward.

The model does not ignore the data that you send. If a model cannot use actuals, it refuses the request with ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. Each forecast answer tells which data the model conditioned on.

docs.title: Sending actuals and future dates
docs.text:
Use mode: forecast with a payload (data, or an inline dataset on an endpoint). The payload must have the target along the time dim. For each series:

  • A period with a target value is an actual.
  • A period with an empty target (null, a blank cell, NaN) after the last actual is a period to forecast.
{
  "mode": "forecast",
  "horizon": {"dim": "t", "periods": 8},
  "future_covariates": "carry_last",
  "output": {"summary": ["median", "q5", "q95"]},
  "data": {
    "coords": {"t": {"dims": ["t"], "data": ["1961-01-01", "1961-02-01", "1961-03-01",
                                            "1961-04-01", "1961-05-01"]}},
    "data_vars": {"y": {"dims": ["t"], "data": [417, 391, 419, null, null]}}
  }
}

This request updates the airline model with January to March 1961, and forecasts April and May. In a spreadsheet, the Input sheet of the endpoint is the same table. It has one row for each month. Fill the target column where you have actuals. Leave it blank where you want a forecast. The driver columns are next to the target column.

t y price 1961-01-01 417 10.5 1961-02-01 391 10.5 1961-03-01 419 10.9 1961-04-01 11.0 1961-05-01

GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/schema gives actuals_example for endpoints with a model that can do this. It is a call with inline data for the periods after the fit, with all values empty, for you to fill. The schema also gives input_table for all endpoints. It is the same table as columns: the time column first, then the target, the drivers and the other inputs. Each column tells what it contains. For a forecast endpoint, the table also has the periods after the fit as empty rows. All clients read that layout:

From How Google Sheets The Input sheet of the generated Apps Script (Connect Google Sheets). A second function makes the sheet Python api.endpoints.forecast(alias, rows) with a DataFrame or rows, or actuals= and future= (The Python client) The terminal mapi endpoints forecast ALIAS input.csv (The command line) The web app The Schema tab of the endpoint: Your latest actuals and the dates to forecast, then Use in the call curl, TypeScript, R The snippets of the endpoint add the call for the periods after the fit, for you to fill

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
The source of the forecast periods. If the payload has periods after the last actual, the model forecasts only those periods. It does not use horizon.periods. If the two are different, a warning in issues tells you. If the payload ends with an actual, the model forecasts horizon.periods periods after it. If the actuals only revise fitted periods, the forecast starts after the end of the fit. The fitted periods between them keep their values and get one-step-ahead predictions. Some payloads have no period after the fit and no actual: no rows, or only fitted periods with an empty target. For these payloads, the model forecasts horizon.periods periods after the fit, as for a call without data. horizon.dim always gives the time dim.

Actuals continue the fitted history. The first actual can be the period immediately after the fit, or an earlier period. Actuals in the fitted range replace the fitted values for those periods (revised data), and the forecast conditions on the revision. An empty target in the fitted range keeps the fitted value. An empty target between the end of the fit and the last actual is a gap, and gives ACTUALS_INVALID. The exception is a model that accepts missing observations (its input schema accepts a missing target, as the state-space models do). This model filters the gap as missing data. Empty targets in the fitted range are never gaps. Thus, all models accept revisions of separate fitted periods, with or without new actuals after the fit. Coordinates that skip periods give NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, as for all score requests.

Only the values that you send are actuals. Some pipeline steps fill missing targets. An example is core.impute with ffill or mean, which fills the gaps of the fitted history. Such a step never changes an empty target that you send into an actual. The model forecasts the periods that you leave blank.

Drivers. A model with drivers needs them on the actual periods after the fit. These are the values that occurred with the actuals. If they are missing, the result is ACTUALS_INVALID. On the periods to forecast, empty drivers follow future_covariates:

  • supplied (the default) refuses them (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE).
  • carry_last, seasonal_naive and zero fill them from the fitted history and the drivers of the actual periods. Thus, carry_last repeats the latest value that you sent.

The model never changes the values that you send.

Panels. For a univariate model, each series conditions on its own actuals and forecasts from its own last actual. (A series is a cell of the other dims of the target, for example a store or a geo.) Thus, the series can end at different dates. Series that the model models jointly are one system: the variables of ts.var, ts.vecm, ts.varmax and ts.dynamic_factor. Each of these series needs a value on each actual period after the fit. If not, the result is ACTUALS_INVALID.

The parameters do not change. Conditioning is a filter, not a fit. For a state-space model, it is results.append(new, refit=False) of statsmodels (or apply when actuals revise the fitted range). For an autoregression, it is the new lags. Fit the model again at intervals, so that the parameters use the new data.

docs.title: What the answer says
docs.text:
Each forecast has a conditioning record. It is in the inline summary (ScoreCallResult.summary.conditioning), in the result.json of the run and in the root attribute conditioning of the result tree:

{
  "dim": "t",
  "fit_end": "1960-12-01",
  "conditioned": true,
  "n_actuals": 3,
  "actuals_through": "1961-03-01",
  "revised": 0,
  "series_conditioned": 1,
  "n_series": 1,
  "horizon_source": "rows",
  "periods": 2,
  "parameters": "fitted",
  "series": [{"series": {}, "n_actuals": 3, "first_actual": "1961-01-01",
              "actuals_through": "1961-03-01", "revised": 0, "missing": 0,
              "origin": "1961-03-01", "forecast_from": "1961-04-01",
              "forecast_to": "1961-05-01", "n_forecast": 2}],
  "message": "Forecast updated with 3 actuals (1961-01-01 to 1961-03-01) after the fitted history, which ends 1960-12-01; the model's parameters were not re-estimated. 2 periods forecast from 1961-04-01 to 1961-05-01."
}

The summary table covers all the periods that you sent and the added horizon. On the actual periods, it shows one-step-ahead predictions (how well the model predicts each period). On the other periods, it shows the forecast. A forecast without actuals gives "conditioned": false and the end of the fitted history where it started.

docs.title: Which models can
docs.text:
All the built-in statsmodels models can do this (ts.sarimax, ts.arima, ts.unobserved_components, ts.ets, ts.theta, ts.ardl, ts.ecm, ts.var, ts.vecm, ts.varmax, ts.dynamic_factor, ts.markov_switching). This includes the models that the ts_readiness_arimax workflow fits. The PyMC time-series models (ts.hsgp_trend, ts.gaussian_hmm), the marketing-mix models and the tabular models refuse. As an alternative, ts.gaussian_hmm runs its forward filter on new observations with mode: filter.

A model declares this with capabilities.conditions_on_actuals (see Capabilities). GET …/schema shows it as snapshot.conditions_on_actuals. The check uses the plugin build that scores. Thus, a model that you fitted before its plugin could condition can do it now, without a new fit. Some promotions move a version that cannot condition onto an endpoint with a version that can. This is a breaking change for the callers of the endpoint. The promotion gate counts it together with the input-schema changes, under the schema_change policy of the endpoint (blocked by default). All other models refuse a forecast with a target value in the payload:

{
  "type": "urn:mapi:error:ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED",
  "title": "The model cannot update its forecast with supplied actuals",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED",
  "errors": [{
    "code": "ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED",
    "pointer": "/data",
    "message": "model 'ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0' cannot update a forecast with actuals: the payload has values of the target 'y' for 3 periods (1961-01-01 to 1961-03-01). It would forecast from the end of its fitted history (1960-12-01) without them.",
    "suggested_action": "Refit the model with the new data to forecast from it, or leave the target empty (null) to forecast from the end of the fitted history (1960-12-01)."
  }]
}

Only forecast requests read targets as actuals. predict and evaluate payloads have targets for other reasons (metrics, features), and this function does not change them. If a predict payload has target values after the fitted history, a warning in issues tells you that the model does not use them. To condition on them, use mode: forecast.

Models fitted in a transformed space. Some workflow models fit on the output of transform.log, transform.box_cox or transform.difference. These transforms do not have an equivalent preprocessing step, so the endpoint cannot apply them to the data that you send. Such a model has the label mapi.io/data-space: transformed. It refuses actuals with ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED, because it would read them as transformed values. Its snapshot.conditions_on_actuals is false. Each answer has a warning that the predictions are in the transformed space. To prevent this, put the transform in the model (an ARIMA order d). Or put it in the pipeline of the model (core.log1p through transform.steps). Then the model transforms the actuals, and the forecasts come back in the units of the data.

Code HTTP Raised when What to do ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 The payload has target values and the model cannot condition on them Fit again with the new data, or leave the target empty ACTUALS_INVALID 422 Actuals leave a gap after the fit (and the model needs a complete history), or actuals after the fit do not have their drivers Fill the gap, or send only the actuals before it. Send the drivers MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE 422 A driver is empty on a period to forecast and future_covariates is supplied Fill it, or set future_covariates to carry_last, seasonal_naive or zero SCHEMA_INVALID 422 A target or driver cell has text where the schema needs a number ("#N/A", or a number as text from a client that sends it with no change) Send numbers. Leave the cell empty for no value

The API checks inline payloads before it starts a run. It does a null check of the JSON for the target and for the drivers that a forecast needs. It also does a type check for text. (The platform never decodes values outside the sandbox.) These checks see the union of all series. The sandbox checks each series again. Thus, a problem in only one series of a panel causes the run to fail with the same code. An example is one store without its driver on an actual month. In this case, the answer is 200 with the problem in run.problem, not a 422.

docs.title: For plugin authors
docs.text:
Declare conditions_on_actuals=True and override CustomModel.forecast_with_actuals:

def forecast_with_actuals(
    self,
    fitted: Fitted,
    ds: xr.Dataset,              # the canonicalised payload: actuals, periods to forecast, drivers
    actuals: ForecastActuals,    # which period is which, per series
    req: ScoreRequest,
    ctx: ScoreContext,
) -> xr.DataTree: ...

ForecastActuals (mapi_sdk.actuals) has these attributes:

  • dim, fit_end and targets.
  • The boolean mask observed: a supplied actual. In the fitted range, it replaces the fitted value.
  • The boolean mask future: a period to forecast.
  • The derived revised, gap and last_actual().
  • The conditioning record of the answer.

Return the predictions group for all periods of ds, as score does. Before the hook, the harness refuses the requests that the model cannot do. It also adds the horizon, fills the future drivers and checks the gaps and the drivers. The default implementation refuses. Thus, a plugin that declares the capability but has no hook never ignores actuals. toy.ar1 in mapi_sdk.testing.toy is a small reference. The forecast_actuals check of the contract kit makes sure of two things. Conditioning on the fitted values gives the plain forecast again, and a new actual changes the forecast.

docs.title: Governance v0.5
docs.text:
A model that helps people make decisions must show that it learned a real effect. Governance policies give the checks that a model must pass before it is validated. For example, the model must do better than on shuffled data, give no effect to fake drivers and do better than a naive forecast. Its errors must look like noise, and there are more checks. The checks run in the sandbox as a governance workflow and keep their evidence. A policy can make approval by a reviewer necessary, and an endpoint can refuse a model that is not validated.

Status

The contracts are in mapi_spec.governance. The NOT_VALIDATED rule of the promotion gate is in mapi_spec.scorecard. The server and the sandbox do all the checks. Validate models with governance policies gives the procedure, the meaning of each check in plain language and the default policies. The HTTP API reference gives all the operations.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text:
{
  "name": "Forecast models",
  "applies_to": {"families": ["ts"]},
  "checks": [
    {"check": "baseline.beats_naive", "severity": "blocking"},
    {"check": "null.permutation_target", "params": {"n_permutations": 20}},
    {"check": "residuals.whiteness", "severity": "warning"},
    {"check": "holdout.accuracy", "thresholds": {"warn": 0.1, "fail": 0.2}}
  ],
  "require_approval": true,
  "require_validated_for_promotion": true
}

  • Scope. A policy belongs to a project, or to the full tenant (/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/governance/policies). Policies for the full tenant are a minimum. All projects get them. The policy of a project can add checks or make thresholds stricter, but it cannot make them less strict. effective_checks keeps the stricter severity and thresholds.

    Check parameters merge with the same rule:

    • The stricter number applies. For max_missing, the lower number applies. For min_history_periods, n_permutations, n_noise, n_sims and lags, the higher number applies.
    • The lists merge (methods, shifts, params, scales).
    • The expected signs merge. If they conflict, the sign of the tenant applies.
    • Other parameters that the tenant sets (for example, a metric or a block length) keep the value of the tenant. A project can only add the parameters that the tenant did not set.

  • Matching. applies_to limits a policy to model families (mmm, ts, tabular, choice, ...), model ids or guided templates. Empty lists match all models. A family matches the family that a model declares, or the namespace of its id. (The statsmodels forecasters declare forecast, ts_multivariate or regime.) Thus, families: [ts] covers all ts.* models.

  • Versions. When you edit a policy, the platform saves a new version. Each validation records the policy versions that it used.
  • Severity. If a blocking check fails or cannot calculate, validation stops. The reviewer sees a warning. An info check gives only evidence.

docs.title: The check catalog
docs.text:
Check What it asks Measured as (pass / warn / fail) null.permutation_target Is the model better than fits again on the same data with the result shuffled? p-value: the share of shuffled fits that are equally good or better (≤ 0.05 / ≤ 0.10 / more) null.noise_regressors Do fake drivers made of noise get no effect (or almost no effect)? The largest share of the effect of the real drivers that goes to a fake driver (≤ 2% / ≤ 5% / more) null.placebo_time_shift Do the effects stop when you move the drivers by some months? Placebo effect / real effect (≤ 0.25 / ≤ 0.5 / more) baseline.beats_naive Is the forecast better than "the same as last week/year"? Relative skill compared with the strongest benchmark (≥ 5% / ≥ 0 / below) residuals.whiteness Do the errors look like random noise in time? Ljung-Box p-value (≥ 0.05 / ≥ 0.01 / below) stability.rolling_params Are the important estimates stable across rolling windows? Variation across windows (≤ 25% / ≤ 50% / more) plausibility.signs Do the effects go in the expected direction (ads help, prices hurt)? The share on the wrong side (≤ 10% / ≤ 25% / more) sensitivity.prior Do the answers stay the same with wider and narrower priors? (Bayesian) The largest relative change (≤ 20% / ≤ 50% / more) recovery.simulated Does the model find known answers in simulated data? 90% interval coverage, target 90% (±10 / ±25 points) convergence Did the fit stop at a stable answer? Maximum R-hat (≤ 1.01 / ≤ 1.05 / more) holdout.accuracy Is the error on unseen periods acceptable? The selected metric, for example MAPE (≤ 15% / ≤ 30% / more) data.quality Is the data sufficiently good to trust the model? The number of data problems found (0 / ≤ 2 / more)

Each check has an About card, a parameter schema and the types of models that it applies to (requires: Bayesian, a holdout, a time series...). If a check does not apply, the platform records it as skipped, with the reason. The results are CheckResults. Each has the measured value, the threshold, a plain message and EvidenceItems (numbers, small tables, plots, stored artifacts). For a permutation test, the evidence shows the real score and the shuffled scores together.

docs.title: Null tests in plain words
docs.text:
The three null.* checks answer the question "Can noise give this result?":

  • Shuffled result. If the model does well after you shuffle the result column, it fits noise. A real model must be better than all shuffled fits (or almost all of them).
  • Fake drivers. Add channels of pure noise to a marketing mix model. They must get an effect near zero. If they get a large share, the shares of the real channels are also doubtful.
  • Shifted drivers. Move the spend by half a year from the time when it occurred. This must stop its effect. If the effect stays, the model finds patterns in time, not the effect of the advertising.

docs.title: Validation status
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> draft
  draft --> checks_running: submit
  checks_running --> checks_passed: checks passed
  checks_running --> checks_failed: checks failed
  checks_running --> draft: cancel
  checks_passed --> validated: validate (no approval required)
  checks_passed --> awaiting_approval: request approval
  awaiting_approval --> validated: approve
  awaiting_approval --> rejected: reject
  checks_failed --> checks_running: resubmit
  checks_failed --> rejected: reject
  rejected --> checks_running: resubmit
  validated --> deprecated: deprecate

mapi_spec.governance.transition is the full state machine as a pure function. All other changes of status give 409 VALIDATION_TRANSITION_INVALID. The platform records each transition in the audit log (model.validation_transition). It also sends each transition to webhooks (model.validation.checks_passed, model.validated, model.rejected, ...).

docs.title: Approval
docs.text: With require_approval, a version that passed its checks waits for a reviewer. A reviewer is a member with the reviewer capability (project admins have it automatically). The reviewer must not be the person who submitted the version (403 SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN). A rejection needs a comment. No API token can approve, with any scopes. Approval is a decision for a person.

docs.title: Promotion
docs.text: If a policy has require_validated_for_promotion, the promotion gate of the endpoint refuses a version that is not validated. The result is 409 NOT_VALIDATED, and the decision of the gate gives the reason NOT_VALIDATED. An override by an administrator does not pass this gate. This is different from a warning on the scorecard.

docs.title: Evidence pack
docs.text:
POST /v1/validations/{validation_id}/evidence-pack exports all the data that an auditor needs in one document (EvidencePack, as JSON or as static HTML). The document has:

  • The validation, with each check result and its evidence.
  • The approvals and the full history of the status.
  • The policies, with their versions.
  • The lineage and the scorecard of the model.
  • A digest of the content.

docs.title: Guided mode v0.4
docs.text:
Guided mode is for analysts who know their business but do not know PyMC. Guided mode uses tasks, not screens. You select what you want to learn and answer questions about your columns. You tell what you already believe. Then you start a run, read a report in plain language and move the what-if sliders. Each answer goes into the same ModelSpec that Expert mode edits. Thus "View as YAML" always shows the real spec, and edits in Expert mode come back to Guided mode.

This page tells about the concepts and the contracts in mapi_spec. The server, the web app and the client use the same contracts. The HTTP API reference gives the endpoints.

Status

The server and the runner serve all the contracts on this page. The data path includes the templates, role detection, drafts, the ingest presets in the sandbox and the persona lock. From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft shows the data path. The modelling path includes business priors, lift tests, the scorecard, the what-if grids and the forecast and counterfactual views. Guided modelling shows the modelling path. The Guided screens of the web app use all of it. Refer to Your first analysis in Guided mode.

docs.title: The persona lock
docs.text:
Each user selects Guided or Expert in the header, and the app keeps the selection. Before a user selects a mode, a self-service workspace starts in Guided mode. All other workspaces start in Expert mode. A project admin can lock a project to Guided mode (Project.guided_locked). In the web app, use Settings > Mode > Lock … to Guided mode. With the API, use PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}. The audit log records the change as project.guided_lock. After the lock, members below admin see only Guided screens.

The API applies the same limit when these members write specs (mapi_spec.guided.guided_lock_issues). A stored spec must be a Guided spec. Its metadata.labels.guided names a template, and model.use is the plugin of that template. The fields that the template marks advanced or hidden keep their values. A revision keeps the values of its parent, and a new spec keeps the values of the template. Members can edit answers, basic settings, business priors and lift tests. All other changes get 403 FORBIDDEN, with one issue for each JSON pointer.

The lock has no effect on admins, static validation, runs or scoring. Thus integrations that call endpoints also have no limit.

docs.title: 1. "What do you want to learn?" - templates
docs.text:
A template (GuidedTemplate) is data. It contains these items:

  • a title and a description in plain words
  • the questions
  • the built-in plugin that it uses
  • a ModelSpec template with {{placeholder}} strings
  • default settings
  • the scorecard checks that apply
  • x-ui-level hints for each field.
Template Plugin For What-if Forecast Business priors geo_mmm - Geo marketing mix mmm.bayesian (mmm-framework) The contribution of each channel in each market; budget changes between channels yes yes yes, and lift tests weekly_forecast - Weekly forecast ts.hsgp_trend One series, some weeks or months ahead, with a range — yes — store_demand - Demand by store tabular.regressor Units for each store and week from prices and promotions (low/median/high) — yes — customer_choice - Customer choice choice.multinomial_logit The product that customers select, and how price changes the selection presets — —

Customer choice: a conditional logit with household effects

customer_choice uses the built-in choice.multinomial_logit. The model has utilities for each alternative from price and promotion. It has a product preference for each household: a random-intercept logit, fitted at its posterior mode. It also has Bayesian-bootstrap draws over households. Thus shares, counterfactual deltas and sums over trips keep their uncertainty. If a product has no price on a trip, the product was not on the shelf. New households draw their preferences from the fitted spread. Choice values must name products in the same way as the price columns (price_cola goes with the choice cola). Refer to Built-in models.

All templates fit with fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit. First, the platform fits the model without the latest periods, to measure its forecast error. Then it fits the model again on all the data. Endpoints need this fit mode.

docs.title: 2. Questions instead of a role mapper
docs.text:
The user does not map columns to dims and roles. The user answers questions, for example "Which column is the result you want to explain?" or "Which columns are media spend (one per channel)?". A question (GuidedQuestion) tells what its answer becomes:

  • a dim (date → the time dim, geo → markets), with the policy of the dim
  • a variable with a role (kpi → the target)
  • one variable along a new dim that the platform makes from some columns (spend → one spend variable along channel, with one label for each column: tv_spend becomes channel tv)
  • some separate variables (controls), or a choice or a number (frequency, holdout length).

docs.title: Role detection
docs.text:
The browser makes a profile of the upload on the local computer. Thus no dangerous data goes to the servers for a preview. The browser sends ColumnProfiles. Each profile has the name, the type, the row and missing counts, the distinct values, the range and the date frequency that the browser found. POST /v1/guided/detect-roles (or the pure function mapi_spec.guided.suggest_roles) ranks the columns for each question and fills in the answers:

  • The function splits names into words (SearchSpend → search spend). It compares the words with the keywords of each question.
  • Types must agree. A date question needs dates. A spend question needs numbers, and numbers that are never negative are better.
  • Columns that look like labels (few values that repeat) are good for dim questions. Columns that are almost empty lose points.
  • Dates in sequence and trip numbers that increase are good for ordered dims. Spend with negative values and columns that do not change lose points.

Each candidate has a confidence between 0 and 1 and a reason_plain, for example "named like a revenue column; never negative". The function fills in an answer when the confidence is 0.5 or more. A column answers a maximum of one question. The function reads the data frequency from the selected date column. If a necessary question has no candidate, the function returns a warning.

Detection also works on a stored dataset version (dataset instead of columns). The ingest run of the version wrote columns.json. This file is the profile that the sandbox made of each uploaded column (for MFF uploads, of the pivoted variables). For versions without this file, the platform makes the profile from the stored schema and summary. The API reads only that JSON.

docs.title: Drafts and "View as YAML"
docs.text:
POST /v1/guided/drafts (mapi_spec.guided.build_draft) changes GuidedAnswers into a GuidedDraft. The draft contains these items:

  • an IngestMapping for the upload. Column names become safe dataset names: Revenue (EUR) → revenue_eur.
  • the ModelSpec document. Each placeholder gets a value from the answers, the template defaults or lookups (for example, the season length from the frequency). The calibration block contains the business priors and lift tests.
  • the same spec as YAML.

The server does a static validation of the draft against the catalog. It uses the schema that the mapping gives (mapi_spec.guided.draft_schema). It returns the findings in issues. The server stores nothing. Upload the data as a dataset version with the mapping. Then save the spec with POST /v1/specs. Incorrect answers come back as GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID, with a pointer to /answers/<question>.

docs.title: File formats and presets
docs.text:
Only a sandboxed ingest run parses uploads. You can give an explicit column mapping. Or the IngestMapping.preset field can name a file contract that marketing teams already use:

Format or preset Contract csv, parquet A column mapping: dims, vars and, for wide tables, wide (WideVarMapping: one variable from one column for each label) mff (format or preset) The MFF long table below meridian The CoordToColumns wide table of Google Meridian (MeridianColumns): time, geo, kpi, controls, and parallel media/media_spend (and reach/frequency) lists for each channel zarr_zip, netcdf Labelled datasets that describe themselves

The MFF ("model feature format") long table has one row for each period, key combination and variable. mmm-framework uses the same MFF convention (mapi_spec.ingest.MFF_COLUMNS):

Column Meaning Period The date. Weekly data must be on the same day of the week. Geography, Product Panel levels. Each column becomes a dim when it has more than one level. A blank label (or National, Total, All) is the total. The ingest spreads a variable that has values only in the total (national TV) across the levels. Geographies get equal parts. Products get parts by the share of the KPI (MffOptions.allocation). mmm-framework does the same. Outlet, Campaign, Creative Breakdowns. The ingest adds together rows that are different only in these columns. MffOptions.split keeps the column as a dim. VariableName The variable (Sales, TV_Spend, ...) VariableValue The value

You can also pivot MFF tables and then map them like a CSV file (the variables become columns). MffOptions.combine joins key columns into one dim. The ingest applies limits on rows, columns, cell length and decompression. It explains each refusal. Refer to File formats and presets.

docs.title: 3. Business priors and lift tests
docs.text:
Users tell what they already believe in business units (BusinessPriors):

calibration:
  business_priors:
    channels:
      tv:     {roi: [1.5, 4.0], credibility: 0.8}   # every euro returns 1.5-4 euros, 80% sure
      search: {roi: [2.0, 6.0], credibility: 0.9}
      social: {contribution_share: [0.02, 0.10]}    # 2-10% of revenue
    baseline_share: {share: [0.5, 0.8]}
  lift_tests:
    - {id: tv-holdout-2026q2, channel: tv, geo: de, start: 2026-04-06, end: 2026-05-03,
       spend_delta: -120000, kpi_delta: -260000, ci: [-380000, -140000], ci_level: 0.9}
  • Credibility is the probability that the true value is in the range. A range [low, high] at credibility c becomes a log-normal (ROI) or a logit-normal (share) distribution. The central c interval of this distribution is exactly that range (lognormal_from_range).
  • Shares must fit in the KPI. The smallest shares (channels plus baseline) cannot add up to more than 100% (BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID).
  • You must give a minimum of one belief, but any one is sufficient. baseline_share alone (no channels) makes only the baseline narrower. Channels without a belief keep the default priors of the model.
  • Lift tests are experiment results that the model uses as calibration data. A lift test has extra (or removed) spend on one channel, optionally in one geo, over a window. It also has the incremental KPI that the spend caused, with a standard error or a confidence interval. The model uses each lift test as an extra observation of the incremental effect of the channel.
  • Only models that declare them (Capabilities.calibration) accept them. For other models, static validation reports CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

To change beliefs into priors in model space, the platform needs the scale of the data and the transforms of the model. Thus this change occurs in the sandbox as a translate_priors run (POST /v1/guided/prior-translations). Its result (PriorTranslationResult) contains the priors to write at /model/settings/priors (apply_prior_translation). It also contains a prior-predictive preview in business units. The preview shows the ROI and contribution-share distributions for each channel, the baseline share and a KPI fan. Thus users see the effect of their beliefs before the fit. Guided modelling gives the math, the lift-test likelihood and the checks that each layer does.

docs.title: 4. Run, then the sanity scorecard
docs.text: Each fit gets a Scorecard of checks in plain language. Each check is pass, warn or fail. It has the measured value, the threshold, a message_plain, a suggested action and a link back to this page. overall is the worst item. Templates select their checks and can make thresholds stricter. The catalog is mapi_spec.scorecard.SCORECARD_CHECKS:

docs.title: Convergence
docs.text: Check Metric Thresholds What to do convergence.rhat (Chains agree) r_hat_max warn above 1.01, fail above 1.05 Run more tuning and draws, or make the model simpler. convergence.ess (Enough independent draws) ess_bulk_min warn below 400, fail below 100 Increase the number of draws. convergence.divergences (The sampler had no problems) divergence_rate warn above 0%, fail above 1% Increase target_accept, or use more informative priors.

docs.title: Holdout error
docs.text:
Check Metric Thresholds What to do holdout.mape (Holdout error) mape warn above 10%, fail above 25% Look for gaps or one-time events in the last periods of data. Add holidays or controls that explain them. holdout.coverage_90 (The uncertainty is correct) coverage_90 warn when more than 10% away from 90%, fail when more than 25% away Look for trends or shifts that the model does not include. holdout.hit_rate (Better than a simple guess) accuracy_lift warn below +2 points, fail below -10 points Add the drivers of the choice for each product (price, promotions, displays). Or collect more trips for each customer.

holdout.hit_rate is the check of the customer_choice template. For each household, the check uses the trip in the holdout. It compares the most probable product of the model with the product that the household bought (accuracy, the hit rate). It also compares the model with a guess that is always the most popular product of the holdout trips (accuracy_naive). This baseline is strict, because it knows the shares of the holdout. accuracy_lift is the difference in percentage points. The template also reports two more values in the metrics of the model. These are the log_score (the mean log probability of the bought product, where higher is better) and the multi-class brier score (0 is perfect).

docs.title: Plausibility
docs.text: Check Metric Thresholds What to do plausibility.negative_roi (No channel loses money) negative_roi_share warn above 10%, fail above 50% Examine the spend data of the channel, or give an ROI range in business priors. plausibility.roi_absurd (Returns are not too high) roi_max warn above 20, fail above 100 Examine the spend units and gaps, or give an ROI range in business priors. plausibility.share_outlier (No channel is too large) max_channel_share warn above 60%, fail above 90% Look for a missing control (price, promotions, seasonality). plausibility.baseline_share (The baseline is in the usual range) baseline_share warn when more than 40% away from 50%, fail when more than 48% away Give a baseline share in business priors, or examine the controls. plausibility.prior_overlap (The data changed the model) prior_overlap_max warn above 90%, fail above 99% Add data where the driver changes (or a lift test). Or give a business prior for it that you trust.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
Check Metric Thresholds What to do data.missing (Few missing values) missing_fraction warn above 5%, fail above 30% Fill the gaps in the source data, or remove the series that have gaps. data.history (Enough history) history_years warn below 2 years, fail below 1 year (the weekly_forecast template: below 0.5) Add more history if you have it. data.spend_variation (Spend changes enough) spend_cv_min warn below 10%, fail below 2% Add a lift test for the channel, or give its ROI in business priors.

Guided modelling tells how the runner measures each check. The scorecard also controls promotion to an endpoint. Refer to Integrations.

docs.title: 5. What-if sliders
docs.text:
Sliders give answers immediately, because each MMM fit calculates response grids for each draw before you use them (ResponseGridView, ui/grids/response_curves.json, format mapi.response-grid/v1). The grid has values for each thinned posterior draw, channel and spend multiplier. It contains the total contribution of the channel over the fit window and the spend at each grid point. It also contains the actual spend and the baseline.

A WhatIfScenario sets a multiplier for each channel (1 = the actual spend). The web app and mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario use the same interpolation contract:

  1. A channel without a multiplier keeps 1. The contract refuses multipliers outside the grid (SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE). It never extrapolates the grid.
  2. For each draw and channel, the contract interpolates the contribution linearly between the two grid points around the multiplier. It does the same for spend.
  3. For each draw, KPI = baseline + the contributions of the channels. The change is the difference from the KPI with all multipliers at 1. The contract calculates means and quantiles after the sum. Thus the uncertainty band stays joint across channels.

The web app calculates the slider answers in the browser with a TypeScript port of this contract. Its unit tests compare the port with golden cases that the spec tests export (packages/spec/tests/snapshots/whatif_golden.json).

Run exact changes the scenario into a counterfactual score request, with one multiply intervention for each changed channel. Then it starts a real score run (POST /v1/guided/requests:compile, then score).

docs.title: Forecasts and counterfactuals
docs.text:
Guided forecasts (forecast_request) need a horizon. They also need a policy for covariates that have no future values from the user (ScoreRequest.future_covariates). The policies are carry_last (the default in Guided mode), seasonal_naive, zero, or supplied with a scenario dataset. Intervention presets make counterfactuals with one click:

  • channel off (ChannelOff): the spend of that channel is zero.
  • budget × k (BudgetScale): the platform multiplies the spend of all channels, or of the listed channels, by k.

The presets apply over the fit window or over a forecast horizon. By default, responses are expected values with the mean and a 90% interval (Q2).

docs.title: Integrations v0.4
docs.text: A fitted model is useful only when other applications can use it. For example, a planning tool scores budgets and a spreadsheet gets a forecast. A dashboard shows a chart, and a pipeline gets a message when a fit is complete. This page tells about the integration concepts of v0.4 and the contracts in mapi_spec that they use. The HTTP API reference gives the endpoints. Endpoints and webhooks shows how to use them with curl.

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text:
An endpoint is a stable alias for one model version: endpoint://growth/geo-mmm-prod. Integrations call the alias. Thus you can promote a better model, or roll back a bad model, and the integrations do not change. Each promotion and rollback is a numbered revision in the history of the endpoint. The revision records who did it and why.

PUT /v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod
X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth

{"model": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3", "expected_revision": 3}

docs.title: The promotion gate
docs.text:
The sanity scorecard and the EvaluationPolicy of the endpoint control promotion (mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate):

The version Gate Result The scorecard passes allowed The platform promotes the version The scorecard warns, or there is no scorecard. Or an evaluate_then_refit fit has a scorecard with no holdout check (no data.split, or no evaluate.metrics: the platform did not evaluate it). Or the checks of the template of a guided version did not all run (NOT_EVALUATED). needs_override 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED, unless a signed-in project admin sends override: true with a reason. The audit log records the override (endpoint.promote_override). The scorecard fails, or the fit stopped before it was complete (partial) blocked 409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED. No override is possible. The fit mode was train_only blocked Endpoints need evaluate_then_refit (Q13), because the context and terminal state must come from all the data. A policy with fit_mode: train_only accepts exploration fits. The version needs input that the callers do not send blocked (policy schema_change: block), needs_override (warn) or ignored (allow) A dim that is removed or changed, a stricter dim policy, a new necessary input, or an input with changed dims or type (schema_breaks)

An override is a human decision. Only project admins have the manage permission on endpoints, and no token scope gives it, not even admin. A token with endpoints:promote (for CI) can promote versions that pass and can roll back. It can never override.

docs.title: Scoring an endpoint
docs.text:
POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score takes an EndpointScoreCall. This is a score request without model. data and scenario can be dataset:// references. They can also be small inline XrJSON datasets (the xr.Dataset.to_dict() shape, a maximum of 5 MB). Thus spreadsheets and scripts do not need an upload. The control plane does a check of only the envelope of inline data (names, nesting, sizes). The sandbox decodes the values.

Send Prefer: wait=60 to get the result in the response if the run is complete in time (200). If the run is not complete in time, the response is 202 with the run to follow. GET …/schema tells what to send (EndpointSchema). It gives the input schema that the platform froze at promotion, the score modes, the dims and an example payload. POST …/validate does a check of a call and does not run it. A forecast call can also contain the actuals that arrived after the fit and the dates to forecast. Refer to Forecasts with actuals and the actuals_example of the schema.

A score:<alias> token can read the endpoint, its schema and its snippets, and can score it. It can do nothing else.

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets returns code that is ready to run. The code scores the endpoint with its example payload. These languages are available:

  • Python (mapi-client)
  • TypeScript (fetch)
  • curl
  • R (httr2)
  • Google Sheets (Apps Script)
  • a notebook cell (Client().endpoint(alias).score(...), which returns an xarray.Dataset).

The generators are pure functions (mapi_spec.snippets.render_snippets). Thus the server, the CLI, the web app and these docs make the same code. The Integrations hub shows and copies the snippets of the server with no changes. Snippets never contain a secret. They read the token from MAPI_TOKEN (a script property in Apps Script). The generators write each value with the literal syntax of the language. Tests parse the generated code to prove that a dangerous payload cannot go out of its string.

curl -sS -X POST 'https://api.mapi.example/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
  -H 'X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth' \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=60' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last"}'

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
A webhook calls your URL when an event occurs in a project:

Event When run.succeeded, run.failed A run is complete model.version.ready A fit made a model version (with the result of its scorecard) endpoint.promoted An alias points to a new version (promotion or rollback) score.completed A score run is complete tenant.deletion.completed The platform purged the tenant (this is the last event that the tenant sends)

Each delivery is a JSON envelope {id, type, created, tenant, project, api_version, data}. Envelopes contain ids and states. They never contain data values, signed URLs or secrets. Use the API to get the results.

docs.title: Verifying a delivery
docs.text:
The platform signs each delivery with the secret of the webhook. The platform shows the secret one time, when you make the webhook or rotate its secret:

Mapi-Signature: t=1792000000,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd

v1 is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>". To verify a delivery, do these steps:

  1. Calculate the HMAC again over the raw body.
  2. Compare the two values in constant time.
  3. Refuse timestamps that are more than 300 seconds from your clock. This limits replays.

During a rotation, the header contains one v1 for each active secret.

from mapi_spec.webhooks import verify_signature

if not verify_signature(raw_body, request.headers["Mapi-Signature"], secret):
    return 401

The platform tries failed deliveries again after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h. If a receiver answers 410 Gone, the platform disables it immediately. The platform disables a webhook after 20 failed events in sequence. The delivery log shows each attempt (status, response code, duration). You can replay each delivery.

docs.title: SSRF protection
docs.text:
A webhook URL is a request that the platform makes for a tenant. Thus the server delivers only under a strict policy (mapi_spec.webhooks.SSRF_POLICY):

  • The URL must use https only, on port 443 or 8443. It must have no credentials or fragment. It must have a host name. An IP literal, localhost or an internal suffix (.internal, .local, ...) is not permitted.
  • The server resolves the host itself. It refuses the URL if one address is private, loopback, link-local, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), CGNAT, unique-local or multicast. It also refuses addresses that are not globally routable for other reasons. This includes IPv4 addresses in IPv6 addresses.
  • The server then connects to the address that it checked. It does no second lookup, thus DNS rebinding cannot change the address. The server follows no redirects. It stops after 5 seconds and reads a maximum of 256 KiB of the answer.

If a URL does not obey the policy, the server refuses it with 422 WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED. A URL can start to resolve to a blocked address later. Then its deliveries fail as blocked. The audit log records this as a security signal (webhook.url_blocked).

docs.title: Plots: rendering, sharing and embeds
docs.text:
• Saved plots keep a plot of a model version, or a plot that you wrote, under a name.
  • Static rendering (POST /v1/plots:render) makes PNG, SVG or PDF files in the sandbox for reports. It uses vl-convert for Vega-Lite, with no network access. Plotly needs kaleido and a Chrome in the runner image. Until an operator turns on Plotly, the platform refuses it with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED.
  • Embed links are read-only links with a token and an expiry date, for BI tools, Slack and Notion. The platform shows the token one time. You can revoke links. allowed_origins limits the sites that can show them in a frame. You can embed only platform recipes. These are plots that the recipes of the platform made from a model version. You cannot embed plots that a plugin or a user wrote. A sandboxed iframe can still navigate itself. Thus shared views run only code that the platform wrote. Requests for other plots get 422 EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED. Links that expired or that you revoked answer 410 LINK_EXPIRED. The link opens the embed page of the plot sandbox. This page can get only the public embed view of the API. Refer to Sharing plots.

docs.title: The trust lifecycle
docs.text:
Public sign-up starts with cut line A. Public tenants run only declarative specs and built-in plugins. The data is not trusted, but the code is trusted.

  1. Sign-up needs an e-mail address, a name and accepted terms. The answer is the same for new and known addresses. Thus nobody can use it to find accounts. A policy hook that you can replace refuses disposable e-mail domains.
  2. E-mail verification uses a link that you can use one time (valid for 24 hours). It makes a tenant on the public tier with a default project. The new user is the admin of the project.
  3. Identity verification is necessary before any uploaded code. Tenants on the verified tier (allow-listed, M4) can upload code after verification. Public tenants can upload code only after cut line B (M5). Until then, VerificationStatus.uploaded_code_allowed is false for all public tenants.
  4. Deleting a tenant starts a grace period of 7 days. During this period, the tenant is suspended (read-only) and you can cancel the deletion. Then the platform purges each store: database rows, objects, queued work, logs and webhooks. It shows the progress for each store. The platform keeps the audit log (pseudonymised) and the cost ledger (amounts only, for tax law) for their legal retention period.
  5. A GDPR export puts all the data that the tenant stored into one archive. It gives a download link that expires after a short time. A suspended tenant can also ask for it.

docs.title: Labelled data
docs.text:
Each model on modeling-api reads one xr.Dataset. The dataset has variables with named dims, and dims with coordinate labels. Nothing depends on position. Thus the platform can safely reorder, subset and extend the data, and add labels. You can also score data that has its stores in a different sequence than at fit time.

A DataSchema describes such a dataset. It tells what each dim is and what can occur to it at score time. It also tells what each variable means to a model.

docs.title: A schema in one look
docs.text:
layout: dense                       # or: long (one row per observation + *_idx variables)
dims:
  market:  {kind: categorical, policy: new_levels, new_level_strategy: hyperprior}
  channel: {kind: categorical, policy: fixed}
  date:    {kind: time, policy: extend, freq: D}
vars:
  revenue: {dims: [market, date], dtype: float64, role: target, units: EUR}
  spend:   {dims: [market, channel, date], dtype: float64, role: spend, units: EUR,
            future_required: true}

docs.title: Dims and their policies
docs.text:
The policy is the most important part of the contract. It tells what a score request can do with a dim.

Policy For At score time Typical errors fixed channels, products, states Only labels from the fit (any subset, any sequence) UNSEEN_LEVELS extend time, observation index New labels after the fitted range, without gaps, up to max_extension NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT new_levels markets, stores, counties, households New labels are permitted. new_level_strategy controls them. UNSEEN_LEVELS when the strategy is error

new_level_strategy tells what a new level becomes:

Strategy Meaning Example hyperprior A new draw from the fitted population distribution, for each posterior draw A new market in a hierarchical MMM: the uncertainty is honest and wider pooled The population average (or an average of fitted levels, weighted by frequency) A new store in an xgboost demand model zero The level adds nothing A new category in a one-hot model error The platform refuses the level The default

Other DimSpec fields:

  • kind: categorical, time, integer, float or index.
  • freq: a pandas frequency for time dims (D, W-SUN, MS). With it, the platform can make forecast coordinates and do a check for gaps.
  • max_extension: the maximum number of periods that a forecast can go past the fit without a new fit.
  • ordered: tells if a categorical dim has a sequence that has a meaning.

Policies only tighten

The schema template of a model declares the least strict policy that the model can use. The schema of your data and the dim_policies of the spec can only make it stricter (fixed is the strictest). If you try to make it less strict, you get DIM_POLICY_LOOSENED.

docs.title: Variables and roles
docs.text:
Field Meaning dims, dtype The shape contract (float64, int64, bool, str, datetime64[ns], …) role What the variable means: target, covariate, media, spend, control, index, mask, constant, weight, exposure units A string in pint style (EUR, units, 1). Steps update it (fx_convert → EUR, scaling → 1), and outputs report it missing forbid (default), allow (NaN is permitted) or mask (a mask variable shows the valid cells) missing_sentinel A code, for example -99.99, that means "missing". core.replace_sentinel changes it to NaN future_required You must supply values over a forecast horizon (planned prices, promotions, budgets) index_of Long layout: this integer variable is the index of that dim (county_idx(obs) → county) bounds The permitted range of values. The platform does a check and reports in plain language

With roles, plugins and plot templates work across datasets. For example, "each spend variable" or "the target over time, one line for each geo".

docs.title: Two layouts for ragged data
docs.text:
Real panels are frequently ragged. For example, households have different numbers of trips, and animals have tracks of different lengths. A schema uses one of two canonical forms. The built-in steps core.to_long and core.to_padded change data from one form to the other.

LongPadded

One row for each observation along an obs dim, plus index variables:

layout: long
dims:
  obs:    {kind: integer, policy: extend}
  county: {kind: categorical, policy: new_levels, new_level_strategy: hyperprior}
vars:
  log_radon:  {dims: [obs], dtype: float64, role: target}
  county_idx: {dims: [obs], dtype: int64, role: index, index_of: county}

A dense cube plus a mask variable:

dims:
  animal: {kind: categorical, policy: new_levels, new_level_strategy: pooled}
  step:   {kind: integer, policy: extend}
vars:
  y:    {dims: [animal, step], dtype: float64, role: target, missing: mask}
  mask: {dims: [animal, step], dtype: bool, role: mask}
ragged:
  - {group_dim: animal, within_dim: step, form: padded, mask_var: mask}

docs.title: Draft a schema from data
docs.text:
infer_schema gives you a schema to start with. Time dims become extend with a frequency that the function finds. Other dims become fixed. Variables become covariate, unless you give a different role.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr
from mapi_sdk import infer_schema, validate_dataset
from mapi_spec import DimPolicy

days = pd.date_range("2026-03-01", periods=28, freq="D")
markets = ["DE", "FR", "UK"]
channels = ["tv", "search"]
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
media = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "revenue": (("market", "date"), rng.gamma(50.0, 20.0, (3, 28))),
        "spend": (("market", "channel", "date"), rng.gamma(5.0, 100.0, (3, 2, 28))),
    },
    coords={"market": markets, "channel": channels, "date": days},
)

schema = infer_schema(
    media,
    targets=["revenue"],
    policies={"market": "new_levels"},
    units={"revenue": "EUR", "spend": "EUR"},
)
print(schema.dims["date"].policy, schema.dims["date"].freq)  # extend D
print(schema.dims["channel"].policy)  # fixed
print(schema.vars["revenue"].role)  # target

docs.title: Data checks in plain language
docs.text:
