Each package is a separate distribution. Install only the packages that you need:

uv add mapi-sdk mapi-steps                 # the runtime and the built-in steps
uv add mapi-pymc                           # PyMC models
uv add mapi-sklearn                        # scikit-learn and xgboost models
uv add "mapi-plots[recipes]"               # plot recipes (Altair, Plotly)
uv add mapi-plugin-mmm mapi-plugin-ts mapi-plugin-tabular   # the built-in models
uv add mapi-plugin-statsmodels "mapi-workflows[runtime]"    # statsmodels models, workflows

Not on PyPI yet

We will publish the distributions with the first tagged release. Until then, you install from the workspace, as the first tab shows.

docs.title: What each package does
docs.text:
Package Import What it gives you Heavy dependencies mapi-spec mapi_spec The contracts: DataSchema, ModelSpec, ScoreRequest, capabilities, error codes, static validation and JSON Schemas none (pure Pydantic) mapi-sdk mapi_sdk The runtime: steps, pipelines, coord plans, summaries, bundles, the in-process executor and the contract kit xarray, numpy, zarr mapi-steps mapi_steps 28 built-in preprocessing steps and the split catalog – mapi-pymc mapi_pymc PyMCModel: you write build(). You get engines, diagnostics, new levels and counterfactuals. PyMC mapi-sklearn mapi_sklearn SklearnModel: you write estimator(). You get stacking, safe persistence and uncertainty. scikit-learn, xgboost, skops mapi-plots mapi_plots The JSON-only plot sanitizer and templates. Recipes come with the recipes extra. Altair, Plotly (extra) mapi-plugin-* mapi_plugin_* Built-in models: marketing mix (mapi-plugin-mmm, on mmm-framework), time series, statsmodels time series (mapi-plugin-statsmodels) and tabular as above; mmm-framework, statsmodels mapi-workflows mapi_workflows The workflow engine, the node implementations and a local runner for notebooks (guide) The engine has none (pure Python, safe for the control plane). The node implementations are the runtime extra (numpy, xarray, scipy, statsmodels). mapi-conformance mapi_conformance The conformance corpus and its runner all of the above mapi-client mapi_client A typed Python client for the HTTP API (guide) httpx (xarray optional) mapi-cli mapi_cli The mapi command line (guide) typer, rich mapi-server mapi_server The control plane: API, orchestrator and executors (AGPL or commercial) FastAPI, SQLAlchemy; no numpy mapi-runner mapi_runner The sandboxed run harness: supervisor and worker (AGPL or commercial) the SDK, in the worker only mapi-gcs-shim mapi_gcs_shim A local emulator of the Cloud Storage features that the platform uses Starlette

Plugins register themselves through Python entry points (mapi.steps, mapi.models, mapi.plots). Thus mapi_sdk.default_registry() finds all the installed plugins.

docs.title: Runs and executors
docs.text:
fit_spec and score_bundle are plain functions. The platform does the same work as runs. A run is a JSON-only submission that goes to an executor. The executor sends progress as events. It also returns a status, and the status is the source of truth. The in-process executor uses that protocol inside your Python process. Thus notebooks, tests and the local-process and docker executors of the platform use one code path.

sequenceDiagram
    participant You as Notebook / API
    participant Ex as Executor
    participant H as Harness (fit_spec / score_bundle)
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: fit, payload: spec}, nonce)
    Ex->>H: resolve dataset refs, fit
    H-->>Ex: progress events
    Ex-->>You: event stream (state, progress, complete)
    You->>Ex: wait(handle) → SUCCEEDED
    You->>Ex: submit(RunSubmit{kind: score, payload: request + bundle})
    Ex->>H: score_bundle
    Ex-->>You: result: xr.DataTree

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
The executor uses a resolver to find the datasets for the dataset:// references in specs and requests. Here, the resolver is a mapping to in-memory datasets. The built-in tabular plugin contains the store-demand data and the spec that this page uses.

import asyncio

from mapi_plugin_tabular.datasets import (
    STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA,
    STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
    store_demand_dataset,
)
from mapi_sdk import InprocExecutor
from mapi_spec.executor import ExecState, RunEventType, RunKind, RunSubmit

history = store_demand_dataset(stores=4, skus=2, weeks=60, seed=1)
recent = history.isel(week=slice(-8, None))  # a window of fitted weeks to re-score

executor = InprocExecutor(
    # dataset refs in specs and requests resolve to in-memory datasets
    resolver={
        "dataset://retail/store_sku_weekly@latest": history,
        "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1": recent,
    },
)
print(executor.caps().isolation.name)  # NONE: your own code, in your own process

docs.title: Submit, wait, score
docs.text:
async def main() -> None:
    fit = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="fit-001",
            kind=RunKind.FIT,
            payload={
                "spec": STORE_DEMAND_SPEC_YAML,
                "raw_schema": STORE_DEMAND_SCHEMA.model_dump(mode="json"),
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-fit-0001",  # resubmitting the same nonce returns the same run
    )
    status = await executor.wait(fit, timeout=300)
    print(status.state)  # succeeded
    for event in executor.events(fit):  # the same event stream a cloud run will produce
        if event.type is RunEventType.PROGRESS:
            print(event.seq, event.payload.get("message"))  # 2 validated the spec and the data

    executor.put_bundle("store-demand@1", executor.result(fit))
    score = await executor.submit(
        RunSubmit(
            run_id="score-001",
            kind=RunKind.SCORE,
            payload={
                "bundle": "store-demand@1",
                "request": {
                    "apiVersion": "mapi/v1",
                    "kind": "ScoreRequest",
                    "model": "endpoint://retail/store-demand-xgb",
                    "mode": "predict",
                    "data": "dataset://retail/last_8_weeks@v1",
                },
            },
        ),
        nonce="nonce-score-0001",
    )
    assert (await executor.wait(score, timeout=300)).state is ExecState.SUCCEEDED
    tree = executor.result(score)  # an xr.DataTree, exactly what score_bundle returns
    print(dict(tree["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sizes))
    # {'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}


asyncio.run(main())  # in Jupyter: `await main()`

succeeded
2 validated the spec and the data
3 split the data
4 fitted quantile model 1
5 persisting the fitted estimators
6 fitted on the training data
7 evaluated the holdout through the score path
8 fitted quantile model 1
9 persisting the fitted estimators
10 fit complete
{'stat': 3, 'store_id': 4, 'sku': 2, 'week': 8}

Look at these points:

  • Payloads are JSON. The spec goes as YAML text or as a dict. The raw schema goes as a dict. Data goes only as references. This is exactly what the API will store and what a sandboxed runner will receive.
  • Submissions are idempotent. If you submit again with the same nonce, you get the same handle. Thus an API call that you try again never starts a second fit. adopt(nonce) finds a run after a restart.
  • Status is the source of truth. Events are for progress bars. status() and wait() tell you if a run succeeded. Failures come back as RFC 7807 problems with a stable code.
  • Cancellation is cooperative. The executor checks cancel(handle) between the phases of the pipeline and inside long fits.

docs.title: Isolation levels
docs.text:
Each executor declares how strongly it isolates a run. The platform does not send untrusted code to an executor that is not sufficiently strong.

Executor Isolation For Status InprocExecutor NONE Notebooks, tests and your own trusted code available Local process / Docker PROCESS / GVISOR Local platform, CI v0.2 Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) MICROVM Hosted runs, one new sandbox for each run v0.3

Never run untrusted code in-process

The in-process executor runs plugins in your interpreter, with your permissions. Use it only for code that you wrote or that you trust. Public plugins run only in the sandboxed executors.

For the sandbox design, see the roadmap.

docs.title: Your first model
docs.text:
In this walkthrough, you fit a demand model for three stores and two products. You forecast the next four weeks, and the forecast includes a store that is not open yet. You also see the errors that stop dishonest answers. You run all the code in a notebook, one cell at a time. The complete script is docs/snippets/quickstart.py. The test suite runs it on each change.

flowchart LR
    D["1. Labelled data<br/><code>xr.Dataset</code>"] --> S["2. Schema<br/>dims, roles, policies"]
    S --> P["3. Spec<br/>pipeline + model"]
    P --> V["4. Static check<br/>no data touched"]
    V --> F["5. Fit<br/>evaluate, then refit"]
    F --> SC["6. Score<br/>forecast, new store"]
    SC --> B["7. Bundle<br/>write, read, verify"]

docs.title: 1. Labelled data
docs.text:
Your data is an xr.Dataset. Each variable has named dims, and each dim has coordinates (labels). No later part of the process uses the sequence of stores or products.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

Coming from pandas?

A long DataFrame with one row for each store, sku and week becomes this dataset with df.set_index(["store", "sku", "week"]).to_xarray().

docs.title: 2. Describe it with a schema
docs.text:
A DataSchema tells what each dim is. It also tells what can occur to the dim when you score:

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)
Dim Policy At score time store new_levels (pooled) Stores that the fit did not see are permitted. They get the pooled prediction. sku fixed Only the fitted products. All other products are UNSEEN_LEVELS. week extend New weeks must continue the fitted range. Gaps are not permitted.

If you do not write the schema, mapi_sdk.infer_schema(data, targets=[...]) makes a draft. In the draft, time dims become extend and all other dims become fixed.

docs.title: 3. Write the spec
docs.text:
A ModelSpec does these things:

  • It names the dataset.
  • It binds your names to the canonical names of the model.
  • It selects a train/holdout split.
  • It lists the preprocessing steps.
  • It selects the model.
from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")
  • bind maps canonical names onto the names in your dataset. Steps and models use the canonical names. Outputs come back with your names.
  • core.calendar adds week-of-year features. core.log1p models log(1 + units). The pipeline inverts it automatically on the way out.
  • tabular.regressor is a built-in quantile model (xgboost underneath). It stacks its rows from the labelled dims. Store and sku become categorical features.

docs.title: 4. Check it before you fit it
docs.text:
This is the same static check that the API does before it accepts a job. It reads no data, and it takes milliseconds.

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)

The check finds these errors, among others:

  • An incorrect variable name.
  • A split on a dim that does not exist yet.
  • A stateful step before the split.

Each error has a stable code and a JSON pointer, for example /pipeline/1/with/vars/0.

docs.title: 5. Fit
docs.text:
from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks

With the default fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, fit_spec does these steps:

  1. It fits each stateful step and the model on the first 44 weeks.
  2. It scores the last 8 weeks through the score path, exactly as a forecast. It calculates rmse, mape and coverage_80 in units sold (it undoes the log1p).
  3. It fits again on all 52 weeks, so that a forecast starts from the latest data. It links the evaluation fit in the bundle.

docs.title: 6. Forecast, with a new store
docs.text:
Supply the plan for the next four weeks. Prices and promotions are future_required. The target is not necessary. The fit did not see west.

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'

The result is an xr.DataTree. summary holds the statistics that you asked for, along a stat dim, with your dim names. Its attributes tell you how to read it:

Attribute Value here Meaning representation quantiles Quantiles for each cell. You can read them, but you cannot add them. output_space {"y_hat": "raw"} The pipeline inverted the values through each value step, back to the space of the raw data. issues UNSEEN_LEVELS (info) The model scored west with the pooled strategy.

docs.title: 7. The errors that protect you
docs.text:
These requests fail before model code runs. Each failure has a stable code:

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))

MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE - forecasting needs future values of ['promo'] at stage 'raw'
CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED - cannot aggregate 'quantiles' output: Quantiles are marginal per cell; summing quantiles is not a quantile of the sum.
UNSEEN_LEVELS - 1 level(s) of 'sku' were not seen at fit and the dim's policy is 'fixed'

So how do I get a total over stores?

Use a model that has a representation that supports totals. sklearn.tabular_bootstrap returns joint draws, and you can add them for each draw. Bayesian models return posterior draws. See Representations.

docs.title: 8. Save and reload the bundle
docs.text:
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

A bundle holds these items:

  • The spec and the binding.
  • The state and the context tail of each step.
  • The fitted groups and the native artifacts of the model (here, the xgboost model as JSON).
  • A manifest with the size, CRC32C, MD5 and SHA-256 of each file.

The bundle contains no pickled objects. See Bundles.

docs.title: The whole script
docs.text:
docs/snippets/quickstart.py 
"""Getting started: fit and score a labelled demand model in a notebook.

Every section between ``--8<--`` markers is included verbatim in the docs, and
``conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py`` runs this file top to bottom.
"""

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import xarray as xr

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
stores = ["north", "south", "east"]
skus = ["apples", "pears"]
weeks = pd.date_range("2025-01-05", periods=52, freq="W-SUN")
shape = (len(stores), len(skus), len(weeks))

price = 3.0 * np.exp(rng.normal(0.0, 0.1, shape))
promo = (rng.uniform(size=shape) < 0.2).astype(float)
units = rng.poisson(np.exp(2.5 - 1.2 * np.log(price / 3.0) + 0.5 * promo)).astype(float)

dims = ("store", "sku", "week")
data = xr.Dataset(
    {"units_sold": (dims, units), "price": (dims, price), "promo": (dims, promo)},
    coords={"store": stores, "sku": skus, "week": weeks},
)

from mapi_spec import DataSchema

schema = DataSchema.model_validate(
    {
        "dims": {
            # a store we have never seen may be scored: it gets the pooled prediction
            "store": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "new_levels", "new_level_strategy": "pooled"},
            # the product range is fixed: an unknown sku is an error
            "sku": {"kind": "categorical", "policy": "fixed"},
            # time extends into the future, one Sunday-ending week at a time
            "week": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"},
        },
        "vars": {
            "units_sold": {"dims": list(dims), "dtype": "float64", "role": "target"},
            "price": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "units": "EUR",
                "future_required": True,  # a forecast must say what the price will be
            },
            "promo": {
                "dims": list(dims),
                "dtype": "float64",
                "role": "covariate",
                "future_required": True,
            },
        },
    }
)

from mapi_spec import load_model_spec

spec = load_model_spec("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: fruit-demand, project: quickstart}
data:
  dataset: dataset://quickstart/fruit_weekly@latest
  bind:                                   # canonical name: your name
    dims: {store: store, sku: sku, time: week}
    vars: {y: units_sold, price: price, promo: promo}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: time, last: 8}
pipeline:
  - {id: cal,  use: core.calendar@^1, with: {along: time, features: [week_of_year]}}
  - {id: logy, use: core.log1p@^1,    with: {vars: [y]}}
model:
  use: tabular.regressor@^1
  settings:
    estimator: {kind: xgboost.XGBRegressor, params: {n_estimators: 60, max_depth: 3}}
    rows: [store, sku, time]
    coord_features: {store: category, sku: category}
  fit: {seed: 7}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_80]}
""")

from mapi_sdk import default_registry
from mapi_spec import validate_spec

registry = default_registry()  # every installed step, model and plot (entry points)
check = validate_spec(spec, registry.catalog(), schema)
print(check.ok)  # True: names, dims, settings, split stage and leakage all check out
print(check.resolved.model.resolved)  # tabular.regressor@1.0.0 (the semver range, pinned)
assert check.ok, check.errors

from mapi_sdk import fit_spec

bundle = fit_spec(spec, data, registry=registry, raw_schema=schema)
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics, in units sold: {'rmse': ..., 'mape': ..., ...}
print(bundle.metrics.n_holdout)  # 48 cells: 3 stores x 2 skus x 8 weeks
assert set(bundle.metrics.values) == {"rmse", "mape", "coverage_80"}
assert bundle.metrics.n_holdout == 48

from mapi_sdk import score_bundle

future_weeks = pd.date_range(weeks[-1] + pd.Timedelta(weeks=1), periods=4, freq="W-SUN")
plan = xr.Dataset(
    {
        "price": (dims, np.full((4, 2, 4), 2.9)),
        "promo": (dims, np.zeros((4, 2, 4))),
    },
    # "west" opens next month: the model has never seen it
    coords={"store": [*stores, "west"], "sku": skus, "week": future_weeks},
)

forecast = score_bundle(
    bundle,
    """
    apiVersion: mapi/v1
    kind: ScoreRequest
    model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
    mode: forecast
    horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
    output: {summary: [median, q10, q90]}
    """,
    plan,
    registry=registry,
)
summary = forecast["summary"].to_dataset()
print(summary["y_hat"].dims)  # ('stat', 'store', 'sku', 'week'), in your names
print(summary["y_hat"].sel(stat="median", store="west").values.round(1))
print(forecast.attrs["representation"])  # quantiles: what this model's uncertainty is
print(forecast.attrs["output_space"])  # {"y_hat": "raw"}: log1p undone, back in units sold
print(forecast.attrs["issues"])  # an info notice: 1 new level of 'store' uses 'pooled'
assert set(summary["store"].values) == {"north", "south", "east", "west"}
assert summary.sizes["week"] == 4

from mapi_spec import ErrorCode, MapiError


def try_score(request_yaml: str, payload: xr.Dataset) -> ErrorCode:
    try:
        score_bundle(bundle, request_yaml, payload, registry=registry)
    except MapiError as err:
        print(err.code, "-", err)
        return err.code
    raise AssertionError("expected a typed error")


FORECAST = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://quickstart/fruit-demand
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}
"""

# 1. a forecast without next month's promotions: promo is future_required
code_1 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.drop_vars("promo"))

# 2. quantiles are per cell, so "total over all stores" would be a made-up number
code_2 = try_score(FORECAST + "output: {aggregate: {over: [store]}}\n", plan)

# 3. a product outside the fitted range: sku is a fixed dim
code_3 = try_score(FORECAST, plan.assign_coords(sku=["apples", "kiwis"]))
assert code_1 is ErrorCode.MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE
assert code_2 is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED
assert code_3 is ErrorCode.UNSEEN_LEVELS

from mapi_sdk import CoordPlan
from mapi_spec import load_score_request, validate_score_request

# What the API stores next to a model version: JSON only, no arrays, no plugin code.
meta = CoordPlan(load_score_request(FORECAST), bundle.resolved, bundle.fit_coords).metadata()
print(f"{len(meta.model_dump_json()) / 1024:.0f} KiB of metadata")

request = load_score_request(FORECAST + "output: {summary: [hdi_90], draws: 100}\n")
for issue in validate_score_request(request, meta):  # no data, no model: milliseconds
    print(issue.code, issue.pointer, "-", issue.message)
# MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE /data - forecasting needs future values of ['price', 'promo'] ...
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/draws - draws were requested but the model's
#                                        representation is 'quantiles'
# CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED /output/summary/0 - summary 'hdi_90' cannot be computed from
#                                            'quantiles' output
assert any(
    i.code is ErrorCode.CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED for i in validate_score_request(request, meta)
)

import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mapi_sdk import Bundle

out = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "fruit-demand-v1"
manifest = bundle.write(out)
print(sorted(p.name for p in out.iterdir()))
# ['bundle.zarr.zip', 'diagnostics.json', 'evaluation', 'manifest.json', 'metrics.json',
#  'plots.json']  - `evaluation/` is the train-only fit that produced the holdout metrics

again = Bundle.read(out, registry)  # every file's size and hashes are verified here
assert again.bundle_id == bundle.bundle_id

print(manifest.role, manifest.plugin["id"], manifest.spec_hash[:19])
# production tabular.regressor sha256:...
print(manifest.files["bundle.zarr.zip"])  # size, crc32c, md5 (GCS forms) and sha256
print(manifest.lineage["evaluation_bundle"])  # the train-only fit behind the metrics

tree = again.to_tree()  # the whole bundle as one xr.DataTree
print(sorted(tree.children))
# ['binding', 'fit_coords', 'model', 'native', 'preprocess', 'schema', 'spec']
print(sorted(tree["preprocess"].children))  # ['cal', 'logy']: one node per step
assert {"model", "preprocess", "native", "spec"} <= set(tree.children)

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• To do the same fit and score as runs through an executor, read Runs and executors.
  • To learn why the split occurred at that position, read Pipelines and stages.
  • To try a Bayesian model, read about the radon model or the marketing-mix model.

docs.title: Quickstart: zero to first model in 10 minutes v0.2
docs.text:
In this quickstart, you start the platform on your own machine and load a demo dataset. Then you fit a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model from the web app. You read its scorecard and plots, and you score an 8-week forecast. You do not need Docker or a cloud account. PostgreSQL is embedded, and the object storage is a local emulator of Google Cloud Storage.

Step What occurs Time on a laptop 1. Install Python and JavaScript dependencies 2–5 min the first time 2. Start the stack Database, object store, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox about 10 s 3. Load the demo Three datasets and a model spec, through the API about 40 s 4. Fit from the browser A sandboxed fit run that you watch live 20–60 s 5. Inspect Scorecard, diagnostics, plots, provenance – 6. Score An 8-week forecast. The run uses the fitted preprocessing again. about 10 s

We did exactly these steps on a new clone when we wrote this page. The time from make dev to a scored forecast was less than three minutes. The screenshots below come from that run.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need these items:

  • macOS or Linux, with about 2 GB of free disk space.
  • uv. If necessary, it installs Python 3.12 for you.
  • Node.js 22 or newer, with pnpm. corepack enable gives the pinned pnpm version.
  • git. If you want to follow the HTTP examples later, you also need jq and curl.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url> modeling-api
cd modeling-api
make install          # uv sync --all-packages, then pnpm install

make install puts all the Python packages of the workspace into .venv. It puts the dependencies of the web app into node_modules. It installs nothing globally.

docs.title: 2. Start the stack
docs.text:
make dev

make dev runs all the services in the foreground. Each output line starts with the name of its service. When the stack is ready, make dev shows all 6 services up. Do not stop make dev. To stop all the services, push Ctrl+C.

The first start also puts a sandboxed describe run in the queue. This run exports the catalog of installed models and steps. It finishes in a few seconds.

Service Address Web app http://127.0.0.1:5173 API http://127.0.0.1:8000 (OpenAPI document at /openapi.json) Plot sandbox (a separate origin, on purpose) http://127.0.0.1:5174 GCS shim (signed URLs point here) http://127.0.0.1:4443

Port 8000 (or any other) already taken?

Export the applicable variable before make dev. Also export it in each other shell that you use:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000
export MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173
export MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174

make dev, make seed, the CLI, the Python client and the web app all read the same variables. We made this page on exactly these ports. Troubleshooting gives more data.

docs.title: 3. Load the demo
docs.text:
In a second shell, type this command:

make seed

API http://127.0.0.1:8000 is ok (version 0.7.0)
uploading eu_media_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/eu_media_daily@v1 ready
uploading fx_daily (17 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/fx_daily@v1 ready
uploading holidays_eu (7 KiB) ...
  dataset://default/holidays_eu@v1 ready
spec spec://default/eu-geo-mmm@r1: valid

make seed uses only the public API. For each table, it does these steps:

  1. It asks for a signed upload URL.
  2. It sends the file directly to object storage.
  3. It starts a sandboxed ingest run. The run opens the file and checks it against its schema. Then it stores an immutable, content-addressed version.

Then make seed saves the model spec and validates it.

The data is the E33 example of the conformance corpus. It contains these tables:

  • 30 weeks of daily spend for each market and channel, for NL, DE and UK.
  • Daily revenue for each market (UK in GBP).
  • An FX table.
  • A holiday calendar.

To score, you need the spend that you plan for the next weeks. Upload it with the CLI:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/     # the demo tables, score payloads and spec
uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future

docs.title: 4. Fit from the browser
docs.text:
1. Open http://127.0.0.1:5173.
  2. Go to Build.
  3. Click the eu-geo-mmm row.

When the editor opened, it validated the spec on the server. All dataset:// references, all steps and the model settings resolve. The panel on the right shows what each step of the pipeline does to the data. The split into training and holdout weeks is after the weekly step. The reason is that a week exists only from that stage on.

Push Fit. The run page follows the run through server-sent events:

  • Starting the sandbox: the supervisor of the run read its one-time bootstrap object. It deleted the object before model code started.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is usual on a laptop. The local executor cannot run the model code as a separate user. Containers and the cloud executor can.
  • The progress bar and the message come directly from the sampler.

The spec uses very small sampler settings, so the fit takes much less than a minute. On a new machine, the first fit also compiles PyTensor code. When the fit succeeds, the platform does these steps:

  1. It checks each file that the run wrote against the checksums of the storage.
  2. It copies the files to a location that runs cannot get to.
  3. It signs a manifest.

Push Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 5. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The scorecard flags R-hat and effective sample size. Two chains of 100 draws are not sufficient to converge. Each warning tells you what to do. The metrics come from the 8 holdout weeks. The model scored these weeks through the same code path as a forecast. This occurred before the model was fitted again on all the data (fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit).

Open Plots → Contribution by channel:

Each plot is a Vega-Lite or Plotly spec that the server sanitized. The plot shows inside an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> that comes from the own origin of the plot sandbox. Provenance shows the signed manifest, each stored object with its generation, and the lineage.

docs.title: 6. Score a forecast
docs.text:
Push Score (top right). What this model needs lists the inputs that the model reads and the data that it was fitted on. The form shows only the modes that this model supports.

  1. Keep Forecast and 8 periods.
  2. Under Values to score, select Use a dataset.
  3. Type dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1. Alternatively, keep Type values and type the planned spend into the grid. Then you do not need an upload.
  4. Under Advanced, keep the fx side table at the version that the fit used. It covers the forecast weeks.
  5. Push Forecast.

The run did not fit the model again. It used the fitted preprocessing again: currency conversion, weekly resampling, scaling, and the last weeks of spend that each market carries into the adstock. Then it inverted the result back to weekly EUR. The output_space of the result tells you this.

docs.title: Stop, and start again later
docs.text:
make stop             # or Ctrl-C in the make dev shell
make dev              # everything you loaded is still there (.local/)
make clean-local      # delete the local database and objects, start from scratch

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Tour every page of the web app

    Datasets and CSV mapping, revisions and dry-runs, run controls, the data tree and counterfactuals.

  • Do the same from the command line

    mapi datasets upload, mapi fit --remote @, mapi score and --json for scripts.

  • Or from Python

    mapi_client.Client: uploads, live events, model versions and xr.DataTree results.

  • Understand what happened

    The control plane, the run sandbox, storage integrity and the event path.

docs.title: Administration v0.3
docs.text:
From v0.3, one deployment serves many organisations. This guide is for the persons who manage the deployment. It tells who can do what, and how the platform limits compute and charges for it. It also tells what to do when a problem occurs. For the concepts, see Tenancy and authentication and Quotas and cost. For sign-in, see Authentication.

There are three administrative jobs, and the platform keeps them separate:

Who Holds Works in Does Platform operator A verified e-mail in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in Admin console, mapi admin …, /v1/admin/* Creates and suspends tenants. Sets trust tiers and quotas. Sets kill switches. Monitors executors. Reads all audit logs. Never reads tenant content (datasets, specs, models, plots). Tenant admin The admin role, tenant-wide Members, Usage (Organisation), /v1/tenants/{tenant}/… Creates projects. Adds and removes persons. Reads the bill and the audit log of the tenant. Project admin The admin role in one project Members, Tokens, Usage Manages the members, endpoints, plugins and the tokens of all persons in that project.

All examples on this page come from one walkthrough, docs/snippets/admin_tour.sh. The test suite runs it against a development stack (make dev). The walkthrough signs in two times through the development identity provider. It signs in as admin@dev.local (a platform operator). It also signs in as analyst@dev.local, who becomes the admin of the new tenant.

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
export MAPI_URL=$API
dev_login() {  # dev profile only: an ID token for one seeded account, valid for an hour
  python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))' "$API" "$1"
}
OPERATOR=$(dev_login admin@dev.local)          # a platform operator
TENANT_ADMIN=$(dev_login analyst@dev.local)    # becomes the new tenant's admin below
MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR mapi whoami

On a real deployment, each person runs mapi login instead (see Authentication). Operator commands always need a sign-in. An API token never has operator powers, also when its owner is an operator.

docs.title: Tenants
docs.text:
A tenant is an organisation. It is the boundary for bills, isolation and quotas. PostgreSQL row-level security keeps the rows of each tenant separate. Each storage key starts with t/{tenant}/. Only operators create tenants:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin tenants create "$TENANT" --name "Acme Retail" --tier verified \
    --residency eu --admin-email analyst@dev.local --yes
mapi admin tenants ls
Field Values Effect id A lowercase slug (acme) Part of each reference (dataset://growth/eu_media_daily is in a project of a tenant) and of each storage key. You cannot change it. Trust tier internal, verified, public, self-hosted-trusted Where the runs of the tenant can execute, and its default quotas (below) Status active, suspended, deleting suspended: persons can read and download. They cannot create, change or run anything. deleting: there is no access. Data residency eu, us, asia or one region (europe-west1) The platform puts runs only on executors in a region that matches. A change applies only to new runs. Admin e-mail Any address The platform invites this person as tenant admin. The person claims the invitation at the first sign-in with that verified e-mail.

The Admin console lists each tenant with its tier, status and residency. Only operators can use it. Other persons see an explanation. New tenant and Edit do the same as the commands above. To suspend or delete a tenant, you must give a reason and type the id of the tenant.

To stop an organisation in a reversible way, suspend it. Its persons keep read access to their work. The platform refuses each change, upload and run with 403 FORBIDDEN. Operators can still do actions on the tenant.

mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status suspended --reason "contract ended" --yes
mapi admin tenants update "$TENANT" --status active --yes

docs.title: Trust tiers
docs.text:
The tier controls where the code of a tenant can run. The dispatcher enforces this in code. Tenant configuration never controls it. The dispatcher never submits a run to an executor that does not have the isolation that the tier needs. It fails the run with INFRA_ERROR and a detail that tells what is necessary. An example is verified tenants require an executor with isolation >= gvisor and enforced egress/DNS. The tier also sets the default quotas of the tenant, until an operator overrides them.

Tier Executor must provide vCPU-s / day vCPU-s / month Concurrent runs Fan-out tasks Largest class Storage Egress / month Requests / min internal isolation ≥ process — — 100 1,000 — — — 6,000 self-hosted-trusted isolation ≥ process — — — — — — — — verified isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 86,400 1,000,000 20 256 L 100 GiB 100 GiB 600 public isolation ≥ gvisor, egress and DNS enforced 3,600 36,000 2 16 S 2 GiB 5 GiB 60

Platform-wide (global) defaults: concurrent_runs = 700. A dash means no limit at that level.

Which executors can take verified and public tenants today

Shared tiers need an executor with gVisor or microVM isolation and enforced egress and DNS. In v0.3, these executors can do this:

  • cloudrun-jobs, when MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED=true. The default is false. The reason is that nobody has verified the DNS response policy against a real Cloud Run Jobs execution yet. This is the first item of the M0 checklist. Until then, verified and public runs fail at dispatch. They do not run on a weaker executor.
  • docker-gvisor, only with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=none. This setting needs an HTTPS bootstrap URL. Thus it is not available with the local GCS shim.

internal and self-hosted-trusted tenants run on all executors, also on local-process. (local-process does not start under MAPI_PROFILE=multi-tenant.)

docs.title: Projects and members
docs.text:
A project is a workspace inside a tenant. It is the unit of access control. Tenant admins create projects and control who works in them. There is no CLI command for members yet. Thus the walkthrough uses the HTTP API:

as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects" \
    -d '{"id": "growth", "name": "Growth marketing"}' | jq -c '{tenant_id, id, name}'
as_admin -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    -d '{"email": "viewer@dev.local", "role": "runner"}' | jq -c '{project_id, email, role}'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t(tenant-wide)"'
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/projects/growth/members" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.email // .principal_id)\t\(.role)\t\(.project_id // "(tenant-wide)")"'

A membership grants one role. The role applies to one project, or tenant-wide (to the tenant and all its projects). In a project, the effective role of a person is the higher of the two. The platform reads membership at each request. Thus, when you remove a person from a project, their sessions and their tokens in that project stop immediately.

Members shows the members of the project. With Organisation, it shows the tenant-wide grants. Admins can change a role in the list or remove a member. They can also use Add member with an e-mail address. If nobody has signed in with that address, the platform makes an invitation. The person claims it at the first sign-in. A grant with the mark organisation comes from a tenant-wide membership. You change it in that membership.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
There are four roles. Each role includes the role before it. Permission to run is above permission to edit on purpose. The reason is that compute costs money. Thus you can let a person edit a spec, but not start a 200-task sweep.

Role Adds viewer Read all items in the project. Validate specs. Mint tokens for themselves. editor Create and change datasets, specs and saved plots. runner Spend compute: submit, cancel and retry runs, score models and endpoints, and render plots. admin Manage members, endpoints, plugins and the tokens of other persons. Delete items.

Since v0.5, the workflow and governance rules use the same sequence of roles. Editors write workflows. Runners run workflows and submit models for validation. Project admins edit policies, and tenant admins edit the tenant-wide policies. Admins also deprecate validated versions.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A capability is a grant in addition to a role, for each project membership. At this time, the only capability is reviewer. A reviewer is the second person who approves model validations when a governance policy asks for it (Validate models with governance policies). Admins grant it in the Reviewer column of Members, or with capabilities on the membership. Project admins have it implicitly. Viewers cannot have it. Nobody can approve their own submission or approve through an API token.

Capability Needed for What it allows reviewer model approve Approve or reject model validations that wait for a second person (POST /v1/validations/{id}/approvals), never the member's own submissions (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and never through an API token. Granted per project membership (capabilities on the membership, or the Reviewer column of Members); viewers cannot hold it.

This is the complete matrix. It comes from mapi_spec.tenancy.PERMISSIONS, the table that each component checks. tenant-wide means that only a tenant-wide grant counts. The platform refuses a pair that is not in the list to all persons:

Resource Action viewer editor runner admin Operator tenant read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ update ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ delete ✓ manage (tier, status, residency, identity verification) ✓ tenant_member read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ tenant-wide delete ✓ tenant-wide project read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ delete ✓ tenant-wide member read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ token read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ delete (own tokens; manage covers everyone's) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ manage (list and revoke other members' tokens) ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ run read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ delete ✓ validate (submit, resubmit or cancel a governance validation) ✓ ✓ approve (needs the reviewer capability; never the submitter, never a token) ✓ with reviewer ✓ with reviewer ✓ update (deprecate a validated version) ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run (score) ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ manage (override a promotion gate; sessions only) ✓ plot read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ run (render) ✓ ✓ delete (saved plots) ✓ ✓ ✓ embed read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ ✓ ✓ webhook read ✓ create ✓ update (includes rotating the secret and replaying deliveries) ✓ delete ✓ plugin read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ delete ✓ usage read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ billing read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ audit read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ quota read ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ kill_switch read ✓ update ✓ executor read ✓ update ✓ event create — — — — internal services only tenant_deletion read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ create ✓ tenant-wide cancel (within the grace period) ✓ tenant-wide manage (purge, retry) ✓ tenant_export read ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ tenant-wide workflow read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ update ✓ ✓ ✓ delete ✓ run ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ policy read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ tenant_policy read ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide ✓ tenant-wide create ✓ tenant-wide update ✓ tenant-wide delete ✓ tenant-wide

The Permissions reference has the same matrix. It shows the token scopes and the permissions of the operators next to it.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs use API tokens. Examples are the Python client, the CLI in CI and BI exports. A person mints a token in one project. The token is bound to that project. It acts as that person, but its scopes limit what it can do. All persons with a role can mint tokens for themselves. Project admins can list and revoke the tokens of all persons.

export MAPI_TOKEN=$TENANT_ADMIN
mapi use "$TENANT/growth"
mapi tokens create nightly-report -s models:read --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 60 \
    --budget 3600 --budget-period day > nightly-report.token   # the secret, once
mapi tokens ls

New token asks for these items:

  • A name.
  • The scopes.
  • Optional endpoint aliases.
  • An expiry. The default is 90 days. The maximum is 365 days.
  • A limit of requests for each minute.
  • A vCPU-second budget for each day or month.

The form also shows your role. Your role is the maximum that your tokens can do.

The platform shows the secret one time only. The server stores only an HMAC of it. Thus, if you lose a token, you revoke and replace it. You cannot get it back. A revocation has an effect on the next request.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Scopes can only make a token more limited. A token can never do more than the role of its owner. The role and the scope must both permit an action. admin covers all that the role of the owner permits. This table comes from mapi_spec.tokens.scope_allows:

Resource Action models:read runs:create score:* plugins:publish datasets:write endpoints:promote webhooks:manage workflows:write workflows:run models:validate policies:manage project read ✓ ✓ catalog read ✓ ✓ ✓ dataset read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ spec read ✓ ✓ run read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ ✓ ✓ cancel ✓ ✓ model read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ ✓ validate ✓ endpoint read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ run ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ promote ✓ delete ✓ plot read ✓ ✓ run ✓ webhook read ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓ plugin read ✓ create ✓ delete ✓ usage read ✓ ✓ workflow read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ ✓ run ✓ cancel ✓ policy read ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ create ✓ update ✓ delete ✓

score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:geo-mmm-prod). score:* covers all endpoints of the project. A token can never do tenant-level actions (members, the bill, the audit log) or operator actions.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text:
The platform limits compute in vCPU-seconds. It checks three levels, in this sequence:

  1. The limits of the token.
  2. The policy of the tenant, or the defaults of its tier (above).
  3. The platform-wide limits that protect the cloud project.

The first limit that a request would exceed answers 429 with QUOTA_EXCEEDED or RATE_LIMITED. The answer has a detail that names the level and the limit. It also has Retry-After with the time when the limit resets. Quotas and cost explains each limit. Operators override the defaults of a tenant:

export MAPI_TOKEN=$OPERATOR
mapi admin quotas set tenant "$TENANT" --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 \
    --concurrent-runs 40 --max-fanout-tasks 256 --storage 200GiB \
    --note "private beta customer" --yes
mapi admin quotas ls

set replaces the policy. It removes the limits that you do not give. For those limits, the tier default applies again. mapi admin quotas rm tenant acme removes the override.

docs.title: Cost and usage
docs.text:
When you submit a run, the platform makes an estimate of its cost. It checks the estimate against the quotas. When each attempt ends, the platform meters the run. It uses the vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds of the resource class of the run, at the versioned price table of the deployment. It writes the result to an append-only cost ledger. Amounts are exact integer micros of a currency. Each amount names the price table that it used. The page of a run and mapi runs get show its cost. Usage pages add the costs.

mapi usage --group-by resource_class             # the selected project, this UTC month
mapi usage --tenant "$TENANT" --period day       # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)

Usage shows the cost, compute, runs and memory of a project for a UTC day or month. With Organisation, it shows these values for the full tenant. It also shows these items:

  • A daily chart.
  • How near each quota is. It gives warnings at 70 % and 90 %.
  • The totals for each token and for each resource class.

All persons in a project can see its usage. The tenant-wide view needs a tenant-wide admin. The amounts are an estimate of compute cost at list prices. They are not an invoice.

docs.title: Kill switches
docs.text:
Two platform-wide switches stop compute quickly. The platform audits both, and both need a reason:

Switch Effect Uploaded code (untrusted_execution_enabled) Off: the platform does not accept or lease runs of plugin code that a tenant uploaded. Built-in models continue to work. Global spend cap When the spend of the platform in the current UTC day or month gets to the cap, no new compute starts. Only internal tenants can still start compute. 
mapi admin kill-switches set --spend-cap 500 --spend-cap-period month \
    --reason "private beta budget" --yes
mapi admin kill-switches get

The first step of the sandbox-escape runbook (ops/runbooks/sandbox-escape.md) is to turn off uploaded code. At 70 % of the cap, spend opens a ticket. At 90 %, it pages a person (Observability).

docs.title: Executors
docs.text:
Executors in the admin console (and mapi admin executors ls) show these data for each execution backend:

  • Health and isolation.
  • Resource classes.
  • Work that runs and work in the queue.
  • Failures in the last hour.
  • The jobs.run rate against the limit.
  • If it passed the executor conformance suite.

trusted tenants only marks an executor that never gets runs of verified and public tenants.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text:
The platform adds security-relevant actions to an audit log. These actions are:

  • Sign-ins, and sign-ins that failed.
  • Changes to tenants, projects and memberships.
  • Token creation, revocation and failed use.
  • Changes to quotas and kill switches, and quota denials.
  • Run creation and cancellation.
  • Integrity failures.
  • Artifact links and dataset downloads.
  • Refused run events.

Each entry records who did the action, and if that person was an operator. It records what the action was, on which resource, the result and a problem code. The platform keeps IP addresses and user agents only as keyed hashes. You can correlate entries, but you cannot get the original values back.

mapi admin audit --tenant "$TENANT" -n 10        # operators: any tenant
# tenant admins: their own tenant's log
as_admin "$API/v1/tenants/$TENANT/audit?limit=5" \
    | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.ts)  \(.action)  \(.resource_kind):\(.resource_id)  \(.outcome)"'

Tenant admins read the log of their own tenant (GET /v1/tenants/{tenant}/audit). Operators read the logs of all tenants in the Audit log tab or with mapi admin audit. They can filter by tenant, project, actor, action, result and time.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Authentication: browser sign-in, the development IdP, Identity Platform, API tokens and the CLI.
  • Permissions: the generated matrices.
  • CLI reference: all mapi admin and mapi tokens options.
  • HTTP API: multi-tenant API: the endpoints.
  • Observability: the metrics, alerts and runbooks for the kill switches and quotas.

docs.title: Authentication v0.3
docs.text:
A v0.3 deployment answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED to all callers that it does not know. There are three ways in, one for each type of caller:

Caller Signs in with Sends Reference A person in a browser The identity provider of the organisation (OpenID Connect) An HttpOnly session cookie. The app never sees a token. Browser sign-in A person in a terminal mapi login: the same provider, from the command line The ID token of the provider as Authorization: Bearer The command line A program Nothing. A person mints an API token for it. Authorization: Bearer mapi_… API tokens

In all three ways, the caller is a user (usr_…) with roles in projects. The platform checks each request against those roles at that time (Administration). This page is for the persons who sign in and who set up sign-in. For the protocol details (cookies, CSRF, PKCE, JWKS, the database roles), see Authentication and tenant isolation.

docs.title: Browser sign-in
docs.text:
If you open the web app without a session, it shows Sign in to your workspace. Continue to sign in goes to /auth/login on the API. The API sends the browser to the identity provider. After the sign-in at the provider, the browser comes back to the page where it started.

The API does all the OpenID Connect work. This work is the authorization code with PKCE, a nonce, and the verification of the ID token against the keys of the provider. The API keeps the tokens. The browser holds only two cookies: a __Host- session cookie that scripts cannot read, and a CSRF token. A session ends after 2 hours without activity or after 12 hours in total. It also ends when you click Sign out.

After you sign in, the project switcher at the top left lists each tenant and project where you have a role. It shows that role and the trust tier of the tenant. All that the app shows and does applies to the selected project. The app sends the project as X-Mapi-Project on each request. The avatar menu shows who you are. A shield marks a platform operator.

The first sign-in of a person creates their user from the (issuer, subject) of the provider. If the provider tells that the e-mail is verified, the platform also claims all invitations to that address. Invitations come from Add member (a tenant admin) or --admin-email (an operator). A person with no membership yet sees You are not in a project yet.

docs.title: The development IdP
docs.text:
make dev (and Docker Compose) run the servers in the dev profile. This profile mounts a small OpenID provider inside the API at /dev/idp. Then sign-in works offline, through exactly the same code path as a real provider. It uses RS256-signed ID tokens, PKCE and single-use codes.

There are no passwords. All persons who can get to a dev API can sign in as any listed account. The accounts come from MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS:

Account Gets at start-up admin@dev.local Admin of the default tenant and a platform operator analyst@dev.local runner in default/default viewer@dev.local (and all other addresses) viewer in default/default

Scripts sign in without a browser with mapi_client.oidc.dev_idp_login(api_url, email). This function does the same flow and returns an ID token that is valid for an hour. make seed, the end-to-end tests and the walkthroughs on this page use it. A server in any other profile answers 404. Thus you cannot use the function against production. The walkthrough below is docs/snippets/auth_tour.sh. The test suite runs it against make dev:

API=${MAPI_URL:-${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}}
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'anonymous: %{http_code}\n' "$API/v1/me"      # 401: sign in first
# dev profile only: what `mapi login` gets from a real identity provider, without a browser
ID_TOKEN=$(python -c 'import sys; from mapi_client.oidc import dev_idp_login
print(dev_idp_login(sys.argv[1], "analyst@dev.local"))' "$API")
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" \
  | jq -c '{email: .principal.email, auth, operator,
            projects: [.tenants[].projects[] | "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id) \(.role)"]}'

anonymous: 401
{"email":"analyst@dev.local","auth":"session","operator":false,"projects":["acme/growth admin","acme/retail admin","default/default runner"]}

MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant make dev turns off sign-in fully. This is the v0.2 behaviour: each request acts as the local administrator of default.

docs.title: Set up a real identity provider
docs.text: The API can sign in persons with any OpenID Connect provider that has the authorization-code flow. The provider needs an issuer whose /.well-known/openid-configuration lists an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint and a JWKS.

docs.title: Google accounts
docs.text:
Google accounts are the default of the Google Cloud deployment. They are the simplest selection for an organisation on Google Workspace.

  1. In the Google Cloud console (APIs & Services → Credentials), create an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Set the authorized redirect URI to https://<your app domain>/auth/callback.
  2. Give the id to Terraform (oidc_client_id in terraform.tfvars). Give the secret as the ephemeral variable TF_VAR_oidc_client_secret, with oidc_client_secret_version = 1 (step 4 of the deployment).
  3. If you do not use Terraform, set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET on the API.
  4. Put the e-mails of the operators in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS.
  5. Create the tenant of each organisation with an --admin-email (Administration).

MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS='{"hd": "acme.com"}' selects a Workspace domain in advance in the account chooser of Google. It is only a hint. Memberships control who can do what. The e-mail domain never controls it.

docs.title: Identity Platform
docs.text:
Terraform also enables Identity Platform in the control project (infra/terraform/modules/control/identity.tf). It registers the domain of the app as an authorized domain. It turns off anonymous sign-in and, by default, e-mail/password sign-in. You add SAML and OIDC providers for enterprise single sign-on in Identity Platform. Add them in the console, or with google_identity_platform_*_idp_config resources outside the module. Keep these resources outside the module, because their secrets must not be in its state.

Known gap in v0.3

The sign-in of the API cannot use the tokens of Identity Platform yet. You get those tokens (issuer https://securetoken.google.com/<project>) with the client SDK of Identity Platform. That issuer has no authorization-code endpoint for the API to redirect to. Until that adapter exists, point MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER at Google (above). As an alternative, point it directly at the own OpenID provider of the organisation (below). Until then, the Identity Platform configuration that Terraform creates causes no problems.

docs.title: Other providers
docs.text:
Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0 and all other standard providers work in the same way:

  1. Register a web client with the redirect URI https://<your app domain>/auth/callback.
  2. Set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER to its issuer.
  3. If its discovery document is not under the issuer, set MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL.
  4. Set MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID and MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.

ID tokens must have a signature with an asymmetric algorithm (MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS, default RS256,ES256).

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
mapi login signs in with the same provider, from the terminal:

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • With a browser, it opens the page of the provider. It listens one time on 127.0.0.1 for the redirect (authorization code with PKCE).
  • --device shows a short code. Type the code on a different device. This works with providers that support the device flow.
  • --with-token reads an API token from standard input and stores it instead (CI).

The CLI keeps the sign-in in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600). It sends the ID token of the provider as Authorization: Bearer. The API accepts such a token only when its audience is one of MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS (default mapi-cli). Register the CLI with your provider as a public installed app client. Use a loopback redirect, PKCE and the openid email scopes. The installed-app clients of Google need a client secret. The CLI reads it from MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and never shows it.

To sign in against the development IdP, use this command:

mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost \
           --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp

Then select the project where commands act. Use mapi use <tenant>/<project>, --project or MAPI_PROJECT. mapi whoami shows who you are, how you signed in and your projects. See The command line.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs never sign in. A person mints a token for them in one project, with only the scopes that the program needs. The token then acts as that person, but only in that project. Its scopes limit what it can do. To mint a token, use one of these methods:

  • In the web app, use Tokens → New token (Administration).
  • From the CLI, use mapi tokens create.
  • Over HTTP, use this request:
CREATED=$(curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" \
  -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "auth-guide", "scopes": ["models:read"], "expires_in_days": 1}')
TOKEN=$(jq -r .secret <<<"$CREATED")             # shown once: store it now
TOKEN_ID=$(jq -r .token.id <<<"$CREATED")
jq -c '.token | {id, display, scopes, project: "\(.tenant_id)/\(.project_id)", expires_at}' \
  <<<"$CREATED"

{"id":"tok_01m50mxfqh4k95ed2dv2jc005v","display":"mapi_hhb9gjzf_…","scopes":["models:read"],"project":"default/default","expires_at":"2026-10-16T20:44:02.161164Z"}

The secret (mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>) is in the response one time only. The server keeps only an HMAC of it. Lists show the prefix (mapi_hhb9gjzf_…). Clients and secret scanners use the built-in checksum to reject an incorrect or invented token. They do not have to ask the server.

A program sends the token as a bearer. The token is bound to its project, so it does not need an X-Mapi-Project header:

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{auth, operator}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/runs?limit=2" \
  | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.id) \(.kind) \(.state)"'   # bound to its project: no header needed

The Python client accepts the token as Client(token=…) or MAPI_TOKEN. The CLI accepts it as --token, MAPI_TOKEN or mapi login --with-token (Python client). Both refuse to send a token over plain HTTP to an address that is not a loopback address.

docs.title: What a token cannot do
docs.text:
Scopes can only make a token more limited. A models:read token cannot start a run, also when its owner is a runner. A token cannot act in a different project. No token has operator powers:

# models:read cannot spend compute, even though its owner is a runner
curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"kind": "fit", "spec": "spec://default/eu-geo-mmm"}' \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
# a token never acts outside its project, or as an operator
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth' "$API/v1/runs" \
  | jq -c '{status, code}'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/admin/tenants" | jq -c '{status, code}'

{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}
{"status":403,"code":"FORBIDDEN"}

Tokens expire. The default is 90 days, and the maximum is 365 days. If you revoke a token, or remove its owner from the project, the token stops at the next request:

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'revoke: %{http_code}\n' -X DELETE "$API/v1/tokens/$TOKEN_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ID_TOKEN" -H 'X-Mapi-Project: default/default'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/v1/me" | jq -c '{status, code}'   # at once

revoke: 204
{"status":401,"code":"UNAUTHENTICATED"}

The platform writes failed uses of a known token to the audit log as token.auth_failed. Examples are an incorrect secret, or an expired or revoked token. No error ever shows the token.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text: Browser session mapi login API token Identity The person The person The person who minted it Projects Each project with a role (select one for each request) Same Only the project where it was minted Permissions The role The role The role and the scopes Operator powers Yes, for operators Yes, for operators Never Needs CSRF token Yes, for changes No No Ends 2 h without activity, 12 h total, sign-out mapi logout. If the provider gave a refresh token, the CLI uses it to renew the ID token. If not, use mapi login again. Expiry or revocation

docs.text:

  • Authentication and tenant isolation: the view of the operator, with cookies, CSRF, row-level security and Pub/Sub push authentication.
  • Tenancy and authentication: the concepts and the request-authorization pipeline.

docs.title: Choosing a model v0.5
docs.text: You do not need to know what "SARIMAX" means to select a good forecast model. Also, you do not need to read a statistics textbook to know when not to use one. Each model, preprocessing step, workflow node, governance check and template has an About card in plain words. Help me choose asks some questions about your goal and your data. Then it gives a ranked shortlist with the reasons. This page shows the two tools. Then it compares the model families, for persons who want the details. For the contract behind the tools, see About cards and choosing.

docs.title: Answer a few questions
docs.text:
There are eight questions. All are optional. The goal has the most weight:

Question Answers What do you want to do? measure what marketing adds · plan a budget · forecast · understand drivers · predict per item · understand choices · find regimes · see series move together · check data · validate a model What does your data look like? one number over time · a few related numbers · the same numbers for many markets, stores or products · purchases or choices · a table without time How often do you record the data? daily · weekly · monthly or less often · not over time How much history? under a year · one to three years · more Other columns that could explain it? yes (prices, promotions, weather, spend) · no Do you need a range? essential · it would be good · one number is enough How much do you know about statistics? new to it · the basics · expert How quickly do you need results? seconds · minutes · can wait TerminalPythonHTTPWeb app 
mapi choose                                   # questions, one at a time; Enter skips one
mapi choose -a goal=forecast -a data_shape=one_series -a drivers=yes -a experience=beginner
mapi about ts.sarimax                         # one item's About card
mapi about ts.sarimax --expert                # ... with the maths and references

mapi choose asks the questions one at a time. Type a number. For questions that accept more than one answer, type more than one number. To skip a question, push Enter. The command shows the shortlist, and then the About card of the first three items. This is the result for the four answers above, on a local stack (shortened):

Recommended for you

━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╇━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   │                     │                   │      │              │                    │ over time

Smooth trend forecast  model ts.hsgp_trend
Forecasts one regular series with a smooth, flexible trend and a repeating seasonal pattern, and gives a range of likely values.
difficulty: beginner   typical time: minutes
…
unanswered (answer them to sharpen the ranking): frequency, history, uncertainty, speed

The answer "new to it" (statistics) has an effect. Models that need more experience have a caution, and they rank below the models for beginners. Examples are ts.ardl above and ts.sarimax in position six. The models for beginners include the readiness workflow, which selects the settings of an ARIMAX for you. If you answer experience=intermediate, or skip the question, ts.ardl and ts.sarimax come first. These are the models that use the drivers.

from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()  # MAPI_URL, the `mapi login` sign-in (or MAPI_TOKEN) and MAPI_PROJECT

result = api.catalog.recommend(
    goal="forecast", data_shape="one_series", drivers="yes", experience="beginner", limit=3
)
for item in result.items:  # best first, with the reasons in plain words
    print(f"{item.score:.0%}  {item.title}  ({item.kind.value} {item.id})")
    for reason in item.reasons_plain:
        print("     +", reason)
    for caution in item.cautions_plain:
        print("     !", caution)

card = api.catalog.about("ts.sarimax", kind="model")  # any item's About card
print(card.summary_plain)
print("use it when:", "; ".join(card.use_when))
print("pick something else when:", "; ".join(card.avoid_when))

api GET "/v1/catalog/chooser"        # the questions
api GET "/v1/catalog/recommendations?goal=forecast&data_shape=one_series&drivers=yes&experience=beginner&limit=3"
api GET "/v1/catalog/abouts?kind=model"

Help me choose on the model, template and workflow pickers asks the same questions. It shows the same ranking. Each card has About. About shows the plain explanation first. The expert details are folded away.

The ranking is deterministic, and you can see why each item has its position:

  • An answer that matches adds the weight of the question. An answer that does not match subtracts it.
  • Items that are more difficult than your experience lose points. Items that are slower than your answer for speed also lose points.
  • Each recommendation lists its reasons ("Suits: forecast the future").
  • Each recommendation lists its cautions ("Needs expert-level statistics knowledge", "Usually takes long").

Without a kind, the candidates are the items that you start from: models, guided templates and workflow templates. --kind step, node or check ranks only one type of item.

docs.title: Read an About card
docs.text:
mapi about ts.ets

Exponential smoothing forecast  ts.ets
Forecasts a series by giving recent values more weight than older ones, with optional trend and
seasonality, and is quick and robust.
difficulty: beginner   typical time: seconds
Use it when
  • You need a fast, reliable baseline forecast
  • The level, trend and seasonality shift slowly
Pick something else when
  • Outside drivers explain most of the movement
It needs
  • One number over time at a regular frequency
It assumes
  • Recent history is the best guide to the near future
You get
  • A forecast with a range
  • Level, trend and seasonal parts
Example: Forecast monthly demand 12 months ahead with a damped trend.
Related: ts.theta, ts.arima, evaluate.baseline
(--expert shows the maths and references)

Each card has the same parts:

  • A summary of one or two sentences, without jargon.
  • When to use the item, and when not to use it.
  • The data that it needs, and what it assumes.
  • What you get.
  • How difficult it is, and how long it usually takes.
  • A very small example, and related items.

--expert (or Expert detail in the web app) adds the maths and the references. The platform refuses catalog items that do not have a complete card. Thus each model that you can select explains itself. This also applies to your own plugins (the About check).

docs.title: The model families, compared
docs.text:
You want to Start with Why Then consider Measure what each marketing channel adds. Plan budgets. mmm.bayesian Pooled over markets. Adstock and saturation, business priors and lift tests. Ranges on all values. Budget optimisation. mmm.frequentist for a quick first look. The mmm_governed workflow to gate it on null tests. Forecast one series with known drivers (price, promotions) ts.sarimax Past values, season and drivers. Prediction intervals. Forecasts from planned drivers. The ts_readiness_arimax workflow. It selects the differencing and orders, and proves that the model is better than naive. Forecast without drivers, fast and robust ts.ets or ts.theta Strong, simple baselines that are difficult to beat The forecast_bakeoff workflow, which lets them compete See the trend under the noise ts.unobserved_components Level, trend, season and noise as separate parts ts.hsgp_trend for a Bayesian smooth trend Know how an effect builds up over weeks ts.ardl Lags of the drivers, selected automatically ts.ecm when the result and drivers have the same trend Several series that drive each other ts.var Impulse responses, variance decompositions, Granger tests ts.vecm when they are tied in the long run. The var_vecm_cointegration workflow decides. Find regimes (normal or caused by promotions) ts.markov_switching Probability of each regime for each period ts.gaussian_hmm for a Bayesian hidden-state model Predict a value for each store, product or customer sklearn.tabular_regressor Gradient boosting or forests. Quantiles and conformal intervals. tabular.hierarchical_glm when groups must borrow strength Understand which product people select choice.multinomial_logit Price and promotion effects, household effects Check data before you model it the Data Explorer Stationarity, cross-correlation with the KPI, STL, VIF, quality warnings Make sure that you can trust a model a governance policy Null tests, benchmarks, residuals, stability, signs

For the details of each family, see these pages: Marketing-mix models, statsmodels time-series models, forecasting, tabular models and the built-in models.

docs.title: When the chooser is not enough
docs.text:
• Compare. Do not guess. Fit two candidates and compare them on the same holdout. Use mapi explore compare model://growth/a@v1 model://growth/b@v1 (metrics, ranking and Diebold-Mariano tests). Alternatively, run a bake-off workflow.
  • Let the data decide the details. The readiness workflow selects differencing and ARMA orders with tests and information criteria. It records the reasons.
  • Make "good enough" explicit. A governance policy changes "it looks fine" into checks. The checks have thresholds, evidence and the approval of a second person.

docs.title: The command line v0.2
docs.text:
mapi (package mapi-cli, Apache-2.0) works in two locations:

  • Locally, without a server. You scaffold a spec, check it, fit it and score it in your own Python process, with the installed plugins (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec).
  • Remotely, against the HTTP API of a platform that runs. You upload datasets, fit, follow runs and score model versions (datasets, runs, and --remote on check, fit, score and catalog).

The generated CLI reference lists all commands and options. The examples on this page are scripts that the test suite runs. The default suite runs the local scripts. make e2e runs the remote scripts.

Running the commands

make install puts mapi into the workspace environment. You can activate the environment (source .venv/bin/activate). Alternatively, you can put uv run before each command (uv run mapi --help).

docs.title: Without a server
docs.text:
Scaffold a spec from a template. --with-data also writes the sample data of the conformance fixture that matches. This option needs the mapi-conformance package. The workspace has this package.

mapi new tabular -o spec.yaml --with-data     # an XGBoost demand model plus its sample data
Template What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Hierarchical geo MMM (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend and seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02

Check the spec statically against the installed plugins and the schema of the data. --stages shows the schema after each pipeline step. If there are errors, the exit status is 1. Thus the command works in CI:

mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --stages

Fit in-process. The bundle goes to bundles/<name>/. It contains the zarr zip, sidecars, plots, metrics and the evaluation bundle of evaluate_then_refit. --side-table NAME=PATH supplies side tables:

mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip       # in-process: writes bundles/<name>/
ls bundles/tabular

mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/<name> --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip scores a local bundle with a ScoreRequest document.

Local means trusted

Local fit and score import and run the plugins in your own process (isolation NONE), exactly as a notebook does. Use them only with code and data that you trust. On the platform, the same work runs in a sandbox.

Inspect the catalog of installed plugins. Upgrade spec documents across apiVersions:

mapi catalog models
mapi --json catalog steps | jq -r '.steps[].id' | head -n 5
