mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check           # exit 0: already the current apiVersion

mapi plugin init NAME scaffolds a plugin package (model, entry point, contract-kit tests). mapi plugin test NAME runs its tests. See Write a plugin.

docs.title: With a server
docs.text: First, start the stack (make dev, then make seed). See the quickstart.

docs.title: Select the API
docs.text:
Each remote command finds the API in the same way as the Python client. The first match in this list wins:

  1. --url and --token. These are global options. Put them before the command: mapi --url http://… runs ls.
  2. MAPI_URL, MAPI_TOKEN and MAPI_PROFILE. If MAPI_URL is not set, the CLI uses MAPI_API_URL, the name that make dev uses.
  3. The selected profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml. If $MAPI_CONFIG or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml is set, the CLI uses that file.
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.
# ~/.config/mapi/config.toml
profile = "local"

[profiles.local]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

[profiles.other-ports]
url = "http://127.0.0.1:18000"
timeout = 60

mapi config show shows the resolved URL, profile, project and credentials. It also shows the source of each value. It never shows a token. An API token shows as mapi_<prefix>_…. A sign-in shows as the person who signed in and the time when the sign-in ends. mapi config path shows the location of the file.

mapi config set KEY VALUE and mapi config unset KEY change the selected profile. The selected profile is --profile. If you do not give it, it is MAPI_PROFILE, and then the default of the file. These commands write the file again with mode 0600. They do not keep comments. You cannot set secrets in this way. Use mapi login --with-token.

--remote @ on check, fit, score and catalog means "the configured API". --remote URL overrides it for one command.

Tokens

v0.2 is single-tenant and has no authentication. The API listens only on 127.0.0.1. When MAPI_TOKEN is set, the client sends it as a bearer token. The client refuses to send it over plain HTTP to an address that is not a loopback address.

docs.title: Sign in and choose a project v0.3
docs.text:
A multi-tenant API (v0.3) needs credentials and a project (Tenancy and authentication).

mapi --profile prod --url https://api.mapi.example login \
    --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id 1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
mapi --profile prod login --device              # no browser here: enter a code elsewhere
mapi --profile ci login --with-token < ci.token # an API token, read from stdin
mapi whoami                                     # who, how, and your projects and roles
  • mapi login opens the identity provider in your browser. It uses OpenID Connect and the authorization code with PKCE. The provider redirects to a one-time listener on 127.0.0.1.
    • --device signs in with a code that you type on a different device.
    • --no-browser only shows the address.
    • The CLI saves --issuer, --client-id and --discovery-url in the profile. Thus later logins do not need them.
    • Against a local MAPI_PROFILE=dev stack, use mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp. Then select an account on the page that opens.
    • The CLI keeps the sign-in in credentials.json next to the config file (mode 0600). It renews the sign-in automatically with its refresh token. It sends the sign-in only to the API that it was made for.
  • mapi login --with-token reads an API token from stdin and checks its checksum. Thus it finds an incorrect character before it sends a request. Then it verifies the token with GET /v1/me and saves it in the profile. It writes the config file again with mode 0600. An API token in the profile or in MAPI_TOKEN has priority over a browser sign-in.
  • mapi whoami shows who you are and how you signed in. It also shows each project where you can act, with your role there.
  • mapi logout removes the sign-in and revokes its refresh token at the identity provider. It also removes the token of the profile. --revoke also revokes that token on the server.

Each v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) is now in a project. mapi use checks that you are a member. Then it saves the selection in the profile. The CLI sends the project as X-Mapi-Project, but only on project-scoped requests. --project overrides it for one command. MAPI_PROJECT overrides it for one shell. An API token acts only in its own project.

mapi use acme/growth                            # sent as X-Mapi-Project from now on
mapi --project acme/retail runs ls              # another project, for one command
mapi use                                        # show the selection and where it came from

docs.title: Tokens, usage and cost v0.3
docs.text:
mapi tokens create budget-planner -s score:geo-mmm-prod -s models:read \
    --expires-in-days 30 --rate-limit 120 > planner.token   # the secret, once, on stdout
mapi tokens ls
mapi tokens revoke tok_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0      # asks first; --yes for scripts
mapi usage --group-by resource_class            # this month: cost, compute, quota headroom
mapi usage --tenant acme --period day           # the whole tenant today (tenant admins)
mapi runs get run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0    # includes the run's metered cost

mapi tokens create shows the secret of the new token one time, alone on stdout. Thus, if you redirect stdout to a file, the file contains exactly the token. --save stores the token in the profile instead. No other command ever shows a token. Lists, whoami and config show use the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_….

mapi usage shows these data:

  • The exact cost of the period, in integer micro-units of the currency. A named price table gives the prices.
  • The vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds behind the cost.
  • How much of each quota is used, and when it resets.

mapi runs get and mapi runs ls show the cost of each run. While the cost is still an estimate, it has a ~.

When the API answers 429, the client does these actions:

  • For RATE_LIMITED, the client waits and then tries again. It waits for the Retry-After of the server, and then uses exponential back-off.
  • For QUOTA_EXCEEDED, the client stops immediately. It shows the reason and the time when the quota resets (retry after 1h 30m). With --json, it also gives retry_after_seconds.

docs.title: Operators v0.3
docs.text:
Platform operators use mapi admin to manage tenants, quotas, kill switches and executors. Each change shows a before-and-after table and asks for confirmation. For runbooks, --yes skips the confirmation. The server audits each change. Kill-switch changes need --reason.

mapi admin kill-switches set --untrusted-code off --reason "incident 2026-10-15"
mapi admin quotas set tenant acme --vcpu-seconds-per-day 172800 --concurrent-runs 40 \
    --storage 200GiB --note "beta customer"
mapi admin tenants update acme --status suspended --reason "payment overdue"
mapi admin executors ls
mapi admin executors disable cloudrun-jobs --reason "incident 2026-10-15: contain"
mapi admin audit --tenant acme --action token.create --since 2026-10-01

mapi admin quotas set replaces the full policy of a subject. It removes the limits that you do not give. The tier defaults and the other levels still apply.

docs.title: Upload data
docs.text:
mapi datasets upload does these steps:

  1. If the dataset does not exist, it creates the dataset.
  2. It sends the file to the signed URL that the API returns.
  3. It starts the sandboxed ingest run.
  4. It waits until the version is ready.

CSV and Parquet files need --mapping mapping.yaml. This file is an IngestMapping that gives the column of each dim and variable:

python scripts/seed.py --export demo/      # the E33 tables, score payloads and spec
mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future
mapi datasets ls

docs.title: Fit and follow
docs.text:
mapi fit SPEC --remote @ creates the spec. If the text changed, it adds a revision. Then it submits a fit run and follows its event stream until the run ends. It shows warnings, diagnostics and metrics when they arrive. With --no-wait, the command returns after it submits the run. mapi runs watch RUN follows a run at a later time.

mapi check demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @   # the server's static validation
mapi fit demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml --remote @     # create or revise the spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --kind fit --limit 3

mapi runs cancel RUN asks for cancellation. mapi runs retry RUN --resource-class L starts a new run from a run that failed.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
cat > forecast.yaml <<'EOF'
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: time, periods: 8}
data: dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest
side_tables: {fx: dataset://default/fx_daily@latest}
output: {kind: expected, summary: [mean, hdi_90]}
EOF
# the CLI has no `models` command yet: take the model id and version from the API
# (with the same credentials as the CLI when MAPI_TOKEN is set)
AUTH=(-H "X-Mapi-Project: ${MAPI_PROJECT:-default/default}")
[ -z "${MAPI_TOKEN:-}" ] || AUTH+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN")
MODEL=$(curl -s "${AUTH[@]}" "${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}/v1/models" \
  | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
mapi score forecast.yaml --remote @ --model "$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")" \
  --version "$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")" -o forecast.zarr.zip

mapi score --remote @ sends Prefer: wait=60. To change the time, use --wait. If the run takes longer, the command follows the run. It shows the outputs with their sizes and CRC32C. With -o, it downloads the result tree and checks it against that CRC32C.

docs.title: Endpoints, webhooks and sharing v0.4
docs.text:
mapi endpoints promote geo-mmm-prod model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3   # asks first; --yes skips
mapi endpoints ls
mapi endpoints schema geo-mmm-prod --example > call.json           # a valid score call
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod call.json -o result.zarr.zip
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --mode forecast --periods 8 --draws 100
mapi endpoints score geo-mmm-prod --data plan.nc                   # inline XrJSON (≤ 5 MB)
mapi endpoints snippets geo-mmm-prod -l python > score.py
mapi endpoints rollback geo-mmm-prod --reason "v3 over-forecasts"

promote goes through the promotion gate. A scorecard with warnings needs --override --reason TEXT from a signed-in project admin. The gate blocks a scorecard that fails. Promotions and rollbacks change what each integration that calls the alias receives. Thus both commands show the current version and ask before they act.

score sends a JSON EndpointScoreCall. The call comes from a file, from stdin (-) or from --example. Flags set these values:

  • The mode and the horizon.
  • --data/--scenario: a dataset:// reference, an XrJSON .json, a .zarr.zip or a netCDF file. The command sends the file inline.
  • --draws.

score waits in the same way as mapi score --remote. -o downloads the result tree. With one --language, snippets shows only the code.

mapi endpoints schema ts-forecast                           # the Input table's columns
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv               # actuals + blank-target future rows
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast --actuals new.csv --periods 6
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast --actuals new.csv --future 1961-04-01 --future 1961-05-01
mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv --dry-run     # print the call, send nothing

forecast sends actuals and the dates to forecast without a new fit. The CSV has a header row with the columns of the input table of the endpoint: the time column, the target and the drivers. schema lists them.

  • Rows with a target value are actuals.
  • Rows after the actuals with an empty target are the forecast.
  • If there are no such rows, the command adds --periods (default 8) after the last actual.
  • The command carries empty drivers on future rows forward (--future-covariates).

The command shows the data that the forecast used ("Forecast updated with 3 actuals …") and the summary table. score also shows them.

mapi webhooks create https://hooks.example.com/mapi -e endpoint.promoted -e run.failed > hook.secret
mapi webhooks ls
mapi webhooks deliveries WEBHOOK_ID --status failed
mapi webhooks replay WEBHOOK_ID DELIVERY_ID
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID --enable           # back on after --inactive or an auto-disable
mapi webhooks update WEBHOOK_ID -e run.failed --description "on-call"
mapi webhooks rotate WEBHOOK_ID > hook.secret      # asks first; the old secret signs for 24 h
mapi webhooks rm WEBHOOK_ID                        # asks first

create and rotate show the signing secret of a webhook one time, alone on stdout, as for tokens. Lists show whsec_…<last 4>. update changes the events, --url or --description. -e replaces the full list of events. --enable/--disable turns deliveries on or off.

A webhook that you created with --inactive goes back on with --enable. This also applies to a webhook that the platform disabled automatically after many failures. --enable also resets the failure count. Delivery responses are the text of the receiver. The CLI shows them with control sequences removed. Receiving webhooks tells how to verify deliveries.

mapi plots render --model MODEL_ID --version 3 --plot mmm.response_curves -f pdf -o curves.pdf
mapi plots render --saved PLOT_ID --width 1200
mapi plots embed PLOT_ID --expires-in-days 30 --allow-origin https://bi.example.com
mapi plots embeds PLOT_ID
mapi plots revoke PLOT_ID EMBED_ID                 # asks first

render draws the plot in the sandbox (vl-convert) and downloads the file. embed shows the link one time. The link contains its token (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Guided mode and business priors v0.4
docs.text:
mapi guided templates [geo_mmm]
mapi guided detect geo_mmm --csv media.csv          # or --dataset dataset://growth/media@v2
mapi guided draft geo_mmm --name eu-geo-mmm --dataset eu_media --csv media.csv --detect \
    -a spend=tv_spend,search_spend -a holdout_periods=8 --yaml-out spec.yaml
mapi priors preview --beliefs beliefs.yaml --spec SPEC_ID --revision 2 -o priors.json

detect and draft --csv profile the file locally. They find the types, counts, ranges and some sample values of each column. They send only those summaries, as the web app does.

  • --detect fills each answer that detection is sure of.
  • -a QUESTION=VALUE answers one question, or overrides the answer. Use a,b,c for lists and JSON for numbers.

A draft stores nothing. Examine spec.yaml. Then upload the data with the mapping (--mapping-out) and fit. priors preview changes ROI ranges or contribution-share ranges into model priors in a sandboxed run. It shows what the model then believes, for each channel (Guided modelling).

docs.title: Sign-up and your workspace v0.4
docs.text:
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example signup --email ana@acme.example --name "Ana Analyst" --accept-terms
mapi --url https://api.mapi.example verify-email mev_…   # the token from the e-mail link
mapi tenant status                                       # verification, any scheduled deletion
mapi tenant export -o acme-export.zip                    # GDPR export, waited for and downloaded
mapi tenant delete                                       # type the tenant id to confirm
mapi tenant delete --cancel                              # within the grace period

signup and verify-email send no credentials. tenant delete tells what the platform purges and what it keeps. Then it asks you to type the tenant id. Scripts give --confirm TENANT. The tenant is --tenant. If you do not give it, the tenant is the tenant of the selected project. If there is no selected project, it is your only tenant (Deleting and exporting data).

docs.title: Workflows, governance and explorers v0.5
docs.text:
Help me choose and About cards, in the terminal:

mapi choose                                   # questions, one at a time; Enter skips one
mapi choose -a goal=forecast -a data_shape=one_series -a drivers=yes -a experience=beginner
mapi about ts.sarimax                         # one item's About card
mapi about ts.sarimax --expert                # ... with the maths and references

Workflows: start from the gallery and check the file on the server. Then save it, run it and watch each node live. If the run fails, --watch exits with status 1. Thus it works in CI:

mapi workflows templates                      # the gallery, in plain words
mapi workflows init ts_readiness_arimax --name weekly-readiness   # writes weekly-readiness.yaml
mapi workflows validate weekly-readiness.yaml # checked by the server: pointers to every problem
mapi workflows apply weekly-readiness.yaml -m "first version"     # create, or save a revision
mapi workflows run weekly-readiness \
  --input data=dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  --param 'drivers=["price"]' --param window=104 \
  --watch                                     # live node status; exit 1 if the run fails

validate and apply show the sequence in which the nodes will run. This output is from a local stack, with the document of the cookbook:

weekly-readiness.yaml: valid (23 nodes)
order: adf → kpss → pp → za → seas → folds → holdout → wanders → seasonal → naive → order → sdiff → backtest → fit → diff → compare → dm → acf → select → governance → report → trusted → pack

The cookbook shows the live board of --watch and the summary at its end. Then examine a run, one node at a time:

RUN=$(mapi --json workflows runs weekly-readiness -n 1 | jq -r '.[0].run_id')
mapi workflows status "$RUN"                  # nodes, what each found, decisions, outputs
mapi workflows node "$RUN" order              # one node: parameters, result, outputs
mapi workflows output "$RUN" diff data --out diff.zarr.zip   # a derived dataset, verified

 node        order
 uses        search.arma_order@1.0.0
 status      succeeded
 attempt     1
 child runs  run_01m53hawz719exdgb6kcw5ysp3
 params      {"d": 1, "exog": ["price"], "max_p": 3, "max_q": 3, "trend": "c", "criterion": "aic"}
 result      {"best_p": 1, "best_q": 1, "best_order": [1, 1, 1], "criterion": "aic",
              "best_score": 430.4823790539326, "n_failed": 0, "suggested_p": 0, "suggested_q": 0}
 outputs     table: table

This is the output of mapi workflows node "$RUN" order. Here, we folded the JSON onto fewer lines. The differencing decision gave d = 1 to the search, and the run gave the price driver. The search selected ARIMA(1, 1, 1) by AIC.

mapi workflows schedules add weekly-readiness "0 6 * * 1" --tz Europe/Berlin \
  --input data=dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest
mapi workflows triggers add weekly-readiness dataset://growth/weekly_sales --debounce 600
mapi workflows schedules ls weekly-readiness

-i name=ref binds a workflow input. When the run starts, the platform pins @latest to a version. -p name=value sets a parameter. If the value parses as JSON, the CLI sends it as JSON (-p 'horizons=[1,4,13]'). The workflow cookbook has complete documents that you can start from.

Governance: the check catalog, policies, validations and approval by a second person. mapi validate model waits for the checks. It shows each result in plain words with the suggested action. mapi approve needs a signed-in reviewer who did not submit the model:

mapi governance checks                        # what a policy can require
mapi governance checks --about null.permutation_target --expert
mapi governance policies ls                   # in force here: tenant-wide first
mapi governance policies create forecast-policy.yaml
mapi validate model model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1   # runs the checks, waits
mapi validations ls --queue                   # reviewers: what waits for a decision
mapi approve "$VALIDATION" --comment "Null tests convincing; beats naive by 25%"
mapi validations pack "$VALIDATION" --out evidence.html          # for the auditor

Explorers and budget plans:

mapi explore dataset dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  -s overview -s stationarity -s ccf -s stl --kpi sales --out views/
mapi explore dataset weekly_sales --show stationarity            # one view as JSON
mapi explore model model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1 -s params -s residuals
mapi explore compare model://growth/arimax@v3 model://growth/ets@v1 --horizon 4

mapi optimize model://growth/geo-mmm@v7 --change-pct 0 \
  --channel 'tv={"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}' \
  --objective p10 --frontier 8

These are the forms of a model reference: model://project/name@vN, name@vN, name with -v N, or a model id. Dataset references have the same forms with dataset://. All commands accept --json.

docs.title: Use --json in scripts
docs.text:
--json is a global option. It shows one JSON document on stdout instead of tables. runs watch --json and workflows watch --json show one JSON event on each line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1. Usage errors exit with status 2.

RUN=$(mapi --json runs ls --kind score --limit 1 | jq -r '.[0].id')
mapi --json runs get "$RUN" | jq '{state, attempt, kind}'
mapi runs logs "$RUN" | tail -n 5

The CLI removes ANSI and control sequences from text that came from the server, a plugin or a run log. Thus a hostile log line cannot write over your terminal.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev. It does the database migrations. Then it runs the API and the orchestrator in one process. It uses an embedded PostgreSQL, unless DATABASE_URL is set. It uses an in-process GCS shim, unless a shim already listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT. This is the smallest way to get an API for the CLI or the client. If you also want the web app, use make dev (Local deployment).

docs.title: Conformance corpus
docs.text:
The corpus is how the platform defines "supported". It is a set of small, realistic modelling problems. These problems are ports of pymc-challenges and of the examples of the plan. They must continue to work, from start to end, after each change. Each fixture goes through exactly the same process as the model of a user:

  1. validate: The runner checks the spec statically against the step, model and plot catalogs. The API does the same before it accepts a run.
  2. fit: The runner does a fit run on the in-process executor. It obeys fit.mode (also evaluate_then_refit).
  3. score: The runner does each request in score_requests.yaml as a score run. For requests that must fail, it checks the typed error code (for example HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT or UNSEEN_LEVELS).
  4. evaluate: The runner scores the holdout through the score path. The metrics must be equal to the metrics that the fit calculated.
  5. contract: The runner does the full check_model contract kit.
  6. plots: The runner renders the outputs.plots of the spec from real outputs.
  7. expectations: The runner does the own checks of the fixture (for example, recovered effects or the terminal state).

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
python -m mapi_conformance list
python -m mapi_conformance run                         # every fixture at size tiny
python -m mapi_conformance run --fixture e24 --fixture c08
python -m mapi_conformance run --size full --json corpus.json
make conformance                                       # the same as `run` at size tiny
make conformance FIXTURE=e33                           # one fixture
make conformance-full                                  # every fixture at size full
python -m mapi_conformance list --deferred             # plus the plan fixtures not ported yet

The runner shows one row for each fixture. If a step failed, the exit status is not zero:

fixture           model                           validate  fit  score   evaluate  contract  plots   expectations  ...  result
----------------  ------------------------------  --------  ---  ------  --------  --------  ------  ------------       ------
e02               tabular.hierarchical_glm@1.0.0  ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
c08               ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0             ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 13/13  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e24               ts.gaussian_hmm@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 15/15  ok 2/2  ok                 PASS
xgb_store_demand  tabular.regressor@1.0.0         ok        ok   ok 6/6  ok        ok 16/16  ok 3/3  ok                 PASS
e33               mmm.bayesian@1.0.0              ok        ok   ok 5/5  ok        ok 17/17  ok 4/4  ok                 PASS
mmm_frequentist   mmm.frequentist@1.0.0           ok        ok   ok 4/4  ok        ok 18/18  ok 1/1  ok                 PASS

--size tiny is the default, and pytest -m conformance uses it. It keeps the data small and the MCMC short. --size full uses the own fit settings of the spec and larger data.

docs.title: Through a stack that runs
docs.text:
The default runner does not use the control plane. --stack sends the same fixtures through the API of a stack that runs (make dev), as a user does: spec → ingest → fit → score.

  1. The runner uploads the data, the side tables and the score payloads as dataset versions. It uses a signed PUT, and then a sandboxed ingest run.
  2. The spec points at the uploads. The platform validates it, creates it and fits it through the dispatcher, the runner and FINALIZING.
  3. Each score request runs against the registered model. An expected typed error can come from the failed run. It can also come from the API, if the API refuses the request at the start.
  4. The runner checks the holdout metrics and the stored plots on the model version.
  5. The runner downloads the bundle through signed URLs and verifies each hash. Then the bundle goes through the check_fit of the fixture.
python -m mapi_conformance run --stack http://127.0.0.1:8000 --fixture e33 --fixture xgb_store_demand
uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_corpus_stack.py   # E33, xgboost and sklearn (`make e2e`)

The contract kit does not run in this mode. It needs the plugin in-process.

docs.title: The fixtures
docs.text: Fixture Model Exercises e02 tabular.hierarchical_glm Long layout, shuffled county labels, new counties from the hyperprior, LOO, CRN counterfactual c08 ts.hsgp_trend Sentinel codes, max_extension from anticipated coords, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, contiguity e24 ts.gaussian_hmm Padded data with a mask, terminal state, forecast and filter, relabelling, LOO that is not valid xgb_store_demand tabular.regressor Pooled new stores, refused quantile aggregation, covariates that must have future values sklearn_store_demand sklearn.tabular_conformal The same panel with plain scikit-learn (histogram boosting, skops): split-conformal intervals, refused interval aggregation, pooled new stores e33 mmm.bayesian FX (supplied) and holiday (pinned) side tables. Split after resample. mmm-framework owns scaling and carry-over (history added before the data at score time). New market from the hyperprior. Weekly EUR plan through inputs_stage. CRN counterfactual (intervention and baseline-vs-scenario). Derived quantities in EUR. mmm_frequentist mmm.frequentist The ridge estimator of mmm-framework with bootstrap draws. A model that owns scaling, carry-over and units. A score window is equal to the same weeks of the full series. e84_lite choice.multinomial_logit A ragged household × trip panel with a text target. last_per_group split. Products off the shelf. New households from the fitted spread. A price-rise counterfactual. Next trips. Categorical holdout metrics (hit rate against the naive guess, log score, Brier). guided_mmm mmm.bayesian The draft of the geo_mmm Guided template with business priors (ROI, contribution share, baseline share). The fit translates the priors, and a lift test is in the likelihood. Both agree with the simulation. ROI, baseline share and lift are checked against the truth. A forecast and the channel-off preset.

docs.title: Deferred
docs.text:
The corpus of the plan also lists fixtures that need plugins or run kinds that do not exist yet. mapi_conformance.fixtures.DEFERRED lists them with the reason. A test makes sure that the list of the plan, the fixtures and the deferrals agree:

Plan fixture Waits for E13 state-space A state-space plugin with the filter mode (vetted plugins, M4) E82-slim GP Bayesian optimisation The recommend mode and Campaign runs (M6) E45 A plugin for its model (vetted plugins, M4)

docs.title: Time to port
docs.text:
The M0 exit criteria ask for the time to port each fixture. The target is less than one day for each fixture, for the model plugin and the fixture. This time is a measure of human effort. Thus you cannot get it from the code or from commit timestamps. Record it here when you port a fixture, or port it again.

Fixture Time to port Recorded e02 not measured yet – c08 not measured yet – e24 not measured yet – xgb_store_demand not measured yet – sklearn_store_demand not measured yet – e33 not measured yet – mmm_frequentist not measured yet –

docs.title: Add a fixture
docs.text:
1. Create a package conformance/src/mapi_conformance/fixtures/<id>/.
  2. Put <id> in the list in fixtures/__init__.py.
  3. Add the files below to the package.

data.py makes the data:

def generate(seed: int = 0, size: str = "tiny") -> tuple[xr.Dataset, dict[str, xr.Dataset]]:
    """The dataset and its side tables (name -> dataset)."""

def schema() -> DataSchema:            # optional: the raw schema (else inferred)
    ...

def payload_new_store(data, seed, size) -> xr.Dataset:   # optional payload builders
    ...

spec.yaml is a usual ModelSpec with the fit settings of a full run.

score_requests.yaml lists the requests to score. The runner fills in apiVersion, kind and model for you:

- name: forecast_with_new_store
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}}
  payload: new_store          # none | fit_data | "tail:<n>" | a payload_<name> builder
  drop_targets: true          # remove target variables from the payload (default)
  side_tables: true           # pass the fixture's side tables to the run (default)
  expect: {vars: [y_hat], sizes: {week: 4}, issues: [UNSEEN_LEVELS], groups: [summary]}
- name: quantiles_are_not_summed
  request: {mode: forecast, horizon: {dim: time, periods: 4}, output: {aggregate: {over: [store_id]}}}
  payload: new_store
  expect_error: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED

expectations.py (optional) adds checks for the fixture. To make a check fail, raise AssertionError:

TINY_FIT = {"tune": 150, "draws": 100, "chains": 2}       # fit overrides at size tiny
TINY_SETTINGS = {"m": 20}                                  # model-settings overrides
MODEL_CHECKS = None                                        # or a subset of check_model checks

def check_fit(bundle, data): ...
def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data): ...
def check_evaluate(tree, bundle, data): ...

A hook that declares a keyword ctx parameter also receives a FixtureContext. The context holds the seed, the size, the registry, the side tables and results. results holds the trees of the score requests that succeeded before this one. Use it to compare requests. E33 does this. It checks that a weekly EUR plan forecasts exactly the same as the raw daily path:

def check_score(name, tree, bundle, data, *, ctx):
    if name == "weekly_eur_plan" and "forecast_8w" in ctx.results:
        ...

A side table can have score_policy: supplied. Then each score request that replays its step must name the side table (request.side_tables). The runner supplies the data with that name.

From Python, mapi_conformance.run_fixture("e24") returns a FixtureReport. run_corpus() returns a CorpusReport with .table() and .to_json().

docs.title: Deleting data and exporting it v0.4
docs.text: A tenant admin can export all the data that the workspace stored (GDPR access). The tenant admin can also delete the full workspace (GDPR erasure). Both actions need a signed-in session of a tenant admin. API tokens never administer a tenant. The HTTP API reference gives the HTTP operations. The configuration reference gives the settings.

docs.title: Export first
docs.text:
# queue the export (everything by default: metadata, datasets, models, audit, usage)
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
# poll it; once "ready", download_url is a signed link valid for 15 minutes
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports/exp_01jaf3r1s2t3v4w5x6y7z8a9b0"
# every export of the workspace, newest first (any admin, any browser)
curl -s -b cookies "$API/v1/tenants/acme/exports"

Settings > Data shows the newest export from that list. Thus a different admin (or a different browser) sees an export that the platform still makes. That admin can also download a finished export. The Python client has client.tenants.exports("acme").

The orchestrator makes the archive in the background, usually in less than a minute. The archive is a zip:

Path Content README.txt, manifest.json What is in the archive, with the size and SHA-256 of each file metadata/<table>.jsonl Each record of the workspace, with one JSON object on each line. Examples are projects, members, API tokens, datasets and versions (schemas, profiles), specs and revisions (YAML), runs, models and versions, plots, endpoints and webhooks. The maximum total is MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES (256 MiB). If the export stops a table early, skipped lists the table with the rows that it wrote. datasets/<dataset>/v<n>/... The stored dataset objects, byte for byte. The maximum total is MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES (256 MiB). manifest.json lists the remaining objects under skipped, with sizes and checksums. models/<model>/v<n>/manifest.json, model_version.json The signed bundle manifest, lineage, diagnostics, scorecard and metrics of each model version audit/audit_events.jsonl, usage/cost_ledger.jsonl The audit log and the metered usage of the workspace

The platform never exports credentials. Token hashes, signing keys, nonces and webhook secrets show as [redacted]. The platform reads the records through the own row-level-security session of the workspace. Thus an archive can contain only the rows of its own workspace.

One export runs at a time. The maximum is MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY (3) each day. More exports get 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The platform deletes an archive after MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S (7 days). A suspended workspace can still export. This includes a workspace with a scheduled deletion.

docs.title: Request the deletion
docs.text:
curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"confirm": "acme", "reason": "closing the account"}'

confirm must contain the tenant id again. A deployment can also make a recent sign-in necessary (MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S). Older sessions get 401 and must sign in again. You cannot delete the own tenant of the platform.

The platform schedules the deletion for the end of a grace period (MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S, 7 days). These things occur immediately:

  • The platform suspends the workspace. You can still read all its data. You cannot create or run new items, and nothing spends compute.
  • The platform cancels the unfinished runs of the workspace.

Until the grace period ends, the admin can still export. The admin can also cancel the deletion:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X DELETE "$API/v1/tenants/acme/deletion"

When you cancel, the workspace gets back the status that it had before. This is not the case if an operator changed the status after the request. The audit log records tenant.deletion_request and tenant.deletion_cancel.

docs.title: What happens when the grace period ends
docs.text:
The deletion becomes deleting. You cannot undo this. The platform does these steps:

  1. The status of the tenant becomes deleting. The platform refuses each request for the tenant, from its members and from its tokens. Operators can still read the progress of the deletion.
  2. The platform revokes the API tokens of the tenant. It ends the browser sessions of persons who belong to no other workspace. Components that give links (webhooks, embed links) revoke their links.
  3. The platform cancels the unfinished runs again. The purge waits for them to stop, for a maximum of MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S (one hour). After that time, a run that has not stopped can possibly continue to upload results under the prefix of the workspace. It can do this while its signed upload links are valid (its timeout plus 30 minutes). Thus the purge then waits for those links to expire before it deletes anything. The detail of the queue store shows the time until which it waits.
  4. The platform cancels exports that are in the queue or that it still makes (state failed). The purge waits for a build in progress to end. The maximum wait is the MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S lease of the build. A cancelled build never uploads its archive. If an archive arrived after the purge listed the objects, the build deletes it.

Then the purge goes from store to store. GET /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion shows the progress of each store:

Store What is purged queue Background jobs of the runs of the tenant, and their bootstrap objects database Each record of the workspace in each table, children before parents. The platform also deletes persons who belonged only to this workspace. object_store Each object under t/<tenant>/ in the quarantine, runs, bundles and data buckets: uploads, run scratch, model bundles, dataset versions and export archives logs Not purged (see below) webhooks The platform sends the tenant.deletion.completed webhook to the endpoints that were registered before the purge.

When all stores are complete, the deletion is purged. The audit log gets the tombstone event tenant.purged. This event contains the tenant id, but no content.

docs.title: What is kept, and why
docs.text: Record Kept Audit log 1 year after deletion, pseudonymised: actor ids and keyed digests of client addresses, no content Cost ledger 7 years for tax law: amounts and run ids, no content The own record of the deletion Its ids, dates and counts for each store The tenant id A tombstone row (status deleting, no name), so that nobody can use the id again Sign-up records Only the keyed digests that the platform uses against repeated abuse. The platform erases the e-mail, name and organisation. Platform logs Not purged: see below

docs.title: Retention locks
docs.text: Model bundles are in a bucket with a retention policy (Terraform bundle_retention_days, 30 days, locked in production). Nobody can delete an object that is younger than that. The purge records each such object with the time when it can be deleted (time_created plus MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS). It shows object_store as running, with a plain explanation. When the retention expires, the purge continues automatically. All the other data is already gone, and nobody can get access to the workspace.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
You cannot delete Cloud Logging entries one at a time. Thus a deletion does not purge logs. The platform keeps tenant content out of the logs. Structured log lines contain tenant, project, run and request ids, and keyed digests of client addresses. They never contain request bodies, data or tracebacks of tenant code.

The logs expire with the retention of their bucket. Terraform sets the _Default log bucket of the control project to log_retention_days (30 days by default, infra/terraform/modules/control/logging.tf). The run-event sink only sends events to Pub/Sub and stores nothing. Thus 30 days after a deletion, its logs are also gone.

docs.title: When a store fails
docs.text:
If a store fails, the deletion becomes failed. The orchestrator tries it again with back-off. The back-off starts at 5 minutes and doubles each time, up to 6 hours. The maximum is MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS (8) attempts. After that, an operator examines last_error in the logs and starts the deletion again:

curl -s -b cookies -H "X-CSRF-Token: $CSRF" -X POST \
  "$API/v1/admin/tenants/acme/deletion/retry"

The purge is idempotent. A new attempt starts where the last pass stopped.

docs.title: For operators
docs.text:
• The scheduler runs in the orchestrator (mapi-server worker) each MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S. Purges and exports run as procrastinate jobs on the lifecycle queue, one at a time for each deletion or export. If a worker stops unexpectedly, the platform puts the job in the queue again.
  • An export build can take MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S (one hour). After that, it fails. Possibly, an export is still running five minutes after that time. Then it belongs to a process that stopped unexpectedly (an OOM kill, a lost orchestrator). The scheduler makes the export one more time. If that build also stops, the scheduler fails the export. Thus a workspace can always ask for a new export.
  • The orchestrator makes the archive in memory. Give the orchestrator memory for MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES plus MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES.
  • Where the request-path role can delete database rows, the platform deletes them through the own row-level-security session of the tenant. Thus a purge cannot touch the rows of a different tenant.
  • Components that own credentials or links of a tenant register a mapi_server.services.trust.TenantRevoker. The webhooks component gives the DeletionNotifier that sends tenant.deletion.completed.

docs.title: Explore a dataset v0.5
docs.text:
The Data Explorer answers the questions to ask before you fit a model. It answers these questions:

  • What is in the data, and how does it move over time?
  • Where are values missing or unusual?
  • Which drivers move with the result, and with how much delay?
  • Do series wander, or do they return to a level?
  • How strong is the season?
  • Which drivers overlap?
  • What must you correct first?

The sandbox calculates each view. The control plane never reads your data. Each view comes with Vega-Lite plots and captions in plain language. The web app shows all views. The other parts of this guide use the HTTP API, which the web app calls.

docs.title: In the web app
docs.text:
1. Open a dataset.
  2. Click Explore this version. Alternatively, go to /datasets/<dataset>/versions/<n>/explore.

The page starts with the About of the dataset. It lists the thirteen sections in three groups:

  • The basics: overview, data quality, distributions, over time, missing values and unusual values.
  • Relationships: correlations, leads and lags, overlapping drivers and group comparison.
  • Time patterns: memory (ACF/PACF), stable or wandering, and trend and season.

A tick marks a section that is ready. An empty circle marks a section that the platform calculates when you ask for it. A dash marks a section that does not apply to this data. The dash shows the reason.

  • Guided mode shows the plain summary of each section first ("4 series return to a stable level, 3 series wander (model their changes)…"). To see the numbers, click Show the statistics. Run the deeper checks calculates all the sections that the ingest did not calculate. It uses sensible defaults (the target of the dataset as the KPI).
  • Expert mode shows all statistics: test statistics and p-values, quantiles, VIFs and the condition number, and the significant lags. It also shows All series: the plots of the platform that are ready for export (ui/explore/plots/<section>.json). Explore with options sets the request of the run. The request contains the sections, the KPI and the dimensions that split the series. It also contains the lags, the season length, α, the correlation and outlier methods, and prewhitening.
  • Pickers select the variable or series that a plot shows. Examples are one line for each market, the STL decomposition of a series, or the cross-correlation of a driver with the KPI. The plots render in the isolated plot sandbox, as all plots do.
  • A section that is not calculated yet has a Compute it now button. This button starts an explore run for this section and for the other missing sections. The id of the run goes in the address (?run=). Thus you can share or reload the page. If you ask again with the same options, the platform answers immediately from the cached run.

docs.title: From Python and the command line
docs.text:
ds = api.datasets.find("weekly_sales")
assert ds is not None and ds.latest_version is not None
api.datasets.describe(ds.id, "Weekly sales and price by region, from the finance warehouse")
print(api.datasets.about(ds.id).summary_generated)  # "Weekly data from ... for 5 regions ..."

explored = api.datasets.explore(  # computed in the sandbox; the same request is cached
    ds.id,
    ds.latest_version,
    sections=["overview", "stationarity", "ccf", "stl", "quality"],
    kpi="sales",
    max_lag=12,
)
for section in explored.index.sections if explored.index else []:
    print(section.section, section.status, section.message_plain or "")
stationarity = api.explorations.view(explored, "stationarity")  # the view, as JSON

mapi explore dataset dataset://growth/weekly_sales@latest \
  -s overview -s stationarity -s ccf -s stl --kpi sales --out views/
mapi explore dataset weekly_sales --show quality      # one view as JSON

docs.title: Views written at ingest
docs.text:
Each ingest writes the quick sections next to the dataset: overview, distributions, timeseries, missingness, outliers, correlation and quality. Get the index, and then any view, through the artifact route:

api "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/artifacts/ui/explore/index.json"
api "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/artifacts/ui/explore/quality.json"

Each answer is a signed link (ArtifactLink) to the JSON view. The index lists each section with its status:

  • ok.
  • skipped, with the reason in plain words. An example is "the data has no time dimension".
  • error.

The plots for a section are at ui/explore/plots/<section>.json. This file is a list of PlotSpecs to render in the plot sandbox.

docs.title: Everything else, on demand
docs.text:
The heavier sections run as an explore run. These sections are stl, stationarity, ccf, acf_pacf, vif and groups. All sections with other options also run as an explore run:

api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/versions/1/explore" -d '{
  "sections": ["stationarity", "stl", "ccf", "vif"],
  "kpi": "revenue",
  "facet_by": ["geo"],
  "max_lag": 12,
  "prewhiten": true
}'

The answer (202) is an Exploration with the run. Poll GET /v1/explorations/{run_id}. When the state is done, it holds the index and a signed link for each view. If you ask again with the same request, the platform answers 200 from the last run. Thus, after the platform calculates the explorers one time, they are instant.

Option Default Meaning sections all 13 The sections to calculate vars each numeric variable The variables to include kpi the target variable The result that the cross-correlations use time_dim the time dim of the schema The dimension that "over time" means facet_by none (each series) A maximum of two dims that split the series. For spend, media and the target, the platform adds the other dims. For all other variables, it calculates the average. group_by the first categorical dim The dim that groups compares max_lag 26 The lags for ACF/PACF and cross-correlations period from the frequency (52 weekly, 12 monthly, 7 daily) The season length for STL alpha 0.05 The significance level of the tests correlation pearson Or spearman outliers, outlier_threshold mad, 3.5 The robust score (mad, iqr or zscore, all on a standard-normal scale) and its threshold prewhiten true Filter the two series with the own AR model of the driver before the cross-correlation. To see the raw correlations, turn it off. max_series 50 The number of series in each view. The platform counts the other series as omitted.

docs.title: The sections
docs.text:
Section What you see Read it like this overview Dims, variables, roles, the fraction of missing values, a summary and a quality score "104 weeks for 3 markets; 2 data problems to look at." distributions For each variable: histogram, mean, spread, skew, quantiles and fraction of zeros Heavy tails or many zeros can need a transform or a different likelihood. timeseries Each variable over time, in facets It is easier to see breaks, level shifts and gaps than to test for them. missingness A heatmap of the fraction of missing values by variable and period, and the longest gap You cannot impute long gaps reliably. outliers Values that are far from the typical value, with their coordinates Are they errors or real events? For real events, add a control variable. correlation The correlation matrix with p-values It is difficult to separate drivers that move almost together. ccf The correlation of each driver with the KPI at each lag. A positive lag means that the driver leads. A peak at lag 2 means that the effect shows two periods later. Prewhitening is on by default. The significance band uses the formula of Bartlett for two autocorrelated series. Thus the platform does not flag two smooth but unrelated series at half of their lags. acf_pacf Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation with the significance band, and suggested AR/MA orders Bars outside the dashed band are more than chance. stationarity ADF and KPSS for each series, with one verdict stable, difference (it wanders: model the changes), trend_stable or unclear (the tests do not agree: look at the plot). stl Trend, season and remainder, with their strengths (0 to 1) If the seasonal strength is more than about 0.6, model the season explicitly. vif The variance inflation for each driver, and the condition number Above 10, the model cannot identify the separate effect of the driver well. groups Each variable across markets or stores, with an ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test Very different groups can need a hierarchical model. quality Warnings in plain language, the most serious first. Each warning has a suggested action. Correct errors before you model. Look at the warnings.

The data.quality governance check also counts the quality warnings (see Validate models with governance policies).

docs.title: Dataset About
docs.text:
GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/about describes the latest version in plain words. It uses the schema and the coordinates of the version ("Weekly data from 2023-01-01 to 2024-12-29 (104 weeks) for 10 markets …"). The response also shows the own description of the owner. PATCH changes that description:

api -X PATCH "$API/v1/datasets/$DATASET_ID/about" \
  -d '{"description_user": "Weekly media spend and revenue from the finance warehouse."}'

In the web app, the dataset page and the Data Explorer show the two descriptions next to each other (About this dataset). Editors change the description on the page with Edit.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Views have limits. The maximums are 200 series in each view, 5,000 points in each series, 256 variables and 200 lags. The platform thins longer series evenly and flags them downsampled.
  • The statistical tests come from statsmodels and scipy. The test suite validates them against their reference outputs.
  • Strings in views come from your data. Render them only as text.

docs.title: Endpoints and webhooks v0.4
docs.text:
An endpoint gives a model version a stable name, endpoint://<project>/<alias>. Other applications call this name. You can promote a better version, or roll back a bad version, and the applications do not change. A webhook tells another application when an event occurs in a project. For example, a run finished, a model version is ready, or an endpoint changed.

This guide uses curl for endpoints and webhooks. Integrations gives the concepts: the promotion gate, signatures and the SSRF policy. The HTTP API reference lists all the operations.

In the examples, MAPI_TOKEN holds an API token and MAPI_PROJECT holds the <tenant>/<project> for the token. API holds the base URL:

export API=http://127.0.0.1:8000
api() { curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: $MAPI_PROJECT" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$@"; }

docs.title: Promote a model version
docs.text:
PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} makes the alias, or points the alias at a different version. Give the version by reference or by id:

api -X PUT "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod" \
  --data '{"model": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3", "expected_revision": 0}'

{
  "alias": "geo-mmm-prod",
  "ref": "endpoint://growth/geo-mmm-prod",
  "model_ref": "model://growth/eu-geo-mmm@v3",
  "revision": 1,
  "evaluation_policy": {"fit_mode": "evaluate_then_refit", "schema_change": "block"},
  "gate": {"outcome": "allowed", "scorecard_overall": "pass", "reasons": []},
  "overridden": false
}

expected_revision makes the call safe if a colleague promotes at the same time:

  • 0 means "the alias must be new".
  • N means "the alias must still be at revision N".
  • If the alias does not agree, the answer is 409 CONFLICT.

If you send the same body again, nothing changes.

The promotion gate decides if the version can serve:

The version Answer Its scorecard passes, the fit used evaluate_then_refit, and it takes the input that the callers of the endpoint send Promoted Its scorecard warns, or it has no scorecard. Or it had no score on a holdout (no data.split). Or a check that its guided template asks for did not run (NOT_EVALUATED) 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED, unless a project admin overrides Its scorecard fails, the fit stopped before it finished, or the fit used train_only 409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED It expects different input (for example, a removed dim or a new necessary variable) Blocked by default. The schema_change policy of the endpoint can change this to warn or allow

A less strict evaluation_policy on the endpoint stops the gate, as an override does. For example, schema_change from block to warn or allow, or fit_mode to train_only. Thus only a signed-in project admin can send a less strict policy. An endpoints:promote token gets 403 FORBIDDEN. The token can send the same policy or a stricter policy. The audit event of the promotion records the policy before and after.

Each refusal gives the reasons of the gate in the errors of the problem. Each reason has the scorecard check that caused it:

{
  "code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED",
  "status": 409,
  "errors": [
    {"code": "OVERRIDE_REQUIRED", "severity": "warning",
     "message": "Holdout error: The forecast error on the holdout periods was 14%.",
     "context": {"gate_code": "SCORECARD_WARN", "check": "holdout.mape"}}
  ]
}

Evaluated, then refitted. An endpoint serves versions with a fit that evaluated the holdout and then fitted again on all the data. This is fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit, the default of all specs. Thus forecasts start from the full history. The two steps occur in the same fit run. The lineage of the version links the evaluation. To serve an exploration fit, give the endpoint the policy {"fit_mode": "train_only"}.

docs.title: Overriding
docs.text:
An override is a human decision. A signed-in project admin sends override: true with a reason. The admin sends it from the web app or from a session. An API token cannot override, for all scopes:

{"model_version_id": "mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0", "override": true,
 "reason": "Holdout MAPE is high because of the strike in week 41; accepted by the CMO."}

The endpoint history and the audit log (endpoint.promote_override) keep the reason. The reason is next to the checks that warned.

docs.title: History and rollback
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/history"
api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/rollback" \
  --data '{"reason": "v4 over-forecasts after the price change"}'

A rollback points the alias at the version of an earlier revision. By default, this is the last revision that served a different version. to_revision selects a revision. A rollback is a new revision, and the audit log records it with its reason. The gate does not run again. DELETE /v1/endpoints/{alias} removes the alias and its history. The model versions stay.

docs.title: Score an endpoint
docs.text:
Ask the endpoint what it expects. The answer has the input schema from the time of the promotion. It also has an example body that is valid:

api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/schema" | jq .example

{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
 "future_covariates": "carry_last", "output": {"kind": "expected", "summary": ["mean", "hdi_90"]}}

Then score the endpoint. Prefer: wait=60 waits for a maximum of one minute:

  • If the run finished, the answer is 200 with links to the outputs.
  • If the run did not finish, the answer is 202 with the run.

A finished answer also has the numbers in summary. There is one table for each output. The table has the coordinate columns, then one column for each statistic. By default, the statistics are the mean and the 90% HDI. Thus a spreadsheet or a shell script does not need a zarr or Arrow reader. If a result has more than 100,000 cells, the server cuts it (truncated). score.zarr.zip always has all the data.

"summary": {"tables": [{"variable": "revenue",
                        "columns": ["geo", "time", "mean", "hdi_90_lower", "hdi_90_upper"],
                        "rows": [["de", "2026-01-05", 1520.4, 1402.1, 1633.9]]}],
            "truncated": false}

api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score" \
  -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H 'Idempotency-Key: plan-2026-11' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last"}'

To get a result that took more time, send the same call again with the same Idempotency-Key. The answer is for the run that the first call started. If you ask, the call waits again. This works with the smallest token, score:<alias>. This token can read and score one endpoint and nothing more.

docs.title: Inline data
docs.text:
data and scenario can be dataset:// references. They can also be small datasets that you send inline as XrJSON. XrJSON has the shape of xr.Dataset.to_dict(), with a maximum of 5 MB each. Thus scripts and spreadsheets do not need an upload.

A caller that cannot read datasets (a score:<alias> token) sends data inline. Or it gives the dataset that the model of the endpoint was fitted on. All other references get the same 403 FORBIDDEN. A reference to a dataset that does not exist also gets 403 FORBIDDEN. Thus such a token cannot score the other datasets of the project. It also cannot find which datasets exist:

{
  "mode": "predict",
  "data": {
    "coords": {
      "market": {"dims": ["market"], "data": ["de"]},
      "channel": {"dims": ["channel"], "data": ["search", "tv"]},
      "date": {"dims": ["date"], "data": ["2025-12-30"]}
    },
    "data_vars": {
      "spend_local": {"dims": ["market", "channel", "date"], "data": [[[1200.0], [5300.0]]]}
    }
  }
}

Before a run starts, the server checks the payload against the input contract of the endpoint:

  • Each variable must be a variable that the endpoint takes, with its dims.
  • Coordinates must be dims of the input.
  • A predict call must send all the inputs.

Then the server does the usual coordinate checks: modes, horizon, unseen levels and future covariates. For these checks, it reads only the coordinates of the payload. The sandboxed score run decodes the values. The API never decodes them. The score run gives each coordinate the type of the dim of the model. Dates arrive as ISO strings. Thus an inline payload gives the same score as the same rows in an uploaded dataset.

The input contract (GET …/schema → snapshot.input_schema) uses the dim and variable names that the spec uses after data.bind. For example, if the spec binds time: week and y: revenue, an inline payload sends a time dim, not week. The score run changes the payload names to the names of the dataset before it scores. The results use the names of the dataset, as for all scores. POST …/validate does the same checks and answers 200 with the issues. It does not run anything.

The server refuses bodies of more than 10.25 MB with 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE. For larger data, upload a dataset and give its reference.

docs.title: Forecasts with your latest actuals
docs.text:
A forecasting endpoint takes two things in one call, without a new fit (Forecasts with actuals):

  • The actuals that arrived after the fit.
  • The dates to forecast.

Send inline data along the time dim. Fill the target on the periods that you have. Leave the target empty (null) on the periods to forecast.

api -X POST "$API/v1/endpoints/ts-forecast/score" -H 'Prefer: wait=60' \
  --data '{"mode": "forecast", "horizon": {"dim": "t", "periods": 8},
           "future_covariates": "carry_last",
           "data": {"coords": {"t": {"dims": ["t"], "data": ["1961-01-01", "1961-02-01",
                                     "1961-03-01", "1961-04-01", "1961-05-01"]}},
                    "data_vars": {"y": {"dims": ["t"], "data": [417, 391, 419, null, null]}}}}'

This call updates the model with January to March. It forecasts April and May, the two empty rows. A warning tells you that the server did not use horizon.periods. If you send only the three actuals, the server forecasts the 8 periods after March. The summary.conditioning of the answer tells what occurred. It tells this in fields (conditioned, n_actuals, actuals_through, fit_end, horizon_source, details for each series) and in words (message).

GET …/schema gives the same table for spreadsheets and scripts:

  • input_table lists the columns: the time column first, then the target, the drivers and other inputs. The periods after the fit are empty rows.
  • snapshot.conditions_on_actuals tells if the model can use actuals.
  • actuals_example is a call over those periods that is ready for you to fill.

If a model cannot use actuals, it refuses target values in a forecast with 422 ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. It does not ignore them. For inline data, it refuses before a run starts. Actuals get 422 ACTUALS_INVALID if they have a gap that the model cannot filter. They also get it if they do not have the drivers that were observed with them.

In Python, api.endpoints.forecast("ts-forecast", rows) takes the same table as a DataFrame or a list of rows. You can also give actuals= and future= separately. result.conditioning.message tells what the forecast used. In a terminal, mapi endpoints forecast ts-forecast input.csv reads the table from a CSV file (The command line). In Google Sheets, the table is the Input sheet (Connect Google Sheets).

docs.title: Snippets
docs.text:
api "$API/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/snippets?language=python&language=curl"

This call gives code that is ready to run for these languages:

  • Python
  • TypeScript
  • curl
  • R
  • Google Sheets (Apps Script)
  • A notebook cell.

The code has the address of this server and the example payload of the endpoint. For a forecasting endpoint, it also has a call over the periods after the fit, for you to fill with actuals. It also has an Apps Script that reads the actuals from an Input sheet. base_url= puts a different address in the code, for example a public address behind a proxy. Snippets read the token from MAPI_TOKEN and never contain a secret.

In Python, Client().endpoint("geo-mmm-prod").score(ds) sends an xr.Dataset and returns an xr.Dataset (The Python client). The CLI has mapi endpoints score. To optimise a budget, use the model version (Optimise a budget).

docs.title: Tokens for integrations
docs.text:
Scope For score:geo-mmm-prod An application that scores this endpoint. It can also read the schema and snippets of the endpoint score:* All endpoints and models of the project endpoints:promote CI that promotes versions that pass and rolls back. It never overrides webhooks:manage A script that manages webhooks

Each call counts against the rate limit of the token (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After). Each score run counts against the vCPU-second budget of the token (429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED). These limits are in addition to the limits of the tenant.

docs.title: Subscribe
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks" \
  --data '{"url": "https://hooks.example.com/mapi",
           "events": ["run.succeeded", "run.failed", "endpoint.promoted"]}'

The answer holds the signing secret, whsec_…. You see it only one time. Keep the secret with the receiver. To manage webhooks, you need the project admin role, or a webhooks:manage token of an admin. The reason is that deliveries show what a project does.

The URL must be https on port 443 or 8443, and it must give a public host. The server resolves the host. It refuses (422 WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED) a host with an internal address. This includes private, loopback, link-local and metadata addresses. The server checks again at each delivery. It connects only to the address that it checked. Thus a DNS answer that changes later cannot send a delivery into the platform.

docs.title: What a delivery looks like
docs.text:
POST /mapi HTTP/1.1
Host: hooks.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: mapi-webhooks/1
Mapi-Signature: t=1792000000,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd
Mapi-Event-Id: evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0
Mapi-Event-Type: run.succeeded
Mapi-Webhook-Id: whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0
Mapi-Delivery-Id: whd_01jaf3m1n2p3q4r5s6t7v8w9x0

{"api_version":"v1","created":"2026-10-15T09:30:00Z","data":{"kind":"fit","model_version_id":"mv_01jaf3e1f2g3h4j5k6m7n8p9q0","run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"succeeded"},"id":"evt_01jaf3k1m2n3p4q5r6s7t8v9w0","project":"growth","tenant":"acme","type":"run.succeeded"}
Event data run.succeeded, run.failed run_id, kind, state, model_version_id. Failures also have failure_class and code model.version.ready model_id, model_version_id, ref, scorecard_overall endpoint.promoted alias, ref, revision, model_version_id, overridden, action (promote or rollback) score.completed run_id, model_version_id, outputs (names), and endpoint (alias, ref, revision) if the score came through an endpoint tenant.deletion.completed deletion_id, requested_at, completed_at

The server records each event in the same database transaction as its cause. Thus the server sends an event only if the event occurred, and always if it occurred. Delivery is at least once. Use Mapi-Event-Id to remove duplicates. Envelopes have ids and states. They never have data, signed URLs or secrets. Use the API to get the results.

No plot attachments. Webhooks do not attach rendered plots. The platform plan had them as an option. A receiver is a third party on the internet. It is frequently a chat or automation service that logs or sends on what it gets. Thus a chart in the body, or a signed link to a chart, would publish model results outside the project. If a receiver wants a chart, it renders the chart with its own token when the event arrives:

  1. On model.version.ready, call POST /v1/plots:render with Prefer: wait=60 and this body: {"source": {"model_id": ..., "version": ..., "plot_id": "core.ppc_fan"}, "format": "png"}.
  2. Download the PNG from the link in the answer.

Render runs need a token with runs:create.

docs.title: Verify it
docs.text:
1. Calculate the HMAC again over the raw body, before you parse the body.
  2. Compare the values in constant time.
  3. Refuse timestamps that are more than five minutes from your clock.
PythonNode 
from mapi_client.webhooks import verify
from mapi_spec.errors import MapiError

def handle(raw_body: bytes, headers: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    try:
        event = verify(headers, raw_body, SECRET)  # a WebhookEnvelope
    except MapiError:
        return 401
    ...

Receiving webhooks has complete FastAPI and Flask receivers.

import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verify(rawBody, header, secret, now = Date.now() / 1000) {
  const parts = Object.groupBy(header.split(","), (p) => p.split("=")[0]);
  const t = Number(parts.t?.[0]?.split("=")[1]);
  if (!Number.isInteger(t) || Math.abs(now - t) > 300) return false;
  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  return (parts.v1 ?? []).some((p) => {
    const got = Buffer.from(p.split("=")[1] ?? "", "hex");
    return got.length === 32 && crypto.timingSafeEqual(got, Buffer.from(expected, "hex"));
  });
}

Answer with a 2xx quickly, and do the work after. The platform waits for a maximum of 5 seconds. It reads a maximum of 256 KiB of the answer. The platform does not follow redirects.

docs.title: Retries, failures and replays
docs.text:
If a delivery does not get a 2xx, the platform tries again after these times: 1 minute, 5 minutes and 30 minutes. Then it tries after 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours. Each time has a maximum of 10% jitter. There are 8 tries in total. If an event is still not delivered, it counts as one failure of the webhook. After 20 such events in a sequence, the platform disables the webhook. The webhook tells the reason (disabled_reason). If a receiver answers 410 Gone, the platform disables the webhook immediately.

The audit log records the two types of disable (webhook.disabled). To enable the webhook again:

  1. Repair the receiver.

  2. Enable the webhook:

    api -X PATCH "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0" --data '{"active": true}'

    Or, in the command line, use mapi webhooks update whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0 --enable.

The delivery log has each delivery with its status (pending, retrying, succeeded, failed, blocked). It also has the last response code, the duration and the start of the answer:

api "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0/deliveries?status=failed"
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0/deliveries/whd_01jaf3m1n2p3q4r5s6t7v8w9x0:replay"

A replay sends the same event again (with the same event id) as a new delivery.

docs.title: Rotate the secret
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/webhooks/whk_01jaf3h1j2k3m4n5p6q7r8s9t0:rotate-secret"

This call gives the new secret, one time. For 24 hours, deliveries have two v1 signatures, one for each secret. Thus the receiver can change to the new secret and lose no deliveries.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
The worker (mapi-server worker) sends deliveries. The API never sends them. A relay loop looks for deliveries that are due at each MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S. It gives each try to the webhooks procrastinate queue. The database keeps the schedule of the retries. Thus, if a worker stops during a delivery, the delivery is only late.

The configuration reference gives the settings. Observability lists the metrics, for example:

  • mapi_webhook_deliveries_total
  • mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total
  • mapi_webhooks_disabled_total
  • mapi_endpoint_promotions_total
  • mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total.

For development, a receiver on your own machine is not a public host. You must allow it explicitly. The multi-tenant profile refuses these settings:

export MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST=localhost
export MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP=true   # only for the allow-listed hosts

docs.title: Your first model in the web app v0.2
docs.text:
This guide fits a hierarchical geo marketing-mix model on the local stack. The model is the E33 example of the corpus. Then the guide uses the model. You do all the work in the browser:

  1. Upload these datasets: daily spend and revenue for each market and channel, an FX table and a holiday table.
  2. Paste the model spec into the editor. The editor validates the spec while you type.
  3. Fit the model and monitor the sampler live.
  4. Read the sanity scorecard, the posterior predictive check and the channel decomposition.
  5. Score an 8-week forecast, a market that the model did not see, and a weekly budget in EUR.

The guide takes about ten minutes. You use most of this time to read. The fit uses very small sampler settings. It finishes in less than one minute on a laptop.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Start the stack and let it continue to run (Local development):

make install
make dev                      # PostgreSQL, GCS shim, API, worker, web app, plot sandbox
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

Port 8000 taken?

You can move the API with export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010 before make dev. All the other commands in this guide (make seed, make e2e) read the same variable. You can move the other three ports in the same way. See Port conflicts.

This guide clicks through all the steps, and the uploads too. For the short path, see the quickstart. In the short path, make seed loads the data and the spec for you. For all the pages of the app, see The Expert web app.

Then write the demo files to a folder. This command does not upload the files:

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/
File What it is Upload it as eu_media_daily.zarr.zip 30 weeks of daily spend_local(market, channel, date) and revenue_local(market, date) for NL, DE and UK (UK in GBP) eu_media_daily fx_daily.zarr.zip Daily EUR for each GBP, for the fit window and the forecast horizon fx_daily holidays_eu.zarr.zip A daily holiday indicator holidays_eu eu_media_future.zarr.zip Planned daily spend for the 8 weeks after the data (no revenue) eu_media_future eu_media_future_fr.zarr.zip The same weeks and FR, a market that the model did not see eu_media_future_fr eu_media_weekly_plan.zarr.zip A budget from a planner: weekly spend in EUR eu_media_weekly_plan eu_media_window.zarr.zip The last four weeks of the data, for counterfactuals eu_media_window eu-geo-mmm.yaml The model spec. It points at dataset://default/<name>@latest (paste it)

make seed does steps 1 and 2 for you through the HTTP API. This guide clicks through them.

docs.title: 1. Upload the data
docs.text:
1. Open Datasets → New dataset.
  2. Name the dataset eu_media_daily and make it. The upload panel opens.
  3. Select eu_media_daily.zarr.zip.
  4. Click Upload and ingest.

The browser sends the file directly to object storage through a signed URL. Then a sandboxed ingest run opens the file and checks it. The run keeps an immutable, content-addressed version. The page refreshes automatically until the version is ready.

The schema came with the file:

  • market allows new levels at score time, with a hyperprior.
  • channel is fixed.
  • date can be extended into the future.
  • revenue_local is the target and spend_local is spend. Both are in local currency.

A CSV upload asks you for the same mapping, one column at a time.

Do the upload steps again for the other six files. Use the names in the table above.

docs.title: 2. Write and validate the spec
docs.text:
1. Open Build → New spec.
  2. Select all the text in the editor.
  3. Paste eu-geo-mmm.yaml.

The editor validates the spec while you type. The server resolves each dataset:// reference and each step. It checks the settings. It moves the schema through the pipeline, but it does not run anything. Problems show as wavy lines at the exact YAML path.

The pipeline panel shows what each step does to the data:

  • to_eur changes spend and revenue to EUR with the fx side table.
  • weekly resamples days to weeks. A week exists only from this stage. Thus the train/holdout split is immediately after this step.
  • scale_spend, scale_y and lags learn state from the training weeks only.

To see the variables and dims at a stage, open Schema after this step on the card.

When the spec is valid, click Save spec. The spec becomes revision r1 of spec://default/eu-geo-mmm.

If you ran make seed before, the name is not available. In this case, change metadata.name first. Or open the seeded spec under Build.

docs.title: 3. Fit it
docs.text:
Click Fit. The run page monitors the run through server-sent events.

  • Starting the sandbox: The supervisor of the run read its one-time bootstrap object and deleted it. Thus the credentials of the object are gone before model code runs.
  • DEV_MODE_ISOLATION is usual on a laptop. The local executor cannot change to a different user for the model code. Containers and Cloud Run can.
  • The progress bar and the message come directly from the sampler (chain 1/2: sampling 39/100).

fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit makes the run do three things:

  1. The run fits the training weeks.
  2. It scores the 8 holdout weeks through the usual score path.
  3. It fits again on all the data.

Thus the model that you use has seen the latest weeks, and its metrics are honest. When the run succeeds, the platform does three things:

  • It checks each file that the run wrote against the checksums of the storage.
  • It copies the files to a location that the run cannot get to.
  • It signs a manifest.

When the run succeeds, click Inspect model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1.

docs.title: 4. Inspect the model
docs.text:
The Overview tab opens on the sanity scorecard, the holdout metrics and the things that the model can do.

With 2 chains of 100 draws, the sampler did not converge. The scorecard shows warnings for R-hat above 1.01 and for fewer than 200 effective samples. Each warning has a suggested action. The very small settings have this result on purpose. For a model that you will use, increase tune and draws, and use more chains. Diagnostics lists the same checks for each variable.

Plots has the recipes that the spec asked for. Each plot renders in an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> from a separate origin (port 5174). Thus a malicious plot spec cannot read the app, its cookies or your data.

Fit and forecast compares the predictions of the model for the holdout weeks with the actual results:

  • The line is the median.
  • The bands are the 50% and 90% intervals.
  • The dots are the actual weekly EUR revenue.

Contribution by component divides revenue over time into the baseline, each channel, seasonality and holidays, in EUR. The totals and their uncertainty are below. Response curves shows the return of one more euro of spend for each channel. Sampler convergence has the trace and rank plots for the scorecard. Provenance shows these items:

  • The signed manifest.
  • Each stored object with its generation.
  • The lineage: the versions of the data and the side tables, the spec hash, the plugin, the seed and the library versions.

docs.title: 5. Score it
docs.text:
Click Score. The form shows only the modes that the model can do. The server uses the same preprocessing as the fit. It does not fit the model again.

An 8-week forecast.

  1. Keep Forecast with 8 periods.
  2. Under Values to score, select Use a dataset.
  3. Type dataset://default/eu_media_future@v1.
  4. Click Forecast.

For a quick plan, you can keep Type values and type the spend into the grid. The grid starts with the periods after the fit for each market and channel. By default, the fx side table is the table that the fit used. This table includes the horizon. Thus the server can change the planned spend from local currency to EUR. The result shows a fan for each market. Then it shows the outputs: the result tree (score.zarr.zip) and its summary as a table. It also shows a quick chart that you can plot again by any column.

A new market. Score again with dataset://default/eu_media_future_fr@v1. The training data did not have FR. The model draws the effects of FR from the hierarchical prior over markets. Thus the band of FR is clearly wider than the bands of the other markets. The issues of the result have an UNSEEN_LEVELS note that tells this.

A weekly plan in EUR. Planners use weekly euros, not daily local currency.

  1. Under Advanced, set Inputs enter at stage to weekly.
  2. Use the dataset dataset://default/eu_media_weekly_plan@v1.
