The request goes into the pipeline after to_eur and weekly. Thus you do not need an FX table. This plan has the same spend as the daily file. Thus the forecast is the same as the first forecast. This is the result that the server promises when it uses the same preprocessing again.

A counterfactual.

  1. Select What if.
  2. Use the dataset dataset://default/eu_media_window@v1.
  3. Add a change to spend_local where channel=tv, and multiply by 1.2.
  4. Under Advanced, select Predictive output.
  5. Set Draws to 100.

With 0 draws, you get the means, but not the uncertainty of the change. The result has the baseline, the scenario and their difference. The server calculates them with common random numbers. Thus the sampling noise does not hide the difference.

docs.title: What was checked along the way
docs.text:
Two automatic suites run the same flow against the running stack (make e2e):

  • tests/e2e/test_m1_stack.py runs the flow through the Python client. It also verifies these items:

    • The manifest signature.
    • Each bundle object is in the bundles bucket at its signed generation.
    • The bundle reads back with all hashes correct.
    • The bootstrap object is gone.
    • The server refuses forged run events.
    • apps/web/e2e/m1-flow.e2e.spec.ts clicks through the pages above with Playwright. It checks that the plot frame is an opaque origin with no access to its parent.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Marketing-mix models: the model, its priors, derived quantities and budget plots.
  • Spec format and the steps that this guide uses.
  • Web app and plot sandbox: all the pages, and how the app isolates plots.

docs.title: Validate models with governance policies v0.5
docs.text:
If a model gives information for decisions, it must show that it learned something real. This guide shows how to do these tasks:

  • Tell which checks a model must pass (a policy).
  • Run the checks on a model version (a validation).
  • Get a second person to approve the version.
  • Export the evidence pack for an auditor.
  • Make endpoints refuse models that are not validated.

Governance gives the concepts and the full state machine. The HTTP API reference gives all the operations.

You can also do all these tasks in the web app. See In the web app. Can you trust this model? tells why the null tests are important, in plain words and in statistics. In Python, use api.governance and api.validations (client guide). In a terminal, use mapi governance, mapi validate model, mapi validations and mapi approve (CLI guide):

mapi governance checks                        # what a policy can require
mapi governance checks --about null.permutation_target --expert
mapi governance policies ls                   # in force here: tenant-wide first
mapi governance policies create forecast-policy.yaml
mapi validate model model://growth/wf-weekly-readiness-fit@v1   # runs the checks, waits
mapi validations ls --queue                   # reviewers: what waits for a decision
mapi approve "$VALIDATION" --comment "Null tests convincing; beats naive by 25%"
mapi validations pack "$VALIDATION" --out evidence.html          # for the auditor

The examples below use curl with an API token. For the api helper, see Endpoints and webhooks:

api() { curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: $MAPI_PROJECT" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' "$@"; }

docs.title: What the checks mean, in plain words
docs.text:
Each check has an About card (GET /v1/catalog/governance-checks). The governance checks reference lists each check with its card, metric, default limits, necessary conditions and parameters. In summary:

Check It asks How the platform measures it null.permutation_target Is the model better than versions of itself that were fitted on shuffled data? A model with drivers keeps its result. The platform shuffles its drivers together in blocks of time. Thus trend, season and controls cannot pass alone. For a model without drivers (or a model that ignores them), the platform shuffles the changes from period to period of its result. Then it adds them up again from the same start. For a series that does not wander, it shuffles the plain values. This keeps the quantity of wander, but removes all that is predictable. The platform fits the model again n_permutations times. It scores each fit on its held-out skill against the null forecast (the last value, or the mean). This skill does not change with the level where a shuffle lands. The p-value is the fraction of shuffled fits that did as well as the real fit, (1 + #as good) / (n + 1). With 20 shuffles, the smallest possible p is 0.048. Thus, for a 5% test, use a minimum of 19. null.noise_regressors Does the model give fake drivers made of pure noise almost no credit? The platform adds n_noise placebo drivers. Each placebo is a real driver shuffled in time, or Gaussian noise with the mean and spread of a real driver. The placebos are new channels of a marketing-mix model, or new variables of other models. Then the platform fits the model again. Placebos get the default prior of the model. The platform does not copy the priors and calibration of the real channels (business priors, lift tests). The platform switches each placebo off and scores again. Thus it measures the share of each placebo in the total effect of the real drivers. If it cannot measure the effect of the drivers, it uses the share of the result. The check flags a Bayesian model when a placebo share is above the warn limit with a minimum of 90% posterior probability. It does not flag it when the interval does not include zero, because the positive-only effects of a marketing mix model always do this. For frequentist models, the check uses Holm's correction for the number of placebos on the placebo p-values. null.placebo_time_shift Do the effects go away when the drivers move months away? The platform shifts the drivers (shifts, default ±26 periods, wrapped around) and fits the model again. The check gives the placebo effect as a share of the real effect. If a model still finds most of the effect, it finds trend or season, not the drivers. baseline.beats_naive Is the model better than simple benchmarks on held-out periods? The platform scores the train-only model on the held-out periods. It compares the model with "same as last period", "same as last season", the mean and the drift line. It forecasts these benchmarks from the training history. Skill is 1 - error(model) / error(best benchmark). The check also gives MASE. residuals.whiteness Is there no pattern left in the errors? Ljung-Box on the in-sample residuals of each series. The smallest p-value counts. ARMA orders decrease the degrees of freedom. stability.rolling_params Are the key estimates stable over time? The platform fits the model again on rolling windows of history. The check gives the largest coefficient of variation of the key estimates across the windows. plausibility.signs Do effects go in the expected direction? By default, media and spend must increase the result. If you switch a channel off, the prediction must decrease. For Bayesian models, this applies to each posterior draw. List other expectations in expected, for example {"price": "negative"}. sensitivity.prior For Bayesian models: do the data control the answers, and not the assumptions? The platform multiplies each prior width of the model by each value of scales. This includes the default values of the plugin that the settings do not give. For mmm.bayesian, these are the default ROI prior LogNormal(0, 1), seasonality.prior_sigma, trend.growth_prior_sigma and hierarchy.media_geo_sigma. It also includes business priors that the platform translates at fit time. Widths are sigma, scale, sd and tau under a prior… key, and keys named …prior_sigma or …_sigma. Beta/Gamma beta or b parameters are not widths, and the platform never changes them. The check gives the largest relative change of a key posterior mean. recovery.simulated Does the model find known answers? The platform simulates data from the fit: its expected values and block-bootstrapped residuals. It fits the model again n_sims times. The check counts how frequently the 90% intervals contain the fitted values. The target is 90%. This is a parametric-bootstrap version of simulation-based calibration. convergence Did the fit finish correctly? Bayesian: the largest split R-hat. Divergences and the effective sample size are evidence. One divergence changes a pass to a warning. Other models: the converged flag of the optimiser. holdout.accuracy Is the error on unseen data below your limit? The holdout metric of the fit (mape by default, as a fraction). For rmse or mae, set thresholds in the units of the KPI. data.quality Is the data sufficiently good? The quality warnings of the Data Explorer that are more than information: missing shares above max_missing, fewer than min_history_periods, constant drivers, negative spend, values outside declared bounds, duplicated periods, long gaps and collinear drivers.

Each result has these items:

  • The measured value.
  • The threshold.
  • A plain-language message_plain.
  • A suggested_action, if the check did not pass.
  • Evidence (tables, numbers) for the auditor.

docs.title: Model families
docs.text:
The checks change for the method that estimates the model (mapi_spec.governance.model_kind):

  • Bayesian (MCMC, VI, SMC): A new fit uses a budget of a maximum of 200 draws and 200 tuning steps on 2 chains (RefitBudget). Intervals are highest-density intervals. sensitivity.prior applies.
  • Frequentist (statsmodels, MAP, Kalman, ridge): A new fit runs as configured. Intervals are confidence intervals from standard errors. convergence reads the optimiser flag.
  • Machine learning (scikit-learn, xgboost, quantile and conformal models): There are no parameter intervals. If the model has no coefficients, the platform skips recovery.simulated and stability.rolling_params. The null tests and the benchmarks apply with no change.

If a check does not apply, the result is skipped with the reason. For example: "the model has no test period (add a data split and refit)". If the platform cannot calculate a check, the result is error. If the check is blocking, error blocks the validation. A governance run fits the model again a maximum of max_refits times (120 by default).

docs.title: The default policies
docs.text:
When a project uses governance for the first time, the platform makes three tenant-wide policies. They decide what a validation checks. But they do not gate promotion and do not need approval. An admin can switch on these functions.

Policy Families Blocking Warning Information Marketing mix models mmm data quality, convergence, holdout accuracy (MAPE ≤ 15% warn / 30% fail), shuffled results (20), fake drivers (3), effect signs beats benchmarks, time-shift placebo, prior sensitivity residual whiteness Forecasting models ts, forecast, ts_multivariate, regime data quality, convergence, beats benchmarks, holdout accuracy residual whiteness, shuffled results parameter stability Regression and machine learning tabular, choice, sklearn data quality, holdout accuracy, shuffled results fake drivers convergence

The thresholds are the catalog defaults:

Measure Passes Warns Shuffled-result p-value ≤ 0.05 ≤ 0.10 Fake-driver share ≤ 2% ≤ 5% Placebo effect ≤ 25% ≤ 50% Benchmark skill ≥ 0.05 ≥ 0 Ljung-Box p ≥ 0.05 ≥ 0.01 Rolling variation ≤ 25% ≤ 50% Wrong-sign share ≤ 10% ≤ 25% Prior sensitivity ≤ 20% ≤ 50% Interval coverage within 10 points of 90% within 25 points R-hat ≤ 1.01 ≤ 1.05 Holdout MAPE ≤ 15% ≤ 30% Data problems none a maximum of 2

docs.title: Write a policy
docs.text:
Project admins add policies to a project. Tenant admins add tenant-wide policies. Each project gets the tenant-wide policies as a minimum. A project can make a threshold stricter, but it can never make it less strict:

api -X POST "$API/v1/governance/policies" -d '{
  "name": "Forecasts we publish",
  "applies_to": {"families": ["ts"]},
  "checks": [
    {"check": "baseline.beats_naive"},
    {"check": "null.permutation_target", "params": {"n_permutations": 20}},
    {"check": "residuals.whiteness", "severity": "warning"},
    {"check": "holdout.accuracy", "thresholds": {"warn": 0.10, "fail": 0.20}}
  ],
  "require_approval": true,
  "approvals_required": 1,
  "require_validated_for_promotion": true
}'
  • PUT …/policies/{policy_id} saves the next version. To refuse an edit that occurs at the same time with 409, send expected_version.
  • GET …/versions lists all the versions.
  • DELETE retires the policy, but keeps its versions for audit.
  • GET /v1/governance/policies lists the policies in force in the project. The tenant-wide policies are first.

docs.title: Validate a model version
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/models/$MODEL_ID/versions/7/validations" -d '{"note": "Q4 refresh"}'

The answer (202) is a validation in checks_running. It has the checks that apply to it. It also has the governance run (workflow_run_id) that measures the checks in the sandbox.

All the policies in force for the model always apply to a validation. These are the tenant-wide minimum and the policies of the project. policy_ids can only add more active policies. It can never remove a policy. The platform locks the version while it checks a request. Thus two requests at the same time make one validation. A request and the submission of a workflow also make one validation. The other request gets 409 VALIDATION_TRANSITION_INVALID.

Monitor the run as you monitor other runs (GET /v1/runs/{run_id}, or its event stream). When the run finishes, the validation moves to the next status automatically:

checks_running -> checks_passed -> validated              (no approval required)
checks_running -> checks_passed -> awaiting_approval      (approval required)
checks_running -> checks_failed                           (a blocking check failed or errored)

GET /v1/validations/{validation_id} shows the status, all the results and the history. GET …/evidence gives the results with their evidence, one page at a time.

If the validation fails, or a reviewer rejects it, do these steps:

  1. Repair the model or the data.
  2. Send POST /v1/validations/{id}:resubmit. A new round starts under the policies that are in force now.

:cancel stops the checks that run. The validation goes back to draft.

docs.title: Approve as a second person
docs.text:
When a policy needs approval, a different person from the submitter decides. This person must have the reviewer capability, or be a project admin. Give the capability on the membership:

api -X PATCH "$API/v1/tenants/acme/projects/growth/members/$USER_ID" \
  -d '{"capabilities": ["reviewer"]}'

Reviewers find their queue at GET /v1/validations?status=awaiting_approval. They decide in a signed-in session. API tokens can never approve:

curl -X POST "$API/v1/validations/$VALIDATION_ID/approvals" -d '{"decision": "approve",
  "comment": "Null tests are convincing; benchmarks beaten by 30%."}'
  • The platform refuses the submitter (403 SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN).
  • Each reviewer decides one time in each round.
  • approvals_required approvals validate the version.
  • One rejection rejects the version. A rejection needs a comment.

If a validated version must not be used again, retire it with :deprecate and a reason.

docs.title: Promotion requires validation
docs.text:
A policy in force can say require_validated_for_promotion. If it does, you can promote a model version to an endpoint only when these conditions are true:

  • The latest validation of the version is validated.
  • The latest validation covered each such policy as it is now.

A validation covers a policy in one of two ways:

  • It gives the policy at its current version.
  • It applied each check of the policy at the same strictness or stricter (severity, limits and settings). It also had the reviewers that the policy asks for.

If a version was validated before a gating policy was added or made stricter, the platform shows it as validated under other or older policies. In this case, request a new validation. The platform refuses all other promotions with 409 NOT_VALIDATED. No administrator override changes this. The audit log records the refusal as endpoint.promote_not_validated.

docs.title: Export the evidence pack
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/validations/$VALIDATION_ID/evidence-pack" -d '{"format": "html"}'

The answer is the pack as JSON (format: mapi.evidence-pack/v1). The pack has these items:

  • The validation with all the results, their evidence, the approvals and the history.
  • The policies at the versions that applied to the validation.
  • The lineage and the sanity scorecard of the model.
  • A digest (sha256 of the canonical content).

With format: html, the answer also has download. This is a signed link to a static HTML page that contains all its content. The page has only inline styles. It has no scripts and no external assets, because a Content-Security-Policy prevents them. The page escapes all values. The audit log records exports (model.evidence_export).

docs.title: In the web app
docs.text:
Governance in the sidebar (G then V) has three tabs:

  • In force here: The tenant-wide policies first, then the policies of the project. For each policy, the tab shows what it covers and its number of checks. It also shows if the policy needs a reviewer and if it gates promotion.
  • Tenant-wide.
  • Check catalog: Each check has its About card, what it measures and its default limits.

docs.title: Editing a policy
docs.text:
Project admins edit project policies. Tenant admins edit tenant-wide policies. Other users can only read the policies.

  1. Open a policy, or click New policy.
  2. In Covers, set the model families, the model ids and the Guided templates. Empty lists match all models.
  3. In Required checks, add a check from the catalog. Its About card shows before you add it.
  4. Set the severity of the check: Blocking, Warning or Information.
  5. To set the warn and fail values of the check, switch on Custom limits.
  6. Adjust the settings of the check. The form for the settings comes from the parameters of the check, for example the number of shuffles.
  7. In Sign-off and promotion, set Require approval by a reviewer and the number of reviewers.
  8. Set Only validated models can be promoted to an endpoint and Active.
  9. Click Save version N. The app saves the next version.

The page refuses a fail limit that is less strict than the warn limit, as the server does.

If a different person edits the policy at the same time, the app refuses your save. Your edit stays on the screen. Versions lists all the versions and compares two versions side by side. Retire policy keeps the versions of the policy for audit.

docs.title: Validating a model version
docs.text:
The page of a model version has a Validation button. The button lists the validations of the version and requests a new validation. A new request has these items:

  • The policies that apply. All the policies in force always apply. If you tick other policies, they also apply.
  • The data to check against (optional).
  • A note.

The validation page then shows these items:

  • Status: The position of the validation on its path. The path is draft → checks running → checks passed → awaiting approval → validated. Other statuses are checks failed, rejected and deprecated. The status also shows the history of each transition, with the person who made it and their note.
  • Checks: Failures first. Each check has its plain-language message and What to do if it did not pass. It also has the measured value against its limit, and its evidence. The evidence is small tables and numbers. For the shuffled-result test, it is also a plot. The plot shows the distribution of the errors of the shuffled fits, with a mark at the error of the real model. The plot sandbox draws the plot.
  • Approvals, Evidence pack and Held to (the policy versions).

The page shows these buttons for the applicable states:

  • Cancel checks.
  • Resubmit, after failed checks or a rejection.
  • Deprecate, with a reason, for a validated version. Only project admins can deprecate.

Export evidence pack saves the HTML page or the JSON as a file. The app never opens the HTML.

docs.title: Reviewing
docs.text:
Reviewers find Review queue on the Governance page, with the number of validations that wait. They can also use Validations with the filter Awaiting approval. The approval form shows only to members who can approve. These are project admins, and editors or runners who have the reviewer capability. A rejection needs a comment.

On your own submission, the form tells you that a second person must review it. Its buttons are disabled. The server also refuses your decision (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN).

Project admins give and remove the capability in the Reviewer column of Members. Admins have the capability automatically. Viewers cannot have it.

docs.title: Promotion in the app
docs.text: A policy can gate promotion. In this case, if you promote a version that is not validated from Integrations, the app refuses. It shows A governance policy requires a validated model and the current validation status of the version. It also shows links to the validation, or to request a validation. The app gives no override, because no override passes this rule.

docs.title: Audit and webhooks
docs.text:
The audit log records these events:

  • Each policy change (policy.create, policy.update, policy.delete).
  • Each request (model.validation_request).
  • Each transition (model.validation_transition, with from, to and the actor).
  • Each decision (model.approve, model.reject).
  • Each deprecation.

To start review queues and release pipelines, subscribe webhooks to these events:

  • model.validation.checks_passed
  • model.validation.checks_failed
  • model.validation.awaiting_approval
  • model.validated
  • model.rejected
  • model.deprecated.

docs.title: From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft v0.4
docs.text:
This guide follows the Guided data path over the HTTP API. You do these steps:

  1. Select a template.
  2. Let the platform suggest which column answers each question.
  3. Change the answers into a draft. A draft is an ingest mapping and a ModelSpec.
  4. Upload the data with that mapping.
  5. Save the spec.

The Guided screens of the web app and the Python client make the same calls. Guided mode gives the concepts.

All calls are project-scoped. Send X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project>, or use a token that is bound to the project. The examples use the single-tenant development server.

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser or client
    participant API as API (JSON only)
    participant S as Sandbox (ingest run)
    B->>API: GET /v1/guided/templates
    B->>B: profile the file locally (ColumnProfile per column)
    B->>API: POST /v1/guided/detect-roles {template_id, columns}
    API-->>B: RoleSuggestions (answers pre-filled, reasons)
    B->>API: POST /v1/guided/drafts {answers, columns}
    API-->>B: GuidedDraft (mapping, spec, YAML, issues)
    B->>API: POST /v1/datasets/{id}/uploads, PUT the file, POST …/versions {mapping}
    API->>S: ingest run (parse, caps, columns.json)
    B->>API: POST /v1/specs {yaml}

docs.title: 1. Pick a template
docs.text:
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/templates | jq '.items[] | {id, title, plugin}'
Template Built-in model Data that it expects geo_mmm mmm.bayesian (mmm-framework) One row for each market and week: the result, one spend column for each channel, and optional controls weekly_forecast ts.hsgp_trend One row for each week (or day): the series to forecast store_demand tabular.regressor One row for each store and week: the units sold and the drivers (price, promotions) customer_choice choice.multinomial_logit One row for each household and shopping trip: the product chosen, and one price (and promotion) column for each product

GET /v1/guided/templates/{id} gives one template with these items:

  • Its questions.
  • The spec template.
  • The scorecard checks.
  • The x-ui-level of each field.

docs.title: 2. Let the platform suggest the answers
docs.text:
The browser profiles the upload locally. Thus no hostile data goes to the servers only for a preview. The browser sends one ColumnProfile for each column:

curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/detect-roles -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "template_id": "geo_mmm",
  "columns": [
    {"name": "Week", "dtype": "date", "n_rows": 520, "n_distinct": 104, "detected_freq": "W-SUN"},
    {"name": "Region", "dtype": "string", "n_rows": 520, "n_distinct": 5},
    {"name": "Revenue", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 10, "max": 90000},
    {"name": "TV_Spend", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 0, "max": 50000},
    {"name": "Search_Spend", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 0, "max": 20000},
    {"name": "avg_price", "dtype": "number", "n_rows": 520, "min": 1, "max": 3}
  ]}' | jq '.questions[] | {question_id, answer}'

Each question comes back with ranked candidates, a confidence and a reason_plain. An example reason is "named like a revenue column; never negative". The heuristics look at these properties:

  • Names. The heuristics split names into words and compare them with the keywords of each question.
  • Types.
  • The number of distinct values. Labels are good for dims.
  • Ordered dates and trip numbers.
  • Negative or constant values. These are bad candidates for spend.
  • Columns that are almost empty.

A column answers a maximum of one question. If a necessary question has no good candidate, it comes back as a warning in issues.

docs.title: From a stored dataset
docs.text:
Instead of columns, give a stored version: {"template_id": "geo_mmm", "dataset": "dataset://growth/eu_media@v2"}. Each ingest run from v0.4 writes columns.json. This file has the profile of each uploaded column, which the sandbox calculates. Detection reads this file. You can also download it with GET /v1/datasets/{id}/versions/{v}/artifacts/columns.json.

For an MFF upload, the profiles are the profiles of the pivoted table. These are Period, the key columns that vary, and one column for each VariableName. Thus TV_Spend answers the spend question. For versions ingested before v0.4, and for zarr or netCDF uploads, detection uses their dims and variables. It reads them from the stored schema and summary. In all cases, the API reads only JSON metadata, never the data.

docs.title: 3. Turn the answers into a draft
docs.text:
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/guided/drafts -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "template_id": "geo_mmm", "name": "eu-geo-mmm", "dataset": "eu_media",
  "answers": {"kpi": "Revenue", "date": "Week", "geo": "Region",
              "spend": ["TV_Spend", "Search_Spend"], "controls": ["avg_price"]},
  "columns": [ ...the same profiles... ]}'

The GuidedDraft holds these items:

  • mapping: The IngestMapping for the upload. Column names become safe dataset names (Avg Price → avg_price). Spend columns become one spend variable along a new channel dim. The labels come from the names (TV_Spend → tv). For the choice template, price_cola and promo_cola both give the label of the product cola.
  • spec and yaml: The ModelSpec for the project, with fit.mode: evaluate_then_refit.
  • issues: Answer warnings (a column with a type that does not agree with the question) and the findings of the static validator. The validator checks the draft against the catalog with the schema that its mapping promises, before data exists. For example, a control with the name Fourier would conflict with the seasonality that the template adds (/pipeline/4).

Impossible answers get 422 GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID, which points at /answers/<question>. Impossible answers are these:

  • A necessary answer is missing.
  • A column is used two times.
  • Two columns would get the same dataset name.
  • A choice or a number is out of range.

For an MFF upload, send "format": "mff". Then the answers give Period, the MFF key columns and the VariableName values. The mapping uses the mff preset.

The draft call stores nothing. Upload the data with the mapping of the draft, then save the spec:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/datasets/$DS/versions -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"upload_id\": \"$UPLOAD\", \"mapping\": $(jq .mapping draft.json)}"
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/v1/specs -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"yaml\": $(jq .yaml draft.json)}"

docs.title: File formats and presets
docs.text:
A sandboxed ingest run parses each upload. Tabular uploads are CSV or Parquet. A CSV file can use comma, semicolon, tab or | separators. It must be UTF-8, and it can be gzip-compressed. zarr_zip and netcdf files have their own descriptions.

Mapping What the ingest does dims, vars, wide One column for each dim and variable. wide collects one column for each label into one variable along a new dim. Wide variables that share a dim must use the same labels preset: mff (or format: mff) Pivots the MFF long table. Period becomes the time dim. Key columns with more than one value become dims. Each VariableName becomes a variable. With vars/wide, these select and rename the pivoted variables, as for CSV columns. mff.combine joins key columns into one dim. For example, {"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches preset: meridian The CoordToColumns contract of Google Meridian on a wide table: time, geo, kpi (target), revenue_per_kpi, population, controls, and media/media_spend (and reach and frequency) along channel

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The ingest checks what a file declares before a parser allocates memory. It checks each cell after the parse. IngestJob sets the limits. The table below gives the defaults of the server.

Limit Default Checked rows 50 million CSV: the parse stops one row after the limit. Parquet: from its metadata columns 4,096 The CSV header or the Parquet schema. MFF: distinct variables characters for each cell or column name 4,096 (names: 256) Each header and text cell decompression ratio 50 × the stored size gzip CSV (streamed), Parquet, zip archives, netCDF (decoded bytes). The ingest never refuses files that decode to less than 64 MiB because of their ratio uncompressed size The scratch budget of the ingest run: 3 GiB (class S), 6 GiB (M), 12 GiB (L) The same, as an absolute size. The class is the smallest class with a dataset cap that holds the upload dataset size 250 million values, and 8 bytes for each value in the scratch budget The dense dataset that a table pivots to (each combination of the dim labels, multiplied by the variables). The ingest checks it before it builds the dataset (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE)

Some dates have a UTC offset or a time zone, for example 2024-01-07T00:00:00+01:00 or a tz-aware Parquet timestamp. The ingest reads them as the local date and time that they give, and removes the offset. Thus midnight labels stay on their day. The ingest gives this as an info issue.

The ingest refuses bzip2, xz and zstd compressed uploads. Each refusal is one plain-language message and a suggested action. For example:

Problem Message Suggested action a mapped column is missing column 'week' (dim 'week') is not in the upload Did you mean 'Week'? repeated rows 52 rows repeat a (week) combination Columns such as 'Region' vary within a combination: map them as dims too, or aggregate the rows first. text in a spend column column 'TV' ('spend' for 'tv') has 3 cells that are not numbers Use plain numbers without currency signs or thousands separators. not UTF-8 the upload is not UTF-8 text Save the file as 'CSV UTF-8' (in Excel: File > Save As > CSV UTF-8). a decompression bomb the gzip file expands to more than … bytes Upload the CSV uncompressed, or split it into several files. dims that rarely repeat the mapped dims span 100,000 store x 100,000 day = 10,000,000,000 combinations, so the dataset would hold … values Most combinations have no row: map fewer columns as dims (keep the others as variables), use a long layout with one id dim, or split the upload.

If an ingest fails, the dataset version becomes failed. Its issues have the messages. The events of the run also have them as diagnostics with message_plain and suggested_action. The platform quotes cell values only in untrusted_text.

docs.title: Locking a project to Guided mode
docs.text:
A project admin can lock a project in two ways:

  • In the web app: Settings > Mode > Lock … to Guided mode.
  • With PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project} {"guided_locked": true}.

The audit log records the lock as project.guided_lock. Then members below admin see only the Guided screens. Their spec writes (POST /v1/specs and new revisions) must stay Guided specs:

  • The spec gives its template in metadata.labels.guided, and it uses the plugin of that template. Drafts do this.
  • Fields that the template marks advanced or hidden keep their values. A revision cannot change them from its parent. A new spec has the values of the template where the template sets them. For geo_mmm, these are the pipeline, the adstock and saturation settings, the fit settings and the execution block.
  • Answers, basic settings (such as pooling), business priors and lift tests can change.

All other writes get 403 FORBIDDEN, with one issue for each pointer that is not permitted. The issue suggests that you ask an admin. The lock does not apply to admins, POST /v1/specs:validate, runs and scores. The lock also does not apply to the score calls of integrations.

docs.title: Guided modelling: priors, lift tests and the scorecard v0.4
docs.text:
This guide tells what occurs behind the Guided-mode tasks of Guided mode when the model is a marketing-mix model (mmm.bayesian, on mmm-framework). It tells these things:

  • How beliefs in business units become priors in model space.
  • How experiment results calibrate a fit.
  • How the platform measures the sanity scorecard.
  • Which views the what-if sliders, forecasts and counterfactuals read.

All the tasks that touch data run in the sandbox. The control plane only validates JSON.

Task Where it runs What it writes Business priors → model-space priors a translate_priors run priors.json (PriorTranslationResult), plots.json Lift-test calibration in the fit mmm-framework experiment likelihoods, learned.calibration Sanity scorecard at the end of the fit scorecard.json (Scorecard), stored on the model version What-if sliders at the end of the fit ui/grids/response_curves.json (ResponseGridView) Forecast a forecast score run ui/guided/forecast.json (ForecastView) and a fan chart with the split line Counterfactual a counterfactual score run ui/guided/counterfactual.json (CounterfactualView)

docs.title: Business priors
docs.text:
A business prior gives a belief about one channel, in the units that persons use:

calibration:
  business_priors:
    channels:
      tv:     {roi: [1.5, 4.0], credibility: 0.8}           # "80% sure each euro returns 1.5 to 4"
      search: {contribution_share: [0.05, 0.15], credibility: 0.9}
    baseline_share: {share: [0.5, 0.8], credibility: 0.8}   # KPI without any media

docs.title: From beliefs to priors: the math
docs.text:
mmm.bayesian gives the effect of each channel as its return on spend. A channel with an ROI prior samples:

roi[c]  ~ LogNormal(mu[c], sigma[c])
beta[c] = roi[c] * spend[c] / (y_std * sum over observations of S[c](x))

In this equation, S[c] is the carried-over, saturated spend of the channel. This is the adstock and saturation of mmm-framework, with the same parameters. y_std is the scale of the KPI. On the observed data, the contribution of the channel over the fit window, divided by its spend, is roi[c]. This is the quantity that a business ROI belief is about. Thus the translation has a closed form:

  • An ROI range [L, H] with credibility p is the log-normal that has this range as its central p interval. Thus mu = (log L + log H) / 2 and sigma = (log H - log L) / (2 z). Here, z is the (1 + p) / 2 quantile of the standard normal.
  • A contribution-share range [l, h] is the ROI range [l Y / spend[c], h Y / spend[c]]. The reason is that share[c] = roi[c] * spend[c] / Y. Here, Y is the observed KPI total over the window.
  • The fitted factors of the pipeline change business units to model units. The model does its own scaling, thus these factors are usually 1.

The platform shows edge cases as issues. It never hides them:

  • A range that starts at 0 becomes [H / 20, H], because a log-normal has no mass at zero.
  • A range can be narrower or wider than a prior can usefully give. Then the platform clamps its spread to [0.02, 4] on the log scale. It gives a warning.
  • A channel that the data does not have is an error. A share for a channel without spend is also an error.

Channels without a belief keep their prior (priors.roi_default, or the default of mmm-framework). The platform writes the result as priors.roi.<channel> = {mu, sigma}.

The baseline share is the KPI that occurs without media: intercept, trend, seasonality, panel levels and controls. It is linear in the intercept Normal(m, s), in KPI standard deviations: B = a (m + s eps) + E. Here, a = n y_std / Y, and E is the rest of the baseline, drawn from the prior of the model in mmm-framework. The platform uses bisection to find s, so that the central interval of B has the given width. Then m puts the interval at the center. If the rest alone is already wider than the given range, s stops at its minimum and a warning tells this.

The result is priors.intercept = {mu, sigma}.

The preview then samples the prior predictive of the translated model. It uses the graph of mmm-framework, with a different seed. The preview gives ROI, contribution share, baseline share and a KPI fan in business units. It also gives the prior mass in each given range (coverage).

Amounts translate only through linear preprocessing (currency conversion). The model does its own scaling. If a non-linear step applies to the KPI or the spend, the platform refuses the translation with CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

docs.title: The prior-translation run
docs.text:
You can ask for a translation while you write a draft. Use an unsaved document or a saved revision:

curl -X POST "$MAPI/v1/guided/prior-translations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"spec_id": "spc_…", "revision": 2, "draws": 500,
       "business_priors": {"channels": {"tv": {"roi": [1.5, 4.0], "credibility": 0.8}}}}'

First, the API checks the beliefs statically:

  • It checks the channels against the levels of the dataset, and finds shares that cannot add up (BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID).
  • It finds a model without the business_priors capability (CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED).

Then it answers 202 with the queued run. The run fits the preprocessing of the pipeline on all the data. These are the scales that a production refit learns. The run solves the equations. Then it samples the translated priors again for the preview.

When the run is done, GET /v1/guided/prior-translations/{run_id} gives the PriorTranslationResult:

  • priors: The model-space priors in the settings.priors form, to write at apply_at (/model/settings/priors). mapi_spec.calibration.apply_prior_translation writes them. It also records the run in calibration.prior_translation_run.
  • preview: The distributions of ROI and contribution share for each channel, and the baseline share. It also has a KPI fan in business units against the observed KPI.
  • coverage: The prior mass in each given range. If the translation is correct, this value is near the given credibility.
  • issues: All the items above in plain words. Also, the lift tests with an implied ROI that is outside the 90% range of the prior.

The plots of the run (GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots) are these:

  • mmm.prior_beliefs: The prior interval of each channel over the range that you gave.
  • core.prior_predictive: The KPI that the priors can make, against your data.

A spec can have business_priors without a recorded translation run. In this case, the platform translates the priors at fit time. It uses the same solve over the scales of the training data. The priors that the fit used are in learned.calibration.translated_priors of the model.

docs.title: Lift tests
docs.text:
A lift test is calibration data. It gives the extra spend on one channel during a window, optionally in one geo. It also gives the incremental KPI that the spend caused, with its uncertainty:

calibration:
  lift_tests:
    - id: tv-holdout-2026q2
      channel: tv
      geo: DE
      start: 2026-04-06
      end: 2026-05-03
      spend_delta: -120000      # TV off: the spend removed
      kpi_delta: -260000        # the revenue lost
      ci: [-380000, -140000]    # or se: 73000
      ci_level: 0.9

The fit adds each test to mmm-framework as an experiment likelihood (BayesianMMM.add_experiment_calibration). This is a likelihood term on the estimand that the model implies. It updates the effect of the channel, its saturation curve and its adstock kernel together:

The test mmm-framework measurement extra spend (spend_delta > 0) Marginal ROAS: the lift when the spend of the window increases by 100 x spend_delta / window spend percent, for each extra unit of spend, against kpi_delta / spend_delta a holdout that removes all (or almost all) of the spend of the channel in the window The contribution of the channel over the window, against -kpi_delta a partial cut (less than a full holdout) Skipped, with the reason. A partial cut measures the return below the current spend. mmm-framework can calibrate only on the return above the current spend (an increase) or on a full holdout. With diminishing returns, the two are different. Thus, if the platform used one for the other, the curve would have a bias

geo limits the measurement to the observations of that geo. se is the standard error of the measurement. If you give ci, the standard error is the half-width of ci divided by the normal quantile. The fit does not count carry-over after the window, because tests give the lift measured during the test. Only the KPI likelihood stays in log_likelihood. Thus the meaning of elpd_loo does not change. learned.calibration.lift_tests tells which tests the fit used or skipped, and why.

The platform checks tests three times. Each check occurs where the information is:

  1. At submit, against the summary of the dataset version. The channel and the geo must exist, and the window must be in the data (SCHEMA_INVALID at /calibration/lift_tests/<i>/…).
  2. In the sandbox, before the fit, against the raw data.
  3. At the model stage. The window must include a minimum of one model period. A holdout (negative spend_delta) can remove a maximum of the spend that the data shows. The time labels must be dates.

During evaluate_then_refit, the evaluation fit skips some tests and logs them. These are tests with a window after the training periods, or a window that the end of the training periods cuts. The production refit uses these tests.

docs.title: The sanity scorecard
docs.text:
At the end of each fit, the runner measures each check of the catalog that it can answer. It writes scorecard.json. The finalizer stores the scorecard on the model version (GET /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v} → scorecard). The promotion gate reads it. A guided spec (metadata.labels.guided: <template>) runs the checks of its template with its thresholds. All other specs run the full catalog.

Metric Measured on r_hat_max, ess_bulk_min The free parameters of the production posterior (the convergence diagnostics of the plugin) divergence_rate sample_stats.diverging, as a share of all draws mape, coverage_90 The holdout, through the score path. They must be in evaluate.metrics. metrics.json gives mape in percent (1.4 is 1.4%). The check compares it as a fraction (0.014 against 0.10/0.25) accuracy_lift Choice models: the holdout hit rate minus the hit rate of a guess that is always the most common product of the holdout. A hit is when the most probable product is the product bought (accuracy, accuracy_naive). The customer_choice template evaluates them negative_roi_share, roi_max The response_curves grid at the actual spend. For each channel: the share of draws with a negative return, and the largest posterior-mean ROI max_channel_share, baseline_share The share of a channel (or of the baseline) in the baseline plus all channels, posterior mean prior_overlap_max The overlap of the prior and posterior draws of the media parameters of the model (PyMCModel.prior_overlap_vars, forward-sampled at fit time, at a low cost) missing_fraction The numeric variables of the raw dataset history_years The time dim of the model stage, in years. This is its periods divided by the periods in a year at the frequency of the dim (or the frequency of its dates). Thus 105 days and 15 weeks both count as about 0.3 years spend_cv_min The raw spend for each channel over time

If the runner cannot measure a check, the check is in skipped with the reason. Examples are no holdout split, no response curves, or a model that is not MCMC. Each item has these fields:

  • message_plain.
  • message_expert: What the runner measured, and on which parameter or channel.
  • suggested_action, if the item is not a pass.
  • docs_anchor: A link back to the catalog.

docs.title: What-if grids and "Run exact"
docs.text:
Fits with response_curves write ui/grids/response_curves.json. For each thinned draw, channel and spend multiplier, the file has the total contribution of the channel over the fit window, in KPI units. The number of draws is a maximum of outputs.ui_draws, and never more than 500. The file also has these items:

  • The spend at each grid point.
  • The actual spend.
  • The baseline (intercepts and controls).
  • The grids for each geo, if they are in the size cap.

The sliders interpolate the grid for each draw (the contract).

"Run exact" compiles the scenario into a counterfactual score request. The request has one multiply intervention for each changed channel. At grid points, the two results agree for each draw to float precision. The reason is that the grid comes from the same fitted curves. Also, linear preprocessing does not change the multiplier. packages/runner/tests/test_guided.py checks this.

docs.title: Future covariates
docs.text:
A forecast needs the future values of its covariates, for example spend and prices. Guided forecasts do not ask for an upload. ScoreRequest.future_covariates tells how the runner extends the covariates that the payload does not have. It does this for each series, from the fitted history. The server gives the fit dataset of the model to the score run as its history input:

Policy Future values supplied (default for API callers) From the data or the scenario of the request. Missing values get MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE carry_last (default in Guided mode) The last observed value of each series seasonal_naive The value one year before, by date (52 weeks, 12 months, 365 days, and so on). Thus the last observed year repeats, also after a gap. If a value is missing, the runner goes back one more year. If the value is missing in all years, or the history is shorter than one year, the runner uses carry_last with a warning zero Zero: "no spend planned"

The runner never replaces values that the payload gives. Interventions apply after the fill. Thus budget × k over a horizon scales the carried-forward spend. The issues of the score result tell which values the runner filled.

docs.title: Forecast and counterfactual views
docs.text:
A forecast score run writes ui/guided/forecast.json (mapi.forecast/v1). The file has these items:

  • The actual KPI over the fitted history (fan.observed).
  • The forecast quantiles after split_at (fan.values). The run adds the geos together for each draw before it calculates the quantiles.
  • The KPI total over the horizon.

Its core.ppc_fan plot shows the history and the dashed split line.

A counterfactual score run writes ui/guided/counterfactual.json (mapi.counterfactual/v1). An example is a preset from mapi_spec.whatif.counterfactual_request, such as channel off or budget × k. The file has these items:

  • The totals of the scenario, the baseline and the change.
  • The change as a share of the baseline.
  • A band of the change for each period.

The scenario and the baseline share their noise (common random numbers). Thus the change is precise, also when the totals are uncertain.

The two views exist only for models with outputs that are posterior draws. The platform cannot add other representations across geos.

docs.title: Your first analysis in Guided mode v0.4
docs.text:
Guided mode takes you from a spreadsheet to a trustworthy answer. You do not write YAML, and you do not need to know statistics. You select what you want to learn. You answer some questions about your columns, and you tell what you already believe. Then the platform fits a model in a secure sandbox and tells you what it found in plain words. Each screen uses the same ModelSpec that Expert mode edits. See Guided mode for the concepts.

This tutorial shows a geo marketing mix: weekly revenue and media spend for each market. The tutorial takes about ten minutes. If you do not have your own data, use the sample in the repository, apps/web/e2e/fixtures/guided-geo-mmm.csv. The sample has 40 weeks, two markets, spend for TV, search and social, and an average price. The screenshots come from the web app in mock mode (pnpm --filter @mapi/web dev:mock). Thus the numbers are only examples.

Every step has its own address

The app saves an analysis immediately when you upload its data. Each step has its own URL (/guided/<analysis>/<step>). Thus you can bookmark the step or send it to a colleague. You can also close the browser during a fit. Later, you can continue from Guided → Continue where you left off.

docs.title: 1. Choose what you want to learn
docs.text:
If you signed up for the workspace, the workspace opens on this page. In other workspaces, use one of these methods:

  • Set the header to Guided. The app remembers the choice for your account.
  • Open Guided in the sidebar.
  • Click Start a guided analysis on Home.

Each card is a template. The card shows the question that the template answers, the data that it needs, and what you can do with the result.

Template Use it for Geo marketing mix What each channel adds to your results for each market, ROI for each channel, what-if budgets Weekly forecast One weekly or daily series, forecast with a probable range Demand by store Units for each store and week from prices and promotions, with low and high estimates Customer choice Which product shoppers select on each trip, and how prices change the choice

Select Geo marketing mix.

docs.title: 2. Your data
docs.text:
1. Give the analysis a name.
  2. Drop your file on the page (CSV or Parquet).

Your browser reads the file first. The page profiles each column: the type, the range, and how frequently the dates repeat. It sends only that profile to the platform. The platform suggests which column answers each question. The app does not upload the file until you click Upload and continue.

  • Each question shows the suggested column, how sure the suggestion is, and why. An example reason is "named like a revenue column; never negative". Change each answer that is wrong. The app does not show a column again if a different question already uses it.
  • The preview on the right gives each column a label with its role. It draws a small line for each series that you selected, added up for each week. Thus you can quickly see a column of zeros or a broken week.
  • The app recognises MFF long tables (Period, Geography, VariableName, VariableValue, as mmm-framework uses them) automatically. It also recognises Google Meridian tables (time, geo, kpi, <channel>_spend). It fills in the answers from their standard names.
  • The app opens Parquet files only in the sandbox. Thus, for Parquet files, you type the column names.
  • More options has the settings that most persons never change. An example is the number of latest weeks to keep back to test the model.

When all the necessary questions have an answer, the panel shows Everything the model needs is answered.

Then click Upload and continue. The app makes the dataset and uploads the file to storage. It starts the sandboxed check of the data and saves the analysis.

docs.title: 3. What you believe
docs.text:
You can already know something about your channels, from earlier studies, industry benchmarks or experiments. If you do, tell it on this step. All the items on this step are optional.

  • Return on spend or Share of results: Use one of these to describe each channel. A range of 1.5 to 4 means "each euro spent brings back between 1.5 and 4 euros". How sure? sets how strictly the model keeps to the range.
  • Channels start unticked. Without a belief, only the data decides. To give a channel a range, tick it. The range starts from a wide, sensible range.
  • Results without any media (optional) is the share of results that would occur without media.
  • Experiments you have run take lift tests or geo holdouts. For each experiment, give the channel and the market, the dates, the change in spend, and the measured change in results with its uncertainty. The model uses each experiment as extra evidence.

Preview what this means runs a quick simulation in the sandbox. It shows what your beliefs mean before a fit:

  • The range that the model now believes for each channel that you ticked. The shaded bar is the range that you gave.
  • The results that the model expects, week by week.

A sentence for each channel tells how much of the belief of the model is in your range. The preview gives the names of the unticked channels below the charts, but does not draw them. The model starts them from a default that is wide on purpose. This default is not a belief. If the expected results are far from your usual numbers, a belief is probably wrong.

Save and continue keeps the beliefs in the analysis. If you previewed exactly these beliefs, the fit uses the same translation again. If not, the fit translates them itself.

docs.title: 4. Fit the model
docs.text:
Click Fit the model. The page monitors the run live. It shows what occurs in plain words, a progress bar, the approximate time that is left, and a Cancel button.

First, the platform fits the model without the latest weeks. Thus it measures how well the model forecasts weeks that it did not see. Then it fits the model again on all the data. You can go away from the page, and the fit continues. Technical details opens the run in Expert mode.

docs.title: 5. Results and the sanity scorecard
docs.text:
• Headline numbers: These are:
    • How much of your results media caused.
    • The channel with the best return.
    • The forecast error on the weeks that the fit kept back.
    • How many weeks were in the 90% range. If this is near 90%, the ranges are honest.
  • Per channel: Spend, return for each 1 spent, and share of results. The bold number is the best estimate. The bracket and the bar show where the true value is, with 90% probability.
  • Charts: The model against your actual results. Also, how much each channel adds when its spend increases. The dot is your actual spend.

The sanity scorecard puts its checks into groups by the question that they answer:

  • Did the model settle?
  • Does it forecast well?
  • Are the numbers believable?
  • Is the data sufficiently good?

Each check is Pass, Check or Fail. It tells what it found in plain words. If it is not a pass, it tells what to do.

Inspect in Expert mode opens the diagnostics of the model, so that you can look more closely. Guided mode lists the checks and their thresholds.

A check under Did the model settle? can show Check or Fail. In this case, the page shows Fit again, more carefully. This button fits the same data and beliefs with longer and more careful sampling. The fit takes about two times as long. Usually, this repairs those checks. Guided mode hides the settings that the button changes. Thus the button is the only way to change them in Guided mode. In a project that is locked to Guided mode, a project admin must click the button.

docs.title: 6. What if…
docs.text:
• Change the budget: Move the slider of a channel to spend more or less over the same period. The change in results updates while you move the slider. It shows the range of probable outcomes. Your browser calculates the answer from response curves that the fit calculated before, for each posterior draw. Thus the range stays honest when many channels move at the same time.
  • Run exact asks the full model the same question, with a real score run. It shows its answer below the instant answer. The two answers must be near.
  • Quick scenarios: What occurs if a channel is off, or if all the budgets change by a percentage.
  • Forecast: How the results can develop over the next weeks (or days, for daily data), if you continue as in the latest weeks. A mark shows the split between history and forecast. A weekly forecast goes only as far as the horizon that you gave at setup. For a longer forecast, you need a new fit with a longer horizon.

The sliders cover the range that the fit calculated before: from zero to three times your spend.

docs.title: 7. Share
docs.text:
• Put the model live gives other tools a stable address (an endpoint) to ask the model questions. Before you click the button, the page tells you about the promotion gate:

    • A model that passed all its checks goes live immediately.
    • A model with checks to look at needs a project admin. The admin approves it with a short reason. The audit log keeps the reason.
    • A model with a failed check cannot go live.

    See Integrations.

  • Share a chart makes a read-only link to one chart, for a slide, a Notion page or a dashboard. The app shows the link one time. The link expires, and you can revoke it. You can share only charts that the platform drew itself (Embed a chart).

  • When the model is live, Code for this endpoint opens its page in the Integrations hub on the Snippets tab. The tab has code for Google Sheets, Python, a notebook cell and more. Create a token for it makes a key that can score only this endpoint. Connect Google Sheets uses the two. You can revoke the chart link later under Plots and links.
  • Open the Integrations hub for spreadsheets, BI tools, scheduled exports and webhooks. In a project that is locked to Guided mode, the hub stays in the navigation.

docs.title: View as YAML and Expert mode
docs.text:
Each step has View as YAML. It shows the specification that your answers made, as read-only text. Edit in Expert opens the specification in the Expert editor. In this editor, you can change all the settings. The Back to Guided mode link in the editor takes you back to Guided mode. Your changes stay as they are. The analysis shows Advanced settings applied and lists the changes.

Projects locked to Guided mode

A project admin can lock a project to Guided mode. Then members below admin see only Guided screens. They see no Expert switch and no Expert pages in the navigation. They can change only the basic settings, their answers and their beliefs. See the persona lock.

docs.title: On a phone
docs.text: All Guided screens work on a phone. The steps collapse to "Step 4 of 6" with a progress bar. The panels show one above the other.

docs.title: What happens behind the screens
docs.text:
Step Calls Templates GET /v1/guided/templates Your data POST /v1/guided/detect-roles, POST /v1/guided/drafts, then POST /v1/datasets, the upload, POST /v1/datasets/{id}/versions and POST /v1/specs What you believe POST /v1/guided/prior-translations (preview), POST /v1/specs/{id}/revisions Fit POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/runs/{id}/events (live progress), POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel Results GET /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v} (scorecard, metrics), its plots and ui/grids/response_curves.json What if… POST /v1/guided/requests:compile, then POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score Share PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}, POST /v1/plots, POST /v1/plots/{id}/embeds

From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft and Guided modelling make the same calls with curl.

docs.title: The HTTP API v0.2
docs.text:
All the actions of the web app, the CLI and the Python client are calls to the versioned /v1 HTTP API. This guide does the main flow with curl and jq. Thus you can see each request. The script is docs/snippets/http_tour.sh. make e2e runs it against a live stack. The outputs below come from one of those runs, and are shorter.

Where What HTTP API reference Conventions, errors, pagination, idempotency, SSE and all the endpoints with their DTOs OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, which you can browse, with all the schemas and examples GET /openapi.json on a running API The same document, from the API Error codes All the stable error codes and their HTTP status

First, start the stack and load the demo (see the quickstart):

  1. Run make dev.
  2. Run make seed.
  3. Run uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/.
  4. Run uv run mapi datasets upload demo/eu_media_future.zarr.zip --name eu_media_future.

From v0.3, make dev needs sign-in. Set MAPI_TOKEN to an API token. You get the token from the Tokens page of the web app, or from mapi tokens create. Set MAPI_PROJECT to the <tenant>/<project> for the token. The api function of the script then adds Authorization: Bearer … and X-Mapi-Project to each API call. It never sends them to signed storage URLs, because these URLs have their own authorization. See authentication.

docs.title: Health and the catalog
docs.text:
API=${MAPI_API_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:8000}
api() {  # curl the API; signed in when MAPI_TOKEN is set (every multi-tenant stack, v0.3)
  if [ -n "${MAPI_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" \
      -H "X-Mapi-Project: ${MAPI_PROJECT:-default/default}" "$@"
  else
    curl -s "$@"
  fi
}
curl -s "$API/readyz" | jq -c '{status, version, checks: .checks | map_values(.status)}'
api "$API/v1/catalog/models" \
  | jq -r '.items[].manifest | "\(.id)@\(.version)  \(.capabilities.representation)"'

{"status":"ok","version":"0.7.0","checks":{"postgres":"ok","object_store":"ok","catalog":"ok"}}
mmm.bayesian@1.0.0  draws
mmm.frequentist@1.0.0  draws
sklearn.tabular_bootstrap@1.0.0  draws
…
ts.hsgp_trend@1.0.0  draws

/healthz tells if the process is alive. /readyz checks PostgreSQL, the object store and the catalog. If one of them is not ready, it answers 503 with the same body. The catalog is what the runner image supplies. A sandboxed describe run exports it. The server validates specs against the catalog.

docs.title: Upload a CSV
docs.text:
Data never goes through the API. Do these steps:

  1. Make a dataset.
  2. Ask for an upload session.
  3. PUT the bytes to the signed URL that the session gives.
DS=$(api "$API/v1/datasets?limit=200" | jq -r '.items[] | select(.name == "weekly_sales") | .id')
if [ -z "$DS" ]; then
  DS=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"name": "weekly_sales", "description": "a CSV upload from the HTTP guide"}' | jq -r .id)
fi
echo "dataset $DS"
printf 'week,sales\n2026-01-04,120\n2026-01-11,131\n2026-01-18,127\n2026-01-25,140\n' > sales.csv
SIZE=$(wc -c < sales.csv | tr -d ' ')
UP=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/uploads" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"filename\": \"sales.csv\", \"content_type\": \"text/csv\", \"size_bytes\": $SIZE}")
HEADERS=()  # the signed URL binds these headers: send them exactly
while IFS= read -r h; do HEADERS+=(-H "$h"); done \
  < <(jq -r '.upload.headers | to_entries[] | "\(.key): \(.value)"' <<<"$UP")
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'PUT %{http_code}\n' -X PUT "${HEADERS[@]}" \
  --data-binary @sales.csv "$(jq -r .upload.url <<<"$UP")"

dataset ds_01m4zy65cdbxtaa4vgsvpeb4rt
PUT 200

The URL is a V4-style signed URL for one object in the quarantine bucket. It is valid for one hour. Send the headers from upload.headers exactly, because they are part of the signature:

  • content-type must be the type that you declared.
  • x-goog-content-length-range limits the size to size_bytes.
  • x-goog-if-generation-match: 0 makes the object write-once. Thus the storage refuses a second PUT to the same URL.

Then change the upload into a dataset version. For CSV and Parquet, the mapping gives the column of each dim and variable. It also gives its kind, its score-time policy and its role:

MAPPING='{
  "format": "csv",
  "dims": {"week": {"column": "week", "spec": {"kind": "time", "policy": "extend", "freq": "W-SUN"}}},
  "vars": {"sales": {"column": "sales", "role": "target", "units": "units"}}
}'
DV=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"upload_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$UP"), \"mapping\": $MAPPING}")
V=$(jq -r .version <<<"$DV")
STATUS=ingesting
while [ "$STATUS" = ingesting ]; do  # a sandboxed ingest run parses and checks the file
  sleep 1
  STATUS=$(api "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq -r '.status // "ingesting"')
done
api "$API/v1/datasets/$DS/versions/$V" | jq '{ref, status, dims: .data_schema.dims | keys}'

{
  "ref": "dataset://default/weekly_sales@v1",
  "status": "ready",
  "dims": ["week"]
}

POST …/versions answers 202 with the version in status ingesting. The answer also has the id of the sandboxed ingest run that parses the file. The call accepts an Idempotency-Key. If you send the request again with the same key and body, you get the same version. The platform does not ingest the file two times.

docs.title: Validate and fit a spec
docs.text:
jq -Rs '{yaml: .}' demo/eu-geo-mmm.yaml \
  | api -X POST "$API/v1/specs:validate" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- \
  | jq '{valid, issues: [.issues[] | {code, pointer}], stages: [.stages[] | .name]}'

{
  "valid": true,
  "issues": [],
  "stages": ["raw", "to_eur", "weekly", "scale_spend", "scale_y", "lags", "season", "hols"]
}

POST /v1/specs:validate answers 200, also for a spec that is not valid. The result is in valid. Each problem is in issues with its code and JSON pointer. The server uses non-2xx statuses only for requests that it cannot validate. Examples are YAML that it cannot parse, or a request that is too large.

SPEC=$(api "$API/v1/specs?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
RUN=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/runs" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d "{\"kind\": \"fit\", \"spec_id\": $(jq .id <<<"$SPEC"), \"revision\": $(jq .latest_revision <<<"$SPEC")}" \
  | jq -r .id)
echo "run $RUN"

POST /v1/runs answers 201 with the run in state created or queued. If you send the same Idempotency-Key with the same body, the answer is 200 with the same run. If you send it with a different body, the answer is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Make one key for each user intent. Use the same key again when you try again.

docs.title: Follow the run
docs.text:
# server-sent events: a snapshot, the persisted events, live progress, then `end`
api -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "$API/v1/runs/$RUN/events" | grep '^event:' | uniq -c
api "$API/v1/runs/$RUN" | jq '{state, output_model_version_id}'

   3 event: snapshot
   1 event: state
   1 event: warning
   2 event: state
   6 event: progress
   1 event: state
   5 event: diagnostic
   3 event: metric
   1 event: state
   1 event: complete
   1 event: state
   2 event: snapshot
   1 event: end
{
  "state": "succeeded",
  "output_model_version_id": "mv_01m4zy6yc82qy97jzjmv9phv1j"
}

With Accept: text/event-stream, the events endpoint is a live stream. It sends these items:

  1. A snapshot of the run.
  2. The persisted events. Each event has an id:.
  3. Live progress and log frames. These have no id, and the server never sends them again.
  4. A new snapshot at each change of state.
  5. end when the run is terminal. Then the server closes the stream.

To continue exactly after the last persisted event, connect again with Last-Event-ID: <id>. Without that Accept header, the same URL gives the persisted events as a JSON page. See Run events.

docs.title: Read the model version
docs.text:
MODEL=$(api "$API/v1/models?limit=200" | jq -c '.items[] | select(.name == "eu-geo-mmm")')
M=$(jq -r .id <<<"$MODEL")
MV=$(jq -r .latest_version <<<"$MODEL")
api "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV" \
  | jq '{ref, scorecard: .scorecard.overall, metrics, signed: .manifest.signature.alg}'

{
  "ref": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
  "scorecard": "warn",
  "metrics": {"mape": 7.59, "elpd_loo": 183.47, "coverage_90": 0.875},
  "signed": "KMS-EC-P256-SHA256"
}

GET …/artifacts/{name} gives a signed GET URL for a bundle object or a ui/ view. The server makes the link only after it verifies the signed manifest of the version. Each link is pinned to an object generation. It supports HTTP Range requests and expires after 15 minutes.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
RES=$(api -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Prefer: wait=60' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"request": {
        "apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
        "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest",
        "mode": "forecast",
        "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest",
        "side_tables": {"fx": "dataset://default/fx_daily@latest"}}}')
jq '{done, state: .run.state, outputs: [.outputs[] | {name, size, crc32c}]}' <<<"$RES"
curl -s "$(jq -r '.outputs[] | select(.name == "result.json") | .url' <<<"$RES")" \
  | jq '{mode, representation, output_space}'

{
  "done": true,
  "state": "succeeded",
  "outputs": [
    {"name": "plots.json", "size": 4122, "crc32c": "d8PGZA=="},
    {"name": "result.json", "size": 406, "crc32c": "PonvmQ=="},
    {"name": "score.zarr.zip", "size": 9396, "crc32c": "Uwymhw=="},
    {"name": "ui/summary.arrow", "size": 27266, "crc32c": "hxiS8w=="}
  ]
}
{
  "mode": "forecast",
  "representation": "draws",
  "output_space": {"contributions": "weekly", "y_hat": "weekly"}
}

Prefer: wait=60 keeps the request open until the score run finishes, for a maximum of 60 seconds. Then it answers 200 with done: true and signed links to the outputs. If the run takes more time, the answer is 202 with done: false. In this case, do one of these steps:

  • To get the result of the same run, send the request again with the same Idempotency-Key.
  • Follow the run.

The response header Preference-Applied tells which wait the server used. Over HTTP, the ScoreRequest needs its apiVersion and kind. The Python client fills them in.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
api -X POST "$API/v1/models/$M/versions/$MV:score" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"request": {"apiVersion": "mapi/v1", "kind": "ScoreRequest",
       "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@latest", "mode": "filter",
       "data": "dataset://default/eu_media_future@latest"}}' | jq '{status, code, detail}'

{
  "status": 422,
  "code": "MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED",
  "detail": "validation failed with 2 errors; first at /mode: model 'mmm.bayesian@1.0.0' does not support mode 'filter'"
}

Each error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json). It has a stable code, an HTTP status, and each individual problem in errors[] with a JSON pointer. Tracebacks and plugin messages show only in an untrusted_text field. Render them as text. The server refused the score request above statically. It did not make a run.

docs.title: Other clients
docs.text: The server makes the OpenAPI document itself. apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py writes apps/web/openapi.json, and CI fails if the file and the server do not agree. Thus all OpenAPI generators can make a typed client. The TypeScript client of the web app comes from this method (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch). For Python, use mapi_client.

docs.title: The Integrations hub v0.4
docs.text:
Integrations in the sidebar of the web app (G then I) is where a fitted model goes out of the platform. For example, a spreadsheet scores the model, a dashboard embeds its chart, or your pipeline gets a message when a fit is ready. Each action on these pages is one or two calls of the HTTP API. Integrations tells the concepts: the promotion gate, signed webhooks, and embed links only for platform recipes. Endpoints and webhooks does the same tasks with curl.

The hub has four tabs:

  • Overview: The Guided cards and the entry points for developers.
  • Endpoints.
  • Webhooks.
  • Plots and links.

The last step of Guided mode, Share, goes to the hub. If you make an endpoint or a chart link in that step, the hub lists it immediately. Its Code for this endpoint button opens the snippets of the endpoint. In a project that is locked to Guided mode, the hub stays in the navigation.

docs.title: Overview: connect in a few steps
docs.text:
Three cards cover the usual cases. You do not need to read API documentation:

Card What you get You need Google Sheets The Apps Script that scores an endpoint from a sheet, with the steps to install it. The script reads the rows of a sheet with the name Input, or it uses the example call. The Input sheet has a header row with the dims and inputs of the endpoint, and one row for each coordinate. For a forecast, it has your actuals and the dates to forecast, with the target empty. The card shows a preview. The script writes the summary of the answer (mean and 90% interval for each coordinate) to a sheet with the name Result. Above the summary, it writes a note that tells the conditions of the forecast An endpoint. A token from Create a token. This token can only score that endpoint BI dashboard A read-only embed link that expires, for Looker Studio, Power BI or Notion. Slack shows a link as a card without the chart. For Slack, post the PNG A saved plot of a platform recipe Webhook A signed call to your URL when a model is ready or a run fails The project admin role

Below the cards, For developers has links to these items:

  • The endpoints.
  • Scoped tokens.
  • The interactive API documentation of the server (/docs).
  • The OpenAPI 3.1 document of the server (/openapi.json).

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text: The Endpoints tab lists the endpoints of the project. For each endpoint, it shows the alias, the model version that it serves and its revision. It also shows the gate that it passed and the date of the promotion. To open the page of an endpoint, click it.

docs.title: Promoting through the gate
docs.text:
Only project admins can promote.

  1. Click Promote a model.
  2. Type the name of the endpoint, and select a model and a version. The dialog shows the sanity scorecard of the version and the expected gate.
  3. Click Promote. The server decides:

The gate says The dialog What to do Passes The endpoint page opens on the new revision - Needs an override (409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED) The reasons, each with its check (holdout.mape), and an Override reason field A project admin who is signed in to the app writes the reason and clicks Override and promote. The audit log records the override as endpoint.promote_override. An API token cannot override Blocked (409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED) The reasons. No override The cause is a scorecard that fails, a fit that stopped, a train_only fit or an input change that breaks callers. Repair the cause and promote a new version

The server also checks two things that the app cannot see:

  • The version was fitted again on all the data after its holdout evaluation.
  • Its input contract still agrees with what callers send.

Thus an expected Passes can still come back blocked. Description and evaluation policy sets the EvaluationPolicy of the endpoint. With it, you can accept exploration fits. You can also block, warn about or allow changes to the input contract. If a different person promoted the endpoint while the dialog was open, the server refuses the old revision. The dialog tells you this.

docs.title: An endpoint's page
docs.text:
• Version and history: This shows these items:

    • The version that serves now, with a link to its model page.
    • The person who promoted it, and how.
    • The reasons of the gate.
    • Each promotion and rollback with its reason.

    Roll back goes back to the version of the previous revision. Roll back here goes back to an earlier revision. The two buttons ask for a reason, and the audit log records it. A rollback does not run the gate again, because that version passed it before. Delete endpoint needs you to type the alias. Integrations that call a deleted endpoint get 404.

  • Schema and Try it: This shows the input contract from the time of the promotion. The contract has the score modes, the dim that a forecast extends, and the dimensions and variables. It also shows the example call. To try your own call, edit the call first.

    • Validate runs the static checks of the server (POST …/validate).
    • Score does a real score run (POST …/score with Prefer: wait=30). It needs the runner role.

    A forecasting endpoint also has Your latest actuals and the dates to forecast. This is its input table: the time column, the target and the drivers. The periods after the fit are rows. To use it, do these steps:

    1. Fill the target where you have actuals.
    2. Leave the target empty on the dates to forecast. Use Add a period or Paste from a spreadsheet.
    3. Click Use in the call.

    After Score, a note above the first summary tables tells the conditions of the forecast. Examples are Conditioned on 3 actuals through 1961-03-01 and From the end of the fitted history (Forecasts with actuals).

  • Snippets: Code that is ready to run for Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script and Notebook. Notebook is a Jupyter or marimo cell that returns an xarray.Dataset. The server makes the code with the example call. The app shows and copies the code exactly as the server wrote it. Each snippet tells what to install first. Snippets never contain a secret. They read the token from MAPI_TOKEN.

Token for this endpoint opens the New token dialog of the Tokens page. Create a score:… token on the Snippets tab opens the same dialog. The dialog is filled for a score:<alias> token. This token can read and score that endpoint and nothing more. Its initial limit is 120 requests each minute.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
The Webhooks tab is for project admins. Other users see why the tab is empty. The tab lists each webhook with its events, its status and its last delivery. New webhook asks for an https URL, a description and the events to send. The platform refuses URLs on private or internal addresses (WEBHOOK_URL_BLOCKED). It tells you this below the URL field.

The app shows the signing secret one time, immediately after you make the webhook. Copy the secret into the configuration of your receiver. The Done button of the dialog stays disabled until you copy the secret, or tick that you stored it. The dialog also shows the lines of code that verify the Mapi-Signature of a delivery.

The page of a webhook has these items:

  • Settings: Enable or disable the webhook, and change its events. Rotate secret makes a new secret. The app shows the new secret one time. The old secret continues to sign for 24 hours.

  • Delivery log: Each try, newest first. For each try, the log shows the event and its status (Delivered, Retrying, Failed, Blocked, Pending). It also shows the try number, the response code of your receiver and the duration.
