Read the output as the planning module intends. The plan protects the cautious result (the 10th percentile). Thus, its expected revenue is a little less than the current revenue. The plan is better than the current plan in only 48% of the draws. On this model, money that moves from search to TV gives insurance, not growth. The next euro returns about the same (2.9) in the two channels. Thus, the current split is already almost efficient.

The frontier is the more useful answer. Up to about 1 million EUR, each extra euro returns 2.8 or more. Above 1.13 million, the return decreases to 1.2 and then to 0.4. The notes (on standard error) tell which solver ran and why. With --objective mean, the same request maximises the expected revenue.

A workflow can do all these steps on a schedule. The mmm_governed gallery template fits mmm.bayesian on a geo panel. It runs the policy with submit: true and keeps the evidence pack (mapi workflows init mmm_governed).

docs.title: The frequentist model
docs.text:
mmm.frequentist uses the same data and settings (but no priors, likelihood or GP trend). mmm-framework finds the adstock and saturation with an out-of-sample (rolling-origin) criterion, and then fixes them. It solves the model, which is now linear, by ridge regression with channel effects that are not negative. Then it solves the model again on block-bootstrap samples. These replicates are the "draws" of all outputs. Thus, the ranges are confidence intervals.

This model has no convergence diagnostics, business priors or lift tests. The seed sets its results, and it fits in seconds.

model:
  use: mmm.frequentist@^1
  settings:
    hierarchy: {pool_over: [geo]}
    adstock: {kind: geometric, l_max: 6}
    saturation: {kind: logistic}
    bootstrap: 200
    search_budget: 200
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, seed: 7}

estimator: constrained (a convex program) needs the optional cvxpy dependency of mmm-framework. The images of the platform do not install it. Thus, the fit fails with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED.

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• The platform does not give these mmm-framework features: the multiplicative (log-log) specification, effects that change with time, price and promotion levers, events and interactions between channels. The forward pass of the platform is for the additive model only.
  • The mmm_extensions of mmm-framework (nested/mediated models and models with many outcomes) are not available yet. mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate have About cards but no plugin.
  • Fits run on the CPU. Only the NumPyro backend uses JAX.

docs.title: Trust, but verify
docs.text:
The two models pass the SDK contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model). The kit tests these items:

  • Bundle round trips.
  • Shuffled markets and subsets of markets.
  • New levels.
  • Typed errors for gaps and for periods before the data.
  • A holdout that the plugin scores through the same path as a forecast.
  • Additive contributions.
  • The plots.

The conformance corpus fits these specs from start to end: e33 (a geo panel with a GBP market, side tables and a weekly plan), guided_mmm (business priors and a lift test) and mmm_frequentist. A recovery test fits simulated data with known contributions. It makes sure that the split of the contributions across channels is correct.

docs.title: statsmodels time-series models
docs.text:
The mapi-plugin-statsmodels package adds twelve classical time-series models from statsmodels (BSD-3-Clause) to the platform. These are the model groups:

  • The usual forecast models (ARIMA, exponential smoothing, theta).
  • Models with drivers (ARIMAX, ARDL, error correction).
  • Systems of series that have an effect on each other (VAR, VECM, VARMAX, dynamic factors).
  • Regime switching.

All of these models fit in seconds. They run in the time-series runner image (mapi/base-forecast). They pass the same contract kit as all other plugins.

docs.title: Which model should I use?
docs.text:
Each model has an About card in the catalog. Help me choose in the web app, mapi choose and api.catalog.recommend() rank the models for your goal and data (see Choosing a model). This table gives a short summary:

Plugin In plain words Choose it when ts.sarimax Forecast with past values and drivers You forecast one series a few periods ahead and know the future prices, promotions or holidays ts.arima Forecast from past values You have only the series itself ts.ets Exponential smoothing forecast You need a fast, robust baseline with trend and season ts.theta Simple strong baseline You want a simple model that is difficult to beat, to compare other models with ts.unobserved_components Trend, season and noise You want to see the underlying trend without the noise ts.ardl Effects that increase over time The effect of a driver spreads over many periods ts.ecm Long-run and short-run effects The result and its drivers have the same trend. You want the immediate effect and the lasting effect. ts.var Series that have an effect on each other Many series have an effect on each other. You want shocks and Granger tests. ts.vecm Series that stay tied together Series with a trend keep a stable long-run relation ts.varmax Series that have an effect on each other, with drivers Like VAR, with outside drivers that you know ahead ts.dynamic_factor Common movements across many series Many series follow a few hidden common forces ts.markov_switching Changes between regimes The behaviour jumps between different modes (normal / with promotions)

Is the series ready? If you are not sure, use the time-series readiness workflow template. It does these steps:

  1. It runs the unit-root tests.
  2. It selects the differencing and the AR/MA orders.
  3. It does a backtest of ts.sarimax against a naive forecast.
  4. It keeps ts.sarimax only if it wins.

See Workflows.

docs.title: Your data, in the model's names
docs.text:
The models use canonical names. Bind the names of your dataset to them in data.bind:

Canonical name What it is t The time index: dates (default) or period numbers (settings.time_kind: integer). Policy extend: forecasts continue it. y The target. Univariate models: y(t), or y(<series...>, t) for panels. Multivariate models: y(variable, t). variable Multivariate models only: the series that the model uses together (realgdp, realcons, ...). <series...> Panel dims that you name in settings.series_dims (geo, product). The plugin fits one model for each series. <exog...> Drivers that you name in settings.exog, as (<series...>, t). Forecasts need their future values.

A table with one column for each series (realgdp, realcons, realinv) becomes y(variable, t) with the wide variables of the ingest mapping. See From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft.

Panels are a per-series loop

With series_dims: [geo], each geo gets its own model, with its own orders, parameters and residual checks. Geos are a fixed dim. The platform refuses a forecast for a geo that the model did not see, with UNSEEN_LEVELS. Multivariate models do the same loop. For example, there is one joint VAR for each geo.

docs.title: An ARIMAX per geo
docs.text:
from mapi_plugin_statsmodels.datasets import sales_dataset, sales_schema
from mapi_sdk.harness import fit_spec, score_bundle
from mapi_spec import load_score_request

SPEC = """
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {name: weekly-sales-arimax, project: retail}
data:
  dataset: dataset://retail/weekly_sales@latest
  bind:
    dims: {t: date}            # the model's time dim is called t
    vars: {y: sales}           # ... and its target y
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 8}
model:
  use: ts.sarimax@^1
  settings:
    order: [1, 0, 0]           # one past value (AR 1), no differencing, no MA term
    exog: [price, promo]       # drivers you know ahead
    series_dims: [geo]         # one model per geo
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, seed: 1}
evaluate: {metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_90]}
"""

history = sales_dataset(periods=104, geos=["north", "south"], seed=0)
bundle = fit_spec(SPEC, history, raw_schema=sales_schema(geo=True))
print(bundle.metrics.values)  # holdout metrics of the evaluation fit
params = bundle.model.groups["params"]
print(params["estimate"].sel(param=["price", "promo"]).round(2).values)
# [[-7.96 11.62] [-7.32 12.18]] - per geo, close to the true -8 and +12

The params group of the bundle is the parameter table. For each parameter of each series, it gives the estimate, standard error, z/t statistic, p-value and 95% interval.

docs.title: Forecasts and the drivers' future
docs.text:
plan = sales_dataset(periods=112, geos=["north", "south"], seed=0).isel(date=slice(104, None))
request = load_score_request("""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://retail/weekly-sales-arimax
mode: forecast
horizon: {dim: t, periods: 8}
output: {summary: [median, q5, q95]}
""")
forecast = score_bundle(bundle, request, plan.drop_vars("sales"))
print(forecast["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sel(geo="north").round(1).values)
# rows median, q5, q95 - the 90% prediction interval around the median

For all models, a score gives these results:

  • In the fitted range: the one-step-ahead predictions of the model from the fitted history. The model does not use the targets and drivers of the payload there. The only exception is a forecast with actuals (see below).
  • After the fitted range: a multi-step forecast from the end of the fit, with the drivers in the payload. If a driver or a value of a driver is missing, the score fails with MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE (422). With future_covariates: carry_last, seasonal_naive or zero, the platform extends the drivers that you do not give (see Forecasting).

A what-if on the future is another payload. Change the planned drivers, for example a promotion each week or a 5% price increase. Then forecast again.

The outputs are quantiles (y_hat(quantile, ..., t), with the representation quantiles). The default quantiles are 2.5%, 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 95% and 97.5%. Thus, you get the median and the 50/80/90/95% bands. settings.quantiles changes them, but the outputs always include 5%, 50% and 95%.

The quantiles are prediction intervals for the two output kinds. They include the noise of the next value, because statsmodels has no separate interval for the expected value. Each quantile is for one cell. Thus, the platform refuses totals across geos or series (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED). To get a total, add the series in the pipeline and model the total.

The plugin does not give the score modes counterfactual, simulate and filter (MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED). To update a forecast with new data, use a forecast with actuals.

docs.title: Forecasting from new actuals
docs.text:
All statsmodels models can move their forecast origin forward without a new fit (capabilities.conditions_on_actuals). The rules are on Forecasts with actuals. Send the periods that came after the fit, with their target values and drivers. Then send the periods to forecast, with an empty target:

import json

# Weeks 105-108 arrived for north, 105-106 for south: send them with the weeks to forecast
# (sales left empty) and the planned drivers. Nothing is refitted.
latest = sales_dataset(periods=112, geos=["north", "south"], seed=0).isel(date=slice(104, None))
weeks = latest["date"].values
latest["sales"].loc[{"geo": "north", "date": weeks[4:]}] = float("nan")
latest["sales"].loc[{"geo": "south", "date": weeks[2:]}] = float("nan")
updated = score_bundle(bundle, request, latest)
print(json.loads(updated.attrs["conditioning"])["message"])
# Forecast updated with 6 actuals (2024-12-29 to 2025-01-19) across 2 of 2 series after the
# fitted history, which ends 2024-12-22; the model's parameters were not re-estimated. ...
north = updated["summary"].to_dataset()["y_hat"].sel(geo="north")
print(north.sel(date=weeks[4:]).round(1).values)  # the forecast from north's last actual

A univariate model updates each series with its own actuals. Thus, the series of a panel can end at different dates. The answer includes all the periods that you sent. It gives one-step-ahead predictions on the actuals, and the forecast after the last actual of each series. Actuals for periods in the fitted range replace the fitted values (revised data).

The fitted parameters never change. The fitted noise variance, and thus the width of the bands, also never changes. This table shows how each model uses the new data:

Model Updated with the actuals by ts.sarimax, ts.arima, ts.unobserved_components, ts.varmax, ts.dynamic_factor the Kalman filter with the fitted parameters over the history and the actuals. This is statsmodels' results.append(new, refit=False). Differencing and seasonal differencing are part of the model. Thus, actuals and forecasts are in the units of the data. The filter uses empty periods in the actuals as missing values (the univariate state-space models accept missing targets). ts.ets the exponential-smoothing recursions with the fitted smoothing weights and initial states ts.theta the fitted SES weight (or IMA(1,1) filter with use_mle), drift and seasonal indices ts.ardl, ts.ecm the fitted equation on the lags of the result and the drivers that you supply (apply(refit=False); the ECM uses its levels ARDL) ts.var, ts.vecm the fitted equations on the lags that you supply (levels for the VECM). The deterministic trend continues. ts.markov_switching the Hamilton filter with the fitted parameters. The regime probabilities after the last actual start the forecast.

Joint models of series (ts.var, ts.vecm, ts.varmax, ts.dynamic_factor) need a value of each series for each period with actuals after the fit. If not, the score fails with ACTUALS_INVALID. The platform applies the preprocessing steps of the spec (for example a core.log1p or a standardisation) to the actuals before the update. It reverses them on the forecast, as for all payloads.

A transform.log, transform.box_cox or transform.difference of a workflow is not such a step. A model that you fit on its output refuses actuals (see Forecasts with actuals). Use the differencing of the model (order d, seasonal D) instead. Fit the model again from time to time, so that the parameters learn from the new data.

docs.title: The models
docs.text:
Each section starts with the About card of the model. The web app, mapi about and api.catalog.about() show this card. A docs test makes sure that the quotes are the same as the catalog. Then each section gives a minimal spec. For models with drivers, it also gives a forecast from planned drivers.

All the specs use this small wrapper. The wrapper has the data binding and a holdout of the last 8 periods. The plugin scores the holdout before it fits the model again on all the data. The specs use synthetic or public data from mapi_plugin_statsmodels.datasets. The documentation tests run each spec (docs/snippets/statsmodels_catalog.py):

from mapi_plugin_statsmodels.datasets import (
    ECM_SCHEMA,
    GROWTH_SCHEMA,
    MACRO_SCHEMA,
    REGIME_SCHEMA,
    ecm_dataset,
    macro_dataset,
    macro_growth,
    regime_dataset,
    sales_dataset,
    sales_schema,
)
from mapi_sdk.harness import fit_spec, score_bundle
from mapi_spec import load_score_request


def spec(model: str, bind: str = "{dims: {t: date}, vars: {y: sales}}") -> str:
    """A complete ModelSpec around a ``model:`` block: the data binding and a holdout of the
    last 8 periods, scored before the model is refitted on everything."""
    return f"""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ModelSpec
metadata: {{name: example, project: growth}}
data:
  dataset: dataset://growth/example@latest
  bind: {bind}
  split: {{kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 8}}
model:
{model}
  fit: {{mode: evaluate_then_refit, seed: 1}}
evaluate: {{metrics: [rmse, mape, coverage_90]}}
"""


def forecast(bundle, future, periods: int = 8):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    """Forecast ``periods`` ahead from planned drivers (the future rows of ``future``)."""
    request = load_score_request(f"""
apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: ScoreRequest
model: endpoint://growth/example
mode: forecast
horizon: {{dim: t, periods: {periods}}}
output: {{summary: [median, q5, q95]}}
""")
    return score_bundle(bundle, request, future)["summary"].to_dataset()


weekly = sales_dataset(periods=112, seed=0)  # sales(date) with price and promo
history, plan = weekly.isel(date=slice(0, 104)), weekly.isel(date=slice(104, None))
panel = sales_dataset(periods=104, geos=["north", "south"], seed=1)  # sales(geo, date)

docs.title: ts.sarimax - forecast with past values and drivers
docs.text:
Forecasts a series from its recent past, its seasonal pattern and outside drivers that you know in advance, such as planned prices or holidays.

Use it when you forecast one regular series a few periods ahead, and known future drivers (prices, promotions, holidays) are important. Use a different model when you have less than about 50 periods, or when many series have an effect on each other (use ts.var).

SARIMAX = """
  use: ts.sarimax@^1
  settings:
    order: [1, 0, 0]          # AR(1) errors, no differencing, no MA term
    exog: [price, promo]      # drivers you know ahead
"""
sarimax = fit_spec(spec(SARIMAX), history, raw_schema=sales_schema())
fan = forecast(sarimax, plan.drop_vars("sales"))  # next 8 weeks from the planned price/promo
print(fan["y_hat"].sel(stat="median").round(1).values)

This is seasonal ARIMA with drivers, that is, a regression with ARIMA errors. The Kalman filter estimates it by exact maximum likelihood. Missing target values are permitted (the filter skips them). The forecast needs the planned future values of the drivers (here plan without sales). If one is missing, the forecast fails with MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE. The exception is when the request tells how to extend the driver.

Setting Default Meaning order [1, 0, 0] (p, d, q): past values, times differenced, past errors seasonal_order [0, 0, 0, 0] (P, D, Q, s) for a pattern that repeats each s periods trend auto n, c, t, ct. auto is a constant, unless the series is differenced. exog [] drivers series_dims [] panel dims: one model for each series

Are you not sure about order? The readiness workflow selects it from unit-root tests and a search on an information criterion. It keeps the model only if it is better than a naive forecast.

docs.title: ts.arima - forecast from past values
docs.text:
Forecasts a series from its recent past and trend, without outside drivers.

Use it when you have only the series itself and want a solid, well-known method. Use a different model when outside drivers explain most of the movement (use ts.sarimax).

ARIMA = """
  use: ts.arima@^1
  settings: {order: [1, 1, 1], series_dims: [geo]}   # one ARIMA(1,1,1) per geo
"""
arima = fit_spec(spec(ARIMA), panel, raw_schema=sales_schema(geo=True))

This is the same estimator as ts.sarimax, without drivers. Here, there is one ARIMA(1,1,1) for each geo of a panel. ts.arima refuses a constant together with differencing (use trend: t for a drift).

docs.title: ts.ets - exponential smoothing
docs.text:
Forecasts a series and gives recent values more weight than older values. It has an optional trend and seasonality, and it is quick and robust.

Use it when you need a fast, reliable baseline, and the level, trend and season change slowly. Use a different model when outside drivers explain most of the movement.

ETS = """
  use: ts.ets@^1
  settings: {trend: add, damped_trend: true}
"""
ets = fit_spec(spec(ETS), history, raw_schema=sales_schema())  # drivers are not used

This is the error-trend-season model (ETSModel): error, trend (add/mul), damped_trend, and seasonal with seasonal_periods. Additive models have closed-form intervals. The plugin simulates the intervals of multiplicative models (simulate_repetitions paths). The seed of the request sets the paths. Thus, the same request gives the same quantiles.

docs.title: ts.theta - a simple, strong baseline
docs.text:
Forecasts a series with a combination of a straight-line trend and smoothed recent values. This simple method is hard to beat.

Use it when you want a strong, simple baseline to compare other models against. Use a different model when outside drivers are very important, or when you need detailed explanations.

THETA = """
  use: ts.theta@^1
  settings: {series_dims: [geo]}
"""
theta = fit_spec(spec(THETA), panel, raw_schema=sales_schema(geo=True))

This is the theta method with optional seasonal adjustment (period, deseasonalize, method, theta). It is the benchmark to beat in a forecast bake-off.

docs.title: ts.unobserved_components - trend, season and noise
docs.text:
Divides a series into a level and a trend that change slowly, a seasonal pattern and noise. It forecasts the series from these parts.

Use it when you want to see the underlying trend without the noise, and the trend and season change slowly. Use a different model when you only need a quick baseline.

UC = """
  use: ts.unobserved_components@^1
  settings: {level: local linear trend, exog: [price]}
"""
uc = fit_spec(spec(UC), history, raw_schema=sales_schema())
print(sorted(uc.model.groups["components"].data_vars))  # the smoothed level, trend, ...
uc_fan = forecast(uc, plan.drop_vars("sales"))

This is a structural model. It has a level (local level, local linear trend, smooth trend, ...), and optional stochastic seasonal, cycle, autoregressive noise and drivers. The components group of the bundle keeps the smoothed level, trend and season. The decomposition of the Model Explorer shows them. With drivers, forecasts need the planned values of the drivers.

docs.title: ts.ardl - effects that build up over time
docs.text:
Explains a series from its past and from the current and past values of drivers. You can see how an effect increases over several periods.

Use it when the effect of a driver spreads over many periods. Use a different model when the effects are only immediate (a simple regression is sufficient).

ARDL = """
  use: ts.ardl@^1
  settings: {lags: 2, order: 2, exog: [price, promo]}   # or auto: true to choose them
"""
ardl = fit_spec(spec(ARDL), history, raw_schema=sales_schema())
ardl_fan = forecast(ardl, plan.drop_vars("sales"))

This model uses least squares on lags of the result and on order lags of each driver. With auto: true, the plugin selects them for each series by ic, up to those maximum values. The parameter table shows the effect of each lag. Thus, you can see how a price change has an effect over the subsequent weeks.

docs.title: ts.ecm - long-run and short-run effects
docs.text:
Separates the short-term effect of a driver from its long-term effect on one series. It also tests if a long-run relationship exists.

Use it when one result and some drivers have the same trend, and you want the immediate effect and the lasting effect of a driver. Use a different model when the result and the drivers have no trend.

ECM = """
  use: ts.ecm@^1
  settings: {lags: 1, order: 1, exog: [income]}
"""
monthly = ecm_dataset(periods=126, seed=4)  # sales tied to income in the long run
ecm = fit_spec(
    spec(ECM, "{dims: {t: month}, vars: {y: sales}}"),
    monthly.isel(month=slice(0, 120)),
    raw_schema=ECM_SCHEMA,
)
group = ecm.model.groups["ecm"]  # speed of adjustment, half-life, the bounds test
print(round(float(group["half_life"]), 1), float(group["bounds_p_upper"]) < 0.05)
ecm_fan = forecast(ecm, monthly.isel(month=slice(120, None)).drop_vars("sales"), periods=6)

This is the same model in error-correction form (statsmodels UECM):

  • The coefficient on y.L1 is the speed of adjustment. Its half-life is in the ecm group.
  • The long_run.* rows of the parameter table are the long-run effects, with delta-method standard errors.
  • The Pesaran-Shin-Smith bounds test tells if a long-run relation exists. The trend sets the case (c is case 3). The result is levels_relationship, none or inconclusive. The scorecard also shows it as a diagnostic (ECM_BOUNDS_TEST).

docs.title: ts.var - series that drive each other
docs.text:
Models two or more series that change each other over time, such as the prices and sales of two brands. It forecasts them together.

Use it when many series move together and have an effect on each other, and you want to see how a shock to one series spreads to the others. Use a different model when you have one series, or when the series stay tied together in the long run (use ts.vecm).

VAR = """
  use: ts.var@^1
  settings: {max_lags: 4, ic: aic}     # the lag order chosen by AIC
"""
MACRO_BIND = "{dims: {t: quarter, variable: series}, vars: {y: value}}"
var = fit_spec(spec(VAR, MACRO_BIND), macro_growth(quarters=120), raw_schema=GROWTH_SCHEMA)
print(sorted(var.model.groups))  # ... fevd, granger, irf, params, residuals ...

This model uses least squares. To select the order by ic up to max_lags, do not give a value for lags. The data has the series along one dimension (y(variable, t)). The bundle contains these items:

  • Orthogonalised impulse responses with asymptotic 95% bands (irf).
  • The forecast-error variance decomposition (fevd).
  • Granger causality tests for each pair of series (granger).

docs.title: ts.vecm - series tied together for good
docs.text:
Models series that wander but stay tied together in the long run, such as the prices of close substitutes. It shows how fast they go back after a gap opens.

Use it when the series have a trend but keep a stable long-run relation. Use a different model when the series have no trend, or when a long-run relation is not plausible.

VECM = """
  use: ts.vecm@^1
  settings: {k_ar_diff: 2, deterministic: ci}   # the rank from the Johansen test
"""
vecm = fit_spec(spec(VECM, MACRO_BIND), macro_dataset(quarters=160), raw_schema=MACRO_SCHEMA)
print(int(vecm.model.groups["cointegration"]["rank"]))

This is a Johansen VECM. If you do not give a value for coint_rank, the Johansen rank_test (trace or max-eigenvalue) at rank_signif selects it. The plugin refuses some ranks with a SETTINGS_INVALID in plain language:

  • A rank of 0. There is no long-run relation. Model the changes with ts.var.
  • A rank that is equal to the number of series. The series are stationary. Use ts.var on the levels.

The cointegration group has the Johansen table, the rank, alpha (speed of adjustment) and beta (the long-run relations, normalised on the first series). The VAR/VECM recipe selects one of the two models for you.

docs.title: ts.varmax - series that drive each other, with drivers
docs.text:
Models two or more series that change each other and also respond to outside drivers that you know in advance. It forecasts them together.

Use it when many series have an effect on each other, and outside drivers are also important. Use a different model when you have one series, or many series and a short history.

VARMAX = """
  use: ts.varmax@^1
  settings: {order: [1, 0]}            # VARX(1): q = 0
"""
varmax = fit_spec(spec(VARMAX, MACRO_BIND), macro_growth(quarters=90), raw_schema=GROWTH_SCHEMA)

This is VARMA(p, q) with drivers in state-space form (VARX when q = 0). As with ts.sarimax, the exog drivers need their planned values for a forecast.

docs.title: ts.dynamic_factor - common movements across many series
docs.text:
Finds a few hidden forces that move many series together, such as the general economy behind the sales in many categories.

Use it when you have many related series and want their shared drivers. Use a different model when you have one or two series.

DFM = """
  use: ts.dynamic_factor@^1
  settings: {k_factors: 1}
"""
dfm = fit_spec(spec(DFM, MACRO_BIND), macro_growth(quarters=90), raw_schema=GROWTH_SCHEMA)
print(sorted(dfm.model.groups["factors"].data_vars))

In this state-space model, some hidden factors follow a VAR and drive many series. The factors group has the smoothed factors and loadings. Standardise the series first (core.standardize), because factor models assume comparable scales.

docs.title: ts.markov_switching - switching between regimes
docs.text:
Finds if a series changes between regimes, such as periods of high growth and low growth. It estimates the behaviour in each regime.

Use it when the behaviour jumps between different modes, and you want the probability of each mode now. Use a different model when the changes are gradual, or when you have a short history.

MARKOV = """
  use: ts.markov_switching@^1
  settings: {k_regimes: 2, time_kind: integer}   # weeks numbered 0, 1, 2, ...
"""
regimes = regime_dataset(periods=150, seed=3).drop_vars("regime")
markov = fit_spec(
    spec(MARKOV, "{dims: {t: week}, vars: {y: demand}}"), regimes, raw_schema=REGIME_SCHEMA
)
print(markov.model.groups["regimes"]["mean_level"].round(1).values)  # about 10 and 16

This is the regime-switching regression of Hamilton (order: 0) or autoregression (order > 0). The level, the driver effects and the noise can change between k_regimes hidden regimes. The regimes group has these items:

  • The smoothed and filtered probability of each regime for each period.
  • The transition matrix.
  • The expected durations.
  • The mean level of each regime.

Forecasts are mixtures of regimes. They are analytic for regressions. For autoregressions, they are simulated (simulations seeded paths). The start values come from a fit on the standardised series. This prevents the failures of the default start values of statsmodels on series that are far from zero.

docs.title: Forecasting through an endpoint, the client and the CLI
docs.text:
After you promote a version, you can get the same forecast from the endpoint. Send the plan of the drivers inline (an xr.Dataset with the future rows):

from mapi_client import Client

api = Client()
fan = api.endpoint("weekly-sales").score(plan_ds, mode="forecast", horizon={"dim": "t", "periods": 8})
print(fan["y_hat"].sel(stat="median").values)

mapi endpoints score weekly-sales --data plan.json --periods 8 -o forecast.zarr.zip
mapi explore model model://growth/weekly-sales@v3 -s forecast -s residuals --horizon 8

docs.title: What is stored, and why there is no pickle
docs.text:
The plugin never keeps a statsmodels results object, because pickles cannot cross the sandbox boundary. A bundle keeps these items:

  • The training data at the model stage (observed_data, and the drivers in constant_data).
  • All estimated parameters (params), with the order that the model needs in learned.
  • Fit statistics (fit_stats: AIC, BIC, HQIC, log-likelihood, observations, noise variance, and if the optimiser converged), residuals and residual tests (Ljung-Box, Jarque-Bera, ARCH-LM).
  • The groups for each model that the sections above give.

When you score, the plugin makes the results again:

  • State-space models (SARIMAX, ARIMA, UnobservedComponents, VARMAX, DynamicFactor) and the ETS and Markov-switching models apply the stored parameters to the stored data. They use their own filter (model.filter(params), smooth(params)).
  • Least-squares and closed-form models (VAR, VECM, ARDL/ECM, Theta) estimate again on the stored data with the stored orders. The plugin compares the result with the stored parameters. If they are different, the score fails with INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

docs.title: The Model Explorer
docs.text:
StatsmodelsModel.explorer_views(fitted) changes a bundle into sections of the Model Explorer (mapi_spec.views DTOs):

  • params: the table with 95% intervals and p-values.
  • diagnostics: fit statistics, and Granger, Johansen and bounds tests.
  • residuals: the residuals over time, their autocorrelation, Q-Q points and the residual tests for each series.
  • irf, fevd and decomposition.

Panels show as facets. views.forecast_view(predictions, observed=...) changes the quantiles of a forecast score run into the forecast section. There is one fan for each series (with the recent history), because you cannot add quantiles of different series into one fan.

docs.title: How it is tested
docs.text:
• The contract kit (check_model) passes for each plugin, with About cards necessary.
  • Parameters, in-sample predictions and forecast intervals are equal to direct statsmodels calls on the same data. This is true for SARIMAX, ARIMA, UnobservedComponents, ETS, Theta, ARDL, UECM, VAR, VECM, VARMAX, DynamicFactor and Markov switching. A test also does a check of the UECM on the Danish money-demand data of Johansen and Juselius. The VAR(2) on US macro growth gives the same coefficient table as the statsmodels documentation.
  • Forecasts with actuals are equal to statsmodels with the fitted parameters on the extended data. The tests use results.append(new, refit=False) for the state-space models and ARDL. They also use the VAR/VECM forecast on the supplied lags, the fixed-parameter ETS smoother, theta and the Hamilton filter. For each model, the last values of the fit as actuals give the plain forecast again. A jump in these values changes the forecast. A model from the ts_readiness_arimax workflow forecasts from new monthly actuals in the original units.
  • The conformance fixtures sm_arimax (an ARIMAX panel with drivers) and sm_vecm_macro (a VECM on the public-domain macrodata of statsmodels) run the full path: fit, score and evaluate. See Conformance corpus.

docs.title: Deployment v0.3
docs.text:
You can run the whole platform on one machine in two ways. The two ways start the same services on the same ports. Because of this, the URLs, the CLI, the Python client and the tests work with the two ways. v0.3 adds Google Cloud, with Terraform for each project and scripts that deploy, migrate and roll back. All three ways run the same multi-tenant code. Only the executor, the store and the identity provider change.

Local, without Docker Docker Compose Google Cloud (v0.3) Command make dev make docker-build && make compose-up deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env ENV PostgreSQL embedded (pgserver) or your DATABASE_URL the official postgres:16 image Cloud SQL Object storage the GCS shim, in .local/gcs the GCS shim image, in a volume Cloud Storage Runs execute as mapi-runner subprocesses of the worker subprocesses of the worker container, or one container for each run Cloud Run Jobs, one new sandbox for each run Code your working tree, with hot reload the container images the same images Sign-in the development IdP the development IdP Google or another OpenID provider Use it for development, demos, the end-to-end tests a full check of the production images a multi-tenant private beta: start with the [verify M0] checklist 
flowchart LR
    browser(("browser")) -->|":5173"| web["web app"]
    browser -->|":5174"| plots["plot sandbox<br/>(separate origin)"]
    browser -->|":8000 /v1"| api
    browser -->|":4443 signed URLs"| shim
    cli["mapi CLI ·<br/>Python client"] -->|"/v1"| api
    api["api<br/>(mapi-server api)"] --> pg[("PostgreSQL")]
    api --> shim["GCS shim"]
    worker["worker<br/>(dispatcher · reconciler ·<br/>finalizer · events)"] --> pg
    worker --> shim
    worker -->|"starts"| runner["mapi-runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    runner -->|"signed URLs only"| shim

These items apply to the two local ways:

  • Sign-in is for development only. The two local ways run the servers in the dev profile. Each person who can get access to the API can sign in as one of the seeded accounts, through the built-in identity provider. MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant turns sign-in off. The API listens on 127.0.0.1, and compose publishes each port on 127.0.0.1 only. Do not connect a local stack to networks that you do not trust. Refer to the security model.
  • State is the database and the object store. Make a backup of the two. Locally, they are in .local/pg and .local/gcs. Under compose, they are the pgdata and gcsdata volumes. Also make a backup of the bundle signing key (.local/keys/) if you want to download the model versions that you have now.
  • Migrations run first. make dev and compose both run mapi-server migrate before the API and the worker start. If the migration fails, they stop.

docs.text:

  • Docker Compose: the compose stack, its network layout and how to select the executor.
  • Container images: the six images, how the build makes them, and the checks that keep them correct.
  • Deploying to Google Cloud: the [verify M0] checklist, then the Terraform and deploy scripts, step by step, until you have the first tenant.
  • Security hardening on Google Cloud: what each control does, and the M0 verification checklist.
  • Authentication and isolation: sign-in, API tokens, operators, row-level security and Pub/Sub push.
  • Cloud Run Jobs executor: the v0.3 execution backend.
  • Observability: metrics, logs, traces, and the dashboards, alerts and runbooks in ops/.
  • Security suite: the sandbox-escape probes and the actions that each isolation level must stop.
  • M2 verification: the M2 exit criteria that we verified without a cloud project, the measured numbers, and the steps that a real project still needs.
  • M3 verification: the Guided journey and the integrations through the live stack, the times and fixes from testers without help, and the protocol for the five testers.
  • M3.5 verification: workflows, governance, the explorers, mmm-framework and Help me choose through the live stack, the defects that we found and repaired, and how to run the journeys again.
  • Configuration reference: all the environment variables.
  • Troubleshooting: port conflicts and all other problems.

docs.title: Authentication and tenant isolation v0.3
docs.text: This page is for the person who operates mapi-server. The concepts (roles, scopes, project selection) are in Tenancy and authentication. Each variable on this page is in the configuration reference.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
MAPI_PROFILE Who can call the API Sign-in single-tenant (default) All persons who can get access to the API (it listens on loopback). Requests without credentials act as the local administrator of the default tenant. Sessions and API tokens also work Optional multi-tenant Only callers with a browser session or an API token. All other requests get 401 MAPI_OIDC_* dev The same as multi-tenant The built-in development IdP (below)

These rules apply in all profiles:

  • The server does a check of each request against the rule of the operation in mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS. A route without a rule cannot start.
  • The server reads the roles of the caller from the memberships at that moment.
  • Each database query of a request runs in a transaction that is pinned to the tenant of the request (row-level security, below).

docs.title: Browser sign-in (BFF)
docs.text:
The web app never sees an OAuth token. The API does the OpenID Connect work:

  1. GET /auth/login?return_to=/runs keeps a login transaction (state, nonce and PKCE verifier) on the server. It sets a __Host-mapi_login cookie for 10 minutes. Then it redirects to the provider (Authorization Code flow, PKCE S256, nonce).

  2. GET /auth/callback uses the transaction one time only. It compares state in constant time and exchanges the code with the verifier. Then it verifies the ID token against the JWKS of the provider. It verifies these items:

    • The signature. Only asymmetric algorithms are permitted, and alg must agree with the key.
    • The issuer, the audience (and azp), the expiry, the issue time and the nonce.

    The server keeps the keys in a cache for one hour. If a token names a key id that the server does not know (rotation), the server gets the keys again. 3. The server finds the user by (issuer, subject). At the first sign-in with a verified e-mail, the user gets the pending invitations for that address. An e-mail that is not verified gets no invitations. 4. The server starts a session on the server and sets two cookies:

    Cookie Attributes Purpose __Host-mapi_session HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ The session (the server keeps only its SHA-256). 2 h idle, 12 h absolute __Host-mapi_csrf Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/ (the app can read it) The CSRF token

Without TLS, the cookies are mapi_session and mapi_csrf without Secure. This occurs with MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE=false, which is the default for http:// API URLs. Use this configuration only for local development.

CSRF. Each POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE that uses cookie authentication must send the token of the session in X-CSRF-Token. This includes logout. The token is in the mapi_csrf cookie, or in the X-CSRF-Token response header of GET /auth/session. The server also refuses requests with Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site. It also refuses requests whose Origin is not the web app or the API. API-token requests do not use cookie authentication, and they do not need a CSRF token.

GET /auth/session tells if the browser is signed in. POST /auth/logout stops the session. If a sign-in fails, the server sends 401 with a general message. The reason is in the audit log (auth.login_failed).

docs.title: Google sign-in
docs.text:
1. In the Google Cloud console, make an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Set the authorized redirect URI to https://<api host>/auth/callback.

  2. Configure the API:

    MAPI_PROFILE=multi-tenant
MAPI_API_URL=https://api.mapi.example
MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER=https://accounts.google.com
MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=1234-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com
MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=...            # from Secret Manager, never in images
MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS=oncall@mapi.example

    Google ID tokens use the issuer https://accounts.google.com. Older tokens use accounts.google.com. The server accepts the two issuers. MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS='{"hd": "acme.com"}' selects a Workspace domain in the account chooser before the user selects. It is only a hint. The memberships control who can do which actions.

Other providers include Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0, and an Identity Platform tenant behind an OIDC-compliant provider. For these providers, set MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER to the issuer. The /.well-known/openid-configuration of the issuer must list an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint and a JWKS. The BFF does not accept the client-SDK tokens of Identity Platform yet. These tokens have the issuer securetoken.google.com/<project>, and you get them without an authorization-code endpoint.

docs.title: The development IdP (offline)
docs.text:
MAPI_PROFILE=dev mounts a small OpenID provider in the API at /dev/idp. Thus sign-in works without a network:

  • /auth/login redirects to /dev/idp/authorize. This page lists the accounts in MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS. The default accounts are admin@dev.local, analyst@dev.local and viewer@dev.local.
  • At start-up, the server invites these accounts. The first account becomes the admin of the default tenant and a platform operator. The second account becomes runner of the default project, and the other accounts become viewer.
  • The IdP signs its ID tokens with RS256 and a key that it makes at start-up. These tokens go through the same verification as the tokens of a real provider. The IdP enforces PKCE, and you can use each code only one time.

There are no passwords. Each person who can get access to a dev API can sign in as each listed account. The IdP does not mount in other profiles.

The CLI can also use the IdP (refer to The CLI). Its issuer is the identifier https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost. The API serves its discovery document:

mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost \
           --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp

docs.title: The CLI
docs.text:
mapi login signs in with the identity provider directly. It uses the authorization code flow with PKCE and a temporary listener on 127.0.0.1. Then it sends the ID token as Authorization: Bearer. The API accepts this bearer only when all of these conditions are true:

  • It is a JWT, not a mapi_ API token.
  • The configured issuer signed it (the server does a check against the JWKS of the issuer), and it is not expired.
  • Its audience is one of MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS (default mapi-cli). The server does not accept the client id of the BFF.

The caller is then the same user as in a browser session. At the first use, the user gets a pending invitation, in the same way as with /auth/callback. The CLI does not use a cookie. Thus it does not need a CSRF token, and GET /v1/me reports auth: session. To accept only API tokens, set MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS= (empty). Register the CLI with your provider as a public "installed app" client. The client needs a loopback redirect URI, PKCE and the openid email scopes.

docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Programs send Authorization: Bearer mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum>. The server mints a token for its caller in the selected project (POST /v1/tokens). The server shows the token one time only. The token acts as its owner, with the limits of its scopes, and it is bound to that project. These rules apply:

  • The server keeps only the HMAC-SHA256 of the token, with a pepper from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET. It compares in constant time. The checksum finds a typing error before the server looks in the database. No error message shows the value that the caller sent.
  • Tokens that are expired, revoked or orphaned (the owner is disabled) get 401. The audit log records a wrong secret for a known prefix, an expiry and a revocation as token.auth_failed. It records a maximum of five of these events for each token prefix in each minute. Each person who knows a prefix can cause them. An unknown prefix and a wrong secret get the same answer, the API token is invalid.
  • A disabled account stays disabled. If the user signs in again, the server refuses it with a general 401 and records auth.login_failed. Only an invitation becomes active at its first sign-in.
  • A token never has operator powers, also when its owner is an operator.
  • A token cannot mint tokens, with all scopes (also admin). A child token would not have the expiry, budget, rate limit and revocation of its parent. Thus POST /v1/tokens needs a signed-in session (mapi login or the browser).
  • Each token has a rate_limit_per_minute (RATE_LIMITED, Retry-After) and a budget of vCPU-seconds for each UTC day or month. These limits apply in addition to the quotas of the tenant.

Change the root secret only together with all tokens. When you change it, all the tokens that you have now stop working.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Users whose verified e-mail is in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS are platform operators. The server decides this for each request from the current configuration. Thus, when you remove an address, the change applies immediately for browser sessions and mapi login ID tokens. Nobody must sign in again. With a browser session, operators can use /v1/admin/* (tenants, quota policies, kill switches, executor health, the platform audit log). They can also read the metadata of all tenants: tenants, members, token lists, runs and usage.

No role, flag or token lets operators read datasets, specs, models or plots. The audit log records each change and each refused attempt at an operator endpoint.

docs.title: Row-level security
docs.text:
mapi-server migrate makes three roles for the full cluster. It turns on FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY for each table that holds tenant data. The policy is fail-closed, on current_setting('app.tenant_id', false):

Role Used by Row-level security mapi_app Request handlers (one transaction for each request, pinned with set_config('app.tenant_id', <tenant>, true)) Applies: the role sees and writes only the rows of that tenant. It owns no table mapi_gateway The look-ups that the API and the events service do before they know the tenant: authentication (which token is this, which tenants this user is a member of), the administration of tenants and members, operator endpoints, and the routing of a pushed event to the tenant of its run Applies, with explicit policies: tenants, projects, memberships, API tokens (read, and touch last_used_at) and audit events (read, append). Also some metadata columns of runs and cost_ledger (state, estimate, attempt, executor, amounts) for global quotas, the spend cap and executor health. No access to datasets, uploads, specs, models, plots, attempts, events or logs mapi_system Only the orchestrator: dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer, housekeeper (plan §9) BYPASSRLS if the login that migrates is a superuser, and also an explicit policy. Thus the role also works on managed Postgres and for logins that are members of it

Each API request runs its platform sessions as mapi_gateway, independently of what the handler does. In a cloud deployment, the API and events services cannot read the URL of the login of the orchestrator. Thus, if a handler makes an authorization error before it knows the tenant, row-level security still contains the error.

If a transaction does not pin a tenant, it fails closed. On a new connection, each query gives an error. On a pooled connection, the setting is empty and agrees with no row. To prove this, the test suite runs unscoped queries for two tenants over one pooled connection.

The audit log (audit_events) and the cost ledger (cost_ledger) are append-only. The runtime roles cannot UPDATE or DELETE them. A trigger refuses all changes to a row that is there now, for all users. Thus a bug or an injection cannot change the audit trail or the billing history of a tenant. Only the table owner can purge them (tenant deletion, retention). Before the purge, the owner must drop the *_append_only trigger.

With one DATABASE_URL (local development, the default Compose file), the two pools log in as the user that migrates. They select their role with the start-up option role=... (RESET ROLE goes back to that role). In production, give each pool its own login:

CREATE ROLE mapi_api LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_app;
CREATE ROLE mapi_api_gateway LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_gateway;
CREATE ROLE mapi_orchestrator LOGIN PASSWORD '...' IN ROLE mapi_system;

Then set MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL (API and worker), MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL (API) and MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL (only worker). After this, only mapi-server migrate and procrastinate need DATABASE_URL (the owner).

docs.title: Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
In the cloud, run events go to POST /internal/events from a Pub/Sub push subscription with OIDC authentication. To configure it, do these steps:

  1. Configure the subscription with a dedicated service account and the audience https://<api host>/internal/events.

  2. Set these variables:

    MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE=https://api.mapi.example/internal/events
MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=pubsub-push@mapi-prod-control.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# optional: only accept pushes from these subscriptions
MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS=projects/mapi-prod-control/subscriptions/mapi-run-events-push

Each push must have an ID token that Google signed (RS256, with a check against MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL). The token must agree with these conditions:

  • The issuer is Google.
  • The audience is the configured audience.
  • email is the service account, with email_verified: true.
  • The token is not expired.

A valid Google token for a different audience or account gets 403. If you set MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS, the envelope must also come from one of those subscriptions. Without these settings, the server needs MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN if it is set. A multi-tenant deployment with neither of the two refuses all pushes. The audit log records refused pushes as event.rejected.

docs.title: Cloud Run Jobs executor
docs.text:
The cloudrun-jobs executor runs each attempt as a new Cloud Run Jobs (gen2) execution. Each run gets a microVM, which the executor makes from a small, fixed set of Jobs. This executor is the primary backend of the hosted platform (v0.3).

Tested against fakes only

The executor, the Pub/Sub push endpoint, the KMS signer and the Cloud Storage driver use the real Google client libraries. But we tested them only against test doubles: an in-memory Cloud Run API (FakeCloudRun), local OIDC keys, a KMS double with local keys and a fake storage client. Items with the mark [verify M0] depend on Cloud Run behaviour that we must still confirm in a real project.

docs.title: Install and select it
docs.text:
pip install 'mapi-server[gcp]'      # google-cloud-run, -storage, -pubsub, -kms
export MAPI_EXECUTOR=cloudrun-jobs
export MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT=mapi-prod-exec-paid
export MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION=europe-west1

The orchestrator (mapi-server worker) authenticates with Application Default Credentials. On Cloud Run, these are the credentials of its own service account. The service account needs run.jobs.run, run.executions.get, run.executions.list, run.executions.cancel and run.tasks.list on the exec project. Use roles/run.developer, or a custom role with only these permissions.

docs.title: The Job inventory
docs.text:
Execution overrides can change only environment variables, the task count and the timeout. They can never change the image, CPU or memory. Thus the platform deploys one Job for each base image and resource class, and it selects one Job for each attempt:

S (2 vCPU, 8 GiB) M (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) L (8 vCPU, 32 GiB) base-bayes (mmm.*, tabular.*, ingest, describe) mapi-prod-base-bayes-s mapi-prod-base-bayes-m mapi-prod-base-bayes-l base-ml (sklearn.*) mapi-prod-base-ml-s mapi-prod-base-ml-m mapi-prod-base-ml-l base-forecast (ts.*) mapi-prod-base-forecast-s mapi-prod-base-forecast-m mapi-prod-base-forecast-l

The names use MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE (default mapi-{env}-{base}-{class}). The infrastructure must make exactly these Jobs. Each Job must have:

  • max-retries = 0 (the platform decides about retries).
  • The execution service account (get and delete on the bootstrap bucket, and no other permissions).
  • The static environment MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL=gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce}.
  • The deny-all network and the restricted Google APIs VIP.

XL runs are for the GKE executor (M6). The dispatcher refuses XL runs for cloudrun-jobs.

docs.title: What one attempt looks like
docs.text:
1. The dispatcher writes the intent row (run, attempt, nonce) and the bootstrap object bootstrap/<nonce>. The bootstrap object is the RunSpec with signed URLs and the HMAC key.

  2. The dispatcher calls jobs.run on the selected Job with only these overrides:

    • MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE.
    • taskCount.
    • The task timeout. This is the timeout of the run plus MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S. Thus the supervisor can flush checkpoints before the backstop.

    Nothing goes in args. 3. The metadata of the operation names the execution. The dispatcher keeps the execution name as the handle of the attempt, and it logs the operation name. 4. The supervisor reads and deletes its bootstrap object. It runs the worker and prints events with HMAC signatures. The events go from Cloud Logging to Pub/Sub to POST /internal/events. 5. The reconciler polls executions.get. After the execution is complete, it also polls tasks.list for the exit codes. If there are no events, the reconciler only marks the run stalled. The status from the executor decides if the run is alive.

Execution outcome Reported as Run outcome All tasks succeeded succeeded, exit 0 finalized after the complete event Supervisor exit 16 (checkpoints flushed) failed or cancelled, exit 16 finalized as partial Exit 137, or "memory limit exceeded" failed, exit 137 failed (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), retry with the next larger class Task timeout failed, exit 143 failed (TIMEOUT) Cancelled through executions.cancel cancelled cancelled, or partial if it flushed Execution not found unknown cancelled and confirmed gone, then retried as an infrastructure failure

docs.title: Orphans and duplicates
docs.text:
Cloud Run selects the execution names. Thus the nonce identifies an execution. The dispatcher can stop after jobs.run but before it keeps the handle. If this occurs, the reconciler calls adopt(nonce). It lists the recent executions of each Job in the inventory. Then it finds the MAPI_NONCE override in the execution template [verify M0].

If two executions have the same nonce, the reconciler keeps the oldest and cancels the others. A duplicate that starts finds no bootstrap object, because the first execution deleted it. The duplicate then stops and does no work.

A jobs.run call can fail in a way that is not clear, for example a timeout or a 5xx after the dispatcher sent the request. The dispatcher never retries this call without a check. The next submit of that nonce adopts first.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
jobs.run has a limit for each project and region (180 calls a minute [verify M0]). Each orchestrator keeps a token bucket at MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE (default 150). Divide the quota between the orchestrator replicas.

A 429 answer means that Cloud Run made nothing. The executor then does these steps:

  1. It puts all submitters into a shared cool-down. This is an exponential back-off from MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S. It is at least the Retry-After of the server, but never more than MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S.
  2. It counts the answer as an alarm. The alarm shows in these locations:
    • ALARM cloudrun-jobs: jobs.run answered 429 in the log.
    • throttled_last_hour in the executor health.
    • mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total{executor} at /metrics. The MapiJobsRun429 alert monitors this metric.
  3. It retries the same nonce.

After MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES answers in sequence, the run goes back to the queue for a new attempt. This does not use one of its MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES. Thus a large quantity of throttled calls makes runs late, but it never makes them fail.

While a dispatcher works through a batch, it extends the leases of the runs that it has not submitted yet. Thus the reconciler never takes a run whose submit is only slow. If one submit stops for more than ten lease lengths, the renewals stop. The leases then expire. The reconciler adopts what jobs.run made (by nonce), or it retries the attempt.

docs.title: Fan-out with taskCount
docs.text:
Homogeneous children of a fan-out parent can run as the tasks of one execution (RunSubmit.task_count). Homogeneous children have the same kind, class, base and timeout. Each task i does these actions:

  • It reads its own bootstrap object at a nonce. The nonce comes from the execution nonce and CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX (mapi_server.executors.tasks.task_nonce).
  • It gives numbers to its events from task_seq(i, 0). Thus the event dedupe keeps the events of all tasks.
  • It writes its outputs under .../a{n}/tasks/{i}/.

The execution succeeds only when all tasks succeed. A cancel stops all of them. Fan-out parents (Sweep, SBC, Backtest) come in v0.5. The executor side is ready.

docs.title: Events: authenticated Pub/Sub push
docs.text:
A Cloud Logging sink with the filter jsonPayload.mapi_event:* publishes the event lines of the supervisors to a topic. A push subscription with OIDC authentication sends them to POST /internal/events. Configure the expected token:

export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE=https://api.example.com/internal/events
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT=mapi-events-push@mapi-prod-control.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS=projects/mapi-prod-control/subscriptions/mapi-run-events-push

The server then does a check of each push in this sequence, before it reads the body:

  1. The RS256 signature of the bearer token, against the JWKS of Google. The server keeps the JWKS in a cache, as Cache-Control tells. An unknown key id causes a maximum of one new fetch each 30 s. If the JWKS is not available for a short time, the cached keys continue to work.
  2. The claims of the token. The issuer is Google, and the audience is ours. The push service account has a verified e-mail. The token is not expired (60 s leeway).
  3. The subscription name, against MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS.

If a check fails, the server answers 401/403, and Pub/Sub retries. Configure a dead-letter topic. The server then decodes the message: the base64 Cloud Logging entry, jsonPayload.mapi_event and the run.googleapis.com/execution_name label. The server verifies the HMAC of the event with the key of its attempt. It removes duplicates on (run, attempt, seq) and merges the event into the progress row of the run.

If an event is forged or replayed, the server acknowledges it (200) and changes nothing. It counts the event as a sandbox violation.

In the multi-tenant profile, the endpoint refuses all requests until you configure push authentication. For a local setup, you can set MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN instead.

docs.title: Bundle signatures with Cloud KMS
docs.text:
export MAPI_SIGNER=kms
export MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION=projects/mapi-prod-control/locations/europe-west1/keyRings/mapi/cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/2
export MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS=projects/.../cryptoKeys/bundles/cryptoKeyVersions/1

The server sends only the SHA-256 digest of a manifest to asymmetricSign (EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256 or RSA_SIGN_PSS_*_SHA256). It does a check of the response for verified_digest_crc32c, the key version name and signature_crc32c. It verifies the signature locally before it keeps it. At startup, the server loads the public keys of the active and trusted versions. Thus, before the server mints URLs, it verifies a manifest locally and never waits for KMS.

To rotate the key, do these steps:

  1. Make a new key version.
  2. Set MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION to the new version.
  3. Keep the old version in MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS until no model version that it signed is in use.

With Terraform, these settings are control.kms_key_version and control.kms_trusted_key_versions (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md).

docs.title: Cloud Storage
docs.text:
GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run(...) signs V4 URLs and POST policies through the IAM Credentials signBlob API. It uses a token that it refreshes (the control-plane service account). It signs create-only POST policies as an uploader account. This account can make objects, but it cannot delete them. GCS POST forms do not accept a generation precondition. Thus an account that cannot delete cannot overwrite.

The URLs are byte-identical to the URLs from the V4 signer of google-cloud-storage. The store does a check of each write against the CRC32C and MD5 that Cloud Storage calculated. Copies pin the source generation and compare the result. Refer to GCS shim.

docs.title: Executor conformance and load
docs.text:
An executor gets shared tiers only after it passes two suites. These are the executor conformance suite (mapi_spec.conformance_executor) and the security suite. The conformance suite has these cases:

  • Submit, and orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash.
  • Duplicate submit, and cancel during a run.
  • Timeout, and stalled-not-lost.
  • Confirmed cancel before retry, and checkpoint resume.
  • OOM classification and fan-out.
  • Generation verification and 429 back-off.
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py      # fake-cloudrun, local-process
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py -m docker   # needs a daemon
uv run pytest packages/server/tests/test_load_cloudrun.py -s           # 100 fits; prints metrics

Each case runs the real dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and finalizer. It does a check of the exact sequence of run states, which a database trigger records. The load test sends 100 concurrent fits through cloudrun-jobs over the fake backend. It has these conditions:

  • The outputs are on the GCS shim.
  • The events come as Pub/Sub pushes that are late and duplicated.
  • There are three 429 answers and two lost jobs.run responses.

At the default of 150 submits a minute, the test measures a p95 time-to-running of about 46 s. No run is lost, and each run has exactly one execution. Real Cloud Run cold starts add more time.

docs.title: The shared-tier gate
docs.text:
The code enforces the gate. The dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on an executor only when these two conditions are true:

  1. The caps of the executor permit it: an isolation of gVisor or higher, with egress and DNS enforced.
  2. A passing executor-conformance report and a passing security-suite report are on record. They must be for exactly the caps that the executor reports now. Neither report can be older than MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S. The default is 3 days, so the nightly suites keep the gate open.

A security-suite report is evidence of enforced egress and DNS only under one condition. The http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes must run, and the executor must stop them. A skipped probe is not evidence. Record results with PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence (only operators, with an audit record). Include the target of the suites:

curl -X PUT "$API/v1/admin/executors/cloudrun-jobs/evidence" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"target": {"executor": "cloudrun-jobs", "caps": <caps from GET /v1/admin/executors>,
                  "remote_control_api": true, "enforces_memory_limit": true},
       "conformance": <ConformanceReport>, "security": <mapi-security --json output>}'

Until you record the evidence, the dispatcher keeps verified and public runs in the queue. It never makes them fail because evidence is missing. GET /v1/admin/executors shows shared_tiers_enabled: false, with the reason in message. It also shows conformance_passed and security_passed.

The executor stays enabled for the trusted tiers. enabled and the disabled status are the switch of the operators (PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}, incident containment). They are never the switch of the evidence gate. Evidence for other caps does not count, for example after a change to the region list or to MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED. The gate does not apply to internal and self_hosted_trusted tenants.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT — Exec project that holds the Job inventory (necessary) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 Region of the inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} Rule for Job ids MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to base (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes Base for runs without a plugin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 Token bucket in front of jobs.run (maximum 180) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 Number of 429 answers in sequence before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 Exponential back-off after a 429 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + margin MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false The DNS response policy is verified for Jobs [verify M0]. verified and public tenants need the two settings, and also recorded evidence MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption looks MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT — Expected push token (set the two) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any Accepted subscriptions (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL Google's The source of the OIDC signing keys MAPI_SIGNER local local (PEM key file) or kms MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION, MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS — Active key versions and key versions that are still trusted

docs.title: Configuration reference v0.3
docs.text:
You configure each component with environment variables. Only three components read a config file: the CLI and the Python client (~/.config/mapi/config.toml), and Docker Compose (.env). This page lists each MAPI_* variable in the code base, in groups for the component that reads it. A test (conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py) looks for the variables in the source tree. If a variable is not on this page, the test fails.

Each docs build makes two tables from the code:

  • The server settings: each mapi-server field with its type and default.
  • The index of environment variables: each MAPI_* name in the code, the images, the Terraform and the deploy scripts. The index tells which files use the name, and which section below explains it.

New in v0.3

Sign-in and tenancy (MAPI_PROFILE, MAPI_OIDC_*, MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, MAPI_SERVER_SECRET, the two database roles), quotas and cost (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH, MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED), the Cloud Run Jobs executor (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_*), Cloud Storage and KMS (MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs, MAPI_SIGNER=kms), Pub/Sub push authentication and observability (MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN, MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT). On Google Cloud, Terraform sets them (the deployment contract).

The short version

For a local stack, you need only the four addresses, and only when a different process uses a port: MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN. Export the same values in each shell that runs make dev, make seed, make e2e, mapi or the Python client. Troubleshooting has an example.

docs.title: Topology (every component)
docs.text:
These variables come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev. This is the one contract that these components share: the API, worker, runner, GCS shim, make dev, make seed, the end-to-end tests and (through VITE_*) the web app. Thus all components agree about the location of each service.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_ENV local Environment name. The buckets are mapi-{env}-quarantine, -bootstrap, -runs, -bundles, -data DATABASE_URL (or MAPI_DATABASE_URL) unset A postgresql:// URL. If unset, make dev and mapi serve start an embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver) in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/pg MAPI_API_URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 The address where the API listens and where clients connect. make dev gets the host and port of the API from it MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT http://127.0.0.1:4443 The object store (the GCS shim). Signed URLs point here MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5173 The origin of the web app. The API and the shim permit it for CORS MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The origin of the plot sandbox. Must be different from MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN. All components refuse a configuration where they are equal MAPI_DATA_DIR .local Local state: pg/, gcs/ (objects and the keys of the shim), keys/ (the bundle-signing key), executions/, dev/

docs.title: mapi-server (API and worker)
docs.text:
mapi-server api, worker, migrate and dev read mapi_server.settings.Settings. Each field is the variable MAPI_<FIELD>. These are the variables in addition to the topology above:

Identity and API

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev (multi-tenant with the built-in development identity provider). The local-process executor refuses multi-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID, MAPI_PROJECT_ID default The tenant and project of the platform. They are the only tenant and project of a single-tenant installation. Platform runs, for example describe, are in them MAPI_API_HOST, MAPI_API_PORT 127.0.0.1, 8000 The bind address of mapi-server api when you start it without --host/--port MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS 127.0.0.1,localhost,api The Host header values that the API answers (comma-separated). The host of MAPI_API_URL is always permitted. * turns the check off. This is the DNS-rebinding guard of the unauthenticated M1 API MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES unset The addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of the API, comma-separated. Examples are the load balancer, the Cloud Run front end and the /v1/ proxy of the web container. For a request from one of these proxies, the client address is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop that is not a trusted proxy. The limits for each address (sign-up, verification, embed views), the Sybil same_ip check and the audit fingerprints use this address. none: clients connect directly, and the server ignores X-Forwarded-For. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile. make dev sets none for its multi-tenant stack MAPI_DEBUG false Put tracebacks into the untrusted_text of problem documents. Never use this in production MAPI_LOG_LEVEL info debug, info, warning or error MAPI_LOG_JSON true One JSON object for each log line (structlog, with trace_id/span_id and the context of the request, run and tenant). false gives a console format for persons MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve Prometheus metrics at GET /metrics (refer to Observability) MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset The bearer that a scraper must send on GET /metrics. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile, which refuses scrapes without it (the series contain tenant ids and spend) MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 Serve the GET /metrics of the worker (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer series) on this address. The same bearer rule as the API applies MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Make OpenTelemetry spans for requests, outgoing HTTP calls and runs MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset The OTLP/HTTP collector that gets the spans. The server also reads it from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT. If unset, the server makes spans but does not export them MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN unset If set (and Pub/Sub push authentication is not set), POST /internal/events needs this bearer token. A multi-tenant profile with neither refuses all pushes MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset Set the two to make POST /internal/events need an OIDC token that Google signed for the service account of the push subscription. Refer to Authentication and the Cloud Run settings below MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S 15 The seconds between : keepalive comments on event streams MAPI_SSE_POLL_S 5 The fallback poll of an event stream when no PostgreSQL NOTIFY comes MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S 60 How frequently an open event stream does a check of the credential of its caller again. Revoked tokens, ended sessions and lost access close the stream MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES 8 MiB The largest JSON sidecar (plots.json, diagnostics.json, …) that the control plane parses

MAPI_PROFILE means two things

Do not export a client profile name in a shell that starts make dev or mapi-server. The server refuses all values other than single-tenant, multi-tenant or dev. The CLI and the Python client read MAPI_PROFILE as the name of a config-file profile. The server reads it as the deployment profile.

Database

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE 10 Request-path connections for each process (and the same number of overflow connections) MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_POOL_SIZE 5 Platform-role connections for each process (the orchestrator) MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_POOL_SIZE 5 Gateway-role connections for each process (the API and events service) MAPI_DB_ECHO false Log each SQL statement MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL unset The dedicated login of the request-path role (row-level security applies). If unset: DATABASE_URL with the start-up option role=$MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL unset The dedicated login of the platform role. It is the only role that bypasses row-level security. The dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and housekeeper of the orchestrator use it. The API never needs it. If unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL unset The dedicated login of the gateway role. The API and events service use it for look-ups before they know the tenant (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, pushed events). Row-level security applies. If unset: DATABASE_URL with role=$MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE, MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE mapi_app, mapi_system, mapi_gateway The three runtime roles that mapi-server migrate makes and grants (refer to Authentication)

Authentication (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_AUTH_REQUIRED on, but not for single-tenant Make all routes that are not public need a session or API token. You cannot turn it off in a multi-tenant profile MAPI_SERVER_SECRET from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH The root secret of the API-token pepper, the audit fingerprints and the key that seals webhook secrets. All API and worker instances must share it. If you change it, all tokens and webhook secrets become invalid MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH server-secret next to the bundle-signing key The file that holds the root secret (0600). mapi-server migrate makes it. Compose keeps it on the keys volume MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE on when MAPI_API_URL is https Session cookies with the __Host- prefix and Secure. Off: mapi_session/mapi_csrf for development with plain HTTP MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER unset The OpenID provider (for example https://accounts.google.com). If unset outside the dev profile, browser sign-in is off, but tokens still work MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration The location of the metadata of the provider MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET unset The OAuth client that you registered for the BFF. The secret is optional for public clients. The server always uses PKCE MAPI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI $MAPI_API_URL/auth/callback The registered redirect URI MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS RS256,ES256 The ID-token algorithms that the server accepts (only asymmetric) MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS mapi-cli Public OIDC clients of the same issuer. The API accepts their ID tokens as Authorization: Bearer (what mapi login sends). Comma-separated. If empty, the API accepts only API tokens. In the dev profile, these clients can also use the built-in IdP with a loopback redirect MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS {} More authorization parameters as JSON, for example {"hd": "acme.com"} MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS unset The verified e-mails that sign in as platform operators (comma-separated) MAPI_DEFAULT_TENANT_ADMINS unset The e-mails that the server invites as admins of the default tenant at start-up. The user gets the invitation at the first sign-in with that verified e-mail MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS admin@dev.local,analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local The accounts of the dev profile. The first is an operator and tenant admin, the second is a runner, and the other accounts are viewers

Quotas and cost (v0.3)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH unset A JSON PriceTable. If unset: list prices like Cloud Run prices (mapi_spec.cost.DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE) MAPI_ESTIMATE_WALL_S fit 300, score 30, ingest 60, … For each run kind, the wall time in seconds that the server charges against vCPU-second quotas until it meters the run (JSON). The maximum is the timeout of the run MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED true Enforce requests_per_minute at token, tenant and global level MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES 500 The queued runs that the fair-share planner of the dispatcher looks at in each pass. This does not include runs that are held by a suspended tenant, the kill switches or the spend cap MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT 50 The maximum number of these runs for each tenant. Thus the held runs of one tenant cannot push out the runs of other tenants MAPI_EXECUTOR_REPORT_INTERVAL_S 10 How frequently each dispatcher reports executor health for /v1/admin/executors MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S 259200 (3 days) How long a recorded conformance or security-suite report lets an executor take verified and public tenants (the shared-tier gate)

Plot rendering and embed links (v0.4)

Refer to Sharing plots.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S 300 The wall-clock limit of a POST /v1/plots:render run. The sandbox stops the run after this time MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED false Accept Plotly plots for static rendering. This needs kaleido and a Chrome or Chromium in the runner image. The base images do not include them. While this setting is off, the server refuses Plotly renders with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE 300 The public views in each minute for one embed link. More views get 429 RATE_LIMITED MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE 120 The public embed requests in each minute from one client address, valid or not valid. This makes token guesses slower MAPI_EMBED_CACHE_S 60 How long an API instance uses the resolved plot of an embed again. The server still does a check of expiry and revocation on each request.
