Responses are Cache-Control: private, no-cache. Thus a revoked link stops on the next load MAPI_EMBED_IMAGE_URL_TTL_S 900 The life of the signed URL of the PNG fallback of an embed

Object storage

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim shim (the GCS shim at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT), gcs (real Cloud Storage. It needs the gcp extra, MAPI_URL_SIGNER and MAPI_URL_UPLOADER) or memory (only for tests) MAPI_GCP_PROJECT unset With gcs: the project of the Cloud Storage client (default: the project of the environment) MAPI_URL_SIGNER unset With gcs: the service account that signs URLs through IAM signBlob. Thus no key file is necessary MAPI_URL_UPLOADER unset With gcs (necessary): the account that signs create-only upload policies. Each run uses these policies for its outputs. It must be different from MAPI_URL_SIGNER. It can make objects, but it must never delete them. A GCS POST form has no generation precondition. Thus only a signer without storage.objects.delete makes the form create-only. The server does not start without this account MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT The base URL in signed URLs, when browsers or containers connect to the shim with a different host name MAPI_GCS_ROOT $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs The state directory of the shim. The server reads the key files of the principals under _shim/keys/ MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE $MAPI_GCS_ROOT/_shim/keys/control.json The key file of the principal of the control plane MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN from exec.json The bearer token of the exec principal of the shim. The server gives it to local runs (only local executors, never in the cloud)

Executors

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process local-process, docker, docker-gvisor or cloudrun-jobs (Cloud Run Jobs executor, with its own settings) MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND mapi-runner next to the interpreter The command line of the supervisor (shell-quoted) for local-process MAPI_EXECUTOR_WORKDIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/executions The scratch directory of the local executor for each run MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE mapi/base-bayes:<version> The runner image of the docker executors for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to runner image (JSON), with the tag of the workspace version MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK none The network of the run containers: container:<gcs-shim container>, or an internal network that contains only the shim. The server refuses none while the bootstrap URL is HTTP MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED false Declare that MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK is an internal network with only the shim. Then docker-gvisor reports enforced egress and DNS. verified and public tenants also need a recorded security-suite run in which the network probes were stopped (docker) MAPI_DOCKER_RUNTIME_GVISOR runsc The OCI runtime of docker-gvisor MAPI_CANCEL_GRACE_S 10 The seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when you cancel a run

Dispatcher and reconciler

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_DISPATCH_RATE_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_DISPATCH_BURST 180, 10 The token bucket in front of the executor (the jobs.run quota of Cloud Run) MAPI_DISPATCH_BATCH, MAPI_DISPATCH_POLL_S 10, 1 The queued runs that the dispatcher leases in each pass, and the pause between passes MAPI_DISPATCH_LEASE_S 120 How long the lease of a dispatcher on a run lasts. While the run waits for submission, a live dispatcher extends the lease after each third of this time. The maximum is ten lease lengths for each submit MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS all The trust tiers whose runs this orchestrator leases (comma-separated). If many orchestrators serve different exec pools, they need lists with no common tiers. If not, each orchestrator leases the runs of all tenants MAPI_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S 10 The level-triggered loop of the reconciler MAPI_STALL_INTERVALS 15 A run is stalled (a warning) after this number of progress intervals without events MAPI_COMPLETE_EVENT_GRACE_S 60 How long to wait for the complete event of a run after the executor reports an exit MAPI_LOST_EXECUTION_GRACE_S 60 How long an execution can be missing from the executor before the attempt is lost MAPI_DEADLINE_GRACE_S 60 The extra time after the timeout of a run before the reconciler stops it MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES 2 The automatic retries after infrastructure failures MAPI_HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_S 300 The sweep of expired upload intents (the server deletes their quarantine objects), expired browser sessions and abandoned sign-ins MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_WINDOW_S 1800 No automatic retry of a run that has continued for longer than this time MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR 2 No automatic retry when the cost of a run is this multiple of its estimate MAPI_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS 5 The attempts of the finalizer job before a run fails

Catalog and signing

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CATALOG_PATH unset A catalog JSON that the image build exports. If unset, the worker puts a sandboxed describe run in the queue MAPI_IMAGE_DIGEST sha256 of uv.lock The digest of the runner image. The catalog cache uses it as the key MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH found above the working directory The uv.lock whose hash is the local image digest MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH $MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem The EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests (in place of Cloud KMS). The worker signs and the API verifies, thus the two must load the same file. mapi-server migrate makes it MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS none Old bundle-signing keys (PEM files, public or private, comma-separated) whose signatures still verify. Thus a key rotation does not break the models that the old key signed (ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md) MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE true Make the key at the first use if it is missing. Compose turns it off for api and worker. Thus, if the key is missing, start-up fails, and the server does not mint a new key MAPI_SIGNER local local: the key file above. kms: a Cloud KMS asymmetric key version signs (gcp extra) MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION unset With MAPI_SIGNER=kms: the projects/…/cryptoKeyVersions/N that signs new manifests MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS none Older key versions whose signatures still verify (comma-separated, for rotation)

Cloud Run Jobs (MAPI_EXECUTOR=cloudrun-jobs; refer to Cloud Run Jobs executor)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT unset (necessary) The exec project that holds the Job inventory MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION europe-west1 The region of the inventory MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY derived The data residency of the platform tenant, of tenants that the migrations adopt, and of tenants that you make without a residency. Default: with cloudrun-jobs, the multi-region of MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION (eu for europe-west1). If not, us MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} The rule for Job ids. It must agree with the Jobs that the infrastructure makes MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES mmm, tabular: base-bayes; sklearn: base-ml; ts: base-forecast Plugin namespace to base image family (JSON) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE base-bayes The base for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST 150, 10 The token bucket in front of jobs.run for each orchestrator (maximum 180, the regional quota) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES 6 The number of 429 answers in sequence before a submit fails MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S 1, 64 The exponential back-off after a 429 (never shorter than Retry-After) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S 120 Task timeout = run timeout + this margin. The reconciler stops runs at their deadline. This margin is the backstop MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED true The exec network denies all egress, but not the restricted Google APIs VIP MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED false We verified that the DNS response policy applies to Jobs (the M0 DNS red-team gate). The dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on the executor only when the two settings are true and passing suite evidence is on record (the shared-tier gate). verified is the default tier. Until then, the server refuses their runs at submission MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S 93600 How far back orphan adoption lists executions

Webhooks (v0.4) (refer to Endpoints and webhooks)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S 2 How frequently the relay of the worker looks for due deliveries. The relay gives them to the webhooks procrastinate queue MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 The tries for each delivery (1 to 8). Retries wait 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h and 24 h, plus a jitter of up to 10% MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER 20 Disable a webhook after this number of consecutive events that the server could not send. A 410 Gone disables it immediately. The audit log records webhook.disabled MAPI_WEBHOOK_MAX_PER_PROJECT 25 The maximum number of webhooks for one project (more get 409) MAPI_WEBHOOK_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The days that the server keeps events and their delivery logs MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE unset An extra PEM CA bundle that the server trusts for receivers (a private CA). The server always uses the system trust store MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP false Only for development: accept http:// URLs for the hosts in MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST. Refused in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST none Only for development: host names (comma-separated, optionally host:port) that the SSRF address and port checks do not apply to, for example a receiver on localhost. Refused in the multi-tenant profile

The server seals webhook signing secrets with a key from MAPI_SERVER_SECRET. If you change the server secret, you cannot use the webhook secrets. Rotate them after the change.

Workflows (v0.5) (refer to Workflows)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WORKFLOW_TICK_S 1 How frequently (seconds) the workflow loop of the orchestrator moves active workflow runs forward, and fires due schedules and debounced triggers MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS 20 The workflow runs that one project can have at the same time, with sub-workflow runs. More runs get 429. A subworkflow.run node over the limit fails with QUOTA_EXCEEDED MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_SCHEDULES 20 The active cron schedules for each project MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_TRIGGERS 20 The active dataset-version triggers for each project MAPI_WORKFLOW_NODE_TIMEOUT_S 1800 The timeout of the child run of a node when the node sets no timeout MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_JSON_OUTPUT_BYTES 1048576 The largest JSON output (tables, metrics, reports) that a node can return

Pub/Sub push events (POST /internal/events)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE unset The expected audience of the OIDC token of the push subscription. When set, each push needs a token that Google signed MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT unset The service account that the subscription signs as (set it together with the audience) MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS any The accepted subscription names (comma-separated) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs The OIDC signing keys of Google

Sign-up, e-mail and abuse controls (v0.4) (refer to Sign-up and abuse controls)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED on in dev and multi-tenant when a mailer works, off in single-tenant Self-service sign-up at POST /auth/signup. If you set it on without a mailer that works, the server does not start MAPI_MAILER outbox in dev, smtp in multi-tenant, console in other profiles console (log the message), outbox (JSON files that you read at GET /dev/outbox in dev), smtp or none. multi-tenant refuses console and outbox while sign-up is on, because each person who reads the logs or the disk could verify all addresses MAPI_MAIL_FROM modeling-api <no-reply@mapi.localhost> The From: header MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR $MAPI_DATA_DIR/outbox The directory where the outbox mailer writes (mode 0600, the newest 200 messages stay) MAPI_SMTP_HOST, MAPI_SMTP_PORT unset, 587 The SMTP server. Without a host, the smtp mailer is off, and sign-up is also off MAPI_SMTP_TLS starttls starttls (necessary, not opportunistic: the server refuses an SMTP server without it) or ssl (implicit TLS, port 465). The server verifies the certificate against the system trust store MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME, MAPI_SMTP_PASSWORD unset SMTP authentication (keep the password in a secret store) MAPI_SMTP_TIMEOUT_S 10 The connection and command timeout MAPI_SIGNUP_VERIFY_URL $MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN/verify-email?token={token} The link that the server sends in the e-mail for a sign-up. The server replaces {token} MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKED_DOMAINS none The e-mail domains that the server refuses, in addition to the built-in disposable list (comma-separated, subdomains included) MAPI_SIGNUP_BLOCKLIST_PATH unset A file of disposable domains, one on each line (# comments), for example a public list that a group keeps current MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR 5 The sign-ups that the server accepts for each client address in each hour MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY 25 The verified sign-ups for each e-mail domain in each day. Unverified sign-ups do not count. The shared free-mail domains are exempt MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR 500 The verified sign-ups in each hour on the whole platform (unverified sign-ups do not count) MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS built-in list (gmail.com, outlook.com, ...) Free-mail domains that persons with no relation share (comma-separated, replaces the built-in list). These domains have no cap for each domain and no domain_burst flag MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE 20 The e-mail verification attempts for each client address in each minute MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS 30 The look-back of the Sybil heuristics MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD 3 The workspaces from one client address, browser or e-mail in the window. After this number, the server flags the next workspace for review. The server flags a domain at two times this number in one hour MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND false Suspend the workspace of a flagged sign-up until an operator approves it. Default: the workspace works and waits in the review queue MAPI_SIGNUP_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The server deletes unverified sign-ups, with their e-mail, after this number of days MAPI_PUBLIC_CODE_UPLOAD_ENABLED false Cut line B (M5): let identity-verified public tenants run uploaded code. Off: public tenants run only built-in models and declarative specs

Tenant deletion and GDPR export (v0.4) (refer to Deleting data)

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S 604800 (7 days) The grace period of a deletion. During this period, the tenant is suspended and can cancel the deletion MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S unset To request a deletion, also need a sign-in that is not older than this number of seconds. If unset, only the confirmation phrase is necessary MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S 3600 How long a purge waits for the cancelled runs of the tenant to stop before it continues MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS 8 The automatic retries of a failed purge, with back-off from 5 minutes to 6 hours. After this, an operator retries MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS 30 The retention period of the bundles bucket (Terraform bundle_retention_days). It tells when a purge retries the objects that a retention lock kept MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S 15 The interval of the deletion and export scheduler of the orchestrator MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES 256 MiB The dataset bytes in an export archive. The manifest lists the remaining bytes MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S 604800 (7 days) How long the server keeps an export archive MAPI_EXPORT_LINK_TTL_S 900 The life of the signed download link of an export (a new link on each GET) MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY 3 The exports that a tenant can request in each day (one at a time) MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES 256 MiB The metadata rows in an export archive. The manifest lists the tables that are not complete MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S 3600 The maximum time of an export build. If a build is still running five minutes after this time (its process stopped), the server builds it again one time. Then the build fails

docs.title: The runner (per run)
docs.text:
Executors start mapi-runner with exactly these variables. Its arguments contain nothing secret. Never set these variables manually.

Variable Meaning MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE The run, and the 256-bit nonce of its one-time bootstrap object MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL A template with {nonce}: the location where the supervisor reads (and deletes) the bootstrap object MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN Only local executors: the exec principal of the shim. It can only get and delete bootstrap objects MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The interpreter of the worker (default: the interpreter of the supervisor) MAPI_BASE_IMAGE The base image in the lineage of the run MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION The docker executor sets it to 1. The supervisor then fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION, and it does not run the worker in dev mode MAPI_TRACEPARENT The W3C traceparent of the dispatching span. Thus the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor contain the trace id of the run. Nothing goes out of the sandbox MAPI_LOG_JSON 1 (the default) makes the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor JSON lines. 0 makes plain text

The supervisor gives the untrusted worker only an allow-list of variables (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, locale and thread-count variables, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, XLA_FLAGS, …). The supervisor removes all MAPI_* variables.

In the runner images, MAPI_CACHE_SEED (/opt/mapi/cache) is the read-only PyTensor and Numba cache that the image build makes. MAPI_CACHE_DIR (/tmp/mapi-cache) is the writable symlink farm that the entry point builds over it (Container images).

docs.title: The GCS shim
docs.text: mapi-gcs-shim serve gets its defaults from the topology: MAPI_DATA_DIR (state in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs), MAPI_ENV (bucket names), MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT (host and port) and MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN (the CORS origin). Each has a command-line flag. Refer to the GCS shim reference. If you set MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS, it is also the locked retention of the bundles bucket in days when the shim makes its state. 0 means no retention. If unset, the bucket is write-once, for about 100 years.

docs.title: The CLI and the Python client
docs.text:
Variable Meaning MAPI_URL The API. If unset, the client uses MAPI_API_URL, then the profile, then http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_TOKEN An API token (mapi_…), sent as Authorization: Bearer. It has priority over a stored mapi login sign-in. The client never sends it over plain HTTP to a host that is not loopback MAPI_PROJECT The project to act in, <tenant>/<project> (v0.3). The client sends it as X-Mapi-Project on project-scoped requests. It has priority over mapi use MAPI_PROFILE The profile of the config file to use (refer to the warning above) MAPI_CONFIG The config file (default $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mapi/config.toml, if not set ~/.config/mapi/config.toml) MAPI_CREDENTIALS The file where mapi login keeps sign-ins (default credentials.json next to the config file, mode 0600) MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER The identity provider for mapi login (https, or plain http on a loopback address for a local development provider) MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID The OIDC client id of the CLI (default mapi-cli) MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL The location of the discovery document of the issuer, when it is not under the issuer. The built-in IdP of the dev profile has the issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost. It serves its document at <api>/dev/idp MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Only for identity providers that need a secret from installed apps (for example Google "desktop" clients). The CLI never prints it

Arguments (--url, --token, --project, --profile, or Client(base_url=…, token=…, project=…)) have priority over the environment. The environment has priority over the file. mapi config show prints the result and the source of each value. mapi login, mapi use and mapi config set write the config file again atomically with mode 0600.

docs.title: make dev
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py reads the topology variables and these variables:

Variable Meaning MAPI_STACK_PROFILE The MAPI_PROFILE of the servers. dev is the default: sign-in through the built-in development IdP, the default tenant and project, and the seeded accounts of MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS, with admin@dev.local as tenant admin and platform operator. The other values are single-tenant (the M1 API without credentials) or multi-tenant. The name is different, so a CLI MAPI_PROFILE in your shell never goes to the servers MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN Outside the single-tenant profile, the script makes a random bearer for POST /internal/events in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/internal-token. It gives the bearer to the servers. The end-to-end suite reads it there MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE, MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST If you do not set them, the dev profile writes a temporary CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/ (ca.pem, cert.pem, key.pem). It trusts the CA and puts the two hosts on the allow-list. Thus webhooks can get to an HTTPS receiver on your machine (the receiver of the M3 end-to-end suite) MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD Replace the command of one service (shell-quoted). <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS, for example MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --port 8000" NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR Disable or force coloured service prefixes

make dev ONLY=api and make dev WITHOUT=web,plots select services. make seed SIZE=full loads the large demo. These are make arguments, not environment variables.

make seed, make e2e and python -m mapi_conformance run --stack sign in to a stack that needs sign-in. If MAPI_TOKEN is set, they use it. If not, they sign in through the development IdP as MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT (default admin@dev.local). They act in MAPI_PROJECT (default default/default).

docs.title: The web app and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
These are Vite build-time variables. make dev sets them from the topology. For a production build, set them yourself.

Variable Default Meaning VITE_API_BASE http://127.0.0.1:8000 The API that the app calls (it must permit the origin of the app) VITE_PLOTS_ORIGIN http://127.0.0.1:5174 The plot sandbox. It must be different from the app origin VITE_STORAGE_ORIGINS http://127.0.0.1:4443 The origins of signed storage URLs. The CSP connect-src of the app permits them VITE_APP_ORIGINS (sandbox) http://127.0.0.1:5173,http://localhost:5173 The origins that can frame the sandbox and send messages to it VITE_AUTH_BASE VITE_API_BASE The location of the sign-in routes (/auth/*), when they are not on the API base VITE_TERMS_URL /terms The terms of service that sign-up links to (an http(s) URL or a path on the origin of the app). The default is the plain-language summary in the app VITE_ACCEPTABLE_USE_URL /acceptable-use The acceptable-use policy that sign-up links to, in the same way. A public installation must publish its own versions of the two documents

The Playwright smoke suite of the web app serves the app on 5173 and the sandbox on 5174. If other processes use these ports, set MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT and MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT. The suite then builds the app for that sandbox origin. It exports the origin to the specs as MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_ORIGIN.

The index.html of the sandbox has a %MAPI_CSP% placeholder. Its Vite build replaces the placeholder with the Content-Security-Policy. It is not a variable that you set.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example).

Variable Default Meaning POSTGRES_PASSWORD necessary The database password. Compose does not start without it MAPI_VERSION the workspace version The mapi/* image tag (make compose-up sets it) MAPI_ENV local The same as above MAPI_STACK_PROFILE dev The MAPI_PROFILE of the servers, the same as for make dev MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process The executor of the worker MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY, MAPI_WORKER_CPUS 4g, 12g, 4 The /tmp of the worker (the scratch of each local-process run), the memory limit and the CPUs DOCKER_GID 0 With the docker executor override: the group that owns the Docker socket

docs.title: The mapi/web image (nginx)
docs.text:
The container puts these variables into the nginx configuration when it starts. It replaces only MAPI_* variables.

Variable Default Meaning MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT the local defaults The origins in the CSP and frame-ancestors headers MAPI_API_UPSTREAM http://api:8000 The location where nginx sends /v1/ (a URL without a path) MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES 127.0.0.1 localhost The host names that the app server answers (space-separated). All other Host values get no response. Keep it in step with MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA empty Extra script-src sources for the app. A wider CSP needs a review NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR /etc/nginx/templates/all …/web or …/plots serves only one of the two apps

docs.title: Image build arguments
docs.text:
Use docker build --build-arg NAME=value. The Makefile gives VERSION, VCS_REF and BUILD_DATE. The defaults define each image. Change them only to build a variant.

Argument Meaning MAPI_PACKAGES The workspace packages that the build installs into the image (mapi-runner mapi-steps mapi-pymc …) MAPI_WORKER_PACKAGES The packages that the worker target adds to base-bayes (mapi-plugin-ts mapi-server[docker]) MAPI_NO_INSTALL The distributions that the build never installs (the 300 MB nvidia-nccl-cu13) MAPI_APT_PACKAGES The system packages of the runtime stage (tini, and g++ for PyTensor) MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT, MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT The distributions that must be installed, and that must not be installed. If not, the build fails MAPI_IMAGE_NAME, MAPI_DESCRIPTION OCI labels, and the name that the catalog export records PYTHON_IMAGE (and the other base images) Base images, pinned by tag and digest (make docker-pin)

docs.title: Deploying to Google Cloud
docs.text:
The deploy scripts under deploy/gcp/ get their settings as flags (--help on each). One variable changes the location of their local files:

Variable Meaning MAPI_DEPLOY_OUT The local scratch directory of deploy/gcp/*.sh: images files, saved plans and Terraform outputs. The default is deploy/gcp/.out, with one directory for each environment. Never commit it MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL A repository secret of the nightly workflow: the Pushgateway that gets mapi_security_probe_unexpected from the security jobs. If unset, the jobs do not push (ops/README.md)

Deploy to Google Cloud lists the variables that Terraform sets on the Cloud Run services (the deployment contract with mapi-server).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_E2E pnpm --filter @mapi/web e2e sets it: run the Playwright @e2e suite against a stack that runs MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT The development-IdP account that make seed and the end-to-end suites sign in as (default admin@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_ACCOUNTS The two development-IdP accounts that the M2 tenancy suite makes tenant admins (default analyst@dev.local,viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_UI_ACCOUNT The tenant admin of the M2 browser flow and the fit burst (default analyst@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS Opt-in: the number of concurrent real fits that tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py submits (M2 verification) MAPI_E2E_SIGNUP_ACCOUNT The address that the M3 trust-lifecycle suite (tests/e2e/test_m3_trust_stack.py) uses to sign up. It must be a development-IdP account, so that it can sign in (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_GUIDED_ACCOUNT The address that the M3 journey (tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py) uses to sign up. It is a development-IdP account (default viewer@dev.local) MAPI_E2E_KEEP 1 keeps the project that the M3.5 journeys make (tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py, apps/web/e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts). It also keeps the project of the forecasts-with-actuals journey (tests/e2e/test_forecast_actuals_stack.py). Thus you can look at the project in the app (M3.5 verification) MAPI_E2E_WEBHOOK_TLS_DIR The location where the webhook receiver of the M3 journey finds cert.pem and key.pem (default $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls) MAPI_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS 1 makes the contract snapshot of mapi_spec and the Guided catalog fixture of the server tests again (make snapshots) MAPI_HYPOTHESIS_EXAMPLES The examples for each property in the wire-format round-trip tests (default 60) MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA The data/ directory of a local copy of pymc-challenges. The from_challenges loaders of mapi-plugin-science read the real data files there, and the tests that use them run. If it is not set, these tests are skipped

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Variable Meaning MAPI_DOCS_SPEC The spec that scripts/docs_screenshots.mjs (make docs-screenshots) opens and fits, default eu-geo-mmm. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN MAPI_DOCS_PROJECT The project that scripts/docs_screenshots_admin.mjs (make docs-screenshots-admin) selects after it captures the project switcher, default Default project. The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_API_URL and MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT MAPI_GUIDED_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/guided-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the screenshots of the Guided tutorial from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-guided sets it, with MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT/MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT at the defaults 15173/15174. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_EXPLORER_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/explorer-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the explorer, About-card and budget-plan screenshots of the docs from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-explorers sets it, with the same port defaults. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_WORKFLOW_SCREENSHOTS Set to 1 to run apps/web/e2e/workflow-screenshots.spec.ts. This spec captures the screenshots of the docs for workflows (gallery, editor, run monitor, schedules, Guided recipe) and governance (policies, policy editor, review queue, validation, evidence), from the app in mock mode. make docs-screenshots-workflows sets it, with MAPI_SMOKE_WEB_PORT/MAPI_SMOKE_PLOTS_PORT at the defaults 15183/15184. If not set, the smoke suite skips it MAPI_SHOTS_DIR A directory. When set, the workflow and governance smoke specs (apps/web/e2e/workflows.spec.ts, governance.spec.ts) also save full-page screenshots of their screens there MAPI_EMBED_VIEW The EmbedView JSON that scripts/docs_screenshots_tutorials.mjs (make docs-screenshots-tutorials) serves to the embed page of the plot sandbox. scripts/docs_embed_view.py writes it (default .local/embed-view.json). The script also reads MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN and MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (default ports 15173/15174) MAPI_EMBED_API The API origin where the embed page asks for the view in that script. Playwright answers (default http://127.0.0.1:8000, the VITE_API_URL of the sandbox dev server). No process must listen there

docs.title: Docker Compose v0.2
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml runs the container images of the platform as a local stack on one machine. It uses the dev profile, the same as make dev (sign in as admin@dev.local, refer to signing in). It runs the same services as make dev, on the same ports, but from the exact images that production uses.

You do not need Docker for development (refer to Local, without Docker). Use compose to do a full check of the images, or to run a self-contained demo. Container images tells what is in each image, how the build makes it, and the build-time checks.

cp .env.example .env               # set POSTGRES_PASSWORD
make docker-build                  # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make compose-up                    # docker compose up -d --wait
make seed                          # load the E33 demo through the API
open http://127.0.0.1:5173
make compose-logs SERVICE=api      # follow one service
make compose-down                  # VOLUMES=1 also deletes the database and objects

docs.title: The stack
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph ns["shared network namespace (gcs-shim)"]
        shim["gcs-shim :4443"]
        api["api :8000"]
        worker["worker<br/>(local-process runs)"]
    end
    pg[("postgres :5432")]
    web["web :8080"]
    plots["plot-sandbox :8081"]
    browser(("browser")) -->|127.0.0.1:5173| web
    browser -->|127.0.0.1:5174| plots
    browser -->|"127.0.0.1:4443 (signed URLs)"| shim
    web -->|/v1/ proxy| api
    api --> pg
    worker --> pg
    migrate["migrate (one-shot)"] --> pg
Service Image Published on the host postgres postgres:16 (pinned by digest) not published. Refer to the override example gcs-shim mapi/gcs-shim 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 (the API, which shares this namespace) migrate mapi/server, migrate. Compose waits until it stops with status 0 — api mapi/server, api through gcs-shim worker mapi/worker, mapi-server worker, MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process — web mapi/web with only the app server block 127.0.0.1:5173 plot-sandbox mapi/web with only the sandbox server block 127.0.0.1:5174

Why api, worker and gcs-shim share one network namespace. Signed URLs contain the address of the object store. The bootstrap URL template also contains it for runner processes. The API could connect to the shim as gcs-shim:4443, while the browser needs 127.0.0.1:4443. Then each URL would need a public form and an internal form. With a shared namespace, 127.0.0.1:4443 and 127.0.0.1:8000 mean the same thing to the browser, the API, the orchestrator and each runner subprocess. This is exactly the make dev topology, and it agrees with the LocalDev defaults. The web container connects to the API as api:8000, which is a network alias of the container of the shim.

Durable state. Three named volumes stay after the containers stop: pgdata (the database), gcsdata (the objects and principal key files of the shim) and keys (the bundle-signing key). The finalizer of the worker signs each bundle manifest. The API verifies that signature before it gives an artifact link, a ui/ view or a plot. It also verifies the signature before it accepts a score request. Thus the two services must load the same key, and the key must stay after restarts.

migrate makes the key one time at /var/lib/mapi/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem (MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH). api and worker mount the volume read-only, with MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE=false. Thus, if the key is missing, start-up fails with a clear error, and the services do not mint a new key without a message. MAPI_DATA_DIR (/tmp/mapi-data) is the scratch directory of each container.

Caution

Do not delete the key without the database and the objects. A new key cannot verify old bundles. make compose-down VOLUMES=1 deletes the key together with the data.

Hardening. Each mapi/* service runs as a non-root user, with a read-only root filesystem, a tmpfs on /tmp, all Linux capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges. Compose publishes ports on 127.0.0.1 only. The PostgreSQL password comes from .env, and compose does not start without it. The official postgres image is the one exception. It starts as root to set the owner of the data directory, then it changes to the postgres user.

Host names. The M1 API has no authentication. An attacker can point the host name of a web page at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding). The page is then same-origin to itself, so CORS does not stop it. Thus the API answers only the Host names in MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS (default 127.0.0.1, localhost, api, and also the host of MAPI_API_URL). For all other names, it returns 400.

The nginx server of the app answers only MAPI_WEB_SERVER_NAMES (default 127.0.0.1 localhost). It closes the connection for all other hosts. The GCS shim does the same, for loopback names and the hosts of its endpoints (--allowed-host adds more). If you connect to the stack with a different name, for example a LAN host name, add it to the two variables.

docs.title: Executor choice: local-process vs docker
docs.text:
The compose worker runs the local-process executor inside a runner-capable image. Each run is a mapi-runner subprocess of the worker container. This is the default, because it needs no Docker socket and works with all daemons. The two executors have these differences:

local-process in mapi/worker (default) docker executor (compose.override.example.yml) Isolation Process only: runs share the uid, filesystem (with its keys, refer to the text below), /tmp and memory limit of the worker One container for each run, from the exact runner image, with its own limits and a network that connects only to the shim Images One large image with all plugins and the control plane mapi/worker for the orchestrator. For each run, the mapi/base-* image that contains the plugin of the run (MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES) Privileges Only the privileges of the worker The worker mounts /var/run/docker.sock, which is root-equivalent on the host Networking Runs connect to 127.0.0.1:4443 directly Run containers join the gcs-shim network namespace (MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=container:mapi-gcs-shim) Use it for Daily development, demos, CI A full check of the production images, and self-hosted setups (gVisor runsc in v0.3)

Docker executor settings. MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES maps a plugin namespace to its runner image. mmm.* and tabular.* run in mapi/base-bayes, sklearn.* in mapi/base-ml and ts.* in mapi/base-forecast. A workflow node run goes to the image of the model that it runs. This is its model parameter (for example a backtest or search of ts.sarimax). If there is no model parameter, it is the plugin of the model version that is bound to the node. Examples are a forecast, an evaluation or a governance check of a fitted model. Runs without a model plugin (ingest, describe, statistical tests) use MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE. The defaults are the tags that make docker-build makes for the current version.

MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK must give the run a path to the object store, because the bootstrap object and each signed URL point at it. In compose, the run joins the network namespace of the shim (container:mapi-gcs-shim). An internal Docker network that holds only the shim also works, if MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT names the shim on that network. With none, the runner cannot get its bootstrap object. Thus the worker does not start with none.

docker-gvisor for verified and public tenants. Shared tiers need an executor with egress and DNS enforced. You cannot use none. Thus, do these steps:

  1. Make an internal network that holds only the shim (docker network create --internal mapi-sandbox).
  2. Attach the shim to this network, and to no network that routes out.
  3. Set MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK=mapi-sandbox.
  4. Declare the network with MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED=true. The executor refuses host, bridge and default.

The executor then reports enforced egress and DNS. But the dispatcher puts verified and public tenants on it only after these conditions:

  • The security suite ran against it, and the executor stopped the http_egress, dns_egress and metadata_token probes.
  • That result and a passing conformance run are on record (the shared-tier gate).

Worker isolation in run containers. A run container starts its supervisor as root, with no-new-privileges. All Linux capabilities are dropped, but not the few that the uid split needs. The supervisor then starts the untrusted worker as uid 10001, which has no capabilities. Thus the worker cannot signal the supervisor or write to its event pipe. It also cannot read the environment of the supervisor or of the init process. The executor also sets MAPI_REQUIRE_ISOLATION=1. With this setting, the supervisor fails the run with SANDBOX_VIOLATION, and it does not run the worker under its own uid.

The two modes are not a multi-tenant boundary. They are single-tenant local stacks. The local-process executor refuses all multi-tenant profiles.

What a local-process run can reach. Each run is a subprocess of mapi-server worker, and it runs as the same uid, 10001. There is no uid split before v0.3. Thus run code (the plugins and the steps that they load) can read all that the orchestrator can read:

  • The control key of the shim (/shim/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json). It gives storage.admin on all buckets. This is sufficient to read or write bundles, datasets and run outputs again, and to mint signed URLs.
  • The bundle-signing key (/var/lib/mapi/keys/). This is sufficient to forge a manifest that the API accepts.
  • The executions directory under /tmp/mapi-data. This includes the pid files that name the nonces of the runs that are in progress.

Thus, in this mode, bundle signatures and the output checks of the finalizer protect against accidents, but not against hostile plugin code. The orchestrator marks itself non-dumpable. Thus run code cannot ptrace it or read its memory. Run code also cannot read its /proc/<pid>/environ (DATABASE_URL with the password). The worker also logs this warning at start-up.

Warning

Run only trusted plugin code under local-process. Other code can read the keys above.

The docker executor does not have this risk. Each attempt runs in its own container, and none of these files are mounted. The /tmp of the worker is the scratch space for local-process runs. Set its size with MAPI_WORKER_TMPFS, MAPI_WORKER_MEMORY and MAPI_WORKER_CPUS in .env.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Compose reads .env in the repository root (copy .env.example). POSTGRES_PASSWORD is necessary. These variables are optional:

  • The MAPI_WORKER_* sizes.
  • The image version (MAPI_VERSION, which the Makefile sets).
  • MAPI_API_UPSTREAM and MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA of the web image.

All the variables are in the configuration reference.

compose.override.example.yml shows the two usual changes: it publishes PostgreSQL on the host, and it changes the worker to the docker executor. To use it, copy it to compose.override.yml. Version control ignores this file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Troubleshooting tells about these problems: a missing Docker daemon, a missing POSTGRES_PASSWORD, an unhealthy api container, a read-only /tmp and ports that are already allocated.

docs.title: Deploy to Google Cloud v0.3
docs.text:
This page tells how to change empty Google Cloud projects into a multi-tenant platform that operates. It applies to an environment (dev, staging or prod). At the end, you have these items:

  • The API and the web app on Cloud Run.
  • Runs that execute as Cloud Run Jobs in a zero-egress sandbox project.
  • Data in private buckets behind a VPC Service Controls perimeter.

All the configuration is in infra/terraform. Four scripts in deploy/gcp operate it.

Status: written, validated and tested offline; not yet applied

The Terraform passes terraform validate for each environment. It also passes a terraform test suite that applies each module against mocked providers (refer to Testing the infrastructure). We have not applied it to a real organisation yet. The cloud adapters of the server (Cloud Run Jobs executor, Cloud Storage, KMS signing, Pub/Sub push verification) are in the same release. We tested them only against fakes. The environment variables that they read are below. Read the next section before you start.

docs.title: Before you start: the [verify M0] checklist
docs.text:
The design depends on cloud behaviours that the Google Cloud documentation suggests. But nobody has confirmed them against a real Cloud Run Jobs execution yet. The plan marks each behaviour [verify M0]. These behaviours do not break a dev environment. But do not admit untrusted tenants until each one has a recorded pass. The full procedure, with the probe for each item, is the M0 verification checklist. The steps that remain after the offline M2 verification are in M2 verification.

Assumption What depends on it If it is not true The Direct VPC egress resolver obeys the DNS response policy (*. to NXDOMAIN, Google APIs to the restricted VIP) DNS exfiltration is stopped. You can set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED to true. Only this setting lets verified and public tenants run Cloud Run Jobs cannot host untrusted code. Keep shared tiers off it. Use GKE Sandbox behind the same executor protocol Deny-all egress and VPC Service Controls apply to Jobs executions Runs cannot connect to the internet or to buckets outside the perimeter The same as above gen2 permits the supervisor/worker uid split with no_new_privs, seccomp and no ptrace The worker cannot read the credentials of the supervisor Runs report DEV_MODE_ISOLATION. The runner images must start the supervisor as root for the split Execution overrides are env-only (no image, resources, service account or network) jobs.run can give only the run id and nonce The role of the dispatcher must have fewer permissions The limits of the in-memory filesystem operate as planned (no ephemeral disk, exit 137 at the limit) Scratch budgets of 3/6/12 GiB for classes S/M/L. RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with a retry in the next larger class Fits with large data move to GKE You cannot restore a deleted bootstrap object The nonce in the audit log points at nothing Terraform already sets the soft-delete window of the bootstrap bucket to 0. If you can still restore a copy, examine the bootstrap design again before launch Quotas: 180 jobs.run in each minute and 1,000 running executions in each region The token bucket of the dispatcher (150 a minute by default) and the global limit of 700 concurrent runs Decrease MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE. Divide the work across exec projects The cold start of a base image of about 2.5 GB keeps the p95 of time-to-RUNNING below 90 s The M2 latency target (met offline, only against the fake backend) Smaller images, or warm capacity (M6) The path from the Logging sink to Pub/Sub carries the labels of the execution in some seconds. Pub/Sub can push to an internal-only service Run events and progress Runs still finish (the status of the executor decides if a run is alive), but there is no progress Cloud SQL managed connection pooling works in transaction mode with the driver of the server. The migrate role can grant BYPASSRLS Row-level security for requests. The platform role for the orchestrator Give mapi_orchestrator its own policy-based access (the explicit policy is already there) run.jobs.runWithOverrides works without iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the execution account The least-privilege role of the orchestrator Grant actAs on that one account Cloud Run accepts the image indexes that build-push.sh pushes (with attestations) Deploys Build with --no-attestations

Two more limits of v0.3 are not cloud facts, but they are important on the first day:

  • Browser sign-in uses an OpenID provider with an authorization-code endpoint (Google by default). The server does not accept the tokens of Identity Platform yet. Refer to Authentication.
  • The nightly security suite has no probe Job in Terraform yet (Security suite).

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
One environment has five types of project, one for each trust zone (plan §8.1):

flowchart TB
    users(("browsers ·<br/>clients")) -->|HTTPS| lb["global HTTPS load balancer<br/>app.example.com · plots.example.net"]
    subgraph control["control project (trusted)"]
        lb --> api["api<br/>Cloud Run"]
        lb --> web["web · plots<br/>Cloud Run"]
        events["events<br/>Cloud Run, internal"]
        orch["orchestrator<br/>worker pool"]
        sql[("Cloud SQL<br/>PostgreSQL 16")]
        kms["KMS<br/>bundle signing"]
        topic["Pub/Sub<br/>run events"]
        api --> sql
        orch --> sql
        events --> sql
        topic -->|"push + OIDC"| events
    end
    subgraph perimeter["VPC-SC perimeter"]
        subgraph exec["exec-paid · exec-public (hostile)"]
            jobs["Cloud Run Jobs<br/>3 bases × S/M/L<br/>deny-all egress"]
            sink["Logging sink<br/>mapi_event lines"]
        end
        subgraph data["data project"]
            buckets[("quarantine · bootstrap · runs<br/>bundles · data")]
        end
    end
    subgraph build["build project"]
        ar["Artifact Registry<br/>images · curated PyPI"]
    end
    orch -->|"jobs.run (env: run id, nonce)"| jobs
    jobs -->|"signed URLs only<br/>(restricted VIP)"| buckets
    jobs --> sink -->|Publish| topic
    jobs -. pull .-> ar
Module Project Creates control control Cloud Run api, events, web, plots. Orchestrator worker pool. migrate job. Cloud SQL (private IP, managed connection pooling). Secret Manager secrets. Pub/Sub topic, push subscription and dead letters. One Logging sink for each exec project. KMS signing key. Identity Platform. Optional load balancer exec each exec project VPC without a default route, deny-all egress firewall, restricted-VIP route and DNS zone, DNS response policy, the Job inventory, the execution service account, the dispatcher role data data The five buckets of plan §8.6 with lifecycle rules, retention, CORS and bucket-level IAM build build Docker repository (immutable tags), curated PyPI remote, Binary Authorization attestor (stub), GitHub Workload Identity Federation perimeter organisation The VPC-SC perimeter around the exec and data projects stack all Connects the modules and enables the APIs

envs/<env>/main.tf holds the policy of each environment, where code review sees it. The policy includes the database size and availability, the deletion protection, the retention lock and the perimeter mode. terraform.tfvars holds only names and ids.

dev staging prod Database Enterprise, 1 vCPU, zonal, no pooler Enterprise Plus, zonal, pooler Enterprise Plus, regional (HA), pooler VPC-SC perimeter dry-run (optional) enforced, necessary enforced, necessary Load balancer + domains optional optional necessary Deletion protection off on on Bundle retention 1 day, unlocked 7 days, unlocked 30 days, locked Signing key software software HSM Minimum instances (api) 0 1 2

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An organisation with an Access Context Manager policy (gcloud access-context-manager policies list --organization ORG_ID). Without a policy, you can deploy only dev, without the perimeter. Each plan then shows a warning.
  • Projects that the project vending of your organisation makes: control, data, build, and one exec project for each pool. The pools are exec-paid, and also exec-public when you have public tenants. Link all projects to billing. Put nothing else in the exec projects.
  • Tools: Terraform ≥ 1.11 (tested with 1.14), gcloud, Docker with buildx, python3 and curl.
  • Permissions for the first run: project owner (or equivalent) on each project, and roles/accesscontextmanager.policyEditor on the organisation policy. Later runs use the CI identities that Terraform makes.
  • An OAuth client (web application) for the app origin, for browser sign-in.

docs.title: 1. Bootstrap the projects
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh --env staging --region europe-west4 \
  --control-project acme-mapi-stg-control --data-project acme-mapi-stg-data \
  --build-project acme-mapi-stg-build \
  --exec-project paid=acme-mapi-stg-exec-paid --exec-project public=acme-mapi-stg-exec-public \
  --state-project acme-mapi-stg-build --dry-run       # read what it will do, then drop --dry-run

The script enables the APIs of each project. It uses the same lists as modules/stack/apis.tf, and a test keeps the lists identical. It makes the state bucket (uniform access, public access prevention, object versioning). Then it writes infra/terraform/envs/staging/backend.hcl.

docs.title: 2. Describe the environment
docs.text:
cp infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars.example infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars
$EDITOR infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars

Type these values:

  • The project ids and the region.
  • The bucket location. Use the data residency of your tenants.
  • The exec pools and the access policy id.
  • The domains, the OAuth client id and the GitHub repository.

The file holds no secrets. Do not commit it.

Data residency and the exec region

The dispatcher puts a run only on an executor whose region satisfies the data residency of its tenant. The default residency is the residency that the region of the dispatch pool satisfies: eu for europe-west4. This default applies to the platform tenant and to each tenant that you make without a residency. To change the default, use the default_residency of the control module.

The exec region can be unable to satisfy the residency of a tenant. Then the server refuses its runs at submission (403, "no executor of this platform can run this tenant's work"). The worker also logs a warning for the tenant at start-up. To change the residency of a tenant, use PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{id} (data_residency).

docs.title: 3. Apply the foundation
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging --foundation

A foundation apply makes all resources except the Cloud Run workloads and Jobs, which need images. It makes the registry, networks, DNS policy, database, secrets, buckets, perimeter and CI identities. deploy.sh always shows the plan. Before it applies the plan, it asks you to type the environment name.

During this apply, ephemeral resources make the database passwords, the token pepper and the session key. Write-only arguments write them. They are in Secret Manager only. They are not in the state and not in the plan file.

docs.title: 4. Add the OAuth client secret
docs.text:
export TF_VAR_oidc_client_secret='...'      # from the OAuth client
# in terraform.tfvars: oidc_client_secret_version = 1

The secret is an ephemeral Terraform variable. Terraform writes it to Secret Manager as a new version and never keeps it. When you rotate the secret, increase oidc_client_secret_version. Add the identity providers that you want to Identity Platform. Use the console, or google_identity_platform_*_idp_config resources outside this module.

docs.title: 5. Build and push the images
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/build-push.sh --env staging

The script builds server, web, base-bayes, base-ml and base-forecast for linux/amd64. It pushes them as <version>-<git sha>. Tags are immutable in the registry. Thus, if you run the script again for the same commit, it uses the images that are there. The script writes the digests of the images to deploy/gcp/.out/staging/images.tfvars.json. Terraform refuses all images that are not pinned by digest.

docs.title: 6. Deploy the release
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging

The script does these steps:

  1. It does a terraform plan with terraform.tfvars and the images file, and saves the plan to a plan file.
  2. It asks for confirmation. Type the environment name. In automation, --yes skips this step.
  3. Migrations first: it points the mapi-staging-migrate job at the new server image and executes the job (deploy/gcp/migrate.sh). Migrations are expand/contract. Thus the release that serves now continues to work on the new schema. On the first release, the job is not there yet. Thus the migrations run immediately after the apply.
  4. It does a terraform apply of exactly the saved plan.
  5. It records the images file as a release in gs://<state bucket>/mapi/staging/releases/<UTC timestamp>-<release id>.json. The release id is a hash of the images. Thus, if you retry a deploy of the same images, it is the same release.
  6. It does a smoke test. The test does a check of the API /healthz and /readyz, the web app (with a Content-Security-Policy) and the plot sandbox. It also makes sure that the events service refuses requests from the internet.

docs.title: 7. Point DNS at the load balancer
docs.text:
terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/envs/staging output lb_ip

Make A records for the two domains. The Google-managed certificate becomes available when DNS resolves. This often takes 15–60 minutes. Until then, run deploy.sh --skip-smoke. Without domains, the services answer on their run.app URLs (terraform output urls).

docs.title: 8. Verify the controls
docs.text:
Before the first production deploy, read the security hardening page and do the M0 verification checklist. When the DNS item has a recorded pass, tell the orchestrator in the main.tf of the environment. Then deploy again:

control = {
  # ...
  extra_env = {
    orchestrator = { MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" }
  }
}

Until then, the executor declares that DNS is not enforced. The dispatcher then does not put verified and public tenants on it (trust tiers).

docs.title: 9. Name the operators and create the first tenant
docs.text:
Platform operators are the persons whose verified e-mail is in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS. Set it on the API. Use only plain values. Never put secrets in extra_env:

control = {
  # ...
  extra_env = {
    api = { MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS = "oncall@acme.example,platform@acme.example" }
  }
}

Run deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env staging. Then an operator signs in to the web app, or with mapi login --issuer https://accounts.google.com --client-id <the CLI's client id>. The operator makes the tenant of each organisation with its first admin. The server sends an invitation to the admin by e-mail. The admin becomes tenant admin at the first sign-in:

mapi admin tenants create acme --name "Acme Retail" --tier verified --residency eu \
    --admin-email it@acme.example

After this, the tenant admin makes projects and invites persons (Administration). Monitor the platform with the observability dashboards. Import the alerts before you let users in.

Verified tenants cannot run until DNS enforcement is verified

verified and public tenants need an executor with egress and DNS enforced. verified is the default tier of new tenants (the private beta). A new stack does not set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED and has no suite evidence. Thus the server refuses their runs at submission (INFRA_ERROR, 503). Only internal and self_hosted_trusted tenants run. To open the shared tiers, do these steps:

  1. Pass the DNS red-team gate of the M0 checklist from a Job of this environment.
  2. Set MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" for the orchestrator through control.extra_env ({ orchestrator = { MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED = "true" } }). Then deploy.
  3. Run the executor conformance suite and the security suite against the deployed executor. Record the two results with PUT /v1/admin/executors/cloudrun-jobs/evidence (the shared-tier gate). Evidence expires after MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S, so record the nightly runs.

docs.title: Continuous deployment
docs.text:
.github/workflows/deploy.yml deploys only on manual dispatch, without service-account keys:

Job GitHub environment Google identity Does build <env>-build mapi-<env>-ci-push build-push.sh. Uploads the images file plan <env>-plan mapi-<env>-planner (read-only) deploy.sh --plan-only. The plan goes to the job summary apply <env> mapi-<env>-deployer deploy.sh --apply-plan: migrations, apply of that plan, release record, smoke test

Do these steps for each environment:

  1. Make the three GitHub environments. Put required reviewers on <env> (the apply).
  2. Restrict <env> to protected branches.
  3. Copy the values of terraform output github into environment variables: GCP_WIF_PROVIDER, GCP_CI_PUSH_SA, GCP_PLANNER_SA, GCP_DEPLOYER_SA.
  4. Also add GCP_IMAGE_REPOSITORY (terraform output image_repository), TF_STATE_BUCKET and TERRAFORM_TFVARS (the contents of the terraform.tfvars of the environment).
  5. Optionally, add OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET as a secret of <env>-plan and <env>. You must give an ephemeral variable to the plan and to the apply.

The workload identity provider accepts tokens only from your repository. Each service account trusts exactly one GitHub environment. Thus a job can never get more permissions than its environment permits. A person runs the first apply of an environment, which makes these identities.

The perimeter is an organisation-level resource. Project-level grants cannot include it. Thus give these roles on the access policy yourself, or use a scoped access policy for the projects of the platform:

  • roles/accesscontextmanager.policyEditor to the deployer.
  • roles/accesscontextmanager.policyReader to the planner.

When the perimeter is enforced, persons outside it need an access level (vpc_sc.access_levels) to run Terraform or to read the logs of the exec projects. The deployer has its own ingress rule.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Bucket names are global. The storage contract names buckets mapi-{env}-{purpose} (mapi_spec.storage.bucket_name). Thus mapi-prod-data must be free in all of Cloud Storage. If a different user has the name, select a more specific environment name as a new envs/ directory. The name must agree with ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,15}$, for example acme-prod.
  • KMS key rings are permanent. If you make a destroyed environment again, you must do a terraform import of its key rings.
  • --traffic-only rollbacks apply only to the HTTP services. To roll back the orchestrator and the Jobs, deploy a release again.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The alert policies in ops/alerts/cloud-monitoring-alerts.yaml and the Cloud Monitoring dashboard read the mapi_* series from Managed Service for Prometheus. Nothing outside an instance can scrape them. The load balancer routes only /v1, /auth/* and the health checks, and the orchestrator has no ingress. Thus each server workload (api, events, orchestrator) runs a collector sidecar.

The sidecar is an OpenTelemetry Collector. It scrapes the /metrics of the workload over 127.0.0.1 each 30 s, with the metrics-token bearer. It writes the series to Managed Service for Prometheus. The orchestrator serves its own series on 127.0.0.1:9464: dispatch latency, finalize outcomes, integrity failures, running executions and jobs.run 429s. The runtime identities already have roles/monitoring.metricWriter.

Copy the collector image from Google into the registry of the build project. Pin it by digest, and set it for each environment:

gcloud artifacts docker images copy \
  us-docker.pkg.dev/cloud-ops-agents-artifacts/google-cloud-opentelemetry-collector/otelcol-google:<version> \
  europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/<build project>/mirror/otelcol-google:<version>
# terraform.tfvars
metrics_collector_image = "europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/<build project>/mirror/otelcol-google@sha256:<digest>"

Without the image, a release still deploys, but Terraform shows a warning (check.metrics_collection). Then no mapi_* series goes to Cloud Monitoring, and the PromQL alerts (integrity failure, STALLED rate, spend caps) can never fire. control.metrics_collector also accepts scrape_interval, cpu and memory. The api and events services get CPU only while they serve requests. Thus the sidecar scrapes an idle instance late. This is satisfactory for alerts that use a period of 5 to 15 minutes.

The security-suite series (mapi_security_probe_unexpected) comes from the nightly workflow. The workflow pushes it to the Pushgateway that the MAPI_PUSHGATEWAY_URL repository secret names (ops/README.md).

docs.title: Day-2 operations
docs.text:
Rollback. There are two procedures:

deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --list            # recorded releases, newest first
deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --previous        # redeploy the release before the deployed one
deploy/gcp/rollback.sh --env prod --traffic-only    # seconds: services back to their previous revision

A release rollback goes through deploy.sh (plan, confirmation, apply, smoke test) with --skip-migrate, because schema changes only move forward. The script records it as <UTC timestamp>-<id of the release it redeployed>-rollback.json. --previous reads the records again. A retried deploy counts one time. After a rollback from a bad release, a second --previous goes one more release back. It does not go back to the bad release.

--traffic-only moves traffic with gcloud and does not change Terraform. Use it for incidents. It does not change the orchestrator and the Jobs. The next deploy moves traffic to the newest revision again.

Migrations by themselves. deploy/gcp/migrate.sh --env prod --image <server@sha256:...>.

Rotate secrets. Increase one of these values in the main.tf of the environment:

  • control.database.password_version. All three database roles and their connection URLs change in one apply.
  • control.secret_versions.session_secret. This signs out all users.
  • token_pepper. This makes all API tokens invalid.

New Cloud Run revisions use the latest secret versions.

Rotate the bundle-signing key. Do these steps (refer to ops/runbooks/rotating-keys.md):

  1. Make a KMS key version.
  2. Set control.kms_key_version to it.
  3. List the previous version in control.kms_trusted_key_versions.
  4. Deploy.

If you remove a version from the trusted list, each model that it signed fails with INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

Add an exec pool. Add an entry to exec_pools. Run bootstrap.sh for its project, then run deploy.sh. The perimeter, the Logging sink, the image-pull grant and the bootstrap-bucket grant change automatically.

Tear down dev. You cannot delete KMS keys. You can only schedule their versions for destruction. Thus the two signing keys have prevent_destroy. First, remove them from the state. Then destroy. Dev has no deletion protection and lets Terraform empty its buckets. Staging and prod refuse this:

cd infra/terraform/envs/dev
terraform state list | grep 'google_kms_crypto_key\.' | xargs -n1 terraform state rm
terraform destroy

docs.title: Environment of the Cloud Run workloads
docs.text:
This is the deployment contract between Terraform (modules/control/locals.tf) and mapi-server. Each name is a mapi-server setting (refer to the configuration reference). If Terraform sets a variable that the server does not read, tests/infra fails. These are the plain values:

Variable Workloads Value MAPI_ENV all Environment name. Buckets are mapi-{env}-* MAPI_PROFILE all multi-tenant (the local-process executor refuses it) MAPI_OBJECT_STORE all gcs: real Cloud Storage, URLs signed without a key file MAPI_GCP_PROJECT all The project of the Cloud Storage client MAPI_URL_SIGNER all The service account whose signBlob signs URLs (no key file is necessary) MAPI_URL_UPLOADER all The service account whose signBlob signs create-only upload policies (run outputs). It can make objects in runs and quarantine, but it can never delete them MAPI_SIGNER, MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION all kms and …/cryptoKeyVersions/<control.kms_key_version> of the EC P-256 key that signs bundle manifests MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE, MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE, MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE all mapi_app (row-level security), mapi_orchestrator (the platform role, the only RLS bypass) and mapi_gateway (the look-ups of the API before it knows the tenant, RLS applies) MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY all The residency of the platform tenant and of tenants that you make without a residency. It is the default_residency of the control module. If not set, it is the residency that the region of the dispatch pool satisfies (eu for europe-west4) MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES all 169.254.0.0/16 (the Cloud Run front end), 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22 (Google load balancer front ends) and the address of the load balancer. The API skips these hops when it reads the address of the caller from X-Forwarded-For. After the first deployment, make sure that the audit fingerprint of a sign-up is different between two networks. If your topology has more hops, add them through extra_env MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN all, web Public origins (the API shares the app origin behind the load balancer) MAPI_DATA_DIR all /tmp/mapi (in-memory scratch) MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS api, events The host names that the service answers MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER, MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID api Browser sign-in MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS events The values that a valid Pub/Sub push token must contain, and the one subscription that can push MAPI_EXECUTOR orchestrator cloudrun-jobs MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST orchestrator 9464 on 127.0.0.1: the /metrics of the orchestrator (dispatch, reconcile, finalize series), for the collector sidecar MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT, MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION orchestrator The exec pool that it dispatches to (control.dispatch_pool, default the first pool that is not public). Its Jobs use the default mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} names MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL Jobs gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce} (set on each Job, read by the runner)

These values come from Secret Manager (references that resolve when a revision starts):

Variable Workloads Secret MAPI_DATABASE_URL api, events db-url-app-direct: mapi_app, direct (the LISTEN that feeds SSE) MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL api, events, orchestrator db-url-app: mapi_app through the pooler (transaction mode). Tenant sessions MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL api, events db-url-gateway: mapi_gateway through the pooler. Sign-in look-ups, operator routes, the routing of pushed events (no RLS bypass) MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL orchestrator db-url-orchestrator: mapi_orchestrator, direct. The loops of the orchestrator. Only the service account of the orchestrator can read this secret (plan §9) MAPI_DATABASE_URL orchestrator db-url-orchestrator (procrastinate needs LISTEN) MAPI_DATABASE_URL migrate db-url-migrate: role mapi_migrate (schema owner), direct MAPI_SERVER_SECRET all The root of the API-token pepper and the audit fingerprint key. If you rotate it (control.secret_versions.server_secret), all API tokens become invalid MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN api, events, orchestrator, collector sidecars The bearer that a scraper sends on GET /metrics (the multi-tenant profile refuses scrapes without it) MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET api Only when a client secret version is available

One orchestrator serves one exec pool, and an environment deploys one orchestrator. Runs go only to control.dispatch_pool. Until tier placement across pools (M5), keep all tenants on that pool. A second pool, for example a separate exec project for public tenants, needs a second orchestrator outside this module.

The two orchestrators must then set MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS with no common tiers. For example, set internal,self-hosted-trusted,verified through control.extra_env.orchestrator here, and public on the other orchestrator. If not, leases do not look at pools. Each orchestrator then takes the queued runs of all tenants, and public-tier code can go into the paid pool. Terraform exec_pools[*].public selects only the default dispatch_pool. The server does not read it.

Each workload can get more plain variables through control.extra_env in the main.tf of the environment. Never put secrets there.

docs.title: Testing the infrastructure
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/infra -q                     # everything below
TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR=~/.terraform.d/plugin-cache uv run pytest tests/infra -q   # reuse providers
  • Static invariants (they always run): deny-all egress with exactly two exceptions, no public buckets or principals, max_retries = 0 and gen2 on each Job, the VPC-SC perimeter and DNS policy, write-only secrets, and digest-pinned images. They also make sure that the infrastructure agrees with the mapi_spec contracts (bucket names, resource class sizes, runner environment, the push endpoint).
  • terraform fmt, terraform validate for each environment (with -backend=false).
  • terraform test for each module. The test applies each module against mocked Google providers. Thus it evaluates each expression and connection, and it asserts the security properties on the result values. It uses no credentials and makes no cloud calls.
  • Deploy scripts: --help, argument checks, the confirmation guard and full dry runs. These tests use stub terraform/gcloud/docker/curl binaries that prove that nothing executes. They run under /bin/bash 3.2 and under the bash on PATH. If shellcheck is installed, it also runs.

If terraform is not installed, the Terraform tests are skipped. The first run downloads the Google providers (about 250 MB). It puts them into a temporary cache, but not if TF_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR is set.

docs.title: Container images v0.2
docs.text:
The platform has six images (and a worker target). The build makes them from images/<name>/Dockerfile, with the repository root as the build context. The images have three purposes:

  • To run the exact production artifacts locally (Docker Compose).
  • To support the docker executor.
  • To become the Cloud Run Jobs in v0.3.
make docker-build                      # every image, tagged mapi/<name>:<version>
make docker-build IMAGES="server web"  # a subset
make docker-pin-check                  # every base image pinned by digest?

docs.title: The images
docs.text:
Image Contents Runs as Entry point mapi/base-bayes mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-pymc, the mmm.* and tabular.* plugins, a C++ compiler for PyTensor 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-ml mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-sklearn (sklearn.* plugins). No PyMC. 10001 mapi-runner mapi/base-forecast mapi-runner, SDK, steps, plot recipes, mapi-pymc, the ts.* plugins 10001 mapi-runner mapi/worker base-bayes with the ts.* plugins and mapi-server (target worker of the base-bayes Dockerfile). Only for compose 10001 mapi-server worker mapi/server The control plane: mapi-server, mapi-spec, the JSON-only mapi-plots core, docker-py. No science dependencies. 10001 mapi-server api (or worker, migrate) mapi/gcs-shim The local Cloud Storage emulator 10001 mapi-gcs-shim mapi/web nginx that serves apps/web (port 8080) and apps/plot-sandbox (port 8081) 101 nginx

make docker-build IMAGES="server web" builds a subset. make docker-build builds all images. It also builds mapi/worker when base-bayes is in the set. Each image has the OCI labels title, version, revision (git commit) and created.

docs.title: How the Python images are built
docs.text:
Each Python image uses the same multi-stage pattern:

  1. manifests copies the build context. It deletes all files except the pyproject.toml and uv.lock files. Thus its output changes only when dependencies change.
  2. builder installs the third-party dependencies of the package set of the image. It uses only those manifests (uv sync --frozen --no-install-workspace, one time for each package, into /opt/mapi/venv). BuildKit keeps this layer in a cache. Thus, when you edit source code, the build does not install PyMC again. The builder then copies the sources and installs the workspace packages, non-editable. Each version comes from uv.lock.

  3. runtime starts again from the same python:3.12-slim base. It adds tini (and g++ for the PyMC images) and makes user 10001. Then it copies in only the virtual environment.

    The images that run mapi-server (mapi/server and mapi/worker) also copy uv.lock to /opt/mapi/uv.lock and set MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH to it. Its SHA-256 is the image digest. The API and the orchestrator use this digest as the cache key of the step and model catalog. make dev calculates the same value. The build makes the two images from one lock, so api and worker agree.

The package set is the MAPI_PACKAGES build argument. images/common/install_packages.py changes it into uv sync calls. The build never installs the xgboost dependency nvidia-nccl-cu13 (MAPI_NO_INSTALL). This is a 300 MB wheel that only multi-GPU training uses.

docs.title: Build-time guards
docs.text:
If an image is not what it claims to be, the build fails:

  • Package assertions. images/common/assert_dists.py does a check of MAPI_ASSERT_PRESENT and MAPI_ASSERT_ABSENT against the real environment. For example, base-ml must not contain pymc, pytensor or numba. server must not contain numpy, xarray, pandas, scipy, pyarrow, PyMC, mapi_sdk, mapi_runner or a plugin.
  • Import contracts in the control-plane image. The contracts stage of images/server/Dockerfile installs import-linter (hash-pinned from uv.lock) into a temporary copy of the environment. It runs the contracts of the repository against the packages exactly as they are installed. The runtime stage depends on that stage, so BuildKit cannot skip it.
  • Catalog export. The runner images load each installed step, model and plot plugin. They write /opt/mapi/catalog.json with its digest (/opt/mapi/catalog.digest). If no steps or models are registered, the build fails.

We also prove the same claims without Docker. tests/devops/test_container_invariants.py calculates the dependency closure of each image from uv.lock (scripts/lock_closure.py). Then it does a check of the closure against the assertions.

docs.title: Compile caches and the read-only root filesystem
docs.text:
PyTensor compiles C at run time, and Numba keeps machine code in a cache. During the build, a small hierarchical model compiles and fills the two caches. The build then puts the caches read-only into /opt/mapi/cache. PyTensor needs a writable compile directory, because it takes a lock and adds new modules.

Thus, at start-up, the entry point (images/common/runner-entrypoint.sh) builds a symlink farm of the cache under /tmp/mapi-cache. The farm has real directories, with files that are symlinks to the objects in the cache. This uses some KiB of RAM. This is important on the in-memory filesystem of Cloud Run. PyTensor accepts the moved entries and does not compile them again.

HOME, PYTENSOR_FLAGS, NUMBA_CACHE_DIR and MPLCONFIGDIR all point under /tmp. The first three are on the worker-environment allow-list of the runner (mapi_spec.run.WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST). Thus plugin code sees them after the supervisor removes the other variables from the environment. As a result, each image runs with --read-only and a tmpfs on /tmp.

docker run mapi/base-bayes runs the runner. The image gives arguments that start with - to the runner. All other commands replace the runner (docker run mapi/base-bayes python -c ...).

docs.title: The web image and the plot sandbox
docs.text:
mapi/web builds the two Vite apps with pnpm. It uses --frozen-lockfile and --ignore-scripts, so no package lifecycle scripts run. One unprivileged nginx with two server blocks serves the apps. NGINX_ENVSUBST_TEMPLATE_DIR selects which blocks nginx uses: /etc/nginx/templates/all (the default), web or plots. Origins are runtime settings. At start-up, nginx puts them into the headers.

App (:8080, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN) Plot sandbox (:8081, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN) CSP default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' (no unsafe-eval, no inline scripts); frame-src = the plots origin; connect-src = self, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT; frame-ancestors 'none' default-src 'none'; scripts, styles and images only from its own origin; connect-src = only its own /topojson/; frame-ancestors = the app origin Other headers X-Frame-Options: DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, COOP and CORP same-origin, Trusted Types in report-only mode nosniff, no-referrer, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * API access nginx sends /v1/ to MAPI_API_UPSTREAM, unbuffered, with a read timeout of one hour for SSE None: no proxy, and the CSP blocks it

The app frames the sandbox documents with sandbox="allow-scripts" and no same-origin access. Thus they have an opaque origin, and the browser gets their module scripts, styles and topojson in CORS mode. For this reason, the sandbox answers with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. The assets are static and public, and there are no cookies. For the same reason, its CSP lists the plots origin explicitly next to 'self'.

MAPI_WEB_SCRIPT_SRC_EXTRA (empty by default) adds sources to the script-src of the app. Use it only after a review, for example if a library needs 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Trusted Types stay in report-only mode until the SPA has its policy.

docs.title: Base images and pinning
docs.text:
Each base image is a build argument with a readable tag and a digest:

ARG PYTHON_IMAGE=python:3.12-slim-trixie@sha256:a6e3…11b1

The Dockerfile frontend (# syntax=) and the compose postgres image are pinned in the same way. make docker-pin resolves each tag again through the registry API. It needs no Docker daemon. Examine the diff that it makes as you examine each dependency update. make docker-pin-check fails if an image is not pinned. CI and make release-check also run it.

docs.title: Licences in the images
