docs.text: Each image has the licence files of the project and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in /usr/share/doc/mapi/. The notices list each third-party Python and JavaScript package in the image set, with its version and licence. They also contain the NOTICE files, and the licence texts of the JavaScript packages that the build compiles into the web app. When uv.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml changes, run make notices to make the file again. While the file is not current, the test suite and make release-check fail. Refer to Licensing.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/ci.yml builds each image, and the worker target, on each push and pull request. It uses the GitHub Actions layer cache. CI never pushes the images. A separate job does a check of the digest pins. It also validates the two compose files with docker compose config.

You can do a smoke test when you have built the images and a Docker daemon runs. Then uv run pytest tests/devops/test_compose_smoke.py -m docker starts postgres, gcs-shim, migrate, api and worker under a temporary project name. It publishes no host ports. Then it makes sure that api and worker started. It also makes sure that they agree on the values that bundle verification needs: the image digest and the bundle-signing key.

docs.title: Local, without Docker v0.2
docs.text:
make dev runs the whole platform on your machine without Docker. PostgreSQL comes from the pgserver wheel, and object storage comes from the GCS shim. Thus you need only the uv workspace and, for the web app, Node.js with pnpm.

make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make dev              # start everything; Ctrl-C stops everything
make seed             # in another shell: load the E33 demo data and spec
open http://127.0.0.1:5173

The quickstart tells how to fit, examine and score the demo model from the browser. This page tells what make dev runs, how to work on one component, and where the local state is.

docs.title: Signing in v0.3
docs.text:
make dev runs the servers in the dev profile. This profile is multi-tenant, with a development identity provider in the API. The browser shows a sign-in screen. Select one of the seeded accounts on the page of the provider:

Account Role admin@dev.local Admin of the default tenant and a platform operator (the admin console) analyst@dev.local runner in the default project viewer@dev.local viewer in the default project

make seed and make e2e sign in automatically as admin@dev.local. To change the account, set MAPI_DEV_ACCOUNT. The CLI signs in with mapi login --issuer https://dev-idp.mapi.localhost --discovery-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/dev/idp. Each person who can get access to the API can sign in as each of these accounts. For this reason, the profile is only for local development. MAPI_STACK_PROFILE=single-tenant make dev gives the v0.2 API without credentials. For more data, refer to Authentication and isolation.

docs.title: Signing up v0.4
docs.text:
Self-service sign-up (POST /auth/signup) is on in the dev profile. The server does not send its e-mails. The dev mailer writes each e-mail to an outbox under MAPI_DATA_DIR/outbox. make outbox prints the newest e-mails with their verification links. TO=<address> shows only the e-mails of one recipient. The API serves the same data at GET /dev/outbox?to=<address>.

A verified sign-up makes a public-tier workspace. To sign in to it, sign up with one of the seeded addresses above, because the development identity provider knows only those addresses. A public workspace runs only built-in models and declarative specs. It runs only on an executor with enforced egress and DNS. Thus the local-process executor of make dev refuses its runs (cut line A, refer to Sign-up and abuse controls).

docs.title: What make dev starts
docs.text:
scripts/dev.py is a small process supervisor. It starts each service in the sequence of its dependencies. It waits until a service is ready before it starts the services that need it. All output goes to one terminal. Each line starts with the name of its service (in colour when the output is a terminal).

flowchart LR
    pg[(postgres<br/>.local/pg)] --> migrate
    shim[gcs-shim<br/>:4443] --> api
    migrate --> api[api<br/>:8000]
    migrate --> worker
    shim --> worker
    api --> web[web<br/>:5173]
    plots[plots<br/>:5174]
Service Command Ready when postgres Embedded PostgreSQL 16 (pgserver), data in .local/pg, unix socket only. Skipped when DATABASE_URL is set. pg_ctl reports that it runs, and the mapi database is there gcs-shim mapi-gcs-shim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4443 --cors-origin <web origin> --root .local/gcs The port accepts connections migrate mapi-server migrate (runs one time) It stops with status 0 api mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 GET /healthz returns 2xx worker mapi-server worker with MAPI_EXECUTOR=local-process: dispatcher, reconciler, event ingestion and the finalizer queue. Each run is a mapi-runner supervisor process that starts its own worker process. Started web pnpm --filter @mapi/web dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort The port accepts connections plots pnpm --filter @mapi/plot-sandbox dev --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174 --strictPort The port accepts connections

Each service gets the same resolved environment: MAPI_ENV, DATABASE_URL, MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, MAPI_API_URL, MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN, MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN and MAPI_DATA_DIR. The values come from mapi_spec.localdev.LocalDev. The services read the same contract, so they always agree about ports. The configuration reference lists all the variables.

The plot sandbox is a separate origin

Plots show in an <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> that comes from MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN (port 5174), never from the app origin (port 5173). LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts the two on the same origin.

docs.title: Shutting down
docs.text:
Ctrl+C (or make stop from a different shell) stops the services in the opposite sequence of the start. Each service runs in its own process group. The supervisor sends SIGTERM to that group. If the group still runs after the grace period, the supervisor sends SIGKILL. The grace period is 10 s (change it with --grace). Child processes, for example the esbuild of Vite, stop with their parent. A second Ctrl+C stops all processes immediately. The embedded PostgreSQL stops last, but not if you ran scripts/dev.py up --keep-db.

If a long-running service stops without a command, the supervisor stops the whole stack. The supervisor then stops with a status that is not zero. It never starts a service again without a message. The log above the shutdown shows the reason.

docs.title: The first start
docs.text:
At its first start against a new environment, the worker logs no catalog for sha256:…: queued describe run. The catalog contains the steps, models and plot recipes in the runner, with their settings schemas and schema effects. A sandboxed describe run of the real runner makes the catalog. The server keeps it in a cache for each uv.lock digest. Thus the server builds it again only when the locked dependencies change. Until the catalog is ready, spec validation reports that the catalog is not available. This takes some seconds.

Runs use the same isolation as in production, but not the parts that a laptop cannot do. The run event DEV_MODE_ISOLATION tells that the worker process runs as your user, without a uid split or no_new_privs.

Plugin code runs as you, next to the platform's keys

Run only plugin code that you trust in make dev. Without a uid split, run code (plugins and the steps that they load) can read all the files that your user can read. These include the control key of the shim (.local/gcs/_shim/keys/control.json, full access to all buckets), the bundle-signing key (.local/keys/) and the executions directory. Thus a hostile plugin could forge a signed bundle, or change outputs after the finalizer did a check of them. On Linux, the orchestrator makes itself non-dumpable. Thus run code cannot read its environment (DATABASE_URL) or its memory. The worker logs the same warning when it starts.

docs.title: Everyday commands
docs.text:
Command What it does make dev (or make run) Starts the stack in the foreground make dev ONLY=api Starts api and its dependencies (gcs-shim, migrate) make dev WITHOUT=web,plots Starts all services, but not the two Vite servers (for example, while the web app is not built yet) make stop Stops a stack that runs in a different shell, then its embedded PostgreSQL make status Shows which services operate, and if PostgreSQL runs make migrate Applies database migrations one time. If necessary, it starts the embedded PostgreSQL, and then it stops it again. make db-shell psql on the dev database (the embedded server or DATABASE_URL) make seed Loads the E33 demo datasets and the eu-geo-mmm spec through the HTTP API (make seed SIZE=full for the large variant) make e2e Runs the end-to-end suites against the stack: pytest -m e2e (tests/e2e, through the Python client), then the Playwright @e2e suite (apps/web/e2e, through the browser) make outbox Shows the newest e-mails of the dev mailer and their links (sign-up verification). TO=<address> filters make clean-local Deletes MAPI_DATA_DIR (database, objects, supervisor state). It refuses while a service runs. YES=1 skips the prompt. uv run python scripts/dev.py env Prints the resolved environment as export lines, so that you can run a component manually

make seed uses only the public API. It does these steps:

  1. It makes the datasets eu_media_daily, fx_daily and holidays_eu.
  2. It uploads each table to the signed URL that the API returns.
  3. It waits for the sandboxed ingest runs.
  4. It makes the spec that points at the new dataset versions.

If you run it again, it adds new dataset versions and a new spec revision. It uses the same datasets again. make reads SIZE only from the make command line, because some toolchains (the compilers of conda) export their own SIZE variable.

uv run python scripts/seed.py --export demo/ writes the same tables, the E33 score payloads and the spec as files. You can then upload these files through the web app.

docs.title: End-to-end tests
docs.text:
make e2e does the M1 flow through the stack:

  • It uploads the E33 data, validates and fits the spec, and follows the run over SSE.
  • It does a check of the signed manifest and the bundle.
  • It scores an 8-week forecast, a new market, a weekly EUR plan and counterfactuals.
  • It probes the security boundaries that are visible from outside. The bootstrap object is gone, the server refuses forged events, and the plot iframe is an opaque origin.

Start make dev first. The two suites read the same MAPI_* variables. Thus, if you moved a port, export the variables in the shell that runs make e2e. The browser suite writes screenshots to apps/web/e2e/screenshots/ (git ignores them).

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010   # only if you moved the API
make dev                                     # shell 1
make e2e                                     # shell 2: about 25 minutes

make e2e also runs the M2 tenancy suite and the M3 suites. The M3 suites are the trust lifecycle and the whole Guided journey to an endpoint, webhooks, embeds, budget optimisation, export and deletion (refer to M3 verification). Two settings make the deletion checks complete:

  • Start the stack with MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S=0 (no grace period).
  • On a new MAPI_DATA_DIR, set MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0 (no retention lock on model bundles).

If not, those checks stop where the platform waits, and the suite skips them. Each run signs up two workspaces. The default sign-up limits are 5 for each address in each hour, and 25 for each dev.local in each day. These limits permit two runs in each hour. Thus, on a stack that you test many times, increase MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR and MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY.

Webhooks can get to receivers on your machine. In the dev profile, make dev writes a temporary CA and a certificate for 127.0.0.1 and localhost to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/. The servers trust the CA and permit the two hosts. Serve HTTPS with cert.pem and key.pem from there. Then register https://127.0.0.1:<port>/....

The mocked Playwright smoke suite (pnpm --filter @mapi/web test) serves its own build on port 5173. Thus run it only while make dev is stopped.

docs.title: Working on one component
docs.text:
You can run a component yourself, for example with a debugger or auto-reload. There are two procedures. In the first procedure, exclude the component and start it manually with the same environment:

make dev WITHOUT=api,web           # web depends on api, so exclude it too
eval "$(uv run python scripts/dev.py env)"
mapi-server api --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000

In the second procedure, replace its command with MAPI_DEV_<NAME>_CMD. The command is shell-quoted. <NAME> is GCS_SHIM, MIGRATE, API, WORKER, WEB or PLOTS:

MAPI_DEV_API_CMD="uvicorn mapi_server.app:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000" make dev

The readiness probe still applies. Thus a replacement api must answer GET /healthz.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
make dev reads your shell environment. It does not read .env, which is only for docker compose. If you set nothing, all services use the defaults above. To change a value, export the variable first:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000          # move the API (and its probe) to port 9000
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://me@localhost/mapi  # use your own PostgreSQL instead of pgserver
make dev

Export the same MAPI_* URLs in each shell that connects to the stack (make seed, make e2e, the CLI, the Python client). The configuration reference lists all the variables. This includes the variables that only compose or the images use.

docs.title: Where state lives
docs.text:
All local state is under MAPI_DATA_DIR. The default is .local/ in the repository root, and git ignores it.

.local/
├─ pg/                    PostgreSQL data directory (pgserver); log in pg/log
├─ gcs/                   GCS shim objects (buckets mapi-local-*)
│  └─ _shim/keys/         the shim's principals: control.json (control plane), exec.json (runs)
├─ keys/                  bundle-signing-p256.pem: signs bundle manifests (stands in for KMS)
├─ outbox/                the dev mailer's e-mails (make outbox, GET /dev/outbox)
├─ executions/            per-run scratch of the local executor (removed when a run ends)
└─ dev/supervisor.json    pid of the running supervisor and its services (make stop/status)

Caution

Do not delete keys/. If you delete it, you cannot use the registered model versions. Their manifests do not verify, and the API does not mint download links for them (INTEGRITY_FAILURE).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Troubleshooting tells about these problems: port conflicts, an old supervisor, PostgreSQL that does not start, failed migrations, an API that never becomes ready, and blank plots.

docs.title: M2 verification v0.3
docs.text:
Milestone M2 (cloud and multi-tenant core) has five exit criteria:

  1. 100 concurrent fits without loss.
  2. Chaos and executor conformance green.
  3. The security suite green each night.
  4. p95 time-to-RUNNING below 90 s.
  5. The cost of each run shown in the UI.

This page records how much of each criterion we verified locally. It also tells what still needs a real Google Cloud project. The local run had no Docker daemon and no cloud credentials:

  • Cloud Storage was the GCS shim.
  • Postgres was the embedded pgserver.
  • The Cloud Run Jobs executor ran against its in-memory fake Admin API (FakeCloudRun).
  • Locally signed OIDC tokens simulated the Pub/Sub pushes.
  • We validated the Terraform, but we did not apply it.

We did the verification on 2026-10-15 at commit feat/m2-e2e (v0.3 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Exit criterion Verified locally Result Still needs real GCP 100 concurrent fits without loss make load-test: 100 fits through the real dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and events path on the Cloud Run executor (fake Admin API) and the GCS shim. A second mode keeps all 100 executions live at the same time. A burst of 32 real fits ran on the live dev stack. 100/100 succeeded, with one execution and one attempt for each run. 32/32 real fits succeeded, with one attempt, ledger entry and model version for each run. The same burst on Cloud Run Jobs (real cold starts, real jobs.run quota) Chaos green make chaos 5/5 passed Cloud SQL failover. Pub/Sub redelivery from the real subscription Executor conformance green 12 cases on fake-cloudrun and on local-process, and the gate 24 passed, 3 skipped (documented capabilities that local-process does not have), 0 failed The 12 cases against the real Cloud Run Admin API (there is no live target yet, refer to the text below) Security suite nightly green make security-suite EXECUTOR=local-process. The nightly workflow is written. PASS: all 17 outcomes are acceptable for PROCESS Probes in a gVisor container (needs Docker) and in a Cloud Run Jobs execution (MICROVM) p95 time-to-RUNNING < 90 s Measured in the load test, and on the live stack Fake Cloud Run: p95 45.9–46.5 s (100 fits). Live local stack: p95 3.0 s (16 real fits) and 8.9 s (32) The real cold start of a base image of about 2.5 GB [verify M0] adds more time (refer to the warning below) Per-run cost shown in the UI Playwright against the live stack: the run page, the runs list and the usage page show the metered cost $0.0003 metered on the run page and in the list. The usage totals agree with the ledger The price table against real Cloud Run billing

M2 also adds multi-tenancy. We verified these items from end to end on the live stack:

  • Two users in two tenants, signed in through the development identity provider.
  • The API and row-level security refuse cross-tenant access.
  • Token scopes.
  • Quotas.
  • The spend-cap kill switch, which holds runs at dispatch.
  • The cost of each run.
  • The audit trail.

p95 time-to-RUNNING on real Cloud Run

For a burst of 100 fits, almost all of the 46 s p95 comes from the submit rate. MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE=150 divides 100 submissions over about 40 s. The regional jobs.run quota is 180 a minute ([verify M0]). The fake provisions in 0.3–1.5 s. On Cloud Run, the cold start of each execution adds to that time.

The p95 cold start of a base image can be more than about 40 s. Then a cold burst of 100 fits is longer than the 90 s budget. This is true also when each fit starts quickly. Measure the cold start first (refer to What remains for real GCP). Homogeneous fan-out (sweeps, SBC) uses one execution with taskCount, and thus it does not have this limit. Independent fits cannot do this.

docs.title: Load: 100 concurrent fits
docs.text:
make load-test                                    # default: fits of 0.2–3 s
LOAD_TEST_FIT_MS=40000-60000 make load-test       # 40–60 s fits: all 100 live at once

packages/server/tests/test_load_cloudrun.py submits 100 fits. They go through the production rate limits: the token bucket of the dispatcher and the 150 a minute of the executor. The backend makes errors on purpose:

  • It answers the first jobs.run calls with 429.
  • It loses two responses. This makes orphans that the executor must adopt. The executor must not submit them again.

A synthetic supervisor reads its bootstrap object. It writes its outputs through signed URLs on the real GCS shim. Its events come as OIDC-authenticated Pub/Sub pushes, with random lag and 5 % duplicates.

Mode Runs p50 / p95 / max time-to-RUNNING Most executions live at the same time Pushes (duplicates) Wall default 100/100 succeeded 28.95 / 46.45 / 48.53 s 9 525 (24) 50.5 s LOAD_TEST_FIT_MS=40000-60000 100/100 succeeded 28.47 / 45.93 / 48.09 s 100 525 (24) 105.8 s

The two modes asserted exactly one execution and one attempt for each run (no double dispatch). They also asserted that each run succeeded (no loss).

Real fits on the live stack. This test is opt-in, because each fit is a pair of processes on the host:

make dev   # with the MAPI_* ports below
MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS=32 uv run pytest -q -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py
Burst Result p50 / p95 / max time-to-RUNNING p95 queued → finished 16 real store-demand fits 16/16 succeeded 1.32 / 3.0 / 3.23 s 38.3 s 32 real store-demand fits 32/32 succeeded 3.66 / 8.91 / 9.61 s 82.0 s

For each run, the test made sure of two things. The run has exactly one row in each of run_attempts, cost_ledger and model_versions (counted directly in Postgres). The run registered a different model version.

docs.title: Chaos
docs.text:
make chaos

5/5 passed:

  • The test stopped the worker during PROVISIONING.
  • The test stopped the worker during RUNNING.
  • Event redelivery and a changed sequence of events.
  • A redelivered event with a bad HMAC. This event never moves the run forward.
  • A Postgres restart during a run.

Each case came to the correct terminal state, with no lost or duplicated attempt.

docs.title: Executor conformance
docs.text:
uv run pytest -q -rs packages/server/tests/test_executor_conformance.py

24 passed, 3 skipped. The 12 cases are:

  • Submit.
  • Orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash.
  • Safety of a duplicate submit.
  • Cancel during a run.
  • Timeout.
  • STALLED without a false LOST.
  • Confirmed cancel before retry.
  • Checkpoint resume.
  • OOM classification.
  • Fan-out with taskCount.
  • Generation verification.
  • 429 back-off.

All cases passed on fake-cloudrun. The gate test (test_conformance_report_gates_the_executor) passed for the two backends.

On local-process, the suite skipped three cases. They need capabilities that this executor does not declare: memory_limit, fanout and remote_control_api. The gate needs exactly those skips.

The suite did not select the 12 cases of the docker backend, because there is no Docker daemon.

docs.title: Security suite
docs.text:
make security-suite EXECUTOR=local-process

Result: PASS: all 17 probe outcomes acceptable for this executor. The tests of the suite also passed (9). The outcomes agree with the expected matrix for PROCESS isolation. For this isolation, the suite accepts the two outcomes for the isolation probes. But the executor must stop all platform probes:

Probe Category Outcome metadata_token, http_egress, dns_egress isolation blocked (no metadata server or egress on this host) write_outside_scratch, reuse_foreign_url, pth_injection, fork_bomb, memory_bomb, disk_bomb, log_flood isolation allowed (accepted: PROCESS is not a security boundary) read_proc1_environ, read_supervisor_mem isolation skipped (no procfs on macOS) forged_stdout_event, tampered_manifest, redos_schema, plot_xss_exfil, reuse_foreign_manifest platform blocked

The probes remove what they make. The suite removed the .pth file and the file that it wrote outside scratch.

We repaired two defects in the suite:

  • The docker and gVisor runner ran python -m mapi_security in the runner image, but the runner image never contains the suite. Now the suite is mounted read-only into the probe container.
  • --executor cloud probed the host where it ran. Now it does not run outside a Cloud Run Jobs execution.

.github/workflows/nightly.yml schedules these jobs each night:

  • Chaos.
  • Executor conformance.
  • The two load-test modes.
  • The security suite on local-process.
  • The security suite in gVisor (it installs runsc and builds the worker image).

We did a check of the workflow as YAML here. It has not run on GitHub yet.

docs.title: Multi-tenancy through the live stack
docs.text:
make e2e    # API suites (M1 + M2), then the browser @e2e suites

The M2 API suite, tests/e2e/test_m2_tenancy_stack.py (11 tests, about 2 minutes), does these steps:

  1. The platform operator makes two internal tenants. Each tenant has an invited admin, the dev accounts analyst@dev.local and viewer@dev.local.
  2. Each admin signs in, which accepts the invitation, and makes project growth.
  3. Each admin uploads data under the same dataset names. Each admin fits the scikit-learn store-demand model of the corpus and scores it.

On that state, the suite proves these items.

Sign-in

  • The BFF flow works: /auth/login, the IdP, then /auth/callback, with PKCE S256.
  • A replayed callback gets 401.
  • A cookie mutation without X-CSRF-Token, or from a foreign origin, gets 403.
  • Logout stops the session.
  • ID-token bearers work.
  • API tokens work and are bound to their project. After revocation, they do not work (401).

API isolation. The other tenant always gets 404 or 403, never a 2xx or a 5xx:

  • On 18 project-scoped reads: datasets and versions, the preview, the data artifact, specs, runs, logs, run plots, models, versions, artifacts, ui/ views and plots.
  • On the SSE stream.
  • On 10 writes: cancel, retry, resume, spec revision, dry-run, score, evaluate, fit, upload and new version.
  • On tenant routes: tenant, projects, members, audit and usage.
  • When the caller names the project of the other tenant explicitly.

Lists never show the rows of the other tenant. The same dataset://growth/... ref resolves to the data of each tenant. The lineage dataset hashes are different.

Row-level security, directly in Postgres (as mapi_app)

  • FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is on for each table that we examined.
  • A new connection without a tenant fails closed.
  • With app.tenant_id set, each table shows the rows of the caller and none of the rows of the other tenant.
  • The caller cannot see or update the run of the other tenant by id.
  • If you move a row to a different tenant, this violates the policy.
  • The setting is local to the transaction. After commit, a pooled connection sees nothing.

Scopes

  • A models:read token can read. It gets 403 on fit, score and token minting, and on the project of a different tenant.
  • A runs:create token can fit. The audit log shows that token as the source of the run.

Quotas. These two limits answer 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. They have no effect on the other tenant:

  • A tenant cap of vcpu_seconds_per_day=1.
  • A token vcpu_seconds_budget=1.

Kill switch. This test pauses the worker for a short time (SIGSTOP). Thus a run is always first in the queue. Then:

  • The operator makes the tenant verified and sets global_spend_cap_micros=1.
  • The queued run stays queued across many dispatcher polls. Thus the dispatcher holds it.
  • New runs of that tenant get 429 with the spend-cap message.
  • The dispatcher continues to admit and dispatch an internal tenant.
  • When the tenant is internal again, the dispatcher leases the held run, and the run succeeds.

Cost. For each fit and score:

  • Run.cost is metered (estimated=false, one attempt billed, amount_micros > 0, a price version, and vCPU- and GiB-seconds).
  • There is one actual ledger row for each attempt, in the correct tenant.
  • GET /v1/usage and the tenant usage are equal to the ledger or more.

Audit

  • The tenant log has project.create, run.create, token.create and token.revoke.
  • The platform log has tenant.create, quota.update, kill_switch.update and auth.login.
  • The other tenant cannot read the log.

docs.title: The browser flow
docs.text:
MAPI_E2E=1 pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec playwright test e2e/m2-flow.e2e.spec.ts

Chromium runs the M2 browser flow, apps/web/e2e/m2-flow.e2e.spec.ts (4 tests):

  1. Sign in through the account chooser of the IdP.
  2. Use the tenant switcher. Change to the seeded tenant. The selection stays after a reload.
  3. Fit from the spec editor and wait for succeeded. The run page shows Metered · price table … · 1 attempt billed and cost $0.0003. The runs list and the usage page also show the cost.
  4. Mint a models:read token, then revoke it. Before revocation, the API refuses a fit with it (403). After revocation, the token gets 401.
  5. In the admin console, do these steps:
    1. Make the tenant verified.
    2. Set a spend cap.
    3. The next fit of the tenant admin gets the spend-cap message.
    4. Remove the cap (type REMOVE).
    5. Find kill_switch.update and tenant.update in the audit log.

tests/e2e/m2_browser_seed.py seeds the tenant, and puts the stack back after the test. We examined the screenshots in apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m2-*.png (git ignores them). They caused these fixes:

  • Costs below one cent showed as $0.00. A 3 s ingest cost $0.000047. The spend-cap badge for a 1-micro cap showed "$0.00 per day". Now amounts below $0.0001 keep two significant digits.
  • Session usage showed as "-" in "By token". The group key of the server is -. Now the page shows the label "Signed-in users".
  • Memory showed "0 GiB·h". Now it shows GiB-seconds below one hour.
  • A finished run without output showed "No output captured yet".
  • The project switcher cut tenant and project names short, also on wide screens.

docs.text:

  • The nightly workflow has not run yet. .github/workflows/nightly.yml has no remote to run on here. Its gVisor job (which installs runsc on the runner) is not tested.

docs.title: What remains for real GCP
docs.text:
All items below need a Google Cloud project. Use a temporary dev environment. Build it as Google Cloud deployment tells. The values below are placeholders from infra/terraform/envs/dev/terraform.tfvars.example:

export ENV=dev REGION=europe-west4
export CONTROL=acme-mapi-dev-control EXEC=acme-mapi-dev-exec DATA=acme-mapi-dev-data
export EXEC_SA=mapi-$ENV-exec@$EXEC.iam.gserviceaccount.com
export NET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid SUBNET=mapi-$ENV-exec-paid-jobs

docs.title: 1. Stand the environment up
docs.text:
deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh --env $ENV --region $REGION --control-project $CONTROL \
  --data-project $DATA --build-project acme-mapi-dev-build --exec-project paid=$EXEC \
  --state-project acme-mapi-dev-build
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV --foundation
deploy/gcp/build-push.sh --env $ENV
deploy/gcp/deploy.sh --env $ENV            # migrations, apply, smoke test

docs.title: 2. Work through the M0 checklist
docs.text:
The M0 verification checklist lists each [verify M0] item, with its pass condition. The checklist has four areas:

  • DNS response policy: the Direct VPC resolver obeys it, with root wildcard and bypass rules.
  • Network: egress is really denied, and VPC-SC applies on Jobs.
  • Sandbox: gen2 uid split with seccomp, no_new_privs and ptrace denial. Env-only overrides. Ephemeral disk and the in-memory filesystem limits. Bootstrap read-then-delete.
  • Platform:
    • Quotas: 1,000 Jobs and 1,000 running executions in each region, 180 jobs.run a minute.
    • The Logging → Pub/Sub path and its labels.
    • Push to an internal service.
    • Pooled connections.
    • BYPASSRLS on Cloud SQL.
    • runWithOverrides without actAs.
    • Image indexes.

docs.title: 3. Cold start and p95 time-to-RUNNING
docs.text:
Measure one cold execution for each base image. Overrides change only env. Thus this measures exactly what the dispatcher does:

for base in base-bayes base-ml base-forecast; do
  gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-$base-s --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
    --update-env-vars MAPI_RUN_ID=coldstart,MAPI_NONCE=none --wait --format='value(name)'
done
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name:mapi-$ENV-" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='table(timestamp,resource.labels.job_name,textPayload)'

The supervisor stops immediately, because it finds no bootstrap object. The cold start is the time from the createTime of the execution to its first log line. Then run the burst through the deployed API with a token that has the admin scope:

MAPI_API_URL=https://api.$ENV.example.com MAPI_TOKEN=<token> MAPI_PROJECT=<tenant>/<project> \
MAPI_E2E_BURST_RUNS=100 uv run pytest -q -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m2_burst_stack.py

The test asserts no loss or duplication (through the API) and a p95 time-to-RUNNING below 90 s. It prints the percentiles.

docs.title: 4. Security suite inside a Cloud Run Jobs execution
docs.text:
--executor cloud runs only in a Job execution. The runner images do not contain the suite. Thus build a probe image on the deployed base, and run it as its own Job. Use the same network and identity as the inventory Jobs:

REPO=$(terraform -chdir=infra/terraform/envs/$ENV output -raw image_repository)   # …/mapi-$ENV-images
IMAGE=$REPO/base-bayes@sha256:<digest from deploy/gcp/.out/$ENV/images.tfvars.json>
PROBE=$REPO/security-probe:$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
printf 'FROM %s\nCOPY security/src /opt/mapi-security\nENV PYTHONPATH=/opt/mapi-security\n' "$IMAGE" \
  | docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$PROBE" -f - . && docker push "$PROBE"
gcloud run jobs create mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION \
  --image "$PROBE" --command python --args=-m,mapi_security,run,--executor,cloud \
  --service-account $EXEC_SA --network $NET --subnet $SUBNET --network-tags mapi-exec \
  --vpc-egress all-traffic --execution-environment gen2 --max-retries 0 --task-timeout 15m
gcloud run jobs execute mapi-$ENV-security-probe --project $EXEC --region $REGION --wait
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_job AND resource.labels.job_name=mapi-$ENV-security-probe" \
  --project $EXEC --freshness 1h --format='value(textPayload)'

Pass: PASS: all 17 probe outcomes acceptable for this executor. On MICROVM, each isolation probe must be BLOCKED or SKIPPED. The DNS probe passes only if the authoritative query log of the zone also never sees the name of the probe (checklist, network section). After the test, delete the probe Job. To run this each night, add the probe image to build-push.sh and the Job to infra/terraform/modules/exec. We have not done this yet.

docs.title: 5. Executor conformance against the real Admin API
docs.text:
There is no live conformance target yet. packages/server/tests/mapi_server_testkit/conformance.py operates only fake-cloudrun, local-process and docker. A cloudrun-live target needs a harness that does these actions:

  • It builds CloudRunJobsExecutor from settings (MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT=$EXEC, the dev inventory).
  • It causes the faults through real means. It stops an execution with gcloud run jobs executions cancel. It causes an OOM with a run that is larger than class S. It causes a 429 when it sets MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE above the quota.
  • It marks itself cloud.

Until then, run the chaos cases manually against the deployed stack:

# orphan adoption: scale the orchestrator worker pool (manual scaling) to 0 right after a
# submit, then back (`gcloud beta run worker-pools update --help` names the flag of your gcloud)
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 0
gcloud beta run worker-pools update mapi-$ENV-orchestrator --project $CONTROL --region $REGION --scaling 1
# Cloud SQL failover (regional/HA instance)
gcloud sql instances failover mapi-$ENV-pg --project $CONTROL

After each case, each run that the case affects must come to a terminal state, with exactly one attempt for each execution.

docs.title: 6. Cost
docs.text: Compare the cost_ledger of one day with the billing export for the exec project. If list prices or discounts are different, adjust the price table (MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH).

docs.title: M3 verification v0.4
docs.text:
Milestone M3 (Guided mode and integrations) has three exit criteria:

  1. Five non-technical testers complete upload → report → scenario without help in less than 30 minutes.
  2. An external budget optimiser works against an endpoint.
  3. Cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins (untrusted data, trusted code).

This page records how much of each criterion we verified locally, and the measured numbers. It also tells what the runs found and fixed, and what remains. We cannot simulate real testers. Thus we prepared the first criterion, but it is not met. An automated "unaided tester" script measures the minimum of the time budget. We also examined the screens as an analyst who uses them for the first time. The protocol for the five testers below is the work that remains.

We did the verification on 2026-10-16 on branch feat/m3-e2e (v0.4 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS), against a live make dev stack:

  • The API, worker, web app and plot sandbox on ports that are not the defaults (API 18000, GCS shim 14443, web 15173, plot sandbox 15174).
  • The dev profile: the development identity provider and the outbox mailer.
  • The GCS shim in place of Cloud Storage, and the embedded pgserver Postgres.
  • All runs on the local-process executor (no Docker daemon, no cloud project).
  • MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S=0 and MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0, so that we could watch a deletion to the end.
  • Higher MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR and MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY, because each run signs up new workspaces from one address.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Exit criterion Verified locally Result Still needs 5 non-technical testers: upload → report → scenario without help in < 30 min The browser script apps/web/e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts clicks through the whole Guided flow on a realistic spreadsheet, and measures the time of each step. We examined each screen for plain language, next steps and dead ends 135 s of automated wall time. The system used almost all of this time (the beliefs preview, the fit, the exact runs). We found and repaired six usability defects. Two of them were dead ends Five real testers (protocol) An external optimiser works against an endpoint The optimiser adapter of the v0.4 client (removed in v0.5) against the live endpoint. The optimiser uses the protocol of the external framework Under the model, the selected allocation is better than the current one: +0.22 % revenue for next quarter at the same budget. It came from 25 candidate allocations (22 score requests) in 220 s The in-sandbox optimize job (M4) Cut line A A self-service sign-up makes a public workspace. The e-mail is verified, and the server refuses uploaded code (uploaded_code_allowed: false). Built-ins and declarative specs run. Here they ran on an internal workspace that an operator promoted, because the local executor admits only trusted tiers Pass Public workspaces that run on docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs. Shared tiers can use only these executors

tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py (15 tests, 7 minutes) also tested all M3 additions from end to end through the API: 15 passed.

docs.title: The API journey
docs.text:
make dev        # with the variables above
make e2e        # or: uv run --with-editable ../optimizer-framework python -m pytest -s -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py

The tests use the workspace of one analyst, from outside the processes. Each row is one test, in sequence. The times are the wall-clock seconds of the last run.

Step What is checked Time Sign-up POST /auth/signup → the test reads the verification e-mail from GET /dev/outbox → POST /auth/verify-email makes a public workspace, with the person who signed up as admin. The operator promotes it to internal (the local executor runs only trusted tiers) 0.03 Guided data All four templates are in the list. The test profiles the CSV of the analyst locally, as the browser does (5 regions × 3 channels × 104 weeks, columns Week, Region, Revenue, TV Spend, Search Spend, Social Spend, Avg Price). Role detection answers each question correctly, each with a plain reason. The draft validates. The upload ingests with the mapping of the draft. Detection on the stored version (columns.json) gives the same answers 13.3 MFF The same data as an MFF long table (Period, Geography, VariableName, VariableValue) ingests to the same variables and roles 8.3 Business priors ROI and share ranges and a baseline share (true to the simulation), and a lift test. A sandboxed translate_priors run translates them. The translated priors hold 81 %, 76 % and 80 % of their mass in the stated 80 % ranges. The test writes them into the spec with the id of the run 13.3 Tiny fit 150 tuning steps and draws × 2 chains. The test measures each check of the scorecard of the template, in plain words with a docs anchor and an action. Its gate (blocked: the chains do not agree) is exactly what mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate calculates. The server refuses the promotion with the checks of that gate 30.9 Endpoint fit 1000 × 4 chains, target_accept 0.95. Convergence passes or gives a warning. The holdout error is below 1 %, coverage passes, and each plausibility check passes 61.0 What-if vs Run exact The response grid for each draw answers a slider immediately. "Run exact" (compiled by the server) scores the fit window. tv × 0.5 → grid −454,590 vs exact −454,241 (sd 14,003). search × 1.5 and tv × 0.8 → −4,762 vs −4,255 (sd 14,980). The server refuses multipliers outside the grid 10–13 for each exact run Forecast, channel off An 8-week forecast fan with history and the split line. tv off over the fit window gives −1,046,519, against −1,046,414 from the multiplier 0 of the grid 10 each Promotion 409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED, which names the checks with warnings. Then an admin override with a reason, which the audit log records. History, schema with an example call, and snippets (no snippet contains a secret) 0.01 Score token A score:<alias> token scores the example of the endpoint (8-week forecast) as an xarray tree. It gets 403 on datasets, specs, webhooks and models 10.0 Webhooks An HTTPS receiver on 127.0.0.1 (with the certificate of the dev profile) gets run.succeeded, model.version.ready, endpoint.promoted and score.completed. The test verifies each with mapi_client.webhooks.verify. No body contains a data value, link or secret. The delivery log shows them. A replay comes as the same event with a new delivery id. A different secret fails verification 0.3 Embed A saved platform-recipe plot as an embed link. The public view needs no credentials. Each write method answers 405. The sandbox page has its CSP. After revocation, 410 LINK_EXPIRED < 1 Budget optimisation Refer to An external optimiser 219.6 GDPR export A zip with 49 files downloads. It holds the records and objects of the workspace. It does not contain the webhook secret, the score token or the ID token 16.4 Deletion 645 tenant rows and 285 objects before the purge. After the purge, no table with a tenant_id has a row, but these are retained: audit_events (53), cost_ledger (33) and the deletion record. There is no object under t/<tenant>/ in the five buckets. A signed tenant.deletion.completed goes to the receiver. The server refuses the admin and the score token 13.4

docs.title: An external optimiser against the live endpoint
docs.text:
An external optimisation framework (a sibling project) has the model and optimiser interfaces. The test registered the endpoint-backed model adapter of the v0.4 client as one of its models. Then it ran an optimiser that uses its protocol. The optimiser moves a step of budget between two channels while this increases the predicted revenue of the endpoint. When no move increases it, the optimiser makes the step half as large. Each candidate is one score request against the live endpoint (inline XrJSON, score:<alias> token).

Search Social TV Predicted revenue (13 weeks) Current plan 16,136 9,737 37,890 929,612 Chosen 19,324 9,737 34,702 931,620 (+0.22 %)

25 candidates used 22 requests (the cache answered the others). The total time was 220 s. Each request is a sandboxed score run, so the wall time is mostly run start-up. You cannot put the markets of a geo MMM into one request (new markets are pooled). For this reason, the in-sandbox optimize job (M4) is the path for longer optimisations.

docs.title: The unaided-tester script
docs.text:
MAPI_E2E=1 pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec playwright test e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts

tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py makes a new project and writes the spreadsheet of the analyst. The script then does the tasks that the five testers will do, without hesitation, as the admin of the default tenant. Screenshots go to apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m3-*.png (git ignores them). The times go to m3-timings.json.

The times below are from the release check of v0.4.0 on the integrated develop branch (2026-10-16, the same laptop and settings). The first run on feat/m3-e2e took 137 s.

Step What the script does Wall time (s) 1. Template Starts where sign-in goes (/) and finds Guided. "What do you want to learn?" → Geo marketing mix 0.7 2. Your data Gives the analysis a name and selects the CSV. Makes sure that each question has the correct answer. Upload and continue (upload, sandboxed check) 4.7 3. What you believe Selects tv, states an ROI of 1.5 to 4, shows a preview of what it means (a sandboxed run) and continues 20.7 4. Fit the model Fit the model. Phases and progress in plain language. See the results 78.5 5. Results Headline numbers, ROI and share for each channel, two charts, the sanity scorecard 0.4 6. What if… Search spend +20 % on the slider (immediate), Run exact, Turn off tv, a 13-week forecast 29.6 Upload → report → scenario 134.6 7. Share The gate explained. The reason of an admin. Approve and go live. An embed link 0.4

The system uses almost all of the 135 s: the beliefs preview, the fit (79 s), the exact run, the channel-off run and the forecast. Clicks, typing and page loads take some seconds. A person reads, hesitates and explores. Thus the 30-minute budget is mostly the time that the testers need to understand each screen. The script shows that the system uses about two and a half minutes of it on this laptop.

The second test goes through the Integrations hub:

  • The overview cards and the endpoint page.
  • Try it (validate, then score: 8.6 s), and a copy of the curl snippet.
  • A score:<alias> token from the shortcut of the snippet.
  • A webhook with its one-time secret.
  • The embed link. It shows read-only in a new page (no button to push). After the hub revokes it, the page shows "This link has expired or was revoked".

docs.title: What the review found and fixed
docs.text:
We read each screenshot as an analyst who uses the app for the first time. We asked these questions: Is the language plain? Is the next step clear? Is there a dead end? Does the app explain each error? We fixed these items on this branch, each with a test:

Finding Where Fix "Run exact" always failed on the live stack ("User or plugin code failed"). The compiled counterfactual named no data What if… POST /v1/guided/requests:compile names the fit dataset in data for what-ifs and presets over the fit window. The server refuses a score request without data with 422 before a run starts "Forecast error on held-back weeks: 83 %" for an error of 0.8 % (mapi_sdk reports MAPE in percent) Results The headline reads the measured fraction of the scorecard Dead end: the fit of the template failed the convergence checks on two years of weekly data. The advice of the checks ("raise target_accept") names settings that Guided screens do not show. Share showed "cannot go live" Results, Share The geo_mmm template (1.1.0) samples longer and more carefully. A convergence check with a warning or failure offers Fit again, more carefully. A blocked Share step links to it Beliefs that the analyst did not state: each channel started selected with an ROI range of 0.5–4 (the true ROI of search was 6.3). But the page says "leave a channel unticked if you have no view" What you believe Channels start not selected. When you select one, it starts from the sensible range "Results without any media: between −164 % and 271 %" Beliefs preview Without a stated baseline: "anything from none to all of your results - the model has no view yet" A revoked embed link continued to show for one minute (Cache-Control: public, max-age=60) Embed page private, no-cache: revocation applies on the next load Jargon: "y_hat" on the axis and caption of the fit chart. "evenly spaced (W-SUN)". "the host did not resolve (gaierror)". "Sampler convergence" first under Share a chart Report, data step, webhook dialog, Share The name of the dataset ("revenue"). "weekly, on Sundays". "no such name". Result charts first

We also fixed this item: mapi_client refused to upload an MFF table (a CSV file) with the mapping of a Guided MFF draft.

We saw these items and left them for later. They do not block the flow, and we noted them for the sessions of the testers:

  • The fit chart showed markets under the dim name geo. The y axis of the forecast chart started at zero, and this made the fan flat. The M3 review fixed the two items: panels use the name of the dataset, and the axis fits the band.
  • The endpoint page showed the user id of the person who promoted a version, not a name. The M3 review fixed this: names come from the members of the project.
  • The header showed Expert mode on the Integrations hub. That test runs in a new browser context, and there the default tenant (not a self-service tenant) started in Expert mode. The browser remembers the selection. Since then, a self-service workspace starts in Guided mode, and Expert navigation and Home link to Guided.
  • The fit takes about 80 s with the stronger settings (30 s before). This is still well in the budget.

docs.title: Protocol for the five non-technical testers
docs.text: The exit criterion needs people. Do this protocol with five testers, one at a time. Use a stack like the stack above (or staging). Record the results on the observation sheet.

docs.title: Who
docs.text:
• Five persons who analyse marketing or sales results in spreadsheets (marketing analysts, media planners, finance business partners). They must have no statistics or programming training, other than spreadsheet formulas. Select them with two questions: "Have you fitted a regression or written Python or R?" (no) and "Do you work with weekly spend and sales by market?" (yes).
  • None of them has seen modeling-api before. Nobody from the team that built it.

docs.title: Setup (before each session)
docs.text:
1. Make a new workspace for the tester. Sign up at /signup with their work address, in a new browser profile. Sign in after the e-mail link. This opens an empty Guided page. A self-service workspace starts in Guided mode on all browsers. If you use an internal tenant that an operator made (a stack without a sandboxed executor), the session starts on Expert Home. Then the tester must find Guided in the sidebar as part of T1.
  2. Put the spreadsheet on the desktop of the tester. uv run python tests/e2e/m3_browser_seed.py seed --run <id> writes weekly_media_by_region.csv (two years, five regions, three channels). You can also use the anonymised data of the tester in the same shape.
  3. Prepare a screen recorder, a stopwatch and the observation sheet. The facilitator sits next to or behind the tester. The facilitator does not touch the keyboard.

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
Read this aloud, word for word:

"Thank you for your help. We test the software, not you. If something is difficult, it is our fault. Please think aloud: say what you look for and what you think will occur. I cannot help you during the tasks. If you would stop in real life, tell me, and we go to the next task. You have a maximum of 30 minutes for all tasks."

Then give one task card at a time.

Task Card Success means T1 Upload "Here is last two years' media spend and revenue by region. Load it into the tool so it can explain what each channel brings in." The analysis gets to "What you believe" with correct answers for Revenue, Week, Region, the three spend columns and Avg Price T2 Report "Get the tool to tell you which channel returns the most per euro, and whether you can trust the numbers." The fit finishes. The tester names the best channel and its range, and says in their own words what the scorecard concluded T3 Scenario "Next quarter you could move 20 % more into search. What would it do to revenue? How sure is the tool?" The tester gives the change in revenue with its range (immediate or exact), from the What if… step

The optional "What you believe" step is part of T1 to T2. Testers can skip it.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Unaided: the facilitator answers no question about the product. Permitted: say the task card again, "what would you do if I were not here?", "please keep thinking aloud". All other help is an assist. Record it. A task with an assist is not unaided.
  • Give-up: the tester says that they stop, or 12 minutes go by on one task. Record it and give the next card. A later task can need the result of an earlier task. If this occurs, the facilitator does that step without comment. The time of the later task starts after this step.
  • The time to wait for the fit is part of the 30 minutes (about 1.5 minutes on a laptop).

docs.title: Metrics and pass mark
docs.text:
For each tester and task, record these items:

  • Completion (unaided, assisted or failed).
  • Time on task.
  • The number of errors (a wrong turn that the tester had to undo).
  • The Single Ease Question (1 = very difficult to 7 = very easy) after each task.

After the session, record the System Usability Scale (10 items) and two open questions: "What was most confusing?" and "What would you trust least?".

The criterion is met when all five testers complete T1, T2 and T3 unaided with a total under 30 minutes. Also report the median and maximum total time, the mean SEQ for each task and the mean SUS (target: more than 68). Each assist, give-up or error that occurs again is a defect. Repair it before the public launch, also when the five testers pass.

docs.title: Observation sheet
docs.text:
Copy one sheet for each tester.

Field T1 Upload T2 Report T3 Scenario Start / end (mm:ss) Completed (unaided / assisted / failed) Errors (wrong turns, with the screen) Assists (what was said) Words or screens the tester did not understand Answer given (T2: best channel, trust; T3: change and range) SEQ (1-7) Session Tester (role, years of experience; no name) Total time SUS score Most confusing Would trust least Facilitator notes (quotes, hesitations, where the cursor went first)

docs.title: What remains unverified
docs.text:
• The five testers. We did only the automated minimum and an expert review (above).
  • Real Google Cloud. Cloud Storage (the GCS shim was in its place), Cloud Run Jobs (the local-process executor ran all runs), Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL, Identity Platform, Cloud Armor (the policy is Terraform, validated and never applied) and Cloud Logging retention. The cold start of the base images adds time to each fit, exact run and optimiser evaluation.
  • Docker. There is no daemon here. We did not run the images, the docker and docker-gvisor executors or the compose stack. Thus public (shared-tier) workspaces never ran a fit. We did a check of the admission rule of cut line A, but not of its sandbox.
  • Plotly rendering. Static renders and embeds were only Vega-Lite. Plotly needs kaleido and a Chrome in the runner image (MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED). This laptop does not have them.
  • Identity verification by a vendor. Only the fake IdentityVerifier and the manual verification of the operators are available. We did not test a vendor integration.
  • Real e-mail. The dev outbox was in place of SMTP. We did not test deliverability, SPF/DKIM and bounce handling.
  • Webhooks to the internet. Deliveries went to a receiver on 127.0.0.1 through the dev allow-list. Only unit tests include the full SSRF policy for public hosts.
  • Bundle retention. With a retention lock (the default, and 30 days when deployed), a purge stops at the model bundles. It continues when the lock expires. Locally, we did a check only up to the stop, not of the continuation after 30 days. The deletion test of the journey does this check on a stack without MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS=0.
  • The in-sandbox optimize job came later (v0.5, on mmm-framework). Here the optimiser ran on the client.

docs.title: M3.5 verification v0.5
docs.text:
M3.5 adds these items: workflows, governance policies and validations, the Data and Model Explorers, mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, the statsmodels time-series models, About cards and Help me choose. Each part has unit, integration and mocked-browser tests. This page records the next step. The five journeys below run through the running stack, from outside its processes. Real fits run in the runner, the real orchestrator operates the workflow runs, and the web app sends requests to the real API.

We did the verification on 2026-10-16 on branch fix/m35-e2e (v0.5 development), on an Apple-silicon laptop (8 cores, 16 GB, macOS), against a live make dev stack:

  • The API, worker, web app (Vite dev server) and plot sandbox on ports that are not the defaults (API 18000, GCS shim 14443, web 15173, plot sandbox 15174), with their own MAPI_DATA_DIR.
  • The dev profile: the development identity provider (admin@dev.local submits, analyst@dev.local reviews) and the outbox mailer.
  • The GCS shim in place of Cloud Storage, and the embedded pgserver Postgres.
  • All runs on the local-process executor (no Docker daemon, no cloud project).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Journey Verified through the live stack Result 1. The canonical time-series workflow A weekly KPI with a unit root (a random walk and a price driver with a true effect of -3). It went through the ts_readiness_arimax template. We followed it over server-sent events (API), in the run monitor (browser, Expert) and as a Guided recipe that we started from the Data Explorer ADF (p = 0.62), KPSS, Phillips-Perron and Zivot-Andrews all show that the series wanders. The branch differences it (and skips the seasonal difference), and records the four values that it read. The AIC search selects ARIMA(1, 1, 1). The fitted ARIMAX and the backtest use exactly [1, 1, 1] with price. Six expanding-window folds score ARIMAX and the naive benchmarks for each horizon. ARIMAX is better (MAE 1.45 against naive 1.68), and the workflow selects it. The governance node passes the default forecasting policy. Pass, after two fixes (the workflow graph of the dev server, the first run of a recipe) 2. Governance A project policy that needs null.permutation_target and null.noise_regressors with the approval of a reviewer. ARIMAX fitted on real signal and on pure noise Noise: the shuffled-target test fails (across runs, 13 to 18 of 19 shuffled fits were equally good, p = 0.7-0.95). The validation is checks_failed, and promotion answers 409 NOT_VALIDATED. Signal: p = 0.05 (better than all shuffled fits), and fake drivers get 0.1 % of the result, awaiting_approval. The server refuses promotion until approval. The approval of the submitter gets SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN. The reviewer (an editor with the reviewer capability) approves, and the result is validated. Promotion succeeds. The evidence pack exports as HTML (no script) and JSON (with its digest). Pass, after three fixes (the families of the policy, the reviewer capability in the client, an upload of the same data again) 3. mmm-framework mmm.bayesian (150 tuning steps and draws, 2 chains), pooled over 3 regions, 2 channels, 40 weeks Fitted in about 30 s. The Model Explorer shows the contributions and response curves (they do not decrease when spend increases, for the two channels). A budget plan keeps the total and obeys the 0.5-1.5x bounds of tv. It reports the chance to be better than the plan of today, and a 5-point efficient frontier, in about 10 s. Pass, after one fix 4. Explorers and the chooser The Data Explorer of the unit-root series. A statsmodels VAR(2) on three weekly series. Help me choose for "forecast weekly sales with drivers" Stationarity for each series. Impulse responses with bands, and a variance decomposition whose shares add up to 1. The browser shows the two in the plot sandbox. The chooser now puts ts.sarimax first with four reasons and no caution, and its About card opens. Pass, after two fixes 5. The CLI mapi workflows validate, apply and run --watch on the canonical document of the cookbook, exactly as docs/snippets/cli_v05.sh runs them (with a different project name) 23 nodes are valid. The live board prints each node and decision. The rolling-origin backtest (window 104) and the Diebold-Mariano node run. The exit status is 0, with the reference of the fitted model. Pass

Two suites pass:

  • tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py (5 tests, the API and the CLI, about 5 minutes).
  • apps/web/e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts (7 tests, the browser in Expert and Guided mode, about 3 minutes with a 90-second seed).

The unit-root tests of the canonical run did not change. Thus the cookbook run from the CLI gets them from the cache (cached_from names that run). We also ran the earlier end-to-end suites (M1 to M3) against the same stack. Refer to Full verification set.

docs.title: What the runs found and fixed
docs.text:
The runs found eight defects. The unit, integration and mocked-browser tests could not find them. Each fix has a regression test.

Found in Defect Fix Governance A policy with applies_to: {families: [ts]} applied to no statsmodels model. This policy is the example on all governance pages and in forecast-policy.yaml. The manifests of the statsmodels models declare the family forecast (or ts_multivariate, regime). Thus the checks, approval and promotion gate of the policy never applied, and there was no message. The model fitted on noise got only the default policy. It became validated, and it was promoted. A family agrees with the declared family of a model, or with the namespace of its id (mapi_spec.governance.PolicyMatch). Governance The client could not give a member the reviewer capability (add_member and set_role removed it). Thus you could not set up the second person without raw HTTP. tenants.add_member(..., capabilities=[...]) and tenants.set_capabilities(...), sync and async. Each upload An upload of data that was uploaded before failed its ingest with INTEGRITY_FAILURE ("ui/explore/index.json already holds different content"). This occurred for the same file as the next version, or in a different dataset or project. Ingest outputs are stored under the content hash of the data. Since v0.5, the Data Explorer views that an ingest writes name the dataset version and contain plot timestamps. The explorer views of each ingest are stored under its run (t/<tenant>/datasets/<sha>/runs/<run>/ui/explore/). The data and its sidecars keep the strict same-content check. mmm-framework api.explorations.view(..., "response_curves") (and mapi explore --show) returned the list of plots of the section, not its view. This occurred for each section whose name comes after plots in alphabetical sequence (residuals, response_curves, stationarity, stl...). The code looks for the exact view first. Plot files never agree. Chooser Help me choose put ts.sarimax in position six for "forecast weekly sales with drivers". But it is the only model that agrees with all four answers. Items that did not answer a question also got a score of 1.0, and the difficulty decided ties. The number of answers that an item agrees with explicitly decides ties. Browser On the dev server, the first page that opened a workflow graph crashed with "Invalid hook call" in ReactFlowProvider. A route that loaded while the YAML worker of the spec editor started for the first time failed with "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module". Vite found React Flow and the dependency of the worker late. It optimised them in a second pass and loaded the page again. The dev server pre-bundles the two when it starts (apps/web/dev-prebundle.ts). A test makes sure that the list includes each package that a web worker imports. Production builds were not affected. Data Explorer The overview of the most usual upload, a time dimension with the name time, showed "2 variables over 156 time". The name of the time dimension is now its frequency ("156 weeks"). Guided recipes The first run of a recipe in a project by a Guided user failed with "The recipe did not start: Not Found". The click made the workflow from the template. Then it sent the run to /v1/workflows//runs with the id from when the page was shown. The mock project always had the workflow. A run can name its workflow. The recipe runs the workflow that it made.

docs.title: The earlier journeys, brought up to date
docs.text:
We ran the M1 and M3 journeys against the same stack. Four of their assertions were not correct after M3.5, but the product was correct:

  • The E33 spec on mmm-framework does not have scaling or lag steps now. M1 now does a check of its currency, weekly and holiday steps.
  • Its scores have six components, not five. The M1 browser flow counts the rows.
  • A Guided draft records no units. Thus the test finds the budget plan by the name of its KPI.
  • The M3 webhook receiver verified deliveries some minutes after they came. This was later than the 5-minute signature tolerance. Now it verifies each delivery when it comes, as a real receiver does.

docs.title: An observation, since fixed
docs.text:
We had a project policy that made the shuffled-target test blocking. Under this policy, the ARIMA(1, 1, 1) of the cookbook on the random walk failed the test. 4 of 19 shuffled refits were equally good (p = 0.25). But the model was 25 % better than the naive forecast on the held-out weeks. The null shuffled the target in blocks. This kept most of the persistence that a differenced model uses.

The M3.5 review replaced this null before the release. Now, for a model with drivers, the null shuffles the drivers in blocks and does not change the result. For a model without drivers, the null shuffles the differences and integrates them again. The null test scores each fit by its holdout skill against the null forecast (refer to null tests explained). On the same data, the model of the cookbook is now better than all 20 shuffled fits (p = 0.048).

docs.title: How to rerun
docs.text:
Start a stack on free ports with its own data directory. The variables are those of local development:

export MAPI_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18000 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:14443
export MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15173 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:15174
export VITE_API_BASE=$MAPI_API_URL MAPI_DATA_DIR=$PWD/.local/m35e2e
make dev                    # in one shell; `make stop` with the same variables stops it

Then, in a different shell with the same variables:

uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py -s          # the API and CLI journeys
pnpm --filter @mapi/web exec env MAPI_E2E=1 \
  playwright test e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts                    # the browser journeys
make e2e                                                      # or every end-to-end suite

Each suite makes its own project in the default tenant (m35e2e-<id>, m35ui-<id>). It deletes the project at the end. To keep the project and look at it in the app, set MAPI_E2E_KEEP=1. The suites write the times to $MAPI_DATA_DIR/e2e/m35-timings.json and apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m35-timings.json. The browser suite saves its screens as apps/web/e2e/screenshots/m35-*.png (git ignores them).

docs.text:
These are the wall-clock seconds of the last run, on the laptop above (no Docker, no cold starts):

Step Seconds Upload and ingest of a small dataset (the sandboxed ingest with its Data Explorer views) 8-13 The canonical workflow, 19 nodes, through the orchestrator and the runner 37-40 The cookbook workflow from the CLI, 23 nodes 45 A validation with the null tests (19 shuffled refits and 3 fake drivers) 26 mmm.bayesian, tiny settings, 3 regions x 2 channels x 40 weeks 31-34 A statsmodels VAR(2) fit 13 A Model Explorer request served from the views of the fit 8 A budget plan with a 5-point frontier 10-16

docs.text:
On the final tree of fix/m35-e2e:

Check Result uv run pytest -q -n 6 6988 passed, 12 skipped (Docker, Linux-only and cloud-library tests), 0 failed make conformance 11 of 11 fixtures make lint (ruff, the 5 import contracts), make typecheck, make release-check clean, clean, passed pnpm -r lint, pnpm -r typecheck, pnpm -r build clean. The entry chunk is 598 kB of its 640 KiB budget Vitest web 373, plot sandbox 97 Playwright smoke (mock mode, CSP and Trusted Types enforced, ports 15173/15174) 78 passed, 2 skipped (the opt-in screenshot specs) The generated fixtures and types (gen_*_fixtures.py --check, openapi:check) current uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict passes All end-to-end suites against the live stack: uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e (M1, M2, M3, M3.5 and the corpus) and the browser @e2e specs (M1, M2, M3, M3.5 and the stack spec) Python: 48 passed, 1 skipped (the opt-in fit burst). docs.title: What remains unverified
docs.text:
• Real Google Cloud. Cloud Storage (the GCS shim was in its place), Cloud Run Jobs (each workflow node, fit, governance, explore and optimise run used the local-process executor), Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL and Identity Platform. Each workflow node runs as its own sandboxed run, and the cold starts of the runner images add time to each node. A 19-node workflow starts about 15 of these runs.
  • Docker. There is no daemon here, so we did not build the images. In particular, we did not build base-bayes with mmm-framework, JAX and nutpie, and base-forecast with statsmodels and the workflow runtime. The docker and docker-gvisor executors never ran a workflow, a validation or an optimisation. Thus public (shared-tier) workspaces also never ran them.
  • People. No non-technical user tried the Guided recipes, Help me choose or the About cards. No reviewer used the approval screens on real models. Nobody tried the app with a screen reader. The protocol of the M3 testers applies. Add this task: "run the readiness recipe on your weekly sales and say whether you would trust the forecast".
  • Scale and real fits. Only tiny MCMC settings and small panels ran here. We did not measure the time of full-size mmm-framework fits (4 chains, thousands of draws, dozens of geos), of governance refit budgets on them, or of workflows with hundreds of nodes.
  • Not operated live by these journeys (the integration tests of the server with embedded Postgres include them): schedules and dataset triggers that fire, workflow cancellation, sub-workflows, the workflow.run.* and validation webhooks, tenant-wide policies, deprecation and resubmission. Also the visual workflow editor and the policy editor (only their mocked Playwright specs).

docs.title: Final integration (v0.5.0)
docs.text:
We merged the M3.5 review fixes: modeling and statistics, platform server, web, client/CLI/docs, and the v0.5 documentation site. Then we ran the whole set above again on the integrated develop. We used the same laptop and ports, with a new MAPI_DATA_DIR:

Check Result uv run pytest -q -n 6, two times 7116 passed, 12 skipped. The first run also had one failure that depended on the test sequence (two runner tests left their test models in the shared plugin registry). We repaired it make conformance 11 of 11 fixtures make lint, make typecheck, mkdocs build --strict, make tf-validate clean pnpm -r lint, typecheck, build; Vitest clean. web 384, plot sandbox 97 Playwright smoke (mock mode, ports 15173/15174) 79 passed, 4 skipped (the opt-in screenshot specs) uv run pytest -m e2e tests/e2e (M1, M2, M3, M3.5) 46 passed, 3 skipped (opt-in burst, two purge checks that need a zero grace period). This was after we updated two M3.5 assertions that were not correct (the readiness branch now also reads the over-differencing guard) Browser @e2e specs (M1, M2, M3, M3.5, stack) 23 passed, after the M3.5 spec used the seasonal-first readiness sequence

We captured the outputs of the governance walkthrough in What's new, the cookbook and null tests explained again from this stack.

docs.title: Observability v0.3
docs.text:
The API and the worker send three signals:

  • Metrics: Prometheus text at GET /metrics on each API process. The worker records the series of the orchestrator (dispatch, reconciliation, finalization, pipe event ingestion). When MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT is set, the worker serves them on that port.
  • Logs: one JSON object on each line on stderr. Each line has trace_id and span_id, and the request, run and tenant that it is related to.
  • Traces: OpenTelemetry spans for each request, each outgoing HTTP call, and the dispatch and finalization of each run. The server exports spans over OTLP/HTTP only when you configure a collector.

Nothing goes out from inside a sandbox. Each execution gets the traceparent of the dispatching span in MAPI_TRACEPARENT. Thus you can join the stderr diagnostics of the supervisor to the trace of the run, and no telemetry goes out of the exec project.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Effect MAPI_LOG_JSON true JSON logs. false gives a console format that is easy to read for local work MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED true Serve GET /metrics MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN unset The bearer that a scraper must send. Necessary in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT, MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 The address where the worker serves its own /metrics (the same bearer rule) MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED true Make spans (their ids go into the logs also without a collector) MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT unset OTLP/HTTP collector (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT also works). Needs the otlp extra of mapi-server

docs.title: Scraping /metrics
docs.text:
The series contain tenant ids and spend. Thus /metrics is not a public route. It authenticates its own bearer, as the Pub/Sub push endpoint does:

# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: mapi-api
    authorization:
      type: Bearer
      credentials_file: /etc/prometheus/mapi-metrics-token
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["api.internal:8000", "worker.internal:9464"]

In the multi-tenant profile, a server without MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN refuses all scrapes (401). The single-tenant and dev profiles serve /metrics without authentication on their loopback API, if no token is set.

docs.title: The metric set
docs.text:
This table comes from mapi_server.observability.metrics.Metrics. This is the one registry that defines all series. Thus the table always agrees with what /metrics serves. The number of label values is limited on purpose. tenant_id is the only unlimited label, on the two counters that have no meaning without it. HTTP series have the route template as label, never the raw path.

Metric Type Labels Meaning mapi_runs_total counter kind, state Runs that reached a terminal state, by kind and terminal state. mapi_runs_active gauge state Runs currently in a non-terminal state (sampled each reconcile pass). mapi_run_transitions_total counter state Run state transitions, by target state (every edge, terminal or not). mapi_dispatch_latency_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to the executor accepting its submission. mapi_time_to_running_seconds histogram — Seconds from a run entering QUEUED to its first event (RUNNING). mapi_event_ingestion_lag_seconds histogram — Seconds between a run event's timestamp and its ingestion. mapi_events_ingested_total counter result Run events seen by the ingestor, by result (accepted, duplicate, bad_hmac, ...). mapi_finalize_outcomes_total counter kind, outcome Finalize attempts, by outcome (succeeded, partial, integrity, infra, retry). mapi_integrity_failures_total counter tenant_id Output-integrity verification failures at FINALIZING (a security signal). mapi_sandbox_violations_total counter reason Sandbox violations observed by the control plane, by reason. mapi_quota_rejections_total counter scope, code Requests denied by a quota or rate limit, by scope and error code. mapi_cost_micros_total counter tenant_id Billed compute cost in currency micros, by tenant (cost ledger). mapi_global_spend_micros gauge — Current spend against the global cap, in currency micros (0 until set). mapi_global_spend_cap_micros gauge — The configured global spend cap, in currency micros (0 = no cap set). mapi_sse_clients gauge — Live Server-Sent-Events subscribers connected to this process. mapi_executor_submit_throttled_total counter executor 429 answers from an executor backend to a submission (Cloud Run jobs.run), each one, retried or not. Not the API's own 429s to tenants. mapi_executor_running_executions gauge executor Runs holding a live execution on this executor (fleet-wide, from the run table; each orchestrator reports the same value, so aggregate with max). mapi_http_requests_total counter method, route, status HTTP requests handled by the API, by method, route template and status. mapi_http_request_duration_seconds histogram method, route HTTP request handling time, by method and route template. mapi_endpoint_promotions_total counter outcome Endpoint promotion and rollback decisions, by outcome (allowed, overridden, needs_override, blocked, forbidden, rollback). mapi_endpoint_score_requests_total counter result, inline POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score calls, by result (accepted, replayed, invalid) and whether the payload was inline XrJSON. mapi_webhook_events_total counter type Webhook events written to the outbox, by event type. mapi_webhook_deliveries_total counter status Webhook delivery tries, by resulting status (succeeded, retrying, failed, blocked). mapi_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds histogram — Time of one webhook delivery try (resolution, connection, answer). mapi_webhook_ssrf_blocked_total counter stage Webhook URLs refused by the SSRF policy, by stage (create, update, replay, delivery). mapi_webhooks_disabled_total counter reason Webhooks the platform disabled, by reason (failures, gone).

Monitor these series first:

  • mapi_time_to_running_seconds: the M2 target is a p95 below 90 s.
  • mapi_integrity_failures_total and mapi_sandbox_violations_total: each increase is a security signal, not a reliability signal.
  • mapi_global_spend_micros against mapi_global_spend_cap_micros: the window of the kill switch.
  • mapi_runs_active{state="stalled"}: runs that sent no events for some time. The status of the executor decides what occurs to them, not the absence of events.

The security suite adds one more series from outside the server, mapi_security_probe_unexpected{executor}, through a textfile collector or a Pushgateway (Security suite).

Each response has X-Request-Id. This is the header of the caller if the caller sent one. If not, it is the trace id. When you report a problem, give this id. It finds the log lines and the trace.

docs.title: Dashboards, alerts and runbooks
docs.text: All the files that operators need are in ops/ at the root of the repository. ops/README.md tells how to import each one. The tables below come from those files.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text:
A Grafana dashboard and a Cloud Monitoring dashboard show the same series:

File Dashboard Sections ops/dashboards/cloud-monitoring-mapi-overview.json Cloud Monitoring: modeling-api — control plane 15 tiles: Running, Stalled, SSE clients, Integrity failures (1h), Active runs by state, Terminal outcomes (rate), Dispatch latency p95, Time to RUNNING p95 (SLO 90s), Event ingestion lag p95, Finalize outcomes (rate), Sandbox violations (rate), Quota rejections (rate), Cost per tenant (micros/s), HTTP requests by status, jobs.run 429 (Cloud Run) ops/dashboards/grafana-mapi-overview.json Grafana: modeling-api — control plane 18 panels in 6 rows: Fleet overview, Runs, Dispatch & time-to-RUNNING, Events & finalize, Security & abuse, HTTP API

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
ops/alerts/prometheus-rules.yml has the Prometheus rules, with recording rules such as mapi:global_spend_ratio. ops/alerts/cloud-monitoring-alerts.yaml has the same policies for Cloud Monitoring.
