  • The generated node reference (docs/reference/workflow-nodes.md).
  • runner: the workflow_node run kind executes one node in the sandbox, with model inputs loaded from their bundles.
  • server: workflows (migration 0011_workflows, seven tables under forced row-level security): documents and revisions validated at every save, runs as workflow parent runs driven by the orchestrator's workflow loop, nodes as workflow_node, fit and child workflow runs, derived datasets registered as wf-<workflow>-<node> versions, cache reuse across runs, cancellation through the run state machine, SSE events, output links, cost roll-up, cron schedules, dataset.version.created triggers with debounce, webhooks and audit; the dispatcher and reconciler skip parent runs.
  • docs: the workflows guide (docs/guides/workflows.md) with the canonical document and a cookbook whose fragments are validated by a test.
  • Governance (server, runner): policies, validations and approvals end to end.
  • Every check of the catalog runs in a sandboxed governance run (new run kind, GovernanceJob → governance.json), model-family aware (Bayesian, frequentist, machine learning) under a refit budget: block-permutation null test, placebo noise drivers (new channels or variables, measured by ablation through the score path), time-shift placebos, naive and seasonal-naive benchmarks out of sample, Ljung-Box whiteness, rolling-window stability, effect signs, prior sensitivity, parametric-bootstrap recovery, convergence, holdout accuracy and data quality, each with message_plain, a suggested_action (new on CheckResult) and evidence.
  • Migration 0012_governance: versioned governance_policies, model_validations and validation_approvals (forced row-level security) and memberships.capabilities.
  • Policy CRUD for projects and tenants with versions and retirement; the platform's default policies per model family (DEFAULT_POLICIES, seeded on a tenant's first use; they never gate promotion by themselves); validation requests, resubmission, cancel and deprecation; second-person approval with the reviewer capability (never the submitter, never an API token); the promotion gate refuses unvalidated versions with NOT_VALIDATED when a policy requires it (audited as endpoint.promote_not_validated); evidence packs as JSON and self-contained HTML; audit rows and webhook events for every step.
  • Explorers (runner, plots-core, server): the 13 Data Explorer sections (overview, distributions, time series, missingness, outliers, correlation, cross-correlation, ACF/PACF, stationarity, STL, VIF, group comparisons, quality warnings) and the 11 Model Explorer sections (parameters, diagnostics, fit vs actual, residual tests, decomposition, response curves, IRF, FEVD, forecasts, backtests, comparisons) computed in the sandbox: the quick data sections at every ingest, the model sections at every fit, the rest in explore runs (POST …/explore, cached per request). POST /v1/models:compare compares several versions with Diebold-Mariano tests. Vega-Lite recipes for every view in mapi_plots.explorer (JSON-only). Dataset About (GET/PATCH …/about). Statistical helpers are validated against statsmodels/scipy reference values.
  • docs: guides "Validate models with governance policies", "Explore a dataset" and "Explore a model".
  • integration (M3.5 parts working together):
  • Workflow model nodes fit the real models: mapi_workflows.testing.test_registry() registers the statsmodels plugin (extra mapi-workflows[testing]), and the canonical readiness -> ARIMAX workflow runs end to end on the real ts.sarimax (in-process, through the server and on the real runner). Model nodes bind a model's target, other roles, time dim and categorical dims (a panel's geo, a multivariate model's variable) to the data automatically, and rewrite carried transform steps and holdout splits in the model's names. Multivariate nodes read the series along the data's series dimension (the layout of ts.var/ts.vecm); test.vif expands a channel dimension into columns. The mmm_governed template fits mmm.bayesian on a geo panel.
  • Governance inside workflows: mapi-runner exports every governance check as a workflow check runner (entry point mapi.governance_checks), so governance.policy and governance.check nodes measure models with the same family-aware implementations as a validation request. In the server the policies in force come from the policy store, and submit: true on a passing node records the evidence as a validation (validated, or awaiting_approval when a policy wants a reviewer).
  • Checks and explorers on every family (statsmodels, mmm-framework Bayesian and frequentist, PyMC time series, tabular, scikit-learn, choice), tested on every conformance fixture: the Model Explorer prefers a plugin's own views (explorer_views, e.g. the statsmodels IRF/FEVD and test tables); predictions are compared with the observed target at the model's stage (pipelines that resample or convert currencies); score requests name the spec's supplied side tables.
  • Catalog About cards and Help me choose are served: GET /v1/catalog/abouts, GET /v1/catalog/chooser and GET /v1/catalog/recommendations; every operation of the endpoint table is now served. About cards for the five scikit-learn models; a test holds every selectable item of the installed catalog (models, steps, splits, guided and workflow templates, workflow node kinds and nodes, governance checks) to a complete card.
  • Images assert the workflow runtime, statsmodels and scipy in the runner images (JAX with mmm-framework in base-bayes) and the JSON-only workflow engine in the server image; packages/sdk joins the strict mypy list.
  • web: About cards, Help me choose, the explorers and budget optimisation.
  • About cards (plain language first, expert notes and references collapsed) in the catalog's new Browse tab (every selectable item, filtered by kind, difficulty and text), the model and step details, the spec editor (an About tab, a button on every pipeline step) and the Guided template cards; dataset About (the owner's description, editable, next to the generated summary) on the dataset page and the Data Explorer.
  • Help me choose (/choose, and on Home and at the top of Guided mode): one question at a time, live ranked matches with reasons and cautions, and Start with this into a Guided analysis, a new spec with the model, or a workflow template.
  • The Data Explorer of a dataset version: all thirteen sections from the ingest's views and explore runs (polled, cached, kept in the URL), with variable and series pickers, interactive Vega-Lite plots in the plot sandbox, plain readings first in Guided mode and every statistic (and the platform's export-ready plots) in Expert mode.
  • The Model Explorer of a model version: parameters (sortable, with intervals), diagnostics, fit vs actual, residual analysis, contributions, response curves, IRF and FEVD, forecasts and backtests on demand, governance evidence with the validation status, and lineage; Compare (POST /v1/models:compare) with Diebold-Mariano tests.
  • Optimise budget for marketing-mix models (POST …:optimize): budget, caution, per-channel bounds in multiples or money, groups and the frontier, with impossible bounds explained before the run; the plan with its allocation, expected result, chance of beating today's plan and the efficient frontier; Guided What if… leads to it.
  • Mock-mode fixtures computed by the real runner and plots-core (apps/web/scripts/gen_explorer_fixtures.py, --check in CI) and generated TypeScript types of the explorer views; the guides' screenshots (make docs-screenshots-explorers).
  • web: workflows and governance screens (both personas).
  • Workflows: the list and the template gallery with About cards; a "use this template" wizard (name, parameter defaults, bound data); a Guided "run this recipe on my data" flow. The visual editor (React Flow 12.12.0, MIT, lazy-loaded with the editor and the run graph) has a node palette grouped by kind with About cards, typed ports that refuse an incompatible edge with the reason, branch arms that gate nodes, a node editor whose settings form is generated from each node's JSON Schema (values, workflow parameters or expressions) with catalog pickers for models, checks and sub-workflows, a branch condition editor checked live by the server (never evaluated in the browser), and a YAML/JSON view kept in sync. Problems are pinned to nodes by their JSON pointers; revisions are saved with expected_revision and compared side by side.
  • The run monitor follows the SSE stream with Last-Event-ID resume and shows the graph by status, the steps in plain words, decisions with the values they read, outputs and events, cancel and cost. A node drawer shows test verdicts, cached-vs-ran, outputs (tables, scores, folds, reports, evidence, charts in the plot sandbox, file downloads), child runs and logs. Schedules use a cron editor with presets and a preview of the next firing times that matches mapi_spec.cron; triggers fire on new dataset versions.
  • Governance: the policy editor (project and tenant-wide; covers, checks with About cards, severity, limits checked like the server, parameters; approval and promotion switches; versions with a diff; retire), the check catalog, validations with the status path and history, per-check evidence with plain messages, what to do and the shuffled-result distribution, approve/reject (never the submitter; hidden without the reviewer capability), resubmit, cancel, deprecate and the evidence-pack export. Model versions have a Validation page, Members a reviewer column, and the promotion dialog explains a NOT_VALIDATED refusal with a link to the validation.
  • Mock API (--mode mock, tests): workflows, runs replayed live, schedules, triggers, policies, validations and approvals. apps/web/scripts/gen_workflow_fixtures.py writes their data from mapi_spec and a real local run of the canonical template and two governed fits (checked by make web-check and CI).
  • web: the M3.5 screens work as one app.
  • Navigation per persona: Guided mode lists Guided, Help me choose and Recipes (the workflow gallery as recipes) first, as does a Guided-locked project; Expert mode has Workflows, Governance and Help me choose (G O).
  • Start with this opens a workflow template as a recipe (Guided) or in the template wizard (Expert), and a governance check in the check catalog.
  • A finished workflow run links each model it fitted to the Model Explorer and the version's validations (run summary, fit step, outputs); a workflow run's run page opens its monitor, and lineage links the workflow run that fitted a version.
  • The Model Explorer shows the validation status in its header (a link to the version's validations) and links the latest validation and the policies; a validation links the Model Explorer and the run that computed its checks. Explorer and governance screens share one validation cache and badge.
  • The Data Explorer offers the readiness workflow with the data bound (?data= on the recipe and template wizard pages).
  • One About card component for every screen (framed or plain, compact for side panels).
  • Playwright journeys: Data Explorer → recipe run → Model Explorer → validations, and Guided what-if → budget optimisation and back.
  • client (v0.5 calls): a request builder for every M3.5 operation of mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS (checked against the contract; the strict coverage test is no longer an expected failure) and sync and async resources: Client.workflows (documents from a WorkflowSpec, a mapping, YAML text or a file; upsert by metadata.name that adds a revision only when the document's hash changed; runs with wait; stream_events, an SSE iterator of WorkflowSnapshot, WorkflowEventFrame and WorkflowEnd that resumes with Last-Event-ID and never repeats an event; node outputs downloaded and CRC32C-verified; schedules, triggers and the template gallery), Client.governance (the check catalog, project and tenant-wide policies - a fetched policy can be edited and sent back as it is), Client.validations (requests that wait for the checks, the review queue, evidence, resubmission, approve/reject never resent after a lost response, evidence packs as HTML or JSON), Client.explorations, and on catalog (abouts, about, chooser, recommend with the answers checked before sending, workflow nodes, governance checks), datasets (about, describe, explore) and models (explore, compare, optimize with the keyed Prefer: wait long-poll, validate). Failed workflow runs raise the failing node's error. Tested with respx and against the real server (embedded Postgres, the storage front, children executed in-process).
  • cli: mapi workflows (init from a gallery template, validate a file on the server, apply, create, run with --watch - a live node-status board fed by the SSE stream, exit status 1 when the run fails - watch, status, runs, nodes, node, output, cancel, archive, rm, nodes-catalog, schedules, triggers), mapi governance (checks with their About cards, policies per project or tenant with versions and retirement), mapi validate model (waits and prints every check in plain words with the suggested action) and validate workflow, mapi validations (review queue, evidence, resubmit, deprecate, evidence pack), mapi approve (--reject with a comment), mapi explore dataset|model|compare|get (views written as JSON), mapi optimize (the plan, the uplift and the frontier), mapi choose (Help me choose in the terminal, or --answer for scripts) and mapi about. Tested with respx and against a real server over HTTP.
  • docs: "What's new in 0.5"; the workflow cookbook (the canonical unit roots -> differencing -> AR/MA order search -> rolling-origin backtest -> ARIMAX vs naive -> select -> governance document in full, with the client and CLI commands, plus VAR/VECM cointegration and a forecast bake-off); "Can you trust this model?" (governance and null tests for non-technical readers and for statisticians); "Choosing a model" (About cards and the chooser); one section per statsmodels model (About card, minimal spec, forecast with future drivers); budget optimisation end to end with the client; the client and CLI guides and reference for v0.5; a home page that leads with the new capabilities; the roadmap moves plugin upload and MCP to v0.6. The cookbook documents validate and run with the local runner, the client walkthrough runs unchanged against a real server, every command in the CLI walkthrough is checked against the CLI, and the statsmodels page quotes the catalog's About cards (conformance/tests/test_docs_v05.py, packages/server/tests/test_docs_client_v05.py).
  • tests, docs: the M3.5 journeys through the running stack (make dev, then make e2e): tests/e2e/test_m35_stack.py (the canonical readiness workflow on a series with a unit root, governance null tests that block a model fitted on noise and a second-person approval, mmm-framework with its explorer views and a budget plan, the Data Explorer, a VAR's impulse responses, Help me choose, and mapi workflows run --watch on the cookbook document) and apps/web/e2e/m35-live.e2e.spec.ts (the same screens in the browser, Guided and Expert, seeded by tests/e2e/m35_browser_seed.py); docs/operations/m35-verification.md records what they verified, the defects they found and what remains. The M1 and M3 journeys were brought up to date with v0.5 (the E33 spec on mmm-framework, the plan's KPI name, webhook deliveries verified as they arrive).
  • docs: the site for v0.5. The home page shows the new screens at work and leads its measurements with the M3.5 journeys; "Why modeling-api?" covers workflows, governance, About cards and the Data Explorer and compares workflows with general orchestrators; "Use cases" adds a governed forecasting pipeline and macro/VAR analysis; the roadmap marks v0.5 available (with its own page) and M4 next (plugin upload for allow-listed experts, an MCP server). Screenshots of the workflow gallery, editor, run monitor, a step's drawer, decisions, schedules, the Guided recipe, policies, the policy editor, the review queue, a validation and its evidence (make docs-screenshots-workflows, apps/web/e2e/workflow-screenshots.spec.ts). Terminal outputs on the What's new, cookbook, choosing, Python client, CLI, mmm-framework and budget pages are captured from a live stack instead of illustrated. A generated governance-check reference (reference/generated/governance-checks.md, every check with its About card, limits and parameters, and the default policies); the permissions reference groups each resource's actions, marks approve as needing the reviewer capability, lists every scope including the v0.5 ones and has a Capabilities section; Tenancy and authentication lists the v0.5 roles, scopes and capability.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• spec: a dataset's generated summary shows dates without a midnight time ("from 2023-01-01", not "from 2023-01-01T00:00:00").
  • workflows: the var_vecm_cointegration template (and test.johansen, search.var_lag_order, search.coint_rank) take the series along the data's series dimension; vars is optional (labels or variable names) and the template's series parameter was dropped.

  • governance: whiteness leaves out the start-up residuals of differencing; driver effects fall back to the coefficient for models whose in-sample predictions follow the stored history (statsmodels); recovery is skipped for autoregressive models; parameter stability is relative to the estimate's own uncertainty near zero and tolerates windows the model cannot be refitted on; checks that compare numeric predictions skip choice models instead of failing.

  • spec: workflow_run_events declares the after and limit query parameters the server already serves for the JSON page of events.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• spec: BayesInsight (mapi_spec.bayesinsight, mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model, the bayesinsight ingest preset with BayesInsightMetadata/BayesInsightModelDef, BayesInsightImport, draft_from_bayesinsight, POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight) and the atlas snippet language. The geo_mmm guided template (2.0.0) targets mmm.bayesian (mmm-framework). mmm-framework is the only MMM engine.
  • server, runner, client, plugins: the BayesInsight import route, ingest preset, client calls and the mmm.bayesinsight plugin; the "Import a BayesInsight model" tutorial.
  • plugins/mmm (breaking): mmm.hierarchical_geo and the pymc-marketing adapter mmm.pymc_marketing (and the pymc-marketing dependency); specs move to mmm.bayesian and drop their scaling and core.lag_tensor steps. The pymc_marketing conformance fixture is now mmm_frequentist.
  • client, web, docs, images (breaking): Atlas. mapi_client.atlas (RemoteModel) and the atlas extra, the Atlas snippet tab, the "Optimise a budget with Atlas" tutorial and snippet, the Makefile's Atlas targets and the e2e Atlas step; budgets are optimised with POST …:optimize. The base-bayes and base-forecast images warm mmm-framework instead of pymc-marketing.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• web, workflows, spec (M3.5 review): the run monitor explained branch decisions only as raw expressions and "then/else arm" ("Decisions: Difference? -> then", "Took the then arm") and named the winner by its node id ("backtest has the best average error", "Best: backtest"). branch.if now takes plain explain_then / explain_else texts, recorded as BranchDecision.explain_plain and set in every gallery template; the report summary, the Steps table and the Decisions tab lead with them ("The tests found that the series wanders ..., so it was differenced"), list the verdicts of the tests a condition read, and keep the expression under For experts. Steps not needed say why in the same words, and selections and comparisons name candidates by their step labels ("ARIMAX", "Naive forecast"); the gallery templates label their candidates.
  • web (M3.5 review): the budget plan showed Guided users the planning library's own wording ("Goal: expected KPI (posterior mean)", "the greedy allocator's exactness precondition fails", "posterior interval", "Marginal ROI"), and its result tiles read "90% likely 1.3M – 1.3M". In Guided mode the goal and the known notes are now plain sentences, the original wording is under For experts, and the tiles use as many digits as their ranges need ("1.305M – 1.312M").
  • web (M3.5 review): Help me choose scrolled sideways on a 375 px phone: its five suggestion tabs were wider than the screen and "Where to start" wrapped onto three lines. A switch with more options than fit now scrolls inside its own strip, on every page.
  • web (M3.5 review): Start with this on a model in Help me choose or the catalog dropped a Guided user into the Expert YAML spec editor, with placeholder data and an error badge. In Guided mode a model now starts the guided template built on it (tabular.regressor → store demand, mmm.bayesian → geo marketing mix, ...); a model with none says it needs Expert mode and switches only on a click (never in a project locked to Guided mode).
  • licensing, images: LICENSE.md and the licensing page now list packages/workflows (Apache-2.0) with the other Apache-2.0 components. The licensing page now names the third-party libraries v0.5 added: statsmodels (BSD-3-Clause), NumPyro and JAX (Apache-2.0) and nutpie (MIT), which mmm-framework brings in, and @xyflow/react (MIT). A new THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, generated from uv.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml by make notices, lists every Python and JavaScript package the images ship with its version and licence. It reproduces the NOTICE files and the licence texts of the JavaScript packages compiled into the web app. Every image now carries it, with the licence files, in /usr/share/doc/mapi/. make release-check and the test suite fail when it is stale.
  • spec, server (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): a governance policy with applies_to: {families: [ts]} - the example of every governance page - covered none of the statsmodels models, which declare the family forecast, ts_multivariate or regime; its checks, approval and promotion gate silently never applied. A family now matches a model's declared family or the namespace of its id (ts for ts.sarimax).
  • server (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): uploading data that was uploaded before - the same file as the next version, or into another dataset or project - failed its ingest with INTEGRITY_FAILURE ("ui/explore/index.json already holds different content"). Ingest outputs are stored under the data's content hash, and the v0.5 Data Explorer views written at ingest name the dataset version and carry plot timestamps. Each ingest's views are now stored under its run (t/<tenant>/datasets/<sha>/runs/<run>/ui/explore/); the data and its sidecars keep the strict same-content check.
  • client, cli (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): explorations.view (and mapi explore --show) returned a section's plot list instead of its view for every section whose name sorts after plots (residuals, response_curves, stationarity, stl, ...): ui/explore/plots/<section>.json matched first, and the call failed with "the view is not a JSON object". The exact view is now looked up first; plots never match.
  • spec (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): Help me choose ranked ts.sarimax sixth for "forecast weekly sales with drivers" although it is the only model that fits all four answers: items silent on a question scored the same 1.0 and ties broke on difficulty. Ties now break on the number of answers an item fits explicitly first.
  • web (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): on the dev server (make dev), the first page to open a workflow graph crashed with "Invalid hook call" in ReactFlowProvider, and a lazy route loading while the editor's YAML worker first started failed with "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module": Vite discovered React Flow and the monaco-yaml worker's dependency late, optimised them in a second pass and reloaded. Both are now pre-bundled at start-up (apps/web/dev-prebundle.ts, with a test that every package a web worker imports is listed); production builds were not affected.
  • runner (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): the Data Explorer's overview read "2 variables over 156 time" for the most common upload, a time dimension called time; the time dimension is now named by its frequency ("156 weeks", "36 months").
  • web (found by the M3.5 live-stack verification): a Guided user's first run of a recipe in a project - the workflow created from the template in the same click - failed with "The recipe did not start: Not Found": the run was posted to /v1/workflows//runs, with the workflow id the page was rendered with. Starting a run can now name its workflow, and the recipe runs the one it just created.
  • client: members could not be given the reviewer capability (needed to approve validations) without raw HTTP: tenants.add_member(..., capabilities=[...]) and tenants.set_capabilities(...).
  • workflows: compare.diebold_mariano with no more paired errors than the horizon (three folds tested at horizon 4) returned a NaN p-value and failed the node with an internal validation error; it is now a plain data error that says to add folds, and a non-finite long-run variance is refused like a zero one.
  • Web dev server: opening the app as http://localhost:5173 now redirects to http://127.0.0.1:5173. Before, the API's CORS allow-list and SameSite=strict session cookie only matched 127.0.0.1, so every call failed and the home page said the API was not reachable.

docs.title: Fixed (M3.5 review: modeling and statistics)
docs.text:
• spec, server: a schedule whose run was missed during the repeated hour of a daylight-saving fall-back (or that was created or edited in that hour) fired on every workflow-loop tick: next_fire compared local times and returned the first occurrence of the hour, which was already in the past. It now returns only times strictly after the given instant (a repeated local time still fires once), and the schedule loop refuses a next_run_at that is not in the future.
  • spec (security): a project policy could weaken a tenant policy's check parameters (for example data.quality max_missing: 1.0, or an empty plausibility.signs expected): parameters of a check named by both were overwritten by the project's. Parameters now merge by strictness (the stricter number, the union of lists and of expected signs, the tenant's value otherwise), so tenant policies are a floor for parameters too.
  • spec, server, web: Help me choose with a goal no starting point was made for ("Check or prepare my data") listed every model and template anyway, the first as "Best match" at 0% with "Not made for: check or prepare my data". An item made for other goals is now never recommended; when no model or template fits the goal, the building blocks that do (preparation steps, workflow nodes, governance checks) are ranked instead; the time-series readiness workflow template is now offered for "Check or prepare my data"; and the web app only calls an item the best match when it fits more answers than it misses.
  • spec, server: the About card of mmm.frequentist said it gives estimates "without the ranges a full Bayesian model provides" and "bootstrap ranges optional", although its bootstrap (at least 20 replicates) always produces ranges; it now says it gives simpler bootstrap ranges instead of full Bayesian uncertainty. The main MMM card listed the models mmm.nested and mmm.multivariate, which are not installed, as related items (shown as bare ids); GET /v1/catalog/abouts now leaves out related items that are not in the catalog.
  • spec: the gallery template Series that move together (VAR or VECM) failed on stationary series (growth rates, changes): Johansen rejects every null, the rank equals the number of series, and the template sent that rank to ts.vecm, which refuses it. Stationary series now get a VAR on their levels (a new stationary branch), and the VECM's rank is kept between 1 and one less than the number of series. The cookbook example and the workflows guide show the same three paths.
  • spec, workflows (statistics): the canonical Time-series readiness to ARIMAX template over-differenced seasonal series: its unit-root tests ran on the raw levels, so a seasonal random walk (no first difference needed) got a first difference on top of the seasonal one in 93% of simulated draws. The seasonal decision now comes first and the unit-root tests run on the seasonally differenced series, with an over-differencing guard (no first difference when it would leave a lag-1 autocorrelation below -0.5); in simulation the seasonal random walk is first-differenced in 1 of 30 draws and plain random walks are still differenced. Its AR/MA order search also scored models without the seasonal difference the final ARIMAX uses and searched every period, including the backtest's test windows: search.arma_order now takes D and period (it fits ARIMA(p,d,q)(0,D,0)s, the model that is fitted) and an optional split plan (it searches only before the plan's first test window), and the template uses both.
  • workflows (statistics): test.granger decided on the smallest p-value over lags 1..maxlag without correction, so an unrelated driver "helped predict" the result about twice as often as the stated alpha (0.11 at 0.05 in simulation). The verdict's p-value is now Holm-corrected for the lags tried (size 0.05 in simulation; correction: holm), or the exact F test at one prespecified lag (new parameter); the per-lag p-values and the uncorrected min_p_value stay as descriptive results.
  • workflows (statistics): compare.diebold_mariano treated one h-step error per backtest fold as errors from consecutive forecast origins: its long-run variance used h - 1 autocovariances in fold units and the small-sample factor of horizon h, which for folds 4 periods apart at horizon 4 shrank the statistic by 0.41 (or left no variance at all), and refused horizon 8 on 6 folds. Folds step periods apart only overlap up to ceil(h / step) - 1 folds; the node now reads the spacing from the folds (backtest and benchmark metrics carry each fold's origin, origins) or a step parameter, and uses that many autocovariances with the matching correction (details.variance_lags).
  • runner (statistics): the Model Explorer's comparison ran Diebold-Mariano tests with horizon 1 on the held-out errors of time-series forecasters, which are 1..H-step errors from one forecast origin (a single, strongly dependent path): equally accurate forecasts were called different in 74% of simulated cases. For such models (statsmodels and the other ts forecasters) the comparison now shows the metrics and rankings without a significance test and says to compare backtests instead; for models that predict from each period's observed drivers the test uses a Newey-West number of autocovariances.
  • spec, runner, web (statistics): the Data Explorer's cross-correlations were raw by default and judged against the white-noise band 1.96 / sqrt(n), valid only when one series is white: for two independent persistent series (AR(1), phi = 0.9) 53% of the lags were flagged significant and every run had a spurious peak. Prewhitening is now on by default (prewhiten: true, also in the web's explore dialog), and the band follows Bartlett's formula for two autocorrelated series (it is the white-noise band when either series is white), so the raw view no longer flags such lags either (under 10% in simulation).
  • workflows (statistics): the residual tests of a workflow (test.ljung_box, test.jarque_bera, test.arch_lm, test.breusch_pagan, test.white, test.cusum, evaluate.residuals) on an integrated or unobserved-components model included its diffuse first residual - the level itself, since the first prediction is 0 - so for ARIMA(0,1,0) on a series around 500 Jarque-Bera gave p = 0.0 instead of 0.47. The fit's own burn-in (statsmodels' loglikelihood_burn, stored per series) is now dropped.
  • runner (statistics): the governance check residuals.whiteness passed (Ljung-Box p = 1.00) on strongly autocorrelated errors of unobserved-components and other diffuse-initialised statsmodels models: it only dropped the start-up periods of an (S)ARIMA order, so the first residual - the level itself - stayed in and swamped every autocorrelation. The fit's own burn-in (stored per series) is now dropped as well.
  • statsmodels plugin, runner (statistics): the Ljung-Box test stored with every statsmodels fit (the RESIDUAL_AUTOCORRELATION diagnostic and the Model Explorer's residual view) reduced its degrees of freedom by every parameter - constant, drivers and the variance - so a correctly specified regression with AR(1) errors was flagged autocorrelated 23% of the time (and the rule silently switched to no correction when a model had many parameters, e.g. ETS). It now counts ARMA terms only (ar.L*, ma.L*, seasonal terms, ARDL/ECM lags of the target), stored per series as model_df, which residuals.whiteness also uses (it previously ignored seasonal AR/MA terms).
  • runner, spec, web (statistics, critical): the governance null test null.permutation_target had the wrong size and no power on time series. It shuffled blocks of the result's levels (which keeps the series' own persistence and adds a level jump at every block edge, including the train/test boundary) and compared raw holdout errors, whose spread came from which levels landed in the test periods: in simulation it rejected 35% of random walks and 33% of real AR alternatives, and a marketing mix model with no media signal passed. It now compares a scale-free statistic - the held-out skill against the null forecast (the last value of an integrated series, else its mean) on each dataset - under a null that matches what is tested: a model with drivers keeps its result and gets its drivers shuffled in time (so trend, season and controls cannot pass on their own; a model that ignores its drivers is tested as one without); a model without drivers gets the d-th differences of its result shuffled and re-integrated from the same start (d from its ARIMA order or ADF/KPSS). In simulation the test keeps its 5% size on random walks and rejects real dynamics far more often; data without a time order keep the classic row permutation of the result. The evidence names the null and the statistic, and the web's null-distribution chart labels its axis from it.
  • runner, spec (statistics): the governance check null.noise_regressors could never pass for a Bayesian marketing mix model: mmm-framework's channel effects are positive, so every posterior draw of a placebo channel's effect is above 0, its 90% interval never covers 0, and the check reported "clearly not zero" and WARN or FAIL even at a 0.5% share. A Bayesian model is now flagged when a placebo's share is above the warn limit with at least 90% posterior probability (practical equivalence); the share is taken of the real drivers' total effect (of the result only when that cannot be measured), so the limit does not depend on the size of the baseline. Placebo channels also inherited the source channel's per-channel priors and calibration (a tight business-prior or lift-test ROI), so a calibrated model failed because of the prior: they now get the model's default prior (carry-over and saturation shapes are still copied). Frequentist placebo p-values are judged with Holm's correction for the number of placebos (the uncorrected 5% rule flagged a good model 14% of the time with three placebos).
  • runner, mmm plugin (statistics): the governance check sensitivity.prior was always skipped for a default mmm.bayesian model ("the model's priors are not set in its settings"), although the default MMM policy lists it: mmm-framework's default priors are not in the spec's settings. The check now writes out every prior the model uses before scaling - the plugin's settings defaults (seasonality.prior_sigma, trend.growth_prior_sigma, hierarchy.media_geo_sigma), the defaults a plugin declares for values its engine fills in (mmm.bayesian: priors.roi_default, LogNormal(0, 1)) and business priors translated at fit time - and no longer multiplies Beta/Gamma beta or b parameters, which moved the prior instead of widening it.
  • workflows (statistics): nested split plans were not nested. search.grid ignored the inner folds of a split.nested plan and picked its winner by the outer folds' score - the optimistic selection bias nested cross-validation exists to remove - and reported that score as best_score; with a k-fold outer plan, search.grid and model.backtest sent the plan to the time-window scorer and failed ("horizon.periods ... -90"). Each outer fold now tunes on its own inner folds, refits the inner winner on its outer training window and scores it on the outer test window: best_score is that honest estimate (new results nested, outer_scores, selected_per_fold), and the outer plan's kind decides how folds are scored.
  • mmm plugin (statistics): a lift test that cut a channel's spend by up to 25% was mapped to mmm-framework's marginal-ROAS estimand for a spend increase of the same size: the experiment measured the slope below today's spend, the model was fitted to the slope above it, and under diminishing returns the backward slope is larger (1.49 times for 1 - exp(-2x) at a 20% cut), so the calibration pushed the saturation curve (and the budget optimiser) away from what the experiment measured. mmm-framework's MROAS takes only increases and its off-panel route has no marginal estimand, so partial cuts are now skipped with the reason (listed in learned.calibration.lift_tests.skipped); increases and full holdouts calibrate as before.
  • web, runner: the Data Explorer overview's missingness chart printed duplicate rounded ticks ("0% 0% 0% 0.1% 0.1% ...") on small ranges - its axis had a fixed precision; Vega now picks the precision from the tick step (the tooltip keeps two decimals). The overview and the quality section also said "No data problems found." above a list of good-to-know items (a little missing spend, extreme values); they now say "No problems to fix; 2 things to know."
  • runner, spec (conformance): MFF ingest disagreed with mmm-framework's MFF semantics, although the two are documented to give the same model. National rows (a blank Geography) became a phantom '' geo - national TV only there, sales missing there - where mmm-framework's MFFLoader spreads a national variable across the geos; and rows that differ only by Campaign, Outlet or Creative became their own dims where mmm-framework sums them. The mff preset now follows mmm-framework: a blank (or National, Total, All) label is the coarser level, and a variable given only there is spread across the levels (geographies equally, products by the KPI's share, as mmm-framework's defaults; new MffOptions.allocation and kpi), a variable may not mix the two levels, and the breakdown columns are summed unless MffOptions.split keeps them as dims. Ingest notes say what was spread. A parity test compares the panel with mmm_framework.load_mff on national media and campaign rows.

docs.title: Fixed (M3.5 review: platform server)
docs.text:
• server (security): a submitter could skip the tenant's strict policy - and the second-person approval it requires - by naming a lenient policy (even one for another model family) in policy_ids, and the promotion gate only looked at the latest status. A validation is now always held to every policy in force (tenant floor and project); policy_ids only adds policies. The gate accepts a validated version only when that validation covered every gating policy in force as it stands now (by version, or by checks, limits, settings and reviewers at least as strict); a version validated before a policy was added or made stricter reads "validated under other or older policies" and may be validated again.
  • server: two simultaneous validation requests for one model version (or a request and a workflow's submit: true) both passed the "no open validation" check and created two validations and two governance runs. The version row is now locked while the check runs.
  • server (security): a workflow's governance.policy node with submit: true recorded its validation under the one policy the node named, dropping the tenant floor, and as submitted by system, so the person who started the workflow could approve their own model. The submission is now held to every policy in force (evidence missing a required check fails), is submitted by the run's creator (the schedule's or trigger's creator for automated runs) and the second-person rule applies to them; a validation no person submitted cannot be approved (reject and resubmit it).
  • server, workflows: when a node failed while starting (invalid settings, a missing input), the run's fail-fast did not stop the siblings already started: the list of nodes to stop lived in memory only and was dropped before the next pass, so a long fit ran to the end before the run reported failed. Running siblings are now stopped in the same pass, and a restored failed or cancelled run lists them again.
  • server: cancelling (or failing) a workflow run while a search.* node was between its backtests and the winner's refit started the refit anyway - a fit run nothing cancelled, billed and registered after the run was cancelled. The refit is no longer started once the run is stopping, and a child started in the same pass is stopped by its current run id.
  • server: search.grid (and the other searches with a winner refit) always failed with SPLIT_INVALID "model.fit takes a holdout plan" when its split was a backtest plan - rolling origin, expanding window - which is what a search needs: the refit of the winner reused the backtest plan as a fit split. The winner is now fitted on all the data for a backtest plan (a holdout plan is still kept).
  • spec, server (security): an exception other than MapiError while advancing a workflow run - a 400-digit number parameter multiplied by a float in a $expr (OverflowError), or deeply nested data compared in a condition (RecursionError) - escaped the orchestrator's pass, left the run queued until its deadline (up to 7 days) and, with enough such runs at the head of the loop's queue, stopped every tenant's workflows. The condition language now raises only EXPRESSION_ERROR (arithmetic guarded, equality iterative and bounded to 64 levels), number parameters (and defaults) are limited to 1e15 in magnitude, and a run the orchestrator cannot advance is failed (INTERNAL_ERROR) with its children stopped instead of being retried at the head of the queue.
  • server (security): sub-workflow runs were exempt from MAPI_WORKFLOW_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS, so one start of a workflow with 32 subworkflow.run nodes (and nesting up to 8 deep) created far more active runs than the limit. Sub-workflow runs now count against it, and a subworkflow.run node over the limit fails with QUOTA_EXCEEDED. (The children's executions were and are held by the dispatcher's per-tenant concurrency and vCPU limits.)
  • server (security): schedules and dataset triggers kept firing - and spending quota - for a member who had been removed from the project, demoted, or whose API token had been revoked: nothing re-checked the creator at fire time. They now pause themselves (active: false, audited as workflow.schedule_update/workflow.update) when the creator may no longer run workflows there, and their runs are created by the person (a token's owner, with the token recorded) rather than by the token id.
  • server: a dataset version that became ready while its trigger was firing could be lost for good: the finalizer wrote the new pending_version over the fired row without its pending_since, so no pass ever selected the trigger again until another version arrived. The pending version and its time are now set together in one atomic update that waits for a firing pass holding the trigger.
  • server: a workflow run's cost left out everything its sub-workflows ran (a subworkflow.run node's child is a workflow run with no attempts of its own); the roll-up now follows sub-workflow runs down to their node runs.
  • server: POST /v1/workflow-runs/{id}:cancel racing the run's completion reopened a finished run as cancelling; the next pass flipped it back and sent workflow.run.succeeded (event and webhook) a second time. The cancel now locks the run and leaves a finished run as it is.
  • server: POST /v1/runs/{id}:retry on a failed workflow run crashed with a 500 (NotImplementedError), and on a failed workflow node or governance run created a run that nothing collected. These are now refused with 409 CONFLICT naming what to do instead: start the workflow again (unchanged nodes come from the cache) or resubmit the validation.
  • server: workflow node runs carried no plugin label, so the Docker and Cloud Run executors ran every node in the default base-bayes image, which does not ship the statsmodels plugin: backtests, forecasts, evaluations and governance checks of ts.* models (the readiness-to-ARIMAX template) could not resolve their model in production images. A node run now goes to the image of its model parameter, or of the plugin of the model version bound to it.

docs.title: Fixed (M3.5 integration)
docs.text:
• web, spec: requesting a validation still offered "Policies it is held to" as checkboxes, all ticked, as if unticking one left it out. Since the review the server holds every validation to every policy in force (policy_ids can only add policies), so an unticked policy applied anyway. The form now says every policy in force always applies and its checkboxes, unticked by default, add a policy; the mock and the ValidationRequest description say the same.
  • docs: the governance outputs in What's new, the workflow cookbook and the null-tests guide were captured again on the integrated stack: the shuffled-driver test now passes on the cookbook's ARIMAX (p = 0.048) instead of failing it, and the note about the old null's weakness on random walks is gone.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
• No human testers yet. No non-technical user has tried the Guided recipes, Help me choose or the About cards, and no reviewer has used the approval screens on real models. The M3 tester protocol applies, with the readiness recipe as an extra task.
  • Real Google Cloud and Docker are unverified. Every workflow node, validation, exploration and optimisation ran on the local-process executor against the GCS shim. The images (in particular base-bayes with mmm-framework, JAX and nutpie, and base-forecast with statsmodels and the workflow runtime), the docker and docker-gvisor executors and Cloud Run were never run. Routing a workflow node to the image of its model's plugin is tested with fakes only, and a node whose models live in different images is not refused. The licence files and notices the images copy are checked statically.
  • mmm-framework's extensions are not exposed: mmm.nested (nested and mediated effects) and mmm.multivariate (several outcomes, cross-product effects) are not in the catalog. Partial spend-cut lift tests are skipped with the reason, because mmm-framework's marginal ROAS estimand only takes spend increases.
  • Plotly static rendering still needs kaleido and a system Chrome and has not run in an image (MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED); Vega-Lite renders out of the box.
  • The null tests' size and power were simulated on statsmodels, regression and a small PyMC channel model, not on mmm.bayesian or mmm.frequentist (minutes per refit); they share the same code paths. The noise-regressor share is now measured against the real drivers' effect, so existing 2%/5% limits are stricter for models with a small media share; tuned policies may want a review.
  • The Data Explorer's prewhitened cross-correlation (the new default) hides a driver whose spend follows a fixed periodic flighting pattern; the raw view is one switch away.
  • Child runs a workflow's orchestrator starts are bounded by the active-run limit and the dispatcher's per-tenant concurrency and vCPU budgets, but not by the per-token admission quotas, which need a request. Schedules and triggers re-check their creator only when they fire (they pause themselves then); the reason is in the audit log, not in their API representation.
  • mapi workflows run --watch and the engine's skip reasons still say "took the then arm"; the web monitor and reports use the plain explanations.
  • Help me choose ranks ts.hsgp_trend first for a beginner forecasting one series with drivers, although it does not use them (ts.sarimax comes first for other experience levels).
  • The licences of a few Python packages with ambiguous metadata come from a hand-kept table in scripts/third_party_notices.py; re-check it when the lock bumps one of them.
  • The documentation's captured terminal outputs are kept in step by hand, and the Model Explorer comparison screenshot still shows a Diebold-Mariano verdict for forecasters.
  • Timing-sensitive tests can fail once on a fully loaded laptop (the canvas drag test of the workflow editor, the runner's checkpointed-chain test) and pass when run again.

docs.title: [0.4.0] — M3: Guided mode and integrations — 2026-10-16
docs.text:
Analysts who do not write code can now build a model from a spreadsheet, read it and try scenarios on it, and teams can wire a model they trust into the tools they already use. Everything was verified on a laptop against a live local stack (the GCS shim, embedded Postgres, the local-process executor). The real Google Cloud, Docker and the five non-technical testers are still to come (see Known gaps). In summary:

  • Guided mode: a task flow for non-technical analysts. Pick a template (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice), upload a CSV, Parquet, MFF or Meridian table, confirm the detected column roles, state business beliefs (ROI or contribution-share ranges, a baseline) and lift tests, fit, and read a plain-language report with a scorecard. What-if sliders answer at once from a per-draw response grid (a TypeScript port of the model's own maths), and "Run exact" checks a scenario, a forecast or a counterfactual with a real score run.
  • modelling: business priors translated into model priors (translate_priors runs and a preview chart) and lift tests as calibration in mmm.hierarchical_geo and mmm.pymc_marketing; the mmm.bayesinsight built-in and a BayesInsight importer; a scorecard per version and a promotion gate that needs an audited admin override for a failing or unevaluated version.
  • endpoints and integrations: endpoints with aliases, promotion, history and rollback; generated snippets (Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, notebook, Atlas); score answers with the summary inline; webhooks signed with HMAC, behind an SSRF guard, with an outbox, a delivery log and replays; saved plots, static PNG/SVG/PDF rendering with vl-convert and expiring embed links served by the plot sandbox; the Integrations hub in the web app.
  • trust and data lifecycle: self-service sign-up with e-mail verification, identity verification and Sybil flags with a review queue, trusted-proxy client addresses, per-tier draw and egress caps, GDPR export and tenant deletion with a grace period, and a Cloud Armor policy in Terraform.
  • client and CLI: the v0.4 Python client (endpoints, webhooks, plots, Guided, tenants) and Atlas RemoteModel, which lets Atlas optimise a budget against an endpoint; mapi endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors, signup and tenant.
  • docs: a new landing page, Why modeling-api, use cases, a Tutorials section (Google Sheets, embeds, BayesInsight, webhook receivers, a first Guided analysis, Atlas), Guided and Integrations guides, the security model for v0.4, and the M3 verification report.

Every workspace package and both web apps are versioned 0.4.0. Contract v0.1 gains only additive changes. Upgrading from 0.3 runs migrations 0007 to 0010 (Guided drafts, endpoints and webhooks, saved plots and embeds, the trust lifecycle). Multi-tenant deployments must now set MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES (none when clients connect directly), or the server refuses to start.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• web: the Integrations hub (/integrations). Guided cards for Google Sheets (the endpoint's Apps Script and a score:<alias> token), a BI embed link and a webhook; endpoints and aliases with the promotion dialog (the version's scorecard, the expected gate, the server's reasons on 409 and the audited admin override), history and rollback, the frozen input contract with Try it (validate or score the example call), snippets for Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script and Atlas plus an Open-in-notebook cell; webhooks with an event picker, the secret shown once, rotation, Resend newest (a replay of the newest delivered event; there is no synthetic test event), the delivery log (status, attempts, response code) with replays and the auto-disabled notice; saved plots with PNG/SVG/PDF downloads (Plotly disabled with the server's reason on MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED) and expiring embed links with allowed sites and revocation; a Share button in the plot gallery; /tokens?preset=score:<alias>.
  • web: the trust pages. Public /signup (disposable-address and terms errors at their fields, the "check your inbox" state, the development outbox link) and /verify-email; Settings > Data for organisation admins (GDPR export and download, tenant deletion with the typed confirmation, grace period, cancel and per-store progress); a banner for scheduled deletions; in the admin console, the sign-up review queue and per-tenant identity verification and deletion status with a retry.
  • docs: The Integrations hub guide (with screenshots) and the Integrations section of the web app guide; make docs-screenshots-integrations.
  • spec: the M3 contracts for Guided mode and integrations, shared by the server, runner, web app and client components (contract v0.1, additive only).
  • mapi_spec.guided: four guided templates (geo_mmm, weekly_forecast, store_demand, customer_choice - the last needs a built-in choice model that is not shipped yet), plain-language questions, role detection from column profiles, drafts (ingest mapping + ModelSpec + YAML) and the BayesInsight model_def.json import.
  • mapi_spec.ingest: ingest presets (mff, meridian, bayesinsight), wide variables and the mff format; IngestMapping moves here (still exported by mapi_spec.api).
  • mapi_spec.calibration: business priors (ROI or share ranges with a credibility), lift tests, the ModelSpec.calibration block and the sandboxed translate_priors run kind.
  • mapi_spec.scorecard: the check catalog, items with check ids, categories and docs anchors, and the promotion gate (pass → allowed, warn → admin override with a reason, fail → blocked); Scorecard moves here (still exported by mapi_spec.api).
  • mapi_spec.whatif and ResponseGridView: per-draw response grids, the slider interpolation contract, "Run exact" and forecast/counterfactual presets; ScoreRequest.future_covariates.
  • mapi_spec.endpoints, mapi_spec.xrjson, mapi_spec.snippets: endpoints and aliases, score calls with inline XrJSON, input-schema compatibility, example payloads and pure snippet generators (Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, Atlas).
  • mapi_spec.webhooks: events, envelope, Mapi-Signature signing and verification, retries and the SSRF policy; mapi_spec.sharing: saved plots, renders (PNG, SVG, PDF) and embed links for platform recipes; mapi_spec.trust: sign-up, e-mail and identity verification, tenant deletion and GDPR export.
  • mapi_spec.api.M3_ENDPOINTS (45 operations) with their access rules; new permissions (webhook, embed, tenant_deletion, tenant_export, plot delete, endpoint manage for gate overrides), scopes (endpoints:promote, webhooks:manage), audit actions, problem codes and Project.guided_locked.
  • docs: Guided mode and Integrations concept pages; the v0.4 section of the HTTP API reference.
  • server: the Guided data path. GET /v1/guided/templates (paged) and /{template_id}; POST /v1/guided/detect-roles from browser profiles or a stored dataset version; POST /v1/guided/drafts and POST /v1/guided/import/bayesinsight, validated statically against the catalog with the schema the draft's mapping promises. Every operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in the OpenAPI document.
  • Migration 0007_guided: projects.guided_locked and dataset_versions.columns.
  • The persona lock is persisted, audited (project.guided_lock) and enforced: in a locked project, members below admin store Guided specs only, and only their basic fields may change (403 FORBIDDEN with the pointers otherwise).
  • The finalizer validates and stores an ingest's columns.json, which detection reads and …/artifacts/columns.json serves.
  • runner: sandboxed ingest for Guided mode: wide variables (one column per channel or product), the Meridian preset, MFF tables mapped like a CSV after the pivot, MffOptions.combine, and the BayesInsight preset (allowed_* values, period range, necessary variables). Caps on rows, columns, cell and name length, and decompression (gzip CSV streamed under a budget, Parquet, zip and netCDF by their declared sizes) are checked before a parser allocates; every refusal is a plain message with a suggested action. Ingest writes columns.json, the profile of every uploaded column.
  • plugins: choice.multinomial_logit in mapi-plugin-tabular, a conditional logit with household product effects and Bayesian-bootstrap draws, so the customer_choice template is real. The e84_lite conformance fixture replaces the corpus deferral.
  • spec: mapi_spec.bayesinsight.import_bayesinsight maps model_def.json onto mmm.hierarchical_geo - adstock, Hill saturation and pooling with BayesInsight's own priors where they have equivalents, controls, seasonality, trends - and reports every feature without one as an IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warning (BayesInsightImport.target keeps the mmm.bayesinsight draft). Role detection gains ColumnProfile.monotonic and origin, profiles_from_dataset, draft_schema and guided_lock_issues; GuidedAnswers.format accepts mff; IngestJob gains the ingest caps.

  • docs: the "From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft" guide; the Guided mode concept page, the built-in models and the conformance guide describe the served parts.

  • mmm: mmm.hierarchical_geo declares business_priors and lift_tests calibration.

  • Business priors (ROI or contribution-share ranges at a credibility, a baseline share) become per-channel LogNormal beta_channel priors (and an intercept prior) through a vectorised location/scale bisection over Monte Carlo draws of the other priors, with a prior-predictive preview in business units and the prior mass inside each stated range (mapi_plugin_mmm.calibration; property tests check the round trip).
  • Lift tests add kpi_delta ~ Normal(implied lift, se) over the test window; the extra spend is carried over through the lag tensor and the implied lift is kept as lift_tests__model.
  • response_curves carries the baseline (intercepts and controls), closing the expected KPI.
  • mmm.pymc_marketing takes lift tests through pymc-marketing's add_lift_test_measurements.
  • runner: translate_priors runs (priors.json and the mmm.prior_beliefs / core.prior_predictive plots); every fit writes scorecard.json (the whole check catalog, or the guided template's, each measured or skipped with a reason) and the what-if grid view ui/grids/response_curves.json; forecast and counterfactual score runs write ui/guided/forecast.json and ui/guided/counterfactual.json, and a forecast's fan chart shows the fitted history with the split line. Lift tests are checked against the raw data before a fit.
  • server: POST /v1/guided/prior-translations and GET …/{run_id} (static checks of the beliefs and lift tests against the dataset summary, a pinned translate_priors run, its verified priors.json). The finalizer stores the runner's scorecard on the model version and validates priors.json; spec validation checks a spec's lift tests against the dataset.
  • sdk: FitContext.calibration and FitContext.to_original (the fitted scales); prepare_model_stage for runs that build but do not fit a model; the optional translate_priors plugin hook. sdk-pymc: PyMCModel.prior_overlap_vars keeps cheap prior draws for the scorecard's new plausibility.prior_overlap check.
  • sdk/runner/server: forecasts extend the covariates their payload lacks (ScoreRequest.future_covariates: carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero) from the fitted history (mapi_sdk.future); the server passes the fit dataset as the score run's history input. mapi_server.services.scorecards.promotion_decision derives the promotion gate from a stored model version.
  • plots: mmm.prior_beliefs (each channel's prior ROI or share against the stated range).
  • docs: Guided modelling (the translation math, the lift-test likelihood, how each scorecard check is measured, the what-if, forecast and counterfactual views).
  • server: endpoints and aliases (/v1/endpoints, migration 0008_endpoints_webhooks).
  • PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} promotes a model version through the promotion gate: the sanity scorecard, the endpoint's evaluation policy (evaluate_then_refit by default, so endpoints serve versions refitted on all data after their holdout evaluation) and input-schema breaks. A warn needs a signed-in project admin's override with a reason (audited endpoint.promote_override; no API token can override); a fail blocks. expected_revision guards concurrent promotions.
  • History, rollback (audited with its reason) and delete; GET …/schema with an example payload, POST …/validate, and GET …/snippets rendered with the server's base URL.
  • POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score: inline XrJSON payloads are checked against the endpoint's input contract and the CoordPlan rules, stored as run inputs and decoded only in the sandbox; Prefer: wait, Idempotency-Key (repeat the call to collect a result), score:<alias> tokens, and the per-token rate limit and vCPU budget. Bodies are capped (413) and depth-checked before parsing.
  • server: webhooks (/v1/webhooks).
  • CRUD with the signing secret shown once and stored sealed (AES-GCM under a key derived from the server secret); rotation keeps the old secret signing for 24 hours.
  • A transactional outbox: run.succeeded, run.failed, model.version.ready, score.completed and endpoint.promoted are written in the transaction of the change; emit_tenant_event serves tenant.deletion.completed.
  • Deliveries from the worker on a webhooks procrastinate queue: signed (Mapi-Signature), retried with exponential backoff and jitter, auto-disabled after MAPI_WEBHOOK_AUTO_DISABLE_AFTER consecutive failed events or a 410 (audited), with a delivery log and replays.
  • The SSRF guard: static URL checks, one resolution with every address checked, a pinned connection with the original name as SNI and Host, no redirects, time and size caps; MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP and MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST for development only.
  • Metrics for promotions, endpoint calls, events, delivery tries, SSRF refusals and disabled webhooks; every new operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in OpenAPI.
  • docs: the Endpoints and webhooks guide and the webhook settings.
  • server: saved plots, static rendering and embed links (plan §10.3 items 4-5).
  • POST/GET/DELETE /v1/plots[/{plot_id}]: a model version's plot (after its signed manifest verifies) or a user-authored PlotSpec, sanitized on save and on every read. User-authored plots are recorded with author provenance whatever they claim.
  • POST /v1/plots:render (Prefer: wait, Idempotency-Key) and GET /v1/plots/renders/{run_id}: a render run of one sanitized plot. The API writes its plots.json input and pins each bundle dataset as a plotdata.<n> input. Plotly is refused with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED unless MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED.
  • POST/GET/DELETE /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds[/{embed_id}]: tokenised links for platform recipes only (EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED otherwise), stored as keyed hashes, with expiry, revocation, view counts and audit events. A PNG fallback is rendered when the caller may start render runs, and copied write-once into the bundles bucket on first use.
  • The public GET /v1/embeds/{token}: no credential is read (cookies and Authorization are dropped), CORS for the plot-sandbox origin only, rate limits per link and per address, every dataset inlined from the verified bundle without decoding it.
  • Migration 0009_plots_embeds: saved_plots and plot_embeds with forced row-level security; the gateway role may read only the embed lookup columns.
  • Every new operation documents its RFC 7807 problems in the OpenAPI document.
  • runner: render runs draw PNG, SVG and PDF with vl-convert (pinned in the new mapi-plots[render] extra) with network access off, refuse anything that could fetch a resource, read plotdata.<n> inputs, apply width/height and cap images at 32 MiB. Plotly needs kaleido and a system Chrome (MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise; no browser is ever downloaded).
  • plot-sandbox: the embed page /embed/<token>. It fetches the embed view with no credentials under its own CSP (connect-src adds only the API's /v1/embeds/ path), validates and decodes it, honours the link's allowed origins and offers the PNG fallback. The mapi/web image serves it with the API origin filled in at start-up.
  • docs: the "Sharing plots" guide and the new settings in the configuration reference.
  • spec: the sign-up review queue (SignupReview, SignupReviewDecision, the SYBIL_FLAGS catalog), GET /v1/admin/signups, POST /v1/admin/signups/{signup_id}/review and POST /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id}/deletion/retry; the auth.signup_flagged, auth.signup_review and tenant.deletion_retry audit actions; the deletion record and platform logs in RETAINED_RECORDS.
  • server: the trust lifecycle (migration 0010_trust_lifecycle).
  • Self-service sign-up (POST /auth/signup, POST /auth/verify-email): single-use e-mail tokens stored as HMACs (24 h), the same answer for new and known addresses, a mailer protocol (SMTP with required TLS, a file outbox read at GET /dev/outbox in the dev profile, console), the disposable-domain blocklist plus configured domains and files, per-address, per-domain and platform-wide sign-up limits, and Sybil heuristics (same address, browser cookie, e-mail, domain burst) that flag sign-ups for the operators' review queue. Verification creates a public tenant, its default project and the admin grant.
  • Identity verification (GET /v1/tenants/{id}/verification, operators' PUT /v1/admin/tenants/{id}/verification, an IdentityVerifier provider protocol with a fake) and cut line A at run admission: uploaded code needs a trusted tier or identity verification (IDENTITY_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED); public tenants run built-ins and declarative specs only.
  • Tenant deletion: a confirmed request suspends the tenant and cancels its runs; after the grace period the orchestrator makes it deleting (tokens revoked, sessions ended, revoker hooks) and a procrastinate job purges the queue, every tenant table, every t/{tenant}/ object prefix (resuming after retention locks), then notifies and writes the tenant.purged tombstone; progress per store; automatic and operator retries.
  • GDPR export: a zip of every tenant record (credentials redacted), dataset objects and bundle manifests, with a short-lived signed link.
  • infra: a Cloud Armor policy on every load-balancer backend (OWASP CRS sqli, xss, lfi, rce and scanner rules in preview-then-enforce, per-IP rate bans on sign-up, /auth/*, embeds and endpoint scoring, Adaptive Protection), and an explicit retention for the control project's _Default log bucket (tenant deletion does not purge logs).
  • docs: Sign-up and abuse controls, Deleting and exporting data, and a Cloud Armor section in Security hardening.
  • integration: the M3 parts work together.
  • Tenant deletion revokes the tenant's embed links and disables its webhooks when it starts, purges every M3 table (endpoints and their history, webhooks, events and deliveries, saved plots, embeds, column profiles) and then delivers a signed tenant.deletion.completed to the webhooks that subscribed to it, through the same SSRF-guarded sender as every delivery (mapi_server.services.tenant_hooks).
  • Webhook events come from the finalizer's terminal transitions (run.*, model.version.ready with the runner's scorecard), promotions and rollbacks (endpoint.promoted), score runs (score.completed) and deletions.
  • Endpoint promotion gates on the scorecard the runner measured at fit (services.scorecards.promotion_decision, the single gate derivation).
  • Sign-up workspaces are public tier: built-ins and declarative specs only, on executors with enforced egress and DNS (cut line A).
  • server: POST /v1/guided/requests:compile turns a what-if scenario, a forecast or an intervention preset into its ScoreRequest, checked against the model version's score metadata ("Run exact").
  • runner: score runs read an endpoint call's inline XrJSON payloads (inline.data, inline.scenario) with the wire-format caps and the model's dim types.
  • mmm: mmm.bayesinsight, a BayesInsight model_def.json as a built-in model (Q8): Normal, log-normal, Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated likelihoods; coefficient and intercept priors in the KPI's own units; Hill, linear and S-shaped curves before delayed, geometric, Weibull or no carry-over; enforced sign constraints; fixed and partially pooled effects per row id (new levels pooled); Fourier seasons and local spline trends. Contributions sum to the expected KPI (a log-mean Divisia split for log links); lift tests observe the incremental KPI under the model's own likelihood. It passes the contract kit; mapi_plugin_mmm.bayesinsight_examples simulates a project with known parameters.
  • spec: mapi_spec.bayesinsight_model types model_def.json as the plugin runs it (the mmm.bayesinsight settings); import_bayesinsight(target="mmm.bayesinsight") now drafts a runnable spec - every row id a panel dim, the KPI bound to y, lagged media - falling back to BayesInsight's defaults with IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED warnings (and info issues for faithful but surprising behaviour).
  • mmm: business-prior translation for mmm.pymc_marketing (1.1.0): ROI and share ranges become per-channel log-normal saturation_beta priors and a baseline share an intercept prior (narrowing the control and seasonality priors when needed), solved on prior draws of pymc-marketing's own model; settings.priors hands them to pymc-marketing's model_config; a translate_priors hook previews them and a fit without a translation run translates them itself.
  • sdk: categorical holdout metrics - accuracy, accuracy_naive, accuracy_lift, log_score and brier - for a text target scored as one probability per category.
  • spec/runner: the holdout.hit_rate scorecard check (the holdout hit rate against always guessing the most popular product, in plain words) for the customer_choice template.
  • conformance: the guided_mmm fixture (the geo_mmm Guided draft with business priors and a lift test, true to its simulation); e84_lite evaluates the categorical metrics; the dedicated BayesInsight import ingests, validates and fits end to end.
  • docs: the built-in models reference covers mmm.bayesinsight and every plugin's calibration; Guided modelling covers business priors for the pymc-marketing adapter and the BayesInsight lift likelihood.
  • docs: the v0.4 site. A new landing page (both personas, how it works, the Guided quick path, the v0.4 feature grid and the numbers measured in the M3 verification), "Why modeling-api?" (compared with notebooks and ad-hoc apps, MMM vendors and libraries, and generic model serving, with when to use something else) and "Use cases"; a Tutorials section with new tutorials "Connect Google Sheets" (an Apps Script that writes an endpoint's forecast into a sheet, run in the tests against stand-ins for Apps Script), "Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI" and "Import a BayesInsight model" (import, check and a local fit that recovers the simulated parameters), and "Receive webhooks" as a tutorial with a tested Flask receiver; the roadmap with v0.4 released and v0.5 (expert plugins, MCP, optimise jobs) next; the security model and architecture pages for v0.4; make docs-screenshots-tutorials.
  • cli: mapi tokens create --scope lists the endpoint, endpoints:promote and webhooks:manage scopes.
  • dev: make outbox (dev.py outbox) prints the dev mailer's newest e-mails and verification links; make dev sets MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR and the plot sandbox's VITE_API_URL; compose keeps the outbox on a volume. make api-types and make snapshots regenerate the web API types and the snapshots.
  • web: Guided mode, the task flow for non-technical analysts (plan §11 Guided 1-7), replacing the placeholder page.
  • "What do you want to learn?": the templates as cards, and the analyses in progress. A session is a stored spec (metadata.labels.guided); every step has its own URL (/guided/<spec>/<step>) and is rebuilt from server state, so it can be resumed or shared.
  • Your data: the upload (CSV, Parquet, MFF; Google Meridian tables recognised) is profiled in the browser and only the column profiles go to role detection; questions with suggested answers, confidence and reasons; a live preview with a sparkline per chosen series; plain validation messages; then the dataset, the signed upload, the sandboxed ingest with the draft's mapping and the spec.
  • What you believe: ROI or contribution-share ranges per channel with a confidence, the baseline share and lift tests, a translate_priors preview (prior ROI/share distributions and a KPI fan in the plot sandbox) and the translated priors applied when they match the beliefs saved.
  • Fit the model: plain-language phases, progress, time left and cancel, live over SSE.
  • Results: headline numbers, ROI and share per channel with 90% ranges, the fit and response-curve plots, and the sanity scorecard grouped by question with what to do.
  • What if…: per-channel spend sliders answered instantly from the per-draw response grid (a TypeScript port of mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario, checked against golden cases the spec tests export), "Run exact" next to the instant answer, scenario presets (channel off, budget × k) and a forecast fan chart with its split line.
  • Share: promotion to an endpoint with the gate explained (a warning needs a project admin's reason), an embed link for a platform chart, and the way to the Integrations hub.
  • "View as YAML" on every step (read-only Monaco) and "Edit in Expert" with "Back to Guided mode"; settings Expert mode changed are kept and marked "advanced settings applied". The Guided/Expert choice is remembered per user, and in a project locked to Guided mode members below admin see Guided screens only.
  • Mock-mode handlers for every Guided call (src/mocks/guided.ts), Vitest unit and route tests and the Playwright smoke spec e2e/guided.spec.ts (the whole flow, the lock, the persona and a 375 px phone).
  • spec: tests/snapshots/whatif_golden.json, golden what-if cases shared with the web app (make snapshots regenerates it).
  • docs: "Your first analysis in Guided mode", a step-by-step tutorial with screenshots (make docs-screenshots-guided recaptures them from mock mode).
  • client: the v0.4 Python client. Every operation of ENDPOINTS has a request builder (the coverage test now checks the whole v0.4 table), sync and async.
  • api.guided (templates, role detection, drafts, the BayesInsight import, "Run exact" compilation, preview_priors), api.endpoints (promote, history, rollback, schema, validate, keyed Prefer: wait scoring, snippets), api.webhooks (secrets returned once; deliveries, replay, rotation), saved plots, renders (waited for, CRC32C-checked download) and embeds on api.plots, api.signup/api.verify_email (sent without credentials), verification, deletion and the GDPR export (size-checked atomic download) on api.tenants, and the sign-up review queue on api.admin.
  • Client().endpoint(alias) (RemoteEndpoint): schema(), validate(ds) and score(ds) -> xr.Dataset with inline XrJSON (mapi_client.xrjson, the SDK wire format); the generated Python snippet runs as-is.
  • mapi_client.webhooks.verify(headers, body, secret) for receivers.
  • mapi_client.atlas.RemoteModel: Atlas's model interface, structurally (Atlas is never imported at import time): KPI at the mean or as draws, batching along an independent dim into one score request, an LRU cache, backoff on RATE_LIMITED; register_with_atlas(); the atlas extra; make test-atlas runs the tests with Atlas installed in a throwaway overlay.
  • cli: mapi endpoints ls|get|history|promote|rollback|schema|score|snippets, mapi webhooks ls|get|create|update|rotate|deliveries|replay|rm, mapi plots render|embed|embeds|revoke, mapi guided templates|detect|draft (CSV files are profiled locally), mapi priors preview, mapi tenant status|export|delete, mapi signup and mapi verify-email. Promotions, rollbacks, rotations, deletions and revocations ask first; webhook secrets and embed links are printed once, alone on stdout.

  • docs: the v0.4 sections of the Python client and command-line guides, "Optimise a budget with Atlas" and "Receiving webhooks" (FastAPI and Flask), with offline, tested snippets.

  • integration (web): Guided mode and the Integrations hub work as one.

  • The Share step links into the hub: the promoted endpoint's snippets, a score:<alias> token, the chart link under Plots and links, and the hub itself (typed routes). A project locked to Guided mode keeps Integrations in the navigation.
  • Both use the same endpoint and saved-plot queries and the same promotion-gate preview (the port of promotion_gate), so a promotion or link made in one shows in the other at once; in mock mode they share one endpoint, history, plot and embed state.
  • Every snippet the app shows and copies is the server's (mapi_spec.snippets), the notebook cell included; the mock's fixture endpoint, example call and snippets are generated from mapi_spec (apps/web/scripts/gen_integration_fixtures.py, checked by make web-check and CI, rewritten by make snapshots), and a test checks each tab against them.

  • spec: a notebook snippet language: a Jupyter or marimo cell that scores the endpoint with Client().endpoint(alias).score(...) and shows an xarray.Dataset; the client's tests run it as generated.

  • e2e: the M3 exit criteria through the running stack. tests/e2e/test_m3_guided_stack.py (in make e2e) follows one analyst from sign-up and e-mail verification through the geo_mmm Guided flow (CSV and MFF), business priors and a lift test, the scorecard and its gate, what-if vs "Run exact", forecast and channel-off, an endpoint scored with a score:<alias> token, signed webhooks to a local HTTPS receiver with a replay, an embed link and its revocation, Atlas optimising a budget through RemoteModel against the live endpoint, the GDPR export and a tenant purge checked in Postgres and the GCS shim. apps/web/e2e/m3-guided.e2e.spec.ts is the timed "unaided tester" script (upload → report → scenario) and the Integrations hub flow. make e2e overlays Atlas from ATLAS_DIR when it is there.

  • dev: the dev profile trusts a local webhook receiver: a throwaway CA and certificate for 127.0.0.1/localhost in $MAPI_DATA_DIR/dev/webhook-tls/, with MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE and MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST set unless given.
  • gcs-shim: --bundle-retention-days (default $MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS) chooses the bundles bucket's locked retention when a root is created (0: none), so a test stack's tenant deletions can finish.
