  • Holdout metrics no longer invert the predictions of models that own inverse_units a second time.
  • Score outputs that declare their own units (e.g. state probabilities) no longer go through the target's inverse transforms.
  • The contract kit runs its shuffled, subset and new-level checks on long layouts (index variables are remapped) and shifts calendar-frequency time coords by whole periods.
  • The in-process executor no longer resolves a score request's side-table refs when the run payload already supplies those tables.
  • The contract kit's score requests name the spec's score_policy: supplied side tables, so models with supplied tables (E33's FX) pass the scoring checks.
  • The E33 and pymc-marketing fixtures use the corpus runner's fixture layout and run in python -m mapi_conformance run.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: spec and SDK)
docs.text:
• Counterfactuals: score_bundle takes a baseline data payload and a separate scenario payload, and scores the scenario's interventions against the baseline. A scenario without baseline data, or a named scenario that was not supplied, is SCHEMA_INVALID.
  • owns is enforced: catalog steps declare provides (scaling, carryover), and validate_spec rejects such a step on the target, media or spend variables of a model that owns that preprocessing (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • Target dependence follows the model template's target roles, even with an inferred raw schema, so RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED fires reliably. The recursion and future-covariate checks measure how far the payload extends past the fit, not only horizon.
  • No target leakage into evaluation lags for dynamic or cell-level splits. as_of gap periods stay in the holdout with masked targets and are excluded from metrics.
  • Pinned side tables always replay the fit-time version; a request that names one fails with SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE.
  • Score payloads are sorted along ordered/extend dims before the pipeline; duplicate labels are COORD_NOT_ALLOWED.
  • Chained look-back steps (adstock then lag) replay with fit-time history. A score window that starts inside the fitted range and loses look-back history gets a WARNING.
  • Long-layout per-group context works end to end.
  • Inverses: steps declare additive inverses, and decompositions along component only go through additive steps (otherwise they stay at the blocking stage, with a WARNING). Smearing residuals come only from target-shaped outputs. The moments sd uses the delta method.
  • Model-owned outputs are labelled per variable with their units and output_space.
  • Derived quantities named in output.vars come back from the fit cache. An uncached one is refused.
  • PyMC CRN counterfactuals give identical draws in untouched cells for Poisson, negative binomial and binomial likelihoods (crn_ppf).
  • Wire and bundle hardening: XrJSON budgets decoded bytes (max_decoded_bytes), caps declared dim sizes and accepts only ISO-8601 dates. Zarr-zip decoding is bounded by declared shapes, string lengths and an expansion ratio. Pickle is detected by opcode stream, in object .npy and inside archives. The evaluation sub-bundle is verified and never kept stale. Entry points can no longer replace registered or built-in plugin ids.
  • Spec parsing rejects non-finite floats and reports oversized JSON integers as SpecParseError.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: models and steps)
docs.text:
• core.formula: scalar ~ is logical not; overflow and division by zero give inf/nan, and other arithmetic errors are reported as SCHEMA_INVALID rather than escaping.
  • PyMC checkpoints: the codec rebuilds only classes defined in PyMC step-method modules (plus pymc.util and mapi_pymc), at exactly the encoded module:qualname.

docs.title: Fixed (M0 review: plots, conformance and tooling)
docs.text:
• Plot sanitizer (Plotly): updatemenus/sliders method args are checked in the positional [attr, value] form and inside nested frame/trace objects, so external image sources, href/url paths, tile-map subplots and tile-map trace types can no longer hide there.
  • Plot sanitizer (Vega-Lite): select.toggle strings and bind.legend event filters are checked as expressions, event['view'] is rejected like event.view, and usermeta.embedOptions is rejected.
  • from_plotly strips HTML from (and scans) the strings it moves into Arrow datasets, which the JSON sanitizer never decodes.
  • Plugin-originated error text stays out of trusted fields: render_plots and the step/model wrappers (Pipeline, harness fit/score/derive) move a plugin MapiError's detail into untrusted_text and keep its code only when plugin code may raise it (mapi_spec.errors.from_plugin_error, PLUGIN_ERROR_CODES).
  • Contract kit, check_step: effect_matches_output also compares each dim's kind and frequency and each variable's units; the toy FX and scale steps now set the units they declare.
  • Contract kit, check_model: new horizon_exceeds_fit, missing_future_covariate, recursive_unsupported, fast_score_matches_exact (plugin check_fast_score hook, provided by PyMCModel), plots_sanitize and outputs_match_manifest checks; extend_typed_errors covers integer extend dims; output_space_and_units covers outputs that inherit the target implicitly.
  • OutputDecl.dims_of (additive) lets a manifest declare settings-dependent data dims; the sklearn models (and so tabular.regressor) and mmm.pymc_marketing use it, so their static output dims match what score returns.

make install          # uv sync --all-packages (+ pnpm install once apps/ exist)
make help             # every developer entry point
Command What it does make test Runs the default test suite (all tests, but not the Docker, cloud and end-to-end tests) make test-fast Runs only the unit tests. It does not run the slow MCMC tests make lint Runs ruff, the ruff format check and the import-linter contracts make typecheck Runs mypy on each package that has type checks make conformance Runs the conformance corpus at size tiny (FIXTURE=e33 for one fixture) make docs-serve Shows this site and loads it again when a page changes make docs-build Makes the generated reference pages again and builds the site in strict mode make docs-test Runs all the documentation snippets and the checks of the docs make dev Runs the whole stack locally without Docker (Local, without Docker) make docker-build / make compose-up Builds the images / runs the compose stack (Docker Compose) make release-check Does a check of version consistency, the changelog entry, plan files (there must be none), pinned images and current third-party notices make notices Makes THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md again after a change to uv.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml (Licensing)

docs.title: Branching model
docs.text:
We use git flow with two permanent branches, main and develop.

gitGraph
    commit id: "v0.1.0" tag: "v0.1.0"
    branch develop
    checkout develop
    commit id: "integration"
    branch feat/m1-runner
    checkout feat/m1-runner
    commit id: "feat(runner): …"
    commit id: "test(runner): …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-runner
    branch feat/m1-docs
    checkout feat/m1-docs
    commit id: "docs: …"
    checkout develop
    merge feat/m1-docs
    checkout main
    merge develop tag: "v0.2.0"
Branch Purpose main Releases only. We merge each milestone from develop and tag it vX.Y.Z. Nobody commits to main directly. develop Integration. We merge feature branches here with --no-ff. feat/<milestone>-<topic> One unit of work. Make the branch from the latest develop. 
git checkout -B feat/m1-my-change develop
# ... small, logical commits ...
make fmt lint typecheck test

Do not rebase or rewrite develop or main. Keep changes to shared files small, and only add to them. The shared files are the root pyproject.toml, the Makefile, uv.lock and CI. Tell about these changes in your pull request.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text: Write all text for users in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. This includes the documentation, the text in the web app, and the messages that the server sends for the app to show. The rules are in Writing style.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Use Conventional commits, with the package as the scope:

feat(sdk): replay context tails at each step's input stage
fix(server): reject score requests whose horizon exceeds the fit
docs: add the porting guide
test(conformance): add the e24 filter fixture
chore: bump ruff

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Use Python 3.12 and ruff (line length 100). Use type hints in all code. Use mypy strict for the core packages.
  • Tests are in tests/ in each package. PyMC fits in tests use very small settings (tune: 50–150, draws: 50–150, chains: 2). If a test takes more than about ten seconds, mark it slow.
  • Write short docstrings (Google style). The contract tests are the executable documentation.
  • mapi_spec must not import numpy, xarray or pandas. The server must not import plugin code or array code. make lint makes sure of the two rules.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site uses MkDocs Material. mkdocs.yml is at the repository root, and the pages are in docs/.

  • The tests run all Python examples. The examples are in docs/snippets/*.py. Pages include them with --8<-- "file.py:section". conformance/tests/test_docs_snippets.py
  • Platform examples run against a live stack. make e2e runs the client, HTTP and remote-CLI walkthroughs (docs/snippets/client_tour.py, http_tour.sh, cli_remote.sh). The default suite runs the local CLI walkthrough (cli_local.sh) in conformance/tests/test_docs_platform.py. Shell snippets use the same section markers.
  • Scripts make the reference pages. scripts/gen_docs_catalog.py writes the pages for the steps, models, plot recipes, spec schema and error codes. scripts/gen_docs_reference.py writes the CLI reference, the server settings and a copy of apps/web/openapi.json. The two scripts write into docs/reference/generated/, which git ignores. An MkDocs hook runs the two scripts before each build.
  • New MAPI_* variables go into the configuration reference (docs/operations/configuration.md). A test looks for these variables in the source tree.
  • Screenshots are in docs/assets/screenshots/. Each screenshot must be 300 KB or less, and a page must use it. make docs-screenshots captures them again from a stack that runs and has seed data.
  • make docs-build must pass (mkdocs build --strict, with anchor validation).
  • Write for two types of readers. An analyst wants to know what a feature does for them. A data scientist wants to know exactly how it works.

modeling-api uses a split licence. The copyleft licence does not apply to persons who write models and integrations. The copyleft licence protects the hosted platform.

docs.title: What this means in practice
docs.text:
Plugins you write are yours

A step, model or plot recipe that you write with mapi-sdk, mapi-pymc or mapi-sklearn uses Apache-2.0 libraries. You can use the licence that you want for it, and a proprietary licence is also possible.

Applications that call the platform are not derivative works

Your application can call the platform over HTTP, with the Python or TypeScript client, through webhooks or through MCP. These calls do not make your application subject to the AGPL.

If you modify and host the platform

If you modify the platform components (server, runner, apps) and offer them as a network service, the AGPLv3 says that you must publish your modifications. This does not apply if you hold a commercial licence. For commercial terms, send an email to mattreda@mattreda.pro.

docs.title: Third-party libraries
docs.text:
The SDK uses xarray, numpy, pandas, zarr and Pydantic. The model packages use PyMC, ArviZ, scikit-learn, xgboost and skops. The marketing-mix models run on mmm-framework (Apache-2.0). mmm-framework adds NumPyro and JAX (Apache-2.0) and nutpie (MIT). The time-series models (ts.sarimax, ts.var, ts.ets and the other time-series models) run on statsmodels (BSD-3-Clause). The plot recipes use Altair and Plotly.

The visual workflow builder in the web app uses @xyflow/react (MIT). The API server connects to PostgreSQL through psycopg (LGPL-3.0). The server uses psycopg without modification, as a library that you install separately. Each library keeps its own licence.

THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the repository root is the full list. It gives each Python and JavaScript package in the container images, with its version and SPDX licence. It also contains the NOTICE files of Apache-2.0 packages. It also contains the licence texts of the JavaScript packages that the build compiles into the web app and the plot sandbox.

A script makes this file from uv.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml. After you change a lock file, run make notices. If the file is not current, make release-check and the test suite fail. Each image contains this file and the licence files above, in /usr/share/doc/mapi/.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: The project accepts contributions under the Contributor Licence Agreement (CONTRIBUTOR-LICENSE.md). With this agreement, the project can continue to offer the platform under the two licences. Refer to Contributing.

docs.title: Writing style: Simplified Technical English
docs.text:
All text for users in this project is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (STE). STE makes instructions clear and short. It also makes them easy to read for persons who do not speak English as a first language, and easy to translate.

This page gives the rules that we use. It does not replace the ASD-STE100 specification. When you are not sure, read the specification (Issue 9), section 1 (words) and section 2 (writing rules).

docs.title: Where these rules apply
docs.text: Text Rules Documentation (docs/) Yes, all pages. Procedures and descriptions. Text in the web app Yes: labels, buttons, hints, help text, empty states, errors and tooltips. Text that the server sends for the app to show Yes: About cards, scorecard messages, suggested actions and plain-language error messages. New CHANGELOG entries Yes. Older entries stay as they are. Code, identifiers, API field names and log text for developers No. Keep the names that the code uses. Code comments, docstrings and commit messages No.

docs.title: Words
docs.text:
1. Use approved words from the STE dictionary. Use each word only with its approved meaning and its approved part of speech. For example, "test" is a noun and a verb, but "check" is a noun only. Use "do a check of" or "make sure that".
  2. You can use technical names and technical verbs (see the project word list). Use a technical name only as a noun or an adjective.
  3. Use one word for one thing. Do not use synonyms. For example, always write "dataset", not "data set", "table" or "file" for the same thing.
  4. Do not use the "-ing" form of a verb as a noun or as an adjective, except in a technical name. Write "when you score a model", not "when scoring a model".
  5. Use "the", "a" or "an" before nouns where possible.
  6. Do not make noun clusters of more than three words. Write "the input table of the model", not "model input table layout".

docs.title: Words to replace
docs.text: Do not write Write ensure make sure utilize, leverage use perform, carry out do obtain, retrieve get require, requirement need, necessary prior to before in order to to via through, with approximately about assist help may (possibility) can, possibly e.g. for example etc. (give the full list) i.e. that is simply, just, easily, please (remove the word) allows you to you can in the event that if a number of some, many (or give the number)

docs.title: Verbs
docs.text:
1. Use only these tenses: the simple present, the simple past and the simple future ("shows", "showed", "will show").
  2. Use the active voice in procedures. Use the active voice as much as possible in descriptions. Write "The server checks the request", not "The request is checked".
  3. Use the imperative in instructions: "Select the model".
  4. Do not use "-ing" forms after a verb. Write "Start to type", not "Start typing".

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
1. Write a maximum of 20 words in a procedural sentence.
  2. Write a maximum of 25 words in a descriptive sentence.
  3. Write about one topic in each sentence.
  4. Do not use semicolons to join sentences. Write two sentences.
  5. Use a vertical list when there are more than three items.

docs.title: Procedures
docs.text:
1. Write one instruction in each sentence. You can write two instructions in one sentence only when you do them at the same time.
  2. Write the instructions in the sequence that the user does them.
  3. Put a condition before the instruction: "If the model forecasts, type the periods."
  4. Use numbered steps for a sequence. Use a bulleted list for items that have no sequence.
  5. Use a note to give information that is not an instruction. Do not put an instruction in a note.

docs.title: Descriptions
docs.text:
1. Start each paragraph with a topic sentence.
  2. Write a maximum of six sentences in a paragraph.
  3. Give the most important information first.

docs.title: Warnings and cautions
docs.text:
1. Start with a clear command: "Do not delete the dataset."
  2. Then give the risk: "Model versions that use it will not score."
  3. A warning tells about a risk to persons or to security. A caution tells about a risk to data or to equipment.

docs.title: Text in the app
docs.text: Element Rule Example Button A verb and, if necessary, an object "Save spec", "Add a row" Field hint One or two short sentences. Tell what to type, then the limits. "Type the number of periods. The maximum is 200." Empty state Tell what is missing, then what to do "This project has no datasets. Upload a CSV file to start." Error Tell what is wrong, then what to do "The YAML is not correct. Correct the line that shows in red." Tooltip One sentence "Shows the inputs that the model needs." Confirmation Tell the result of the action "Delete the dataset? You cannot undo this."

docs.title: Project technical names and verbs
docs.text:
You can use these words as technical names (nouns) or technical verbs in this project.

Technical names: actual, adstock, API, argument, artifact, backtest, band, binding, bundle, catalog, channel, coordinate, counterfactual, covariate, CSV file, dashboard, dataset, dimension (dim), draw, driver, endpoint, evidence pack, forecast, governance, horizon, input table, intervention, JSON, level, market, metric, mode, model, model version, node, payload, period, pipeline, plot, plugin, posterior, prior, project, quantile, revision, run, sandbox, scenario, scorecard, side table, spec, stage, step, summary, target, tenant, token, variable, webhook, workflow, YAML.

Technical verbs: click, deploy, download, fit, forecast, log in, log out, paste, promote, roll back, score, select, sign in, type, upload.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Not STE STE Ensure that the dataset has been uploaded prior to scoring. Upload the dataset before you score the model. The form only offers what this model supports, and the fitted preprocessing is replayed exactly: nothing is refitted. The form shows only the modes that the model can do. The server uses the same preprocessing as the fit. It does not fit the model again. Clicking Save will create a new revision. Click Save revision. The app makes a new revision. You may want to check the scorecard. Look at the scorecard.

docs.title: CLI and Python client v0.5
docs.text:
Two Apache-2.0 packages send requests to the /v1 HTTP API:

  • mapi-client (mapi_client): a typed Python client. It has a sync and an async version. It uses httpx.
  • mapi-cli (mapi): the command line. It uses the client, and the SDK for local runs.

The two packages use the Pydantic DTOs from mapi_spec.api for each request and response. For errors, they raise mapi_spec.errors.MapiError subclasses. They make these subclasses from RFC 7807 problem documents.

This page is a short summary. The guides give tested examples for each package (command line, Python client). The CLI reference shows the --help text of each command. The installed CLI makes that page.

docs.title: Python client
docs.text:
from mapi_client import Client

with Client() as api:  # MAPI_URL / MAPI_TOKEN / ~/.config/mapi/config.toml / 127.0.0.1:8000
    version = api.datasets.upload("eu_media.zarr.zip", dataset="eu_media_daily")
    rev = api.specs.upsert(open("spec.yaml").read())
    run = api.runs.fit(rev.spec_id, rev.revision)
    for item in api.runs.stream_events(run.id):  # SSE, resumes with Last-Event-ID
        print(item)
    run = api.runs.wait(run.id, raise_on_failure=True)
    result = api.models.score(
        model_id,
        1,
        {
            "model": "model://default/eu-geo-mmm@v1",
            "mode": "forecast",
            "horizon": {"dim": "time", "periods": 8},
        },
    )
    result.tree  # xr.DataTree with the `xarray` extra
Resource Calls projects list, get catalog get, models, model, steps, plots, schema datasets create, list, get, find, ensure, create_upload, create_version, versions, version, wait_version, upload, artifact, download specs validate, create, list, get, find, revise, upsert, revisions, revision, dry_run runs create, fit, get, list, wait, stream_events, events, logs, plots, cancel, resume, retry models list, get, versions, version, artifact, download, score plots list, get, validate tenants (v0.3) list, get, rename, projects, create_project, update_project, delete_project, members, add_member, set_role, remove_member, usage, audit tokens (v0.3) list, create, get, revoke usage (v0.3) get (the project), tenant admin (v0.3, operators) tenants, tenant, create_tenant, update_tenant, quotas, set_quota, delete_quota, kill_switches, set_kill_switches, executors, executor, audit; v0.4: signups, review_signup, set_verification, retry_deletion guided (v0.4) templates, template, detect_roles, draft, compile, translate_priors, prior_translation, wait_prior_translation, preview_priors endpoints (v0.4) list, get, promote, delete, history, rollback, schema, validate, submit, score, snippets webhooks (v0.4) list, create, get, update, delete, rotate_secret, deliveries, replay plots sharing (v0.4) save, saved, get_saved, delete_saved, render, render_status, render_output, download_render, create_embed, embeds, revoke_embed, embed tenants trust (v0.4) verification, request_deletion, deletion, cancel_deletion, export, export_status, wait_export, download_export catalog About cards (v0.5) abouts, about, chooser, recommend, workflow_nodes, workflow_node, governance_checks datasets About and explorer (v0.5) about, describe, explore models explorers and plans (v0.5) explore, compare, optimize, optimization, validate, validations explorations (v0.5) get, wait, link, view workflows (v0.5) list, find, create, validate, get, update, delete, revisions, revision, revise, upsert, run, runs, get_run, wait, cancel, stream_events, events, nodes, node, output_link, download_output, schedules, schedule, update_schedule, delete_schedule, triggers, trigger, delete_trigger, templates, template governance (v0.5) checks, policies, policy, create_policy, update_policy, retire_policy, policy_versions (tenant_id= for tenant-wide policies) validations (v0.5) request, list, for_model, get, wait, evidence, cancel, resubmit, decide, approve, reject, deprecate, evidence_pack, download_evidence_pack

v0.4. api.endpoint(alias) is a RemoteEndpoint (schema(), validate(ds), score(ds) -> xr.Dataset with inline XrJSON). api.signup() and api.verify_email() are public calls. The client sends them without credentials. mapi_client.webhooks.verify(headers, body, secret) does a check of the Mapi-Signature of a delivery (Receiving webhooks). mapi_client.xrjson encodes and decodes inline payloads. The platform optimises budgets (Optimise a budget). Each operation in the endpoint table has a request builder. The tests of the client do a check of each builder against the contract.

v0.5. api.workflows.stream_events(run_id) follows the server-sent events of a workflow run. It gives these items:

  • WorkflowSnapshot: the run with all its nodes. It is the first item on each connection.
  • WorkflowEventFrame: workflow.node.*, workflow.branch.decided and other events. Its id is the seq of the event.
  • WorkflowEnd.

If the connection stops, the client continues with Last-Event-ID. It does not give an event two times.

The client accepts a workflow document as a WorkflowSpec, a mapping, YAML text or a file path (api.workflows.validate(Path("wf.yaml"))). upsert adds a revision only when the hash of the document changed. models.optimize sends a keyed Prefer: wait request again until the plan is ready. datasets.explore, models.explore and models.compare wait for the explore run. explorations.view(exploration, section) downloads one view.

catalog.recommend(goal=..., data_shape=[...]) does a check of the answers against the questions of the chooser before it sends them. The client does not send validations.decide (and approve, reject) again after a lost response. Reviewers sign in (mapi login), because an API token cannot approve. If a workflow run fails, wait and run(wait=True) raise the error of the node that failed. With raise_on_failure=False, they return the run.

  • AsyncClient has the same resources with await and async for.
  • List calls return lazy paginators that follow next_cursor.
  • If a call accepts an Idempotency-Key and you do not give one, the client makes a new UUID. The client tries idempotent calls again after 502, 503, 504 and connection errors. It obeys Retry-After.
  • For 429 RATE_LIMITED, the client waits (Retry-After, then exponential back-off). Then it sends the request again, for all methods. This is safe because the server refused the request before it did an action. After RetryPolicy.rate_limit_retries attempts, the client raises RateLimited.
  • 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED raises QuotaExceeded immediately. retry_after_of(exc) gives the number of seconds until the quota resets (v0.3).
  • api.tokens.create returns the secret of the token one time (TokenCreated.secret). The secret is not in the repr. The client does not send the call again after a lost response. Thus it cannot make two tokens.
  • datasets.upload accepts a path, bytes or an xr.Dataset (with the xarray extra). It makes the dataset if necessary. Then it PUTs the file to the signed URL and starts the ingest run. Then it waits until the version is ready. If a dataset has its raw schema in the mapi_schema attribute, the dataset keeps its dim policies and roles.
  • runs.stream_events gives RunSnapshot, RunEventFrame (persisted events, with an id), RunLiveFrame (live progress and log frames, without an id) and at the end RunEnd.
  • models.score sends Prefer: wait=N. While the run continues, the client sends the same request again with the same Idempotency-Key. The idempotent replay of the server returns the completed ScoreCallResult with new output links.
  • The client gets signed storage URLs without the Authorization header of the API. It does a check of each transfer against the CRC32C and size that the storage calculated.

Configuration. The client uses the first value that it finds in this sequence:

  1. Arguments.
  2. MAPI_URL (fallback MAPI_API_URL), MAPI_TOKEN, MAPI_PROJECT and MAPI_PROFILE.
  3. A profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml ($MAPI_CONFIG, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME).
  4. http://127.0.0.1:8000.

The client does not send a token over plain HTTP to a host that is not a loopback host. v0.2 has no authentication.

Credentials and project (v0.3). The client authenticates with an API token (argument, MAPI_TOKEN or the token of the profile). If there is no token, the client uses the OpenID Connect sign-in from mapi login. mapi login keeps this sign-in for the profile in credentials.json (mode 0600, next to the config file, or $MAPI_CREDENTIALS). The client uses a stored sign-in only for the API URL of that sign-in. The client renews the ID token with the refresh token a short time before it expires, and after a 401.

The client sends project (Client(project=…), MAPI_PROJECT, the project of the profile) as X-Mapi-Project: <tenant>/<project>. It sends this header only on project-scoped requests. It does not send it on identity, tenant and operator routes, or when the path names the project.

File Mode Holds ~/.config/mapi/config.toml 0600 when mapi writes it Profiles: url, project, token, timeout, max_retries, verify, oidc_issuer, oidc_client_id, oidc_client_secret ~/.config/mapi/credentials.json 0600 For each profile: the API URL, issuer, client id, ID token, refresh token and expiry of a mapi login sign-in

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
mapi new geo-mmm -o spec.yaml --with-data   # template + tiny sample data (needs mapi-conformance)
mapi check spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip   # full static validation against installed plugins
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip \
    --side-table fx=fx.zarr.zip --side-table holidays=holidays.zarr.zip   # in-process fit
mapi score request.yaml --bundle bundles/geo-mmm --data future.zarr.zip -o result.zarr.zip

mapi serve                                  # the local stack in one process (see below)
mapi fit spec.yaml --data data.zarr.zip --remote @   # upload, create/revise spec, fit, follow
mapi runs ls --state running | get RUN | logs RUN | watch RUN | cancel RUN | retry RUN
mapi datasets ls | upload file.csv --name sales --mapping mapping.yaml
mapi score request.yaml --remote @ --model MODEL_ID --version 1 -o result.zarr.zip
mapi catalog [models|steps|plots] [--remote @]

mapi plugin init acme-demand && mapi plugin test acme-demand   # scaffold + contract kit
mapi spec upgrade spec.yaml --check
mapi config show | path | set KEY VALUE | unset KEY

Multi-tenant commands (v0.3). Authentication and Administration show these commands step by step. The test suite runs the two guides:

mapi login [--device | --no-browser | --with-token] [--issuer URL --client-id ID]
mapi whoami
mapi use [TENANT/PROJECT | --unset]          # --project / MAPI_PROJECT for one command
mapi logout [--revoke]
mapi tokens ls [--all] | get TOKEN | create NAME -s SCOPE... [--save] | revoke TOKEN
mapi usage [--period day|month] [--start DATE] [--group-by KEY] [--tenant TENANT]
mapi admin tenants ls | get | create | update     # operators; changes ask first (--yes)
mapi admin quotas ls | set SCOPE SUBJECT --LIMIT... | rm SCOPE SUBJECT
mapi admin kill-switches get | set --reason TEXT [--untrusted-code on|off] [--spend-cap N]
                                  [--cancel-untrusted-runs]  # with --untrusted-code off
mapi admin executors ls | get NAME | disable NAME --reason TEXT | enable NAME --reason TEXT
mapi admin audit [--tenant] [--action] [--since] ...
Command Notes login Browser sign-in: authorization code + PKCE (S256) with a loopback redirect to 127.0.0.1:<port>/callback. The CLI does a check of state and nonce. --device: the device authorization grant. --with-token: an API token from stdin. The CLI does a check of its checksum and verifies it with GET /v1/me. The CLI saves --url, --issuer and --client-id in the profile whoami GET /v1/me: the principal, how you signed in, the operator flag, and the tenants and projects with roles use Does a check of membership with GET /v1/me. If only one tenant has a bare project id, the CLI adds the tenant to it. The CLI saves project in the profile. A token acts only in its own project logout Removes the sign-in and token of the profile. It also revokes the refresh token at the identity provider. --revoke also revokes the token on the server tokens create Prints the secret one time, alone on stdout. With --save, the CLI keeps it in the profile. --json includes it, because you asked for it usage The exact cost (micro-units, with the name of the price table), vCPU-seconds and GiB-seconds, groups, and the use and reset time of each quota runs get, runs ls Show the metered cost of the run (~ while it is an estimate) admin ... Each change prints a before/after table on stderr and asks you to confirm. --yes skips this step. quotas set replaces the full policy

Guided mode and integrations (v0.4). The command-line guide shows these commands step by step:

mapi endpoints ls | get ALIAS | history ALIAS | schema ALIAS [--example] | snippets ALIAS [-l LANG]
mapi endpoints promote ALIAS MODEL_REF [--override --reason TEXT] [--expected-revision N]
mapi endpoints rollback ALIAS --reason TEXT [--to-revision N]
mapi endpoints score ALIAS [CALL.json | --example] [--mode M] [--periods N] [--data FILE|REF] [-o OUT]
mapi webhooks ls | get ID | create URL -e EVENT... [--inactive] | rotate ID | deliveries ID [--status S]
mapi webhooks update ID [--enable|--disable] [-e EVENT...] [--url URL] [--description TEXT]
mapi webhooks replay ID DELIVERY_ID | rm ID
mapi plots render (--saved ID | --model M --version V --plot P | --spec FILE) [-f png|svg|pdf] [-o OUT]
mapi plots embed PLOT_ID [--expires-in-days N] [--allow-origin URL] | embeds PLOT_ID | revoke PLOT_ID EMBED_ID
mapi guided templates [ID] | detect ID (--csv FILE | --dataset REF) | draft ID --name N --dataset D ...
mapi priors preview --beliefs FILE (--spec ID --revision N | --document FILE) [--lift-tests FILE]
mapi signup --email E --name N [--accept-terms] | verify-email TOKEN
mapi tenant status | export [-o FILE] | delete [--confirm TENANT] [--cancel]
Command Notes endpoints promote, endpoints rollback Show the current version and ask you first (--yes skips this step). --override needs --reason webhooks create, webhooks rotate Print the signing secret one time, alone on stdout. rotate and rm ask you first webhooks update --enable turns on a webhook that is paused or that the server disabled. It also sets the failure count to zero. -e replaces the event list plots embed Prints the embed URL one time. The URL contains the token. revoke asks you first guided detect, guided draft --csv Profile the CSV file locally and send only summaries of the columns signup, verify-email Public calls. The CLI sends no credentials tenant delete Shows the data that the server purges and the data that it keeps. Then it asks you to type the tenant id (--confirm TENANT in scripts)

Workflows, governance, explorers and the chooser (v0.5). The command-line guide and the workflow cookbook show these commands step by step:

mapi workflows templates | template ID [--expert] | init ID [--name N] [--into PROJECT] [-o FILE] [--offline]
mapi workflows validate FILE | apply FILE [-m MSG] | create [FILE | --template ID] | ls [--archived]
mapi workflows get WF [--yaml] [-r N] | revisions WF | archive WF [--undo] | rm WF [--yes]
mapi workflows run WF [-i NAME=REF]... [-p NAME=VALUE]... [-r N] [--no-cache] [--watch]
mapi workflows watch RUN [--from N] | status RUN | runs WF [--status S] | nodes RUN | node RUN NODE
mapi workflows output RUN NODE PORT -o FILE | cancel RUN | nodes-catalog [--kind K] [--about ID]
mapi workflows schedules ls WF | add WF CRON [--tz TZ] [-i ...] [-p ...] | pause | resume | rm WF ID
mapi workflows triggers ls WF | add WF DATASET [--input NAME] [--debounce S] | rm WF ID
mapi governance checks [--about ID] [--expert]
mapi governance policies ls [--scope tenant|project] [--tenant T] | get ID | versions ID
mapi governance policies create FILE [--tenant T] | update ID FILE [--expected-version N] | retire ID
mapi validate model MODEL_REF [-v N] [--policy ID]... [--note TEXT] [--no-wait] | workflow FILE
mapi validations ls [--queue | --status S] | get ID | evidence ID | cancel ID | resubmit ID
mapi validations deprecate ID --reason TEXT | pack ID -o evidence.html|evidence.json
mapi approve VALIDATION [--reject] [--comment TEXT] [--yes]
mapi explore dataset REF [-s SECTION]... [--kpi V] [--facet-by D] [--max-lag N] [-o DIR] [--show S]
mapi explore model REF [-s SECTION]... [--horizon N] [--compare-with REF] [-o DIR] [--show S]
mapi explore compare REF REF... [--horizon N] | get RUN
mapi optimize MODEL_REF [--budget N | --change-pct P] [--channel C='{...}'] [--objective O]
              [--frontier N] [--by-geo] [--request FILE]
mapi choose [-a QUESTION=ANSWER[,ANSWER]]... [--kind K] [-n N] [--about N] [--expert]
mapi about ID [--kind K] [--expert]
Command Notes workflows run --watch, workflows watch Shows a live board of the nodes. The SSE stream supplies the data. On a terminal, the CLI draws the board again for each change. Otherwise, it prints one line for each change. Then it prints the summary. The exit status is 1 if the run failed or was cancelled. --json: one JSON event on each line workflows apply Makes the workflow that metadata.name names, or saves the file as the next revision. If the file did not change, the CLI adds nothing workflows init Writes a gallery template as YAML with your name and project. --offline uses the templates that come with the CLI -i, -p name=value. If a -p value parses as JSON, the CLI uses it as JSON (-p 'horizons=[1,4]') validate model MODEL_REF is model://project/name@vN, name@vN, name with -v N, or a model id. The CLI waits for the checks. Then it prints each result with its plain message and suggested action. The exit status is 1 on checks_failed or rejected approve Shows the validation and asks you first (--yes skips this step). --reject needs --comment. The server refuses the submitter (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and API tokens governance policies retire, validations deprecate, workflows rm Ask you first (--yes skips this step) explore … Waits for the explore run. --out DIR writes each view as JSON. --show SECTION prints one view optimize Prints the plan (the current spend and the recommended spend, the return of the next unit, notes), the uplift and its probability, and the frontier choose Asks the questions of the chooser, or uses the -a answers and asks nothing. Then it prints the ranking with reasons, cautions and the top About cards

Errors: for QUOTA_EXCEEDED and RATE_LIMITED, the CLI prints when to try again (retry after 1h 30m). With --json, the error document contains retry_after_seconds. No command prints a token. Tokens show as mapi_<prefix>_….

Template (mapi new) What it is Conformance fixture geo-mmm Geo marketing-mix model on mmm-framework (weekly EUR, adstock, saturation) E33 forecast HSGP trend + seasonality forecast C08 tabular XGBoost demand with quantile uncertainty xgb_store_demand glm Hierarchical GLM, long layout E02
  • --remote @ means "the configured API". --remote URL overrides it for one command.
  • --json prints one JSON document on stdout. runs watch --json prints one JSON event on each line. Errors become {"error": {...}} with exit status 1. Usage errors have exit status 2.
  • Local fit and score run plugins in the same process (isolation NONE). Use them only with code and data that you trust.
  • The CLI removes ANSI sequences, control sequences and bidi overrides from server, plugin and log text before it prints the text.

docs.title: mapi serve
docs.text: mapi serve runs mapi-server dev. This command runs the database migrations. Then it runs the API and the orchestrator (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and event pump) in one process. If DATABASE_URL is not set, Postgres is the embedded pgserver. If nothing listens at MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT, the command starts the GCS shim in the same process. Runs use the local-process executor with the real mapi-runner. To also run the web app, use make dev (Local development).

docs.title: GCS shim (local Cloud Storage)
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim is a local emulator of the parts of Google Cloud Storage that the platform uses. The local stack, the test suites and the runner use it instead of real GCS. It implements:

  • object generations and metagenerations, with generation preconditions
  • CRC32C and MD5 that the server calculates, in the GCS wire forms (base64)
  • V4 signed URLs: GET with HTTP Range, and PUT
  • V4 POST policies that limit uploads to a key prefix and a content-length-range
  • IAM-lite: tokens and keys for each principal, with role bindings for each bucket
  • a retention lock (write-once buckets) and lifecycle (delete after an age).

The control plane uses ShimObjectStore to communicate with the shim. ShimObjectStore implements the ObjectStore protocol from mapi_spec.storage. GcsObjectStore implements the same protocol on real GCS.

docs.title: Start the shim
docs.text:
mapi-gcs-shim                                   # serve .local/gcs on 127.0.0.1:4443
python -m mapi_gcs_shim --root .local/gcs --port 4443
mapi-gcs-shim init --root .local/gcs            # write config + key files, then exit
mapi-gcs-shim key exec --field token            # print the exec principal's bearer token

The defaults come from the local-dev variables:

  • MAPI_DATA_DIR: the root is $MAPI_DATA_DIR/gcs.
  • MAPI_ENV: the bucket names are mapi-{env}-*.
  • MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT: the host and the port.

--port 0 selects a free port. The server stops correctly on SIGINT or SIGTERM. Only one server can serve a root at a time. A lock file controls this.

docs.title: State on disk
docs.text:
Path Content _shim/config.json Buckets and principals, with their secrets. Mode 0600. _shim/keys/{principal}.json One key file for each principal: email, bearer token, HMAC secret and endpoint. Mode 0600. buckets/{bucket}/bucket.json The retention and lifecycle policies of the bucket. buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.json The metadata of the live generation, where h = sha256(object name). buckets/{bucket}/objects/{h[:2]}/{h}.{generation}.bin The bytes of the object. tmp/ The staging area for uploads.

An object name never becomes a filesystem path. The shim hashes the names. Bucket names must agree with the GCS bucket grammar. The shim rejects some names with 400: names with empty, . or .. segments, a leading / or control characters. This rule applies to the JSON API, the XML API and the key of a POST policy.

The shim writes data safely, also if it crashes:

  1. It streams the bytes into tmp/ and calculates the CRC32C and the MD5 during the stream.
  2. It renames the data file into its final location.
  3. It replaces the metadata sidecar atomically. This is the commit point.

When the shim starts, it deletes the staging files that stay from before. It also deletes all data files that it did not commit. The shim keeps only the live generation, as in a bucket without object versioning. Thus, if you read a superseded generation, the shim returns 404.

docs.title: Buckets and principals
docs.text:
By default, init makes the five buckets from the storage layout of the plan:

Bucket Policy mapi-{env}-quarantine Lifecycle: the shim deletes objects after 7 days. mapi-{env}-bootstrap Lifecycle: the shim deletes objects after 1 day. mapi-{env}-runs No policy. mapi-{env}-bundles Locked retention of about 100 years. Nobody can overwrite or delete objects, also not an admin. --bundle-retention-days N (default $MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS) locks it for N days instead, as the deployed bucket does (30). 0 sets no retention. Thus the tenant deletions of a test stack finish immediately. The shim uses this value when it makes the root. A root that exists keeps its policy. mapi-{env}-data No policy.

It also makes two principals:

Principal Bindings control (control@mapi-{env}.iam.gserviceaccount.com) roles/storage.admin on all buckets. The control plane and the finalizer use it. exec (exec@…) storage.objects.get and storage.objects.delete on the bootstrap bucket only. It cannot list that bucket. It has no access to the bundles bucket. Its token is the MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN of the local executor.

You can add principals and bindings to config.json. The predefined roles are:

  • roles/storage.admin
  • roles/storage.objectAdmin
  • roles/storage.objectUser
  • roles/storage.objectViewer
  • roles/storage.objectCreator
  • roles/storage.legacyBucketReader

A binding applies to one bucket, or to all buckets with "*".

The shim does a check of the permissions as follows:

  • JSON-API calls: the shim uses the bearer token of the caller. If the token is missing or unknown, the shim returns 401. If a permission is missing, it returns 403.
  • Signed URLs and POST policies: these have the authority of the signer. The shim does the check when a client uses the URL. The shim refuses a URL that exec signed for the runs bucket.
  • Overwrite of an object that exists: this also needs storage.objects.delete, as in GCS.

docs.title: JSON API
docs.text:
All JSON-API requests need Authorization: Bearer <token>.

Method and path Operation GET /storage/v1/b List buckets. Needs storage.buckets.list. POST /storage/v1/b Make a bucket. The body can set retentionPolicy and lifecycle (Delete with an age condition). GET or DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket} Get a bucket, or delete it if it is empty. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o List objects. Accepts prefix, delimiter, pageToken, maxResults, startOffset and endOffset. GET /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Get metadata. With alt=media, it returns the content. With Range, it returns 206. PATCH /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Update contentType or metadata. This increases metageneration. DELETE /storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Delete an object. Accepts generation. POST /storage/v1/b/{b}/o/{o}/rewriteTo/b/{b2}/o/{o2} Server-side copy. Also available as copyTo. Accepts sourceGeneration. POST /upload/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o Upload with uploadType=media or multipart. Resumable uploads return 501. GET /download/storage/v1/b/{bucket}/o/{object} Download the content.

All object operations accept the preconditions ifGenerationMatch, ifGenerationNotMatch, ifMetagenerationMatch and ifMetagenerationNotMatch. A rewrite also accepts the ifSource… forms.

  • On writes, a failed precondition returns 412.
  • On reads, a failed …NotMatch returns 304.
  • ifGenerationMatch=0 means "the object must not exist yet".

Errors use the GCS JSON shape: {"error": {"code", "message", "errors": [{"reason"}]}}.

docs.title: Signed URLs (XML style)
docs.text:
Method and path Operation GET /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Download. With Range, it returns 206 with Content-Range. If the shim cannot satisfy the range, it returns 416. PUT /{bucket}/{object}?X-Goog-… Upload. POST /{bucket} (multipart/form-data) Upload through a V4 POST policy. The file field must be the last field.

The signature uses GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 with an HMAC key for each principal:

  • Canonical request: the method, the path, all query parameters except X-Goog-Signature, the signed headers (always with host) and UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD.
  • Signed values: X-Goog-Expires (maximum 7 days) and X-Goog-Date. The expiry is strict. But X-Goog-Date can be a maximum of 5 minutes in the future, because clocks can have small differences.
  • Bound to the signature: the method, the path, the host, the query (for example generation) and the values of the signed headers. If you change one of them, the shim returns 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch.
  • Unsigned headers: an x-goog-* header that is not signed returns 400. The exception is x-goog-hash.
  • Expiry: a URL that expired returns 400 ExpiredToken.

Signed GET URLs from sign_get are pinned to a generation. If a client overwrites the object, the URL returns 404. The URL never serves the new bytes without an error.

Signed PUT URLs from sign_put sign these headers. The uploader must send them with no change:

  • content-type
  • x-goog-if-generation-match: 0. Thus the object is write-once by default.
  • x-goog-content-length-range: 0,<max>.

The uploader can also send Content-MD5 or x-goog-hash: crc32c=…,md5=…. If a value does not agree, the shim returns 400 BadDigest and keeps nothing.

POST policies from post_policy are a base64 JSON document of conditions. They have an HMAC signature on the document. The conditions are:

  • {"bucket": …}
  • ["starts-with", "$key", prefix]
  • ["starts-with", "$content-type", ""]
  • ["content-length-range", min, max]
  • the x-goog-* credential fields
  • with create_only=True, {"x-goog-if-generation-match": "0"} (the client also sends it as a form field).

When a client uses the policy, the shim enforces these rules:

  • The signature and the expiration must be valid.
  • All conditions must be true.
  • A condition must cover each form field. The exceptions are x-goog-signature, policy, file and x-ignore-*.
  • The size must be in the range. The shim rejects a body that is too large during the stream.
  • An x-goog-if-generation-match form field is a precondition. Thus a create-only policy returns 412 for a key that exists. This occurs also if the signer has permission to delete.

Real GCS does not accept a generation precondition in a POST form. Thus GcsObjectStore signs create-only policies with uploader_credentials instead. This is a principal without storage.objects.delete, which GCS needs for an overwrite.

success_action_status (200, 201 with an XML PostResponse, or 204 by default) and ${filename} in key operate as in GCS.

docs.title: Shim-only endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /_shim/healthz: no authentication.
  • POST /_shim/v1/lifecycle:sweep?now=<iso>: needs shim.admin. It applies the lifecycle rules now. It never deletes objects that have retention.

The server also applies the lifecycle rules at each --sweep-interval seconds. The default is 300.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from datetime import timedelta
from mapi_gcs_shim import ShimObjectStore

async with ShimObjectStore.from_root(".local/gcs", "control") as store:
    meta = await store.put("mapi-local-runs", "t/default/runs/r1/a1/x.json", b"{}",
                           content_type="application/json", if_generation_match=0)
    url = await store.sign_get("mapi-local-runs", meta.name, expires_in=timedelta(minutes=15))

ShimObjectStore has three constructors:

  • ShimObjectStore(endpoint, credentials, public_endpoint=None). public_endpoint is the host that the shim writes into signed URLs. Thus a sandbox can get access to the shim with a different name. The host is signed.
  • .from_root(root, principal).
  • .from_local_dev(LocalDev).

It has the protocol methods. It also has create_bucket, get_bucket and sweep_lifecycle. Errors map to NotFound, PreconditionFailed, AccessDenied, InvalidRange and StorageError:

  • get(max_bytes=…) raises PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE before it reads the body.
  • A full read with a CRC32C that does not agree raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE.

mapi_gcs_shim.transfer has helpers for a client that has a URL:

  • download_signed
  • upload_signed_put
  • upload_post_policy.

They use only GCS XML semantics. Thus they also operate with real GCS.

docs.title: Real Cloud Storage
docs.text:
GcsObjectStore (install mapi-gcs-shim[gcp]) implements the same protocol with google-cloud-storage. The tests use only a fake client. Nobody tested it with live GCP.

  • Signatures. If you give a BlobSigner (blob_signer=), mapi_gcs_shim.gcs_signing makes the signed GET/PUT URLs and the POST policies. It uses GOOG4-RSA-SHA256, and the result is byte-identical to the V4 signer of the library. Only the string to sign goes to the signer. IamSignBlobSigner signs with the IAM Credentials signBlob API. It uses a token provider that refreshes the token (google_token_provider()), and it retries on 429/5xx. GcsObjectStore.for_cloud_run(service_account_email=..., uploader_service_account_email=...) connects the two accounts. The control account signs URLs. The uploader account (create, but no delete) signs create-only POST policies.
  • Integrity. If the CRC32C, MD5 or size that the server calculates is different from the bytes that it got, the store deletes that write (that generation only). Then it raises INTEGRITY_FAILURE. A copy pins the source generation (ifSourceGenerationMatch). It compares the size and the CRC32C of the destination with the source.
  • Preconditions. Signed GETs are pinned to a generation. Signed PUTs have a signed x-goog-if-generation-match (0, write-once, by default). put, copy and delete send if_generation_match to GCS.

docs.title: pytest fixtures
docs.text:
The package registers a pytest11 plugin. Thus all workspace tests can use these fixtures:

async def test_something(gcs_shim):            # a fresh shim per test, on a free port
    async with gcs_shim.store() as store:       # the control principal; store("exec") also works
        await store.put(gcs_shim.buckets.runs, "t/default/x", b"...")
    headers = gcs_shim.auth_headers("exec")     # for raw httpx calls

gcs_shim_session gives one shim for the full session. To use the shim outside pytest, use ShimServer(root). It is a context manager that runs the shim on a background thread.

docs.title: Differences from real GCS
docs.text:
• There is no object versioning. The shim keeps only the live generation.
  • The shim does not implement resumable uploads (uploadType=resumable). Use media or multipart uploads, or a signed PUT.
  • The signatures use HMAC keys (GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256), not the RSA keys of a service account (GOOG4-RSA-SHA256). GcsObjectStore signs RSA URLs itself through a BlobSigner (IAM signBlob on Cloud Run). If it has no BlobSigner, it uses the signatures of the library.
  • There are no ACLs, CMEK, storage classes, notifications or bucket PATCH. You set bucket policies when you make the bucket, or in config.json.
  • A signed URL is valid only for the method that it was signed for. A HEAD request needs its own signature, as in GCS.

docs.title: HTTP API (v1) v0.2
docs.text:
This page describes the platform API of v0.2 (milestone M1, the local vertical slice). Each request body and each response body is a Pydantic model in mapi_spec.api. The server serves an OpenAPI 3.1 document that it makes from those models. Each model has examples. The endpoint table on this page agrees with mapi_spec.api.M1_ENDPOINTS. If the two are different, a test fails.

See also OpenAPI explorer The OpenAPI 3.1 document, which you can browse, with all schemas and examples (full screen) HTTP API guide The main flow with curl and jq: upload, validate, fit, follow, score Python client The same flow with mapi_client

M1 is single-tenant

A local installation has one tenant and one project. Their names are default. Each resource has a tenant_id and a project_id, and each storage key starts with t/{tenant}/. Thus, the multi-tenancy of v0.3 adds row-level security and does not change the schema. M1 has no authentication. The API listens only on 127.0.0.1. Multi-tenant API describes the tenants, sign-in, tokens and quotas that v0.3 adds.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: Topic Rule Base URL http://127.0.0.1:8000 locally. Resource paths start with /v1. Bodies application/json (UTF-8). The spec text is a string field (yaml) in the JSON. Unknown fields Request bodies reject unknown fields (SCHEMA_INVALID). Clients ignore unknown response fields. Thus, the server can add fields and not make a new version. Timestamps RFC 3339, with a timezone, in UTC (2026-10-15T09:30:00Z). Ids <prefix>_<26 lowercase Crockford base32>, with the ULID layout. You can sort them by the time of creation (run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0). The prefixes are ds, upl, spc, run, mdl and mv. Projects and tenants use slugs (default). Durations "45m", "1h30m", "90s". Actions Actions that are not CRUD use a colon suffix: POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel. Untrusted text Log lines, tracebacks and plugin messages occur only in untrusted_text or LogLine.line. Render them as text. Do not render them as HTML or markdown.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Each error is an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json, model mapi_spec.Problem). It has a stable code:

{
  "type": "urn:mapi:error:LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "title": "A stateful step runs before the split",
  "status": 422,
  "code": "LEAKAGE_RISK",
  "detail": "validation failed with 1 error; first at /pipeline/2: …",
  "errors": [
    {"code": "LEAKAGE_RISK", "severity": "error", "pointer": "/pipeline/2",
     "message": "stateful step 'scale_y' runs before the split"}
  ]
}
  • Incorrect request bodies, path parameters and query parameters return 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. Each problem goes in errors[], with an RFC 6901 pointer into the request (/body/kind, /query/limit).
  • All endpoints can also return RATE_LIMITED (429), INTERNAL_ERROR (500) and INFRA_ERROR (503). The table does not show these codes again.
  • Error codes has the full list of codes and their HTTP statuses.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
List endpoints return Page[T]:

{"items": [ … ], "next_cursor": "eyJpZCI6InJ1bl8wMWphZiJ9"}
  • To get the next page, send ?limit= (default 50, maximum 200) and ?cursor=<next_cursor>. A null cursor tells you that the current page is the last page.
  • Cursors are opaque. A cursor is valid only for the same list and the same filters.
  • The items are in order of id, with the newest item first.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
POST /v1/runs, …:score, …:retry, …:dry-run and POST …/versions (ingest) accept an Idempotency-Key header. The key has 1–255 printable ASCII characters. Its scope is the project, and the server keeps it for 24 hours:

Situation Response First request with the key The usual response, for example 201 Created with the Run Same key, same body (the bytes are equal after canonical JSON) 200 OK with the resource that the first request made. The server does not make a second run. Same key, different body 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT Same key while the first request is in progress 409 CONFLICT. Try again later.

Clients must make one key for each user intent, for example a UUIDv4 when the user clicks Fit. They must use that key again on each network retry.

docs.title: Long-running work and Prefer: wait
docs.text:
Runs are asynchronous. When you make a run, the response gives the Run immediately, in the state created or queued. POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score also obeys the RFC 7240 header Prefer: wait=N. The maximum value of N is 60 seconds:

  • If the score run gets to a terminal state in N seconds, the response is 200 with ScoreCallResult{done: true, run, outputs: [ArtifactLink…]}.
  • If not, the response is 202 with done: false and the run. Follow the run with GET /v1/runs/{run_id} or with its event stream.
  • The response header Preference-Applied: wait=N gives the wait time that the server used.

docs.title: Forecasts with actuals
docs.text:
A forecast request (on a model version or on an endpoint) can send actuals. Actuals are target values for periods after the fit, or new values for the last periods of the fit. The request can also send the periods to forecast, with an empty target. The model uses its fitted parameters to update its state with the actuals. Then it forecasts from the last actual. The model does not estimate its parameters again. Forecasts with actuals gives the rules, the plugin hook and examples.

  • The model forecasts exactly the periods after the last actual that have an empty target. When the payload ends with an actual, the model adds horizon.periods periods after it.
  • ScoreCallResult.summary.conditioning (ForecastConditioning) tells what the model used to condition each forecast. It has fit_end, conditioned, n_actuals, actuals_through, revised, horizon_source (rows or horizon), details for each series and a plain message.
  • A model without capabilities.conditions_on_actuals refuses actuals with 422 ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. The suggested action is to fit again with the new data, or to keep the target empty.
  • Gaps that the model cannot filter, and actuals without their drivers, give 422 ACTUALS_INVALID.
  • EndpointSchema.actuals_example is a forecast call that you can use immediately. It has inline data for the periods after the fit, and all values are empty. Endpoints have this example only when their model conditions on actuals.

docs.title: Run events (server-sent events)
docs.text:
GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events has two representations:

  • Accept: text/event-stream: a live SSE stream.
  • All other Accept values: a JSON Page[RunEventView] of the persisted events. To read the events after a given id, send ?after=<id>.

The stream sends these frames, in this order:

  1. event: snapshot with the full Run JSON. It is the first frame on each connection. It has no id:.
  2. A replay of the persisted events that have an id greater than the request header Last-Event-ID. If the request has no header, the replay starts from the start. Each replayed frame has id: <RunEventView.id>. The ids increase for each run. Thus, a client that connects again continues exactly where it stopped. This is also true after the 60-minute request limit on Cloud Run.
  3. Live frames when the events occur: state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete and error. The data: of each frame is one line of compact JSON (RunEventView).
  4. event: end when the run is terminal (data: the final Run). Then the server closes the stream. A client that gets end must not connect again.

When the state of the run changes, the server also sends a new event: snapshot (no id:). Thus, a client can show the latest Run again and does not have to assemble it from events. The server does not persist progress and log frames. It sends them live without an id: (data: {run_id, attempt, seq, ts, type, payload}) and does not replay them. Last-Event-ID applies only to persisted events.

Between events, the server writes a heartbeat comment (: keepalive) each 15 seconds. The first frame also has retry: 3000.

An open stream does a check of the credential of its caller again each minute (MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S). The server closes the stream without end in these conditions:

  • The token is revoked or expired.
  • The session has ended.
  • The caller does not have access to the project now.

Then the new connection gets 401 or 403. Clients must stop at that point and not try again.

The server combines progress frames into a maximum of one frame each 2–5 seconds. The server persists only state changes, warnings, diagnostics, checkpoints, metrics and terminal events. Only these events can replay. A client that connects again gets the latest progress from the snapshot frame. To get the log lines in pages, use GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs.

retry: 3000
event: snapshot
data: {"id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","state":"running", …}

id: 17
event: state
data: {"id":17,"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","attempt":1,"seq":3,"type":"state", …}

: keepalive

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Data goes into the platform in three steps:

  1. Create the dataset.
  2. PUT the file to the signed URL from an upload session. The URL points into the quarantine bucket. The API does not see the bytes.
  3. Create a version. A sandboxed ingest run parses the upload and validates it. Then it writes the content-addressed data.zarr.zip with its schema, profile and preview.
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/datasets Create a dataset DatasetCreate Dataset 201 CONFLICT (the name is in use) GET /v1/datasets List the datasets — Page[Dataset] 200 — GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id} Get a dataset — Dataset 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/uploads Get a signed PUT URL into quarantine UploadCreate UploadSession 201 NOT_FOUND, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, QUOTA_EXCEEDED POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions Ingest an upload as a new version. This starts an ingest run. Accepts Idempotency-Key. DatasetVersionCreate DatasetVersion (status ingesting) 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the upload is not complete, or a version already uses it) GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions List the versions — Page[DatasetVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version} Schema, summary, and references to the profile and the preview — DatasetVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for data.zarr.zip, schema.json, profile.json or preview.json — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND

docs.title: Specs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/specs:validate Synchronous static validation. It returns all issues at one time with JSON pointers. It also returns the schema at each pipeline stage. ValidateRequest ValidateResponse 200 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID POST /v1/specs Create a spec and its revision 1 SpecCreate SpecDoc 201 SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT GET /v1/specs List the specs — Page[SpecDoc] 200 — GET /v1/specs/{spec_id} Get a spec with its latest revision — SpecDoc 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions Add an immutable revision SpecRevisionCreate SpecRevision 201 NOT_FOUND, SPEC_PARSE_ERROR, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_INVALID, CONFLICT (the parent_revision is not the latest) GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions List the revisions — Page[SpecRevision] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision} Get one revision — SpecRevision 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions/{revision}:dry-run An explicit sandboxed dry run. It is the same as POST /v1/runs with kind: validate. Accepts Idempotency-Key. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, QUOTA_EXCEEDED

How validation gives its results:

  • POST /v1/specs:validate returns 200 also when the document is not valid. The result is in ValidateResponse.valid and issues.
  • The API uses the statuses that are not 2xx only for requests that it cannot validate. These are YAML that it cannot parse, a document that is too large, and a request body that is not correct.
  • When you create a spec or a revision, the API also stores revisions that are not valid. They have valid: false and their issues. Thus, the editor can save work that is not complete.
  • POST /v1/runs refuses revisions that are not valid. It uses the code of the first error. Examples: LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /v1/runs Submit a run. It returns 200 on an idempotent replay. Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunCreate Run 201 NOT_FOUND, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, LEAKAGE_RISK, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED GET /v1/runs List the runs (filters: kind, state, spec_id) — Page[Run] 200 — GET /v1/runs/{run_id} Get a run: state, failure class and problem, attempt, progress snapshot and cost. The cost has placeholders in v0.2. From v0.3, the platform meters it — Run 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/events An SSE stream or a JSON page of the persisted events (see Run events). Accepts Last-Event-ID. — Page[RunEventView] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/logs The captured log lines. Filters: attempt, stream — Page[LogLine] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots The plots that a succeeded run rendered (plots.json: forecast fans, counterfactual bands). The plot sanitizer does a check of them at each read. The response does not include rejected plots. The list is empty until the run succeeds. — Page[PlotSpec] 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:cancel Request cancellation. It is idempotent. It returns the run in cancelling, or in its terminal state if the run is already complete. The API does not change a finalizing run and returns it as it is, because its execution is already complete. — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:resume Resume a partial run from its checkpoints (new attempt) — Run 202 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the run is not partial) POST /v1/runs/{run_id}:retry Start a new run from a failed run. For example, use the next larger resource class after RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Accepts Idempotency-Key. RunRetry Run 201 NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT (the run did not fail, or it is a workflow, workflow node or governance run. For these, start the workflow again or submit the validation again)

The fields that RunCreate needs change with kind:

kind Required Not permitted fit, validate (sandboxed dry run) spec_id, revision model_version_id, request score model_version_id, request (a ScoreRequest document) spec_id, revision evaluate, derive, render model_version_id (params is optional) spec_id, revision, request

POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions creates the ingest runs. In v0.2, you cannot create describe runs, optimize runs or the fan-out parents (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign). Run protocol lists the run states and the transitions between them.

docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/models List the models — Page[Model] 200 — GET /v1/models/{model_id} Get a model — Model 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions List the versions — Page[ModelVersion] 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version} Signed bundle manifest, diagnostics, scorecard, lineage, metrics — ModelVersion 200 NOT_FOUND GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/artifacts/{name} Signed URL for a bundle object or a ui/… view. name can contain / — ArtifactLink 200 NOT_FOUND, INTEGRITY_FAILURE POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:score Score with replayed preprocessing. Accepts Prefer: wait=N (200 if the run is complete, if not 202) and Idempotency-Key. inline holds data/scenario that you type in (XrJSON, maximum 5 MB each). The API does a check of them against the inputs of the version. ScoreCall ScoreCallResult 200 NOT_FOUND, MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED, UNSEEN_LEVELS, COORD_NOT_ALLOWED, HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT, MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION, CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED, QUOTA_EXCEEDED, ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED, ACTUALS_INVALID, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE GET /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/inputs The data that a score call can send. The API makes artifact links only after two checks are satisfactory:

  1. The authorization check.
  2. The verification of the signed bundle manifest of the model version. The tenant, model version, digests and object generations must all agree.

If the second check fails, the response is INTEGRITY_FAILURE and the API gives no URL. Each link is pinned to an object generation. It expires after 15 minutes. It supports HTTP Range requests.

docs.title: Multi-tenant API v0.3
docs.text:
v0.3 (milestone M2) adds tenants, projects, members, API tokens, quotas, cost and an operator console. The models are in these modules:

  • mapi_spec.api
  • mapi_spec.tenancy
  • mapi_spec.tokens
  • mapi_spec.quotas
  • mapi_spec.cost
  • mapi_spec.audit
  • mapi_spec.admin
  • mapi_spec.auth

The endpoint table below agrees with mapi_spec.api.M2_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives each operation its scope and the permission that it checks. This includes the v0.2 operations. If the code, this page and the server are different, tests fail. Tenancy and authentication explains roles, tokens and scopes. Quotas and cost explains limits and prices.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Caller Credential Notes Browser (the web app) Session cookie __Host-mapi_session (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/). GET /auth/callback sets it OpenID Connect Authorization Code flow with PKCE (S256) and a nonce. The API runs the flow as a backend-for-frontend. The browser does not hold an OAuth token. Programs, SDKs, CLI Authorization: Bearer mapi_<prefix>_<secret><checksum> An API token. It acts as its owner, with only its scopes, in the one project that it is bound to. Google Pub/Sub A Google-signed OIDC ID token on POST /internal/events The API does a check of the audience, the issuer and the push service account. No data in the body gives authentication.

Responses for authentication and authorization:

Situation Response No credential, or an expired session, on a route that is not public 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A token that is not correctly formed, or a token with a bad checksum 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. The API does not show the value in the response. A revoked or expired token 401 UNAUTHENTICATED A resource in a project or tenant that the caller cannot see 404 NOT_FOUND, the same as for a resource that does not exist. Thus, callers cannot find ids by tests The caller can see the resource, but the role or the token scopes do not permit the action 403 FORBIDDEN A token used outside the project that it is bound to 403 FORBIDDEN The tenant is suspended Reads work. All other requests return 403 FORBIDDEN.

docs.title: Selecting the project
docs.text:
Each v0.2 resource (datasets, specs, runs, models, plots) is part of a project. From v0.3, a request identifies its project in one of these ways. The list order is the order of precedence:

  1. Path parameters, on routes under /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}.
  2. The X-Mapi-Project header: X-Mapi-Project: <tenant_id>/<project_id>, for example X-Mapi-Project: acme/growth. The API also accepts only the project, for example X-Mapi-Project: growth, when the tenant is clear. This is when the caller is a member of one tenant, or uses a token.
  3. The token binding. A token always acts in its own project. Thus, token clients do not have to send the header. A header that identifies a different project returns 403 FORBIDDEN.
  4. The deployment default, only in the single-tenant local profile (default/default, as in v0.2).

If no rule applies, or the path and the header are different, the request fails with 422 SCHEMA_INVALID. mapi_spec.tenancy.resolve_project_scope implements these rules.

The scope of each v0.2 endpoint (by operation id) and the permission that the API checks:

Scope Operations Permission Public health, ready, get_schema None Authenticated list_projects, get_catalog, list_catalog_models, get_catalog_model, list_catalog_steps, list_catalog_plots All signed-in callers. The lists show only what the caller can see. Project get_project read project Project create_dataset / create_upload, create_dataset_version create / update dataset (editor) Project list_datasets, get_dataset, list_dataset_versions, get_dataset_version, get_dataset_artifact read dataset Project validate_spec, list_specs, get_spec, list_spec_revisions, get_spec_revision read spec Project create_spec / create_spec_revision create / update spec (editor) Project create_run, dry_run_spec, resume_run, retry_run create run (runner). Runs on a model version also need run model. Project cancel_run cancel run (runner) Project list_runs, get_run, run_events, run_logs, list_run_plots read run Project list_models, get_model, list_model_versions, get_model_version, get_model_artifact read model Project score_model run model (runner) Project list_plots, get_plot, validate_plot read plot

In v0.2, the storage keys and rows already had the tenant and the project (t/{tenant}/…). Thus, the change needs no data migration. Postgres enforces the boundary with row-level security on tenant_id in all tables.

For a token, the response also includes the token — Me 200 UNAUTHENTICATED GET /v1/tenants The tenants that the caller is a member of — Page[Tenant] 200 — GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Get a tenant — Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id} Change the name of a tenant (tenant admin) TenantUpdate Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects The projects of the tenant that the caller can see — Page[Project] 200 NOT_FOUND POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects Create a project (tenant admin) ProjectCreate Project 201 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (the id is in use) PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Change the name or the description of a project (project admin) ProjectUpdate Project 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} Delete an empty project (tenant admin) — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT (the project still has data)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
A membership gives one role. A tenant-wide membership gives the role on the tenant and on all projects in it. A project membership gives the role only on that project. The effective role in a project is the higher of the two. Add a member by principal_id. To invite a person who did not sign in before, add the member by email. At the first sign-in with that verified e-mail, the person gets the invitation. If you remove or demote the last admin, the API returns 409 CONFLICT.
