docs.title: API tokens
docs.text:
Tokens are part of the project that X-Mapi-Project selects. POST /v1/tokens returns the full token one time, in TokenCreated.secret. The API cannot show it again. Lists show the redacted form mapi_<prefix>_…. Each member can mint, list and revoke their own tokens. To list the tokens of all members (?all=true) or to revoke the token of a different person, you need manage on token (project admin).

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/tokens The tokens of the caller. Filters: all, status — Page[ApiToken] 200 — POST /v1/tokens Mint a token with scopes and an expiry. A rate limit and a vCPU-second budget are optional TokenCreate TokenCreated 201 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tokens/{token_id} Get a token (the response never includes its secret) — ApiToken 200 NOT_FOUND DELETE /v1/tokens/{token_id} Revoke a token. It is idempotent. — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/usage The cost and the quota of the selected project for a UTC period (day or month). You can also put them in groups (group_by: resource_class, project, day, token, run) — UsageReport 200 — GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/usage The same data for the full tenant (tenant admin) — UsageReport 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/audit The audit log of the tenant (tenant admin). Filters: project_id, actor_id, action, outcome, since, until — Page[AuditEvent] 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN

Each Run now has a cost with values (RunCost):

  • estimated is true until the platform meters the first attempt of the run.
  • amount_micros is in currency (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros).
  • price_version identifies the price table that the platform used.

The v0.2 fields vcpu_seconds, gib_seconds and usd keep their meaning.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator endpoints need a platform operator. Tenant admins get 403 FORBIDDEN. Operators see tenant metadata, usage and audit logs. They do not see tenant content (datasets, specs, models, plots). The API writes each change to the audit log.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /v1/admin/tenants All tenants. Filters: status, trust_tier — Page[Tenant] 200 FORBIDDEN POST /v1/admin/tenants Create a tenant. You can also invite its first admin TenantCreate Tenant 201 FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT GET /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id} Get a tenant — Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PATCH /v1/admin/tenants/{tenant_id} Change the trust tier, the status or the data residency. The statuses suspended and deleting need a reason TenantAdminUpdate Tenant 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/quotas Quota policies. Filters: scope, subject_id — Page[QuotaPolicy] 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/quotas Create or replace the policy for one (scope, subject_id) QuotaPolicyUpsert QuotaPolicy 200 FORBIDDEN DELETE /v1/admin/quotas/{scope}/{subject_id} Remove a policy. The tier default then applies again. For the global policy, subject_id is * — — 204 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/kill-switches The kill switches — KillSwitches 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/kill-switches Change the kill switches. Fields that you do not send keep their value. reason is necessary. cancel_untrusted_runs (with untrusted_execution_enabled=false) also cancels all runs of uploaded code that are not complete. Without it, the runs that are in progress continue KillSwitchUpdate KillSwitches 200 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors All executors: caps, health, submit rate, 429s, conformance report — Page[ExecutorHealth] 200 FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors/{name} One executor — ExecutorHealth 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence The reports of the conformance suite and the security suite for an executor — ExecutorEvidence 200 NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name}/evidence Record the suite results (audited). Shared tiers need the two reports, with a pass, for the current caps ExecutorEvidenceUpdate ExecutorEvidence 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/usage The cost for each tenant for a UTC period (day or month, with start in it). The tenant that spends most is first. The response also has the current spend against the global spend cap (spend_cap). This is always the current window of the cap, with fraction = spent / cap — AdminUsageReport 200 FORBIDDEN PUT /v1/admin/executors/{name} Enable or disable an executor (audited, reason is necessary). The platform does not lease new work to a disabled executor. Orchestrator reports never enable it again ExecutorUpdate ExecutorHealth 200 SCHEMA_INVALID, NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN GET /v1/admin/audit The platform audit log. Filters: tenant_id, project_id, actor_id, action, outcome, since, until — Page[AuditEvent] 200 FORBIDDEN

docs.title: Browser session (backend-for-frontend)
docs.text:
These routes have no version. They are at the root, next to the web app.

Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors GET /auth/login Start the sign-in. It redirects to the identity provider with response_type=code, a PKCE code_challenge (S256), state and nonce. ?return_to= must be a path on the same origin. If it is not, the API uses /. — — 302 — GET /auth/callback Do a check of state. Exchange the code with the PKCE verifier. Verify the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry). Set the session cookie and redirect to return_to — — 302 UNAUTHENTICATED POST /auth/logout End the session and clear the cookies. It works without a valid session. With a valid session, it needs X-CSRF-Token. — — 204 — GET /auth/session Tells if the browser is signed in, the identity, and the expiry time. authenticated: false is a 200, not a 401. — SessionInfo 200 —

The server keeps the login transaction (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) for 10 minutes. A __Host-mapi_login cookie with SameSite=Lax refers to it. The cookie uses this setting because the redirect back from the identity provider is a cross-site navigation, and that navigation does not send a Strict cookie. Sessions expire after 2 hours with no activity or after 12 hours in total. Each API route that changes state accepts only JSON. A cross-site form cannot send JSON without a CORS preflight. The session cookie is SameSite=Strict, thus cross-site requests never send it.

Also, each cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE must send the CSRF token of the session in an X-CSRF-Token header. This includes POST /auth/logout when a session is live. The API refuses the request (403 FORBIDDEN) in these conditions:

  • Its Origin is not the web app or the API.
  • It has Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site.

The web app reads the token from the __Host-mapi_csrf cookie (readable, SameSite=Strict) or from the X-CSRF-Token header of GET /auth/session. Requests with an API token do not need a CSRF token.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text:
Endpoint Purpose Request Response Success Errors POST /internal/events Pub/Sub push of run events from the Cloud Logging sink PubSubPushEnvelope Ingest result 200 UNAUTHENTICATED, SCHEMA_INVALID

The push envelope is {message: {data, attributes, messageId, publishTime}, subscription, deliveryAttempt}. message.data is a base64 Cloud Logging entry. Its jsonPayload.mapi_event is one HMAC-signed run event (see Run protocol). The request must have Authorization: Bearer <Google-signed ID token>. After the server verifies the signature, it does a check of the claims with mapi_spec.auth.check_push_claims:

  • The issuer is https://accounts.google.com.
  • The audience is the configured audience.
  • The verified e-mail is the e-mail of the push service account.
  • The token is not expired.

If an event fails its HMAC, the server acknowledges it with 200, because a new delivery cannot help. The server records it in the audit log as event.rejected.

docs.title: Quotas and rate limits on every endpoint
docs.text:
The platform does a check of requests and submissions against three levels of quota: token, tenant and global (see Quotas and cost).

  • If a request goes above a requests-per-minute limit, the API returns 429 RATE_LIMITED with a Retry-After header. Try again after that number of seconds.
  • If a submission goes above a compute, concurrency, fan-out, resource-class, storage or egress limit, the API returns 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The API sets Retry-After when the limit resets with a window (the UTC day or month). The detail of the problem gives the level and the limit.
  • The platform kill switches (uploaded code paused, global spend cap reached) also return QUOTA_EXCEEDED, at the global level.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
v0.4 (milestone M3) adds the contracts for Guided mode and for the connection of other applications. These contracts are:

  • Guided templates and drafts.
  • Business priors and lift tests.
  • What-if scenarios.
  • Endpoints and aliases.
  • Code snippets.
  • Webhooks.
  • Saved and rendered plots, with embed links.
  • The trust lifecycle (sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and export).

The endpoint table agrees with mapi_spec.api.M3_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ROUTE_ACCESS gives the scope and the permission of each operation. mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the full v0.4 surface (M1, M2 and M3). The route-table test of the server makes sure that the server serves each row. Guided mode and Integrations explain the ideas.

Project-scoped M3 routes get the project from X-Mapi-Project, as all v0.3 routes do.

docs.title: Guided mode
docs.text:
GET /v1/guided/templates lists the built-in templates (GuidedTemplate). Each template has these items:

  • Questions in plain language.
  • The built-in plugin that the questions are for.
  • A ModelSpec template with {{placeholder}} strings.
  • Default settings.
  • The scorecard checks that apply.
  • x-ui-level hints.

Role detection (POST /v1/guided/detect-roles) ranks the columns of an upload for each question. It uses ColumnProfiles that the browser calculates. It can also use a stored dataset version: the columns.json of its ingest, or else its schema and summary. It returns RoleSuggestions. Each candidate has a confidence and a reason_plain.

A draft (POST /v1/guided/drafts) changes GuidedAnswers into an IngestMapping for the upload, a ModelSpec document and its YAML ("View as YAML"). It does not store anything. The findings of the static validator are in issues. To save the draft, use POST /v1/specs.

A sandboxed translate_priors run changes business priors into model-space priors (PriorTranslationRequest → PriorTranslation). The result of the translation is a PriorTranslationResult, with a prior-predictive preview in business units.

POST /v1/guided/requests:compile changes a what-if scenario, a forecast or an intervention preset (GuidedCompile) into the equivalent ScoreRequest. Thus, "Run exact" sends a real score run.

The persona lock is Project.guided_locked. To change it, use PATCH /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id} (ProjectUpdate.guided_locked). In a locked project, members below admin get 403 FORBIDDEN from POST /v1/specs and POST /v1/specs/{spec_id}/revisions. The only exception is Guided specs that keep the advanced and hidden fields of their template.

This release serves the templates, role detection, drafts and the lock (see From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft).

docs.title: Endpoints and aliases
docs.text:
An endpoint is a stable alias (endpoint://<project>/<alias>) for one model version. PUT promotes a version. The promotion gate (PromotionGateDecision) does a check of the scorecard:

  • If the scorecard passes, the gate permits the promotion.
  • If the scorecard has a warning, the gate asks for override: true with a reason from a signed-in project admin (409 OVERRIDE_REQUIRED). The audit log records the override as endpoint.promote_override.
  • If the scorecard fails, the gate blocks the promotion (409 PROMOTION_BLOCKED).

By default, the EvaluationPolicy of the endpoint needs evaluate_then_refit fits. It also blocks changes to the input schema that would break callers.

POST …/score takes an EndpointScoreCall. This is a score request without model. Its data and scenario can be inline XrJSON datasets of up to 5 MB. The answer is the same as for …:score on a model version. With Prefer: wait=60, you get 200 with the result if the run completes in time. If not, you get 202 with the run.

A score:<alias> token can read the endpoint, its schema, history and snippets, and can score it. endpoints:promote tokens can promote and roll back, but they cannot override the gate.

docs.title: Saved plots, rendering and embeds
docs.text:
A SavedPlot keeps a plot of a model version or a PlotSpec that a user wrote. Rendering (PlotRenderRequest → PlotRender) makes PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox. Embed links (PlotEmbedCreate → PlotEmbedCreated, listed as PlotEmbed) have tokens, are read-only and expire. You can embed only plots of platform recipes (422 EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED).

The public GET /v1/embeds/{embed_token} returns an EmbedView with all datasets inline, or 410 LINK_EXPIRED. It does not read credentials. It answers cross-origin reads only from the plot sandbox origin. See Sharing plots.

docs.title: Sign-up, verification, deletion and export
docs.text:
Self-service sign-up (SignupRequest → SignupAccepted) gives the same answer for new and known addresses. Verification of the e-mail (EmailVerify → VerificationResult) creates a public-tier tenant.

VerificationStatus tells if the tenant can upload code. Public tenants cannot upload code before cut line B. After cut line B, they can upload code only after identity verification. Operators record the identity verification with VerificationUpdate.

Deletion starts after a grace period (TenantDeletionRequest → TenantDeletion, with the progress for each store). During the grace period, the tenant is suspended and can cancel the deletion. A GDPR export (GdprExportRequest → GdprExport) puts all the data that the tenant stored into a package.

docs.title: Workflows, governance, explorers and About cards v0.5
docs.text:
v0.5 (milestone M3.5) adds the contracts for these items:

  • Automated workflows: statistical tests, data processing, splits, searches and models in one versioned DAG.
  • Model governance: policies, checks with evidence, validation and approval.
  • The Data Explorer and the Model Explorer.
  • Budget optimisation with mmm-framework.
  • The plain-language About cards, with the Help me choose chooser.

The endpoint table agrees with mapi_spec.api.M35_ENDPOINTS. mapi_spec.api.ENDPOINTS is the full v0.5 surface (V04_ENDPOINTS + M35_ENDPOINTS). ROUTE_ACCESS gives the scope and the permission of each operation. Workflows, Governance and About cards and choosing explain the ideas.

v0.5 also removes an importer route of v0.4, its ingest preset and one snippet language (see the CHANGELOG). Thus, mmm-framework is the only MMM engine. The contract version is 0.2.

Permissions. These rules apply:

  • Viewers read workflows. Editors write them. Runners run and schedule them. Admins delete them.
  • Project admins manage project policies. Tenant admins manage tenant-wide policies. All members of the project can read the policies.
  • To submit a model version for validation, you need run rights (validate on model).
  • To approve or reject, you need the reviewer capability (Membership.capabilities, given with MembershipUpdate). Project admins have this capability automatically.
  • The person who submitted a model version cannot approve or reject it (403 SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN).
  • No API token can approve.

The new token scopes are workflows:write, workflows:run, models:validate and policies:manage.

Long-running work. A workflow run, an explore run and an optimize run are the same as other runs (Idempotency-Key, the quota checks, cost). POST …:optimize obeys Prefer: wait=N. Workflow runs stream their node events on GET /v1/workflow-runs/{run_id}/events (SSE with Last-Event-ID, event types in WorkflowEventType). The terminal events also go to webhooks (workflow.run.succeeded, workflow.run.failed). These events also go to webhooks: validation transitions (model.validated, model.rejected, ...), dataset.version.created and optimize.completed.

Promotion. A governance policy that applies to a model can set require_validated_for_promotion. In this case, PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias} refuses a version if its validation status is not validated (409 NOT_VALIDATED). No override can pass this check.

docs.title: Built-in models
docs.text:
These model plugins come with the platform (tier T0). They register through the mapi.models entry point. Thus default_registry() and the control-plane catalog show them without configuration. Each plugin passes the contract kit (mapi_sdk.testing.check_model). Each plugin also has a conformance fixture (see Conformance corpus). From v0.5, the marketing-mix models run on mmm-framework. This is the only marketing-mix engine of the platform.

Calibration (M3, the calibration block of the spec, Guided task 3): each plugin declares it in Capabilities.calibration. A spec can have calibration data for a plugin that does not declare it. Such a spec fails static validation with CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED:

Plugin Business priors Lift tests mmm.bayesian yes - log-normal ROI priors for each channel (priors.roi) and the intercept yes - mmm-framework experiment likelihoods (marginal ROAS or contribution) mmm.frequentist no no

Guided modelling gives the math of the translation and of each lift likelihood.

Plugin Package Representation Score modes Corpus fixture mmm.bayesian@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate e33, guided_mmm mmm.frequentist@1 mapi-plugin-mmm draws (bootstrap) predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate mmm_frequentist ts.hsgp_trend@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, evaluate c08 ts.gaussian_hmm@1 mapi-plugin-ts draws predict, forecast, filter, evaluate e24 tabular.hierarchical_glm@1 mapi-plugin-tabular draws predict, counterfactual, evaluate e02 tabular.regressor@1 mapi-plugin-tabular quantiles predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate xgb_store_demand choice.multinomial_logit@1 mapi-plugin-tabular draws (Bayesian bootstrap) predict, forecast, counterfactual, evaluate e84_lite ts.sarimax@1 mapi-plugin-statsmodels quantiles predict, forecast, evaluate sm_arimax ts.vecm@1 mapi-plugin-statsmodels quantiles predict, forecast, evaluate sm_vecm_macro sci.lgcp_grid@1 mapi-plugin-science draws predict, forecast, evaluate e07_lgcp sci.fisher_kpp@1 mapi-plugin-science draws predict, forecast, evaluate e50_kpp sci.traction_force@1 mapi-plugin-science draws predict, evaluate e60_traction sci.strong_lens@1 mapi-plugin-science draws predict, simulate, evaluate e80_lens ts.arima@1, ts.ets@1, ts.theta@1, ts.unobserved_components@1, ts.ardl@1, ts.ecm@1, ts.var@1, ts.varmax@1, ts.dynamic_factor@1, ts.markov_switching@1 mapi-plugin-statsmodels quantiles predict, forecast, evaluate contract kit and reference-value tests

statsmodels time-series models describes the statsmodels plugins. These are the ARIMA family, exponential smoothing, theta, ARDL and error correction, VAR, VECM, VARMAX, dynamic factors and Markov switching.

Plugins use canonical names for their inputs. Bind the names of your dataset to them in the data.bind block of the spec. Outputs come back with your names (reverse binding). New variables, for example y_hat, keep their names.

The mapi-sklearn package also registers five general tabular plugins (see Tabular models):

  • sklearn.tabular_regressor
  • sklearn.tabular_quantiles
  • sklearn.tabular_bootstrap
  • sklearn.tabular_conformal
  • sklearn.tabular_classifier

Every setting, generated

The platform makes the models catalog from the installed manifests. It shows the capabilities, outputs and derived quantities. It also shows each setting with its default and Guided-mode level, and the contract for the input data.

docs.title: mmm.bayesian: marketing mix on mmm-framework
docs.text:
This plugin uses the BayesianMMM of mmm-framework. It has these parts:

  • Adstock (geometric, delayed, Weibull) and saturation (logistic, Hill, Michaelis-Menten, tanh, root) for each channel.
  • A trend (none, linear, piecewise, spline, GP).
  • Fourier seasonality.
  • Baselines with partial pooling across geos and products. Channel effects for each geo are optional.
  • Channel effects as returns on spend.

The model owns scaling, carry-over and units (owns: [scaling, carryover, inverse_units]). Thus the pipeline only converts currencies and resamples. With outputs.derived, the fit caches contributions, response curves for each draw and marginal costs. The mmm-framework planning optimises budgets (POST …:optimize). The model declares a decision objective.

Inputs. y(*panel, time), spend(*panel, channel, time), and other numeric variables over time as controls. The panel dims are hierarchy.pool_over (geo, product). New panel levels follow new_levels (pooled by default). channel is fixed. time extends.

Outputs. y_hat(*panel, time) and contributions(component, *panel, time). The components are one for each channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and one for each control. Their sum is y_hat.

Marketing-mix models on mmm-framework tells how the settings map to mmm-framework. It also tells about priors, lift tests and optimisation. For a complete analysis, read the marketing-mix guide.

docs.title: mmm.frequentist: fast marketing mix
docs.text: This plugin uses the ridge estimator of mmm-framework. An out-of-sample search selects the adstock and saturation. The channel effects are not negative. The bootstrap gives confidence intervals (the replicates are the draws). The data contract and outputs are the same as mmm.bayesian. There are no priors, no lift tests and no convergence diagnostics. The same seed gives the same result, and a fit takes seconds.

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend — smooth trend with seasonality
docs.text:
This plugin has a Hilbert-space Gaussian process (HSGP) trend, an optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality. It is for one series with regular spaces between periods (CO2 as at Mauna Loa, sales, traffic).

Inputs. t (time, policy extend) and the target y(t). Missing months are permitted. Replace sentinel codes with core.replace_sentinel. The likelihood then does not use these months, but the model interpolates them. Put core.standardize on y. The priors are on the standardised scale, and the model changes the outputs back to your units.

Forecast horizon. max_extension (default 24 periods) is part of the input schema of the model. At fit time, the model sets the size of the HSGP domain from the anticipated coordinates. These are the fitted range plus max_extension periods. Thus each forecast up to that horizon evaluates exactly the fitted functions. The server rejects a longer horizon with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT (HTTP 409) before it starts to compute. Fit again with a larger max_extension.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 24 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach without a new fit kernel expquad expquad, matern52 or matern32 m, c 30, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation lengthscale_mu, lengthscale_sigma 0.4, 0.5 Log-normal lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] eta_sigma 1.0 Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude linear_trend true Adds intercept + slope * t season_period, season_order 12, 3 Fourier seasonality (periods of t, order) noise_sigma 0.5 Half-normal scale of the observation noise

Outputs. y_hat(t) (the expected value or a predictive draw) and trend(t). trend(t) is the long-term component without seasonality. The two outputs are in the units of the target.

data:
  bind: {dims: {t: date}, vars: {y: co2}}
  split: {kind: time_holdout, dim: t, last: 12}
pipeline:
  - {id: clean, use: core.replace_sentinel@^1, with: {vars: [y], below: 0}}
  - {id: scale, use: core.standardize@^1, with: {vars: [y], over: [t]}}
model:
  use: ts.hsgp_trend@^1
  settings: {max_extension: 24, season_order: 2}
  fit: {mode: evaluate_then_refit, engine: pymc, seed: 11}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm — hidden states with a terminal state
docs.text:
This plugin is a Gaussian hidden Markov model with K states. It uses many sequences at the same time (animal tracks, machine regimes, customer phases). The forward algorithm sums out the hidden states. Thus the sampler is fast and exact.

Inputs. A padded layout with these items: animal (the sequence dim, new_levels with strategy pooled), step (extend), y(animal, step) with NaN padding, and a boolean mask(animal, step).

Terminal state. After the fit, the bundle keeps the filtered state distribution at the last fitted step. It is the terminal_state group of the bundle, alpha_T(chain, draw, animal, state).

  • predict / evaluate use the one-step-ahead state distribution of the fit in the fitted range. After the fitted range, they use alpha_T, propagated by the transition matrix. They do not use targets in the payload.
  • forecast propagates alpha_T over the horizon.
  • filter runs the forward filter over new observations that continue the fitted steps. It returns an updated terminal_state group with the filtered state_prob.
  • New animals start from the initial distribution pi at the first fitted step.

After the sampler stops, the model gives new labels to the draws so that the state means increase (label switching). identification: ordered uses an ordered prior instead. The manifest declares pointwise LOO as not valid, because the steps in a track are dependent. Validation rejects elpd_loo.

Setting Default Meaning n_states 2 Number of hidden states mu_center, mu_sigma 0.0, 2.0 Normal prior of the state means sigma_scale 1.0 Half-normal scale of the sds for each state stickiness 2.0 Additional Dirichlet weight to stay in the same state pi_concentration 1.0 Dirichlet weight of the initial distribution identification relabel relabel (sort the draws by mean) or ordered

Outputs. y_hat(animal, step) in your units, and state_prob(animal, step, state). The units of state_prob are probability. The model does not inverse-transform it.

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm — partial pooling in long layout
docs.text:
This plugin has intercepts that change by group, and optionally slopes that change by group. It has group-level predictors. Examples are the radon model and many similar models (schools, stores, clinics).

Inputs. A long layout with these items:

  • Rows along obs (extend).
  • A group dim (group_dim, default county, new_levels with strategy hyperprior).
  • The index <group_dim>_idx(obs).
  • The target y(obs).
  • Observation-level covariates and group-level group_covariates.

Covariates are part of the input schema. Thus, if a spec names a covariate that is missing, the spec fails validation.

New groups. For a county that the model did not see, the model draws its effect from the fitted hyperprior for each posterior draw. Its group-level covariates move its prior mean in the same way as for fitted counties. Score payloads can list counties in any sequence. The platform maps county_idx again.

Setting Default Meaning group_dim county The grouping dim family normal normal, student_t, poisson (log link) or bernoulli (logit) covariates [] Predictors over obs varying_slopes [] Covariates whose slope varies by group group_covariates [] Predictors over the group dim centered false Use centred group effects

docs.title: tabular.regressor — quantile regression for panels
docs.text:
This plugin is the store-demand model of the plan. The model stacks rows from labelled dims (store × sku × week). The coordinates become categorical features. An estimator from the allow list predicts conditional quantiles. The estimator setting accepts only the estimators of the registry that can predict quantiles. These are xgboost, the gradient boosting and histogram boosting of scikit-learn, and quantile regression. Validation rejects other estimators.

  • Defaults: xgboost (300 trees, depth 5, learning rate 0.05) and quantiles [0.1, 0.5, 0.9].
  • The model pools new stores (new_levels: pooled).
  • The forecast is direct. Thus you must supply the future covariates that have the future_required mark. If you do not, the error is MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE.
  • Quantiles are for each cell. The server refuses to aggregate them across stores (CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED).
  • The manifest lists core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time and ml.feature_importance.

All other settings are the settings of mapi_sklearn (see Tabular models).

docs.title: choice.multinomial_logit — which product customers pick
docs.text:
This plugin is the built-in model of the Guided customer choice template (household panels as in E84). On each shopping trip, a household selects one product. Price and promotions change the choice.

Inputs. A dense hh × trip panel, with the alternatives along product (categorical, fixed). hh is categorical, with new_levels with strategy hyperprior. trip is index and extend. The target y(hh, trip) is text: the product that the household selected. It is empty when a household made no trip (ragged panels are permitted). Covariates are variables for each alternative along product, for example price(hh, trip, product) and promo(hh, trip, product). By default, each numeric variable with the product dim is a covariate. If the covariates of a product are missing on a trip, that product was not available on that trip (not on the shelf).

Model. A conditional logit with product intercepts for each household: U[h, t, j] = asc[j] + Σ_k beta[k]·x_k[h, t, j] + u[h, j]. The choice probabilities are a softmax over the available products. u[h, j] ~ Normal(0, effect_sd) (a random-intercept logit). The fit uses penalised maximum likelihood, that is, the posterior mode of that model.

Uncertainty comes from the Bayesian bootstrap. Each of the fit.draws draws is a new fit with Dirichlet weights on households. Thus each household keeps its own effect in each draw, and the draws are joint. In the draws representation, shares, counterfactual deltas and sums over trips are valid. There is no pointwise log-likelihood, so LOO is not available.

Scoring. y_hat(hh, trip, product) is the choice probability (expected), or one sampled choice for each draw (predictive, one-hot). The fit did not see some households. For each draw, the model draws their preferences from Normal(0, sd). sd is the spread of the fitted effects in that draw. A trip that the household did not make has probability 0 for all products. Thus sums over trips count the expected purchases.

Price scenarios are interventions, for example {var: price, sel: {product: cola}, multiply: 1.1} in a counterfactual request. To match choice values to product labels, the model changes them to lower case and replaces punctuation with _.

Setting Default Meaning covariates each numeric variable along product Covariates for each alternative random_effects [hh] Household product intercepts ([]: none) effect_sd 1.0 Prior sd of the household effects (a smaller value pools more) coef_sd 10.0 Prior sd of the product intercepts and coefficients reference the first product The product whose intercept is fixed at 0 max_iter 500 Iterations of each L-BFGS fit

fit.draws (default 100, maximum 2000) sets the number of bootstrap draws. With fit.seed, you get the same draws each time. The CHOICE_HIT_RATE diagnostic gives the in-sample hit rate.

Holdout metrics. A text target with one score probability for each product gets the categorical metrics of evaluate.metrics:

  • accuracy: the hit rate of the most likely product.
  • accuracy_naive: the hit rate if you always select the most common product of the holdout.
  • accuracy_lift: the difference between the two.
  • log_score: the mean log probability of the product that the household bought.
  • brier: the multi-class Brier score.

The Guided customer_choice template evaluates all five on the last trip of each household. Its scorecard runs holdout.hit_rate. For a text target, the server skips numeric metrics, for example mape.

docs.title: Scientific models (mapi-plugin-science)
docs.text:
These plugins come from the case studies of pymc-challenges. Their data are maps, images and fields on a regular grid. Their outputs are fields with a range for each cell. Each output that is a field declares a grid (OutputDecl.grid: the row dim y, the column dim x, an optional frame dim and an optional component dim for a vector field). The platform then shows the output in two places:

  • The Fields section of the Model Explorer. It shows the mean, the sd, mean ÷ sd, the 5% and 95% maps and single draws, with a frame slider and a draw player.
  • The sci.* plot recipes (see Plot recipes).

The runner images of base-bayes contain these plugins (namespace sci).

Real data

Each data module has a from_challenges(path) function. It reads the real data file of the case study from a local copy of pymc-challenges. To run the tests that use the real files, set MAPI_PYMC_CHALLENGES_DATA to the data/ directory of that copy. Without it, these tests are skipped.

docs.title: sci.lgcp_grid — event counts on a map over time (E07)
docs.text:
A log-Gaussian Cox process on a space-time grid. The total for each period follows a random walk. The share of each cell comes from a 2-D Hilbert-space GP (Matérn 5/2) whose map changes from one era (a group of periods) to the next.

Inputs. period (time, policy extend), row and col (integer, fixed) and the target count(period, row, col). Row 0 is the south edge of the grid.

Outputs. rate(period, row, col) (a field with a frame for each period, log colour scale) and total(period). The sum of rate over the cells is equal to total.

Setting Default Meaning max_extension 8 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach without a new fit era_periods 4 The number of periods in one era. The map changes from era to era field era_walk era_walk (a new map for each era) or static (one map) cell_km 25 The width of one cell in km m_row, m_col, c 10, 14, 1.5 Basis functions and boundary factor of the approximation ell_lower_km, ell_upper_km 15, 100 The 5% and 95% quantiles of the lengthscale prior likelihood negbin negbin or poisson

from_challenges puts the Oklahoma earthquake catalogue into 12 × 9 cells of 25 km for each quarter from 2009 to 2019. A fit on 2009–2017 takes approximately one minute with nutpie.

docs.title: sci.fisher_kpp — a reaction-diffusion PDE (E50)
docs.text:
The Fisher-KPP equation du/dt = D d²u/dx² + lam u (1 - u) moves and grows cells into a scratch wound. The model solves the equation in the model graph (explicit Euler in pytensor.scan, zero flux at the edges). The counts are Poisson. With delay: true, the movement and the growth start slowly after the scratch (tanh(beta t)).

Inputs. t (integer hours, policy extend), x (float positions in µm, equal spaces, fixed) and the target count(t, x). The first time is the initial condition. The likelihood does not use it. Each time after the first must be on the Euler grid.

Outputs. density(t, x) (a field: time on the rows, position on the columns) and the scalar wave_speed (2 sqrt(D lam), µm/h). A forecast continues the PDE to later times.

Setting Default Meaning steps_per_hour 10 Euler steps for each hour delay true Multiply the movement and the growth by tanh(beta t) max_extension 4 The number of periods after the fit that a forecast can reach diffusivity_median, growth_median 1000, 0.05 Prior medians of D (µm²/h) and lam (1/h) capacity_mu, capacity_sigma 122, 15 Prior of the capacity K (cells for each column) cfl_quantile 0.99 The prior quantile of D that must keep the Euler steps stable

If the Euler steps are not stable at the cfl_quantile of the prior of D, the model stops with SETTINGS_INVALID. The message gives the smallest steps_per_hour that is stable.

docs.title: sci.traction_force — cell forces from gel movement (E60)
docs.text:
Fourier-transform traction cytometry as a Gaussian inverse problem. The data are a displacement field of a soft gel. The output is the traction field that the cells apply. NUTS samples only the noise sd and the prior spectrum. The model integrates the field out, with one closed-form likelihood for each Fourier mode. At score time, the model draws each traction field exactly with two FFTs for each posterior draw.

Inputs. component (categorical x, y), row and col (integer, fixed) and the target displacement(component, row, col) in µm. The raster must have no missing pixels. Thus the model has no split: evaluate it in sample. With force_mask: true, the data also has a force_mask(row, col).

Outputs. traction(component, row, col) (a vector field, Pa), displacement_hat, and the scalars strain_energy (fJ) and contractility (µN).

Setting Default Meaning grid_um, young_pa, poisson 1, 10000, 0.49 Grid spacing (µm), Young's modulus (Pa) and Poisson ratio of the gel young_cv 0 Relative uncertainty of Young's modulus (0 = known) prior matern white (Tikhonov), smooth or matern field_draws 100 The number of traction fields to draw for each score force_mask false Sum the strain energy and the contractility inside force_mask only

The NOISE_SPECTRUM_MISMATCH diagnostic compares the power of the data in the finest modes with the model. Correlated noise from overlapping PIV windows causes it, and then the ranges are too narrow. challenges_settings(ds) gives the settings for the real pyTFM colony of from_challenges.

docs.title: sci.strong_lens — a galaxy-scale strong lens (E80)
docs.text:
A pixel forward model of a strong gravitational lens in a telescope image. The mass is a singular isothermal ellipsoid with an optional external shear. Rays from each pixel (and from sub-pixels) go back to the source plane. The source and the lens light are Sérsic profiles, and the model applies the PSF of the image. The model integrates the linear light amplitudes out in closed form. A staged search for the mode starts the sampler, and NUTS samples near that mode with a Laplace preconditioner.

Inputs. row and col (integer, fixed, row 0 at the bottom), the target image(row, col), the inverse variance weight(row, col) (0 leaves a pixel out) and a constant psf(psf_row, psf_col) with odd sides. With use_mask: true, the data also has a bool mask(row, col).

Outputs. model_image(row, col) (a field, grey scale), source(source_row, source_col) (the source on a source-plane grid), the scalar einstein_radius (arcsec) and, when z_lens and z_source are set, einstein_mass (solar masses). The fit keeps the critical curve, the caustic and the cut of each posterior draw as the derived group critical_curves. In simulate mode, the model makes new noisy images from the posterior.

Setting Default Meaning pixel_scale 0.05 Pixel size (arcsec) subsample 2 Rays for each pixel along each axis lens_light_components 2 Sérsic profiles of the lens galaxy light (0 to 2) external_shear true Add an external shear to the mass noise_correlation 0 Correlation of the noise between neighbour pixels (drizzled images) theta_e_median, theta_e_log_sd 1.0, 0.5 Log-normal prior of the Einstein radius n_starts 5 Starts of the search for the mode source_grid, source_half_width 30, 0.45 Size of the source-plane grid (pixels, arcsec) curve_draws 100 Posterior draws with critical curves

The model has no LOO (loo_valid is false). from_challenges reads the HST F814W image of SDSS J1627-0053 (an 81 × 81 cutout and a PSF from the star stamps). On that image the posterior Einstein radius is 1.223 ± 0.001 arcsec. The fit takes approximately 5 to 7 minutes.

docs.title: OpenAPI explorer v0.2
docs.text:
This page shows the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the /v1 API. Redoc renders the document. The document is the committed file apps/web/openapi.json. A script makes it from the FastAPI app of the server and the mapi_spec.api models (uv run python apps/web/scripts/gen_openapi.py). CI fails when the file is different from the server. A running API serves the same document at /openapi.json.

Open full screen Download openapi.json

The explorer loads nothing from outside this site. The script scripts/vendor_redoc.py copies the Redoc bundle (version 2.5.4) into the repository. The script does a check of the integrity of the npm tarball and pins the SHA-256 of the bundle. A Content-Security-Policy on the page permits scripts, styles, images and requests from this site only.

For descriptions of the conventions, idempotency, server-sent events and the errors of each endpoint, read the HTTP API reference. For a full example, read the HTTP API guide.

docs.title: Plots reference (mapi-plots)
docs.text:
mapi-plots has two parts. Each part has different dependencies:

Install Modules Imports Runs in mapi-plots mapi_plots.sanitize, mapi_plots.templates mapi-spec, jsonschema (JSON only) API server, runner, notebooks mapi-plots[recipes] mapi_plots.convert, mapi_plots.recipes, mapi_plots.packs, mapi_plots.examples + altair, plotly, numpy, pandas, pyarrow, xarray runner images, notebooks

An import-linter contract makes sure that the sanitizer and the templates do not import numpy, pandas, xarray, pyarrow, altair, plotly or mapi_sdk. import mapi_plots loads no large modules, because the exports are lazy.

docs.title: The PlotSpec envelope
docs.text:
The contract package mapi_spec.plots defines the envelope:

id: core.ppc_fan                    # [A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,128}
title: Fit and forecast
kind: vega-lite                     # or plotly
spec: {...}                         # Vega-Lite JSON, or Plotly {data, layout, frames, config}
datasets:                           # referenced BY NAME only
  fan: {kind: inline_arrow, data: <base64 Arrow IPC stream>, rows: 84}
  big: {kind: data_ref, path: ui/plotdata/fan.arrow, format: arrow}
bindings: {x: "dim:time", y: "role:target", facet: "dim:geo"}   # templates only
schema_version: v6.4.1
persona: both                       # guided | expert | both
caption_plain: "The line is the model's median estimate ..."
provenance: {recipe: core.ppc_fan@1.0.0, bundle_id: ..., generated_at: ...}
  • Vega-Lite references data with {"data": {"name": "fan"}}.
  • Plotly references a column with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"} in a data-array attribute. It also uses this reference in arrayOk attributes, for example marker.color. The part before the first . is the dataset. The remaining part is the column (trace0.marker.color → dataset trace0, column marker.color). The JSON Schema of the reference is mapi_plots.sanitize.PLOTLY_REF_SCHEMA. It is also in the file mapi_plots/sanitize/schemas/plotly-ref.schema.json:
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "urn:mapi:schema:plotly-dataset-ref:v1",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {"$ref": {"type": "string",
    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_\\-]{0,63}\\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.\\-]{0,127}$"}},
  "required": ["$ref"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}
  • The maximum size of each inline Arrow dataset is 2 MiB of base64. Recipes write datasets in a compact format (float32, int32, dictionary-encoded strings). Timestamps are UTC milliseconds.

docs.title: Sanitizer
docs.text:
from mapi_plots.sanitize import sanitize_plot, check_plot, sanitize_spec, SanitizeLimits

result = sanitize_plot(doc)            # PlotSpec | dict | JSON str | bytes
result.plot                            # validated, sanitized PlotSpec
result.changes                         # list[Issue] (severity info): HTML stripped, $schema pinned ...

issues = check_plot(doc)               # errors + changes, never raises
spec, changes = sanitize_spec("plotly", figure_dict)   # bare spec, no envelope

SanitizeError is a MapiError. err.issues lists all violations, up to max_issues. Each violation has these items:

  • An RFC 6901 pointer.
  • A message that the platform wrote.
  • The rule, in context["rule"].
  • Text from the user, if there is some. This text is only in untrusted_text.

err.rules is the set of rules that fired. The error code is the most severe code that is present:

Code HTTP Rules PLOT_UNSAFE 422 url_data, href, external_image, tile_map, proto_key, script_url, css_url, expression, format_type, config PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 too_large, too_deep, too_many_nodes, string_too_long, array_too_long SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 parse (JSON that is not valid, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity) SCHEMA_INVALID 422 schema, envelope, dataset_ref, typed_array

Changes use the rules html_stripped, schema_url and template_pruned. Changes are not errors.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: SanitizeLimits field Default max_document_bytes 16 MiB (the full PlotSpec, with the inline Arrow data) max_spec_bytes 2 MiB (the spec member) max_depth 48 max_nodes 200 000 max_string_bytes 64 KiB (the envelope sets the limit for inline Arrow payloads) max_array_items 100 000 max_expr_chars 2 000 max_typed_array_bytes 8 MiB max_issues 50

docs.title: Vega-Lite rules
docs.text:
1. $schema must be an official Vega-Lite v5 or v6 URL, or not present. The sanitizer sets it to v6.4.1.
  2. The spec must be valid against the vendored Vega-Lite v6.4.1 JSON Schema (draft-07, local $refs only).
  3. Do not use these items: a url key at any location, href, and the image mark. formatType can only be number, time or utc. Do not enable config.customFormatTypes.

  4. Expressions must use only Vega functions from the allow list. Expressions are:

    • expr, calculate and filter/test strings, and their and/or/not compositions.
    • Each …Expr key, for example labelExpr.
    • Filters in brackets in selection event streams.

    The sanitizer rejects these items: method calls, this/new, assignment, statements, template and regex literals, and \u/\x escapes. It also rejects non-ASCII characters outside strings, and computed member access with a key that is not a literal. It also rejects browser globals (window, document, fetch, globalThis …) and event.view.

docs.title: Plotly rules
docs.text:
1. The top level has only data, layout, frames and config.
  2. The sanitizer does a check of trace types, attribute names and value types against a table. This table comes from the official plotly.js 4.1.1 plot-schema.json. It has enumerations, flag lists, subplot ids, colour scales and info arrays. It also has subplot keys of the xaxis2 type, and template keys of the annotationdefaults type.
  3. Unknown attributes are errors. In layout.template, the sanitizer removes unknown attributes and tile-map sections, and reports them.
  4. Data arrays are inline lists, dataset references or plotly.py typed arrays ({dtype: i1|u1|u1c|i2|u2|i4|u4|f4|f8, bdata, shape?}). The sanitizer does a check of the base64, length and shape of typed arrays.
  5. The sanitizer rejects these items:
    • Tile-map traces and subplots.
    • Image sources that are not data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64. This rule also applies in the relayout arguments of updatemenus/sliders.
    • url/href/topojsonURL keys.
    • Network config options.
  6. Strings can keep only <b> <i> <br> <sub> <sup>. The sanitizer removes attributes and escapes a stray <. <extra> stays in hover templates.

docs.title: Recipes (mapi_plots.recipes)
docs.text:
get_recipe(id) -> Recipe                 # bundled recipes (core + packs)
standard_recipes() -> list[Recipe]       # entry point  mapi.plots: core
mapi_plots.packs.mmm.mmm_recipes()       # entry point  mapi.plots: mmm
mapi_plots.packs.ml.ml_recipes()         # entry point  mapi.plots: ml

Recipe.render(data, **settings) -> PlotSpec       # also Recipe(data, **settings)

# what the runner calls for outputs.plots: never raises for a single bad plot
report = render_plots(tree, ["core.ppc_fan", "mmm.response_curves@^1"],
                      registry=None, options={"core.ppc_fan": {"facet": "market"}})
report.plots          # sanitized PlotSpecs
report.issues         # skipped plots: REF_UNRESOLVED / SCHEMA_INVALID / USER_CODE_ERROR
                      # (warnings) and PLOT_UNSAFE (error)
report.to_json()      # plots.json sidecar body

To write your own recipe, use the decorator. The result works with Registry.register and the mapi.plots entry-point group:

import altair as alt
from mapi_plots.recipes import Figure, RecipeSettings, named, recipe


class Settings(RecipeSettings):
    var: str = "y_hat"


@recipe("acme.weekly_total", title="Weekly total", settings=Settings, persona="guided")
def weekly_total(inp, s: Settings) -> Figure:
    ds = inp.require("summary")
    frame = ds[s.var].sel(stat="mean").sum("market").to_dataframe().reset_index()
    chart = alt.Chart(named("weekly")).mark_line().encode(x="date:T", y=f"{s.var}:Q")
    return Figure(chart, {"weekly": frame}, caption=f"Total {s.var} per week.")

A recipe can also return a Plotly figure (plotly.graph_objects.Figure or a {data, layout, frames} dict) in Figure.chart. Recipe.render then sends it through from_plotly with the same title, caption, persona and provenance. The recipe can also give its own DataFrames in Figure.datasets. The traces then refer to their columns with {"$ref": "<dataset>.<column>"}. The function plotly_plot applies the inline-text rules to the string columns of these DataFrames.

docs.title: Scientific-model pack (sci.*)
docs.text:
The sci.* recipes make Plotly figures for models with gridded outputs, vector fields, profiles and trajectories. They read draws (chain/draw or sample dims) from posterior, predictions or posterior_predictive. They read the actual values from observed_data.

Recipe What it shows sci.field_map One heatmap panel for each statistic of a gridded output. A slider and a Play button show one frame at a time. sci.vector_field The length of a vector as colours, arrows of the mean vector, and the sd of the length. sci.profile_bands The median and the 50% and 90% bands along along, one curve for each level of by, and the actual values. A slider shows one level with its bands. sci.ensemble Some draws as thin lines, the 90% band of all draws, the median and the actual values.

Statistics of sci.field_map:

  • mean, median: the average value and the middle value of the draws.
  • sd: the uncertainty. A high sd shows where the data do not fix the value.
  • z: the mean divided by the sd. Values far from zero are clear.
  • q05, q95: the limits of the 90% interval.
  • draws: n_draws possible fields from the model.

The grid dims come from the settings. If you do not set them, the recipe uses the grid of the output (OutputDecl.grid). It reads the grid from the grid attribute of the variable or from the model manifest in the bundle. The colormap, log and origin settings also come from the grid when you do not set them. If the output has more dims than the plot uses, use select to pick one level of each, for example select: {species: 0}.

The size of a field plot has limits:

  • All the cells of a plot are in one dataset: x, y and one column for each statistic and frame. The recipe keeps this dataset below the inline Arrow limit (2 MB).
  • If the field has too many cells, the recipe calculates the average of each block of k × k cells. A cell with no value (NaN) stays empty. The caption tells the block size.
  • A field of 189 × 193 cells with six panels and one frame has its full resolution.
  • max_frames sets the maximum number of frames. The slider shows frames at equal intervals.

The plot sandbox shows the Plotly frames, sliders and updatemenus of these plots. In dark mode, it changes the palette colours of the traces to their dark variants, the same as for Vega-Lite.

The convergence diagnostics are rank-normalised split R-hat and bulk/tail ESS (Vehtari et al. 2021). The package calculates them with numpy. Tests make sure that the values agree exactly with ArviZ.

docs.title: Run protocol v0.2
docs.text:
This page tells how a run moves from the API to a sandbox and back. It gives:

  • the state machine of the run
  • the bootstrap object and the environment that an execution gets
  • the event stream that the runner writes
  • the output manifest, the checks on it at finalisation, and the signed bundle manifest
  • the storage layout
  • the ports and the environment variables of a local installation.

Each shape on this page is a Pydantic model or a constant in mapi_spec.run, mapi_spec.storage or mapi_spec.localdev. The API server, the executors, the runner and the tests all import them from these modules.

sequenceDiagram
    participant API
    participant D as Dispatcher
    participant S as Object store
    participant X as Executor
    participant R as Supervisor (runner)
    participant W as Worker (plugin code)
    API->>API: CREATED → QUEUED (static validation, quota)
    D->>D: lease → DISPATCHING, intent row (run, attempt, nonce)
    D->>S: PUT bootstrap/{nonce} (RunSpec: signed URLs, HMAC key)
    D->>X: submit(env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE)
    X->>R: start execution → PROVISIONING
    R->>S: GET + DELETE bootstrap/{nonce}
    R->>W: spawn with scrubbed env (socketpair)
    R-->>API: stdout {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC per line) → RUNNING
    W->>R: progress / results
    R->>S: signed POST/PUT outputs + manifest.json
    R-->>API: "complete" event, exit 0
    API->>S: stat + list (metadata only), server-side copy → bundles
    API->>API: FINALIZING → SUCCEEDED, signed BundleManifest

docs.title: Run states
docs.text:
RunState values are in lower case on the wire. This page writes them in upper case.

State Meaning CREATED The API accepted the run. The static validation and the quota check are not complete yet. REJECTED Terminal. This state is for submissions that the static validation or the quota refuses. The current server does not make such runs. Refer to the note below the transition table. QUEUED The run waits for the dispatcher. DISPATCHING The dispatcher has the lease and wrote the intent row. The call to the executor is in progress. PROVISIONING The executor accepted the execution. No event came yet. RUNNING Minimum one verified event came. STALLED No event came for K × the progress interval. This is a warning, not a failure. The status API of the executor is the source of truth about the execution. FINALIZING The execution is complete. The control plane does a check of the outputs and copies them. SUCCEEDED Terminal. A verified bundle exists. PARTIAL Terminal, but you can resume the run. A verified partial bundle exists. The runner wrote it from checkpoints after a SIGTERM or at the deadline. FAILED Terminal, with one of these failure classes: user, resource_exhausted, infra, integrity, timeout or sandbox CANCELLING The user asked to cancel the run. The run waits for the executor to confirm. CANCELLED Terminal

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
mapi_spec.run.transition(state, trigger, actor=...) is a pure function. It returns the rule that matches, or it raises IllegalTransition. IllegalTransition maps to 409 CONFLICT. Callers save rule.target with a compare-and-set on the old state. If rule.new_attempt is set, callers also increase attempt and make a new nonce. A test compares the table below with the code for all 13 × 19 pairs of state and trigger.

From Trigger To Owner Failure class New attempt CREATED accept QUEUED api CREATED reject REJECTED api QUEUED lease DISPATCHING dispatcher DISPATCHING submitted PROVISIONING dispatcher, reconciler (orphan adoption) DISPATCHING infra_retry QUEUED dispatcher, reconciler yes DISPATCHING fail_infra FAILED dispatcher, reconciler infra PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED event RUNNING events PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED complete FINALIZING reconciler PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED infra_retry QUEUED reconciler yes PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STALLED fail_user / fail_resource_exhausted / fail_infra / fail_timeout / fail_sandbox FAILED reconciler user / resource_exhausted / infra / timeout / sandbox RUNNING silence STALLED reconciler STALLED silence STALLED (no-op) reconciler FINALIZING event FINALIZING (no-op) events FINALIZING verified SUCCEEDED finalizer FINALIZING verified_partial PARTIAL finalizer FINALIZING fail_integrity FAILED finalizer integrity FINALIZING fail_infra FAILED finalizer infra every non-terminal state except CANCELLING cancel CANCELLING api CANCELLING cancel / event CANCELLING (no-op) api / events CANCELLING cancel_confirmed CANCELLED reconciler CANCELLING complete FINALIZING reconciler PARTIAL resume QUEUED api yes

A submission that is not valid makes no run. POST /v1/runs and the model :score action do the static validation before a run row exists. If the validation finds an error, the server refuses the request with a 4xx problem. The code of the problem is the code of the first error. The errors list gives each issue with its JSON pointer. The server keeps nothing, thus there is no REJECTED run and no run history for the request.

CREATED → reject → REJECTED stays in the table for a later server that records refused submissions.

All components obey these rules:

  • Events only move a run to RUNNING. All other transitions during the execution come from the reconciler. The reconciler is level-triggered and reads the status of the executor.
  • complete occurs when the executor reports exit code 0 or 16 and the complete event came. Then the finalizer reads OutputManifest.status and starts verified or verified_partial.
  • infra_retry occurs only after the control plane confirms that the old execution stopped. The cost limits the automatic retries (MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR times the estimate). A count also limits them (MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES). If a run used more than 30 minutes, there is no automatic retry without the consent of the user.
  • Late events. The events service ignores verified events for runs that are already terminal. All terminal states reject event.
  • A cancel of a FINALIZING run has no effect at the API. The table permits the transition, but POST /v1/runs/{id}:cancel returns the run with no change. The execution is already complete. The finalizer can possibly have a version number already. It can also have copied write-once bundle objects.

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
The executor does not send credentials, URLs or keys through argv or the environment. The only values for each execution are MAPI_RUN_ID and MAPI_NONCE.

  1. The dispatcher writes an intent row (run, attempt, nonce). The nonce is 256 random bits, written as 64 lowercase hex characters (new_nonce()).
  2. The dispatcher writes a RunSpec to gs://mapi-{env}-bootstrap/{nonce} (mapi_spec.run.RunSpec, schema runspec.json).
  3. The dispatcher calls Executor.submit(RunSubmit, nonce). For all out-of-process executors, RunSubmit.payload stays empty. The executor sees only the run id, the attempt, the kind, the resource class, the timeout and the labels. All secret values go in the RunSpec.
  4. The supervisor resolves MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL, GETs the object, and deletes it immediately. Then it validates the object as a RunSpec. It starts the worker with worker_environ(), an allow-listed environment that has no MAPI_* variable. If the object is missing or not valid, the supervisor exits with code 2 CONFIG_ERROR.
RunSpec field Meaning schema_version mapi.runspec/v1 run_id, attempt, nonce, kind The identity of the run. Parent kinds (sweep, backtest, sbc, campaign) never execute. tenant_id, project_id Always present (default in M1) spec, spec_hash, catalog_digest The resolved spec JSON (with pinned use: ranges), its canonical hash, and the catalog snapshot that the server used to resolve it inputs name → SignedGet{url, expires_at, generation, size, crc32c, md5_hash?}. The well-known names are dataset and bundle. Each URL is pinned to a generation and supports HTTP Range. The runner does a check of the size and the CRC32C after the download. If they do not agree, it exits with 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR. outputs name → SignedPut \| PostPolicy. manifest is a necessary write-once signed PUT for {prefix}manifest.json. artifacts is a create-only V4 POST policy on the attempt prefix with a content_length_range. It cannot replace an object that exists. Thus it cannot overwrite the manifest or replace an output after the runner wrote it. checkpoints is a POST policy on checkpoint_prefix. It is present only for runs that can write checkpoints. resume The checkpoint objects of the newest earlier attempt that wrote checkpoints, as SignedGets. The server ignores an attempt that stopped before its first checkpoint. checkpoint_prefix {attempt prefix}checkpoints/, or null hmac_key The event HMAC key of the run (new_hmac_key()), in base64. It has a minimum of 32 random bytes. The logs never show it: RunSpec.redacted() removes it and all URLs. limits RunLimits: log_line_bytes (4096), log_total_bytes (20 MiB), max_event_bytes (64 KiB), progress_interval_s (2 s), max_output_bytes and scratch_bytes (from the resource class), max_output_objects (10 000) resource_class, deadline, created_at, labels The class (S/M/L/XL), a hard UTC deadline, and metadata

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Variable Set by Value MAPI_RUN_ID executor, for each execution The run id MAPI_NONCE executor, for each execution 64 hex characters MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL executor, static for each Job or backend A template with exactly one {nonce}. Cloud: gs://mapi-prod-bootstrap/{nonce}. The execution service account reads it. This account can get and delete, but it cannot list. Local: http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}. MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN local executor only The bearer token of the exec principal of the GCS shim. This principal can get and delete in the bootstrap bucket. Never set in the cloud.

RunnerEnv.from_environ() parses these variables and gives the name of each missing variable. RunnerEnv.resolved_bootstrap_url() puts the nonce into the template.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The worker cannot write to the real stdout. It sends reports to the supervisor through a socketpair. The supervisor captures the stdout and the stderr of the worker. It removes ANSI and control sequences. Then it writes one JSON object on each line to its own stdout:

{"mapi_event":{"attempt":1,"hmac":"5f0c…","payload":{"chains":[],"fraction":0.4,"phase":"sample"},"run_id":"run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0","seq":12,"ts":"2026-10-15T09:31:00.123456Z","type":"progress"}}

Cloud Logging keeps each line as the jsonPayload of a log entry. The sink filter is jsonPayload.mapi_event:*. The platform compares the identity of the run with the label of the execution. The local executor reads the same lines from the stdout pipe of the supervisor. encode_event_line() and decode_event_line() implement the wire format:

  • A line that is not JSON, or JSON without mapi_event, is not an event. The platform ignores it.
  • A mapi_event object that is not valid, or a line of more than 64 KiB, raises InvalidEvent. This is a SANDBOX_VIOLATION.

Each event has these fields:

Field Rule run_id, attempt Must agree with the run and its current attempt seq Starts at 0 for each attempt and increases by 1 for each line. The receiver removes duplicates on (run_id, attempt, seq). Gaps are permitted, because the logs can lose entries. ts Has a timezone and is normalised to UTC type state, progress, log, diagnostic, warning, checkpoint, metric, complete or error payload Validated against the payload model for type. Refer to the table below. hmac Lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 with the hmac_key of the run

The data that the HMAC signs:

"mapi.run-event.v1" 0x00 ‖ canonical JSON of the event without "hmac"

Canonical JSON (canonical_bytes()) has these rules:

  • The model is dumped in JSON mode with the defaults.
  • The keys are sorted.
  • There is no whitespace.
  • The text is UTF-8 with no ASCII escapes.
  • Floats with integral values are written as integers.
  • NaN and Infinity are not permitted.

The verification uses a constant-time comparison (verify_event()). If an event fails the verification, the platform ignores it and counts a sandbox violation for that run. Such an event never changes the state of the run. Output manifests use the context tag mapi.output-manifest.v1. Bundle manifests use mapi.bundle-manifest.v1. Thus a signature from one domain is never valid in a different domain.

type Payload model Notes state StatePayload{phase, message?} The runner phases: bootstrap, load_inputs, validate, preprocess, fit, sample, score, evaluate, derive, plots, upload, done progress ProgressPayload{phase, fraction?, message?, eta_seconds?, chains[]} Maximum one in each limits.progress_interval_s. The platform writes it into one run_progress row (upsert). log LogPayload{stream, line, truncated} One line, maximum log_line_bytes. After log_total_bytes, the run fails with SANDBOX_VIOLATION (log flood). diagnostic Diagnostic (mapi_spec) Goes into the scorecard warning WarningPayload{code, message, untrusted_text?} checkpoint CheckpointPayload{name, size, crc32c, segment, draws_done?} name is relative to checkpoint_prefix metric MetricPayload{name, value, step?, labels} complete CompletePayload{status, manifest_name, manifest_crc32c, objects, total_bytes} The last event of a successful attempt (complete) or of an attempt with checkpoints (partial) error ErrorPayload{code, failure_class, message, untrusted_text?} code must be equal to failure_class.error_code

make_event(run_id, attempt, seq, payload, key=...) gets type from the payload model and signs the event.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
The supervisor exits with 0 only after it uploads the manifest and sends the complete event. failure_class_for_exit() gives the failure class of the code. All other non-zero codes are infra, for example 1 from a supervisor that crashed.

Code Name Failure class 0 OK — (success) 2 CONFIG_ERROR infra: the environment is bad, or the bootstrap is missing or not valid 10 USER_ERROR user: plugin code or user code raised an exception, or made output that is not valid 11 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED resource_exhausted: MemoryError, or the run used more than the scratch budget 12 INFRA_ERROR infra: the uploads or downloads of the supervisor failed after retries. (An INFRA_ERROR that the worker reports exits with 10.) 13 INTEGRITY_ERROR integrity: the size or the CRC32C of an input was not correct 14 TIMEOUT timeout: the run got to the deadline with no checkpoint to flush 15 SANDBOX_VIOLATION sandbox: log flood, output caps exceeded, or forged or oversized events 16 PARTIAL — (SIGTERM or deadline. The runner flushed a checkpoint and uploaded a partial manifest.) 137 KILLED resource_exhausted: SIGKILL, usually from the OOM killer. The platform offers "retry at class + 1" to the user. 143 TERMINATED timeout: the runner did not stop in the permitted time after SIGTERM

When the user cancels a run, the run is already in CANCELLING. Thus the exit code does not set the result, with one exception. A fit that writes checkpoints can get the SIGTERM. Then it flushes its last checkpoint, uploads a partial manifest, sends a partial complete event and exits with 16. The reconciler then starts complete from CANCELLING, and the finalizer verifies the partial bundle. Thus the run ends in PARTIAL, and you can resume it. All other exits end in CANCELLED.

docs.title: Outputs and finalisation
docs.text:
The runner uploads all outputs below its attempt prefix t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{attempt}/ in the runs bucket. It uses the artifacts POST policy. It streams each object and calculates CRC32C and MD5 during the stream. Last, it PUTs manifest.json, an OutputManifest that it signs with the HMAC key of the run:

{
  "schema_version": "mapi.output-manifest/v1",
  "tenant_id": "default", "project_id": "default",
  "run_id": "run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0", "attempt": 1, "kind": "fit",
  "status": "complete",
  "prefix": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/",
  "spec_hash": "sha256:…", "catalog_digest": "sha256:…",
  "inputs": {"dataset": {"generation": 3, "size": 1048576, "crc32c": "4waSgw=="}},
  "objects": {
    "bundle.zarr.zip": {"key": "t/default/runs/run_01jaf3q2x8m9v7k5h4g3f2e1d0/a1/bundle.zarr.zip",
                        "size": 2097152, "crc32c": "AAAAAA==", "md5": "1B2M2Y8AsgTpgAmY7PhCfg=="}
  },
  "runner_version": "0.2.0", "created_at": "2026-10-15T10:20:00Z", "hmac": "…"
}

The key of each object must be equal to prefix + name. Names must not have empty, . or .. segments. The manifest must not list itself.

The hashes use the GCS conventions:

  • CRC32C is the base64 encoding of the 4-byte big-endian value (crc32c_to_base64()).
  • MD5 is the base64 encoding of the 16-byte digest.

The manifest is a claim. The control plane verifies it in the FINALIZING state. It does not read the content of the objects:

  1. Metadata only. The control plane lists the attempt prefix and does a stat of the objects. This gives the size, crc32c, md5Hash and generation that the server calculated.

  2. Compare. verify_output_objects(manifest, listing, expected_prefix=…) needs these conditions:

    • Each object in the manifest exists with the same size, CRC32C and MD5.
    • No unexpected object exists below the prefix. manifest.json and checkpoints/… are permitted.

    Each difference is an INTEGRITY_FAILURE issue. The run moves to FAILED(integrity), and the platform raises a security alert. 3. Validate sidecars. The control plane reads the JSON sidecars with size caps and validates them with Pydantic. The sidecars are diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json and coords.json, schema.json and summary.json for ingest, and catalog.json for describe. It also sanitizes the plots. 4. Server-side copy. The control plane copies each verified object into the bundles bucket below t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/. The copy pins source_generation to the verified generation and uses if_generation_match=0. Thus bundle objects are write-once. The execution service account has no access to this bucket. 5. Sign. The platform writes a BundleManifest and signs it. The manifest binds the tenant, the run, the base image, the overlay hash, the spec hash, the data hash, the catalog digest and each destination generation. The signature is: - M1 (local): KMS-EC-P256-SHA256 with a local P-256 key. The server keeps the key below MAPI_DATA_DIR/keys/. This is an emulation of the KMS signer. Thus you can replace it with a real KMS key, and the signed bytes do not change. The server refuses bundles with the HS256 signature when it makes URLs. - v0.3 (M2): a Cloud KMS asymmetric signature on the same bytes.

    The control plane makes URLs to the bundle only after verify_bundle_manifest() is successful.

docs.title: Job payloads and object names
docs.text:
mapi_spec.jobs is the contract between the dispatcher and the runner. The dispatcher writes RunSpec.spec and gives the names of the inputs. The runner reads them and gives the names of the outputs. The two sides import the module. Thus, if you change the name of an input or change a payload, the type checks and the tests fail on the two sides.

Kind RunSpec.spec Inputs Outputs that the control plane reads ingest IngestJob (a mapping or the MFF preset. dataset and source are only for information.) upload data.zarr.zip, schema.json (DataSchema), summary.json (DataSummary), profile.json, preview.json describe DescribeJob (image_digest) none catalog.json (Catalog) validate the resolved ModelSpec dataset, side.<name> validation.json fit the resolved ModelSpec (with pinned use: and dataset references) dataset, side.<name> bundle.zarr.zip, diagnostics.json, metrics.json (MetricsSidecar), plots.json, coords.json (ScoreMetadata.fit_coords), ui/… score the ScoreRequest bundle, bundle.manifest, dataset (the data of the request), scenario, side.<name>, history (v0.4: the fit dataset, for forecasts with future_covariates set to carry_last or seasonal_naive), inline.data / inline.scenario (v0.4: the inline XrJSON of an endpoint call, for use when dataset / scenario is not present) score.zarr.zip, result.json, plots.json, ui/summary.arrow. Also ui/guided/forecast.json or ui/guided/counterfactual.json (v0.4). evaluate / derive / render EvaluateJob / DeriveJob / RenderJob from the params of the run bundle, dataset (default: the fit dataset), side.<name>. plots for render. as the runner reference shows

side_table_input(name) makes side.<name>. SCORE_INPUTS maps the data and scenario fields of a ScoreRequest to their input names. A *.zarr.zip dataset can contain its raw DataSchema as JSON in the root attribute DATASET_SCHEMA_ATTR (mapi_schema). Ingest writes this attribute. If an upload has this attribute, the upload keeps its dim policies, roles and units. The platform does not infer a schema for it.

inline.data and inline.scenario (mapi_spec.endpoints.INPUT_INLINE_DATA and INPUT_INLINE_SCENARIO) contain the XrJsonDataset JSON of an endpoint score call. The API keeps them in the quarantine bucket. The worker decodes them with the caps of the wire format: strict JSON, no NaN or Infinity, and a maximum of 5 MB. The worker gives each dim coordinate the type from the raw schema of the bundle:

  • dates from ISO strings
  • whole numbers for integer and index dims
  • text for categorical dims.

If the worker cannot read a value, the run fails with SCHEMA_INVALID.

docs.title: UI views
docs.text:
Small JSON views for the browser go next to datasets and bundles. The control plane never decodes them. The web app gets them through signed URLs. mapi_spec.views defines them, and each view has a format tag:

Object format Model preview.json mapi.preview/v1 PreviewView: the dim columns, then the variable columns, the first rows, and total_rows profile.json mapi.profile/v1 ProfileView: the statistics for each variable, and a grid of missing values along the time-like dim (maximum 1,000 binned columns) ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 TreeIndexView: the dims, coordinates (with values for small coordinates), variables and scalar attributes of each DataTree node. It has no arrays. ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 PreprocessView: each pipeline step in sequence (id, resolved use, kind, stateful). For each step, it gives the learned JSON (maximum 16 KB, learned_truncated). It also gives the numeric state arrays with their labels, if they have a maximum of two dims and 10,000 cells. omitted gives the names of larger arrays.

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
mapi_spec.storage makes each key on the server from validated ids (check_segment). User input never becomes a path.

Bucket (Buckets(env)) Keys Access mapi-{env}-quarantine t/{tenant}/uploads/{upload_id} Signed PUT from the browser. 7-day lifecycle. mapi-{env}-bootstrap {nonce} The execution identity can get and delete, but it cannot list. 1-day lifecycle. mapi-{env}-runs t/{tenant}/runs/{run}/a{n}/[tasks/{i}/], with checkpoints/ in it Written only through signed URLs mapi-{env}-bundles t/{tenant}/models/{model}/{version}/: bundle.zarr.zip, manifest.json, manifest.sig, diagnostics.json, plots.json, metrics.json, ui/… Control plane only. Write-once. mapi-{env}-data t/{tenant}/datasets/{sha256}/: data.zarr.zip, schema.json, summary.json, profile.json, preview.json Content-addressed

The control plane gets access to storage only through the async ObjectStore protocol:

  • read and write: put, get (with byte ranges and a max_bytes cap), stat (metadata only), list, delete and copy
  • sign: sign_get (pinned to a generation), sign_put (write-once by default) and post_policy.

if_generation_match=0 means "only if the object does not exist yet". Failures raise NotFound, PreconditionFailed or AccessDenied.

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
Component Address Override API (FastAPI) http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_API_URL GCS shim (local Cloud Storage emulator) http://127.0.0.1:4443 MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT Web app (Vite dev server) http://127.0.0.1:5173 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN Plot sandbox http://127.0.0.1:5174 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN Postgres 16 Embedded pgserver, with its data in MAPI_DATA_DIR (default .local/) DATABASE_URL (any postgresql:// URL)

The plot sandbox must have an origin that is different from the web app. The reason is that plots render in a sandbox="allow-scripts" iframe with no same-origin access. LocalDev refuses a configuration that puts the two on the same origin.

Other environment variables and helpers:

  • MAPI_ENV (default local) selects the bucket names, for example mapi-local-runs.
  • LocalDev.from_environ(os.environ) resolves the full configuration.
  • LocalDev.bootstrap_url_template() gives the MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL value for the local executor.

You do not need a Docker daemon. Postgres comes from pgserver, and storage comes from the GCS shim.

docs.title: Runner v0.2
docs.text:
mapi-runner executes one run in a sandbox. It implements the side of the execution in the run protocol. Two processes are part of a run:

  • The supervisor is trusted. It has the HMAC key of the run and the signed URLs. It is the only process that writes to the stdout of the execution.
  • The worker is not trusted. It runs the platform harness (mapi_sdk) together with plugin code. It does not get the key or a URL that can write.
sequenceDiagram
    participant X as Executor
    participant S as Supervisor
    participant G as Object store
    participant W as Worker
    X->>S: start (env: MAPI_RUN_ID, MAPI_NONCE, MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL)
    S->>G: GET bootstrap/{nonce}, then DELETE that generation
    S->>W: spawn (scrubbed env, uid 10001), start message over a socketpair
    W->>G: range-read inputs (signed GET)
    W-->>S: state / progress / diagnostic / metric / checkpoint messages
    W-->>S: stdout + stderr (pipes, captured as log lines)
    S-->>X: stdout: {"mapi_event": …} (HMAC + seq per line)
    S->>G: POST outputs (policy), PUT manifest.json
    S-->>X: "complete" event, exit 0

docs.title: Start a run
docs.text:
MAPI_RUN_ID=run_01… MAPI_NONCE=<64 hex> \
MAPI_BOOTSTRAP_URL='http://127.0.0.1:4443/storage/v1/b/mapi-local-bootstrap/o/{nonce}' \
MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN=<local shim exec token> \
mapi-runner

All the configuration of the run comes from the environment. The command-line options tell only about the image. They never contain secrets:

Option Default Meaning --worker-python PATH this interpreter, or MAPI_WORKER_PYTHON The interpreter of the worker environment (the site-packages of the base image and all overlays) --worker-registry MODULE:CALLABLE entry points The factory of the plugin registry for the worker --scratch-dir DIR $TMPDIR The parent directory of the scratch space of the run --keep-scratch off Keep the scratch directory after the run, for debug --term-grace SECONDS 5 The time that the worker gets to stop after SIGTERM. After this time, the supervisor kills the worker. --deadline-reserve SECONDS 15 The time before the deadline for the checkpoint flush and a partial manifest --base-image NAME MAPI_BASE_IMAGE Recorded in the output manifest

docs.title: What the supervisor guarantees
docs.text:
• The supervisor deletes the bootstrap object before code that is not trusted runs. The supervisor reads the object. Then it deletes exactly the generation that it read. If the delete fails, the run stops with exit code 2.
  • Only signed events go to stdout. The supervisor keeps a private copy of the stdout descriptor for its event writer. It points fd 1 at stderr. All text that the worker prints goes into the line of a log event. This is also true for text that looks like an event. Each line has seq and an HMAC with the key of the run.

  • The worker gets a scrubbed environment. Only WORKER_ENV_ALLOWLIST goes through. Thus no MAPI_* variable gets to the worker. The worker starts with python -I -u in a new session, with TMPDIR set to its scratch directory. If the supervisor runs as root (Cloud Run, docker), these rules also apply:

    • The worker runs as uid/gid 10001 with no supplementary groups.
    • The worker has no_new_privs and no core dumps.
    • The supervisor marks itself non-dumpable.
