docs.title: Quotas and scheduling
docs.text:
See Quotas and cost.

Quotas, rate limits, priority classes and fair-share leasing (plan §8.3, §8.8, §9).

Three levels of :class:QuotaPolicy apply to every request and run, most specific first: token, tenant, global. Each sets optional :class:QuotaLimits (None = unlimited at that level). :func:evaluate_quota is the single pure decision function: the first limit a demand would exceed yields a :class:QuotaDecision with problem code RATE_LIMITED (request rate; retryable) or QUOTA_EXCEEDED (everything else).

Quotas are expressed in vCPU-seconds because abuse risk is compute, not run count. :class:PriorityClass weights drive :func:plan_leases, the dispatcher's weighted fair-share choice of which queued runs to lease next, so one tenant's 237-task SBC cannot starve everyone else's interactive scoring.

evaluate_quota(
    levels: Iterable[tuple[QuotaPolicy, QuotaUsage]],
    demand: QuotaDemand,

Check demand against every level; return the first violation or an allowance.

docs.title: plan_leases
docs.text:
plan_leases(
    candidates: Sequence[LeaseCandidate],
    *,
    capacity: int,
    running_tasks: Mapping[str, int] | None = None,
    concurrency_left: Mapping[str, int | None]
    | None = None,
    tenant_weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    weights: Mapping[
        PriorityClass, float
    ] = PRIORITY_WEIGHTS,
) -> list[LeaseCandidate]

Choose which queued runs to lease now (weighted fair share; pure and deterministic).

Repeatedly picks the candidate with the smallest virtual finish (load[tenant] + tasks) / (tenant_weight × priority_weight), ties broken by queued_at then run_id. load starts at the tenant's running_tasks and grows with every pick. A candidate is skipped when its tasks exceed the remaining global capacity or its tenant has no concurrency_left (runs). Returns the picks in order.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text:
Price tables, cost estimates and the per-run cost ledger (plan §8.2, §13 cost floor, §14 M2).

Money is integer micros of a currency (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros); unit prices are integer nanos per vCPU-second and per GiB-second, so every amount is exact and reproducible from a ledger row (round half to even at the micro). Every amount names the :class:PriceTable version it was priced with; changing prices never rewrites history.

Usage of an attempt is vcpu × billed_seconds × tasks vCPU-seconds and ram_gib × billed_seconds × tasks GiB-seconds, from :data:RESOURCE_CLASSES; billed_seconds is wall time rounded up to the table's billing increment.

:data:DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE mirrors Cloud Run's published list prices (CPU 0.000018 USD per vCPU-second, memory 0.000002 USD per GiB-second); deployments configure their own. An E33 fit on class M for five minutes costs about 0.03 USD.

docs.title: Operator controls
docs.text:
Operator controls: kill switches and executor health (plan §9 denial of wallet, §11 Admin).

:class:KillSwitches is a single platform-wide document. :func:kill_switch_decision is the pure check the API (at submit) and the dispatcher (at lease) both apply: when untrusted_execution_enabled is off, no run of uploaded (tenant) code is accepted or leased; when the global spend in the current window reaches global_spend_cap_micros, no new compute is accepted for anyone except internal tenants. Both denials use the QUOTA_EXCEEDED problem code at the global scope.

docs.title: Executor conformance suite
docs.text:
The executor conformance suite, as data (plan §8.4, §13 "Executor conformance").

An executor (local-process, docker, docker-gvisor, cloudrun-jobs, ...) is enabled only after it passes every applicable case of :data:EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE. Each :class:ConformanceCase names the behaviour, the fault the harness injects, what the backend must support for the case to apply, and the :class:Expectation on the run's observed trajectory. The server's pytest suite parametrizes over this tuple and checks each observation with :func:check_expectation; the admin API reports results as a :class:ConformanceReport.

docs.title: EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE
docs.text:
EXECUTOR_CONFORMANCE: Final[tuple[ConformanceCase, ...]] = (
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.SUBMIT,
        title="Submit runs one execution to success",
        behaviour="A submitted attempt starts with identifiers in the environment only, reports status through the executor API, emits verified events and succeeds.",
        steps=(
            "submit a tiny fit with a fresh nonce",
            "poll status until terminal; collect events",
            "assert argv carries no run id, nonce or credential",
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(
                _S.PROVISIONING,
                _S.RUNNING,
                _S.FINALIZING,
            ),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.1", "§8.3", "§8.4"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.ADOPT_AFTER_DISPATCHER_CRASH,
        title="Orphan adoption after a dispatcher crash",
        behaviour="If the dispatcher dies between the executor accepting an attempt and the handle being stored, the reconciler adopts the execution by nonce instead of starting a second one.",
        steps=(
            "write the intent row, submit, crash before storing the handle",
            "restart the orchestrator; reconciler calls adopt(nonce)",
            "the adopted execution finishes the run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DISPATCHER_CRASH_AFTER_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        title="Duplicate submit is safe",
        behaviour="Submitting the same (run, attempt, nonce) twice never yields two live executions; the second call returns or adopts the first, or its execution is cancelled before it does any work.",
        steps=(
            "submit twice with the same nonce",
            "wait for the run to finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.DUPLICATE_SUBMIT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            max_live_executions=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CANCEL_MID_RUN,
        title="Cancel while running",
        behaviour="A cancel during RUNNING moves the run to CANCELLING; the supervisor gets SIGTERM and flushes; the run is CANCELLED only after the executor confirms the execution is gone.",
        steps=(
            "submit a long fit; wait for RUNNING",
            "cancel; poll executor status",
            "assert CANCELLED is recorded after the executor reports a terminal state",
        ),
        fault=Fault.CANCEL_WHILE_RUNNING,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.CANCELLED,
            must_visit=(_S.RUNNING, _S.CANCELLING),
            must_not_visit=(_S.SUCCEEDED, _S.FAILED),
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.TIMEOUT,
        title="Timeout is enforced and classified",
        behaviour="A run that exceeds its timeout is stopped by the backend (hard task timeout as backstop) and ends FAILED with failure class timeout.",
        steps=(
            "submit a run that sleeps past a short timeout",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EXCEED_TIMEOUT,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.TIMEOUT,
            attempts=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.7"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.STALLED_NOT_LOST,
        title="Event silence raises STALLED, never a false LOST",
        behaviour="When events stop but the executor still reports the execution running, the run becomes STALLED (a warning) and returns to RUNNING when events resume; it is never failed or retried because of silence alone.",
        steps=(
            "submit; drop events beyond K x interval while the execution runs",
            "resume events; let the run finish",
        ),
        fault=Fault.EVENT_SILENCE,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.STALLED,),
            must_not_visit=(_S.FAILED,),
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "Key decisions: liveness"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CONFIRMED_CANCEL_BEFORE_RETRY,
        title="Confirmed cancel before an infrastructure retry",
        behaviour="After an infrastructure failure the reconciler cancels the old execution and waits for a confirmed terminal status before re-queueing attempt + 1, so two attempts never run at once.",
        steps=(
            "submit; report an infra failure while the old execution is alive",
            "observe cancel → confirmed terminal → QUEUED(attempt 2)",
            "attempt 2 succeeds",
        ),
        fault=Fault.INFRA_FAILURE_LIVE_EXECUTION,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.QUEUED,),
            attempts=2,
            max_live_executions=1,
            executions_created=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.CHECKPOINT_RESUME,
        title="Checkpoint, PARTIAL and resume",
        behaviour="A SIGTERM after checkpoints were written yields a PARTIAL bundle; resume starts a new attempt from the checkpoints and completes without redoing them.",
        steps=(
            "submit a segmented fit; wait for the first checkpoint",
            "SIGTERM the execution; expect PARTIAL",
            "resume; expect SUCCEEDED with the earlier segments reused",
        ),
        fault=Fault.SIGTERM_WITH_CHECKPOINTS,
        requires=frozenset(
            {Requirement.CHECKPOINT_STORAGE}
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            must_visit=(_S.PARTIAL,),
            attempts=2,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§5 segmented sampling"),
        budget_seconds=300,
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.OOM_CLASSIFICATION,
        title="Out-of-memory is classified as resource exhaustion",
        behaviour="A worker killed for memory (exit 137) ends FAILED with failure class resource_exhausted and an offer to retry one class up.",
        steps=(
            "submit a memory bomb at class S",
            "wait for the run to end",
        ),
        fault=Fault.MEMORY_BOMB,
        requires=frozenset({Requirement.MEMORY_LIMIT}),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
            attempts=1,
            offers_next_class=True,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.5",),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.FANOUT_TASK_COUNT,
        title="Fan-out with taskCount",
        behaviour="One execution with task_count N runs N tasks, each mapping its task index to a child spec and writing under tasks/{i}/; status aggregates all tasks and a cancel stops all of them.",
        steps=(
            "submit task_count=4",
            "assert 4 distinct task indexes and per-task output prefixes",
            "assert one backend execution",
        ),
        requires=frozenset({Requirement.FANOUT}),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.6"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.GENERATION_VERIFICATION,
        title="Output generations are verified at FINALIZING",
        behaviour="An output overwritten after the runner's manifest (new generation or hash) or an unexpected extra object fails the run with failure class integrity; nothing is copied into the bundles bucket.",
        steps=(
            "submit; after the complete event, overwrite one output object",
            "let the finalizer run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.TAMPER_OUTPUT_GENERATION,
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.FAILED,
            failure_class=FailureClass.INTEGRITY,
            must_visit=(_S.FINALIZING,),
            must_not_visit=(_S.SUCCEEDED,),
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.6", "§9 artifact swap"),
    ),
    ConformanceCase(
        id=_C.RATE_LIMIT_BACKOFF,
        title="429 back-off without duplicates",
        behaviour="When the backend's control API answers 429, the dispatcher backs off (exponential, honouring Retry-After), raises the 429 alarm counter and submits exactly once when the limit clears.",
        steps=(
            "make the control API return 429 to the first 3 submit calls",
            "assert growing delays between calls",
            "assert one execution and a SUCCEEDED run",
        ),
        fault=Fault.BACKEND_429,
        requires=frozenset(
            {Requirement.REMOTE_CONTROL_API}
        ),
        expect=_E(
            final_state=_S.SUCCEEDED,
            attempts=1,
            executions_created=1,
        ),
        plan_refs=("§8.3", "§8.8"),
    ),
)

Every case, in suite order.

docs.title: Guided mode v0.4
docs.text:
See Guided mode.

Guided mode: templates, the question flow, role detection and drafts (plan §11; M3).

Guided mode is organised around tasks. The user picks a :class:GuidedTemplate ("What do you want to learn?"), answers plain-language :class:GuidedQuestion s about their columns ("Which column is revenue?") - pre-filled by :func:suggest_roles from column profiles - and gets a draft: an :class:~mapi_spec.ingest.IngestMapping for the upload plus a ModelSpec document (and its YAML, "View as YAML"), built by :func:build_draft.

Templates are data. Their spec_template is a ModelSpec document with {{placeholder}} strings, filled from answers, template defaults and lookups (:func:render_template); every placeholder is covered by a question, a default, a lookup or a value the builder always provides (:data:BUILDER_VALUES), which a test checks.

Built-in templates (:data:GUIDED_TEMPLATES):

================= ========================== ============================================= id plugin for ================= ========================== ============================================= geo_mmm mmm.bayesian marketing mix by market (what-if, priors; mmm-framework's BayesianMMM) weekly_forecast````ts.hsgp_trend one weekly series, forecast ahead store_demand tabular.regressor demand per store and week (quantiles) customer_choice````choice.multinomial_logitwhich product customers choose on each trip (a conditional logit with household effects, in plugins/tabular) ================= ========================== =============================================

        GEO_MMM,

docs.title: GuidedQuestion
docs.text:
Bases: ResponseModel

One plain-language question. Column questions name what the column becomes:

  • dim: the column labels a dataset dim (dim_spec describes it); the placeholder {{<id>}} is the dataset dim name;
  • role (column): the column is a data variable with that role; the placeholder is the dataset variable name;
  • role + wide_dim (columns): the columns become one variable as_var along wide_dim (one label per column, e.g. spend per channel);
  • role without wide_dim (columns): each column is its own variable.

docs.title: Ingest presets v0.4
docs.text:
Ingest presets and file contracts (plan §3.2, §11 Guided task 2, Q8; M3).

An upload becomes a labelled dataset in a sandboxed ingest run. Besides an explicit column mapping (:class:mapi_spec.api.IngestMapping), M3 adds presets for the formats marketing teams already have:

================= =========================================================================== preset file contract ================= =========================================================================== none the explicit dims/vars/wide column mapping mff the MFF long table (:data:MFF_COLUMNS): one row per period, key columns and variable, the value in VariableValue (:class:MffOptions) meridian Google Meridian's CoordToColumns wide table (:class:MeridianColumns) ================= ===========================================================================

Wide tables (one column per channel) become one variable along a new dim through :class:WideVarMapping - the shape Meridian and most spreadsheets use.

This module only describes files; every byte of an upload is parsed inside the sandbox.

docs.title: MFF_COLUMNS
docs.text:
MFF_COLUMNS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "Period",
    "Geography",
    "Product",
    "Outlet",
    "Campaign",
    "Creative",
    "VariableValue",
    "VariableName",
)

The MFF long-format columns, in the order of the MFF convention (and mmm-framework). Every row holds one value: VariableValue of variable VariableName for one Period and one combination of the key columns.

docs.title: MFF_KEY_COLUMNS
docs.text:
MFF_KEY_COLUMNS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = (
    "Geography",
    "Product",
    "Outlet",
    "Campaign",
    "Creative",
)

The MFF key columns besides Period (each becomes a dim when it has >1 value).

docs.title: IngestMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

How an upload becomes a labelled dataset (Meridian CoordToColumns style).

Tabular formats need a mapping; zarr_zip/netcdf are self-describing and may omit dims/vars. Parsing happens only inside a sandboxed ingest run.

With the mff preset the long table is first pivoted to one column per VariableName (plus Period and the key columns); vars and wide then pick and rename those variables (column = a VariableName value) and dims may refine the dims the preset derives (column = an MFF column). Without vars and wide every variable is kept under its own name.

docs.title: effective_mff
docs.text:
effective_mff: MffOptions | None

The MFF options the ingest run uses (defaults for the mff preset).

docs.title: DimMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

A dim of the dataset, read from one column of a tabular upload.

docs.title: VarMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

A data variable read from one column (dtype is inferred during ingest).

docs.title: WideVarMapping
docs.text:
Bases: RequestModel

One variable read from several columns, one per label of dim (a wide table).

{"dim": "channel", "columns": {"tv": "tv_spend", "search": "search_spend"}} gives a variable along channel (plus the table's other dims) with coords tv and search. Several wide variables may share a dim; their labels must then agree.

Bases: StrictModel

The MFF ("model feature format") long-table preset.

One row per (period, geography, product, campaign, outlet, creative, variable) with the value in value_column. Period becomes the time dim; VariableName values become data variables. The rest follows mmm-framework's MFF semantics (its MFFLoader), so both read a file the same way:

  • Geography and Product become dims when they hold more than one level. A blank label (or National, Total, All) is the coarser level: a variable given only there (national TV) is spread across the levels - equal weights, or the KPI's share of each level (allocation; mmm-framework's defaults: geographies equally, products by sales). A variable may not mix the two levels.
  • Campaign, Outlet and Creative are breakdowns: rows that differ only there are summed, unless the column is listed in split (then it becomes a dim).

combine joins several key columns into one dim ({"geo": ["Geography", "Product"]} gives labels such as US|Watches) - a model with one panel dim can then fit a geography x product panel. A combined dim is created even when it has a single label, so {"geo": ["Geography"]} keeps a national table's geo dim.

docs.title: Business priors and calibration v0.4
docs.text:
Business priors, lift tests and prior translation (plan §11 Guided task 3; M3).

Guided users state beliefs in business units instead of model parameters:

  • :class:BusinessPriors - per channel an ROI range [low, high] or a contribution-share range, each held with a stated credibility (the probability that the truth lies inside the range), plus an optional baseline share;
  • :class:LiftTest - the result of an experiment (geo holdout, conversion lift): extra spend on one channel over a window and the incremental KPI it caused, with a standard error or a confidence interval. Lift tests are calibration data: the model treats each one as an extra observation of the channel's incremental effect.

Both attach to a ModelSpec through its optional calibration block (:class:Calibration). A model plugin uses them only if its manifest declares the matching capability (Capabilities.calibration); otherwise static validation reports CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED.

Turning business priors into model-space priors needs the data (spend and KPI scale) and the model's transforms, so it runs in the sandbox as a translate_priors run (:class:PriorTranslationJob → priors.json = :class:PriorTranslationResult), which also samples the prior predictive and reports it in business units (ROI and share distributions, a KPI fan). :func:apply_prior_translation writes the result into a spec.

Pure Pydantic and stdlib (statistics.NormalDist for quantiles): the control plane and the web app (through OpenAPI) share it.

docs.title: BusinessPriors
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

Beliefs in business units, per channel (keys are channel labels as in the data), and/or about the baseline. At least one belief is stated: a baseline belief alone is fine (channels without a belief keep the model's default priors).

docs.title: ChannelBelief
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

What the user believes about one channel: exactly one of roi or contribution_share, held with credibility.

  • roi: KPI units gained per spend unit over the fit window ([1.5, 4] = "every euro returns between 1.5 and 4 euros of revenue");
  • contribution_share: the channel's share of the KPI over the fit window.

docs.title: ShareBelief
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

A share range (for example of the baseline: KPI that happens without any media).

docs.title: LiftTest
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

One experiment: spend_delta extra spend on channel (optionally in one geo) from start to end (inclusive) caused kpi_delta incremental KPI.

Give the measurement's uncertainty as a standard error se or a confidence interval ci at ci_level. A holdout ("turn the channel off") is a negative spend_delta with (usually) a negative kpi_delta.

docs.title: sigma
docs.text:
sigma: float

The standard error (from ci assuming a symmetric normal interval).

docs.title: implied_roi
docs.text:
implied_roi: float

KPI gained per extra spend unit during the test.

docs.title: PriorTranslationJob
docs.text:
Bases: StrictModel

RunSpec.spec of a translate_priors run.

spec is the resolved ModelSpec document (its data.dataset is the dataset input). The runner fits nothing: it builds the model, maps the beliefs to model-space priors and samples draws prior-predictive draws.

docs.title: PriorTranslationResult
docs.text:
Bases: ResponseModel

priors.json of a translate_priors run.

priors are model-space priors in the plugin's settings.priors form (engine-neutral {distribution, <params>, dims} dicts; per-channel parameters are lists in channels order), to be written at :data:PRIORS_POINTER. coverage is the prior mass inside each stated range (close to the stated credibility when the translation is faithful).

docs.title: PriorPreview
docs.text:
Bases: ResponseModel

The prior predictive in business units: what the model believes before seeing the KPI, so users can check that their beliefs came out as intended.

docs.title: DistributionSummary

A distribution in business units: mean, sd and named quantiles ("0.05" …).

Quantile bands of a series along one dim (a KPI fan): values[i][j] is quantile quantiles[i] at coords[j]. observed (if any) is the data over coords.

docs.title: check_business_priors
docs.text:
check_business_priors(
    priors: BusinessPriors, pointer: str = ""
) -> list[Issue]

Cross-field consistency of business priors (BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID issues).

Shares cannot add up to more than the whole KPI: the lower bounds of every channel's share plus the baseline's must stay at or below 1. Upper bounds summing below 1 with a baseline belief leave KPI unexplained, which is a warning.

(mu, sigma) of the LogNormal whose central credibility interval is [low, high] (the translation of an ROI range). low must be positive.

(mu, sigma) of the logit-normal whose central credibility interval is [low, high] (the translation of a share range). Needs 0 < low < high < 1.

docs.title: Scorecard and promotion gate v0.4
docs.text:
The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate (plan §2 Diagnostic, §11 Guided task 5; M3).

A fitted model version carries a :class:Scorecard: plain-language checks in four categories, each pass, warn or fail:

============== ========================================================================= category checks (:data:SCORECARD_CHECKS) ============== ========================================================================= convergence chains agree (R-hat), enough effective draws, no divergences holdout holdout error (MAPE) and interval coverage on the evaluation split; for choice models, the holdout hit rate against always guessing the most popular product plausibility negative or absurd ROI, a channel taking most of the KPI, the baseline share, parameters the data did not inform (prior-posterior overlap) data missing values, years of history, spend that never varies ============== =========================================================================

:func:evaluate_check turns a metric value into a :class:ScorecardItem with the check's message and suggested action; :func:rollup makes the scorecard (overall is the worst item). Templates pick checks and may tighten thresholds (:class:CheckThresholds).

Promoting a model version to an endpoint passes the promotion gate (:func:promotion_gate): pass → allowed, warn → needs an administrator override with a reason (audited), fail → blocked. :func:authorize_promotion applies an override request to a gate decision.

docs.text:
promotion_gate(
    scorecard: Scorecard | None,
    *,
    fit_mode: str = "evaluate_then_refit",
    allow_train_only: bool = False,
    partial: bool = False,
    schema_breaks: Sequence[str] = (),
    schema_change: Literal[
        "block", "warn", "allow"
    ] = "block",
    required_checks: Sequence[str] = (),
    require_validated: bool = False,
    validation_status: str | None = None,
) -> PromotionGateDecision

Decide whether a model version may be promoted (pure).

M3.5: when a governance policy requires validation (require_validated, see :func:mapi_spec.governance.requires_validation), a version whose validation_status is not validated is blocked (NOT_VALIDATED): no override promotes it.

  • a partial version (interrupted fit) is blocked;
  • a train_only fit is blocked unless the endpoint's policy allows it (Q13: evaluate_then_refit is the default for endpoints, so context and terminal state come from all the data);
  • breaking input-schema changes (schema_breaks) follow schema_change;
  • no scorecard needs an override; a fail scorecard blocks, a warn one needs an override, a pass one is allowed;
  • an evaluate_then_refit version whose scorecard measured no holdout check (no data.split, or no evaluate.metrics) was never evaluated and needs an override (NOT_EVALUATED), as does every check of required_checks (a guided template's scorecard_checks) that the scorecard skipped or lacks.

docs.title: What-if scenarios v0.4
docs.text:
Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ui/explore/mapi.model-explorer. quantised posterior rasters of the outputs fields.jsonfields/v1 that declare a grid (:class:FieldsView) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

What-if scenarios, forecasts and counterfactuals for Guided mode (plan §11 tasks 6-7; M3).

Sliders. A :class:WhatIfScenario scales each channel's spend over the fit window. The browser answers it instantly from the fit's :class:~mapi_spec.views.ResponseGridView with the interpolation contract below; :func:evaluate_scenario is the reference implementation (the web app's TypeScript port is tested against the same golden cases):

  1. a channel without a multiplier keeps 1; multipliers outside the grid ([multipliers[0], multipliers[-1]]) are refused (SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE) - the grid is never extrapolated;
  2. per draw d and channel c, the contribution at multiplier x is the linear interpolation of contribution[d][c] between the two grid points around x; spend is interpolated the same way on spend[c];
  3. per draw, kpi = baseline + sum_c contribution and delta = kpi - kpi(all at 1); summaries (mean and quantiles) are taken over draws after summing, so uncertainty stays joint across channels.

Run exact turns the scenario into a counterfactual :class:~mapi_spec.spec.ScoreRequest (:func:scenario_score_request). Forecasts (:func:forecast_request) and intervention presets ("channel off", "budget x k"; :func:counterfactual_request) build score requests the same way, so the server, the CLI and the docs share one implementation (POST /v1/guided/requests:compile).

docs.title: ResponseGridView
docs.text:
Bases: _View

ui/grids/response_curves.json: per-draw response curves for instant what-if sliders.

For each thinned posterior draw d, channel c and spend multiplier m, contribution[d][c][m] is the channel's total contribution to the KPI over the fit window (periods periods, KPI units) when the channel's spend is scaled by multipliers[m]; spend[c][m] is that spend (spend units). Multiplier 1 is the actual spend (current_spend). baseline[d] is the KPI over the window that no channel explains, so baseline[d] + sum_c contribution[d][c][at 1] is the model's expected KPI. *_by_geo variants add a trailing geo axis (geos order).

Sliders interpolate per draw (see :func:mapi_spec.whatif.evaluate_scenario), so uncertainty bands stay joint across channels; "Run exact" submits a real score run.

docs.title: Endpoints and snippets v0.4
docs.text:
See Integrations.

Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (plan §2, §8.2, §11; Q13; M3).

An endpoint endpoint://<project>/<alias> points at one model version at a time. Integrations (the Python and TypeScript clients, Google Sheets, BI exports) call the alias, so a new model version can be promoted - or rolled back - without touching them.

  • Promotion (PUT /v1/endpoints/{alias}) passes the promotion gate (:func:mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate): the scorecard, the endpoint's :class:EvaluationPolicy (evaluate_then_refit by default, Q13) and the input-schema compatibility with what callers already send (:func:schema_breaks).
  • Every promotion and rollback is an :class:EndpointRevision (the history).
  • Scoring (POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score) takes an :class:EndpointScoreCall: a score request without apiVersion/kind/model, whose data and scenario may be dataset references or small inline XrJSON datasets.
  • GET …/schema describes the input (:class:EndpointSchema, with an example payload), POST …/validate checks a call without running it, GET …/snippets returns code (:mod:mapi_spec.snippets).

XrJSON: small labelled datasets inline in JSON requests (plan §3.2; M3 endpoints).

The shape is xr.Dataset.to_dict()::

{"coords": {"time": {"dims": ["time"], "data": ["2026-11-01", ...]}, ...},
 "data_vars": {"spend": {"dims": ["geo", "channel", "time"], "data": [[[...]]]}},
 "dims": {"time": 8, ...},           # optional
 "attrs": {}}                        # optional

It is for payloads up to :data:MAX_XRJSON_BYTES (one scenario, an endpoint score call), so curl, TypeScript and Apps Script callers need no upload. The control plane checks only the envelope here (names, nesting, sizes, element and string caps, ragged lists) and stores the JSON as a run input; the values are decoded into arrays only inside the runner sandbox (mapi_sdk wire format), which also checks dtypes and the schema.

Code snippets for calling an endpoint (plan §11 Integrations hub; M3).

Pure functions, so the server (GET /v1/endpoints/{alias}/snippets), the CLI and the docs render identical code. Every snippet scores POST /v1/endpoints/{alias}/score with Prefer: wait=60 and an example payload, reading the API token from the environment (MAPI_TOKEN; Apps Script: a script property) - a snippet never contains a secret.

Actuals and future dates. With the endpoint's input table (:attr:SnippetContext.input_table, EndpointSchema.input_table) the Apps Script reads an "Input" sheet in that layout - actual rows with the target filled, rows to forecast with it blank, dates as yyyy-MM-dd - even when the example call sends no data, can create that sheet, and writes the forecast's conditioning note above the tables in "Result". The other snippets add a forecast over the table's rows (:attr:SnippetContext.table_call) to fill with actuals (:mod:mapi_spec.actuals).

Quoting. Values are embedded with each language's own literal syntax, never by string pasting: Python literals via repr, JavaScript/TypeScript via JSON (with U+2028/U+2029 escaped), shell via single quotes (' → '\''), R via escaped single-quoted strings. The base URL, project and alias are validated first (:class:SnippetContext), so even a hostile value cannot break out of its literal; tests parse the generated code back.

docs.title: Webhooks v0.4
docs.text:
Outgoing webhooks: events, envelope, signatures, deliveries and the SSRF policy (plan §8.2 Integrations, §9 "Webhook SSRF"; M3).

Events (:class:WebhookEventType) are delivered as a JSON :class:WebhookEnvelope::

{"id": "evt_…", "type": "run.succeeded", "created": "2026-10-15T09:30:00Z",
 "tenant": "acme", "project": "growth", "api_version": "v1", "data": {...}}

Signatures. Every delivery carries Mapi-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex> where v1 is HMAC-SHA256 under the webhook secret of "<t>.<raw body>". While a secret is being rotated the header carries one v1 per active secret. Receivers verify with :func:verify_signature and refuse timestamps more than :data:SIGNATURE_TOLERANCE_S (300 s) away from their clock, which bounds replays.

SSRF. The server delivers only under :data:SSRF_POLICY: https only, allowed ports, no credentials in URLs, blocked internal host names; it resolves the host itself, refuses if any address is private, loopback, link-local, metadata, CGNAT, ULA, multicast or otherwise non-global (:func:ip_is_blocked, including IPv4 embedded in IPv6), connects to the pinned address it checked (SNI and Host keep the name), follows no redirects, gives up after 5 s and reads at most 256 KiB of the response.

docs.title: Plot sharing v0.4
docs.text:
Saved plots, static rendering and embeds (plan §8.2 Plots, §10.3 items 4-5; M3).

  • Saved plots (POST /v1/plots) keep a plot under a name: either a reference to a plot a model version rendered (a platform recipe or a plugin plot) or a user-authored :class:~mapi_spec.plots.PlotSpec (sanitized on save and on every read).
  • Static rendering (POST /v1/plots:render) turns a plot into PNG, SVG or PDF in the sandbox (vl-convert for Vega-Lite, kaleido for Plotly): a render run.
  • Embeds (POST /v1/plots/{plot_id}/embeds) mint a tokenised, read-only, expiring link for BI tools, Slack and Notion. Plan §10.3 item 4: shared views render platform recipes only - never plugin- or user-authored specs - because a sandboxed iframe can still navigate itself; :func:embeddable decides. The public GET /v1/embeds/{token} returns an :class:EmbedView with every dataset inlined (no URLs).

Embed tokens are mpe_<40 base32 characters> (200 random bits); the server stores only an HMAC (like API tokens) and shows the URL once.

docs.title: Trust lifecycle v0.4
docs.text:
Trust lifecycle: self-service sign-up, verification, tenant deletion and GDPR export (plan §9 "Compute abuse", "Data lifecycle", §14 M3 and cut lines A/B; M3).

  • Sign-up (POST /auth/signup): e-mail, name and accepted terms. The answer is the same whether or not the address is new (no account enumeration). A disposable-e-mail policy hook (:class:DisposableEmailPolicy) refuses throwaway domains.
  • E-mail verification (POST /auth/verify-email) with a single-use token that expires after :data:EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL creates a public-tier tenant with a default project, the signer as tenant admin.
  • Cut line A (M3): public tenants run declarative specs and built-in plugins only - untrusted data, trusted code. Cut line B (M5) opens code upload to public tenants, and only after identity verification (:func:uploaded_code_allowed).
  • Tenant deletion (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/deletion) is scheduled with a grace period (:data:TENANT_DELETION_GRACE, the tenant is suspended and can cancel), then purges every store and reports progress per store (:class:TenantDeletion).
  • GDPR export (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/exports) packages everything the tenant stored into one archive with a short-lived download link (:class:GdprExport).

See About cards and choosing.

Plain-language "About" cards and the "Help me choose" chooser (M3.5).

Every item a user picks from a catalog - models, preprocessing steps and splits, guided templates and specs, workflow templates, workflow node kinds and node implementations, governance checks, datasets - carries an :class:About: what it is in one or two sentences without jargon, when to use it and when not to, the data it needs, what it assumes, what you get out, how hard it is, how long it usually takes, a tiny example and related items. Expert detail (maths, references) lives apart in expert_notes and references.

  • :func:about_issues is the completeness rule the catalog and the contract kit apply (mapi_spec.catalog.catalog_about_issues, mapi_sdk.testing.check_about);
  • :class:DatasetAbout combines a user's description of a dataset with a summary generated from its schema and coordinate summary (:func:describe_dataset, pure);
  • the chooser asks :data:CHOOSER_QUESTIONS and ranks candidates by their :attr:About.fits tags (:func:recommend, pure), behind GET /v1/catalog/chooser and GET /v1/catalog/recommendations.

Pure Pydantic and stdlib (no numpy): the control plane, the web app and the docs share it.

About cards of the built-in catalog (M3.5): steps, splits, models and guided templates.

The text is written for people who do not do statistics for a living: the summary says what the item does for them, the lists say when it fits, what it needs and what comes out, and expert_notes keeps the maths apart. Workflow nodes and governance checks keep their cards next to their registries (:mod:mapi_spec.workflow_nodes, :mod:mapi_spec.governance); :func:builtin_about looks up any of them by id.

Built-in steps and models take their card from here when their class does not set one (mapi_sdk.steps.Step.about, mapi_sdk.models.CustomModel.about). Models that are built in other v0.5 components (mmm-framework and statsmodels) are listed too, so their plugins and the chooser agree on the words: :data:PLANNED_MODEL_IDS.

docs.title: recommend
docs.text:
recommend(
    answers: Sequence[ChooserAnswer],
    candidates: Iterable[
        tuple[AboutKind | str, str, About]
    ],
    *,
    limit: int = 10,
    include_about: bool = False,
    fallback: Iterable[tuple[AboutKind | str, str, About]]
    | None = None,
) -> ChooserResult

Rank candidates ((kind, id, About)) against answers (pure, deterministic).

Each answered question an item declares in :attr:About.fits adds the question's weight when an answer matches (a reason) or subtracts it when none does (a caution); undeclared questions are neutral. experience below the item's difficulty and speed below its typical runtime cost one point per level. Scores are normalised to [0, 1]; ties break by the number of answers an item matches explicitly (an item made for every answer before one that is silent on some), then difficulty, then id.

When goal is answered, an item made for other goals is never recommended (items whose goal does not match are dropped). When no candidate matches the goal, fallback (other kinds: the building blocks behind the starting points) is ranked instead.

docs.title: Workflows v0.5
docs.text:
See Workflows.

Workflows: versioned DAGs of statistical tests, data processing and models (M3.5).

A :class:WorkflowSpec (kind: Workflow, YAML or JSON like every spec document) nests tests, transforms, branches, splits, searches, model fits, evaluations, comparisons, selections, governance checks, reports and sub-workflows into one automated pipeline::

apiVersion: mapi/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata: {name: ts-readiness, project: growth}
params:
  alpha: {type: number, default: 0.05}
inputs:
  data: {type: dataset}
nodes:
  - {id: adf, use: test.adf, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, with: {alpha: {$param: alpha}}}
  - {id: kpss, use: test.kpss, inputs: {data: inputs.data}}
  - id: wanders
    use: branch.if
    with: {condition: "nodes.adf.p_value >= params.alpha or nodes.kpss.reject"}
  - {id: diff, use: transform.difference, inputs: {data: inputs.data}, when: wanders.then}
  - id: order
    use: search.arma_order
    inputs: {data: [diff.data, inputs.data]}     # first available: diff ran, or not
outputs: {order: order.table}

Wiring. An input port binds inputs.<name> or <node>.<port>. For a single-value port a list binds alternatives, the first whose node ran (a node gated by a branch arm that was not taken is skipped, and so are its dependants unless they have an alternative); for a multiple port (PortSpec.multiple) a list binds every source that ran. A node whose required port has no available binding is skipped. when: <branch>.then|else gates a node on a branch. Parameters (with) may be literals, {$param: name} (a workflow parameter) or {$expr: "..."} (a value computed from upstream results with the safe expression language, :mod:mapi_spec.expr).

Static validation (:func:validate_workflow, synchronous, JSON only) reports every problem as an :class:~mapi_spec.errors.Issue with a JSON pointer: unknown node implementations, parameter schema violations and missing parameters, unbound required ports, port-type mismatches, references to unknown nodes, ports or parameters, branch conditions that do not parse or read fields their node does not produce, cycles, nodes that can never run (gated by both arms of one branch) and unused results.

Runs. POST /v1/workflows/{id}/runs starts a workflow run (a parent run). The orchestrator walks the DAG in topological order, evaluates branches itself, sends sandbox nodes to workflow_node runs and child_run nodes to ordinary runs (fits), reuses unchanged results by :func:node_cache_key, retries per node, and records a :class:NodeRun per node and a :class:BranchDecision per branch.

The workflow node catalog: node kinds, typed ports and every node implementation (M3.5).

A workflow node names an implementation by id (use: test.adf). Each :class:NodeImplementation declares its kind, typed input and output ports, a JSON Schema for its parameters (with), the result fields branch conditions may read (nodes.<id>.<field>), where it runs, and an :class:~mapi_spec.about.About.

============= =============================================================================== kind implementations ============= =============================================================================== test test.adf, kpss, pp, zivot_andrews, johansen, engle_granger, ljung_box, jarque_bera, breusch_pagan, white, arch_lm, granger, acf_pacf, seasonal_strength, vif, cusum, chow transform transform.difference, seasonal_difference, log, box_cox, steps (catalog preprocessing steps), select split split.holdout, rolling_origin, expanding_window, blocked_kfold, purged_kfold, geo_holdout, nested (:mod:mapi_spec.splitplan) search search.arma_order, sarima_order, var_lag_order, coint_rank, grid model model.fit (any catalog model id), model.backtest, model.forecast evaluate evaluate.metrics, evaluate.baseline, evaluate.residuals compare compare.models, compare.diebold_mariano select select.best, select.threshold governance governance.policy, governance.check report report.summary, report.evidence_pack branch branch.if (a condition in :mod:mapi_spec.expr) subworkflow subworkflow.run (another saved workflow) ============= ===============================================================================

runs_in says who executes a node: orchestrator nodes (branches, selections) work on JSON results in the control plane with the safe expression language; sandbox nodes run in a workflow_node run; child_run nodes start ordinary runs (fits, governance refits) as children of the workflow run. User data is only ever decoded in the sandbox.

The gallery of workflow templates (M3.5): ready-made workflows users start from.

========================== ================================================================ id what it automates ========================== ================================================================ ts_readiness_arimax unit-root tests (ADF, KPSS, PP, Zivot-Andrews) -> differencing and seasonal differencing chosen by branches -> ACF/PACF and an information-criterion search of AR and MA orders -> an expanding-window backtest with a gap and several horizons -> ARIMAX vs naive benchmarks -> select -> governance -> report var_vecm_cointegration Johansen test -> VECM with the selected rank when the series are tied together, else differences + lag search + VAR -> Granger tests -> report mmm_governed driver collinearity check -> mmm-framework marketing mix model with a holdout -> governance policy -> report + evidence pack forecast_bakeoff one expanding-window backtest for SARIMAX, ETS, Theta and the smooth-trend model against naive benchmarks -> compare -> select the winner -> refit it -> report ========================== ================================================================

Templates are complete :class:~mapi_spec.workflow.WorkflowSpec documents that pass :func:~mapi_spec.workflow.validate_workflow (a test checks it); :func:instantiate_template names a copy for a project.

The safe condition language of workflow branches (M3.5).

Branch nodes decide which way a workflow goes from the results of upstream nodes, e.g. nodes.adf.p_value < params.alpha and not nodes.kpss.reject. Conditions are parsed by a small hand-written tokenizer and recursive-descent parser into an immutable AST and evaluated by walking it over plain JSON data. Nothing is ever passed to eval/exec, no attribute of a Python object is ever read (references index dicts and lists only), and every input is bounded (:data:LIMITS), so a hostile condition can at worst be refused.

Grammar (EBNF; keywords are lowercase, whitespace is insignificant)::

expression  = or ;
or          = and , { "or" , and } ;
and         = not , { "and" , not } ;
not         = "not" , not | comparison ;
comparison  = sum , [ compare_op , sum ] ;        (* no chaining: a < b < c is refused *)
compare_op  = "==" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" | "in" | "not" , "in" ;
sum         = product , { ( "+" | "-" ) , product } ;
product     = unary , { ( "*" | "/" | "%" ) , unary } ;
unary       = "-" , unary | primary ;
primary     = number | string | "true" | "false" | "null" | list | call | reference
            | "(" , expression , ")" ;
list        = "[" , [ expression , { "," , expression } ] , "]" ;
call        = function , "(" , [ expression , { "," , expression } ] , ")" ;
function    = "abs" | "min" | "max" | "len" | "round" | "any" | "all" | "exists"
            | "coalesce" | "if" ;
reference   = root , { "." , name | "[" , ( integer | string ) , "]" } ;
root        = "nodes" | "params" | "inputs" | "run" ;
number      = digit , { digit } , [ "." , digit , { digit } ] , [ exponent ] ;
string      = "'" , { character } , "'" | '"' , { character } , '"' ;

Semantics are strict so conditions mean what they say: and/or/not need booleans (no truthiness), ordering compares numbers with numbers and strings with strings, == compares any JSON values (1 == 1.0; true != 1), in tests list membership or a substring, arithmetic is on numbers only, and a missing reference is an error unless it is wrapped in exists(...) or coalesce(...). and/or short-circuit, and so does if(condition, a, b) (only the chosen value is evaluated), which turns a decision into a value: if(nodes.wanders.value, 1, 0).

Five-field cron expressions for workflow schedules (M3.5; pure stdlib).

minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week with *, numbers, ranges a-b, steps */n and a-b/n, lists a,b,c and the names jan-dec / sun-sat (Sunday is 0 or 7). As in Vixie cron, when both day fields are restricted a day matches if either matches. Macros: @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly.

:func:next_fire computes the next time strictly after a given instant in an IANA time zone (zoneinfo); a local time skipped by a daylight-saving jump does not fire, a repeated one fires once. Schedules may not fire more often than every :data:MIN_INTERVAL_MINUTES minutes (checked by :func:check_cron).

docs.title: Split plans and test results v0.5
docs.text:
Split plans: multi-fold train/test designs for workflows and backtests (M3.5).

A ModelSpec holds one train/holdout :data:~mapi_spec.spec.Split (data.split). A :data:SplitPlan describes many folds - a backtest - and is what workflow split nodes produce (port type split_plan) and model/evaluate nodes consume:

==================== ====================================================================== kind folds ==================== ====================================================================== holdout one fold: an existing Split (time_holdout, as_of, ...) rolling_origin a fixed-length training window that slides forward; test windows of max(horizons) periods after an optional gap expanding_window like rolling origin, but training always starts at the beginning blocked_kfold k contiguous blocks; each is the test once, with gap periods left out of training on both sides purged_kfold blocked k-fold with purge periods before and embargo after each test block dropped from training (overlapping labels) geo_holdout whole groups (geos, stores) held out, optionally only over the last test_last periods; repeated over seeded random draws nested an inner plan run inside every training window of an outer plan (tune on inner folds, score on outer ones) ==================== ======================================================================

Folds are computed from metadata only (:func:plan_folds for ordered plans, from the number of positions along dim; :func:plan_group_folds for group plans, from the levels), so the control plane can show them before anything runs. Positions are 0-based half-open windows [start, stop). expanding_window and rolling_origin match scikit-learn's TimeSeriesSplit (test_size=max(horizons), gap, max_train_size) when step == max(horizons) and anchor="end"; blocked_kfold with gap=0 matches KFold(shuffle=False). An expanding fold is exactly an as_of split (:meth:Fold.as_of_split), so the existing split machinery runs it.

Statistical test results: the test_result payload of workflow test nodes and the rows of the Data Explorer's stationarity table (M3.5).

The runner computes tests with statsmodels/scipy in the sandbox; this module fixes what a result looks like and how a p-value becomes a decision, so the control plane (branch conditions), the web app and the docs agree. Every test states its null hypothesis and both possible verdicts in plain words (:data:TEST_DEFINITIONS); :func:decide applies the significance level, including for tests whose null is the "good" case (KPSS: the series is stationary).

docs.title: Governance v0.5
docs.text:
See Governance.

Model governance: policies, the check catalog, evidence, the validation state machine, approvals and the evidence pack (M3.5).

A :class:GovernancePolicy (tenant- or project-scoped, versioned) lists the checks a model of a family must pass before it is validated, with thresholds and severities, and whether a second person must approve. Checks run as governance workflows in the sandbox (governance.policy nodes); their :class:CheckResult s with :class:EvidenceItem s are stored on a :class:ModelValidation.

Validation status (:func:transition, pure and exhaustive)::

draft             --submit-->           checks_running
checks_running    --checks_passed-->    checks_passed
checks_running    --checks_failed-->    checks_failed
checks_running    --cancel-->           draft
checks_passed     --validate-->         validated          (no approval required)
checks_passed     --request_approval--> awaiting_approval  (approval required)
awaiting_approval --approve-->          validated
awaiting_approval --reject-->           rejected
checks_failed     --resubmit-->         checks_running
checks_failed     --reject-->           rejected
rejected          --resubmit-->         checks_running
validated         --deprecate-->        deprecated

Approvals need a reviewer who is not the submitter (:func:check_approver). When a policy says require_validated_for_promotion, promoting a model version to an endpoint needs status validated (:func:mapi_spec.scorecard.promotion_gate, reason NOT_VALIDATED). Every transition is audited and emitted as a webhook event.

docs.title: Explorers and budget optimisation v0.5
docs.text:
Requests for the Data Explorer and the Model Explorer (M3.5).

POST /v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/versions/{version}/explore (a :class:DataExploreRequest) and POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}/explore (a :class:ModelExploreRequest) start an explore run: the sandbox decodes the data (or the bundle), computes the requested sections and writes the views of :mod:mapi_spec.views under ui/explore/. Results are cached per (target, request hash), so asking again is instant. :class:ExploreJob is the run's RunSpec.spec.

Precomputed UI views: small JSON documents the runner writes next to datasets and bundles and the browser reads through signed URLs (the control plane never decodes them).

Every view carries a format tag so readers can refuse versions they do not understand:

===================== ======================== ========================================== file format content ===================== ======================== ========================================== preview.json mapi.preview/v1 a long-format sample: dim then var columns profile.json mapi.profile/v1 per-variable statistics + missingness grid ui/tree_index.json mapi.tree-index/v1 structure of the bundle DataTree (no arrays) ui/preprocess.json mapi.preprocess/v1 learned preprocessing state per pipeline step ui/grids/mapi.response-grid/v1per-draw response curves for what-if sliders response_curves.json (M3; :class:ResponseGridView) ui/guided/mapi.forecast/v1a forecast score run's KPI: history, then the forecast.json forecast fan after the split (M3) ui/guided/mapi.counterfactual/v1a counterfactual score run's change of the counterfactual.json KPI, in total and per period (M3) ui/explore/mapi.model-explorer. quantised posterior rasters of the outputs fields.jsonfields/v1 that declare a grid (:class:FieldsView) ===================== ======================== ==========================================

Views are produced inside the sandbox from untrusted data: strings are capped and readers must render them as text only.

Budget optimisation: POST /v1/models/{model_id}/versions/{version}:optimize (plan §8.2; M3.5), backed by mmm-framework's planning module in the sandbox.

An :class:OptimizeRequest asks how to split a budget across channels (and optionally geos): a total budget (or a change in percent of current spend, or mode="free" to fund every channel up to break-even), bounds per channel as multiples of current spend or in money, portfolio groups ("digital at least 40%"), the objective (the expected KPI, a cautious percentile such as p10, or the mean of the worst draws cvar5), a horizon and an optional efficient frontier. The optimize run answers with an :class:OptimizeResult: the allocation per channel [and geo] with the expected KPI and its interval, the uplift over the current plan with the chance it is positive, the expected regret of committing to one plan, the marginal return of every channel at the plan, and frontier points. Everything is computed from posterior draws in the sandbox; the control plane validates only the JSON.

Mapping onto mmm-framework (planning.budget.optimize_budget, planning.frontier .budget_frontier, optimize_budget_by_geo): total_budget / budget_change_pct / mode / objective / value_per_kpi map one to one; ChannelBounds.min_multiplier / max_multiplier are its bounds and min_spend / max_spend its abs_bounds; groups its portfolio constraints; max_draws, n_steps and seed its sampling controls.

docs.title: FieldsView
docs.text:
Bases: _Explore

fields: the outputs that declare a grid as interactive rasters (intensity maps, images, space-time densities, vector fields), from the in-sample predictions.

Rasters are quantised to uint16 (:class:FieldRaster); one view holds at most :data:MAX_FIELD_CELLS cells. omitted lists the grid outputs that are not shown (more than :data:MAX_FIELDS, or not in the predictions).

docs.title: FieldEntry
docs.text:
Bases: _View

One output drawn as a 2-D field (see :class:mapi_spec.capabilities.GridDecl).

y_coords/x_coords label the raster rows and columns (for a downsampled raster, the coordinate at the middle of each block). Row 0 is drawn at the top unless origin is lower. facet names the level of each other dim of the output (one entry per level). kind is vector when the output has a component dim.

docs.title: FieldFrame
docs.text:
Bases: _View

One frame of a field (one level of its frame dim, or the only frame): the posterior mean, sd, 5% and 95% quantiles and a few draws, each a :class:FieldRaster. For a vector field the rasters are of the magnitude sqrt(u**2 + v**2) (per draw, then summarised) and arrows holds the mean components.

docs.title: FieldRaster
docs.text:
Bases: _View

One quantised raster: height x width cells, row-major (row 0 first).

data is the base64 of little-endian uint16 codes, two bytes per cell. Code :data:FIELD_NAN (65535) is a missing cell; a code q in 0..FIELD_LEVELS decodes to lo + (hi - lo) * q / FIELD_LEVELS (every code is lo when lo == hi). When the field's encoding is log10 that number is log10 of the value (values <= 0 are missing). lo/hi are None only when every cell is missing. The step between two codes is (hi - lo) / 65534: four to five significant digits.

docs.title: cells
docs.text:
cells() -> int

The number of cells data holds (it must be valid base64 of whole uint16s).

docs.title: FieldArrows
docs.text:
Bases: _View

The mean (x, y) components of a vector field on a coarse grid (one arrow per cell).

x/y are the arrow centres in raster pixel units (column, row; fractional, 0 = the centre of the first pixel). u is the component along increasing column index and v along increasing row index (so with origin="lower" a positive v points up), both [row][col] in the field's units.

POST …:optimize: how should the budget be split?

objective: mean (expected KPI), p<q> (the q-th percentile across posterior draws, a cautious plan) or cvar<a> (mean of the worst a% of draws). mode: fixed spends the budget; free funds each channel to break-even (marginal value = 1 per unit of money, with value_per_kpi converting KPI to money) and makes the total an output. horizon is the number of future periods the plan covers (default: the fit window's length, as the response grid).

docs.title: mapi_steps
docs.text:
This package has the built-in core.* steps. For the settings of each step, read the generated steps catalog.

Built-in preprocessing steps for modeling-api (core.*).

Every step implements the :class:mapi_sdk.steps.Step contract and exports static JSON (settings schema, templated :class:~mapi_spec.effects.SchemaEffect, context need) so the control plane can validate specs without importing this package. Steps are discovered through the mapi.steps entry point (:func:builtin_steps); :func:registry returns a ready :class:~mapi_sdk.registry.Registry, and python -m mapi_steps.catalog prints the catalog JSON.

========== =========================================================================== Reshape resample, count_events, filter_coords, to_long, to_padded, stack, unstack Value fx_convert, mean_scale, max_abs_scale, standardize, log1p, logit, impute, replace_sentinel, clip Feature fourier, trend, calendar, holidays, lag, lag_tensor, one_hot, encode_levels, missing_indicator, formula Precompute adstock, saturation (point models) Split time_holdout, as_of, leave_group_out, last_per_group, mask_block (:mod:mapi_steps.splits; chosen in data.split, applied by the harness) ========== ===========================================================================

docs.title: Splits
docs.text:
The five built-in train/holdout splits (plan §4.1 "Split" group).

Splits are not pipeline steps: a spec chooses one in data.split and the harness applies it at the split stage (:func:mapi_sdk.split.split_dataset), after the stateless prefix. This module gives each split kind a catalog identity (core.<kind>@1.0.0) with its settings schema and plain-language summaries for pickers and docs, plus a direct :meth:SplitStrategy.split for notebooks and tests.

======================== ==================================================================== core.time_holdout hold out the last last periods / a fraction / after a label core.as_of train up to and including as_of; optional gap periods core.leave_group_out hold out whole groups (explicit groups or n random ones) core.last_per_group last last rows of each group with at least min_len rows core.mask_block random blocks over dims covering fraction of the cells ======================== ====================================================================

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Every mapi command with its --help, generated from the installed CLI by scripts/gen_docs_reference.py. The command-line guide shows them in use. Global options (--url, --token, --profile, --json) go before the command: mapi --json runs ls.

Command What it does mapi new Scaffold a ModelSpec YAML from a template (geo-mmm, forecast, tabular, glm). mapi check Statically validate a spec (exit status 1 when it has errors). mapi fit Fit a spec locally (in-process) or on the API (--remote). mapi score Score a fitted bundle locally, or a model version on the API (--remote). mapi catalog Show the catalog of the locally installed plugins (or the API's with --remote). mapi login Sign in to the API (browser OIDC, device code, or an API token). mapi logout Forget the stored sign-in and API token of the profile. mapi whoami Who you are, how you are signed in, and the projects you can use. mapi use Select the project commands act in (sent as X-Mapi-Project), or show it. mapi usage Cost and quota use of the selected project (or --tenant) for a UTC day or month. mapi signup Create a workspace: sends a verification e-mail (valid 24 hours). mapi verify-email Redeem a verification token: creates your workspace and its default project. mapi serve Start the local development stack (API, embedded Postgres, GCS shim). mapi approve Approve (or --reject) a validated model version as a reviewer. mapi optimize Split a marketing budget across channels with a fitted marketing-mix model. mapi choose Help me choose: a few questions about your goal and data, then the best fits. mapi about The About card of anything a user can pick: what it does in plain words, when to use it and when not, what it needs, assumes and gives. mapi runs Inspect and control runs on the API. mapi runs ls List runs, newest first. mapi runs get Show one run (state, failure, cost, problem). mapi runs logs Print captured log lines (untrusted text, control characters stripped). mapi runs watch Follow a run's live events until it ends (--json: one JSON event per line). mapi runs cancel Request cancellation (idempotent). mapi runs retry Start a new run from a failed one (e.g. one resource class up). mapi datasets Datasets on the API. mapi datasets ls List datasets. mapi datasets upload Upload a file as a new dataset version (signed PUT + sandboxed ingest run). mapi plugin Plugin authoring: scaffold and test model plugins. mapi plugin init Scaffold a plugin package (model, entry point and contract-kit tests). mapi plugin test Run the plugin's tests (contract kit) with this interpreter; extra args go to pytest. mapi spec Spec document tools. mapi spec upgrade Upgrade a document through the registered converters (N-1 → N). mapi config Client configuration (~/.config/mapi/config.toml). mapi config show Resolved settings and where each came from (secrets are never shown). mapi config path Print the config file location. mapi config set Set a key of the profile (--profile, MAPI_PROFILE, else the default profile). mapi config unset Remove a key from the profile (token too: prefer mapi logout). mapi tokens API tokens of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation). mapi tokens ls List tokens (yours, or everyone's with --all). mapi tokens get Show one token (never its secret). mapi tokens create Mint a token in the selected project. Its secret is shown once. mapi tokens revoke Revoke a token: programs using it stop working at once. mapi admin Platform operator commands: tenants, quotas, kill switches, executors, audit. mapi admin audit The platform audit log, newest first (times in UTC). mapi admin tenants All tenants (create, change tier/status/residency). mapi admin tenants ls List all tenants. mapi admin tenants get Show one tenant. mapi admin tenants create Create a tenant. mapi admin tenants update Change a tenant's name, trust tier, status or data residency. mapi admin quotas Quota policies per token, tenant or the platform. mapi admin quotas ls List quota policies. mapi admin quotas set Create or REPLACE the policy of (scope, subject): limits left out are removed. mapi admin quotas rm Remove a policy (the tier default applies again). mapi admin kill-switches Platform-wide emergency controls (audited). mapi admin kill-switches get Show the kill switches. mapi admin kill-switches set Flip kill switches (confirmation shows the change; the server audits it). mapi admin executors Executor health, capacity and conformance. mapi admin executors ls Executor health, load and conformance. mapi admin executors get One executor. mapi admin executors disable Disable an executor: no new run is placed on it (incident containment). mapi admin executors enable Enable an executor again. mapi endpoints Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (promote, score, snippets). mapi endpoints ls List the project's endpoints. mapi endpoints get Show an endpoint, the version it serves and its promotion gate. mapi endpoints history Promotions and rollbacks, newest first. mapi endpoints promote Point an alias at a model version, through the scorecard promotion gate. mapi endpoints rollback Point the alias back at an earlier revision's version. mapi endpoints schema What to send: the input schema frozen at promotion and an example payload. mapi endpoints score Score the endpoint's current version and wait for the result. mapi endpoints forecast Forecast with your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (no refit). mapi endpoints snippets Ready-to-run code that scores the endpoint (reads the token from MAPI_TOKEN). mapi webhooks Webhooks of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation). mapi webhooks ls List webhooks (never their secrets). mapi webhooks get Show one webhook (never its secret). mapi webhooks create Add a webhook. Its signing secret is printed once. mapi webhooks update Change a webhook: switch it back on after it was paused or disabled automatically, or change its events, URL or description. The secret is unchanged. mapi webhooks rotate New signing secret (printed once); the current one keeps signing for 24 hours. mapi webhooks deliveries The delivery log, newest first. mapi webhooks replay Send a delivery's event again (a new delivery). mapi webhooks rm Delete a webhook and its delivery log. mapi plots Render plots to files and share them as embed links. mapi plots render Render one plot to a PNG, SVG or PDF file. mapi plots embed Create a read-only embed link for a saved plot. Its URL is printed once. mapi plots embeds List a saved plot's embed links (redacted). mapi plots revoke Revoke an embed link: dashboards showing it stop at once. mapi guided Guided mode: templates, column detection and drafts (stores nothing). mapi guided templates List the guided templates, or one template's questions. mapi guided detect Suggest which column answers each question of a template. mapi guided draft Answers -> the ingest mapping and the ModelSpec YAML (nothing is stored). mapi priors Business priors: translate beliefs into model priors. mapi priors preview Translate beliefs into priors in the sandbox and preview them. mapi tenant Your workspace (tenant): verification status, GDPR export and deletion. mapi tenant status Verification (e-mail, identity, code upload) and any deletion of the tenant. mapi tenant export GDPR export: everything the tenant stored, as one zip archive. mapi tenant delete Schedule deletion of the whole tenant (cancellable during the grace period). mapi workflows Workflows: validate, save, run and watch DAGs of tests, transforms and models. mapi workflows validate Check a workflow file on the server (nothing is saved): unknown nodes, parameters, ports, conditions and cycles, each with a JSON pointer. mapi workflows apply Create the workflow named in the file, or save the file as its next revision (an unchanged file adds nothing). mapi workflows create Create a workflow from a file or a gallery template (revision 1). mapi workflows ls List the project's workflows. mapi workflows get Show a workflow (and with --yaml its document at the latest or a given revision). mapi workflows revisions Revisions, newest first, and whether each can run. mapi workflows archive Archive a workflow (it can no longer run) or bring it back with --undo. mapi workflows rm Delete a workflow with its runs, schedules and triggers. mapi workflows templates The gallery of ready-made workflows, each in plain words. mapi workflows template One template's About card and its nodes. mapi workflows init Write a gallery template as a YAML file to edit, validate and apply. mapi workflows run Start a run (inputs are pinned to exact versions when it starts). mapi workflows watch Follow a run live: every node's status, branch decisions, then the summary (--json: one JSON event per line). mapi workflows status A run's status, nodes, decisions and outputs. mapi workflows runs Runs of a workflow, newest first. mapi workflows nodes The nodes of a run with what each found. mapi workflows node One node in full: resolved parameters, result, outputs and child runs. mapi workflows output Download a node output's file (a derived dataset, a fitted bundle), verified. mapi workflows cancel Cancel a run and its running children. mapi workflows nodes-catalog The node implementations a workflow can use, in plain words. mapi workflows schedules Cron schedules of a workflow. mapi workflows schedules ls A workflow's schedules. mapi workflows schedules add Run the workflow on a schedule (at most every 15 minutes). mapi workflows schedules pause Pause a schedule. mapi workflows schedules resume Resume a paused schedule. mapi workflows schedules rm Delete a schedule. mapi workflows triggers Run a workflow when a dataset gets a new version. mapi workflows triggers ls A workflow's dataset triggers. mapi workflows triggers add Run the workflow whenever the dataset gets a new version. mapi workflows triggers rm Delete a trigger. mapi governance Governance: the check catalog and the policies models must pass. mapi governance checks The checks a policy can require, in plain words. mapi governance policies Project and tenant-wide governance policies. mapi governance policies ls Policies in force in the project (tenant-wide first), or a tenant's. mapi governance policies get A policy's latest version with every check and threshold. mapi governance policies create Add a policy from a file (name, applies_to, checks, require_approval, ...). mapi governance policies update Save the file as the policy's next version. mapi governance policies retire Retire a policy (its versions stay for audit). mapi governance policies versions Every version of a project policy, newest first. mapi validate Validate a model version against the governance policies (or a workflow file). mapi validate model Run the governance checks on a model version and show every result. mapi validate workflow Check a workflow file on the server (same as mapi workflows validate). mapi validations Validations: the review queue, evidence, resubmission, deprecation, evidence packs. mapi validations ls Validations of the project, most recently changed first. mapi validations get A validation: status, every result, approvals and history. mapi validations evidence Every check result with its evidence (numbers, tables). mapi validations cancel Stop running checks (back to draft). mapi validations resubmit Run the checks again after a failure or a rejection. mapi validations deprecate Retire a validated model version (audited with the reason). mapi validations pack Export the evidence pack for an auditor (self-contained HTML, or JSON). mapi explore Explore a dataset or a model (sections computed in the sandbox), compare models. mapi explore dataset Explore a dataset version: profile, distributions, time plots, missingness, outliers, correlations, cross-correlation with the KPI, ACF/PACF, stationarity, STL, VIF, group comparisons and data-quality warnings. mapi explore model Explore a model version: parameters, diagnostics, fit vs actual, residual tests, decomposition, response curves, IRF/FEVD, forecasts, backtests and comparisons. mapi explore compare Compare model versions on their shared holdout: metrics, ranking and pairwise Diebold-Mariano tests (is the difference more than luck?). mapi explore get An exploration's sections (and with --out its views).

docs.title: mapi
docs.text:
Usage: mapi [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  The modeling-api command line.

  Local commands (new, check, fit, score, catalog, plugin, spec) need no server. Remote commands
  (runs, datasets, tokens, usage, admin, endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors, tenant,
  signup, workflows, governance, validate, validations, approve, explore, optimize, choose,
  about, --remote) use the API from --url, MAPI_URL or a profile in ~/.config/mapi/config.toml,
  signed in with `mapi login` (or --token / MAPI_TOKEN), in the project chosen with `mapi use`
  (or --project / MAPI_PROJECT). --json prints machine-readable output on stdout.

Options:
  --url <str>           API base URL (default: MAPI_URL, profile, local)
  --token <str>         Bearer token (default: MAPI_TOKEN, profile)
  --profile <str>       Config profile (default: MAPI_PROFILE)
  --project <str>       <tenant>/<project> to act in (default: MAPI_PROJECT, mapi use)
  --json                Machine-readable JSON on stdout
  --version             Show the version
  --install-completion  Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion     Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the
                        installation.
  -h, --help            Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  new           Scaffold a ModelSpec YAML from a template (geo-mmm, forecast, tabular, glm).
  check         Statically validate a spec (exit status 1 when it has errors).
  fit           Fit a spec locally (in-process) or on the API (--remote).
  score         Score a fitted bundle locally, or a model version on the API (--remote).
  catalog       Show the catalog of the locally installed plugins (or the API's with...
  login         Sign in to the API (browser OIDC, device code, or an API token).
  logout        Forget the stored sign-in and API token of the profile.
  whoami        Who you are, how you are signed in, and the projects you can use.
  use           Select the project commands act in (sent as X-Mapi-Project), or show it.
  usage         Cost and quota use of the selected project (or --tenant) for a UTC day or...
  signup        Create a workspace: sends a verification e-mail (valid 24 hours).
  verify-email  Redeem a verification token: creates your workspace and its default project.
  serve         Start the local development stack (API, embedded Postgres, GCS shim).
  approve       Approve (or --reject) a validated model version as a reviewer.
  optimize      Split a marketing budget across channels with a fitted marketing-mix model.
  choose        Help me choose: a few questions about your goal and data, then the best fits.
  about         The About card of anything a user can pick: what it does in plain words,...
  runs          Inspect and control runs on the API.
  datasets      Datasets on the API.
  plugin        Plugin authoring: scaffold and test model plugins.
  spec          Spec document tools.
  config        Client configuration (~/.config/mapi/config.toml).
  tokens        API tokens of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation).
  admin         Platform operator commands: tenants, quotas, kill switches, executors, audit.
  endpoints     Endpoints: stable aliases for promoted model versions (promote, score,...
  webhooks      Webhooks of the selected project (secrets are shown once, at creation).
  plots         Render plots to files and share them as embed links.
  guided        Guided mode: templates, column detection and drafts (stores nothing).
  priors        Business priors: translate beliefs into model priors.
  tenant        Your workspace (tenant): verification status, GDPR export and deletion.
  workflows     Workflows: validate, save, run and watch DAGs of tests, transforms and models.
  governance    Governance: the check catalog and the policies models must pass.
  validate      Validate a model version against the governance policies (or a workflow file).
  validations   Validations: the review queue, evidence, resubmission, deprecation,...
  explore       Explore a dataset or a model (sections computed in the sandbox), compare...
