docs.title: mapi endpoints forecast
docs.text:
Usage: mapi endpoints forecast [OPTIONS] {alias} [table]

  Forecast with your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (no refit).

  The table has the columns of `mapi endpoints schema ALIAS` (Input table): the time column, the
  target and any drivers. Rows with the target filled are actuals: the model updates its state
  with them using its fitted parameters and forecasts from the last one. Rows after them with
  the target empty are forecast; without such rows, --periods (default 8) are appended. The
  answer says what the forecast was conditioned on.

Arguments:
  alias  Endpoint alias  [required]
  table  CSV (header row) or JSON rows in the endpoint's input layout: actuals with the target
         filled, dates to forecast with it empty ('-' = stdin)

Options:
  --actuals <path>           Rows with the target filled (CSV/JSON)
  --future <str>             A date to forecast (repeatable), or a CSV/JSON file of future rows
                             with their driver values
  --periods <int range>      Periods to append after the last actual  [x>=1]
  --future-covariates <str>  Empty future drivers: carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero or supplied
                             [default: carry_last]
  --wait <int range>         Prefer: wait=N  [default: 60; 0<=x<=60]
  --timeout <float>          Give up after N seconds
  --dry-run                  Print the call body (JSON) and send nothing
  -h, --help                 Show this message and exit.

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text: Every error is a MapiError with one of these stable codes. Over HTTP it becomes an RFC 7807 problem document (application/problem+json) whose type ends in the code. Anything your data or a plugin said is returned separately, as untrusted_text.

docs.title: Spec and static validation
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable SCHEMA_INVALID 422 The document does not match its schema – SPEC_PARSE_ERROR 400 The document could not be parsed – PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE 413 The document exceeds a size limit – UNSUPPORTED_API_VERSION 422 Unsupported apiVersion – REF_UNRESOLVED 422 A reference could not be resolved – SETTINGS_INVALID 422 Settings do not match their schema – BINDING_INVALID 422 The data binding is invalid – SPLIT_INVALID 422 The train/holdout split is invalid – LEAKAGE_RISK 422 A stateful step runs before the split – DIM_POLICY_LOOSENED 422 A dim policy can only become stricter – SCHEMA_DYNAMIC 422 Schema needs a dry-run to resolve – SIDE_TABLE_COVERAGE 422 A side table is not available – PLOT_UNSAFE 422 The plot spec violates the plot safety policy – GUIDED_ANSWERS_INVALID 422 The guided answers do not fit the template – BUSINESS_PRIORS_INVALID 422 The business priors are inconsistent – IMPORT_UNSUPPORTED 422 The imported model uses an unsupported feature – ABOUT_INCOMPLETE 422 A catalog item has no complete About card – WORKFLOW_INVALID 422 The workflow is not valid – EXPRESSION_INVALID 422 A branch condition is not a valid expression – NODE_UNKNOWN 422 A workflow node names an unknown implementation – SCHEDULE_INVALID 422 The schedule or trigger is not valid – POLICY_INVALID 422 The governance policy is not valid – EXPLORE_INVALID 422 The explorer request is not valid –

docs.title: Score-time coordinate checks (CoordPlan)
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable UNSEEN_LEVELS 422 Unseen levels on a dim that forbids them – COORD_NOT_ALLOWED 422 Coordinates not allowed by dim policy – HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT 409 Horizon exceeds the fitted range – MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE 422 A future covariate is missing – NON_CONTIGUOUS_EXTENSION 422 Extension is not contiguous – CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED 422 The model lacks this capability – RECURSIVE_UNSUPPORTED 422 Recursive forecasting unsupported – ACTUALS_INVALID 422 The supplied actuals cannot be used for this forecast –

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 Score mode not supported – CALIBRATION_UNSUPPORTED 422 The model cannot use this calibration data – SCENARIO_OUT_OF_RANGE 422 The scenario is outside the precomputed grid – OPTIMIZE_INFEASIBLE 422 The budget constraints cannot all be met – ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED 422 The model cannot update its forecast with supplied actuals –

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text: Code HTTP Meaning Retryable QUOTA_EXCEEDED 429 Quota exceeded – RATE_LIMITED 429 Too many requests yes

docs.title: API

docs.title: Governance checks
docs.text:
Every check a governance policy can require, generated from mapi_spec.governance.GOVERNANCE_CHECKS (the catalog behind GET /v1/catalog/governance-checks, mapi governance checks and the web app's Check catalog). Each entry starts with its plain-language About card. Can you trust this model? explains the null tests in plain words and in statistics.

A policy may set a check's severity (blocking, warning, info), its own warn and fail limits (never looser than the order below allows) and its parameters. A check whose requirement does not hold for a model is reported as skipped with the reason; one that cannot be computed is error, which fails a blocking check.

Check Title Measures Default limits Needs baseline.beats_naive Better than simple benchmarks relative_skill pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0, fail below holdout, time_series convergence The fit is complete and stable r_hat_max pass at ≤ 1.01, warn up to 1.05, fail above – data.quality The data is good enough data_issue_count pass at ≤ 0, warn up to 2, fail above – holdout.accuracy Accurate on test data holdout_error pass at ≤ 0.15, warn up to 0.3, fail above holdout null.noise_regressors No effect from false drivers noise_effect_share pass at ≤ 0.02, warn up to 0.05, fail above – null.permutation_target Better than shuffled data permutation_p_value pass at ≤ 0.05, warn up to 0.1, fail above holdout null.placebo_time_shift No effect after a time shift placebo_effect_ratio pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above time_series plausibility.signs Effects have the correct direction wrong_sign_share pass at ≤ 0.1, warn up to 0.25, fail above – recovery.simulated Finds known values recovery_coverage pass within 0.1 of 0.9, warn within 0.25, fail further away – residuals.whiteness No pattern in the errors ljung_box_p_value pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0.01, fail below residuals, time_series sensitivity.prior The results come from the data prior_sensitivity pass at ≤ 0.2, warn up to 0.5, fail above bayesian stability.rolling_params Estimates are stable over time param_variation pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above time_series

docs.title: baseline.beats_naive - Better than simple benchmarks
docs.text:
Compares the error of the model on the test periods with very simple forecasts, for example 'same as last week' or 'same as last year'. The model must be better.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each forecast model.

Avoid it when: Models that do not forecast over time.

It needs: The test periods of the model and the history before them.

It assumes: The check scores the benchmarks on the same periods.

You get: The skill against the best benchmark (1 - model error / benchmark error).

Example: The error of the model is 30% lower than 'same as last year': skill 0.30, pass.

Related: evaluate.baseline, holdout.accuracy.

Expert detail

Relative skill 1 - L(model)/min_b L(b) on the holdout or backtest folds; MASE-style scaling by the in-sample seasonal-naive error is reported as well. References: Hyndman & Koehler (2006), Another look at measures of forecast accuracy.

Category baseline Metric relative_skill Default limits pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0, fail below Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again); the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description methods list of naive or seasonal_naive or mean or drift ["naive", "seasonal_naive"] metric string mae

docs.title: convergence - The fit is complete and stable
docs.text:
Makes sure that the fit procedure found a stable answer. If you fit the model again, you get the same result.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Every model.

Avoid it when: Models that you fit outside the platform, without diagnostics.

It needs: The diagnostics of the fit.

It assumes: The fit recorded its diagnostics.

You get: R-hat, effective draws and divergences (Bayesian) or the optimiser status.

Example: All chains agree (R-hat 1.003): pass.

Related: recovery.simulated.

Expert detail

Bayesian: max split R-hat (rank-normalised), with ESS and divergences as evidence; frequentist: optimiser convergence flag (value 1.0 when converged, inf otherwise).

Category convergence Metric r_hat_max Default limits pass at ≤ 1.01, warn up to 1.05, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

docs.title: data.quality - The data is good enough
docs.text:
Makes sure that the data is good before you trust the model. The data must have few gaps, enough history, no constant columns and no impossible values.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Every model.

Avoid it when: Synthetic data that you made yourself.

It needs: The dataset that the model fit used.

It assumes: The limits are correct for your data.

You get: The data problems that the check found, each in plain words.

Example: No gaps, 3 years of history, each driver changes: pass.

Related: convergence.

Category data Metric data_issue_count Default limits pass at ≤ 0, warn up to 2, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description max_missing number 0.05 ≥ 0, ≤ 1 min_history_periods integer 52 ≥ 1

docs.title: holdout.accuracy - Accurate on test data
docs.text:
Makes sure that the error of the model on periods that the fit did not use stays below the limit of your organisation.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each model that you use for forecasts or what-ifs.

Avoid it when: Models without a test period.

It needs: A test period or a backtest.

It assumes: The test periods are similar to future use.

You get: The selected error metric on the test data.

Example: MAPE 9% against a limit of 15%: pass.

Related: baseline.beats_naive, evaluate.metrics.

Category holdout Metric holdout_error Default limits pass at ≤ 0.15, warn up to 0.3, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again) Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description metric mape or smape or mase or rmse or mae mape

docs.title: null.noise_regressors - No effect from false drivers
docs.text:
Adds some false drivers that are only noise and fits the model again. A model that you can trust gives them almost no effect.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Marketing mix models and other models that divide a result between drivers.

Avoid it when: Forecast models that have no drivers.

It needs: The data and the settings of the model.

It assumes: The false drivers look like real drivers, but they have no signal.

You get: The largest share of the effect of the real drivers that goes to a false driver; If a false driver is clearly above the limit.

Example: Three false channels get 0.4%, 0.1% and 0.9% of the media effect: pass.

Related: null.permutation_target, plausibility.signs.

Expert detail

Placebo regressors drawn as Gaussian noise or as a driver shuffled in blocks, with the model's default prior (never a real channel's prior or calibration); the statistic is the largest placebo share of the real drivers' total effect (by ablation through the score path). Bayesian: flagged when P(share > warn limit) >= 0.9 over the posterior (practical equivalence, valid for sign-constrained effects); frequentist: placebo p-values with Holm's correction.

Category null_test Metric noise_effect_share Default limits pass at ≤ 0.02, warn up to 0.05, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_noise integer 3 ≥ 1, ≤ 10 kind gaussian or shuffled_driver shuffled_driver seed integer 0 ≥ 0

docs.title: null.permutation_target - Better than shuffled data
docs.text:
Fits the model again on copies of the data where the drivers have a random time order. A real model must be clearly better on the true data than on the shuffled copies.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Each model whose accuracy you use to make decisions.

Avoid it when: Models without a test period (there is nothing to compare).

It needs: The data and the settings of the model, and a test period.

It assumes: A random order of the drivers removes each real link between the drivers and the result; The trend, the season and the result stay as they are; For a model without drivers, the check shuffles the ups and downs of the result.

You get: The fraction of shuffled fits that were as good as the real fit (a p-value); The distribution of the shuffled scores.

Example: The real model forecasts better than all 19 shuffled fits: p = 0.05, pass.

Related: null.noise_regressors, baseline.beats_naive.

Expert detail

Permutation (randomisation) test on a scale-free statistic: holdout skill 1 - L(model) / L(null forecast) on each dataset (the null forecast is the last training value of an integrated series, else its mean). Null: models with drivers keep the result and get their drivers block-permuted jointly (so trend, season and controls cannot pass on their own; a model that ignores its drivers is tested as one without); models without drivers get the d-th differences of the result permuted i.i.d. and re-integrated from the original start (d from the ARIMA order or ADF/KPSS), which keeps the integration order and the increments' distribution but destroys predictable dynamics. Without a time order the result is permuted across rows and the statistic is the holdout error. p = (1 + #{perm >= real}) / (K + 1). References: Ojala & Garriga (2010), Permutation tests for studying classifier performance.

Category null_test Metric permutation_p_value Default limits pass at ≤ 0.05, warn up to 0.1, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no test period (add a data split and fit the model again) Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_permutations integer 20 ≥ 5, ≤ 200 metric rmse or mae or mape or smape or crps rmse block integer – Periods of the drivers shuffled together (default: a twentieth of the series) (≥ 1, ≤ 520)

docs.title: null.placebo_time_shift - No effect after a time shift
docs.text:
Moves the drivers some months away from their real dates and fits the model again. The effects must become much smaller, or else the model finds time patterns, not real effects.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Models that divide results between drivers over time (marketing mix, regressions).

Avoid it when: Very short series (after the shift, the overlap is too small).

It needs: The data and the settings of the model over time.

It assumes: A real effect has a connection to the date of the driver.

You get: The placebo effect as a share of the real effect, for each shift.

Example: A shift of the spend by half a year keeps only 8% of the effect: pass.

Related: null.noise_regressors.

Expert detail

Time-shift placebo (leads/lags beyond any plausible carry-over); ratio of the placebo total effect to the real one, maximised over shifts.

Category null_test Metric placebo_effect_ratio Default limits pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description shifts list of integer [-26, 26] min items 1, max items 6

docs.title: plausibility.signs - Effects have the correct direction
docs.text:
Makes sure that each effect has the direction that business sense expects. For example, advertising must not decrease sales, and higher prices must not increase demand.

Difficulty: beginner. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Each model with effects that you can explain.

Avoid it when: Models that only forecast.

It needs: The estimates of the model and the expected directions.

It assumes: The expected directions are correct.

You get: The share of the estimate (or of the uncertainty) on the wrong side, for each effect.

Example: The effect of radio is negative with a probability of 40%: fail.

Related: null.noise_regressors, test.vif.

Category plausibility Metric wrong_sign_share Default limits pass at ≤ 0.1, warn up to 0.25, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description expected map of positive or negative – Parameter -> expected sign (default: media positive)

docs.title: recovery.simulated - Finds known values
docs.text:
Simulates data from the model with known true values and fits the model again. Then it makes sure that the 90% ranges of the model contain the true values about 90% of the time.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: New models, or models with many changes; Before you trust a complex Bayesian model.

Avoid it when: Models that cannot simulate data.

It needs: The settings of the model and the shape of the data.

It assumes: The simulated data is similar to the real data.

You get: How often the 90% ranges contained the true values.

Example: The true values were in the 90% ranges 88% of the time: pass.

Related: sensitivity.prior, convergence.

Expert detail

Simulation-based calibration lite: N simulate-fit cycles; coverage of central 90% intervals and rank uniformity per parameter. References: Talts et al. (2018), Validating Bayesian inference algorithms with simulation-based calibration.

Category recovery Metric recovery_coverage Default limits pass within 0.1 of 0.9, warn within 0.25, fail further away Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when never Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description n_sims integer 20 ≥ 5, ≤ 100 params list of string –

docs.title: residuals.whiteness - No pattern in the errors
docs.text:
Makes sure that the errors of the model look like random noise over time. If a pattern stays in the errors, the model does not use all of the information in the data.

Difficulty: intermediate. Typical runtime: seconds.

Use it when: Time-series and regression models.

Avoid it when: Models without residuals.

It needs: The in-sample errors of the model.

It assumes: The time steps are regular.

You get: The Ljung-Box p-value and the autocorrelations of the errors.

Example: Ljung-Box p = 0.38 at 10 lags: pass.

Related: test.ljung_box, evaluate.residuals.

Expert detail

Ljung-Box Q on residuals (model_df adjusted for ARMA terms); the minimum p-value over series for panels.

Category residuals Metric ljung_box_p_value Default limits pass at ≥ 0.05, warn down to 0.01, fail below Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the model has no residuals; the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description lags integer 10 ≥ 1, ≤ 200

docs.title: sensitivity.prior - The results come from the data
docs.text:
Fits a Bayesian model again with wider and narrower starting assumptions. The key answers must change very little, so that you know that they come from the data.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Bayesian models, mainly models with business priors.

Avoid it when: Models that are not Bayesian.

It needs: The data, the settings and the priors of the model.

It assumes: The scales that the check tries include all reasonable prior changes.

You get: The largest relative change of a key estimate.

Example: Prior widths that are two times larger move the return of TV by 6%: pass.

Related: plausibility.signs, recovery.simulated.

Expert detail

Power-scaling or refit-based prior sensitivity: relative change of posterior means of key quantities under scaled prior widths. References: Kallioinen et al. (2023), Detecting and diagnosing prior and likelihood sensitivity with power-scaling.

Category sensitivity Metric prior_sensitivity Default limits pass at ≤ 0.2, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when only Bayesian models have priors that the check can change Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description scales list of number [0.5, 2.0] Prior widths tried

docs.title: stability.rolling_params - Estimates are stable over time
docs.text:
Fits the model again on rolling windows of history. Then it makes sure that the key estimates do not change much from one window to the next.

Difficulty: expert. Typical runtime: long.

Use it when: Models with estimates that you use for decisions (effects, returns).

Avoid it when: Short histories (the windows are then too small).

It needs: The data over time and the settings of the model.

It assumes: The true effects change slowly.

You get: How much each key estimate changes between windows.

Example: The return of TV changes by 12% between windows: pass.

Related: test.cusum.

Expert detail

Coefficient of variation (or max relative deviation from the full-sample estimate) of each watched parameter across rolling-window refits; maximum over parameters.

Category stability Metric param_variation Default limits pass at ≤ 0.25, warn up to 0.5, fail above Default severity blocking Applies to every model family Skipped when the data of the model has no time dimension Version 1.0.0

Parameters (params in a policy)

Field Type Default Description window integer – Periods per window (≥ 8) step integer 4 ≥ 1 params list of string – Parameters to watch (default: the key effects)

docs.title: choice.multinomial_logit
docs.text:
Which product customers choose on each shopping trip: a conditional (multinomial) logit over alternative-specific covariates such as price and promotion, with household-specific product preferences. Uncertainty comes from the Bayesian bootstrap over households; new households draw their preferences from the fitted spread.

Version 1.0.0 Inference bootstrap Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: bootstrap draws have no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots core.data_overview, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

docs.text:

docs.title: AdstockSettings
docs.text:
Carry-over of spend into later periods (mmm-framework AdstockConfig).

docs.title: HierarchySettings
docs.text:

docs.title: NormalPrior
docs.text:
Normal(mu, sigma) on the standardised KPI scale (KPI standard deviations).

docs.title: PriorSettings
docs.text:
Prior overrides; business-prior translation (translate_priors) writes them. * roi - per channel, a log-normal prior on the return on spend (mmm-framework's ROI-parameterised channel effect, roi_prior_mu/roi_prior_sigma); * roi_default - the log-normal ROI prior of channels not listed (default LogNormal(0, 1): median break-even); * intercept - the baseline level in KPI standard deviations from the mean.

Field Type Default Description roi map of RoiPrior – Per-channel log-normal ROI priors (channel label -> {mu, sigma}) roi_default RoiPrior (optional) null intercept NormalPrior (optional) null

docs.title: RoiPrior
docs.text:
A log-normal prior on a channel's return on spend (KPI per unit of spend over the fit window): roi ~ LogNormal(mu, sigma), so exp(mu) is the median ROI.

Field Type Default Description mu number required Log of the median ROI (≥ -20, ≤ 20) sigma number required Spread on the log scale (> 0, ≤ 10)

docs.title: mmm.frequentist
docs.text:
mmm-framework's fast frequentist marketing-mix model: adstock and saturation chosen by an out-of-sample search, a ridge solve with non-negative channel effects and bootstrap intervals; seconds instead of minutes.

Version 1.0.0 Inference bootstrap Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions additive Decision objective yes Fast scoring – Owns carryover, inverse_units, scaling LOO invalid: bootstrap replicates are not posterior draws Default plots core.ppc_fan, mmm.decomposition, mmm.response_curves, mmm.marginal_cost Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (time) of y Expected (or predictive) KPI over the panel dims and time contributions (component, time) of y Every channel, the baseline, trend, seasonality and each control; they sum to y_hat

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description contributions (sample, channel, time) target fit Channel, baseline, trend, seasonality and control contributions over the fit window per thinned draw (panel dims included) response_curves (sample, channel, multiplier) target fit Total contribution per spend multiplier and channel (and geo) per thinned draw (Guided-mode slider grids, budget optimisation) marginal_cost (sample, channel) spend per target fit Extra spend per extra unit of the KPI at current spend

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description adstock AdstockSettings {"kind": "geometric", "l_max": 8, "normalize": true} basic saturation SaturationSettings {"kind": "logistic"} basic channels map of ChannelSettings – advanced Per-channel adstock/saturation overrides (channel label -> settings) trend TrendSettings {"kind": "linear", "n_changepoints": 10, "changepoint_range… basic seasonality SeasonalitySettings {"yearly_order": 2, "monthly_order": null, "weekly_order": … basic hierarchy HierarchySettings {"pool_over": [], "media_by_geo": false, "media_geo_sigma":… basic controls list of string (optional) null advanced Control variables (default: every other numeric variable over time) frequency W or D or M (optional) null advanced Data frequency: W (weekly), D (daily) or M (monthly); default: read from the time labels new_levels pooled or hyperprior or zero or error pooled advanced How a geo or product unseen at fit is scored: pooled (the overall level and average channel effects), hyperprior (a level drawn from the fitted spread, so its range is wider), zero (no channel effects) or error (refuse) grid GridSettings {"max_multiplier": 2.5, "points": 26, "marginal_step": 0.01} advanced estimator ridge or constrained ridge advanced ridge (closed form, non-negative channel effects) or constrained (a convex program; needs the optional cvxpy dependency) bootstrap integer 200 basic Bootstrap replicates (the 'draws' of every output) (≥ 20, ≤ 5000) search_budget integer 200 advanced Adstock/saturation candidates evaluated by the transform search (≥ 10, ≤ 5000) ridge_alpha number 1.0 advanced Fallback L2 penalty on the standardised design (> 0, ≤ 1000000.0) Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template)

      "path": "new_levels",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "hyperprior",

      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "time": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "channel": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "{*panel as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{strategy}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*panel}",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "spend": {
        "dims": [
          "{*panel}",
          "channel",
          "time"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "spend",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "strategy": "error"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{*panel as d}": {
            "policy": "fixed"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: sci.fisher_kpp
docs.text:
Cell counts across a closing wound (a scratch assay) as a Fisher-KPP reaction-diffusion equation: cells move with diffusivity D, divide logistically at rate lam up to a capacity K, optionally after a start-up delay. The PDE runs inside the model from the counts at the first time; outputs are the expected density field (a kymograph over time and position) and the front speed 2 sqrt(D lam).

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.profile_bands, sci.field_map Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description density (t, x) of count Cells per column: the expected count K u(x, t), or a Poisson draw wave_speed () um/h Speed of the travelling invasion front, 2 sqrt(D lam)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description steps_per_hour integer 10 – Explicit Euler steps per hour; more steps are slower but stable for a larger diffusivity (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) delay boolean true – Multiply movement and growth by tanh(beta t): the cells start slowly after the scratch (x-ui-level: basic) max_extension integer 4 – Observation periods a forecast may reach past the last fitted time (≥ 0, ≤ 1000) diffusivity_median number 1000.0 – Prior median of D (um^2/h) (> 0) diffusivity_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of D (> 0) growth_median number 0.05 – Prior median of lam (1/h) (> 0) growth_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of lam (> 0) capacity_mu number 122.0 – Prior mean of K (cells per column) (> 0) capacity_sigma number 15.0 – Prior sd of K (> 0) delay_rate_median number 0.1 – Prior median of beta (1/h) (> 0) delay_rate_log_sd number 1.0 – Log-scale sd of the prior of beta (> 0) initial_floor number 0.1 – Smallest initial count, so an empty column can still fill (> 0) cfl_quantile number 0.99 – Quantile of the prior of D that must satisfy D dt / dx^2 <= 1/2 (> 0.5, < 1.0) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 4
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}",
        "description": "Hours since the start of the assay"
      },
      "x": {
        "kind": "float",
        "policy": "fixed",
        "description": "Centre of each column across the wound (um, equal spacing)"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "count": {
        "dims": [
          "t",
          "x"
        ],
        "dtype": "int64",
        "role": "target",
        "units": "cells",
        "bounds": [
          0,
          null
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: sci.lgcp_grid
docs.text:
A log-Gaussian Cox process for event counts on a regular space-time grid: a random-walk total per period times a smooth 2-D map (Matérn-5/2 HSGP) that can change from era to era, with negative-binomial counts. Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, core.ppc_fan, sci.field_map, sci.ensemble Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description rate (period, row, col) of count Events per cell and period: the expected intensity, or a predictive count draw total (period) of count Expected events per period in the whole grid

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description max_extension integer 8 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 400) era_periods integer 4 – Periods in one era: the spatial field changes from era to era (4 quarters = one map per year) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) field era_walk or static era_walk – era_walk: a new map each era (a random walk of maps); static: one map for all periods (the separable model) anchor busiest or first or last busiest – The era whose map gets the marginal prior; the other eras walk away from it (busiest = the fit era with the most events) likelihood negbin or poisson negbin – cell_km number 25.0 – Width of one grid cell in km (> 0) m_row integer 10 – HSGP basis functions along rows (≥ 2, ≤ 60) m_col integer 14 – HSGP basis functions along columns (≥ 2, ≤ 60) c number 1.5 – HSGP boundary factor (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0) ell_lower_km number 15.0 – 5% quantile of the lengthscale prior (> 0) ell_upper_km number 100.0 – 95% quantile of the lengthscale prior (> 0) alpha_sigma number 1.5 – Sd of the log total per period (centred on the fit mean) (> 0) sigma_g_scale number 0.5 – Half-normal scale of the RW step (> 0) eta0_scale number 2.0 – Half-normal scale of the anchor map (> 0) eta_d_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the era increments (> 0) inv_phi_rate number 1.0 – Exponential rate of 1/phi (0 = Poisson) (> 0) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 8
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "period": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}"
      },
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },

        "dims": [

docs.title: sci.strong_lens
docs.text:
A pixel forward model of a galaxy-scale strong gravitational lens: a singular isothermal ellipsoid with external shear traces every pixel to a Sersic source; the lens light, a PSF and correlated noise are modelled; the light amplitudes are integrated out. Gives the Einstein radius, the unlensed source and critical curves.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict, simulate Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the light amplitudes are integrated out over all pixels and the whitened noise couples neighbouring pixels, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.field_map Resources class M (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description model_image (row, col) of image Expected image (lens light, lensed source, sky, PSF), or a simulated observation with noise source (source_row, source_col) of image The unlensed source (parametric Sersic of each draw) on a source-plane grid einstein_radius () arcsec Einstein radius of the isothermal ellipsoid einstein_mass () solar_mass Mass inside the Einstein radius (needs z_lens and z_source)

Derived quantities (outputs.derived)

Name Dims Units Cached Description critical_curves (sample, curve_point) arcsec fit Tangential critical curve (image plane), its caustic and the cut (source plane) for posterior draws, in arcsec and grid pixel indices

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description pixel_scale number 0.05 – Pixel size in arcsec (> 0, ≤ 10) subsample integer 2 – Rays per pixel along each axis (sub-pixel sampling) (≥ 1, ≤ 4) lens_light_components integer 2 – Concentric Sersic profiles for the lens galaxy's light (≥ 0, ≤ 2) external_shear boolean true – Add an external shear to the lens noise_correlation number 0.0 – Lag-one correlation of the noise between neighbouring pixels (separable rows x columns; drizzled images have about 0.2). 0 treats pixels as independent (≥ 0.0, < 0.45) fit_noise_scale boolean true – Scale the noise map by a free factor use_mask boolean false – The data has a bool mask(row, col) of pixels psf_tolerance number 0.001 – Relative error allowed in the separable PSF expansion (> 0, < 1) psf_max_rank integer 12 – Most separable PSF terms (≥ 1, ≤ 40) theta_e_median number 1.0 – Prior median of the Einstein radius (> 0) theta_e_log_sd number 0.5 – Prior sd of log Einstein radius (> 0) mass_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the mass centre (> 0) light_center_sd number 0.1 – Prior sd of the light centre (> 0) ellipticity_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of ellipticity components (> 0) shear_sd number 0.05 – Prior sd of the shear components (> 0) light_size_medians list of any [0.5, 1.5] – Prior medians of the lens-light half-light radii (min items 2, max items 2) source_size_median number 0.2 – Prior median source radius (> 0) source_offset_sd number 0.3 – Prior sd of the source position (> 0) noise_scale_log_sd number 0.2 – Prior sd of log noise scale (> 0) theta_e_start number (optional) null – Start the optimisation at this Einstein radius instead of the radius of the ring found in the light-subtracted image n_starts integer 5 – Starts of the full-model optimisation (source positions) (≥ 1, ≤ 9) max_iter integer 3000 – Iterations per optimisation (≥ 10, ≤ 100000) source_grid integer 30 – Source-plane grid side (pixels) (≥ 4, ≤ 128) source_half_width number 0.45 – Half-width of the source-plane grid (arcsec) (> 0) curve_points integer 128 – Points per critical curve (≥ 16, ≤ 2048) curve_draws integer 100 – Posterior draws with cached critical curves (≥ 1, ≤ 2000) z_lens number (optional) null – Lens redshift (for the mass) z_source number (optional) null – Source redshift (for the mass) h0 number 70.0 – Hubble constant (km/s/Mpc) (> 0) omega_m number 0.3 – Matter density (flat LCDM) (> 0, < 1) Input data contract (schema template)

  "params": {
    "use_mask": {
      "type": "boolean",
      "default": false
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "row": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "description": "Image rows (row 0 at the bottom)"
      },
      "col": {
        "kind": "integer",

      },

        "kind": "integer",

        ],

        "role": "target",

        "description": "Surface brightness of each pixel (for example electrons/s)"
      },
      "weight": {
        "dims": [
          "row",

        ],

      },
      "psf": {
        "dims": [
          "psf_row",
          "psf_col"

      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [

docs.title: sci.traction_force
docs.text:
Traction force microscopy: recovers the 2-D traction field under a cell from the displacement field of the gel. A Gaussian prior in Fourier space (white, squared exponential or Matern spectrum); NUTS on the hyperparameters with the field integrated out, then exact posterior draws of the field.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the likelihood is a potential over Fourier modes of the whole raster; pixels are not conditionally independent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest, sci.vector_field Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description traction (component, row, col) Pa Joint posterior draws of the traction field displacement_hat (component, row, col) of displacement Displacement of each traction draw (expected), plus noise (predictive) strain_energy () fJ Elastic energy the cell put into the gel, inside the force mask contractility () uN Sum of the forces towards the force epicentre, inside the mask

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description grid_um number 1.0 – Grid spacing of the displacement raster (um) (> 0) young_pa number 10000.0 – Young's modulus of the gel (Pa) (> 0) poisson number 0.49 – Poisson ratio of the gel (≥ 0, < 0.5) young_cv number 0.0 – Relative uncertainty of Young's modulus (lognormal sd); 0 = known exactly (≥ 0, ≤ 1) prior white or smooth or matern matern – Prior spectrum of the tractions: white (Tikhonov), smooth (squared exponential) or matern ((1 + k^2 l^2)^-alpha) noise_um number 0.01 – Prior median of the noise sd (um) (> 0) traction_pa number 300.0 – Prior median of the traction scale (Pa) (> 0) lengthscale_um number 5.0 – Prior median of the length scale (um; smooth and matern) (> 0) field_draws integer 100 – Traction fields drawn per score (over all chains) (≥ 1, ≤ 1000) force_mask boolean false – The data has a force_mask(row, col) variable: strain energy and contractility are summed inside it (else over the whole grid) Input data contract (schema template)

docs.title: ConformalUncertainty
docs.text:
Split-conformal prediction intervals (representation interval, never draws). A calibration fraction of the training rows is held out (the most recent periods of time_dim for calibration_by: last, a seeded random subset for random); the interval is point ± q where q is the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest absolute calibration residual. refit refits the point model on all rows afterwards (sharper, but the finite-sample guarantee then only holds approximately).

Field Type Default Description kind conformal conformal alpha number 0.1 > 0, < 1 calibration number 0.2 ≥ 0.05, ≤ 0.5 calibration_by last or random last refit boolean false

docs.title: tabular.hierarchical_glm
docs.text:
A hierarchical generalised linear model in long layout: group intercepts (and optional slopes) partially pooled towards a population mean that may depend on group-level covariates. Unseen groups are drawn from the fitted hyperprior.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.ppc, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (obs) of y Expected response (mean) or a predictive draw per observation

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description group_dim string county – The grouping dim (index var: _idx) family normal or student_t or poisson or bernoulli normal – Likelihood family (its canonical link) covariates list of string [] – Observation-level predictors over obs (max items 256) varying_slopes list of string [] – Covariates whose slope varies by group (max items 32) group_covariates list of string [] – Group-level predictors of the group intercept (max items 64) centered boolean false – Centred group effects (non-centred default) intercept_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the population intercept (> 0) group_sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of group sds (> 0) beta_sigma number 1.0 – Prior sd of the population slopes (> 0) noise_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the noise sd (> 0) Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "group_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "county"
    },
    "covariates": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "group_covariates": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "layout": "long",
    "dims": {
      "obs": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{group_dim}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "hyperprior"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target"
      },
      "{group_dim}_idx": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "int64",
        "role": "index",
        "index_of": "{group_dim}"
      },
      "{*covariates as v}": {
        "dims": [
          "obs"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate"
      },
      "{*group_covariates as v}": {
        "dims": [
          "{group_dim}"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate"

docs.title: tabular.regressor
docs.text:
Tabular quantile regression for panels such as store x sku x week demand: rows are stacked from labelled dims, coordinates become categorical features, new levels are pooled and forecasts are direct. Quantiles are per cell and never aggregated.

Version 1.0.0 Inference custom Representation quantiles Score modes counterfactual, evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: scikit-learn and xgboost estimators provide no pointwise log-likelihood Default plots core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time, ml.feature_importance Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (quantile) – Conditional quantiles of the target over the row dims

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description estimator XGBRegressorChoice or HistGradientBoostingRegressorChoice or GradientBoostingRegressorChoice or QuantileRegressorChoice {"kind": "xgboost.XGBRegressor", "params": {"colsample_byle… – A quantile-capable estimator from the allow-listed registry target string y – rows list of string required – min items 1, max items 8 time_dim string time – time_kind time or integer or index or none time – columns ColumnsSettings – – coord_features map of category or onehot or ordinal or numeric – – new_levels pooled or zero or error pooled – pooled_max_levels integer 256 – ≥ 1, ≤ 10000 weight string (optional) null – mask string (optional) null – forecast_strategy direct or recursive direct – retransform median or smearing median – n_jobs integer 1 – ≥ 1, ≤ 64 uncertainty QuantileUncertainty {"kind": "quantile", "quantiles": [0.1, 0.5, 0.9], "rearran… – Quantile levels (the default gives an 80% band around the median) Nested settings types Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "target": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "y"
    },
    "rows": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "required": true
    },
    "time_dim": {
      "type": "string",
      "default": "time"
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer",
        "index",
        "none"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "new_levels": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "pooled",
        "zero",
        "error"
      ],
      "default": "pooled"
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "{*rows as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "{new_levels}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "{target}": {
        "dims": "{rows}",
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  },

    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "time"

        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "time",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "index"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "{time_dim}": {
            "kind": "index",
            "policy": "extend",
            "new_level_strategy": "error"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]

docs.title: ts.ardl
docs.text:
statsmodels ARDL: the result regressed on its own lags and current and past values of drivers by least squares; optional lag selection by information criterion; one model per series of a panel; forecasts need future drivers.

Version 1.0.0 Inference point Representation quantiles Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: statsmodels estimates are maximum-likelihood or least-squares point estimates without posterior draws; use holdout or backtest metrics instead of LOO Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.fit_vs_actual, core.residuals_over_time Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (t) of y Prediction-interval quantiles of y: one-step-ahead inside the fitted range, a multi-step forecast after it

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description exog list of string required basic Driver variables (at least one); their future values are needed for forecasts (min items 1, max items 64) series_dims list of string – basic Panel dims (geo, product, ...): one model per series cell. Empty for a single series. (max items 4) quantiles list of number – advanced Quantiles of the prediction intervals (must include 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95) (min items 3, max items 16) time_kind time or integer time advanced Whether the time index holds dates ('time') or period numbers ('integer') lags integer 1 – Past values of the result to use (≥ 0, ≤ 12) order integer 1 – Past values of each driver to use (0 = same period only) (≥ 0, ≤ 12) trend n or c or t or ct c – n none, c constant, t trend, ct both auto boolean false – Choose lags and driver orders per series by an information criterion (up to lags/order) ic aic or bic or hqic aic – Criterion for auto causal boolean false advanced Use only past values of the drivers (no same-period effect) Input data contract (schema template)

  "params": {
    "series_dims": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "exog": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{*series_dims as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "forbid"
      },
      "{*exog as x}": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "t": {
            "kind": "integer"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: ts.gaussian_hmm
docs.text:
A K-state Gaussian hidden Markov model over padded sequences (e.g. animal tracks). Hidden states are marginalised with the forward algorithm; forecasts and filters start from the stored terminal state.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, filter, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO invalid: the HMM likelihood is a potential over whole sequences; steps within a sequence are dependent, so pointwise leave-one-out is not defined Default plots core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (animal, step) of y One-step-ahead expected value or predictive draw of y state_prob (animal, step, state) probability Hidden-state probabilities (predicted, or filtered in filter mode)

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description n_states integer 2 – Number of hidden states K (≥ 2, ≤ 8) mu_center number 0.0 – Prior mean of the state means mu_sigma number 2.0 – Prior sd of the state means (> 0) sigma_scale number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the emission sds (> 0) stickiness number 2.0 – Extra Dirichlet weight on staying in the same state (≥ 0, ≤ 1000) pi_concentration number 1.0 – Dirichlet weight of pi (> 0) identification relabel or ordered relabel – relabel: sort states by mean after sampling; ordered: ordered prior Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "animal": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "new_levels",
        "new_level_strategy": "pooled"
      },
      "step": {
        "kind": "integer",
        "policy": "extend"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "animal",
          "step"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      },
      "mask": {
        "dims": [
          "animal",
          "step"
        ],
        "dtype": "bool",
        "role": "mask"
      }
    },
    "ragged": [
      {
        "group_dim": "animal",
        "within_dim": "step",
        "form": "padded",
        "mask_var": "mask"
      }
    ]
  }
}

docs.title: ts.hsgp_trend
docs.text:
A smooth Hilbert-space GP trend with optional linear drift and Fourier seasonality for one regular time series (Mauna-Loa style). Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit; further horizons need a refit.

Version 1.0.0 Inference mcmc Representation draws Score modes evaluate, forecast, predict Contributions none Decision objective – Fast scoring – Owns – LOO valid Default plots core.ppc_fan, core.convergence, core.posterior_forest Resources class S (min S)

Outputs

Output Dims Units Description y_hat (t) of y The series: expected value (trend + seasonality) or a predictive draw trend (t) of y The long-term component (intercept + drift + GP), no seasonality

Settings (model.settings)

Field Type Default Level Description max_extension integer 24 – Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit; sizes the HSGP domain (x-ui-level: basic) (≥ 1, ≤ 10000) kernel expquad or matern52 or matern32 expquad – Covariance kernel of the smooth trend m integer 30 – Number of HSGP basis functions (≥ 4, ≤ 400) c number 1.5 – Boundary factor (L = c on the scaled axis) (> 1.0, ≤ 5.0) lengthscale_mu number 0.4 – Median of the lengthscale prior on the scaled axis [-1, 1] (> 0) lengthscale_sigma number 0.5 – Log-scale sd of the lengthscale (> 0) eta_sigma number 1.0 – Half-normal scale of the GP amplitude (> 0) linear_trend boolean true – intercept_sigma number 1.0 – > 0 slope_sigma number 1.0 – > 0 season_period number (optional) 12.0 – Seasonal period in periods of t (12 for monthly data) season_order integer 3 – Fourier order of the seasonality (≥ 0, ≤ 20) season_sigma number 0.5 – > 0 noise_sigma number 0.5 – > 0 Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "max_extension": {
      "type": "integer",
      "default": 24
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend",
        "max_extension": "{max_extension}"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "allow"
      }
    }
  }
}

Field Type Default Level Description exog list of string – basic Driver variables (prices, promotions, holidays) whose future values are supplied for forecasts (max items 64) series_dims list of string – basic Panel dims (geo, product, ...): one model per series cell. Empty for a single series. (max items 4) quantiles list of number – advanced Quantiles of the prediction intervals (must include 0.05, 0.5 and 0.95) (min items 3, max items 16) time_kind time or integer time advanced Whether the time index holds dates ('time') or period numbers ('integer') irf_horizon integer 12 – Periods of the impulse responses and the variance decomposition (≥ 1, ≤ 60) k_ar_diff integer 1 – Lagged differences in each equation (≥ 0, ≤ 12) coint_rank integer (optional) null – Number of long-run relationships; leave empty to take it from the Johansen test rank_test trace or maxeig trace – Johansen test statistic rank_signif number 0.05 – Significance of the rank test: 0.01, 0.05 or 0.1 deterministic n or co or ci or lo or li or cili or colo ci – Constant/trend: n none, co outside / ci inside the long-run relation, lo/li linear trend outside/inside, combinations Input data contract (schema template) 
{
  "params": {
    "series_dims": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    },
    "time_kind": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "time",
        "integer"
      ],
      "default": "time"
    },
    "exog": {
      "type": "string_list",
      "default": []
    }
  },
  "template": {
    "dims": {
      "t": {
        "kind": "time",
        "policy": "extend"
      },
      "{*series_dims as d}": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      },
      "variable": {
        "kind": "categorical",
        "policy": "fixed"
      }
    },
    "vars": {
      "y": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "variable",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "target",
        "missing": "forbid"
      },
      "{*exog as x}": {
        "dims": [
          "{*series_dims}",
          "t"
        ],
        "dtype": "float64",
        "role": "covariate",
        "future_required": true
      }
    }
  },
  "cases": [
    {
      "when": {
        "time_kind": "integer"
      },
      "merge": {
        "dims": {
          "t": {
            "kind": "integer"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The authorization rules of the platform, generated from mapi_spec.tenancy and mapi_spec.tokens by scripts/gen_docs_platform.py. Every component (the API, the web app through OpenAPI, the tests) checks the same table. The Administration guide explains how to use it.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Roles are ordered viewer < editor < runner < admin; each includes the one before it. tenant-wide means only a tenant-wide membership grants it; otherwise the effective role in the project counts (the higher of the tenant-wide and the project grant). A pair that is not listed is denied to everyone.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Platform operators (verified e-mails in MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS, signed in; never through an API token) hold exactly these permissions, on every tenant: audit read, billing read, catalog read, executor read, executor update, kill_switch read, kill_switch update, member read, project read, quota delete, quota read, quota update, run read, tenant_deletion manage, tenant_deletion read, tenant_member read, tenant create, tenant delete, tenant manage, tenant read, token read, usage read. None of them reads tenant content: datasets, specs, models or plots.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
A capability is granted on top of a role, per project membership; project admins hold every capability implicitly. A rule that needs one says so in the roles table ("✓ with reviewer").

Capability Needed for What it allows reviewer model approve Approve or reject model validations that wait for a second person (POST /v1/validations/{id}/approvals), never the member's own submissions (SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN) and never through an API token. Granted per project membership (capabilities on the membership, or the Reviewer column of Members); viewers cannot hold it.

docs.title: Token scopes
docs.text:
A token acts as its owner, narrowed by its scopes: both the owner's role and a scope must allow an action. admin covers everything the owner's role allows; score:<alias> covers one endpoint (score:* every endpoint of the project).

docs.title: Server settings
docs.text:
Every setting of mapi-server (api, worker, migrate, dev), generated from mapi_server.settings.Settings by scripts/gen_docs_reference.py. Each field reads the environment variable MAPI_<FIELD>; .env files are not read. The configuration reference explains them by task and lists the variables of the other components.

Variable Type Default Description MAPI_ENV str local Selects bucket names mapi-{env}-* MAPI_PROFILE single-tenant | multi-tenant | dev single-tenant MAPI_TENANT_ID str default MAPI_PROJECT_ID str default MAPI_DEBUG bool False Include tracebacks in problem.untrusted_text MAPI_API_HOST str 127.0.0.1 MAPI_API_PORT int 8000 MAPI_API_URL str http://127.0.0.1:8000 MAPI_WEB_ORIGIN str http://127.0.0.1:5173 MAPI_PLOTS_ORIGIN str http://127.0.0.1:5174 MAPI_DATA_DIR Path .local MAPI_ALLOWED_HOSTS list (computed) Host header values the API answers (comma-separated in the environment; '*' turns the check off). The host of api_url is always allowed. The API is unauthenticated in M1, so this is what stops DNS-rebinding pages from using it. MAPI_DATABASE_URL or DATABASE_URL str \| None unset postgresql:// URL; unset = embedded pgserver under data_dir/pg MAPI_DB_POOL_SIZE int 10 MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_POOL_SIZE int 5 MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_POOL_SIZE int 5 MAPI_DB_ECHO bool False MAPI_DATABASE_APP_URL str \| None unset Login of the request-path role (row-level security applies). Unset: connect with DATABASE_URL and SET ROLE db_app_role on every connection MAPI_DATABASE_SYSTEM_URL str \| None unset Login of the platform role: the orchestrator's dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer and housekeeper (bypasses row-level security; the API never needs it). Unset: DATABASE_URL with SET ROLE db_system_role MAPI_DATABASE_GATEWAY_URL str \| None unset Login of the gateway role: what the API and events service look up before a tenant is known (sign-in, memberships, operator metadata, pushed events; row-level security applies). Unset: DATABASE_URL with SET ROLE db_gateway_role MAPI_DB_APP_ROLE str mapi_app MAPI_DB_SYSTEM_ROLE str mapi_system MAPI_DB_GATEWAY_ROLE str mapi_gateway MAPI_OBJECT_STORE shim | memory | gcs shim MAPI_GCS_ENDPOINT str http://127.0.0.1:4443 MAPI_GCS_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT str \| None unset Base URL put into signed URLs when executions/browsers reach the shim under another host name (default: gcs_endpoint) MAPI_GCP_PROJECT str \| None unset Google Cloud project of the Cloud Storage client (MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs) MAPI_URL_SIGNER str \| None unset Service account that signs Cloud Storage URLs through IAM signBlob (keyless; required with MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs) MAPI_URL_UPLOADER str \| None unset Service account that signs create-only upload policies (objects.create, never delete; required with MAPI_OBJECT_STORE=gcs and distinct from url_signer) MAPI_GCS_ROOT Path \| None unset The GCS shim's state directory (default: data_dir/gcs) MAPI_GCS_KEY_FILE Path \| None unset Key file of the shim's control principal (default: gcs_root/_shim/keys/control.json) MAPI_EXEC_TOKEN str \| None unset Bearer token of the shim's exec principal (local executors only; default: read from gcs_root/_shim/keys/exec.json) MAPI_EXECUTOR local-process | docker | docker-gvisor | cloudrun-jobs local-process MAPI_RUNNER_COMMAND list (computed) argv of the supervisor (shell-quoted string in the environment) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGE str mapi/base-bayes:0.7.0 Runner image for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe, ...) MAPI_DOCKER_IMAGES dict (computed) Plugin namespace → runner image (JSON in the environment) MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK str none Network of run containers: 'container:' (share the shim's namespace, so 127.0.0.1:4443 works) or an internal network holding only the shim. 'none' is refused while the bootstrap URL is HTTP (nothing would be reachable). MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK_ISOLATED bool False Declare MAPI_DOCKER_NETWORK an internal network that holds only the GCS shim (no route out, no DNS beyond it), so docker-gvisor reports enforced egress and DNS. Shared tiers still need a passing security-suite run recorded for these caps MAPI_DOCKER_RUNTIME_GVISOR str runsc MAPI_EXECUTOR_WORKDIR Path \| None unset MAPI_CANCEL_GRACE_S float 10.0 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PROJECT str \| None unset Exec project that holds the Cloud Run Job inventory (cloudrun-jobs) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION str europe-west1 Region of the Job inventory MAPI_DEFAULT_RESIDENCY str \| None unset Data residency of the platform tenant, of tenants adopted by the migrations and of tenants created without one (default: the multi-region of MAPI_CLOUDRUN_REGION for cloudrun-jobs, e.g. eu, else us) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_JOB_TEMPLATE str mapi-{env}-{base}-{class} Job id convention; {env}, {base} (base-bayes|base-ml|base-forecast) and {class} (s|m|l) are substituted. Must match the Jobs Terraform creates MAPI_CLOUDRUN_PLUGIN_BASES dict (computed) Plugin namespace → base image family (JSON in the environment) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DEFAULT_BASE str base-bayes Base for runs without a mapped plugin (ingest, describe) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMITS_PER_MINUTE float 150.0 Token-bucket rate of jobs.run calls per orchestrator; the regional quota is 180/min [verify M0], so split it between orchestrator replicas MAPI_CLOUDRUN_SUBMIT_BURST int 10 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_MAX_429_RETRIES int 6 429 answers before giving up MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_BASE_S float 1.0 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_BACKOFF_CAP_S float 64.0 MAPI_CLOUDRUN_TIMEOUT_MARGIN_S int 120 Task timeout = run timeout + margin (the supervisor flushes) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_EGRESS_ENFORCED bool True The exec network denies all egress except the restricted VIP MAPI_CLOUDRUN_DNS_ENFORCED bool False The DNS response policy is verified to apply to Jobs [verify M0]; verified and public tenants are only placed when both egress and DNS are enforced (and suite evidence is recorded) MAPI_CLOUDRUN_ADOPT_LOOKBACK_S float 93600 How far back orphan adoption lists executions MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_AUDIENCE str \| None unset Expected audience of the Pub/Sub push OIDC token (usually the push endpoint URL). When set, POST /internal/events requires a Google-signed token MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SERVICE_ACCOUNT str \| None unset Service account the push subscription signs its tokens as MAPI_PUBSUB_PUSH_SUBSCRIPTIONS list (computed) Accepted subscription names (comma-separated; empty = any) MAPI_GOOGLE_JWKS_URL str https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs JWKS of Google's OIDC signing keys (push token verification) MAPI_DISPATCH_RATE_PER_MINUTE float 180.0 MAPI_DISPATCH_BURST int 10 MAPI_DISPATCH_BATCH int 10 MAPI_DISPATCH_POLL_S float 1.0 MAPI_DISPATCH_LEASE_S float 120.0 MAPI_DISPATCH_TIERS list (computed) Trust tiers whose runs this orchestrator leases (comma-separated); empty: every tier. Give each orchestrator a disjoint list when several serve different exec pools, so tenant tiers never share a pool MAPI_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_S float 10.0 MAPI_STALL_INTERVALS int 15 K: silence > K x progress interval MAPI_COMPLETE_EVENT_GRACE_S float 60.0 MAPI_LOST_EXECUTION_GRACE_S float 60.0 MAPI_MAX_INFRA_RETRIES int 2 MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_WINDOW_S float 1800.0 No auto-retry beyond 30 min MAPI_AUTO_RETRY_COST_FACTOR float 2.0 No auto-retry once a run's metered cost reaches this multiple of its estimate (plan §8.3: retries capped by cost) MAPI_FINALIZE_MAX_ATTEMPTS int 5 MAPI_DEADLINE_GRACE_S float 60.0 MAPI_HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_S float 300.0 Sweep of expired upload intents and other expiring rows MAPI_CATALOG_PATH Path \| None unset Catalog JSON exported at image build (runner describe) MAPI_IMAGE_DIGEST str \| None unset MAPI_UV_LOCK_PATH Path \| None unset MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_PATH Path \| None unset PEM of the bundle-signing key (default: data_dir/keys/bundle-signing-p256.pem); every process that signs or verifies bundles must share it MAPI_SIGNING_TRUSTED_KEY_PATHS list (computed) PEM files (public or private) of retired bundle-signing keys whose signatures still verify (comma-separated): key rotation without invalidating the bundles the old key signed MAPI_SIGNING_KEY_CREATE bool True Create the signing key when it is missing; off where mapi-server migrate creates it on shared storage (compose api/worker) MAPI_SIGNER local | kms local local = PEM key file; kms = Cloud KMS asymmetric key MAPI_KMS_KEY_VERSION str \| None unset projects/…/cryptoKeys/…/cryptoKeyVersions/N that signs bundle manifests MAPI_KMS_TRUSTED_KEY_VERSIONS list (computed) Older key versions whose signatures still verify (comma-separated) MAPI_INTERNAL_TOKEN str \| None unset If set, POST /internal/events requires this bearer MAPI_AUTH_REQUIRED bool \| None unset Require a session or API token on every non-public route (default: required in every profile except single-tenant) MAPI_SERVER_SECRET str \| None unset Root secret of the token pepper and audit fingerprints (default: read or create server-secret next to the bundle-signing key). Changing it invalidates every API token. MAPI_SERVER_SECRET_PATH Path \| None unset MAPI_COOKIE_SECURE bool \| None unset Secure, __Host- prefixed cookies (default: on when api_url is https) MAPI_OIDC_ISSUER str \| None unset OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. https://accounts.google.com) MAPI_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL str \| None unset Default: /.well-known/openid-configuration MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_ID str \| None unset MAPI_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET str \| None unset MAPI_OIDC_REDIRECT_URI str \| None unset Registered redirect URI (default: /auth/callback) MAPI_OIDC_ALGORITHMS list (computed) MAPI_OIDC_CLI_CLIENT_IDS list (computed) Client ids of public OIDC clients (the mapi CLI) whose ID tokens of the same issuer are accepted as bearers (comma-separated; empty: API tokens only) MAPI_OIDC_EXTRA_PARAMS dict (computed) Extra authorization parameters, e.g. {"hd": "acme.com"} (JSON) MAPI_OPERATOR_EMAILS list (computed) Verified e-mails that sign in as platform operators (comma-separated) MAPI_DEFAULT_TENANT_ADMINS list (computed) E-mails invited as admins of the default tenant at start-up (comma-separated; the invitation is claimed at first sign-in) MAPI_DEVIDP_USERS list (computed) Accounts of the development identity provider (MAPI_PROFILE=dev only) MAPI_PRICE_TABLE_PATH Path \| None unset JSON PriceTable (default: mapi_spec.cost.DEFAULT_PRICE_TABLE) MAPI_ESTIMATE_WALL_S dict (computed) MAPI_RATE_LIMITS_ENABLED bool True MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES int 500 Queued runs the fair-share planner considers MAPI_LEASE_CANDIDATES_PER_TENANT int 50 At most this many of them per tenant (a tenant whose runs are held cannot fill the window) MAPI_EXECUTOR_REPORT_INTERVAL_S float 10.0 MAPI_EXECUTOR_EVIDENCE_MAX_AGE_S float 259200.0 How long a recorded conformance or security-suite report lets an executor take verified and public tenants (the nightly suites renew it) MAPI_SSE_HEARTBEAT_S float 15.0 MAPI_SSE_POLL_S float 5.0 Fallback poll when no NOTIFY arrives MAPI_SSE_REAUTH_S float 60.0 How often an open event stream re-checks its caller's credential (a revoked token, an expired session or a lost membership closes the stream) MAPI_MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES int 8388608 MAPI_LOG_LEVEL debug | info | warning | error info MAPI_RENDER_TIMEOUT_S int 300 Wall-clock limit of a POST /v1/plots:render run (the sandbox kills it) MAPI_RENDER_PLOTLY_ENABLED bool False Accept Plotly plots in POST /v1/plots:render. Plotly static export needs kaleido and a Chrome/Chromium in the runner image, which the base images do not ship; while off, Plotly renders are refused with MODE_NOT_SUPPORTED MAPI_EMBED_RATE_PER_MINUTE int 300 Public embed views per minute and embed link (429 beyond) MAPI_EMBED_IP_RATE_PER_MINUTE int 120 Public embed requests per minute and client address, valid or not MAPI_EMBED_CACHE_S float 60.0 How long an API instance reuses an embed's resolved plot (revocation and expiry are still checked on every request; responses are never cached by browsers or shared caches, so a revoked link stops rendering on the next load) MAPI_EMBED_IMAGE_URL_TTL_S int 900 Lifetime of the PNG fallback's signed URL MAPI_LOG_JSON bool True Emit JSON logs (structlog); off gives a human console renderer MAPI_TRUSTED_PROXIES list[str] \| None unset Addresses or CIDR ranges of the proxies in front of the API (load balancer, Cloud Run front end, the web container's /v1/ proxy), comma-separated. A request from one of them takes the right-most untrusted X-Forwarded-For hop as the client address (per-address limits, Sybil checks, audit). 'none': clients reach the API directly and X-Forwarded-For is ignored. Required in the multi-tenant profile MAPI_METRICS_ENABLED bool True Mount GET /metrics (Prometheus) MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_PORT int \| None unset Serve GET /metrics of the worker (dispatcher, reconciler, finalizer, events) on this port; unset: the worker exposes no metrics MAPI_WORKER_METRICS_HOST str 127.0.0.1 Bind address of the worker's metrics endpoint MAPI_METRICS_TOKEN str \| None unset Bearer a scraper must present on GET /metrics; required in the multi-tenant profile (the series carry tenant ids and spend) MAPI_TRACING_ENABLED bool True Install the OpenTelemetry tracer provider MAPI_OTLP_ENDPOINT str \| None unset OTLP/HTTP collector base URL for span export (also read from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT); unset means spans are created but not exported MAPI_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_HTTP bool False Development only: allow http:// webhook URLs, for the hosts in MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST only (refused in the multi-tenant profile) MAPI_WEBHOOK_DEV_ALLOWLIST list (computed) Development only: webhook host names (comma-separated) exempt from the SSRF address and port checks, e.g. a receiver on localhost (refused in the multi-tenant profile) MAPI_WEBHOOK_CA_FILE Path \| None unset Extra PEM CA bundle trusted for webhook receivers (a private CA); the system trust store is always used MAPI_WEBHOOK_POLL_INTERVAL_S float 2.0 How often the worker looks for due webhook deliveries Largest JSON output of a node MAPI_SIGNUP_ENABLED bool \| None unset Self-service sign-up at POST /auth/signup (default: on in the dev and multi-tenant profiles when a mailer is configured, off single-tenant) MAPI_MAILER MailerKind \| None unset How e-mail is sent: console, outbox, smtp or none (default: outbox in dev, console single-tenant, smtp multi-tenant) MAPI_MAIL_FROM str modeling-api <no-reply@mapi.localhost> From: header of the e-mails the server sends MAPI_OUTBOX_DIR Path \| None unset Where the outbox mailer writes messages (default: data_dir/outbox) MAPI_SMTP_HOST str \| None unset SMTP server (MAPI_MAILER=smtp) MAPI_SMTP_PORT int 587 MAPI_SMTP_TLS starttls | ssl starttls starttls (port 587) or ssl (implicit TLS, port 465) MAPI_SMTP_USERNAME str \| None unset A file of disposable e-mail domains (one per line, # comments), e.g. a maintained public list, added to the built-in one MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_IP_PER_HOUR int 5 Sign-ups accepted per client address and hour MAPI_SIGNUP_PER_DOMAIN_PER_DAY int 25 Verified sign-ups per e-mail domain and day (shared free-mail domains are exempt) MAPI_SIGNUP_GLOBAL_PER_HOUR int 500 Verified sign-ups per hour on the whole platform MAPI_SIGNUP_SHARED_EMAIL_DOMAINS list (computed) Free-mail domains shared by unrelated people (comma-separated; replaces the built-in list): no per-domain sign-up cap and no domain-burst Sybil flag MAPI_VERIFY_PER_IP_PER_MINUTE int 20 E-mail verification attempts per client address and minute MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_WINDOW_DAYS int 30 Look-back of the Sybil heuristics (same address, browser, e-mail) MAPI_SIGNUP_SYBIL_THRESHOLD int 3 Workspaces created from one address, browser or e-mail within the window before a new one is flagged for review MAPI_SIGNUP_FLAGGED_SUSPEND bool only) MAPI_TENANT_DELETION_GRACE_S float 604800.0 Grace period of a tenant deletion: the tenant is suspended and may cancel MAPI_DELETION_REAUTH_MAX_AGE_S float \| None unset Also require a sign-in at most this old to request a deletion (re-auth); unset: the confirmation phrase alone MAPI_DELETION_RUN_STOP_TIMEOUT_S float 3600.0 How long a purge waits for the tenant's cancelled runs to stop MAPI_DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS int 8 Automatic retries of a failed purge before operators must retry MAPI_BUNDLE_RETENTION_DAYS int 30 The bundles bucket's retention period (Terraform bundle_retention_days): when a purge may retry objects a retention lock refused MAPI_LIFECYCLE_INTERVAL_S float 15.0 Cadence of the deletion and export scheduler (orchestrator) MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_INLINE_BYTES int 268435456 Dataset bytes a GDPR export archive includes; larger exports list the remaining objects (with sizes and hashes) instead MAPI_EXPORT_RETENTION_S float 604800.0 How long a GDPR export archive is kept MAPI_EXPORT_LINK_TTL_S float 900.0 Lifetime of an export's signed download link MAPI_EXPORTS_PER_DAY int 3 GDPR exports a tenant may request per day MAPI_EXPORT_MAX_METADATA_BYTES int 268435456 Bytes of metadata rows (runs, logs, events, audit, ...) a GDPR export archive includes; the tables cut short are listed in its manifest MAPI_EXPORT_BUILD_TIMEOUT_S float 3600.0 How long one GDPR export build may take; a build still marked running 5 minutes after that (its process died) is built again once, then failed
