docs.title: ModelSpec
docs.text:
The declarative modelling file.

Field Type Default Description apiVersion mapi/v1 required kind ModelSpec required metadata Metadata required data DataBlock required pipeline list of StepCall – max items 64 model ModelBlock required outputs OutputsBlock – evaluate EvaluateBlock – execution ExecutionBlock – calibration Calibration (optional) null Business priors and lift tests the model should respect (M3); needs a model whose capabilities declare them

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The plain-language card of one catalog item. Every field except the expert ones is required, so an About that validates is structurally complete; :func:about_issues adds the editorial rules (one or two sentences, no jargon in the summary, known chooser tags, related ids that exist).

Field Type Default Description title string required A human name summary_plain string required One or two sentences without jargon: what it does for you use_when list of string required min items 1, max items 10 avoid_when list of string required min items 1, max items 10 data_needs list of string required min items 1, max items 10 assumptions list of string required min items 1, max items 10 outputs list of string required min items 1, max items 10 difficulty Difficulty required typical_runtime TypicalRuntime required example string required A tiny example related list of string – Ids of related catalog items (models, steps, nodes, checks, templates) (max items 16) references list of AboutReference – max items 10 expert_notes string (optional) null Maths, estimator details, caveats for experts fits map of list of string – Chooser tags: question id -> the answers this item suits

docs.title: AboutReference
docs.text:
A source for the expert detail (a paper, a book chapter, library documentation).

Field Type Default Description title string required url string (optional) null

docs.title: AsOfSplit
docs.text:
Train on coords up to and including as_of; hold out the rest (optionally gap).

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind as_of required dim string required as_of string or integer or number or boolean required gap integer 0 ≥ 0

docs.title: Binding
docs.text:
Canonical name → dataset name, for dims and variables (geo: market). Names that are not bound keep their dataset name. The binding is stored in the bundle and reversed on every output by default.

Field Type Default Description dims map of string – vars map of string –

docs.title: BusinessPriors
docs.text:
Beliefs in business units, per channel (keys are channel labels as in the data), and/or about the baseline. At least one belief is stated: a baseline belief alone is fine (channels without a belief keep the model's default priors).

Field Type Default Description channels map of ChannelBelief – baseline_share ShareBelief (optional) null kpi_units string (optional) null spend_units string (optional) null

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
The calibration block of a ModelSpec: beliefs and experiment results the model should respect. prior_translation_run records which translate_priors run produced the priors in model.settings.priors (lineage only).

Field Type Default Description business_priors BusinessPriors (optional) null lift_tests list of LiftTest – max items 500 prior_translation_run string (optional) null

docs.title: ChannelBelief
docs.text:
What the user believes about one channel: exactly one of roi or contribution_share, held with credibility. * roi: KPI units gained per spend unit over the fit window ([1.5, 4] = "every euro returns between 1.5 and 4 euros of revenue"); * contribution_share: the channel's share of the KPI over the fit window.

Field Type Default Description roi list of any (optional) null contribution_share list of any (optional) null credibility number 0.8 Probability that the true value lies inside the range (0.8 = 'I am 80% sure') (≥ 0.5, ≤ 0.99)

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text: Field Type Default Description every_draws integer required ≥ 1, ≤ 1000000

docs.title: DataBlock
docs.text:
The dataset, side tables, binding to canonical names and the split.

Field Type Default Description dataset string required Dataset reference dataset://project/name@version side_tables map of SideTable – bind Binding – split TimeHoldoutSplit or LastPerGroupSplit or AsOfSplit or LeaveGroupOutSplit or MaskBlockSplit (optional) null

docs.title: Difficulty
docs.text:
How much statistical background an item needs to use well.

One of beginner, intermediate, expert.

docs.title: EvaluateBlock
docs.text: Field Type Default Description metrics list of string – max items 32

docs.title: ExecutionBlock
docs.text: Field Type Default Description resource_class ResourceClass S timeout string – Duration such as '45m', '1h30m' or '90s'.

docs.title: FitConfig
docs.text:
Platform fit settings. Plugin-specific limits come from the manifest's fit_schema.

Field Type Default Description mode FitMode evaluate_then_refit engine string (optional) null tune integer (optional) null draws integer (optional) null chains integer (optional) null target_accept number (optional) null seed integer (optional) null prior_predictive PriorPredictive (optional) null keep KeepConfig – checkpoint Checkpoint (optional) null

docs.title: FitMode
docs.text: One of evaluate_then_refit, train_only.

docs.title: JsonValue
docs.text: Type: any

docs.title: KeepConfig
docs.text:
Optional groups kept in the bundle.

Field Type Default Description log_likelihood boolean false posterior_predictive PosteriorPredictiveKeep or boolean false prior boolean false

docs.title: LastPerGroupSplit
docs.text:
Hold out the last last rows along dim within each group (min_len kept).

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind last_per_group required dim string required within list of string required min items 1, max items 8 last integer 1 ≥ 1 min_len integer 1 ≥ 1

docs.title: LeaveGroupOutSplit
docs.text:
Hold out whole groups of dim (explicit groups or n random ones).

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind leave_group_out required dim string required groups list of string or integer or number or boolean (optional) null n integer (optional) null seed integer (optional) null

docs.title: LiftTest
docs.text:
One experiment: spend_delta extra spend on channel (optionally in one geo) from start to end (inclusive) caused kpi_delta incremental KPI. Give the measurement's uncertainty as a standard error se or a confidence interval ci at ci_level. A holdout ("turn the channel off") is a negative spend_delta with (usually) a negative kpi_delta.

Field Type Default Description id string (optional) null channel string required geo string (optional) null start string required end string required spend_delta number required Extra spend during the test (spend units) kpi_delta number required Measured incremental KPI (KPI units) se number (optional) null Standard error of kpi_delta ci list of any (optional) null Confidence interval of kpi_delta ci_level number 0.9 ≥ 0.5, ≤ 0.999 description string (optional) null

docs.title: MaskBlockSplit
docs.text:
Hold out random blocks over dims (block sizes per dim) covering fraction.

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind mask_block required dims list of string required min items 1, max items 8 fraction number required > 0, < 1 block map of integer – seed integer (optional) null

docs.title: Metadata
docs.text:
Identity and labels of a document.

Field Type Default Description name string required project string required labels map of string – description string (optional) null about About (optional) null M3.5: a plain-language About card so others can choose this spec, pipeline or workflow (see mapi_spec.about)

docs.title: ModelBlock
docs.text:
The model plugin, its settings and fit configuration. settings.dim_policies is platform-reserved: a mapping dim → policy that may only tighten the plugin's policies. It is removed before plugin settings validation.

Field Type Default Description use string required Registered id with an optional semver range settings map of JsonValue – fit FitConfig –

docs.title: OutputsBlock
docs.text: Field Type Default Description derived list of string – max items 64 plots list of string – max items 64 ui_draws integer 300 ≥ 0, ≤ 2000

docs.title: PosteriorPredictiveKeep
docs.text: Field Type Default Description thin integer 1 ≥ 1, ≤ 10000

docs.title: PriorPredictive
docs.text: Field Type Default Description draws integer required ≥ 1, ≤ 100000

docs.title: ResourceClass
docs.text:
Executor resource class. Ordered: S < M < L < XL.

One of S, M, L, XL.

docs.title: ScorePolicy
docs.text:
Which side-table version is used at score time.

One of pinned, latest, supplied.

docs.title: ShareBelief
docs.text:
A share range (for example of the baseline: KPI that happens without any media).

Field Type Default Description share list of any required min items 2, max items 2 credibility number 0.8 Probability that the true value lies inside the range (0.8 = 'I am 80% sure') (≥ 0.5, ≤ 0.99)

docs.title: SideTable
docs.text:
A small constant dataset (FX rates, holidays ...) used by steps.

Field Type Default Description ref string required Dataset reference dataset://project/name@version score_policy ScorePolicy pinned

docs.title: StepCall
docs.text:
One pipeline step: {id, use: core.resample@^1, with: {...settings}}.

Field Type Default Description id string required use string required Registered id with an optional semver range with map of JsonValue –

docs.title: TimeHoldoutSplit
docs.text:
Hold out the end of an ordered dim: last periods, a fraction or after a coord.

Field Type Default Description after_step string (optional) null Stage the split happens at (a step id or 'raw'); default: end of the stateless prefix allow_leakage boolean false Downgrade LEAKAGE_RISK to a warning (acknowledged) kind time_holdout required dim string required last integer (optional) null fraction number (optional) null after string or integer or number or boolean (optional) null

docs.title: TypicalRuntime
docs.text:
Rough wall-clock time on typical data (S resource class).

One of instant, seconds, minutes, long.

docs.title: ScoreRequest
docs.text:
Score a fitted model with replayed preprocessing.

Field Type Default Description apiVersion mapi/v1 required kind ScoreRequest required model string required endpoint://project/alias or model://project/name@vN mode predict or forecast or counterfactual or simulate or filter or evaluate predict horizon Horizon (optional) null inputs_stage string raw data string (optional) null scenario string (optional) null side_tables map of string – select map of list of string or integer or number or boolean – interventions list of Intervention – max items 256 output OutputSelector – seed integer (optional) null future_covariates FutureCovariates (optional) null M3: how forecasts get future covariates (default: supplied)

docs.title: Aggregation
docs.text:
Reduce outputs over dims before summarising (validity depends on representation).

Field Type Default Description over list of string required min items 1, max items 16 how sum or mean or min or max sum

docs.title: FutureCovariates
docs.text:
Where future values of future_required covariates come from in a forecast (M3). supplied (default) needs them in the request's data or scenario (MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE otherwise). The other policies let the runner extend them over the horizon, per series, inside the sandbox: carry_last repeats the last observed value, seasonal_naive repeats the value one season earlier (the time dim's yearly period), zero sets them to zero (e.g. "no spend planned").

One of supplied, carry_last, seasonal_naive, zero.

docs.title: Horizon
docs.text: Field Type Default Description dim string required periods integer required ≥ 1, ≤ 100000

docs.title: Intervention
docs.text:
Change var on the coords selected by sel: exactly one of multiply/add/set.

Field Type Default Description var string required sel map of string or integer or number or boolean or list of string or integer or number or boolean – multiply number (optional) null add number (optional) null set number (optional) null

docs.title: OutputSelector
docs.text:
What a score request returns.

Field Type Default Description kind expected or predictive expected summary list of string (optional) null Summaries to return; default depends on representation draws integer 0 ≥ 0, ≤ 10000 thin_index bundle bundle units original or model original names dataset or canonical dataset aggregate Aggregation (optional) null vars list of string – max items 256

docs.title: Built-in steps catalog
docs.text:
Generated from the mapi-steps catalog export (python -m mapi_steps.catalog): the same static JSON the control plane uses to validate specs without importing step code. For how the steps behave together, read Built-in steps.

Step Kind Learns state Invertible Looks back Summary core.calendar feature – – – Calendar features (day of week, month, ISO week, ...) core.encode_levels feature yes – – Integer codes for categorical levels core.formula feature – – – Derived variable from an arithmetic expression core.fourier feature yes – – Fourier seasonality features core.holidays feature – – – Holiday indicators per period from a side table core.lag feature – – yes Lagged copies of variables within groups core.lag_tensor feature – – yes Lag tensor (lags 0 .. l_max-1) for in-model carry-over core.missing_indicator feature – – – Indicators of missing values core.one_hot feature yes – – One-hot indicators of categorical variables core.trend feature yes – – Polynomial time trend core.count_events reshape – – – Count events per period on a dense grid core.filter_coords reshape – – – Select labels of a dim core.resample reshape – – – Aggregate a time dim to a coarser frequency core.stack reshape – – – Stack dims into one core.to_long reshape – – – Padded ragged data to long form core.to_padded reshape – – – Long ragged data to padded form with a mask core.unstack reshape – – – Unstack a dim into several core.adstock value – – yes Adstock (carry-over) with fixed parameters core.clip value – – – Clip values to bounds core.fx_convert value – yes – Currency conversion with per-period rates from a side table core.impute value yes – – Fill missing values (mean, median, constant or forward fill) core.log1p value – yes – log(1 + x) of the named variables core.logit value – yes – Logit of proportions core.max_abs_scale value yes yes – Divide by the maximum absolute value over the named dims core.mean_scale value yes yes – Divide by the mean absolute value over the named dims core.replace_sentinel value – – – Turn sentinel codes into missing values core.saturation value – – – Saturation curve with fixed parameters core.standardize value yes yes – Standardise to zero mean and unit variance over the named dims

docs.title: core.calendar
docs.text:
Adds calendar facts such as the month or whether it is a weekend

version 1.0.0 · kind feature

- {id: my_calendar, use: core.calendar@^1, with: {...}}
Field Type Default Description along string time features list of day_of_week or day_of_month or day_of_year or week_of_year or month or quarter or year or is_weekend or is_month_start or is_month_end required min items 1, max items 10 out string calendar Schema effect template 
{
  "template_params": [
    "out",
    "along"
  ],
  "transforms_dims": {

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
modeling-api ships as three products, in this sequence:

  1. A typed modelling runtime.
  2. A job platform around the runtime.
  3. A hosted platform for many users.

Some rules make the hosted platform safe. These rules are in the code from the first release: no pickle, contracts in JSON only, static validation, sanitized plots, and sandboxed runs with verified outputs.

timeline
    title Releases
    v0.1 · M0 · contract layer : SDK, specs and schemas : 28 steps, PyMC and sklearn base classes : 11 built-in models, plots, sanitizer : conformance corpus
    v0.2 · M1 · local platform : HTTP API, queue, sandboxed runner : GCS shim, signed bundles : Expert web app, CLI, Python client : make dev and Docker Compose
    v0.3 · M2 · cloud and multi-tenant : tenants, OIDC sign-in, tokens, row-level security : quotas, fair share, cost ledger, kill switches : Cloud Run Jobs executor, Terraform : observability, security suite, chaos
    v0.4 · M3 · Guided mode and integrations : templates, question flow, business priors : scorecard, what-if, forecasts : endpoints, snippets, webhooks, embeds : sign-up, deletion, GDPR export
    v0.5 · M3.5 · workflows and governance : workflows of tests, transforms and models : governance policies and null tests : Data and Model Explorers : mmm-framework and statsmodels : About cards, Help me choose
    v0.6 · M4 · expert plugins and MCP (next) : plugin upload for allow-listed experts : curated MCP server : sweeps and SBC as parent runs
Release Milestone Theme Status v0.1 M0 The contract layer: specs, the xarray runtime, steps, models, plots and the conformance corpus. All of it runs in your own Python process. available v0.2 M1 The local platform: the same work as API calls and sandboxed runs, with the Expert web app. It runs on a laptop or on one Docker host. available v0.3 M2 Cloud and multi-tenant core: tenants, sign-in, tokens, quotas and cost. Each run gets one new sandbox on Cloud Run. This release is a private beta. available v0.4 M3 Guided mode and integrations: analysts go from a spreadsheet to a report and a scenario. Other apps get endpoints, webhooks and embeds. This release is the first public launch. available v0.5 M3.5 Workflows, governance, explorers, mmm-framework and statsmodels: automated, versioned analyses. Models must pass null tests and get the approval of a second person. Also budget plans, About cards and Help me choose. available v0.6 M4 Expert plugins and MCP: plugin upload for allow-listed experts, a curated MCP server for AI agents, and sweeps and SBC as parent runs. next

docs.title: What v0.5 contains
docs.text:
• Workflows: versioned DAGs of statistical tests, transforms, branches, split plans, order searches, model fits, evaluations, comparisons, governance and reports. Also live events, a cache, schedules and dataset triggers (cookbook).
  • Governance: versioned project and tenant policies and twelve checks. The checks include null tests against shuffled targets and placebo regressors. Also second-person approval, evidence packs and promotion that needs validation (null tests explained).
  • Data and Model Explorers, with side-by-side comparisons and Diebold-Mariano tests
  • mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, with budget optimisation in the sandbox
  • Twelve statsmodels time-series models
  • About cards on each item that you can select, and Help me choose (choosing a model)
  • The Python client and the CLI for all of these items
  • The screens of the web app for all of these items: the visual workflow builder, the run monitor, Guided recipes, the policy editor, the review queue, the explorers, About cards and the chooser, and budget plans

We verified these items end to end on a live local stack (M3.5 verification):

  • the canonical workflow
  • governance with a second person
  • mmm-framework with a budget plan
  • the explorers and the chooser
  • the CLI.

Some work is not done yet, the same as for v0.4. It includes a real Google Cloud project, Docker-isolated executors, and the sessions with five non-technical testers.

docs.title: What v0.4 contains
docs.text:
• Guided mode: four templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice). Also a question flow with role detection, drafts with "View as YAML", and the persona lock (tutorial).
  • Sandboxed ingest of CSV, Parquet, MFF and Meridian-shaped tables. Refusals are in plain language.
  • Business priors as ROI or share ranges. A sandbox translates them and shows a prior-predictive preview. Also lift tests as calibration (Guided modelling).
  • The sanity scorecard that each fit writes, and the promotion gate that uses it
  • What-if sliders over response grids for each draw, "Run exact", and forecast and counterfactual views
  • Endpoints and aliases, score:<alias> tokens, snippets in seven languages, and a Google Sheets card (Connect Google Sheets)
  • Signed webhooks with an outbox, retries, a delivery log, replays and an SSRF guard (Receive webhooks)
  • Saved plots, static renders and embed links (Embed a chart)
  • The endpoints of the Python client, and new CLI commands
  • Sign-up with e-mail verification and abuse controls, tenant deletion, the GDPR export, and a Cloud Armor policy
  • The Integrations hub, trust pages and admin additions in the web app

We verified these items end to end on a laptop (M3 verification). The exit of M3 also needs the sessions with five non-technical testers. These sessions are not done yet. Some work against a real Google Cloud project is not done yet, the same as for v0.3:

  • the [verify M0] checklist
  • cold-start measurements
  • public workspaces on an executor that enforces egress and DNS.

docs.title: Next: v0.6 · M4, expert plugins and MCP
docs.text:
Plugin upload for allow-listed experts. Experts upload their own model plugins. The platform builds them into hash-pinned overlays, with native wheels from a curated mirror. The contract kit checks each plugin on upload. Also fast dev overlays and a vetted tier of ported sibling models.

An MCP server gives AI assistants and agents a small, curated set of tools that are safe from injection. The tools list and describe models, score an endpoint, read a run and get a plot.

Budget optimisations already run as in-sandbox optimize jobs, and backtests run as workflow nodes (v0.5). Sweep and SBC each run as one parent. More.

docs.title: After v0.6
docs.text:
This is the planned sequence:

  1. Public code upload (M5): uploaded plugins for all tenants. This release needs these controls:

    • a separate execution project
    • signed base images
    • verification before code runs
    • Sybil controls
    • a takedown process
    • a rehearsed kill-switch drill
    • an external penetration test.

    The security suite must first be green for two weeks. 2. Scale and depth (M6). Each item comes when real usage needs it: - warm scorers for exact answers in less than one second - GPU and large-data executors - other clouds - recursive forecasting - chained models (full-funnel and KPI graphs) - a plugin marketplace with a consent model.

Dates

We cut a release when it passes its exit criteria, not on a calendar date. Read the changelog to see the changes that we released.

docs.title: Cloud and multi-tenant core v0.3
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.3 (milestone M2), a private beta

v0.3 makes the platform multi-tenant. It also gives the platform a cloud execution backend: each run gets one new sandbox on Cloud Run Jobs. The run protocol (bootstrap object, signed events, verified outputs, signed bundle manifests) did not change from v0.2. v0.3 adds the cloud versions of the local parts. All multi-tenant functions also run on a laptop (make dev). We tested the cloud parts against fakes. A short checklist of cloud behaviours waits for a real project. For instructions, read Administration, Authentication and Deploy to Google Cloud.

docs.title: One sandbox per run
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph SB["Fresh sandbox (one per run)"]
        direction LR
        SUP["Supervisor<br/><i>trusted · holds credentials</i>"] -->|"inputs"| W["Worker<br/><i>separate uid · runs the plugin</i>"]
        W -->|"outputs (claims)"| SUP
    end
    SUP -->|"signed upload"| OBJ[("Object store")]
    SUP -->|"HMAC-signed events"| EV["Events service"]
    OBJ -->|"server-computed hashes"| FIN["Finalizer<br/>verifies, then publishes"]
  • Isolation. Each run gets a new micro-VM sandbox (Cloud Run Jobs, gen2). A trusted supervisor holds the short-lived credentials of the run. An untrusted worker runs the harness and the plugin under a different user. The worker has no credentials and no network.
  • No egress. Sandboxes cannot connect to the internet, and they cannot use DNS. Data comes in and results go out only through signed URLs for one object.
  • Outputs are claims. The finalizer checks each artifact against the hashes and the object generation that the store calculated. Then it copies the artifact to a location where the sandbox cannot write. If a manifest does not agree, the finalizer rejects it as INTEGRITY_FAILURE.
  • Progress you can trust. Only the supervisor writes events. Each line has an HMAC signature and a sequence number. The status from the executor tells if a run is alive.
  • Long fits can resume. Segmented PyMC sampling writes checkpoints to the prefix of the run. Thus a preempted fit resumes where it stopped. (Checkpoints, partial runs and resume already work locally in v0.2.)
Local (make dev, Compose) On Google Cloud in v0.3 local-process / docker executor Cloud Run Jobs, a fixed inventory of base image × resource class Worker as your user (DEV_MODE_ISOLATION) Worker under its own uid, no_new_privs, in a microVM GCS shim with emulated principals Cloud Storage with IAM, VPC Service Controls Events from the supervisor's stdout pipe Cloud Logging → Pub/Sub push → POST /internal/events EC P-256 key in .local/keys/ Cloud KMS asymmetric signatures, same bytes The development IdP, 127.0.0.1 only OIDC for people, scoped tokens for programs

docs.title: Multi-tenant core
docs.text:
• Tenants and projects with role-based access. Postgres applies row-level security on each table. (In v0.2, each row and storage key already has tenant_id and project_id.)
  • Scoped API tokens with their own budgets, and quotas for each tenant in vCPU-seconds. Interactive and batch priority classes stop one big sweep from blocking the scoring of all other users.
  • A cost ledger for each run, which shows in the UI.
  • We already published the contracts for all of these functions. See Tenancy and authentication, Quotas and cost and the multi-tenant HTTP API.
  • Other backends connect through the same Executor protocol. Each backend must pass an executor conformance suite.
  • The infrastructure is code. Terraform sets up the control, exec, data and build projects and the VPC Service Controls perimeter. There are also deploy scripts and a GitHub Actions workflow. See Deploy to Google Cloud and Security hardening on Google Cloud.

Cloud Run Jobs executor describes the Cloud Run executor, the authenticated Pub/Sub event path, KMS manifest signing and the hardened Cloud Storage driver. We tested these parts against fakes. They did not run on a live cloud yet.

docs.title: What it means for plugins
docs.text: You do not change your code. The contract kit already checks the properties that the cloud needs: no pickle, deterministic bundles, typed errors, and the evaluate path is the same as the score path. If a plugin passes check_model now, it is ready for sandboxed execution.

docs.title: Expert plugins and MCP next: v0.6
docs.text:
Status: next (milestone M4)

v0.4 opened the hosted platform to declarative specs and built-in models. v0.5 added workflows, governance, the explorers and budget optimisation in the sandbox (what's new). In v0.6, allow-listed experts can upload their own model plugins. v0.6 also gives AI assistants and agents a curated MCP server. Sweeps and simulation-based calibration become single parent runs. Public code upload for all users comes after v0.6, with its own controls (see the roadmap).

docs.title: Plugin upload for allow-listed experts
docs.text:
Now, a data scientist can run their own PyMCModel or SklearnModel only on a deployment that they control. They install it into the environment of the runner. v0.6 makes this a product feature of a shared deployment. It is available to tenants that an operator put on the allow list:

flowchart LR
    A["mapi plugin push<br/>(your package)"] --> B["Overlay build<br/>source + pre-resolved wheels,<br/>pinned by hash"]
    B --> C["Describe run<br/>catalog entry, schema sanitizer,<br/>contract kit report"]
    C --> D{{"Kit passes?"}}
    D -->|yes| E["Runnable in your project<br/>on the pinned base image"]
    D -->|no| F["Readable report<br/>of what to fix"]
  • Overlays, not images. The platform builds a plugin into a hash-pinned overlay on top of one base-image version. The overlay has the source and wheels that were resolved before, including native wheels from a curated mirror. Runs never install software.
  • The contract kit runs on upload. The kit does the same checks as mapi plugin test on your computer. These checks decide if a version becomes runnable. The platform keeps the report with the version, next to its SBOM.
  • Schema sanitizer. The platform sanitizes the settings schemas of a plugin before the web app makes forms from them.
  • Dev overlays for fast iteration. The target is less than five minutes from push to a runnable version.
  • A vetted tier. We ported the sibling marketing-mix and HMM models as plugins. They are the proof that real models agree with the contract.

docs.title: An MCP server for agents
docs.text: The MCP server gives a curated set of tools to AI assistants and agents. For example, the tools list and describe models, score an endpoint, read a run and get a plot. The server returns each string from a user or a plugin as clearly delimited untrusted text. Thus a model name cannot put hidden instructions into an agent. Tokens and scopes work the same as for other clients.

docs.title: Sweeps as jobs, and what v0.5 already delivered
docs.text:
• optimize runs (delivered in v0.5). The sandbox optimises budgets next to the model with the planning module of mmm-framework. It uses the response curves of the posterior (Optimise a budget).
  • Backtests (delivered in v0.5) run as workflow nodes on rolling-origin and expanding-window plans (cookbook).
  • Sweep and SBC as one parent run that fans out and aggregates the results. For example, a sensitivity sweep over a prior, or simulation-based calibration of a new plugin. (The governance of v0.5 has a parametric-bootstrap version, recovery.simulated.)

docs.title: Exit criteria
docs.text:
• Three sibling models are packaged as plugins and pass the contract kit.
  • A dev overlay is pushed and becomes runnable in less than five minutes.
  • An as-of backtest and a sensitivity sweep each run as a single parent.

We cut a release when it passes its exit criteria. Read the changelog.

docs.title: Guided mode and integrations v0.4
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.4 (milestone M3), the first public launch

v0.4 builds on the multi-tenant core of v0.3. With v0.4, analysts go from a spreadsheet to a trustworthy report and a what-if scenario. They do not write YAML. Other applications can call fitted models through stable endpoints. v0.4 is the first public launch, cut line A. All persons can sign up and run declarative specs and the built-in models on their own data. Only trusted tiers can upload code. For instructions, read the Guided tutorial, the Integrations hub and Tutorials.

docs.title: Guided mode: organised around tasks
docs.text:
The app has two modes over the same ModelSpec. A toggle in the header changes between Guided and Expert. Each Guided screen has "View as YAML". Edits in Expert mode go back to Guided mode.

journey
    title An analyst's first marketing-mix model
    section Set up
      Choose "Geo marketing mix": 5: Analyst
      Upload a CSV, answer "which column is revenue?": 4: Analyst
      Enter beliefs as ROI ranges per channel: 4: Analyst
    section Run
      Watch plain-language progress, with an ETA: 5: Analyst
    section Decide
      Read the report and the sanity scorecard: 5: Analyst
      Drag what-if sliders, see bands update instantly: 5: Analyst
      Share a link or connect a spreadsheet: 4: Analyst
Shipped Where to read about it Four templates (geo marketing mix, weekly forecast, demand by store, customer choice) and a question flow with role detection Your first analysis in Guided mode Sandboxed ingest of CSV, Parquet, MFF and Meridian-shaped tables From a spreadsheet to a Guided draft Business priors (ROI or share ranges) translated in a sandbox, lift tests as calibration Guided modelling The sanity scorecard and the promotion gate Guided mode, Integrations What-if sliders over per-draw response grids, "Run exact", forecast and counterfactual views What if… The persona lock: projects that stay Guided-only The persona lock

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Endpoints and aliases with history, rollback and a frozen input contract; score:<alias> tokens Endpoints and webhooks Generated snippets: Python, TypeScript, curl, R, Apps Script, a notebook cell The Integrations hub, Connect Google Sheets Signed webhooks with an outbox, retries, a delivery log, replays and an SSRF guard Receive webhooks Saved plots, PNG/SVG/PDF renders in the sandbox and expiring embed links Embed a chart, Sharing plots The Python client's endpoints; the CLI's endpoints, webhooks, plots, guided, priors and tenant commands Optimise a budget, The Python client

docs.title: Trust and the data lifecycle
docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Self-service sign-up with e-mail verification, disposable-domain blocking, rate limits and Sybil flags for operators to review Sign-up and abuse controls Identity verification and cut line A at run admission Sign-up and abuse controls Tenant deletion that purges every store, and the GDPR export Deleting and exporting data A Cloud Armor policy on every load-balancer backend Security hardening

docs.title: The exit criteria
docs.text:
Criterion Where it stands Five non-technical testers go from upload to report to scenario without help in less than 30 minutes Prepared. An automated run takes 135 s of system time. We repaired the six usability defects that it found. We wrote the protocol for the testers. The sessions are not done yet. An external optimiser works against an endpoint Met on a laptop: +0.22 % revenue at the same budget against the live endpoint (details). From v0.5, the platform optimises budgets next to the model, in a sandboxed optimize run on mmm-framework planning (Optimise a budget). We removed the external-optimiser adapter. Cut line A: public launch of declarative specs and built-ins Met for admission. Sign-up workspaces are public, and the platform refuses uploaded code. Public runs need an executor that enforces egress and DNS (docker-gvisor or Cloud Run Jobs). This laptop could not run these executors.

We verified all items locally. M3 verification gives the numbers. It also tells which items still need real persons, Docker or Google Cloud.

docs.title: The local platform v0.2
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.2 (milestone M1)

v0.1 defined the documents that the platform accepts (ModelSpec, ScoreRequest). It also defined the error codes that the platform returns and the executor protocol that it controls. v0.2 puts an HTTP API, a job queue, a sandboxed runner, a local object store and the Expert web app around them. All of it runs on one machine. Start with the quickstart.

docs.title: What changed for you
docs.text:
Each thing that you do in a notebook is also an API call. The work runs in a sandbox, not in your process:

In your process (v0.1) On the platform (v0.2) validate_spec(spec, catalog, schema) POST /v1/specs:validate, all problems at one time with JSON pointers, and the live squiggles in the editor fit_spec(spec, data, ...) POST /v1/runs with kind: fit. Progress comes as server-sent events. score_bundle(bundle, request, data) POST /v1/models/{id}/versions/{v}:score with Prefer: wait A bundle directory A model version in a registry, with lineage, metrics, a scorecard, plots and a signed manifest InprocExecutor local-process and docker executors behind the same protocol 
flowchart LR
    C["Web app · CLI ·<br/>Python client · curl"] -->|"/v1 JSON"| API["API<br/>(validates from static JSON)"]
    API --> Q[("PostgreSQL<br/>runs · queue · events")]
    Q --> D["Dispatcher"]
    D --> X["Executor<br/>(local process / Docker)"]
    X --> R["Runner<br/>supervisor + worker"]
    R -->|"outputs + manifest"| S[("GCS shim")]
    R -->|"signed events"| API

docs.title: Design commitments, kept
docs.text:
• The API never imports plugin code and never decodes your arrays. It validates specs and score requests from the exported catalog JSON and stored metadata. An import-linter contract keeps numpy, xarray and all plugins out of the server. The build of the server image checks this contract against the installed packages.
  • Runs are idempotent and observable. Submissions have idempotency keys. The status from the executor is the source of truth. Events control progress bars. They never decide if a run is alive.
  • Errors are RFC 7807 problems with the same stable codes that you see in Python.
  • OpenAPI 3.1 describes each endpoint. CI checks the generated clients for drift.
  • Outputs are verified. The platform checks the outputs of a run against the checksums and generations of the object store. Then it copies the outputs to a location where runs cannot write, and signs them.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• The Expert web app, the CLI, the Python client and the HTTP API
  • Architecture overview and the security model
  • Deployment: make dev and Docker Compose

docs.title: Workflows, governance and explorers v0.5
docs.text:
Status: available in v0.5 (milestone M3.5)

v0.4 made one model easy to fit, read and share. v0.5 makes the analysis around the model repeatable and defensible. v0.5 has these parts:

  • workflows that run the statistics that a careful analyst runs
  • governance policies that make each model pass null tests before a person uses it
  • Data and Model Explorers
  • mmm-framework as the marketing-mix engine, with budget optimisation
  • twelve statsmodels time-series models
  • an About card on each item that a user can select.

For instructions, read What's new in 0.5, the workflow cookbook and Can you trust this model?.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: Shipped Where to read about it Versioned WorkflowSpec DAGs with typed ports, parameters, alternatives, branch gating and sub-workflows, validated with JSON pointers before anything runs Workflows 51 nodes: 17 statistical tests, 6 transforms, 7 train/test plans, 5 searches, fits, backtests, forecasts, evaluations, comparisons with Diebold-Mariano, selection, governance, reports Workflow node reference A safe condition language for branches and computed parameters (mapi_spec.expr, never eval) Conditions Server orchestration: per-node status, server-sent events, retries, caching of unchanged nodes, child runs, cost Where nodes run Cron schedules and dataset triggers Schedules and triggers A gallery: readiness to ARIMAX, VAR/VECM cointegration, governed MMM, forecast bake-off Workflow cookbook A visual workflow builder, a live run monitor and Guided recipes in the web app In the web app
