docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
The five journeys of v0.5 pass on a live local stack, with real fits in the runner and the real orchestrator. The journeys are:

  • the canonical workflow
  • governance with a second person
  • an mmm-framework fit with a budget plan
  • the explorers and the chooser
  • the CLI.

The runs found eight defects that unit tests and mocked tests could not find. We repaired each defect and added a regression test (M3.5 verification). The same as for v0.4, no part of v0.5 ran on real Google Cloud or in Docker yet.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text:
Each tutorial makes one thing work from start to finish. It gives the screens or the code that you need. The code is not only an example. Each Python snippet runs in the test suite. The Apps Scripts run against substitutes for the services of Google.

  • Your first MMM in Guided mode

    Start with a spreadsheet of weekly spend and revenue. Get the ROI for each channel, a sanity scorecard and a budget scenario, without code. It takes about ten minutes.

    For analysts. Start

  • Connect Google Sheets

    An Apps Script writes the forecast of a model into a sheet, with its likely range. It refreshes the forecast each morning.

    For analysts and integrators. Start

  • Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI

    Make a read-only link to the chart of a model, for a doc, a dashboard or a thread. The link expires. You also get a PNG for tools that cannot show live content.

    For analysts. Start

  • Receive webhooks

    Make a FastAPI or Flask receiver. It verifies the signature of each delivery and ignores duplicates. It does an action when a model is ready or when a run fails.

    For developers. Start

  • Optimise a budget

    Ask a fitted marketing-mix model how to divide a budget across channels. Learn about bounds, groups, cautious objectives, the uplift, the probability that it helps, and the efficient frontier.

    For data scientists. Start

  • A forecast that tests itself v0.5

    Make one workflow with unit-root tests, a differencing decision and an AR/MA order search. Add a rolling-origin backtest against naive forecasts, and governance. Run it with --watch and schedule it for Monday mornings.

    For data scientists. Start

  • Prove that a model does not fit noise v0.5

    Write a policy with null tests and validate a model version. Get the approval of a colleague and export the evidence pack. Then set the endpoint to refuse all versions that are not validated.

    For data scientists and reviewers. Start

  • Explore your data, then choose a model v0.5

    Read the quality warnings, stationarity views and lead-lag views of the Data Explorer. Then answer some questions in Help me choose. It gives a shortlist with reasons.

    For analysts. Start · Choosing a model

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A platform to talk to. All tutorials work against a local stack: make install && make dev && make seed (Quickstart). The Google Sheets and public-embed tutorials need a deployment that the internet can get to. The reason is that Apps Script loads from the machines of Google, and embedded charts load from the machines of your viewers.
  • A fitted model. The Guided tutorial makes one. make seed loads a demo marketing-mix spec that you can fit from the web app.
  • An endpoint, for Sheets and other tools. To put a model live, use the Guided Share step or the Integrations hub.

For more guides about tasks, see Guides. For the ideas behind them, see Concepts. Use cases shows which tutorials apply to which problem.

docs.title: Embed a chart in Notion, Slack or BI v0.4
docs.text:
Put the chart of a fitted model where people make decisions. Examples are the page for plans in Notion, the weekly thread in Slack, and the dashboard in Looker Studio or Power BI. An embed link shows one chart, read-only, to all persons who have the link. It works until it expires or until you revoke it. No person needs an account, and the link can read nothing else.

The link opens this page. It shows the chart, its caption in plain language, a PNG fallback and the expiry date.

docs.title: What can be shared
docs.text:
You can share only charts that the platform drew with one of its own recipes (core.*, mmm.*, ml.*, ts.*, choice.*). Examples are response curves, decompositions, forecast fans and scorecard charts. The platform refuses a chart that a plugin or a person wrote (EMBED_NOT_ALLOWED). The reason is that a shared link runs the specification of the chart in the browser of an unknown person. Only specifications that the platform wrote can do that. Share the other charts inside the project, or as a PNG.

A link points at one model version. Thus the chart does not change for your readers when the model is fitted again. If you want them to see the new version, share the chart of the new version.

docs.title: 1. Create the link
docs.text:
In Guided modeIn the Integrations hubPythonCLI
  1. On the last step, Share, select Share a chart.
  2. Select the chart.
  3. Create the link.
  1. Go to Integrations → Plots and links → Save a model plot. Alternatively, use Share in the plot gallery of a model version.
  2. Select the model, the version and the chart.
  3. On the saved plot, click Create link.
  4. Optionally, give it a label, an expiry and the sites that can frame it. The expiry is 7 to 365 days. The default is 30 days.
saved = api.plots.save(
    "EU response curves (v3)",
    model_id="mdl_01jaf3c1d2e3f4g5h6j7k8m9n0",  # the model version that drew the plot
    version=3,
    plot_id="mmm.response_curves",  # one of its plots: a platform recipe
)
print(saved.id, "embeddable" if saved.embeddable else "not embeddable")

link = api.plots.create_embed(
    saved.id,
    label="Weekly marketing review",
    expires_in_days=90,
    allowed_origins=["https://lookerstudio.google.com"],  # leave out: any site may frame it
)
print(link.url)  # shown once: paste it into the tool now
iframe = (f'<iframe src="{link.url}" width="900" height="520" style="border:0" '
          f'loading="lazy" title="{saved.title}"></iframe>')  # fmt: skip

mapi plots embed plt_01jaf3n1p2q3r4s5t6v7w8x9y0 \
  --label "Weekly marketing review" --expires-in-days 90 \
  --allow-origin https://lookerstudio.google.com

The platform shows the link and its <iframe> code one time only. It keeps only a keyed hash of the token, as for a password. Copy the link now.

docs.title: 2. Put it where people look
docs.text:
Tool How Notes Notion Type /embed, then paste the link. Keep sites that may frame it empty, unless you know which origin frames the embed (see below). Slack Paste the link in a message or a canvas. Slack shows links, not live frames. Readers click the link to see the chart. For an image in the thread, post the PNG (step 4). Looker Studio Use Insert → URL embed, then paste the link. If you restrict sites, permit https://lookerstudio.google.com. Power BI On a dashboard, use Add a tile → Web content. Then paste the <iframe> code. Reports have no built-in web frame. Use a custom visual that renders HTML, or use the PNG. Confluence, internal portals, any web page Paste the <iframe> code. In Confluence, use an iframe or HTML macro. Set width and height to fit the page. Slides, PDFs, e-mail Use the PNG (step 4). These cannot show live content.

Sites that may frame it. You can give a list of https:// origins. Then the embed page draws the chart only when the page that directly frames it is in the list. On other pages, it shows This plot can only be shown on the sites it was shared with. If you open the link directly, it always works. Some tools frame embeds through their own embed service. Then the check sees the origin of that service. If the notice shows, add the origin that the developer tools of your browser show as the parent of the frame. Alternatively, create the link without a restriction.

docs.title: 3. Check it
docs.text:
Open the link in a private window. You do not sign in, and you see one chart. From Python, you can get the same public view that the embed page reads. You can also get the list of the links of the plot, with their view counts:

view = api.plots.embed(link.token)  # what the link shows, fetched without credentials
print(view.title, "| expires", view.expires_at.date(), "|", view.plot.provenance.recipe)
for embed in api.plots.embeds(saved.id):
    print(embed.display, embed.label, embed.status, embed.views, "views")

EU response curves (v3) | expires 2026-11-14 | mmm.response_curves@1.0.0
mpe_7k2m9q… Weekly marketing review active 0 views

The list does not show a token again. It shows only the first characters of the token (display).

docs.title: 4. A PNG, SVG or PDF instead
docs.text:
For slides, a PDF report or a Slack thread, render the chart to a file. The render is a small sandboxed run (the runner role). When you download the file, the platform checks it against its checksum:

render = api.plots.render(saved_plot_id=saved.id, format="png", width=1200, height=600)
png = api.plots.download_render(render, Path("eu-response-curves.png"))  # CRC32C-checked

In the hub, the Download buttons of a saved plot do the same thing. On the command line, use mapi plots render --saved plt_… -f pdf -o chart.pdf. When you create a link with the runner role, the platform also renders a PNG. The embed page shows it as Open as PNG for tools that cannot show interactive content.

docs.title: 5. Revoke it
docs.text:
Revoke the link when the meeting is complete. Also revoke it if the link went to a location where it must not be:

api.plots.revoke_embed(saved.id, link.embed.id)  # dashboards showing it stop on next load

In the hub, click Revoke in the list of links of the plot. On the command line, use mapi plots revoke <plot_id> <embed_id>. Each dashboard that shows the link stops when it loads again. It shows This link has expired or was revoked. If you delete the saved plot, the platform revokes all of its links. If you delete the organisation, the platform revokes all links at the same time.

docs.title: What a viewer's browser can and cannot do
docs.text: The embed page comes from the origin of the plot sandbox, not from the origin of the app. It sends no cookie or credential. Its Content-Security-Policy lets it get the one public embed view and nothing else. The browser validates the view again, and the page writes each text as text. The view carries the data of the chart inline (up to 1.5 MB). Thus the page never touches storage. Rate limits for each link and for each address stop persons who try to scrape a link (Sharing plots).

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Connect Google Sheets to get the numbers behind the chart.
  • Sharing plots gives all the options to save, render and embed, with curl.

docs.title: Connect Google Sheets v0.4
docs.text:
At the end of this tutorial, a Google Sheet holds the forecast of your model, week by week. It shows the actual results that the model was fitted on, and the range of possible future values. The sheet refreshes itself each morning. No person needs to open the platform. The sheet holds only a token that can score one endpoint.

You need Where to get it An endpoint that serves a model that forecasts (a geo marketing mix or a weekly forecast) The Guided Share step, or Promote a model in the Integrations hub A platform that the internet can get to Apps Script runs on the servers of Google. Thus it cannot call a stack on 127.0.0.1. Use the deployment of your team. A Google account that can use Apps Script Any Google Workspace account or personal account

docs.title: 1. Create a token that can only score this endpoint
docs.text:
1. In the web app, open Integrations. The Google Sheets card lists your endpoints.
  2. Select your endpoint.
  3. Click Create a token. The Tokens page opens with the data for a score:<alias> token. This token can read and score that endpoint and nothing else.

Alternatively, use a terminal. This command also sets a rate limit and a monthly compute budget:

mapi tokens create sheets-forecast -s score:geo-mmm-prod --rate-limit 60 --budget 600

The platform shows the secret one time only. All persons who can edit the script can see the script properties of a sheet. For this reason, the token must be able to do only one thing: score this endpoint. You can revoke the token at any time on the Tokens page (mapi tokens revoke).

docs.title: 2. Paste the generated script
docs.text:
1. In the sheet, select Extensions → Apps Script.

  2. Replace the empty function with the code from the card. This code is the Apps Script snippet of the endpoint. It is also on the Snippets tab of the endpoint, and you can get it with mapi endpoints snippets geo-mmm-prod -l apps_script. For an endpoint geo-mmm-prod, the code is similar to this:

    // Extensions > Apps Script. Store the token once under Project Settings >
// Script properties as MAPI_TOKEN.
//
// Input (optional): a sheet named "Input" in long format - a header row naming the
// endpoint's dims and input variables, then one row per coordinate - replaces the
// example's inline data.
// The answer's summary (per coordinate) is written to a sheet named "Result", under a note
// on what a forecast was conditioned on.
function scoreGeoMmmProd() {
  const token = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("MAPI_TOKEN");
  const payload = {
    "future_covariates": "carry_last",
    "horizon": {
      "dim": "time",
      "periods": 8
    },
    "mode": "forecast",
    "output": {
      "kind": "expected",
      "summary": [
        "mean",
        "hdi_90"
      ]
    }
  };
  const inputs = null;
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  const input = book.getSheetByName("Input");
  if (input) {
    const key = payload.scenario && payload.scenario.data_vars ? "scenario" : "data";
    const zone = book.getSpreadsheetTimeZone
      ? book.getSpreadsheetTimeZone()
      : Session.getScriptTimeZone();
    const sent = mapiSheetToXr_(input.getDataRange().getValues(), payload[key], inputs, zone);
    const noRows = Object.values(sent.coords).every((c) => !c.data.length);
    if (key === "data" && payload.mode === "forecast" && payload.horizon) {
      // no row left: forecast the horizon's periods after the fitted history
      payload.data = noRows ? null : sent;
      if (!noRows) payload.horizon.periods = mapiForecastPeriods_(payload, payload.horizon.periods);
    } else {
      payload[key] = sent;
    }
  }
  const response = UrlFetchApp.fetch("https://api.mapi.example/v1/endpoints/geo-mmm-prod/score", {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer " + token,
      "X-Mapi-Project": "acme/growth",
      Prefer: "wait=60",
    },
    payload: JSON.stringify(payload),
    muteHttpExceptions: true,
  });
  const out = book.getSheetByName("Result") || book.insertSheet("Result");
  if (response.getResponseCode() >= 300) {
    const problem = mapiProblemRows_(response.getContentText());
    if (problem.length) {
      out.clear();
      out.getRange(1, 1, problem.length, 1).setValues(problem);
    }
    throw new Error(response.getResponseCode() + ": " + response.getContentText());
  }
  const result = JSON.parse(response.getContentText());
  out.clear();
  if (!result.done) {
    const note = "Still running (" + result.run.id + "): run the function again in a minute.";
    out.getRange(1, 1).setValue(note);
    return result;
  }
  const tables = mapiSummaryRows_(result.summary);
  if (!tables.length) {
    const why = result.run.problem ? mapiProblemRows_(JSON.stringify(result.run.problem)) : [];
    const rows = [[result.run.state + ": no summary in the answer"]].concat(why);
    out.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, 1).setValues(rows);
    return result;
  }
  const conditioning = result.summary.conditioning;
  const rows = conditioning ? [[conditioning.message], [""]].concat(tables) : tables;
  const width = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.length));
  const grid = rows.map((r) => r.concat(new Array(width - r.length).fill("")));
  out.getRange(1, 1, grid.length, width).setValues(grid);
  return result;
}

// The summary tables one below the other: a header row ("variable", the coordinate
// columns, the statistics), one row per coordinate, a blank row between tables.
function mapiSummaryRows_(summary) {
  const rows = [];
  for (const table of (summary && summary.tables) || []) {
    if (rows.length) rows.push([""]);
    rows.push(["variable"].concat(table.columns));
    for (const row of table.rows) {
      rows.push([table.variable].concat(row.map((c) => (c === null ? "" : c))));
    }
  }
  if (summary && summary.truncated) {
    rows.push(["(truncated: the full result is in the run's outputs)"]);
  }
  return rows;
}

// A problem answer (or a failed run's problem) as rows: what went wrong, what to do.
function mapiProblemRows_(text) {
  let problem;
  try {
    problem = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch (e) {
    return [];
  }
  if (!problem || !problem.code) return [];
  const first = (problem.errors && problem.errors[0]) || {};
  const rows = [[problem.code + ": " + (first.message || problem.detail || problem.title)]];
  if (first.suggested_action) rows.push(["What to do: " + first.suggested_action]);
  return rows;
}

// A long table (a header row, then rows) as an inline dataset: columns named like a dim
// hold coordinates, columns named like an input variable (`inputs`, else the example's
// variables) hold values (headers are matched trimmed and ignoring case); empty cells
// become null - in a forecast an empty target is a period to forecast - and numbers stored
// as text are numbers. Dates are sent as yyyy-MM-dd.
function mapiSheetToXr_(values, example, inputs, zone) {
  let vars = inputs;
  if (!vars && example && example.data_vars) {
    vars = {};
    for (const [name, spec] of Object.entries(example.data_vars)) vars[name] = spec.dims;
  }
  if (!vars) throw new Error("this endpoint's example call sends no inline data to replace");
  const norm = (h) => String(h).trim().toLowerCase();
  const header = values[0].map(norm);
  const rows = values.slice(1).filter((r) => r.some((c) => String(c).trim() !== ""));
  const used = Object.keys(vars).filter((name) => header.indexOf(norm(name)) >= 0);
  if (!used.length) {
    throw new Error("the Input sheet needs a column named one of: " + Object.keys(vars).join(", "));
  }
  const targets = [];
  const dims = [...new Set(Object.values(vars).flat())];
  const known = new Set(Object.keys(vars).concat(dims).map(norm));
  const unknown = values[0].filter((h) => norm(h) !== "" && !known.has(norm(h)));
  if (targets.length && !targets.some((t) => used.indexOf(t) >= 0) && unknown.length) {
    throw new Error(
      "the Input sheet has no column for " + targets.join(", ") + " (the actuals) but has " +
        unknown.map((h) => '"' + String(h).trim() + '"').join(", ") +
        "; the columns are: " + dims.concat(Object.keys(vars)).join(", ")
    );
  }
  const column = (name) => {
    const i = header.indexOf(norm(name));
    if (i < 0) throw new Error('the Input sheet needs a column named "' + name + '"');
    return i;
  };
  const cell = (v) => (v instanceof Date ? Utilities.formatDate(v, zone, "yyyy-MM-dd") : v);
  const number = (v) => {
    if (typeof v !== "string") return cell(v);
    const text = v.trim();
    if (text === "") return null;
    if (/^[-+]?\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+(\.\d+)?$/.test(text)) return Number(text.replace(/,/g, ""));
    return /^[-+]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?$/.test(text) ? Number(text) : text;
  };
  const coords = {};
  const index = {};
  for (const name of used) {
    for (const dim of vars[name]) {
      if (index[dim]) continue;
      const i = column(dim);
      index[dim] = new Map();
      const seen = [];
      rows.forEach((r, k) => {
        const key = cell(r[i]);
        if (key === "") {
          throw new Error("row " + (k + 2) + ' of the Input sheet has no "' + dim + '"');
        }
        if (!index[dim].has(key)) {
          index[dim].set(key, seen.length);
          seen.push(key);
        }
      });
      coords[dim] = { dims: [dim], data: seen };
    }
  }
  const data_vars = {};
  for (const name of used) {
    const dims = vars[name];
    const i = column(name);
    const value = (r) => (r[i] === "" ? null : number(r[i]));
    if (!dims.length) {
      data_vars[name] = { dims: [], data: rows.length ? value(rows[0]) : null };
      continue;
    }
    const last = dims.length - 1;
    const empty = (k) => coords[dims[k]].data.map(() => (k < last ? empty(k + 1) : null));
    const data = empty(0);
    for (const r of rows) {
      const v = value(r);
      if (v === null) continue;
      const at = dims.map((dim) => index[dim].get(cell(r[column(dim)])));
      let node = data;
      for (let k = 0; k < last; k++) node = node[at[k]];
      if (node[at[last]] !== null && node[at[last]] !== v) {
        throw new Error('"' + name + '" has two different values at one row of the Input sheet');
      }
      node[at[last]] = v;
    }
    data_vars[name] = { dims: dims, data: data };
  }
  return { coords: coords, data_vars: data_vars };
}

// The periods to forecast: the rows after the last one with a target value (every row
// when none has one); the horizon's own periods when the sheet ends with an actual.
function mapiForecastPeriods_(payload, fallback) {
  const dim = payload.horizon.dim;
  const labels = payload.data.coords[dim] ? payload.data.coords[dim].data : [];
  const filled = new Set();
  for (const name of []) {
    const spec = payload.data.data_vars[name];
    if (!spec) continue;
    const axis = spec.dims.indexOf(dim);
    const walk = (node, depth, at) => {
      if (depth === spec.dims.length) {
        if (node !== null) filled.add(at);
        return;
      }
      node.forEach((child, k) => walk(child, depth + 1, depth === axis ? k : at));
    };
    if (axis >= 0) walk(spec.data, 0, -1);
  }
  const order = labels.map((_, k) => k).sort((a, b) => (labels[a] < labels[b] ? -1 : 1));
  if (!filled.size) return labels.length || fallback;
  let after = 0;
  for (let k = order.length - 1; k >= 0 && !filled.has(order[k]); k--) after++;
  return after || fallback;
}

  3. Select Project Settings → Script properties → Add script property.

  4. Type the name MAPI_TOKEN. For the value, paste the token from step 1.
  5. Go back to the editor and select the function.
  6. Push Run. The first run asks you to authorise the script. The script connects to an external service and edits your spreadsheets.

A sheet with the name Result now holds the answer. The platform ran the example call of the endpoint (here, an 8-week forecast) in a sandbox. It returned the requested summary inline, with one table for each output variable. Each table has a header row and one row for each coordinate. The header row contains variable, the coordinate columns (for example geo and time), and then mean, hdi_90_lower and hdi_90_upper.

The payload is the example of the endpoint. The platform made it from the input contract of the endpoint, so it is valid without changes. The script waits for one minute. If the run takes longer, Result shows Still running. Then run the function again to get the result.

You can send your own data instead of the example data. To do this, add a sheet with the name Input in long format. The sheet has a header row with the dims and input variables of the endpoint. Then it has one row for each coordinate. The script reads the sheet into the call. This also applies to a forecast endpoint, although its example call sends no data. You use this sheet to add your latest actuals and the dates to forecast (step 5).

Here, the summary is for each coordinate, that is, for each market and week. The next step writes a different table. That table shows the history that the model was fitted on, next to the range of the forecast. The values are totals over all markets.

docs.title: 3. Write the forecast into a table
docs.text:
A forecast run also writes a small JSON table for Guided mode, ui/guided/forecast.json. The table holds the history that the model was fitted on. Then it holds the quantiles of the forecast for each period. This script gets the table and writes it into a sheet with the name Forecast.

  1. Replace the code with this script:

    // A forecast from a modeling-api endpoint, written into the sheet "Forecast": the weeks the
// model was fitted on (with your actual results), then the forecast with its likely range.
// Extensions > Apps Script: paste this file. Project Settings > Script properties: add
// MAPI_TOKEN (a token that can only score this endpoint).
const MAPI_URL = "https://api.mapi.example"; // your platform's API address
const MAPI_PROJECT = "acme/growth"; // <tenant>/<project>
const ENDPOINT = "geo-mmm-prod";
// The call: the "payload" of the hub's Apps Script snippet for your endpoint.
const CALL = {
  mode: "forecast",
  horizon: { dim: "time", periods: 8 },
  future_covariates: "carry_last",
  output: { kind: "expected", summary: ["mean", "hdi_90"] },
};

function refreshForecast() {
  const token = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("MAPI_TOKEN");
  // One score run per day: running this again the same day collects that run's result
  // instead of starting another (the platform remembers an Idempotency-Key for 24 hours).
  const day = Utilities.formatDate(new Date(), "UTC", "yyyy-MM-dd");
  const response = UrlFetchApp.fetch(`${MAPI_URL}/v1/endpoints/${ENDPOINT}/score`, {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer " + token,
      "X-Mapi-Project": MAPI_PROJECT,
      Prefer: "wait=30",
      "Idempotency-Key": `sheets-${ENDPOINT}-${day}`,
    },
    payload: JSON.stringify(CALL),
    muteHttpExceptions: true,
  });
  if (response.getResponseCode() >= 300 && response.getResponseCode() !== 202) {
    throw new Error(response.getResponseCode() + ": " + response.getContentText());
  }
  const result = JSON.parse(response.getContentText());
  const sheet = forecastSheet();
  if (!result.done) {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue(`Still running (${result.run.state}): run this again in a minute.`);
    return;
  }
  if (result.run.state !== "succeeded") {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue(`The forecast failed: ${result.run.state}. See run ${result.run.id}.`);
    return;
  }
  const link = result.outputs.find((o) => o.name === "ui/guided/forecast.json");
  if (!link) {
    sheet.getRange("A1").setValue("This endpoint's model wrote no forecast table.");
    return;
  }
  // A short-lived signed link: fetch it now, never store it. It needs no token.
  const view = JSON.parse(UrlFetchApp.fetch(link.url).getContentText());
  const fan = view.fan;
  const header = [fan.dim, `Actual ${view.kpi}`].concat(
    fan.quantiles.map((q) => (q === 0.5 ? "Median" : `${Math.round(q * 100)}%`)),
  );
  const rows = fan.coords.map((coord, j) =>
    [coord, cell(fan.observed && fan.observed[j])].concat(fan.values.map((row) => cell(row[j]))),
  );
  sheet.getRange(1, 1, 1, header.length).setValues([header]);
  sheet.getRange(2, 1, rows.length, header.length).setValues(rows);
  const units = view.units ? ` (${view.units})` : "";
  sheet
    .getRange(rows.length + 3, 1, 1, 2)
    .setValues([[`Forecast from ${view.split_at}`, `${view.kind} ${view.kpi}${units}`]]);
}

// An empty cell for a missing value (no actuals after the split, no forecast before it).
function cell(value) {
  return value === null || value === undefined ? "" : value;
}

function forecastSheet() {
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  const sheet = book.getSheetByName("Forecast") || book.insertSheet("Forecast");
  sheet.clearContents();
  return sheet;
}

  2. Set MAPI_URL, MAPI_PROJECT, ENDPOINT and CALL. CALL is the payload of the generated script.

  3. Run refreshForecast.

The Forecast sheet is then similar to this table. The numbers depend on your model.

time Actual revenue 5% 25% Median 75% 95% 2026-09-27 101.5 2026-10-04 98.2 2026-10-11 104.9 2026-10-18 88.0 96.3 101.2 106.4 114.9 2026-10-25 85.1 94.0 99.8 105.2 115.3 Forecast from 2026-10-18 expected revenue (kEUR)

Read the table as follows. In 90% of plausible futures, the week of 18 October is between the 5% and 95% columns. Half of the plausible futures are between 25% and 75%. The model adds the KPI over its other dims (markets, stores) for each posterior draw. Then it calculates the quantiles. For this reason, these ranges are honest totals and not sums of the ranges for each market. To make a chart from the table, use Insert → Chart. Use a line for the median and the actuals, and an area between 5% and 95%.

The script does these things, for these reasons:

  • One run each day. It sends an Idempotency-Key that contains the endpoint and the date. The platform keeps a key for 24 hours. If you run the script again on the same day, you get the same run. The platform does not start (and charge for) another run. If you change CALL, you get a 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT until the next day. To start again, rename the key.
  • Still running? Prefer: wait=30 waits for a maximum of 30 seconds. A cold start in the cloud can take longer. Then the sheet shows Still running. The next run of the script gets the result.
  • Short-lived links. The links of the result are signed URLs that expire after 15 minutes. The script gets the table immediately and does not store the link. The link does not need a token.

docs.title: 4. Refresh it every morning
docs.text:
1. In the Apps Script editor, select Triggers (the clock icon).
  2. Select Add Trigger.
  3. Select the function refreshForecast.
  4. Select the event source Time-driven and Day timer.
  5. Select a time of day.

Each morning, the trigger clears the sheet. Then it fills the sheet with a new forecast from the version that the endpoint serves on that day. Thus, when you promote a better model, the sheet updates. You do not have to change the sheet.

docs.title: 5. Add your latest actuals and future dates
docs.text:
The model was fitted one time, but each month gives a new actual. Type the actual into the sheet, and the next forecast starts from it. The model updates its state with the actuals. It uses the parameters from the fit and does not fit again. Then it forecasts the dates that you list (Forecasts with actuals). This works with the script from step 2. It works for each endpoint that has a model that can condition on actuals. The Sheets card and mapi endpoints schema tell you if the model can do this. The statsmodels time-series models can.

Add a sheet with the name Input, with one row for each period. The sheet has these columns:

  • The date column.
  • The target. Type a value where you have an actual. Keep the cell empty on the dates to forecast.

This example is for the monthly airline endpoint ts-forecast. The model was fitted on 1949-01 to 1960-12, with the target y and no drivers:

t y 1961-01-01 417 1961-02-01 391 1961-03-01 419 1961-04-01 1961-05-01

Run the function. The model updates with January to March 1961, and it forecasts April and May. Result starts with a note in cell A1. The note tells you the data that the forecast used. Then there is an empty row, and then the table:

Forecast updated with 3 actuals (1961-01-01 to 1961-03-01) after the fitted history, which
ends 1960-12-01; the model's parameters were not re-estimated. 2 periods forecast from
1961-04-01 to 1961-05-01.

variable   t            median   q5    q95
y          1961-01-01   …        …     …
…
y          1961-05-01   …        …     …

The rows of the actual months hold one-step-ahead predictions. These are the values that the model would have given in the month before. The empty months hold the forecast.

A model with drivers has a column for each driver. The model needs a driver value on each row, also on the dates to forecast. This example is for a monthly sales forecast with a price driver:

month sales price 2026-10-01 1520.5 9.99 2026-11-01 1610.0 9.99 2026-12-01 10.49 2027-01-01

The price of the last month is empty. Thus future_covariates: "carry_last" in the script uses the latest price that you gave again (10.49). The column names are the names of the endpoint. You can find them in these locations:

  • The Google Sheets card shows the layout of the selected endpoint.
  • mapi endpoints schema ALIAS lists the columns.
  • The generated script has a second function, score<Alias>InputSheet. This function creates the Input sheet with the correct header. It also adds the periods after the fit, all empty.
The generated script for the sales-forecast endpoint 
// Extensions > Apps Script. Store the token once under Project Settings >
// Script properties as MAPI_TOKEN.
//
// Input (optional): a sheet named "Input" in long format - a header row (month, sales,
// price), then one row per coordinate, dates as yyyy-MM-dd - is sent as the call's data.
// Fill sales with your latest actuals and leave it blank on the dates to forecast: the
// model updates its state with the actuals (it is not refitted) and forecasts the blank
// rows. Driver cells left blank on those dates are carried forward. Run
// scoreSalesForecastInputSheet() once to create the sheet with the periods after the fit.
// The answer's summary (per coordinate) is written to a sheet named "Result", under a note
// on what a forecast was conditioned on.
function scoreSalesForecast() {
  const token = PropertiesService.getScriptProperties().getProperty("MAPI_TOKEN");
  const payload = {
    "mode": "forecast",
    "horizon": {
      "dim": "month",
      "periods": 8
    },
    "data": null,
    "scenario": null,
    "output": {
      "summary": [
        "median",
        "q5",
        "q95"
      ]
    },
    "future_covariates": "carry_last"
  };
  const inputs = {
    "sales": [
      "month"
    ],
    "price": [
      "month"
    ]
  };
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  const input = book.getSheetByName("Input");
  if (input) {
    const key = payload.scenario && payload.scenario.data_vars ? "scenario" : "data";
    const zone = book.getSpreadsheetTimeZone
      ? book.getSpreadsheetTimeZone()
      : Session.getScriptTimeZone();
    const sent = mapiSheetToXr_(input.getDataRange().getValues(), payload[key], inputs, zone);
    const noRows = Object.values(sent.coords).every((c) => !c.data.length);
    if (key === "data" && payload.mode === "forecast" && payload.horizon) {
      // no row left: forecast the horizon's periods after the fitted history
      payload.data = noRows ? null : sent;
      if (!noRows) payload.horizon.periods = mapiForecastPeriods_(payload, payload.horizon.periods);
    } else {
      payload[key] = sent;
    }
  }
  const response = UrlFetchApp.fetch("https://api.mapi.example/v1/endpoints/sales-forecast/score", {
    method: "post",
    contentType: "application/json",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer " + token,
      "X-Mapi-Project": "acme/growth",
      Prefer: "wait=60",
    },
    payload: JSON.stringify(payload),
    muteHttpExceptions: true,
  });
  const out = book.getSheetByName("Result") || book.insertSheet("Result");
  if (response.getResponseCode() >= 300) {
    const problem = mapiProblemRows_(response.getContentText());
    if (problem.length) {
      out.clear();
      out.getRange(1, 1, problem.length, 1).setValues(problem);
    }
    throw new Error(response.getResponseCode() + ": " + response.getContentText());
  }
  const result = JSON.parse(response.getContentText());
  out.clear();
  if (!result.done) {
    const note = "Still running (" + result.run.id + "): run the function again in a minute.";
    out.getRange(1, 1).setValue(note);
    return result;
  }
  const tables = mapiSummaryRows_(result.summary);
  if (!tables.length) {
    const why = result.run.problem ? mapiProblemRows_(JSON.stringify(result.run.problem)) : [];
    const rows = [[result.run.state + ": no summary in the answer"]].concat(why);
    out.getRange(1, 1, rows.length, 1).setValues(rows);
    return result;
  }
  const conditioning = result.summary.conditioning;
  const rows = conditioning ? [[conditioning.message], [""]].concat(tables) : tables;
  const width = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.length));
  const grid = rows.map((r) => r.concat(new Array(width - r.length).fill("")));
  out.getRange(1, 1, grid.length, width).setValues(grid);
  return result;
}

// Creates the "Input" sheet: the header row and the periods after the fitted history, every
// value blank. Fill in what you know, then run scoreSalesForecast().
function scoreSalesForecastInputSheet() {
  const book = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
  if (book.getSheetByName("Input")) {
    throw new Error('There is an "Input" sheet already: rename or delete it to start over.');
  }
  const header = ["month", "sales", "price"];
  const rows = [
    ["2026-10-01", "", ""],
    ["2026-11-01", "", ""],
    ["2026-12-01", "", ""],
    ["2027-01-01", "", ""],
    ["2027-02-01", "", ""],
    ["2027-03-01", "", ""],
  ];
  const sheet = book.insertSheet("Input");
  sheet.getRange(1, 1, 1, header.length).setValues([header]);
  if (rows.length) sheet.getRange(2, 1, rows.length, header.length).setValues(rows);
  sheet.setFrozenRows(1);
}

// The summary tables one below the other: a header row ("variable", the coordinate
// columns, the statistics), one row per coordinate, a blank row between tables.
function mapiSummaryRows_(summary) {
  const rows = [];
  for (const table of (summary && summary.tables) || []) {
    if (rows.length) rows.push([""]);
    rows.push(["variable"].concat(table.columns));
    for (const row of table.rows) {
      rows.push([table.variable].concat(row.map((c) => (c === null ? "" : c))));
    }
  }
  if (summary && summary.truncated) {
    rows.push(["(truncated: the full result is in the run's outputs)"]);
  }
  return rows;
}

// A problem answer (or a failed run's problem) as rows: what went wrong, what to do.
function mapiProblemRows_(text) {
  let problem;
  try {
    problem = JSON.parse(text);
  } catch (e) {
    return [];
  }
  if (!problem || !problem.code) return [];
  const first = (problem.errors && problem.errors[0]) || {};
  const rows = [[problem.code + ": " + (first.message || problem.detail || problem.title)]];
  if (first.suggested_action) rows.push(["What to do: " + first.suggested_action]);
  return rows;
}

// A long table (a header row, then rows) as an inline dataset: columns named like a dim
// hold coordinates, columns named like an input variable (`inputs`, else the example's
// variables) hold values (headers are matched trimmed and ignoring case); empty cells
// become null - in a forecast an empty target is a period to forecast - and numbers stored
// as text are numbers. Dates are sent as yyyy-MM-dd.
function mapiSheetToXr_(values, example, inputs, zone) {
  let vars = inputs;
  if (!vars && example && example.data_vars) {
    vars = {};
    for (const [name, spec] of Object.entries(example.data_vars)) vars[name] = spec.dims;
  }
  if (!vars) throw new Error("this endpoint's example call sends no inline data to replace");
  const norm = (h) => String(h).trim().toLowerCase();
  const header = values[0].map(norm);
  const rows = values.slice(1).filter((r) => r.some((c) => String(c).trim() !== ""));
  const used = Object.keys(vars).filter((name) => header.indexOf(norm(name)) >= 0);
  if (!used.length) {
    throw new Error("the Input sheet needs a column named one of: " + Object.keys(vars).join(", "));
  }
  const targets = ["sales"];
  const dims = [...new Set(Object.values(vars).flat())];
  const known = new Set(Object.keys(vars).concat(dims).map(norm));
  const unknown = values[0].filter((h) => norm(h) !== "" && !known.has(norm(h)));
  if (targets.length && !targets.some((t) => used.indexOf(t) >= 0) && unknown.length) {
    throw new Error(
      "the Input sheet has no column for " + targets.join(", ") + " (the actuals) but has " +
        unknown.map((h) => '"' + String(h).trim() + '"').join(", ") +
        "; the columns are: " + dims.concat(Object.keys(vars)).join(", ")
    );
  }
  const column = (name) => {
    const i = header.indexOf(norm(name));
    if (i < 0) throw new Error('the Input sheet needs a column named "' + name + '"');
    return i;
  };
  const cell = (v) => (v instanceof Date ? Utilities.formatDate(v, zone, "yyyy-MM-dd") : v);
  const number = (v) => {
    if (typeof v !== "string") return cell(v);
    const text = v.trim();
    if (text === "") return null;
    if (/^[-+]?\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+(\.\d+)?$/.test(text)) return Number(text.replace(/,/g, ""));
    return /^[-+]?(\d+(\.\d*)?|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?$/.test(text) ? Number(text) : text;
  };
  const coords = {};
  const index = {};
  for (const name of used) {
    for (const dim of vars[name]) {
      if (index[dim]) continue;
      const i = column(dim);
      index[dim] = new Map();
      const seen = [];
      rows.forEach((r, k) => {
        const key = cell(r[i]);
        if (key === "") {
          throw new Error("row " + (k + 2) + ' of the Input sheet has no "' + dim + '"');
        }
        if (!index[dim].has(key)) {
          index[dim].set(key, seen.length);
          seen.push(key);
        }
      });
      coords[dim] = { dims: [dim], data: seen };
    }
  }
  const data_vars = {};
  for (const name of used) {
    const dims = vars[name];
    const i = column(name);
    const value = (r) => (r[i] === "" ? null : number(r[i]));
    if (!dims.length) {
      data_vars[name] = { dims: [], data: rows.length ? value(rows[0]) : null };
      continue;
    }
    const last = dims.length - 1;
    const empty = (k) => coords[dims[k]].data.map(() => (k < last ? empty(k + 1) : null));
    const data = empty(0);
    for (const r of rows) {
      const v = value(r);
      if (v === null) continue;
      const at = dims.map((dim) => index[dim].get(cell(r[column(dim)])));
      let node = data;
      for (let k = 0; k < last; k++) node = node[at[k]];
      if (node[at[last]] !== null && node[at[last]] !== v) {
        throw new Error('"' + name + '" has two different values at one row of the Input sheet');
      }
      node[at[last]] = v;
    }
    data_vars[name] = { dims: dims, data: data };
  }
  return { coords: coords, data_vars: data_vars };
}

// The periods to forecast: the rows after the last one with a target value (every row
// when none has one); the horizon's own periods when the sheet ends with an actual.
function mapiForecastPeriods_(payload, fallback) {
  const dim = payload.horizon.dim;
  const labels = payload.data.coords[dim] ? payload.data.coords[dim].data : [];
  const filled = new Set();
  for (const name of ["sales"]) {
    const spec = payload.data.data_vars[name];
    if (!spec) continue;
    const axis = spec.dims.indexOf(dim);
    const walk = (node, depth, at) => {
      if (depth === spec.dims.length) {
        if (node !== null) filled.add(at);
        return;
      }
      node.forEach((child, k) => walk(child, depth + 1, depth === axis ? k : at));
    };
    if (axis >= 0) walk(spec.data, 0, -1);
  }
  const order = labels.map((_, k) => k).sort((a, b) => (labels[a] < labels[b] ? -1 : 1));
  if (!filled.size) return labels.length || fallback;
  let after = 0;
  for (let k = order.length - 1; k >= 0 && !filled.has(order[k]); k--) after++;
  return after || fallback;
}

Obey these rules, so that the sheet does what you expect:

  • Dates are cells with a date format, or text in yyyy-MM-dd. The script sends them as yyyy-MM-dd in the time zone of the spreadsheet. The rows can be in any sequence.
  • Headers match without the spaces around them, and case is not important. Possibly the script cannot find the target column, and the sheet has columns that the script does not know. Then the script gives an error that lists the expected columns. It never gives a forecast that silently ignores your actuals.
  • Numbers stored as text (a pasted CSV, a Plain-text column) go as numbers. A cell that holds only spaces is empty. The platform refuses other text in a number column (#N/A) with SCHEMA_INVALID. The error names the column and the date.
  • No rows (only the header): the model forecasts the 8 periods after the fit, as without a sheet.
  • An empty target after the last actual is a date to forecast. If the sheet ends with an actual, the model forecasts the 8 periods after it (the horizon.periods of the call).
  • An empty target between actuals is a gap. The refusal ACTUALS_INVALID tells you this. This is not the case if the model accepts missing observations. The state-space models accept them and filter them as missing.
  • Actuals inside the fitted range replace the fitted values (a revised figure). The parameters stay as fitted. Fit the model again from time to time, so that the parameters learn from the new data.
  • A model that cannot use actuals refuses the sheet with ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED. It does not ignore the numbers. To forecast from the end of its fit, keep the target empty. Alternatively, fit the model again. The script writes the refusal and the corrective action into Result.

docs.title: When something goes wrong
docs.text: What the sheet or the editor shows Why What to do 401: … There is no token, or the token is revoked or expired. Examine the MAPI_TOKEN script property. Create a new token. 403: … The scope of the token is not score:<this alias>, or the project header is not correct. Create the token from the Sheets card. Examine MAPI_PROJECT. 404: … A person deleted or renamed the endpoint. Select the endpoint again in the Sheets card. 409: … with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT CALL changed after the first run of the day, with the same key. Wait until the next day, or change the prefix of the key. 422: … with MISSING_FUTURE_COVARIATE, or 409: … with HORIZON_EXCEEDS_FIT The call asks for something that the model cannot answer. Possibly it asks for future values that the model does not have, or for more periods than the model can forecast. Copy the payload from the snippet of the endpoint again. Make the horizon shorter. 422: … with ACTUALS_NOT_SUPPORTED (also in Result) The Input sheet has target values, and the model of the endpoint cannot update a forecast with them. To forecast from the end of the fit, keep the target empty. Alternatively, fit the model again with the new data. 422: … with ACTUALS_INVALID There is an empty target between two actuals. Alternatively, the actuals do not continue the fitted history, or a row with an actual has no driver value. Fill the gap, or remove the rows after it. Start immediately after the fit. Fill the driver. 422: … with SCHEMA_INVALID that names a column A target or driver cell holds text that is not a number (#N/A, n/a). Clear the cell, or type the number in it. failed: no summary in the answer in Result, and then the problem The API accepted the call, but the run failed. For inline data, only the run can do some checks. For example, one series of a panel has no driver on an actual month. (The API check sees all series together.) Read the problem line below it. Correct the rows that it names. the Input sheet has no column for y (the actuals) but has "sales" The header of the target column is not the name that the endpoint uses. Rename the column to the listed name. Copy the header from the Sheets card. the Input sheet needs a column named "t" The header of the Input sheet does not name the columns of the endpoint. Copy the header from the Sheets card. Alternatively, run score<Alias>InputSheet on a sheet without Input. 429: … with RATE_LIMITED or QUOTA_EXCEEDED The rate limit of the token, its budget or a project quota. Increase the limit or the budget on the Tokens page, or refresh less frequently. This endpoint's model wrote no forecast table. The call is not a forecast, or the outputs of the model have no KPI for a table. Use a forecast call. For other outputs, read the result with the Python client.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Embed a chart in a doc or a dashboard, next to the sheet.
  • Receive webhooks to refresh the sheet immediately when a better model goes live. Then you do not need a timer.
  • The Integrations hub gives all the snippet and token options.

docs.title: Optimise a budget
docs.text:
You have a fitted marketing-mix model (mmm.bayesian or mmm.frequentist). You must divide the budget for the next quarter. The platform answers with the planning module of mmm-framework, directly from the posterior of the model. It tells you how much each channel must get and how sure that is. It also tells you what each extra euro would buy. You do not need an external optimiser or a copy of the model in a different location.

You need: a ready model version of an MMM and a token with runs:create on the project. To get a model version, use the Guided tutorial or the marketing-mix guide.

docs.title: 1. Ask for a plan
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$API/v1/models/$MODEL/versions/$VERSION:optimize" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MAPI_TOKEN" -H "X-Mapi-Project: $PROJECT" \
  -H "Prefer: wait=60" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
    "budget_change_pct": 0,
    "channels": {"tv": {"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}},
    "objective": "mean",
    "frontier": {"n_points": 8}
  }'
  • budget_change_pct: 0 divides the current total again. Alternatively, give total_budget. To let the plan select the total, give mode: "free" with value_per_kpi.
  • Bounds keep the plan inside the data that the model has seen. Here, TV can move between half and one and a half times its current spend. Channels that are not in the list move inside default_bounds (0 to 2x).
  • objective: "p10" makes a plan for a cautious result instead of the expected result. The cautious result is the 10th percentile of the KPI across posterior draws.
PythonCommand line 
plan = api.models.optimize(  # mmm-framework's planner on the posterior; waits for the plan
    model_id,
    version,
    budget_change_pct=0,  # reallocate today's total
    channels={"tv": {"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}},
    objective="p10",  # plan for a cautious outcome, not the average one
    frontier={"n_points": 8},
)
assert plan.result is not None
for a in plan.result.allocation:
    print(f"{a.channel:10} {a.current_spend:>12,.0f} -> {a.optimal_spend:>12,.0f}")
uplift = plan.result.uplift
print("uplift", uplift.mean if uplift else None, "P(better)", plan.result.prob_positive_uplift)

mapi optimize model://growth/geo-mmm@v7 --change-pct 0 \
  --channel 'tv={"min_multiplier": 0.5, "max_multiplier": 1.5}' \
  --objective p10 --frontier 8

The command shows the plan as a table, and then the frontier. The table gives the current and recommended spend, the change and the return of the next unit. It also gives a note when a channel goes above the spend that the model has seen. --json gives the full Optimization.

The answer is an Optimization. If the sandboxed run finished within Prefer: wait, you get 200 with the plan. If not, you get 202 with the run. Then poll GET /v1/optimizations/{run_id} until done. The client and the CLI do this for you. They send the request again with the same Idempotency-Key, so that the platform calculates the plan only one time.

docs.title: 2. Read the plan
docs.text:
This is the result of a real plan. It is for the two-channel demo model from the Python client guide, with objective: "mean" and five frontier points. We rounded and shortened the values. The plan took 9 seconds of sandbox time on a laptop:

{
  "format": "mapi.optimize/v1",
  "objective_label": "expected KPI (posterior mean)",
  "kpi": "revenue_local", "kpi_units": "EUR", "spend_units": "EUR",
  "total_budget": 639176, "current_total": 639176,
  "allocation": [
    {"channel": "tv", "current_spend": 370845, "optimal_spend": 417971,
     "change_pct": 12.7, "marginal_roi": 3.48, "stability": 0.705, "extrapolated": false,
     "expected_contribution": {"mean": 1782506, "sd": 191376, "quantiles": {"0.05": 1479072, "0.95": 2104367}}},
    {"channel": "search", "current_spend": 268331, "optimal_spend": 221205,
     "change_pct": -17.6, "marginal_roi": 3.48, "stability": 0.705, "extrapolated": false,
     "expected_contribution": {"mean": 963528, "sd": 222208, "quantiles": {"0.05": 645055, "0.95": 1335924}}}
  ],
  "expected_kpi": {"mean": 16588448, "sd": 62359},
  "current_kpi": {"mean": 16578641, "sd": 43247},
  "uplift": {"mean": 9807, "sd": 42867, "quantiles": {"0.05": -60803, "0.5": 12370, "0.95": 70045}},
  "prob_positive_uplift": 0.625,
  "expected_regret": 45817,
  "shadow_price": 3.48,
  "frontier": [
    {"total_budget": 255670, "expected_kpi": 15069639, "kpi_p5": 14864907, "kpi_p95": 15285515,
     "marginal_roi": 4.12, "allocation": {"tv": 185422, "search": 70248}},
    "…"
  ],
  "n_draws": 200,
  "notes_plain": ["Frontier optimizes the expected KPI (posterior mean) at each budget; …"]
}

For this model, the honest answer is "move a small amount from search to TV, but do not expect much". On average, the plan adds about 10,000 EUR. But the 90% range of the uplift is from -61,000 to +70,000. Only 62.5% of the posterior draws prefer the plan. With the plan, the two channels return the same 3.48 for each extra euro. This is what an optimum looks like.

  • uplift is the KPI of the plan minus the KPI of the current plan, for each posterior draw. prob_positive_uplift is the probability that the change helps.
  • marginal_roi is the return of the next euro on each channel, with the plan. In a good plan, the channels that are not at a bound return about the same.
  • stability is the fraction of posterior draws whose own best plan moves the channel in the same direction. Low values tell you that the data cannot give an answer.
  • expected_regret is the KPI that you lose because you select one plan when there is uncertainty.
  • shadow_price is the KPI that the next unit of money would add, with this plan. extrapolated marks a channel that the plan pushes above the spend range in the data.
  • frontier shows the best plan at other totals. Invest while its marginal ROI stays above the value that a euro has for you.
  • notes_plain gives notes. For example, it tells you when the plan pushes a channel above the spend that the model has seen. Then the numbers of that channel extrapolate the response curve.

The plot of the run, mmm.budget_plans, compares the current allocation and expected KPI with those of the plan (GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/plots).

docs.title: 3. Check it with a forecast
docs.text:
A plan is the answer of a model. It is not a measurement. Before you commit, do these steps:

  1. Score the weekly spend of the plan as a forecast (mode: forecast, inputs_stage: weekly).
  2. If possible, test the largest move with a lift test.
  3. Add the result to the calibration block of the model, so that the next plan uses it.
